idea.name: Treasury hourly ladders: 1c/1c reward pairs on the unclaimed far strikes (KX2/5/7/10/30YRRATEH, $10 per strike-hour)
markets: 15-23 strikes 1 bp apart per hour; weekday hours (closes 07-20Z on 10-13/10-14; programs listed for 09-20Z on 10-15); one $10 liquidity program per strike-hour, target 1,000, discount 5000 bps; settle on the closing Pyth yield of the 1-minute candle before the hour, no averaging; no live bot trades these series
idea.mechanism: Each hour, on every strike whose YES side is empty (far above the yield) or whose NO side is empty (far below) -- in practice >= 6 strikes from the strike trading nearest 50c, so no yield feed is needed -- rest 1,000 at 1c on the safe side and ~1,100 at 1c on the dead side from a dedicated subaccount (~$21 reserved per strike-hour, released at the close). Both sides then hold >= 1,000, so every second counts, and by the filed walk (reference = first level reaching 200, cutoff at 1,000) our 1c stacks are the reference on both sides: ~100% of the dead side and ~95% of the safe side (the only other bids are 19-118 contracts at 89-99c), credit ~ $10 x (1 + 0.95)/2 = ~$9.7 per strike-hour. Orders carry expiration_ts = close-15 s (server-side expiry, no cancel race). Never re-post a side after it is swept (loss capped at ~$11 per strike-hour). The dead-side 1c bid crosses any resting 99c bid on the other side, so 19-118 contracts fill at 1c on arrival ($0.2-1.2): either allow that cross (ordercli forces post_only today) or post only where the opposite best bid is <= 98c. If both sides ever fill we hold a full set bought for 2c (pays $1,000+), so the worst case per strike-hour is one side swept, -$11. The index-ladders lane's 99c/1c version earns the same but needs $990 of collateral and loses it on a crossing -- dominated.
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi pays the pot whether or not anyone trades; nobody qualifies the far strikes because the safe side looks like it needs $990 of 99c collateral, while the filed rule is satisfied by a 1c stack. The one incumbent uses exactly this 1c/1c design but only on strikes within ~3 bp of the yield. Unpaid on 10-13 alone: $8,980 across the five tenors.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Kalshi credits a 1c/1c pair from ONE account -- not measured; consistent with the filing (no price exclusion since 2026-07-30), with the coin-race payment for a lone 1c YES side (+$11.04 to main pool 0, six legs at 98.5-98.9% of the formula) and with the incumbent's near strikes being paid 210 of 210 on 10-13. (2) Sweeps stay rare on far strikes (measured below). (3) Kalshi keeps the program: it can stop it any time, the CRO 'abusive or inconsistent with the purpose' clause is the real tail, and KXTEMPMIAH, the other big unpaid pot, was no longer listed at 07:4xZ 10-15. (4) The incumbent does not extend to every strike (then ~$5, not $10). (5) Payment lands in MAIN pool 0, so the main bot's bank-move checker will see unexplained cash and its size grows with it.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunters (10-13 ~11Z): 10Y 22 strikes, 7 qualify via 1c/1c pairs of 700-1,600, 14-15 have an empty side; 5Y 12 of 19 far strikes empty. Far-strike trade incidence over 94 settled 10Y strike-hours: 2 of 22 far strike-hours, each a single 600-lot 1c sweep (-$6); 5Y far 2 of 16; 30Y far 0 of 26; a 20-minute watch of 4 far 10Y strikes: one 100-lot sweep. 10Y 1-hour move over 2,379 windows: median 1.0 bp, p99 4.9, max 5.9 (CPI/FOMC hours 10-15 bp). MERGER RE-CHECK 10-15 07:4xZ (public GETs; .sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/merge-C2/rateh_hist.json): 4,578 RATEH programs ever listed, every one $10, target 1,000, max_reward_per_account null; 3,287 settled strike-hours (10-09, 10-13, 10-14). 10-13, flags complete: strikes >= 8 bp from the settled yield 0 of 453 paid, 4-7 bp 92 of 498, 2-3 bp 239 of 278, 0-1 bp 210 of 210; strikes >= 8 bp traded at all on 1 of 453 strike-hours (4-7 bp 29 of 498). 10-14 (CPI day): >= 8 bp traded on 34 of 440, 4-7 bp on 64 of 494; paid flags for hours after 09Z still unposted ~20 h later (0 of ~1,100), so the payment lag exceeds 20 h. 1,367 RATEH programs upcoming (10Y: 22 strikes x 12 h on 10-15). Distance is from the settled yield, not the live yield during the hour.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 if a one-account 1c/1c pair is not credited. If credited and alone: ~$9 net per strike-hour. Current bank (~$1,155 main; run from a ~$300 subaccount = ~14 pairs at once): ~$1,500/day theoretical, $300-1,000/day realistic while it lasts (copying and Kalshi's reaction will cut it). $5,000 bank: capital stops binding; the cap is the unpaid pool (~$9,000 on 10-13). Worst plausible day: every posted dead side swept once at the CPI-day incidence (8% of strike-hours) and nothing paid, about -$150 to -$200; arithmetic ceiling -$11 per strike-hour posted.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~1,000-1,450 strike-hours per weekday across the 5 tenors (1,439 on 10-13); 0 on weekends and bond holidays
idea.test_plan: LIVE PROBE (needs operator sign-off; the read-only steps are done): a fresh subaccount with ~$80; 3 consecutive hours on 3 far 10Y strikes (>= 6 strikes from the ~50c strike, opposite side empty): 1,000 NO at 1c + 1,100 YES at 1c (or the mirror on far-below strikes), expiration_ts = close-15 s, no re-post after a sweep. Expected if paid and alone: 9 x ~$9.7 = ~$87. Read main pool 0 unexplained cash (the detector that worked on 10-11) and the 9 programs' paid_out flags >= 48 h after the last hour. PASS: >= $45 credited AND sweep + crossing cost <= $15. FAIL: < $9 credited -> stop the lone-pair family (C2-06's sniper leg dies with it). Max loss ~$100 theoretical (9 x $11), ~$5 realistic.
idea.prior_reason: Largest expected $/day in this merge by far; the one unknown is binary (is a one-account 1c/1c pair paid) and the rule text plus the coin-race payment make yes more likely than not; fill cost is measured near zero on far strikes (1 of 453 traded on a normal day, 34 of 440 on CPI day); an $80, 3-hour probe decides it within ~2 days. Discounted for program risk (Miami's pot vanished) and decay once copied.

index-ladders: Hourly Treasury-yield ladders: far-rung two-sided resting for the unclaimed $10/market-hour reward
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No ledger row touches the hourly Treasury ladders (listed 2026-10-09). SI04/SI15/SI16/SI19/SJ36/U16 were killed or parked on pots read 100x too small or on Miami, where the 99c safe-side buyer sweeps a dead-side bid in minutes. idea.worst_case: -$11 per strike-hour posted if its dead side is swept (both sides filling is a riskless full set); program cancelled after Kalshi notices = $0 reward, no loss; account-level reward eligibility revoked under the CRO clause (would also end any other reward bot).

test.method: Public GETs only, about 720 calls; no orders, no auth, no git. (1) Pulled every KX2/5/7/10/30YRRATEH market (4,711 rows, of which 3,287 are settled strike-hours on 10-09, 10-13 and 10-14) and every RATEH incentive program (4,578, the full 65-page history). (2) Defined far strike-hours EX-ANTE as >= 6 bp from the previous hour's settle, which is what a bot knows at the open; the first hour of each day is dropped. That gives 1,253. For every far strike-hour that was paid or traded (58, so every sweep is counted) plus a seeded random 260 of the 1,195 untouched ones (weight 4.6), I pulled 1-minute candles (top of book) and the full trade tape. (3) Presence = minutes in which the dead-side best bid was exactly 1c, i.e. a stack like ours. A sweep = a trade where the dead-side bid was the maker (taker bought the safe side at 95-99c); trades within 10 s count as one sweep. 14 strike-hours where the strike came back into play are left out of the hazard. (4) Hazard = sweeps per weighted hour of 1c presence. Economics of the hunter's rule (post at the open, hold to close-15 s, never re-post): E[reward] = $9.3 x (1-e^-lamT)/(lamT), E[cost] = P(swept) x $11. Self-tests pass, both on the presence/sweep counters and on the hazard formula against simulated data with a known hazard. Fit = 10-09 + 10-13; test = 10-14 (CPI day). Sources are the trade tape plus Kalshi candles; no replay. Scripts and data are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C2-01/ (pull1.py, pull2.py, analyze.py, analyze2.py, analyze3.py, far_analyzed.json, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 1,253 far strike-hours (ex-ante >= 6 bp) out of 3,287 settled; 318 pulled in detail; about 75 (weighted) had a 1c dead-side stack
test.n_independent_clusters: 31 trading hours over 3 days. 1c stacks at >= 8 bp appeared in only 4 distinct hours and were swept in 3 of them, one on each of the 3 days. At 6-8 bp they appeared in 7 distinct hours and were swept in 3. The five tenors move together, so each hour is about 1-2 independent observations.
test.result:
THE HUNTERS' KEY NUMBER WAS AN ARTEFACT. '1 of 453 far strike-hours traded' was measured on strikes whose dead side was EMPTY: only ~8% of far strike-hours had any dead-side bid at all, and ~6% had a 1c one, so there was nothing for a 99c buyer to hit. Given a 1c dead-side stack is resting, the numbers are:
- ALL far strikes: 29 sweeps over 19.7 stack-hours = 1.47 per hour (90% high 1.99), so 76% of stacks are swept within the hour. Net if paid and alone: -$3.48 per strike-hour (fit -$2.73, test -$3.85).
- >= 8 bp (where the 'unclaimed' pot is): 23 sweeps over 5.5 h = 4.2 per hour, so 98% are swept; 15 of 21 within 43-225 s of the stack appearing. Net -$8.59 per strike-hour even if paid and alone (fit -$10.39, test -$7.44).
- By direction: far-above (NO safe) 9.1 per hour, far-below 1.1 per hour.
- 6-8 bp: 6 sweeps over 14.2 h = 0.42 per hour (90% high 0.80), so 34% are swept, all 15-50 min after the stack appeared (505-1,920 s left). Net +$3.88 per strike-hour (fit +$7.04 on 1 sweep in 6.3 h; test on CPI day +$1.81, -$2.55 at the high hazard).

Sweeps take the WHOLE stack: 25 of 29 were >= 500 lots (other farmers' 600s and 1,600s), so our 1,100 would go whole at -$11.

Paid far strike-hours: 28 of 1,253 (10-09: 23, 10-13: 5, 10-14: 0). The 10-09 far qualifier had its 600-lots swept within about 3 min and pulled the rest.

Payment lag: 10-14 hours from 10Z on are still 0 of ~1,100 flagged paid about 22 h later; the 07-09Z hours were flagged.

Program continuity: no RATEH programs were listed for 10-16 yet at 08:2xZ on 10-15.

AS FILED THE IDEA IS DEAD. Only a narrowed 6-8 bp band survives as a hypothesis, and it is still gated on whether Kalshi pays a one-account pair, which is not measured.
test.artefact_checks: (a) The unconditional trade count looks at the wrong population (empty dead sides), so I replaced it with the hazard conditional on a 1c stack. (b) Candles give the top-of-book price, not its size. Presence may therefore include small bids, which would bias the hazard LOW (the kind direction). The sweep sizes (600/1,600) show the swept stacks were large. (c) Candles are sparse, so the last value is carried forward; each minute's high/low is used to catch presence inside the minute. (d) Strikes are selected ex-ante from the previous settle, not the settled yield, so there is no look-ahead in which strikes we would post. The |settled distance| < 4 bp exclusion applies only to the hazard denominator. (e) The untouched stratum is weighted 4.6; every sweep is counted. (f) Hand check at >= 8 bp: e^-(4.19 x 0.979) = 1.6% survive; reward 9.3 x 0.24 = $2.23; cost 0.98 x 11 = $10.8; net -$8.6, which matches. (g) NOT measured: whether Kalshi pays a 1c/1c pair from one account; today's book sizes (no RATEH market opens before 09:00Z on 10-15, and the snapshot found 0 open); the 10-15 hours. Ticker T07 is 2.5 KB against 3.3 MB at T06; orderbook_delta T07 is 14 KB against 211 MB; there are no T08 ticker/trade/delta files at 08:25Z. Disk: 124 GB free.
test.supply_we_would_get: This is a reward pot, not fills: $10 per strike-hour on KX2/5/7/10/30YRRATEH. The 6-8 bp band has about 200 strike-hours per weekday across the 5 tenors (10-13: 203; 10-14: 214), 10-19 per hour; only 5 of 203 were paid on 10-13, so it is mostly unclaimed. The >= 8 bp strikes have about 370 a day but cannot be captured, because a stack there is swept in about 2-3 min. The fills we WOULD get are whole-stack sweeps by 99c safe-side buyers: on about 34% of 6-8 bp strike-hours and about 98% at >= 8 bp.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: As filed (>= 6 strikes out, which is mostly >= 8 bp) it is NEGATIVE: about -$8.6 per strike-hour posted even if paid, and a $300 subaccount posting 14 an hour loses about $150 an hour. For the narrowed 6-8 bp band, IF the one-account pair is paid and we are alone: point +$3.88 x ~150 strike-hours = about $580/day, with a 90% low end of about $70/day. Weighting for the unknown payment (about 0.5) and for sweepers adapting or copying gives about $50-150/day; that is an estimate, not a measurement. If the pair is not paid: -$3.73 per strike-hour.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Same as now. The limit is the 6-8 bp band (about 200 strike-hours a day x $21 reserved = $210-400 tied up at once), not capital. About $50-150/day after weighting for the risks above; about $580/day ceiling if paid, alone, and the 0.42 per hour hazard holds.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: The 6-8 bp hazard rests on 6 sweeps in 14.2 stack-hours (fit period: 1 in 6.3 h). Its 90% upper bound is 0.80 per hour overall and 0.63 per hour in the fit period. The data cannot tell 0.2 per hour from 0.8 per hour, and that range spans +$7 down to +$0.45 net per strike-hour. At >= 8 bp there are 23 sweeps; the 90% lower bound on the hazard is about 2.9 per hour, which still gives net <= -$7 per strike-hour. That kill holds even at the bound.
test.worst_case: As filed: every far stack is swept within minutes, so -$11 per strike-hour posted, limited only by the subaccount balance (a $300 sub is gone in about 2 hours). The hunter's -$150 to -$200 worst day used the empty-side trade count and is too small. 6-8 bp version: in the CPI hour on 10-14, 5 of about 214 strike-hours moved through the strike (our safe-side 1c bid filled, -$10 each), and sweeps ran 46%+. Worst plausible day running unattended is about -$300, capped by the sub's balance. Kalshi can pull the program at any time, and the Chief Regulatory Officer's 'abusive' clause applied to a one-account 1c/1c pair is the risk at the level of the whole account.
test.next_test: (1) Read-only recorder, 2 normal weekdays with no CPI/PPI/FOMC/NFP/auction hours. Poll the books of strikes 6-9 bp from the yield on 10Y, 5Y and 2Y once a minute (about 0.6 GET/s). Log every 1c dead-side stack's size, start and end, and whether it ended in a sweep. PASS: hazard <= 0.5 per hour for >= 1,000-lot stacks, over >= 20 stack-hours in >= 10 distinct hours. (2) Only then the live probe, which needs operator sign-off: 3 strikes at 6-7 bp (NEVER >= 8 bp) for 3 normal hours, 1,000 safe + 1,100 dead at 1c, expiration_ts = close-15 s, no re-post. Read main pool 0 and the paid flags >= 48 h afterwards (the measured payment lag is > 22 h). PASS: >= $45 credited AND sweep cost <= $25. FAIL: < $9 credited, which kills the whole lone-pair family. Max loss about $100; expected sweep cost about $34. The hunter's original probe on far 10Y strikes would mostly measure sweeps, not payment.

refs.strongest_objection:
Whether this makes money depends on a sweeper bot that comes and goes and hits all five tenors in the same hour.
- On 10-09 at 19:30Z it took 7 stacks across all 5 tenors with 28-30 min left.
- On 10-14 it swept in each of 8 straight hours (12:59-19:59Z). In the zone where distance / sqrt(min left) is 0.9 or more, it took 38 stacks of 500+ lots over 22 stack-hours.
- On 10-13 it took none.

On the latest full day (10-14), the filed hold-to-close rule at 6-8 bp nets between -$2.24 and +$2.36 per strike-hour, even if paid and alone, depending on the hazard model. That is about break-even, not the tester's +$3.88.

Posting ~150 stacks a day would hand that bot about $10.2 per sweep (1,100 x 1c, less its $0.77 fee). So the good quiet-day numbers are the ones least likely to last.

The sweeps are correlated across tenors: our ~14 stacks at once act as 1-2 bets per hour, not 14. Worst plausible day (sweeper active and the pair not paid): about 0.7 x $11 x 14 = ~-$110 an hour, so a $300 subaccount is gone in about 3 hours.

Other execution problems:
- Today (10-15) the yields fell 6-9 bp overnight. Strikes are set once at 06:54Z for all 12 hours, so 71 of 118 strikes are 8 bp or more away and only 10 sit in the 6-8 bp band (20 if the ladder were centred). The previous-settle rule mislabels the first hour.
- Placeholder bids at 89c x 200 on the strikes nearest the yield push the reference to 89c, which scores our 1c safe side at about 0.
- On every far 30Y strike someone already rests NO 1c x ~814, so our safe-side share there is ~53%, not 95%. NO 99c x 76-83 bids are also there, and a post-only 1c YES bid would cross them.
- Anyone resting 1,000 at 2c takes the whole safe side.
- Payment of a one-account 1c/1c pair is still not measured, and the paid flags lag more than 22 h.

The fix the data points to: cancel about 20-30 min before the close instead of holding to the close, and stop for the day after the first far sweep.
refs.independent_number:
My own pull of every settled RATEH strike-hour, with no sampling: 3,287 candle sets plus the full trade tape of all 205 far strike-hours that traded or had a 1c stack (about 790 public GETs, no orders).

With the tester's band (6-8 bp from the previous settle) I get 7 sweeps of 500+ lots over 16.8 stack-hours = 0.42 per hour, which matches the tester exactly. But:
- All 7 are on 10-14, in 2 distinct hours.
- By minutes left, the hazard is 0 with 30-61 min left, then 0.5 / 1.1 / 3.0 per hour with 20-30 / 10-20 / 0-10 min left. Owners cancel early, so late exposure is under-counted.

So a stack held to the close is swept on 10-14:
- 51% of the time with those bucket hazards (model B)
- 71% with hazard by live distance x minutes left, using the yield read off the ladder (model A)
- not the 34% that the constant hazard implies.

Net per strike-hour on 10-14, if paid and alone: +$2.36 (model B) / -$2.24 (model A). Cancelling at 20 min left instead: +$5.32 / -$0.68 (swept 8% / 52%).

Walk-forward check (model A): a hazard fit on 10-09 + 10-13 predicts +$2.25 for 10-14, but 10-14's own hazard gives -$2.24.

Model-free floor on 10-14 (owners may cancel first, so the true share is higher): of stacks present at 45 min left, 15 of 17 at 5-6 bp and 4 of 13 at 6-8 bp were swept later.

refs.strongest_objection:
The +$3.88 per strike-hour that keeps the 6-8 bp band alive assumes the sweep rate stays the same all hour. That rate was measured on other farmers' stacks, and those owners take their stacks down before the end of the hour, and again seconds after a sweeper hits a sibling stack. A stack held to close-15 s can do neither.

My census of all 452 non-CPI band strike-hours (my own pull, no weights): 98 stack episodes, 89 ended with the owner pulling and only 1 reached the close. Stacks were up for 16.2 stack-hours, but only 0.75 of those were in the last 10 minutes. By time left, the sweep rate is:
- 0-0.25/h over the first 40 minutes
- 1.0/h at 10-20 minutes left
- 6.7/h at 5-10 minutes left, or 10/h if the 3 stacks pulled within 150 s of a sweep in the same hour count as swept

With that, the rule as specified (hold to close-15 s) nets +$0.27 per strike-hour if Kalshi pays the one-account pair and we are alone. It nets -$1.65 if the last 5 minutes look like the 5-10 minute window. The chance of being swept is 0.69-0.86, and the rule loses $7.6-9.5 per strike-hour if the pair is not paid. So +$3.88 does not hold.

The evidence is thin: 4 independent sweeper events in 10 distinct hours. Normal days (10-09 + 10-13) give 3.5 stack-hours over 4 hours and one partial hit (151.51 lots, $150 at 99c). That rate's 90% interval is 0.015-1.36/h, which straddles the 0.85/h break-even.

The tester's next tests inherit the same problems. A read-only recorder of other people's stacks has the same censoring, so it will understate the rate in the final minutes. The planned close-15 s probe should expect about $60-85 of sweeps over its 9 strike-hours, which fails its own sweep-cost bar of $25 or less even if the pair is paid. Fix: have the orders expire 10 minutes before the close (server-side expiry). On the same data that gives +$4.07 if paid and -$3.20 if not, but I picked it after seeing the time-left table, with no holdout, so it is a hypothesis.

Also:
- paid_out cannot be read as "someone earned at least $1". On 10-09 the 19:59Z hour shows 80 of 80 strikes paid, including far strikes whose 1c stack was up about 3 minutes, which is worth at most $0.51 by the filed formula, under the $1 floor. The probe must read cash in main pool 0, not the flag.
- One competitor holding 200 or more lots at any higher price on the safe side drops our safe-side share to 0 and our credit to $5 per strike-hour. I saw this live on 1 of 36 snapshots.

idea.name: Coin-race 1c reward filler v2: exit at 115 s by server-side expiry, $1.25 floor, size 1,100
markets: KXCRYPTOLEAD15M: 5 legs x 96 races/day, $20 per leg-window, target 1,000; programs listed ~1 day ahead (380 upcoming at 07:4xZ 10-15)
idea.mechanism: Same bot as the 10-11 live test (research/sweep/racereward_live.py): in the last ~300 s rest a YES bid at 1c on dead legs (best YES <= 3c, YES side < 1,000 without us, NO side >= 1,000, NO best <= 98c), earning the YES side's half of the $20 pot pro rata to seconds ($20 x 0.5 x seconds/900). Three changes: (1) expiration_ts = close-115 s so Kalshi's engine removes the order (the test lost $2.16 of its $12.45 fill cost to fills that landed after the cancel was sent, two cancel_404_still_resting events); (2) post only if the projected credit to the exit is >= $1.25 (the HYPE leg projected $1.04 and paid $0 under the $1 floor); (3) size 1,100 so a small fill cannot drop our side under 1,000 and stop the clock. Credit lands in MAIN pool 0 ~80 min after the window.
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi pays the pot (99.6% of coin-race programs paid). Incumbent 1c stacks are pulled ~3 min before close, leaving dead legs' YES side unqualified, so those seconds pay whoever fills the side. The cost is sellers dumping worthless YES into the 1c bid, which in our live test came almost entirely in the final 110 s.
idea.must_be_true: Fill timing beyond n=3 races: our 16 fill events (1,245 contracts) had 10 contracts with > 120 s left, 9 at 110-120 s, 1,226 (98.5%) at <= 110 s -- but the unconditional 7-day tape (661 races) has 58.5% of contracts sold into 1c YES bids BEFORE 120 s (203 per race in the 300-120 s window, 76 per race in 180-120 s), so the clustering may be 3 Sunday-morning races of luck or a bot that targets 1,000-lot bids; the tape includes sales into incumbent piles, so it is an upper bound on our cost. Dead legs must be postable: in the test 7 of 15 leg-windows stayed < 1,000 without us; at 11Z 10-13 every dead leg carried a 10-39k pile at 1-5c (blocks the rule). The live coin-race TAKER on the main account (20 a leg) must never buy a dead leg's NO at 99c into our own subaccount's 1c YES bid (cross-subaccount self-trade, a wash-trading question; check Kalshi's STP scope).
idea.evidence_so_far: Live 10-11, 3 races, 7 legs: paid $11.04 vs $12.23 model (six legs at 98.5-98.9% of the filing's formula, reconciled to the cent; HYPE $1.04 projected paid $0); fills -$12.45 at a 60 s exit. Same fills re-cut by exit: 120 s -> fills $0.10 vs credit $8.62 (+$8.52); 110 s -> $0.16 vs $9.09 (+$8.93); 60 s -> $12.45 vs $12.07 (-$1.41). test.method:
I rebuilt every Coin Race (KXCRYPTOLEAD15M) leg's order book, second by second, for its last 400 s, from OUR tape: the orderbook_snapshot with levels about 1 min after open, then orderbook_delta (same sid, seq > snapshot), plus 1c sales from the trade channel. Streamed one hour at a time (~40 MB). Days 2026-10-08..10-13 plus 10-15 04-07Z: 2,840 legs. Results came from public /markets (7,260 legs). Program coverage came from paging all /incentive_programs (330 public calls): 24,765 coin-race programs, every one $20 (200000 centi-cents) with a 1,000 target; 96 races a day except Thursdays 03-05 ET (88). I replayed racereward_live.py's rule with the three v2 changes:
- last 360 s; one 1c YES bid of 1,100 at the first second where others' best YES <= 3c, others' YES < 1,000, best NO <= 98c, NO >= 1,000, and projected credit to the exit >= $1.25
- live 1 s later; cancelled if best YES > 5c; removed by the exchange at close-115 s
Credit uses the filing's walk per second x $20/1,800 x 0.987 (the 10-11 payment match), and $0 under the $1.00 floor. I priced our fill cost five ways:
- low / mid / high: queue models on the tape's 1c sales
- x99: high, plus every NO bid ADDED at 99c while we rest (each would have crossed our bid); needed a 4-day re-extract
- latent: the per-second rate at which dead-leg 1c piles of >= 1,100 got sold into, capped at 1,100, applied to our window
Then I applied the bot's real money rail (f): a $30 day budget with every fill counted as lost and credits invisible (they land in main pool 0). Holdout = first half of races vs second half. The parameters were pre-registered by the hunter, not fitted here, so this is a stability check. Sources: tape plus book deltas, calibrated against our own 10-11 live fills. Scripts and outputs are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C2-02/ (extract.py, extract99.py, sim.py, sim2.py, sim3.py, hourcut.py, *.out, RESULT.json).

refs.strongest_objection:
Not refuted, but nobody has measured the cost at the 115 s exit. The tape puts fills at 33-50% of paid credit, and only live fills can settle it. Two of the tester's pessimistic points are measurement mistakes.

(1) "The live run shows the plain tape understates our cost" is not a calibration. On the live legs themselves (10-11 races closing 04:30 and 04:45 ET, clean tape), the tape's 1c sales while we rested match our fills:
- SOL 225 vs 203
- ETH 222 vs 222
- BTC 220 vs 185
- ETH 73 vs 62

The 102%-vs-40% gap is three heavily dumped races set against a 551-race average. At the 115 s exit, those same live fills cost $0.16 against $10.88 of model credit.

(2) The tester's rail numbers are biased low, for two reasons:
- Its rail counts each resting order's eventual fills ON TOP of the order's $11 collateral, which double-counts and uses future fills. The bot's rails_refusal counts at most $11 per order.
- Its full-day filter (at least 80 races) dropped 10-13 (79 races), the cheapest day. So "x99 -$11/day" rests on 10-11 and 10-12 alone.

Against the idea:
- Orders that cross a 1c bid do exist: NO-99c adds paired with a 1c sale in the same second show up every day, 2-33 seconds a day.
- Removing cancel-and-replace re-posts cuts only about 3% of the x99 cost, so about 48-50% of credit is a real cost estimate.
- The newest 8 races (10-15, 00-03 ET) cost 71-79% of credit.
- In the 04:45 ET race, a seller hit each of our two 1,000-lots for 215 contracts between 60 and 115 s left. The same race's other dead legs got 20 and 60. So a seller who targets big bids exists, and may start earlier once we exit at 115 s.
- The HYPE leg paid $0 although the model gave $1.03 after the 0.987 factor.
- If Kalshi stops paying, the bot loses up to $30 a day until someone notices, which can take 16-40 h.

refs.strongest_objection:
We still have not measured what this costs on OUR fills at a 115 s exit; the only live run is 3 races. My other limits and findings:
- **My 18% cost is a floor.** I read the books every 15 s, so I miss 99c NO bids that last less than 15 s. The tester counted every book change and got 30-40% for 04-20 ET and 69% for 00-04 ET. My poll does not contradict that.
- **The 1,100 size gives no cushion.** On 4 of my 19 placed legs, a NO bid of 100-101 at 99c sat on the book. Each one would cross our 1c bid and leave us 999, under the 1,000 target, so that leg's seconds stop counting.
- **The v2 expiry fix rests on a misread.** On 10-11 every fill printed BEFORE our cancel went out: BTC 196 at 62.8 s left, HYPE 20 at 74.8 s, cancels sent at 59.9 s. On all 6 cancels, Kalshi's "reduced by" equals 1,000 minus what was filled. The $2.16 "leak" was the bot's own fill check, which it stops making in the last 15 s before the exit.
- **Wrong field name.** On POST /portfolio/events/orders the field is `expiration_time`, not `expiration_ts`. Kalshi's docs do not say when an expired order is actually removed. Server-side expiry is still worth adding to protect against a crash: after our 10-11 exit, sellers dumped 1,000 + 975 at 46 s left and 707 + 227 at 40-35 s.
- **The $30 day budget caps the money.** With it unchanged, net per day is about $19-25 x (credit / cost - 1), whatever the live test shows.

idea.name: FX 15-minute reward share grab: 300 a side at the scoring references (EURUSD and GBPUSD first, commodities only after)

idea.mechanism: The filed walk scores only the levels from the best bid down to where cumulative size reaches the 300 target (reference where it reaches 60), so the scored set is tiny (150-600 a side) against a $50 pot. A 300-lot at each side's reference -- or one tick inside the incumbent's best bid, the 'cutoff' variant that ends the walk at our level and zeroes the incumbent's deeper 75-lot ladder -- holds 47-52% of the score = ~$24 per EURUSD window. Re-quote the reference every few seconds; quote only in the first ~8-10 minutes and pull before the last 5 (the settlement is one Pyth print, where informed takers hit stale quotes). No maker fee (quadratic, taker-only).
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi pays $4,800/day per FX pair; the pots are 99.2% paid, so this is a share grab from the one incumbent ladder bot, not free money. The share is large because the target cutoff keeps the scored set small.
idea.must_be_true: Our fills at the reference must cost less than ~$24 a window. Pooled tape over 66 settled 15-min Pyth windows (FX + commodities, 9,334 contracts/window): makers -2.2c/contract overall; NO bids 21-80c -7.5c (3,064/window), YES bids 21-80c +1.8c; by pair EURUSD -1.5c (5,550/window), USDJPY -1.8c, GBPUSD +2.9c; commodities -0.6c to -3.9c. A static quote gets hit worse than the whole-maker population (the project's standing lesson); the 2026-09-07 natgas maker test lost 40c each on 60 contracts; D04 lost real money taking here. test.method:
Source: the public trade tape (rank 2). No replay was used. I took 270 settled 15-min windows from 2026-10-07 to 10-14: EURUSD 110, GBPUSD 110, USDJPY 50. They are every 4th window (every 9th for JPY) in close-time order inside the reward hours, not picked by volume. Every tape is complete: the prints sum to volume_fp in 270 of 270 windows.

I simulated the bot on each window:
- It rests S contracts a side at the best bid, in the first 10 minutes only (900 to 300 s before close).
- YES and NO net against each other, and the net position is capped at S.
- Each fill pays won minus price at settlement.
- Reward credit = $50 x time-weighted resting size x our share x 10/15 x 0.9. The 0.9 is what Kalshi actually paid of the formula on the 10-11 coin-race test.

Queue position and share come from the books seen on 10-13 (5 FX book snapshots plus the 3-window EURUSD poll).
- One side has a 562.5-lot (a reward farmer) at the best bid, over a 75-per-cent ladder. We sit behind it and get 300/862.5 = 35% of that side.
- The other side has only 0.1-10-lot pennies on top. We are first in line there, and the filing's walk gives us 43%, 57%, 75% or 97% at S = 60, 100, 200 or 300.
- The tape does not show which side is which, so every window is run both ways. The spread (SD/SE) comes from single runs, not their average.

Also run: queue-free bounds (first in line on both sides, at the touch and one tick inside, the idea's 'cutoff' variant), behind-75 and behind-150 queues, and quote-stop times of 0, 2, 5 and 10 minutes before close.

Holdout: early half against late half of each pair's windows. Nothing was fitted on the tape: the shares came from the books, and the 5-minute stop was set in advance by the idea.

The planned live book poll for 05:00-05:30 ET was not run. The exchange was in Thursday maintenance (no FX markets until 05:00 ET), and I stopped my poller rather than wait an hour. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C2-03/ (pull.py, analyze3.py, analyze5.py = the final model).

- One tick inside the best bid (100% share) is dead. It takes 1,400-2,000 fills per window at -1.1c to -2.4c each. Net: EURUSD -$3.6 (SE 9.8; early -18.6, late +11.4), GBPUSD +$6.1 (SE 9.5; -19.6 / +31.8), USDJPY -$11.1. The extra share is paid away in fills.
- Quoting all 15 minutes instead of stopping 5 minutes early costs about $29 per close time (EURUSD+GBPUSD, behind-75 model: -$5.4 against +$23.5). Stopping 2 minutes early sits in between (+$10.9).

Corrections to the idea:
- Credit at 300 a side is about $10 per window, not about $24. Only 10 of the 15 minutes are quoted, quoting stops when the inventory cap is hit, the payout is 0.9, and the farmer's side gives 35%, not 50%.
- Rewarded windows are 76 a day per pair (programs run 05:00-00:00 ET), not 96.
- The swing is the one-sided inventory left at settlement. Per window it is $28 at S=60, $47 at S=100 and $125-135 at S=300. Per day that is about $240, $400 and $1,100 per pair.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Per pair per window, at the 95% level: about $7 at S=60, $12 at S=100 and $33-50 at S=300. Every measured net is below that line, so the tape neither kills nor confirms the idea. Per contract, the fill-cost estimate is uncertain by about 4c (one SE), which is as big as the reward cushion.
test.artefact_checks:
- Units: prices are in dollars throughout (largest is 1.0; checked over the whole sample). Kalshi's netting rule (YES at p plus NO at q pays exactly 1 - p - q) is built into the P&L.
- Tapes: complete on 270 of 270 (prints sum to volume_fp). Timestamps are to the millisecond, so a taker order is grouped by exact timestamp and side.
- Sample: systematic, not the top-by-volume windows the earlier lane used (that lane also cut each tape to its newest 1,000 trades).
- One artefact was found and fixed. Averaging the two side-assignments within a window had shrunk the swing about 5x (SD $25 instead of $130). The SDs and SEs above come from single runs.
- Credit is only counted while our order is actually resting. The idea's queue-free 300-cap model hid this: with no refill we would rest only 35-73% of the time.
- Still not checkable from the tape:
  1. Our own quote being picked off when Pyth moves before we cancel. One pip is about 8c of fair value with 10 minutes left, and the tape cannot see quotes that were not there.
  2. How the 562.5 farmer and the 75-ladder bot react to us.
  3. Whether the 10-13 book layout holds at other hours. It comes from 6 snapshots and 3 EURUSD windows.
- Recorders: kalshi_collector is alive (cfbenchmarks_value file written 04:19 ET). Trading channels were quiet because of Kalshi's Thursday 03:00-05:00 ET maintenance.
- 313 unauthenticated GETs, 0 authenticated, 0 orders. Scratch folder 2.0 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get:
The pot is $50 per window on each FX pair, 76 rewarded windows a day.
- Our fills: about 65-75 contracts per window per pair at S=60, 105-120 at S=100, about 290-325 at S=300 (the net cap binds).
- Fills come mostly on the thin side, where we are first in line at the best bid. Behind the 562.5 farmer, only takers bigger than 562 reach us.
- Taker flow we sit against in the first 10 minutes: about 2,000-2,800 contracts per window per pair. These are Kalshi FX 15-min markets settled on one Pyth print.
- The book needs no help from us to qualify for the reward: without us, both sides held 300 or more in 84-100% of polled seconds (10-13).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now:
About $100/day central, range -$100 to +$400. Basis: S=60-100 a side on one or two pairs (GBPUSD first) from a subaccount, about $100-150 of capital per pair.

The tape model says +$200-360/day per pair at that size, with a day-to-day swing of $240-400. That figure is the whole-maker population's fills, so it is a hypothesis: our own fill cost is not measured. A 2c-per-contract penalty for being picked off would halve it.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $300-600/day if live fills come within about 2c per contract of the tape, at S=200-300 on EURUSD+GBPUSD (+USDJPY). The tape figure is $700-1,100/day per pair at S=300, but the swing is about $1,100/day per pair. At $5,000, a 1-in-20 day of about -$2,000 means S=200 is the sensible ceiling.
test.worst_case:
- S=300: worst single window -$225 to -$240 per pair, when a one-sided 300 fill loses. A 1-in-20 day is about -$1,500 per pair, about -$2,000 across EURUSD+GBPUSD.
- S=60 on one pair: worst window -$41, bad day about -$250 to -$480.
- The idea's figure of -$300 to -$500 on a bad day at 300 a side understates this about 3x.
- Could be worse than the tape: our quote being picked off on Pyth moves, and the incumbents competing for the same reward.
test.next_test:
Live micro test (needs operator sign-off; new strategy family):
- 60 a side on GBPUSD only, at the best bid. Rest 300 behind the farmer only if size is later raised.
- First 10 minutes of each window only. Net cap 60. Run from a subaccount for 76 rewarded windows (one day).
- Before it starts, also run a recorder of the FX books over the WebSocket, so our queue position and the incumbents' reaction can be replayed exactly.
- Read the credit in main pool 0 about 80 minutes after each window.

Pre-registered pass bar, all three required:
1. Credit paid is at least 80% of the formula for our resting size.
2. Our fills' P&L per contract is no worse than 2c below the tape model's prediction for the same windows and seat (the cushion is 4.5-5c on GBPUSD).
3. Net (credit + fills) is at least 0 over the 76 windows.

Then 100 a side for another 76 windows. Then EURUSD, then 200-300 a side, only after a 48-hour read. Cost of the test if it fails: about -$40 worst window, about -$250 on a bad day. Commodities stay out until FX passes.

refs.strongest_objection:
Our bot would be the slow, stale order at the touch, and the reward cushion is only 3.3-4.0c per filled contract (credit $2.4-2.6 over 64-72 fills a window at S=60).

1. Pyth's live and historical price endpoints all return 401 without an API key (Hermes latest, stream and v1; benchmarks; measured 10-15). Without a key the bot can only follow the Kalshi book, not the settlement feed.
2. My live poll (10-15 09:00-09:25Z, both pairs, about every 2 s): the best bid dropped by 2c or more about 80 times per 10-minute quote period (both sides, average drop about 4c). 79% of those drops had no trade at the old price, so faster makers cancelled and re-posted. Each time, a book-follower is left alone at the old price for its reaction time. Break-even is about 1-1.3 stale 60-lot pick-offs a window, about 2% of those drops.
3. In the 4 live-polled window-pairs, makers at the touch lost 4.15c per contract against the book mid 60 s later (1,185 contracts). Thin-side seats lost 3.6c (258 contracts). That is the whole cushion. It is only 4 windows in 2 time clusters, against a 200-window tape that says break-even, so it is suggestive, not decisive.
4. Every live maker test this project has run on these series lost. Coin-race fills cost 113% of the credit on 10-11, and natgas on 09-07 lost 40c a contract.
refs.independent_number:
I pulled my own 200 settled windows (EURUSD 100, GBPUSD 100, all hours, 10-05 to 10-15; 28 overlap the tester's; prints sum to volume_fp in 200 of 200). I used a 60-120 s markout against a trade-implied mid instead of settlement. It is 4-5x less noisy, and on the live windows it matched the polled book mid within about 1c, so it is not biased toward zero.

- The S=60 first-in-line seat: EURUSD +0.45c (SE 0.62) at 60 s and +0.72c (SE 0.83) at 120 s; GBPUSD -0.64c (SE 0.69) and -0.69c (SE 0.84) per contract. So the tape seat breaks even within about 1c, and the cushion is 3.3-4.0c.
- My own simulation at S=60 nets +$2.76 a window on EURUSD (SE 2.76) and +$2.46 on GBPUSD (SE 2.79).
- Rewarded windows are 96 a day per pair on weekdays (88 on Thursdays because of maintenance), not 76. /incentive_programs showed 96 $50 programs per pair on each of 10-12, 10-13 and 10-14 (target 300, 0.5 a tick, 15-minute periods). The tester's 76 was the count of upcoming rows at one moment.
- Live books on 10-15: big orders sit at the touch on both sides in 35-78% of polls, so a 60 joining the touch gets 10-31% per side. Credit at full resting is $2.9-9.5 a window, and the $1 floor never binds.
- Payouts for every Kalshi program that ended after at least 10-14 17Z were still unpaid at about 08:45Z 10-15 (FX unpaid from 10-14 10Z). This is a global delay, not FX-specific.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tape can't tell whether this makes money. All of the modelled profit is the reward credit, about $2.5-3.5 per window at 60 a side, and I confirmed that size independently. The fills themselves come out at about zero in the tape, so the whole result depends on one cost the tape can't see: how often our slower quotes get picked off.
- Touch fills across all makers earn the half-spread at the moment of the fill (+3.2c EURUSD, +3.8c GBPUSD) and have lost all of it 60 s later: EURUSD -0.43c (95% CI -1.23 to +0.43), GBPUSD -0.33c (-1.59 to +0.82).
- In the tester's seat model, extra pick-off costs above 4.1-4.6c per contract erase the profit. Under the real 10-15 book, EURUSD put 256-280 contracts on us per normal window, not about 76, and that bar falls to about 1c per contract.
- Measured in the settlement feed itself, 1 pip is 10-14c of fair value with 10 minutes left. So the bar is 0.1-0.4 pip of Pyth movement. A quoter sending in 43 ms, not co-located, re-pricing behind a 562.5-lot farmer on every Pyth tick, could easily fall short of it.
- Every earlier live maker test on these one-print series lost money, and so did the coin-race test (fills -$12.45 against +$11.04 credit). So the zero-pick-off tape model is a ceiling, not a central estimate.
refs.independent_number:
My own sample: 140 settled windows (70 EURUSD + 70 GBPUSD, closing 10-05 to 10-15, all hours, none of them in the tester's sample), run through my own code.
- At 60 a side the expected net is +$3.00 a window: credit $2.74 (at 98.5% payout) plus fills $0.26. The honest SE for one real setup is $2.40. It breaks even at 4.3c per contract of extra pick-off.
- The live book on 10-15, 05:00-05:45 ET (650 snapshots), contradicts the tester's layout. The 562.5-lot farmer sits at the best bid on BOTH sides (best level of 300 or more in 56-83% of snapshots), not on one side with pennies on the other.
- Our 60-lot share at the best is 14-22% a side. Resting both sides for the full 10 minutes earns $3.3-4.8 a window in normal windows. A replay against the real book on those windows gave $2.3-4.0 credit a window, so the credit size holds.
- Programs run about 24 hours on weekdays: 96 windows a day Monday to Wednesday, 88 on Thursday, about 470 a week per pair. Not 76 a day.
- FX rewards are paid in a daily batch: paid_out was false for every window after 10-14 10:00Z. The live test has to read the credit the next day, not 80 minutes later.

idea.name: Lend the main bank's idle cash to the side bots: size the main bot on ACCOUNT equity (all subaccounts) or a configured bank figure instead of subaccount-0 cash, keeping a hard cash floor in subaccount 0
idea.lane: kalshi-mechanics-capital (make more) x crypto-lose-less-and-forecaster x lip/maker lanes
markets: main bot: KXBTC15M family + KXBTCD + coin race (unchanged)
any maker/reward subaccount (Trump-approval ATM, first-five-minutes 15M maker, weekly pots, weather 97-99c bid N2-05)
idea.mechanism: pinrun sizes its bet (98 contracts at ~$1,155) with size_for_bank() from subaccount 0's balance, so every dollar moved to a side bot shrinks the main bet. But the main bot never uses most of that cash: across the 392 closes it traded since 2026-10-01 (Kalshi's own ledger), gross outlay per close was median $34, p90 $128, p99 $206, max $272; at most 4 markets per close; money is free ~6 s after each 15-min close. Change sizing to read total equity across subaccounts (GET /portfolio/subaccounts balances) or a configured bank figure, keep a hard floor in subaccount 0, and move the rest into side-bot subaccounts. The main bot keeps its 98 contracts; the side bots get cash that sat idle at every close. Drawdown limits move to account level.
idea.why_mispriced: Not a market mispricing: an internal capital inefficiency. ~$880 of the bank sits unused at every close while the forecaster is sized from a ~$109-137 pot and several maker ideas are labelled 'capital-limited'.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The main bet is limited by risk policy, not cash: of 641 entries since 10-01, 410 filled in full, 52 partially (book ran out), 179 not at all (offer gone); none refused for cash in the records read. (2) MERGER CAVEAT: the $272 peak was measured over a window in which the bet size grew; at today's 98 contracts, 4 markets x 98 x ~$0.97 = ~$380, plus KXBTCD 11 lots, coin race 20 a leg and hedges -- so the subaccount-0 floor must be set from the CURRENT bet (rule of thumb: >= 5 x bet x $1, ~$490 today), which caps the loan at ~$650, not $800. (3) The side bots earn more than they lose per dollar (forecaster lifetime +12.6% per $ bet, +21.7% since r28, per the crypto lane -- not re-measured here). (4) Account-level loss limits are rewritten to cover the total.
idea.evidence_so_far: peak_deploy.py on results/kalshi_ledger.json (392 closes since 10-01): p50 $33.84, p75 $88.35, p90 $127.81, p95 $162.20, p99 $206.38, max $272.09 (26OCT030645, 2 markets); closes above $200: 1.0%, above $300: none. Subaccount balances (own-account GET 10-15): sub0 $1,143.40 shard 2 + $12.53 shard 0, sub1 $86.28, sub2 $137.09, sub3 $42.17, sub4 $42.55. Main bot P&L on Kalshi's books (pinday): about +$19/day over 13 ET days 09-30..10-13 (10-02 not parsed); worst day -$51.18 (10-07).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Directly: avoids the main-bot cut that funding a side bot would otherwise cause -- moving $240 to the forecaster would cut the main bet ~21% (~-$4/day at the measured ~+$19/day). Enables: the carried forecaster-3x idea (+$6-13/day, ~$11/day at its lifetime rate) and other capital-hungry arms with no cut to the 98-contract bet. At $5,000 the same ratio frees ~$3,000+. Worst plausible day: the side bots' own worst day (forecaster at 3x ~-$120 per the crypto lane), after which the main bet shrinks ~10% until it recovers.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~96 closes/day per coin (unchanged); side bots per their own lanes
idea.test_plan: Read-only first: re-run peak_deploy.py weekly AT THE CURRENT bet size (filter to closes since the last size change) and confirm the peak stays under the subaccount-0 floor with margin. Paper-run pinrun's sizing with equity = sum of subaccount balances and show the bet size is unchanged when nothing is lent. Then a version-logged change (VERSIONS.md entry + versioncheck.py) with the operator's sign-off, lending in steps ($200, then more after a week with 0 cash refusals).
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New. The ledger and carried ideas treat side-bot funding as a choice between taking cash from the main bank and a deposit (carried crypto-lose-less 'Grow the forecaster to ~3x by funding its own pot to ~$350': 'operator deposit or a transfer from main while flat'). Nobody had measured that the main bot leaves >= $880 idle at every close. This is the enabler for that carried idea, not a duplicate of it.
idea.worst_case: A side bot loses its whole allocation (e.g. $300): account equity -26% and the main bet falls in proportion; capped by per-subaccount allocation limits. A floor set too low makes the main bot short of cash on a 4-market close -- prevented by the floor rule in must_be_true (2).
idea.prior_reason: Measured on Kalshi's own ledger, cheap, immediate; its own money is modest (~$4/day saved) but it unlocks every capital-limited idea in this hunt without touching the bot that makes the money. Held at 3 because the side bots' edge, not this change, decides most of the dollars.

test.method: Ranked sources: Kalshi's own books (results/kalshi_ledger.json = subaccount-0 settlements; own-account GET /portfolio/settlements?subaccount=1..4, /portfolio/subaccounts/balances, /portfolio/balance, /portfolio/subaccounts/transfers, 11 GETs) > our own live fills/logs (17 pinrun-live logs since 09-27, 184,739 lines; results/forecaster-live-orders.jsonl). No replay, no tape. (1) capital_need.py: per close (all subaccount-0 markets sharing a quarter-hour stamp, incl. KXBTCD and coin race) gross outlay yes+no cost, divided by the bet SIZE live at that moment (192 autosize/loss_cap records) = stake-free $ of cash per contract of bet, rescaled to SIZE 98; earlier vs later half; settlement lag; every order/hedge HTTP status + error; raw scan for 'insufficient'/balance errors. (2) lag_tail.py: markets settled >120 s after close (cash locked past the next close). (3) pinrun sizing read from code: size = bank // (worst_close_cost(1) x BANK_BRAKE), worst_close_cost(1) = (MAX_PER_CLOSE 2 + extra 1) x ceiling 0.98 = $2.94; brake 4.00 -> bank/11.76; day stop = 0.187 x bank. (4) fc_scale.py / fc_perdollar.py: forecaster per-close P&L, return per $ bet by earlier/later half (holdout), fill fraction, ask/paper ratio, a linear full-scale upper bound, overlap and same-close correlation with the main bot. (5) side_money.py: every subaccount's balance and Kalshi-booked P&L by ET day. Scripts and outputs: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N2-02/ (capital_need.py/.json, lag_tail.py, side_money.py/.json, fc_scale.py/.json, fc_perdollar.py, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: Main: 560 subaccount-0 markets in 432 closes, 09-29..10-15 (Kalshi ledger); 900 orders + 20 hedges in the live logs since 09-27. Forecaster: 110 markets in 96 closes, 09-29..10-14 (its own live fills; matches Kalshi's subaccount-2 settlements, +$86.48 vs +$86.12). Ladder: 174 markets (Kalshi, subaccount 1).
test.n_independent_clusters: 432 main closes; 96 forecaster closes (48 earlier / 48 later halves); 60 closes where both traded
test.result:
THE CASH SITS IDLE AND NEVER RUNS OUT: 0 of 900 orders and 0 of 20 hedges failed for cash (the 5 failures were all 'invalid_price'). No 'insufficient' text in any live or side-bot log. Cash needed per close, per contract of bet: p50 $0.38, p90 $1.45, p99 $2.31, max $2.89 (earlier half max $2.89, later half max $2.28). At SIZE 98 that is p99 $226 and max $284 (gross, hedge legs counted twice). The designed ceiling is $2.94/contract = $288 at 98, plus up to ~$137 for two fully hedged legs, ~$16 for KXBTCD and the coin race open cap of ~$44. Settlement lag median 7 s, but 51 markets settled more than 2 min late: one KXBTC15M ($84.45) took 2.0 h (10-01) and coin race took up to 11.8 h (~$19). Measured worst cash out at once ~$390; designed worst ~$580 = ~6 x SIZE.

SAFE LOAN at today's $1,156 subaccount-0 cash: keep the worst designed close (~$490-580) plus the $216 day stop. That leaves ~$450, not the $650-880 in the idea.

ALREADY IDLE TODAY: $42.55 in sub 4 (stopped reward test, pool 2), $42.17 in sub 3 (stopped dip-seller, pool 0) and $12.53 of sub 0 in pool 0 (the bot trades pool 2) = $97.25 earning nothing.

NO CODE NEEDED: move $X to a side subaccount and set --bank-brake 4.00 x (B-X)/B and --loss-cap-frac 0.187 x B/(B-X). For X=$450 that is brake 2.44 and frac 0.306: SIZE stays 98, the day stop stays $216, and each account still sizes from its own fund (the operator's 10-11 rule). pinrun's own comment says the operator can keep the old size by lowering --bank-brake.

WHAT THE CASH EARNS (mostly not measured):
- Forecaster return per $ bet: +14.0% over 96 closes (mean close return 0.132, SE 0.031). Holdout halves: earlier 48 closes +2.7% ($7.27 on $267), later 48 +22.7% ($79.20 on $349).
- Its pot sets its size: scale = pot/630, capped at 1.0, so it can absorb only ~$493 more ($137 -> $630). Today it asks for 11% of what its paper version books and gets 85.5% of the contracts it asks for (135 of 162 orders full, 23 empty).
- Linear upper bound at scale 0.93: bets ~$58/day -> ~$249/day, +$27/day at 14% per $ (+$5..+$43 using the two halves). How fills and prices hold up at 4x the order size is NOT measured.
- Overlap with the main bot: 37 of 110 forecaster markets were also traded by the main bot, so they may compete for the same offers. Same-close P&L correlation -0.20. On 4 closes where the main bot lost and the forecaster also traded, the forecaster won 3.
- Ladder: +$21.26 on $1,035 bet (2.05% per $), positive on all 15 ET days; capacity not measured.
- Main bot (09-29..10-13, Kalshi): +$258.81 = $17.25/day, worst ET day -$51.18. Funding $450 by a plain transfer under today's sizing would cut the main bet from 98 to 59 (~-$7/day).
test.artefact_checks: (1) Per-close outlay counts both legs of a hedged market, so it overstates cash need (the safe direction). (2) Bet size moved between 80 and 100 over the window. Dividing by the size live at each close removes the merge caveat; the two halves agree (max $2.89 vs $2.28 per contract). (3) Grouping by close stamp misses cash held past a late settlement, so the 51 late markets were listed separately; the worst was $84.45 for 2 h. (4) Forecaster log vs Kalshi's subaccount-2 settlements: +$86.48 vs +$86.12, so the per-close figures are real money. (5) Most of the forecaster's good number comes from its later half. The earlier half (+2.7% per $) is only ~1.8 standard errors from zero, so 14% is not a stable per-$ edge. (6) Its scale grew from 0.05 to 0.22 over the window. The per-$ figures do not depend on stake size, but they say nothing about fills at 4x the order size. (7) The full-scale upper bound multiplies each market's live P&L by paper/live contracts, which assumes every extra contract fills at the same price. It is a ceiling, not a forecast. (8) read_bank's $1,156.05 includes the $12.53 in pool 0, which cannot be spent on pool-2 markets: a tiny overstatement of the main bank. (9) No replay or tape behind any number. (10) RECORDER PROBLEM, seen while checking the recorders (nothing touched): at 2026-10-15 08:12 UTC (04:12 ET) the Kalshi collector was still writing cfbenchmarks_value (the T08 file is growing). But its market channels have been almost empty since 07:00 UTC (03:00 ET): ticker T07 is 2.5 KB (T06 was 3.3 MB), orderbook_delta T07 is 14 KB (T06 was 212 MB), and there is no trade, orderbook_snapshot or lifecycle file after T06. test.supply_we_would_get: The side bots set the limit, not the market. The forecaster is capped at scale 1.0 = a $630 pot, so it can use ~$493 more: up to ~$249/day of bets if fills held, vs ~$58/day now. It takes from the 15-min crypto books (KXBTC15M family) in the last ~30 s at 75-98.5c. Those are the same books the main bot takes from (37 of 110 markets shared). test.worst_case: The main bot is unchanged as long as it sizes from its own subaccount at the lowered brake. A side-bot loss cannot shrink or starve it, and its cash still covers ~2.4 designed worst closes. Forecaster at a $587 pot: day stop -20% = -$117 (today -$27), run stop -33% = -$194. Its worst single live close (10-02), scaled up to that size, is ~-$98. Worst plausible account day ~ -$216 (main day stop) - $117 (forecaster) - a few $ (ladder) = ~-$340, vs ~-$250 today. test.result:
**Live's +22.7% is not the rate to scale.** Since r28 the full-size paper made +4.0% on money bet: 81 markets, 11 lost. It makes the same decisions as live. Live did better for three reasons:
- **(a) Crash guard (real, holds at any size).** It refuses when the best offer has fallen more than 10c under the price. It refused paper fills on 21 markets; 7 of them lost, and that group returned -14.1%.
- **(b) Missed markets did worse (probably luck, not a rule).** Of the remaining markets, live got 53. Zero-fill markets lost 3 of 12 (-11.9%); markets skipped while an order was in flight returned +2.1%.
- **(c) Live pays 3.1c per contract less than the paper books.** It sweeps from the best offer. That is worth about 4 points: live re-priced at the paper's prices makes +18.5%. The improvement shrinks at bigger size.

**Forward rate.** Paper minus crash refusals: +10.2% ±7.3 (2 sd) on 65 markets, 6 lost (about 9 times out of 100). By half: +3.3% (21 markets, 3 lost), then +13.5% (44 markets, 3 lost). **Capture.** Live buys 62% of the scaled paper's dollars (0.70 in the first half, 0.59 in the second).

**Projection.**

| pot | scale | bet per day | profit per day at 10.2% |
|---|---|---|---|
| $367 | 0.583 | ~$135 | +$13.8 (worst ET day -$36; 3 losing days of 11; worst market -$48) |
| $137 (today) | 0.2176 | ~$50 | +$5.1 |

| contracts asked | share of contracts filled |
|---|---|
| 1-4 | 85% |
| 5-9 | 83% |
| 10-14 | 87% |
| 15-19 | 89% |
| 20+ | 41 of 41 |

The ratio does not fall as the ask grows relative to the depth still shown at 1 s, up to 0.4 and above (8 orders, 97%). But the largest live order ever sent was 21 contracts, so the fill at about 58 is NOT measured. The bar of 80% or more is neither passed nor failed.

Some of the forecaster's extra contracts would come out of the main bot's cheaper offers; that cost is not measured.

idea.mechanism: Kalshi's docs (getting_started/order_direction, saved under r1-kalshi-mechanics-capital/docs/) say the default of the orderbook subscription flag use_yes_price will flip to true in a future release and the flag will then be removed; after that, NO-side levels in orderbook_snapshot/orderbook_delta move from no-leg pricing (a NO bid at 2c reported 0.02) to yes-leg pricing (reported 0.98). Separately the legacy fields taker_side (trades), action/side/is_yes (orders), purchased_side (fills) are deprecated and 'will not be removed before May 28, 2026' -- that floor has passed, so removal can come in any monthly release. Fix in five steps: (1) every WS subscription passes use_yes_price explicitly and the parsers convert; (2) a per-message convention check (under no-leg, a NO level p must satisfy p + best YES bid <= 1; a stream that breaks it is marked suspect and the bot stands down); (3) livebook reads taker_outcome_side first, taker_side as fallback, and ALARMS when both are missing instead of quietly returning 'no opinion'; (4) tape loaders detect the convention per hour (hard rule 5 applied to book sides); (5) a daily read-only poll of docs.kalshi.com/changelog that alarms on any entry naming use_yes_price, taker_side, purchased_side, is_yes or a removal date -- Kalshi says it will announce concrete dates first, so the real failure mode is nobody reading the announcement.
idea.why_mispriced: Nobody pays; this prevents losses. (a) The main bot's hedge pass computes market_belief from the opposite side's book (our ask = 1 - best NO bid). If the convention flips while our code assumes no-leg, a YES position's ask is read as ~2c instead of ~98c and insurance fires on winning positions whenever the index is stale; entries see fake 2c asks (an IOC at 2c just misses). (b) The toxic-fresh seller check that is being put back on reads only taker_side; if Kalshi removes it, taker_flow returns None and the gate goes silently OFF -- that gate, scored on live fills 10-04..10-13, would have refused 8 of 11 losing markets, so the measured loss class it guards comes straight back. (c) Every tape hour after the flip would be misread by analyses.
idea.must_be_true: Kalshi flips the default or removes the legacy fields while our code still depends on them. Merger checks 2026-10-15: grep of research/ finds use_yes_price in 0 files; research/livebook.py line 605 reads msg.get('taker_side') only (taker_outcome_side appears only in a comment at line 68). Kalshi does carry out removals: the changelog records available_on_brokers removed in the 2026-09-10 release and liquidity_dollars removed in the 2026-10-01 release, each after a deprecation notice. Against urgency: the use_yes_price flip will be announced with dates before it happens, so a watched changelog gives warning.
idea.evidence_so_far: Docs read 2026-10-15 (getting_started__order_direction.md, changelog__index.md). Tape hour 20261015T05 orderbook_delta is still legacy no-leg; trade messages still carry both taker_side and taker_outcome_side. Code audit: use_yes_price 0 files; taker_side read in pinrun.py, livebook.py and sweep/racereward_live.py. Money effect: not measured, because the change has not happened.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 until the change. What it avoids: one or more days of garbage hedges/decisions -- at 98 contracts a misfired insurance order on a winning 97c position costs ~$3-10 per market; a full day of misreads plausibly -$100 to -$500 at the ~$1,155 bank, ~4x that at $5,000; plus every day the toxic-fresh gate is silently off (the losing-market class it blocks). Worst plausible day if NOT done: a silent switch mid-day, -$100 to -$500.
idea.settlements_per_day: n/a (covers every market the bots read: ~900+ 15-min closes/day, 24 KXBTCD closes/day, 96 coin races/day)
idea.test_plan: Read-only paper: open two livebook WS connections on the same 9 markets for 10 minutes, one with use_yes_price:false and one with true; assert the converted books match second by second. Self-test plants both conventions and a mid-stream switch and fails if the detector misses the switch or fires on a clean stream; a second self-test drops taker_side from trade messages and fails if taker_flow returns None without an alarm. Ship the explicit flag + fallback behind a VERSIONS.md entry. Start the changelog poller the same day (1 GET/day).
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New. No ledger row and no repo doc mentions use_yes_price or the legacy-field removal dates; carried crypto-lose-less ideas assume the toxic-fresh gate's input stays present.
idea.worst_case: Doing nothing: a silent convention switch or field removal in the middle of a trading day (-$100 to -$500 at the current bank). Doing it: a conversion bug, caught by the 10-minute two-connection paper test before shipping.
idea.prior_reason: Near-certain to happen eventually (Kalshi removed two deprecated fields in the last 5 weeks; the taker_side floor date has passed), large one-day cost and it silently disables a gate with a measured 8-of-11 loss-market record; but $0 until it happens, and the flip itself will be pre-announced, so expected $/day is a few dollars. Decided in minutes.

test.method:
Five read-only measurements, run 2026-10-15 between 04:05 and 04:20 ET. That is inside Kalshi's Thursday 3-5 AM ET trading pause.
(1) Live test over two WebSocket connections (ws_flag_test.py). Connection A subscribes exactly as our bots do, with no flag. Connection B subscribes to the same markets with use_yes_price:true. 70 markets: 5 crypto 15-min, 1 coin race, 4 KXBTCD rungs and the 60 busiest open markets.
(2) Tape history (field_history.py): one trade hour per day for all 52 days on disk (60k prints each), every orderbook_snapshot hour (1,149), and 1 REST /markets/trades call.
(3) Flip simulation (flip_sim.py): books rebuilt from collector tape 2026-10-15 04:39-07:00 UTC (snapshots plus 17,983,810 deltas) and sampled at 45/30/20/10/5/2 s before each 15-min close. Every NO level was re-reported as 1-p, which is the documented flip, and read with livebook's own formulas.
(4) Real-code probe (live_code_probe.py): imported research/livebook.py and research/pinrun.py with nothing started and no network, then fed them (a) trade frames without taker_side and (b) a flipped YES-favourite book.
(5) Prototype guard (convguard.py) with a self-test that passes. It reads taker_outcome_side first and alarms when every side field is missing. It also runs a per-market trade-print convention detector and a crossed-book check, replayed clean and flipped on tape hour 2026-10-15T06.
Also: a changelog and RSS fetch diffed against the 02:42 ET copy (changelog_probe.py), and the ledger size of the loss class the toxic gate blocks (ledger_stake.py). Sources: live feed, then tape, then ledger. No pinrun replay was used for money.
test.n_markets: WS test 70 markets (1,155 NO and 316 YES levels compared); flip simulation about 190 markets / 1,140 decision-window samples; trade-field scan 3.12M prints; snapshot scan 75,771 two-sided snapshots; convguard 59 markets with enough prints

test.result:
THE FIX WORKS AS DOCUMENTED. Kalshi accepted use_yes_price:true with no error.
- 1,155 of 1,155 NO levels came back at exactly 1-p with identical sizes.
- 316 of 316 YES levels were unchanged.
- Rebuilt books matched after conversion on 70 of 70 markets.
- NOT tested: deltas. The pause produced only 1 delta (a YES one, which matched).

NOTHING HAS CHANGED YET.
- Every sampled trade print on all 52 days carries taker_side, taker_outcome_side and taker_book_side, with 0 disagreements. REST trades carry all three.
- 75,771 of 75,771 two-sided snapshots over 1,149 hours fit the old (no-leg) convention; 0 fit the new one.
- The changelog has no entry naming use_yes_price and 0 new lines since 02:42 ET.

IF taker_side VANISHES SILENTLY (real code):
- livebook.taker_flow returns None. The only trace is stats trade_malformed (3 of 3). There is no alarm, so toxic_fresh can never block.
- The forecaster engine (bettor_paper.on_trade reads msg['taker_side']) raises KeyError on every print, which is caught and logged as bad_trade.
- Stake (ledger, main account, 15-min crypto, 10-04..10-13): 338 markets, 11 losing markets cost -$989.53, period net -$455.85. The brief's 8-of-11 refusal score was not re-measured.

IF THE BOOK CONVENTION FLIPS SILENTLY (real code plus 1,140 tape samples): only YES-buy prices break.
- YES-favourite moments: the YES-ask side was empty in 301 of 399 samples. In the 98 with asks, the bot would read an ask more than 50c too cheap in 98 of 98, and livebook.best() marks none of them suspect.
- The order limit comes from the model. With the fake 3c ask, sweep_limit gives 95.9c (98.0c on the true book), so fills still pass the edge floor.
- The damage is refusals and blind gates. The 10c edge cap refuses every YES entry with more than 20 s left (the fake edge is about 96c). Scale-in caps drop to the fake price, so those orders miss.
- pinrun.market_belief returns None for both sides because of its crossed-book guard. The hunter's claim that insurance fires on winning positions is REFUTED; instead the stale-index belief hedge goes blind on those markets.
- NO-favourite moments (672): our NO-buy price is untouched. The fake YES ask is off by more than 2c in 46 of 672. A cheap insurance leg never reads zero depth (0 of 672).

DETECTORS.
- Crossed-book check: 0 of 1,140 false alarms on the clean stream. It catches 98 of 98 flipped YES-favourite moments that have asks, but only 96 of 672 (14%) NO-favourite ones, where nothing we buy is affected.
- Trade-print matcher: clean prints match the old convention 289,618 vs 8,156 (35 to 1).
- convguard on hour T06: 59 of 59 markets correct on the clean stream and 59 of 59 on the flipped one, 0 wrong verdicts ever. Median 12 s (p90 78 s) from a market's first print to a verdict.

WARNING TIME. Kalshi ships weekly on Thursdays inside the 3-5 AM ET pause.
- Today's release notes were first published Wed 14 Oct 00:56 GMT and Tue 13 Oct 03:25 GMT, 1-2 days ahead.
- The last two field removals (available_on_brokers 09-10, liquidity_dollars 10-01) were posted dated their own release day.
- The legacy-order deprecation gave 0-7 days.
- A daily poll catches a 1-2 day notice; it cannot catch a same-day one.

test.worst_case:
If not done, and taker_side vanishes mid-day with the seller check ON: the check silently stops refusing and the class it blocks comes back. 11 losing markets cost -$989.53 over 10 days at the ~$1,155 bank, so one bad day could carry 2-3 of them, -$100 to -$300 (inferred, not measured); about 4x that at $5,000.

If not done, and the book convention flips mid-day:

- Stale-index hedges are blind on YES-favourite markets.
- Every tape analysis of later hours misreads NO levels.
- The money cost of such a day is NOT measured. Reading the code points to refusals rather than bad fills; plausibly $0 to -$90 (one unhedged 98-contract loser).

If done badly:
- Passing use_yes_price:false, as the hunter's step 1 is worded, stops working when Kalshi removes the flag. Pass TRUE and convert.

refs.strongest_objection:
What is refuted is the dollar case. The fix itself still works: use_yes_price:true gives 1-p on 1,155 of 1,155 NO levels.

(1) The money stake comes from a ledger bug. The tester's ledger_stake.py prices each market as revenue/100 - cost - fee. Kalshi's revenue field leaves out the YES/NO pairs it netted, and that happens on every market where we held both sides. research/pinledger.py payout() documents exactly this trap. Re-run on the tester's own filter (338 markets, 10-04..10-13):
- the losing markets cost -$347.40 (10 markets), not -$989.53 (11);
- the period net is +$190.73, not -$455.85;
- example: KXBTC15M-26OCT131615-15 lost $32.69, not $132.69.

(2) The thing being protected is switched off. --toxic-fresh has been OFF since v-revert0925 (10-04 03:22Z), and the start records from 10-10 to 10-15 say toxic_fresh false. A silent taker_side removal today costs the main bot $0.

(3) Even switched on, the seller check is worth little.
- In its real live days (09-27 to 10-04, 6.9 days, 60 refused markets scored on Kalshi's results) it saved $57.74 and gave up $55.84: net +$1.90, about $0.27/day.
- Its in-sample best case for 10-04..10-13 is at most +$97 to +$123 over 9.8 days. That is an upper bound, since a refused market can be bought later, and it rests on about 7 losing closes.
- So the stake is about $5/day at most if it is turned back on, not "about $99/day".

(4) Expected loss avoided = chance of a removal with no usable notice × days nobody notices × stake. Even if removal within a year is certain, unannounced and unnoticed for 7 days, that is 7 × $5.5 / 365, about $0.11/day. Realistically it is $0.01 to $0.05/day.
- Kalshi gave 7 to 9 days of dated notice before removing fields that still carried data: tick_size, the integer fields, and the fixed-point cleanup.
- Same-day removals were only of fields that were already dead (available_on_brokers, liquidity_dollars).
- For use_yes_price, Kalshi explicitly promises concrete dates first.
- The most a book flip can cost is the YES side's money: YES-held markets netted +$59.45 in 10 days (about $6/day), plus one losing market as a tail.

(5) Scope: the main order path does not use the deprecated order fields. Orders are created on the V2 endpoint /portfolio/events/orders, and pinrun's reconcile reads fill counts only.

Recommendation: build the changelog watcher and a loud alarm when all three side fields are missing (read taker_outcome_side first), and refuse entries on a crossed book. Defer the use_yes_price rewrite of the live parser until Kalshi posts a date; that rewrite is itself a conversion-bug risk in live code.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's ~$1/day rests on a ledger bug and on a seller check that is currently OFF.

(1) LEDGER BUG. The tester's stake for main-account 15-min crypto, 10-04..10-13, was 11 losing markets at -$989.53 and a net of -$455.85. It leaves out Kalshi's netting credit: when we hold both YES and NO in one market, each pair pays $1 at netting time, and that $1 is not in the settlement revenue. I reproduced -$989.53 / -$455.85 exactly with the tester's formula. With the credit added it becomes 10 losing markets at -$347.40 and a net of +$190.73. The corrected number matches, to the cent, two losses recorded separately in HANDOFF: -$32.69 and -$47.13.

(2) GATE OFF. The live pinrun that started 2026-10-15 04:42Z runs with toxic_fresh:false, so losing taker_side today costs $0. The gate's own live-fill score (HANDOFF) puts its net value at no more than about +$100 over 10 days, so about $10/day at most, and it came out about even over its 7 ON days. A day with the gate silently off is the same as today's setup: at most about $10, not the tester's -$100 to -$300.

(3) BOOK FLIP. A silent flip mostly stops YES entries, which were worth +$78 over 21 ET days (about $3.7/day, ledger with the netting fix). It also breaks insurance on NO positions, which the tester missed. The hedge's YES limit becomes the LOWEST NO level + 10c, so it misses whenever the NO book is spread out. The tester checked hedge depth only on calm books (NO bid at 90c or more), not at the moments hedges actually fire. But in our own sample those NO-position hedges were net -$118.54 over 21 days (5 of 8 insured winners). So the expected cost of a flip day is about $0; the 8-market sample cannot tell the sign from zero. The worst case is one unhedged NO loser at about -$90.

(4) WARNING TIME. Kalshi has removed fields that still carried data with no notice: client_order_id from fills on 03-30, a same-day entry. It also broke a written promise of a dated warning (fractional_trading_enabled). So a silent taker_side removal is plausible; it just costs little.

What to do: about 10 lines so the bots read taker_outcome_side first and raise an alarm instead of returning None, before --toxic-fresh goes back on, plus a changelog watcher. Do NOT ship the use_yes_price:true parser migration (about 42 files, on the live book path) before Kalshi posts its promised dates. A bug in that change is the only way this idea can lose money.

idea.name: Trump-approval daily ladder: two-sided reward quote at the references on the at-the-money strike ($600 per strike-day)
markets: KXTRUMPAPPROVE (9 strikes/day, $600 per strike per day, target 1,000; 9 programs active at 07:4xZ 10-15; markets close 16:59Z on the 1 PM ET RCP read)
idea.mechanism: Both sides of every strike already hold >= 1,000 all day (1c and 99c stacks of 10-20k), so every second counts with no qualification work; the scored set near the ATM is only 300-1,400 contracts, so a 300-lot at each side's reference takes a large share (snapshot shares: E38.1 yes 49% / no 18% = $201/day; E38.2 8%/21% = $88; E38.0 10%/11% = $62; U37.8 3%/13% = $47). Rest 100-300 a side on the single ATM strike, re-quote when the reference moves, step out around RCP poll additions and for the last ~30 min before the 1 PM ET read.
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi pays $5,400/day on the series (89% of pots paid = contested, but the ATM scored set is small). Takers are retail following poll headlines; makers net +1.15c/contract over 9 settled strike-days (59,800 contracts per strike-day, 56% of it in the last 10% of life at 1c/99c).
idea.must_be_true: ATM fills must not be picked off when RCP adds a poll: the ATM band trades only 60-600 contracts per strike-day but one-sidedly (NO bids 21-80c +5.3c; YES bids 21-80c -21c on 60 contracts). The reference must stay within a tick or two of our price. Artefact risk: 4 books on one morning; the $75 median is dominated by one strike.
idea.evidence_so_far: series_live.jsonl / econ.txt (lip-economics, 10-13): 4 open books (all qualify), 9 settled tapes (7,526 trades), makers +1.15c; two-sided 300 at the references $75/day gross, $13 fill cost (pro-rata proxy), net +$62 at $293 capital; 1,000 a side $188 gross, $39 cost, net +$150 at $975; 536 of 603 pots paid. Pot still $600 x 9 at 07:4xZ 10-15.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: +$60/day on one ATM strike with ~$300 of capital at the current bank (+$150 at 1,000 a side, $975); two to three strikes at $5,000: $150-400/day -- all before the poll pick-off cost, which the tape cannot price. Worst plausible day: a poll drop moves the average 0.2 and both ATM bids are hit on the way: -$150 at 300 a side (-$500 at 1,000).
idea.settlements_per_day: 9 markets/day, 1 close
idea.test_plan: Cheap pre-step: 3 days read-only, poll the ATM book once a minute and the RCP page: how often the reference moves and by how much around poll additions. Then live (needs sign-off): 100 a side at the references on the ATM strike for 5 trading days from a subaccount ($100-200 locked), logging every fill with the RCP average before and after; read main pool 0 daily (daily pots pay within ~2 days). Bar: credit >= 50% of the modelled share AND settlement loss on fills <= 50% of credit over the 5 days.
idea.prior_reason: Pot real and still listed, share measured on 4 books, whole-maker P&L positive; but the fills that matter are exactly the ones a poll-watcher picks off, and one close a day makes the test 5+ days.

test.method: Read-only, public GETs only (~830 calls, 0 auth). Sources: Kalshi trade tape + 1-minute candles (rank 2) for 20 daily events 26SEP25..26OCT14 (180 markets; full tapes for the 134 that traded near the money: 103,572 trades, 6.54M contracts, totals match volume_fp exactly), the live incentive-program list, and a 20-minute book poll (40 polls, 30 s apart, 04:17-04:37 ET 10-15). Bot rule simulated exactly as proposed: every minute, join the best YES bid and best NO bid of the event's single most-likely strike (highest mid) from the last CLOSED candle (no look-ahead), only inside the reward window (programs run 10:02 ET day-1 to 10:02 ET settle day; the market closes 12:59 ET). Our order is added to the real tape with FIFO: we stand behind Q0 = 0 / 300 / 1,000 contracts when we post; a taker order eats the queue ahead, then us; net inventory capped at +-S per strike. P&L to settlement (makers pay no fee on this series) and a 30-minute markout cross-check. Variants: all-day, night-only (19:00-07:59 ET), night-only with the leftover position sold at 08:00 ET (taker fee included). Holdout: first 10 events vs last 10; the quiet hours were re-chosen on the first 10 and scored on the last 10. Credit side: the filed scoring rule (reference = level where 200 contracts accumulate, walk stops at 1,000, half weight per tick below), our order inserted at the touch. Self-tests: zero-edge world gives +0.91c (planted +1.0c); a planted sweep fills exactly.
