idea.name: 16:00 ET close blackout (and a 16:15 ET flag) for every crypto pin bot -- the US equity close is the one scheduled jump the trailing-sigma model cannot see
markets: KX*15M x 12 coins, closes at 16:00 and 16:15 ET (main pin bot)
KXBTCD hourly at the 16:00 ET close (ladder leg)
idea.mechanism: 1) Refuse every new entry on a market whose close is 16:00 ET (hard skip). 2) Flag 16:15 ET closes and skip them only if the forward read confirms. 3) The rule is written in ET, not UTC: 16:00 ET is 20:00Z today and 21:00Z from 2026-11-01, when the closing auction moves with the clock. 4) pinrun has no time-of-day flag today (only --skip-coin and --skip-band), so this needs a new --skip-close-et 16:00[,16:15] flag, a VERSIONS.md entry with a revert line, versioncheck.py, and the operator's decision. Nothing else changes.
idea.why_mispriced: The NYSE closing auction (MOC imbalance) at 16:00:00 ET, and plausibly the 4 PM ET New York reference rates that US spot BTC/ETH ETFs strike their NAV on (mechanism inferred, not verified), move BTC/ETH spot inside the 15:59-16:00 averaging window. The bot's sigma is a trailing 600-s number, so a scheduled discontinuity is invisible to it and it buys 97-98c offers at its usual cushion. Who pays: us, to whoever posts the offer knowing the auction is coming.
idea.must_be_true: The excess loss at these closes is structural, not six unlucky closes. Multiple-looks: among 96 quarter-hour cells, a two-consecutive-quarter cell this bad (>= 6 losing closes of 34 against the 3.3-per-100 baseline) appears by chance about 2 times in 100. Only the 16:00 close has independent index-tape support; 16:15 is calm on the tape (1.9%) and rests on fills alone (5 lost on 4 closes), so it may be chance or seller selection.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter pro-desk, own fills (results/kalshi_ledger.json, hedged pairs netted as pinday does): 15-min crypto 08-15..10-15, 1,842 markets / 1,298 closes, +$806, 58 lost. At 16:00+16:15 ET: 60 markets / 34 closes, 7 lost on 6 closes (17.6 losing closes per 100 vs 3.3 in the other hours), -$209 over 61 days (16:00: 34 markets / 17 closes, 2 lost, -$87; 16:15: 26 / 17, 5 lost on 4 closes, -$122; one 16:15 loss is the WTI bot). The 16-ET hour is negative in both halves (H1 -5.77 per $100 bet, H2 -1.24, since 10-01 -3.27). Model calibration on those closes (live_markets 09-08..10-08): our-side fair 0.997, realised 88.6% (35 markets / 25 closes) vs 98.4% elsewhere (1,039 / 769). Index tape (cfbenchmarks_value, 28 days to 10-15, BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP, 2,502 closes): P(|settle - 60-s projection| > 5 bp) = 23.1% at the 16:00 ET close vs 9.6% over all closes (weekdays 30.6% vs 11.1%; BTC 2.4x its baseline); 16:00 is jumpy Mon-Fri (19-50%) and quiet Sat/Sun (0-12%) -- the weekday-only pattern fits an equity-close cause; 16:15 1.9%, 16:30/16:45 normal. Funding-hour and US-morning variants were measured NOT to need a rule (both dropped). Other bots at these closes: forecaster 2 markets, ladder 2, coin race 16 (0 lost) -- too few; the rule transfers by mechanism only.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: If structural: about +$3.4/day saved at today's 98-contract size (the -$209 over 61 days avoided); at a $5,000 bank about 4.3x, ~+$15/day. If chance: forgoes the ordinary expectation of those markets, ~$0.43/day (60 markets x the lifetime +$0.44 net per market), ~$1.9/day at $5,000. Worst day it removes: the 09-19 16:00 BTC -$108 class. Refusing cannot lose money directly.
idea.settlements_per_day: 2 closes/day x 12 coins on weekdays; about 1 traded market/day at the bot's fill rate (60 markets in 61 days)
idea.test_plan: 1) Deploy decision for 16:00 now is the operator's (tape-backed, cheap); 16:15 stays a flag. 2) Two free natural experiments, pre-registered here: (a) after 2026-11-01 the jump must move with ET to the 21:00Z close and 20:00Z must go calm -- if it stays at 20:00Z the cause is not the equity close; (b) NYSE closes at 13:00 ET on Fri 2026-11-27: the 13:00 ET close should be jumpy and 16:00 calm that day, and Thanksgiving 11-26 (market shut) should show a calm 16:00. Read both with tape_hourrisk.py / quarter_rank.py (150 s, under 100 MB, in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/r1-pro-desk/). 3) Forward read every Friday with ledger_byhour.py; bar after 8 weeks (>= 40 traded markets at these closes): losing-close rate at 16:00+16:15 >= 2x the other hours OR negative money while the rest is positive -> keep and extend to 16:15. 4) quarter_rank.py weekly as the monitor for any new scheduled hazard (alert if a quarter not on the known list exceeds 3x baseline two weeks running) -- folded in from the dropped US-morning item. Add each read to results/READS_DUE.json when started.
idea.prior_reason: Small money (~$1.5/day expected net at today's size, ~$6 at $5k) but the operator ranks lose-less first; three independent sources (tape, fills, calibration) agree on 16:00; downside of a refusal is ~$3/week; two decisive natural experiments arrive within 6 weeks; it cuts a -$108 worst-close class on three bots.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No hour-of-day rule in the ledger (W/R/P rows are size, tau, price ceiling, coin, Saturday); SI40 (macro-surprise gate) was dead because the 5-min look-back already sees an unscheduled print -- this is a scheduled discontinuity at a fixed clock time, which the trailing sigma by construction cannot see. Not in the carried r1 index.
idea.worst_case: Forgoes ~$3/week of ordinary expectation if the cluster was luck; a refusal cannot itself lose money. Engineering risk: a wrongly-coded ET rule that skips the wrong quarter after 11-01 (check with versioncheck.py and the first post-change day's refusals).

test.result:
The cause is confirmed; the harm to our money is not.

**(a) The cause is CME's daily settlement, not the NYSE close.** CME settles BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP futures daily on the VWAP of 14:59:00-15:00:00 CT. That is 15:59:00-16:00:00 ET, exactly the 60-second window of Kalshi's 16:00 ET close. The NYSE auction prints at 16:00:00, after the window. The index matches CME to the second:
- On weekdays, 1-s moves jump to 2.1-3.0x normal at 15:59:01-02.
- They stay 1.2-1.7x normal through the minute, then spike again at 15:59:56-16:00:00.
- Weekends show nothing inside the window.

**(b) The raw move replicates on the unseen holdout and shows up most days.**
- Median final-minute move on the CME coins: 4.8 bp at weekday 16:00 vs 1.8 bp at other weekday closes. 27 of 33 closes sit above the other-weekday median.
- Share of moves over 5 bp in the holdout: 36.7% vs 10.6% (3.45x).
- Discovery window: 30.6% vs 9.6%, the hunter's number reproduced exactly.

**(c) But the model barely misses more there.** Share of misses beyond 3 of the model's own standard deviations at tau 30:
- Holdout: 1.64x (all 11 coins), 1.83x (CME coins).
- Discovery: 0.92x / 0.95x.
- Pooled: 1.31x / 1.40x; rank 17-25 of 96 weekday quarters.
- At tau 45, pooled: 1.7x / 2.9x, on 6 events.
- Why: the opening spike is already locked into the average by tau 45. What remains is about 1.4-1.5x normal volatility for the last 45 s.
- Pre-registered verdict: INCONCLUSIVE. The raw move passes (3.45x / 1.89x); the miss rate fails the 2.0x bar.

**(d) In the zone where the bot actually buys (fair 0.97-0.999):**
- The model's side lost 3 of 56 rows at weekday 16:00, on 2 of 26 closes (09-14 HYPE; 09-22 DOGE + ADA).
- Other weekday closes: 60 of 4,523 rows, on 57 of 2,034 closes.
- By row that is 4.0x (P = 0.04); by close 2.75x (P about 0.17).
- None of the misses was on the four CME coins (0 of 24 rows / 18 closes), the opposite of what the mechanism predicts.

**(e) Our fills, pin bot only:**

| cell | markets / closes | lost | net | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekday 16:00 (the tape-backed cell) | 16 / 9 | 1 | +$1 | the loss is HYPE 09-14, -$29.90, matching an index miss (z 3.33) |
| weekend 16:00 | 9 / 6 | 1 | -$94 | Sat 09-19 BTC -$107.95: the index moved 5.5 sd against the model at tau 45 on a Saturday, when CME does not settle |
| weekday 16:15 | 9 / 8 | 3 markets on 2 closes | -$64 | index calm at 16:15 (0.94x); BTC 10-06 (-$16.59) and BTC 10-13 (-$32.69) both carry the --toxic-fresh flag; NEAR 10-06 (-$21.93, an 816-s-old offer) does not |
| weekend 16:15 | 6 / 6 | 1 | -$6 | |

- The hunter's -$209 also counted coin race (16 markets, $0) and the WTI commodity bot (-$59).
- Pin up/down alone at 16:00 + 16:15: 40 markets, 6 lost, -$157. $108 of that is the one Saturday.

**(f) Side note, not this idea:** the 08:30 ET weekday close had 7 confident model misses, all on Fri 09-11 (one event).

idea.name: ERCOT daily peak after the peak is physically past: 1c reward-pile join on far strikes plus 1c lottery asks on dead strikes
markets: KXTXERCOTPEAKD (19-21 'above K' strikes at 500 MW; $50 liquidity program per market-day, 19 active at 07:4xZ 10-15, target 1,000; closes 04:55Z; settles on the next-morning NP6-346-CD 'Actual System Load by Forecast Zone' TOTAL, verified 3 of 3 days, the hourly archive differs by ~100 MW and is NOT the source; no maker fee)
idea.mechanism: Two legs on the same books, from a subaccount. (a) Reward: on far strikes the YES side already carries 1c piles of 4,100-5,100 and the NO side 97-98c x 1,250-2,275 (both sides qualify); join the 1c YES pile with 1,100 ($11) for a pro-rata 16-20% of the YES side's half = ~$4-5 per strike-day. A 1c YES bid is hit only by 99c NO buyers (measured: exactly 100 contracts at 1c on each of 6 settled markets, ~$1 a strike-day at full share). (b) Lottery: after ~03:00Z (22:00 CDT) the day's hourly peak is past (Sep/Oct peaks at hour-ending 16-18 CDT; hours 23-24 run 10-15% below); on every strike >= 500 MW above the running max rest YES asks at 1c (= NO bids at 99c, which also score on the reward's NO side); lottery buyers lift them and we keep 1c per contract on 99c of overnight collateral.
idea.why_mispriced: (a) Kalshi pays the pot pro rata; the farmers' piles are cheap, so our slice is real but small. (b) Retail lottery buyers pay 1-2c for an outcome that is physically impossible: 229,950 contracts on the losing side at <= 2c after the peak hour +1 h over 37 days (mean 6,215/day in September, 959/day Oct 1-11 with three zero days); on the one day with trade-level sides (09-11) every post-lock 1c print had the taker on the losing side.
idea.must_be_true: (a) A pro-rata slice of a shared 1c level is credited like the coin race's lone 1c side (same formula, not measured on a shared level), and the farmers do not dilute us by enlarging their piles (1,000 more contracts cost them $10). (b) Our 1c asks get queue share (an ask at 1c existed on every day with candles); the lock rule is hour-based (winter peaks can be hour-ending 20-21); Kalshi's first NP6-346 report is not erroneous; the 99c collateral sits in a subaccount, not the pin bot's bank. The <= 2c candle volume counts both taker directions; one-sided on 1 day only.

Take the hours that opened with the best YES bid at 1c. When 100 or more contracts were sold into that level, it was empty by the end of the hour 45 times out of 45. When nothing was sold, it emptied 25 times out of 303 (8%). Some sells came as one taker order that filled several resting orders, up to 3,147 contracts, so sellers clear the whole level and would take our 1,100 with it. Under that rule, holding to 18.9Z nets -$1.9/day (pile of 2,000 ahead, se $3.3) to -$4.5/day (pile of 4,150, the size measured live today, se $3.2). That is over 12 October days, leaving out 10-02. 10-02 was the strike-reset day (31 strikes; only 4 of 31 programs paid anyone). It alone supplies $94.69 of reward, which is what makes the 13-day mean look positive. Positive money exists only in the windows the sellers skip: (1) 05:55-14:55Z. Zero clearing sells in about 59 far-strike mornings. Net +$4.3/day (se $1.3) with 2,000 ahead, +$2.5/day (se $0.7) with 4,150 ahead. I picked this cancel time after seeing when the sells happen, so it is a post-hoc look on 12 days. (2) 23:00-04:55Z on dead strikes. Mean +$16/day (se $5.9) but median $1, with 5 of 13 nights carrying it. Both windows assume the NO side holds at least 1,000 contracts, and nobody measured that. Before 09:00Z today the NO side on every far strike was exactly 1,000-1,016 contracts, one order sitting right at the target. Competitors react fast. At 09:00-09:05Z today a 2c YES bidder sized 1,008-1,795 (just over the target) appeared on 6 strikes and cut every 1c bid there to zero. The idea's $40-60/day is refuted. idea.name: KPI knife-edge residual: buy the printed side at <= 94c in the hour AFTER an earnings/KPI press release on the +-1-unit strikes (the slow leftover of SI37, not the speed race)
idea.mechanism: 1) Keep the Q3 calendar (AAL+SCHW 10-15, LUV 10-21, AXP 10-23, HOOD 10-27, GOOG/META 10-28, RBLX/AMZN/FSLR 10-29). 2) At release, read the one KPI number from the company press release / IR page -- seconds to minutes is fine. 3) On strikes within +-1 unit of the printed number, buy the decided side as a taker wherever offered at <= 94c, up to bet size; ignore far strikes (already 99c). 4) Hold to Kalshi's early close (DPZ closed 4 h 26 min after its 6:05 AM ET release; BA 56 min after its 11:00 AM ET release).
idea.why_mispriced: Incumbent sweepers take the easy strikes within milliseconds (SI37), but the knife-edge strikes keep a 5-10c 'will Fiscal.ai report exactly that figure' discount for about an hour. Sellers are pre-release holders getting out at the first bid; nobody wants definitional risk at 94c.
idea.must_be_true: The press-release number equals the Fiscal.ai settlement number on the strikes bought (the risk is a definition or rounding mismatch); the <= 94c offers survive at least a few minutes after the print (BA ~55 min, DPZ ~60 min; CAVA 08-11 had nothing under 95c after the first print); Kalshi keeps the markets open after the release (observed 5 min to 4.4 h). Break-even: one mismatch per ~16 knife-edge buys at 94c.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter slow-source, public trade tape, 3 releases: BA 10-13 $644 gross on 3,192 contracts taker-bought under 90c (knife-edge strikes 160/161/162 at 0.94 for ~55 min); DPZ 10-13 $168 on 935 contracts (7,250-store strike at 0.91 for ~60 min); CAVA 08-11 $0 under 90c after the first 95c print. The 09-25 I37 checker measured $14.6k/season taken in the first seconds and $3.35k/season still available 30 s after the filing (~$60/event) -- consistent with this residual. n = 3 events, no holdout. The one_off KPI series return 0 settled markets on the public API (retention), so no wider backtest is possible.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Earnings season only: ~9 releases in the next 2 weeks; if half carry a residual and we take half of ~$270/event: +$60-130/week = $10-20/day at bet size 98 (one strike at 94c = $92 of capital). ~$0 outside the season (averaged over a year ~$3-5/day). At $5,000 the supply caps it near the same dollars. Worst plausible day: one definitional mismatch = -$92 at 98 contracts, -$470 at $5,000-bank sizing.
idea.settlements_per_day: 0.6-1 per day in the 3-week earnings season (9 releases 10-15..10-29, 10-25 strikes each); ~0 otherwise
idea.test_plan: Read-only paper watcher for the 9 Q3 releases, starting with today's AAL/SCHW: from the scheduled release minute snapshot /markets/{t}/orderbook every 10 s for 2 h on every open strike, and poll the company IR page every 5 s to log when the number is readable. Pre-registered bar: on >= 3 of 9 releases, >= $100 of decided-side offers at <= 94c survive >= 5 min after the number is public, AND 0 of 9 Fiscal.ai settlements differ from the press-release figure on the knife-edge strikes. Fail -> dead until next season. Add to results/READS_DUE.json (read 10-30).
idea.prior_reason: Measured supply on 2 of 3 releases and a test that decides itself in two weeks with 9 releases; but n = 3, a hard definitional tail, and money only ~1/4 of the year.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SI37 killed the millisecond sweep (free feeds 13-145 s late); this is the leftover an hour later on the +-1-unit strikes, which needs no speed. SI37's own $3.35k/season-after-30-s number was never turned into a trade. Not in the carried r1 index.
idea.worst_case: Fiscal.ai reports a different definition (segment vs total, adjusted vs reported): the 94c leg is a total loss, -$92 per 98 contracts; Kalshi closing before our order lands costs nothing.

test.method: Source: the public trade tape. That is the only source that can answer this. New data the hunter did not have: /historical/markets and /historical/trades serve every KPI market settled before the 2026-08-16 cutoff, so the hunter's 'no wider backtest is possible' was wrong. Steps: (1) pulled every settled market of all 230 Fiscal.ai-settled series: 1,283 markets, 132 events, 2026-04-22..10-13. (2) Picked the 4 knife-edge strikes per event by settlement RESULT: the two highest YES winners and the two lowest NO winners. This is robust to expiration_value changing units between series, e.g. HD prints 391.1 against strikes of 390,000,000. (3) Fetched their tapes from close-8h to close: 416 markets, 11,883 trades. (4) Found the release time WITHOUT using the outcome: a jump of 25c or more against the trailing 3-120 min VWAP, followed by the largest 10-minute volume burst; fallback = the largest burst, used for 28 events. Checked against known times: BA 10-13 15:01Z (Boeing release 11:00 ET), TSLA 10-02 13:00Z, CAVA 20:10Z, HD/MCD/SCHW on their scheduled minutes. (5) Bot rule: from release + delay, take winner-side asks at 0.94 or less (taker buys of the eventual winner), first 98 contracts per strike, net of taker fee roundup(0.07*C*P*(1-P)). This is an UPPER bound: it assumes perfect reading of the release and first place in the queue. (6) Honest no-outcome control: a 'price follower' that buys whichever side is priced 0.80-0.94 after release + delay. (7) Holdout: events split by close date into earlier and later halves; the parameters (0.94, 5 min, 98) were fixed by the idea before the run. ~990 public API calls. Scripts and outputs are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-03/ (p1_markets.py, p3_trades.py, p4_analyze.py, p5_ba_check.py, p7_wrong.py, p8_tape.py, an_ALL_burst.txt, analysis_ALL_0.94_0.8_burst.json, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 393 knife-edge markets with a detected release (of 416 fetched) in 111 events; universe 1,283 settled KPI markets / 132 events over 174 days (2026-04-22..10-13)
test.n_independent_clusters: 97 company-release clusters (company x release day)
test.result: The leftover the idea needs is not there. Setup: one bot, 98 contracts per strike, perfect knowledge, first in queue, 4 nearest strikes, summed over 111 events / 174 days. Net by start delay after the release: +0 s $3,244; +30 s $1,324; +2 min $792; +5 min (the idea's rule) $301, which is $1.7/day, on 20 events, with $88 of it from one event (BBY); +15 min $64; +30 min $54. Holdout at +5 min: earlier 55 events $96, later 56 events $205. At +2 min: $409 vs $383. Pre-registered bar (about $100 = 106 contracts of winner offers at 94c or less still there 5 min after): met on 8 of 111 events (7 in 100). The chance of the idea's '3 of 9 releases' bar passing is about 2 in 100. The hunter's evidence was a timing artefact. His BA reference time was 14:00Z, but Boeing released at 11:00 ET = 15:00Z, so his 'traded at 0.94 for 55 min' was the hour BEFORE the release. After the real release the 160/161/162 strikes went to 0.92-0.99 inside the release minute. In the first 5 min, 3,994 winner contracts traded at 0.94 or less ($450 gross); after 5 min only 38 ($10). DPZ 10-13: 1,454 contracts in the release minute, 0 after 5 min. Price-follower control after +2 min: 5,797 of 5,799 contracts won, $704 for all takers combined on 42 markets. So the post-release price is right; there is no wrong 'doubt discount' to buy. Definitional mismatch: the post-release market was on the wrong side in 1 of 171 knife markets that had trades 5-30 min after. That one was BBY Q2: headline comparable sales 4.1%, domestic 4.5%, and the 'above 4%' YES traded at 0.08-0.11 for 3.7 h after the 7:00 ET release; about 2,800 contracts were taken in 200-lots by one buyer. The 95% upper bound on the mismatch rate is about 3%; break-even at 94c is 6%. Some releases cannot decide the strike because the published number is rounded: SPOT Q2 MAU strike 777M sat at 0.49 for 4 h after the release.
test.artefact_checks: 1) A release-time artefact in the hunter's BA/DPZ numbers was found and corrected: they counted pre-release trading. 2) The release detector uses no outcome. Known misses only make the release time LATER: BBY found at 10:38 ET vs the true 7:00 ET, WEN 10:11 vs 7:00. The 98-contract cap makes BBY $88 either way. 3) 'Supply' counts only taker buys of the winner, i.e. offers that were actually there, not book snapshots. 4) Knife strikes are picked by settlement result, not by expiration_value, whose unit changes across series. 5) The money is an upper bound: zero mismatch, first in queue. 6) Tape win rates are other takers' fills, not ours. 7) Recorder check (read-only, nothing touched): cfbenchmarks_value and feed_data are writing (09Z files updated at 05:00 ET). BUT kalshi_data ticker, trade and orderbook_* have recorded almost nothing since ~07:00Z today: ticker T07 is 2.5 KB, the last trade file is T06, orderbook_delta T07 is 14 KB. The collector process looks alive but is not recording 15-minute market data. Flag this to the operator. Disk 124 GB free; scratch folder 1.9 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: On the Fiscal.ai KPI ladders (KXBA, KXDPZ, KXCAVA, KXTSLA etc.): after release + 5 min, winner-side offers at 94c or less totalled 2,937 contracts / $671 gross across ALL takers over 174 days, i.e. $3.9/day for the whole market. Our share at 98 contracts per strike is at most 1,368 contracts / $301 net. Almost all the supply goes in the release minute (+0 s: 63,030 contracts, $14.7k gross). That is the speed race SI37 already lost.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0.5/day. Upper bound is $1.7/day at +5 min, assuming perfect reading and first place in the queue. Faster versions reach $4.6/day at +2 min and $7.6/day at +30 s, but those are the speed race SI37 killed. About $1/day during earnings season, about $0 outside it.
test.worst_case: One definitional or rounding mismatch on a 94c buy costs -$92 at 98 contracts, or -$400 to -$470 at $5k sizing. Buying a rounding coin-flip like SPOT's 777M strike loses about half the time. Worst plausible day is about -$92 against about $3 expected gain that day.
test.next_test: None needed for this idea: it is dead at $1.7/day even with perfect knowledge. Two optional follow-ups: (a) A read-only Q3 recorder: orderbook every 10 s on the 4 nearest strikes, from the scheduled release minute to +30 min (AAL/SCHW today, LUV 10-21, AXP 10-23, HOOD 10-27, GOOG/META 10-28, RBLX/AMZN/FSLR 10-29). It would only re-test the +30 s to +2 min speed window. Bar: at least $100 net for one bot starting at +60 s on at least 3 of 9 releases. Expected to fail: the historical +2 min figure is about $7/event. (b) A different shape, seen once in 111 events (BBY): a decided strike still offered at 20c or less hours after the release. Idea: a scanner that, after each release, checks every open KPI strike at least one strike step from the printed number against its best ask. Low prior: 1 in 111 events, about $88 at our size. If it is pursued it is a new idea, not this one.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Supply is measured directly over the full 174-day, 111-event history, so the dollar total is the answer, not an estimate. For the mismatch rate, 1 bad market in 171 gives a 95% upper bound of about 3%, below the 6% break-even at 94c. The tail risk is not what kills this; the lack of supply is.

idea.name: KXBTCD cheap-side (lottery) buyer at two horizons: 3-6c wings 30-45 min out, and 1-5c near rungs 30-120 s out in active vol
markets: KXBTCD (188 rungs $100 apart, 24 closes/day, median 1.44M contracts per close)
merged_from: vol-relative-value: Hourly BTC ladder cheap-wing buyer (KXBTCD rungs at 3-6c, 30-45 min before the hourly close)
crypto-hourly-daily-race: Hourly-ladder near-rung LOTTERY BUYER, volatility-conditioned (the mirror of the pin)
idea.mechanism: Two pre-registered cells, both buying the cheap (unlikely) side as a taker at the displayed ask and holding to the 60-s BRTI settlement, loss capped at the premium. (A) 45 and 30 min before each hourly close, every rung whose cheap side asks 3-6c (YES ask when YES <= 50c, else NO ask = 1 - YES bid; fee ~0.28c). (B) With 30-120 s left and the prior-5-min 1-s realised vol above its 0.40 bp median ('active'), the unsafe side of rungs 2-10 bp from the pin projection at <= 5c, whenever the index-tape base-rate crossing probability for (cushion, tau, vol state) is >= 2 x (ask + fee). Both use the BRTI feed the bot already streams.
idea.why_mispriced: The resting quoter prices all 188 rungs mechanically (1c wide, 99c/1c past the money) off a thin-tailed shape, while realised BTC moves from 1 minute to 1 hour are fat-tailed and vol-clustered; the seller of 1-6c wings pays. It is the mirror of the pin: the pin buys the safe side the quoter under-prices with seconds left; this buys the unsafe side it under-prices when vol clusters. No reward program on KXBTCD.
idea.must_be_true: (1) It holds over weeks: A is 2 days (46 closes, t 1.9, the best of 12 cells -- unremarkable under multiple looks); B is 30 closes with 7 flips in the key cells, and the base-rate model over-stated the realised win rate ~8x. (2) The cheap asks are there at size at our moment (candles carry no size; the hourly BOOK is recorded nowhere). (3) Our taker fills come at the displayed ask (a fast quoter may pull on a move; our fills, not the tape's, decide it). (4) The calm/active split holds out of sample (s5b is in-sample). Checked already: A's quote staleness median 0 s and the result is unchanged with quotes <= 60 s old; settlement from expiration_value; the broken lognormal fit was not used.
idea.evidence_so_far: A (candles 10-11 10:00Z..10-13 10:00Z): 108 qualifying rungs over 46 closes, 11 paid (10.2%) at avg ask 4.2c -> +5.7c per contract after fee; per close +13.3c (se 7.1c, t 1.9); 30-min +3.6c (t 1.3); 5-min +3.5c; 6-12c rungs at 45 min +2.75c (t 0.8); smallest detectable ~+5c/contract. B (public trades, 30 closes, 30,429 trades on the 4 rungs around each settle, last 120 s): takers buying <= 5c at 2-5 bp / 30-60 s +5.8c per contract (3 of 25 rung-markets flipped, 99.6k contracts/day); 5-10 bp / 60-120 s +3.1c (2 of 42, 134.7k/day); 2-5 bp / 60-120 s -0.45c; 5-10 bp / 30-60 s -1.4c; in model-positive cells 780k contracts realised +0.87c gross (~+0.5c after fee) against a model expectation 8x larger. Base rates (index tape, 2,781 quarter-hour closes, 30 days; two-sided): P(|settle - projection| > 3 bp | 60 s) 12.6% all / 20.8% active / 4.5% calm; > 5 bp | 90 s 11.7 / 19.3 / 4.1%; > 10 bp | 120 s 4.6 / 8.2 / 1.0%. Both horizons give the same sign on the same market. Tape/candle numbers are the market's population, not our fills.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not measured for our fills. A at 20 contracts a rung (~1,100 contracts/day, ~$46/day of premium at risk): +$63/day if the 2-day rate held, $15-30 realistic after decay. B at 300 contracts per close in qualifying cells: ~+$36/day at the tape's +0.5c, daily swing +-$150. Honest range at $1,155: $0-30/day. At $5,000: A scales with lots (~3-5x); B is capped by the 1-5c supply (100k+ contracts/day on the tape). Worst plausible day: every lottery loses, ~-$46 (A at 20 lots) plus ~-$10 (B at a 10-contract test); -$230/day at 100 lots in A.
idea.settlements_per_day: 24 closes/day; A ~2.3 qualifying rungs per close; B 2-4 rungs per active close (about half the closes)
idea.test_plan: Cheapest decisive test, public data + our index tape: 3 weeks of KXBTCD (~500 closes) -- minute candles via /markets/candlesticks (80 tickers a call, ~2,000 calls over 2 days; reuse .sweep/hunt-2026-10-13/r1-vol-relative-value/pull_history.py + hourly_analyze.py) for cell A, and /markets/trades for cell B (s3c_lottery.py / s3d_lotto_ev.py in r1-crypto-hourly-daily-race, ~5 GETs a close), with the BRTI tape for the projection and vol state (skip the corrupt 20261012T03 hour; tape gap 10-14 03:29Z..10-15 04:39Z). Fit weeks 1-2, hold out week 3, cells and thresholds frozen before the holdout. Bars: A holdout hit rate >= 7.5% at avg ask <= 4.5c and per-close t >= 2; B holdout net > +0.3c/contract with >= 5 winning rung-markets and no single flip carrying more than half the profit. On a pass: a 1-10 contract live taker test for 100 closes with sign-off (max loss = premiums, ~$5-10/day); bars fills at the displayed ask >= 80%, net >= +2c/contract.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SJ26 bought the FAVOURITE rung 15-60 min out (dead); SJ27 pinned $100 brackets at 20 s (dead); D18 killed taking 99c far rungs; D16 killed SELLING 1-5c lottery on the 15-min series because the buyer is informed -- this is the buyer's side, on the hourly ladder, conditioned on vol. No ledger row buys the cheap side of the hourly ladder at either horizon.
idea.worst_case: A dead-quiet week pays nothing and loses every premium: ~-$46/day at 20 lots in A; no tail beyond the premiums paid.
idea.prior_reason: Two independent weak leads (t 1.9 on candles; +0.5c on trades) agree in sign on the same market and match the index tape's fat-tailed base rates; loss is bounded and supply is large. Docked for small samples, multiple looks and the 8x model over-statement; the test is cheap and fast (public data, ~2 days).

test.result: A: the hunter's 2 days reproduce exactly (45 min: 108 rungs, 11 hits, +5.67c; 30 min: 97 rungs, 8 hits, +3.61c; same rungs). Out of sample: 2,478 entries, hit 3.59% against a 5.16% break-even (avg ask 4.82c), so -1.57c/contract. Per close -6.5c (se 2.2, t -2.94); per day t -3.89; 22 of 28 days lose. 45 min alone -1.36c (t -2.19); 30 min alone -1.82c (t -3.04). Weeks 1/2/3: -2.04/-0.98/-1.82c; week 4 is +0.43c only because it holds the hunter's window. Holdout without the hunter window: hit 3.72%, -1.49c, t -1.19, which FAILS the bar (>=7.5% hits, t>=2). idea.name: NHL in-play leader lean: bid the leading team (= offer the trailing team) once a game is lopsided, priced off a lead-and-clock Poisson model, with the stopping-time taker rule as fallback
idea.lane: sports / in-play calibration (maker lean, taker fallback)
markets: KXNHLGAME (regular season, ~8-13 games/day Oct-Apr; quadratic_with_maker_fees x1; pregame touch depth median ~11,900 contracts at a 1c spread, in-play depth not measured)

idea.mechanism: 1) Pregame: fit each team's scoring rate to the game's own pregame price (3.05 goals/team/60 min base, OT = first-goal race), as nhl_model.py (C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-13/r1-sports/) already does. 2) In play, poll ESPN's NHL summary (wallclocked plays) and the Kalshi book every 5-60 s. 3) Only in lopsided states -- leader's mid >= 85c (equivalently trailer <= 15c) in periods 2-3 -- rest a bid on the leader 1c inside the best bid when model fair exceeds our bid by >= 2c + maker fee (0.0175 x p x (1-p), ~0.15c at 90c); 20 contracts, 98 (the pin bot's size) once proven. 4) Taker fallback (r1-new-listings-flows-timing rule): the first minute the leader's ask is 90-98c with spread <= 3c, buy at the ask if the model agrees. 5) Hold to the final horn; pull resting bids on any goal, penalty or goalie pull until re-priced; never quote the 60-80c band. One entry per game.
idea.why_mispriced: Comeback/lottery buyers of the trailing team in lopsided NHL games overpay, and makers leave stale offers on the leader. Three reads agree in lopsided states: (a) sports lane Poisson model, 30 validated games Oct 7-12 (4,538 game-minutes): trailing-side mid above the model by +1.1 to +3.7c in every state, leader below by -1.6 to -4.4c (cluster se 0.1-0.8c); (b) this run's stopping-time grid (grid2.py, 1-min candles Oct 2-15, no hindsight window): leader first at 90-98c with tight spread won 85 of 89 games, +3.35c a contract after taker fee; 95-98c 72 of 72 (+3.9c); trailing side first falling to 3-10c: buyer at the ask -5.1c gross (se 2.0, 86 events); scheduled-clock anchor 80-90c +5.8c (64 events); (c) maker-portfolio tape: NHL in-play 5-10c maker +7.12c (10 events; close-anchored, so biased upward). The counterparty is the retail comeback buyer.
idea.must_be_true: The regular season keeps the pattern (the sample includes Oct 2-6 preseason games); the lean is a bias, not model error (empty-net goals, power plays and shootouts are not modelled; the realised check at 30 games has se 5-15c per state); the cells sit inside multiple-looks noise on their own (9 sports x 4 bands x 3 rules, z ~1.5-2) -- kept only because the model and the grid agree; our resting leader bids are not filled mainly just before a trailing-team goal or a goalie pull (maker adverse selection unmeasured); the 60-80c band is contradictory (first crossing into 60-80c -8.9c at the ask, se 5.7, 75 events; scheduled-clock anchor +11.6c, se 4.9, 58 events) and must stay excluded. Artefact check before believing it: the 95-98c cell's se 0.10 is 'all won', not precision.
idea.evidence_so_far: Model: 30 games, median spread 1c, Brier market vs model a wash (+-0.01). Stopping-time grid (r1-new-listings-flows-timing grid.out/grid2.out): CROSS-ask NHL 90-95c +3.61c (se 2.24, 87 ev), 95-98c +3.86c (73 ev, all won), earlier half +1.8c (68 games) vs later half +8.4c (21); trailing 1-3c came back 0 of 59, 3-5c 0 of 63, 5-10c 3 of 83 (average ask 8.8c). Our own NHL fills: none. Totals leg: a line/result mismatch was seen (ticker -9 vs floor_strike 8.5), not used.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Taker form, one entry a game: 20 contracts x +3.4c x ~8 games = ~$5/day at the current $1,155 bank; 98 contracts = ~$27/day; at $5,000 ~$27-50/day (depth looks non-binding). Maker form adds ~0.5-1c a contract if bids fill (fill share unmeasured). Worst plausible day: two late comebacks at 98 contracts x ~92c = -$180 (at 20 contracts -$37); expect ~4-5 losing games per 100.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~8-13 NHL games/day, Oct-Apr
idea.test_plan: Read-only first, free: (1) re-run nhl_model.py and grid2.py weekly on new regular-season games (~100-115 public calls a week); (2) paper arm now: every 5 s in play log model fair, best bid/ask and depth, the would-be maker bid and every trade at or through it, and the taker trigger. (2) Kalshi public: all 102 settled KXNHLGAME events closing 2026-10-01..10-15 (99 matched to ESPN, 99/99 results consistent; ESPN and the NHL API both label every game from Oct 1 regular season -- the 'preseason contamination' worry is void), 1-min candles of BOTH markets per game (leader ask = min(ask_L, 100-bid_T)), and the full trade tape in every lopsided window (first P2+ minute any side ask >= 80c, to the final horn; 134,195 trades, 0 truncated, 472 public calls). (3) ESPN summary plays (wallclock) for game state, clock interpolated; minutes within 150 s of any goal dropped (unchanged at 360/600 s); ESPN goal wallclock vs Kalshi price jump: 73% within the same minute. test.n_markets: 198 markets / 99 games (Kalshi, Oct 1-14 2026); history table 3,936 games
test.n_independent_clusters: 99 games (83 reach leader 85-98c in periods 2-3; 78 trigger the 90-98c taker rule; 91 have leader-bid fills)
test.result: THE LEAN IS MODEL ERROR. Kalshi leader price vs 3,936-game history (periods 2-3, spread <= 3c, cluster = game): HADJ - ask = +0.59c (85-90, se 0.20), +0.18c (90-95, se 0.15), -0.10c (95-98, se 0.15); raw history H - ask = -0.01 / -1.01 / -0.78c. The hunter's Poisson says +1.95 / +1.45 / +0.99c. The constant-rate model overstates leaders because it ignores score effects (trailing teams score more) and goalie pulls: a 1-goal lead with 2 min left wins 91.8% of the time in history vs 95.4% in the Poisson. Single-season tables move HADJ-mid (85-98) between +0.36c (2025-26) and +1.27c (2024-25), so the history table is uncertain by about +-0.5c. TAKER FALLBACK (first P2-3 minute with leader ask 90-98c, spread <= 3c): ex-ante HADJ - ask - fee = -0.73c a contract (se 0.18, 78 games); 85-90 -0.67c (se 0.25); 95-98 -0.42c (se 0.19); negative with each single-season table (-0.25 to -1.23c). Realised on the same entries +3.49c (se 2.16; 75 of 78 won at average ask 92.1c). That reproduces the hunter's +3.35c and is luck: history expects ~72 wins, observed 75, about 1.4 sd. Realised P&L is positive in both date halves (+2.05, +4.93c) but ex-ante is negative in both. MAKER LEAN (leader-bid fills on the tape, P2-3, 85-98c, 7.3M contracts): ex-ante +1.08c (se 0.16) with the pooled table, +0.67c (se 0.17) with 2025-26 only, +1.0/+1.1c by half. But fills that clear the level (what a back-of-queue joiner gets; 16% of contracts) are +0.27c (se 0.24) pooled / -0.06c (se 0.24) 2025-26, while front/interior fills are +1.38 / +0.95c. Spread is 1c in 88% of lopsided minutes (0c locked composite 8%), so '1c inside the best bid' is almost never possible; we can only join the queue. Fills just before a trailing-team goal are 5.35% of bid-fill contracts vs 5.14% of ask-fill contracts, so there is no informed-seller signature. Best sub-cell (2-goal lead, period 3): bid-fill ex-ante +1.1 to +1.8c, which sits inside the history uncertainty for those states (seasons differ ~2c) and is one of 9 looks.
test.artefact_checks: (a) Post-horn minutes: close - horn median 63 s; 1 event of 99 had a 90-98c candle after the horn, so post-game minutes are not the source of the grid's '72 of 72'. (b) '95-98c se 0.10' is 'all won', confirmed: history says a 95-98c leader loses ~3.5 in 100, and P(0 losses in 58) ~ 13%. (c) Stale ESPN state at goals: dropped +-150 s; result unchanged at +-360/600 s (HADJ-ask +0.26/+0.22/+0.35c). (d) Season drift of the history table: the taker stopping rule (90-98c) ex-ante after fee is -0.40c (2023-24 table, se 0.21), -0.25c (2024-25, se 0.32), -1.23c (2025-26, se 0.25); 85-90c -0.24 / -0.70 / -0.92c. On the every-minute grid the 2024-25 table alone leaves ~+0.2c after fee; the other two are negative. (e) Preseason contamination: none; Oct 1-14 games are regular season per ESPN season.type=2 and NHL gameType=2. (f) Realised markouts (+2c at 3 min) carry the same sample luck as realised P&L (leaders held more this fortnight than history says, and the drift se is understated because a few comebacks dominate the variance), so they are not used as evidence. (g) Self-tests hist.py, analyse.py (planted -3c shift recovered), maker.py (informed-fill world -3.6c, null -0.2c) all PASS.

test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: Taker form: about -$5.70/day expected at 98 contracts x 8 games (-0.73c each), -$1.20/day at 20 contracts. test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Taker: about -$25/day expected at ~425 contracts x 8 games. Maker: $0 to +$9/day at back-of-queue quality; depth is not the limit.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Price vs history: Kalshi sampling se 0.13-0.20c plus ~0.5c history-table uncertainty, so a lean of about 1c is detectable. (1) Crawled Getty's editorial search (specificpeople=118600, sort=newest, enddate=D) for every ET day from 2026-08-31 to 10-15: 46 days, 138 calls at 4 s spacing. (4) On the tape (39 settled + 8 open KXTRUMPPHOTO markets; hunter cache plus 9 fresh unauthenticated calls) I measured: the lock-side price just before T0, lock-side taker trades after T0 + lag (0/20/30/60/120 s) at <=95c and <=90c net of the 0.07*p*(1-p) taker fee, the first print above 95c, and the first competitor trade. idea.name: Coin-race NO-side reward cutoff: a 1,000-lot NO bid one tick above the best NO bid on dead legs
markets: KXCRYPTOLEAD15M dead legs (best YES <= 3c with ~5 min left)
idea.mechanism: On a dead leg the NO side holds 3,000-4,000 at 93-96c and takes the NO half of the $20 pot. A 1,000-lot NO bid one tick above the best (e.g. 97c, $970 reserved) becomes the best bid and the reference AND reaches the 1,000 target alone, so the filed walk stops at our level and every deeper level scores 0: 100% of the NO side = $10 per leg-window, alongside C2-02's YES side. A fill means someone bought the leg's YES at 3c and we hold NO bought at 97c.
idea.why_mispriced: The incumbents' 93-96c NO piles are paid only while nobody improves on them; the buyer of a dead leg's YES pays 3c for an outcome the market prices at ~2-3%.
idea.must_be_true: The alive rate of legs at <= 3c with ~5 min left must be under ~1% (break-even: P(alive) x $970 ~ the $10 credit) AND fills must not cluster just before a leg comes alive (D16: on crypto 15-min the 1-5c buyer was informed; D13: the coin-race favourite-longshot maker lost on holdout). The incumbents must not re-improve to 97-98c. Capital: one leg at a time at the current bank ($970), five at $5,000. A leg 'came alive' in the 10-11 live test (BTC, race 1).
idea.evidence_so_far: Formula only: the filed walk plus live books (NO 93-96c x 3,000-4,000 on dead legs at 11Z 10-13). Alive rate: not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: If the alive rate is under 1%: $5-10 per race on one leg (~$300-500/day gross at the current bank if most races have a dead leg, minus alive-leg losses); about $0 or negative at a calibrated 2-3% alive rate. Worst plausible day: one leg comes alive after a full fill, -$970.
idea.settlements_per_day: 96 races
idea.test_plan: Offline, free: from our tape with research/pinracefair.py / racerho.py over 30 days: for every leg with best YES <= 3c at 300 s left, the rate it finishes first (alive rate), and the YES-buy volume at 2-5c in its last 300 s split by whether it came alive. GO if alive rate x $970 < $5 per leg-window and the 3c YES buying is not concentrated in the legs that came alive; then 10 live legs at 1,000 (sign-off).
idea.prior_reason: Large per race if real, but it is lottery selling on crypto -- a class the ledger killed twice -- with a -$970 tail per leg; the offline alive-rate check is free and fast, so it earns that check and nothing more yet.
merged_from: lip-mechanics: Coin-race NO-side cutoff post (NO at one tick above the best NO bid on dead legs) -- plausible, capital-limited
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SI21 (coin-race LIP at the reference) died on the 100x unit error; D13/D16 are the same lottery-selling exposure WITHOUT the reward. New: the cutoff mechanic (size at the reference ends the walk) and the corrected $10-per-side pot.
idea.worst_case: -$970 on one leg that comes alive after a fill.

test.method:
The idea as filed is dead: dead legs at about 300 s left, NO one tick above the best NO bid, 1,000 contracts, exit 115 s. A variant survives on the trade tape only: one order per race, placed from 600 s left.

I rebuilt every KXCRYPTOLEAD15M leg's book second by second for its last 900 s from our own tape (rank 2 source). This reused C2-02's validated snapshot-plus-delta rebuild and added the full NO ladder and every taker_side=yes trade by price (extract_no.py, one hour streamed at a time). Settlement results came from public /markets: 14,395 legs, with 20 scalar ties excluded.

I replayed the bot rule in sim_no.py, streaming one leg at a time:
- Placement: at the first second at or below T0 left where others' best YES bid is at or below D, post Z NO at best NO + 1, capped at 98c and never crossing the YES bid. The order is live 1 s later.
- Exits: cancel when others' best YES bid goes above 5c; that second's trades still fill us. The exchange removes the order at close minus E.
- Fills (high model): every YES taker contract printed at or above our YES ask fills us first, because we are the lowest ask.
- Credit: the filed walk per second (reference level at cumulative 200, stop at cumulative 1,000, 0.5 per tick below the reference) x $20/1,800 x 0.987, and $0 if under $1.00.
- Scenario A: a snapshot counts only when others' YES side holds at least 1,000. This is the filing's two-sided exclusion, which I read in the filing text.
- Scenario B: our own C2-02 YES 1c filler supplies the YES side.

I ran a 54-config grid (T0 600/450/300, D 1/3, E 115/60/20, minimum best NO 0/93/95). Configs were chosen on the FIT half (565 races up to 10-07) and read on the TEST half (566 races, 10-07 to 10-15). The one-order-per-race version is causal: it takes the first leg to qualify. Alive-leg fills were stressed at x1.5, x2 and a full 1,000 fill. We have no live NO fills of our own, so this rests on the tape alone.

Scripts and outputs: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C2-07/ (extract_no.py, sim_no.py, agg_no.py, agg2.py, agg3.py, agg_final.out, agg2_final.out, agg3.out, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 5,655 legs in 1,131 complete races. A race counts only with all 5 legs present and no feed silence over 60 s in its last 600 s. Window: ET 2026-10-01 (partial) to 10-15 (partial), 14 ET days, with the 10-14 PC-off gap inside it.
test.n_independent_clusters: 1,131 races (the 5 legs of a race share one outcome). The loss tail clusters by day: 14 ET days.
test.result:
Alive-rate bar (the idea's must-be-true #1, under about 1%): FAILS.
- Legs with YES bid at or below 3c at 300 s left: 44 of 2,811 finished first = 1.57% (95% CI 1.14-2.10%). Fit half 2.12%, test half 0.97%.
- At or below 1c: 1.18%. At 600 s left: 4.50%.

Where the comeback buying lands:
- On legs dead at 300 s, YES bought at 1-4c went to legs that came alive only 0.2-1.0% of the time.
- At 5-10c the share is 1.3-7.8%, up to 5x the base rate.
- Comebacks arrive as informed buys at the incumbents' ask, then one-second sweeps. Example: 10-09 04:45 ET XRP, 639 YES bought at 5c about 40 s before the book moved.

As filed, standalone (300 s, at or below 3c, 1,000, exit 115 s), all legs: 4,169 orders placed.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Credit | $1,244 ($0.30 per leg) |
| Gains from fills on dead legs | +$1,493 |
| Losses from fills on legs that came alive | -$3,730 |
| Net | -$992 (-$0.88 per race) |

With one order per race the net is -$5 total.

Why credit is $0.30 per leg and not the idea's $10:
- A leg is dead only for the last ~300 s, so at most 185 of the 900 seconds can pay (at most $2.03).
- On most of those seconds the YES side holds under 1,000, so the snapshot does not count. Supplying that side with our own YES filler raises it to $1.22 per leg.

Variant (a), standalone, one order per race: first leg with YES bid at or below 3c from 600 s left, NO at best + 1 (average 93.0c), 1,000, exit at close minus 115 s.
- Credit $1.95/race, dead-leg fill gains $0.89/race, alive-leg fill losses -$0.91/race. Net +$1.93/race (se 0.62), or $185/day on the tape.
- Holdout: fit $2.00, test $1.85.
- 13 of 14 days positive. Worst day -$331, worst leg -$613.
- Legs that came alive AND got filled: 7 of 1,131 (0.62%, CI 0.25-1.27%).
- Stress: alive-leg losses x1.5 gives $1.48/race; x2 gives $1.02/race. If every alive leg with any fill filled to 1,000, it is -$3.02/race.
- Exit at 60 s: $2.02/race.

Variant (b), paired with C2-02's YES filler, best NO at least 95c, 300 s, one order per race: +$1.37/race on top of whatever C2-02 itself earns. Fit 1.33, test 1.40, no negative day, worst leg -$119. The same rule standalone makes $0.26/race.

Grid, scenario A: 29 of 54 configs are positive on the test half. The top 5 by fit are all positive on test and all start at 600 s.

Fill P&L per contract is negative in every config. The money comes from the reward paying for lottery selling, not from an edge on the outcome.

Below 1,000 contracts the cutoff stops working, because the walk reaches the incumbents: one order per race goes $0.26, $0.20, $0.14, $0.06 per race at 1,000, 500, 300, 200.
test.artefact_checks:
1. The rebuild is C2-02's validated method, which was checked against our 10-11 live order. Across 15 day-files: 0 non-whole-cent prices, 0 negative book levels, 0 mid-life empty snapshots. The corrupt 10-12 T03 hour and other feed silences were dropped by the over-60-s gap rule and the 5-leg race rule.
2. Price units were decided from the field names (*_dollars); the coin race is linear-cent.
3. Reward unit: $20 = 200000 centi-cents per leg-window. The filing's two-sided snapshot exclusion is applied, and it is exactly what kills the filed $10.
4. The holdout is split by time. The one-order-per-race pick is causal. A look-ahead "deadest book" pick is reported only for comparison ($0.28 vs $0.26 per race).
5. Reaction latency of 0 s or 2 s moves the NO>=95 result by less than $0.03/race.
6. The fill model gives us every YES buyer at our ask or worse. That is right for informed sweeps. It cannot see buyers that our 1c-cheaper ask would ADD, which is why I ran the stresses. The full-fill stress turns variant (a) negative.
7. Per-contract fill P&L is negative in every config; the positive comes entirely from credit.
8. NOT measured: whether Kalshi pays NO-side credit. The only coin-race payment ever checked was YES-side, on 10-11, paid to main pool 0.
9. Resting orders reserve funds, but balance_dollars stays gross (results/BRIEF_FOR_REVIEW.md), so the main bot would not see a $930 hold.

Bar: paid at least 80% of model credit, dead-leg fills within 2x the tape, incumbents above us under 30% of seconds. This test cannot measure the comeback tail.

refs.strongest_objection:
Refuted: the tester's variant (a) (+$1.93/race, $185/day on the tape, $60-100/day at $5k). The verdict stays plausible-needs-data at $0/day now, but only for a different rule with a guard.

Why it fails: the tester's fill model counts only printed trades, so our order is never filled once it goes stale. Variant (a) rests at a FIXED price for up to ~485 s, and the other bidders re-price often (on dead legs the best NO price moved within 30 s in 30% of samples). When a leg starts coming back they pull away, leaving our 2-7c YES offer alone at the top. The tape then shows comeback buyers posting YES bids at or above our price, mostly exact 120-lots. That 120-lot trader also TAKES: 1,357 incoming YES orders of exactly 120 in Oct 1-15, against 27 of 119 and 46 of 121. With our offer in the book, those orders would match us. The tape shows no trade only because nobody else was left at that price. This is the same "stale fill" class that refuted I21 (coin-race reward quoting) on 09-25.

Measured on 3,583 races, ET 09-01 to 10-15:
- Trade prints only (the tester's model): net +$1.13 to +$1.85 per race. On this model the tester's pre-registered September holdout passes (Sep 16-30: +$1.52 to +$2.10).
- Adding crossing 120-lot orders: legs that came back cost $3.74 per race, from 65 such legs filled (6 of them 500+). The losses are spread out: the 6 worst legs are 31% of the total. Net -$0.67 to +$0.05 per race. Oct 1-6 is about -$5 per race. Worst race -$960, worst day -$1,492.
- Adding every crossing order: net -$1.89 to -$1.17 per race.

Legs that came back cost 2.4 to 4.6 times the reward credit; the tester's own bar allows at most 60%. Even on the tester's model and October days, my rebuild finds $1.56 per race lost on legs that came back (tester: $0.91). One leg (SOL, 10-06 06:15 ET, -$458) flips on a 1-2 s timing difference, so the number is fragile.

The filed idea is dead, as the tester found: legs at 3c or less with 300 s left came back 2.29% of the time, more than twice the under-1% bar.

What survives: one guard rule, written before I ran it and not tuned. Cancel as soon as the other bidders' best NO falls 1c further from ours, or on our first fill. Net +$0.58 to +$0.94 per race under every fill model and positive in all four periods. Worst race -$282, worst day -$260. But the reward credit drops to $0.27-0.53 per race (median order life 47 s). It is a replay of our recorded data, so a hypothesis. Kalshi has never paid this account NO-side credit. It still ties up ~$930 per order, which the $1,155 bank cannot spare next to pin; the subaccounts hold $109 and $60.

At $5,000: $56-90 a day on the recorded data, $20-50 a day realistic.
refs.independent_number: Variant (a) with the 120-lot trader's crossing orders counted as fills nets -$0.67 to +$0.05 per race (tester: +$1.93) over 3,583 races, ET 09-01 to 10-15. Built from my own rebuild of our tape's ticker and trade channels (not the tester's order-book rebuild) and my own public /markets settlement query (21,350 legs). Counting trade prints only, it nets +$1.13 to +$1.85. Legs at a YES bid of 3c or less with 300 s left came back 203 times out of 8,868 = 2.29% (95% range about 2.0-2.6%); October alone 52 of 2,993 = 1.74% (tester: 1.57%).

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's fill model only counts trades that actually printed, which quietly assumes every order that would have crossed our 1,000-lot NO bid gets rejected. As a dead leg comes back, the tape shows the same pattern each time: the incumbents pull their 93-96c NO bids, and the 120-lot ladder posts YES bids at 5c over and over. All of this happens BEFORE any YES bid goes above 5c, which is the filed cancel trigger. Our NO bid would still be resting one tick above the old pile, so each of those YES bids would match us unless it was post-only. I checked one case by hand (10-02 12:30 ET, BTC): the best NO fell from 94c to 83c while the ladder re-posted 120 at 5c at least 9 times before the trigger fired with 323 s left.

Counting those crossing orders as fills (my own tape replay):
- Oct 1-13: -$1.57/race; trades-only gives +$1.80.
- Sept 16-30, days the tester never saw: -$2.90/race; trades-only gives +$1.39.
- 117 full 1,000-lot fills in 2,554 races. Worst ET day -$2,162 (09-29).

Variant (a) loses money if more than about 41% of those crossing orders really fill us, and the tape cannot measure that share. Almost all of the loss is where our NO is at 95c or higher (YES ask 5c or less): there every 5c re-post crosses us and the >5c trigger never fires, costing -$10 to -$11/race in both windows.

A redesign survives even if every crossing order fills us: never post NO above 94c, and also cancel when others' best NO falls 3c below its level at placement. That gives Sept +$1.71/race (se 0.55) and Oct +$1.61 (se 0.42), with all four halves positive. But I chose the 94c cap after seeing the data, so it is a hypothesis to pre-register, not a result.

At the current $1,155 bank it is $0 either way. One 1,000 NO reserves about $920 (80% of the bank). A single comeback fill costs $280-$980, and anything over about $231 (20% of the bank) would trip pin's drawdown halt.

refs.strongest_objection:
Refuted: the tester's variant (a) (+$1.93/race). The stats skeptic's crossing-fill argument is not why; the tape contradicts it.

The tape settles the split: YES bids that would cross our NO bid do NOT fill us. The bidders use post-only orders, so the exchange rejects them instead of matching. Over 28 days of our tape (ET 09-16..09-30 and 10-01..10-13):
- The exact-120 bidders posted 1,413,802 resting YES bids at 2-15c.
- Only 57 exact-120 orders ever crossed a resting NO bid, and 15 of those bought the same 120 on several legs at once.
- On dead legs, someone's NO bid sat at or through the bidder's own last price for 10,944 seconds. Blind re-posting would have hit it about 1,350 times; it happened once.

So about 1 in 100 would-be crossings fill (at most 7 in 100 on dead legs). Variant (a) only loses if about 41 in 100 do. Both skeptics' losing numbers (stats -$0.67 to +$0.05/race, execution -$1.57 and -$2.90/race) rest on fills that would not happen.

But the same fact breaks the tester's rule. A YES bid at or above our offer price cannot rest beside our NO bid. So the tester's cancel signal ("others' best YES bid above 5c") can never be seen once our NO is at 94c or more. That is 918 of 1,787 orders, and 203 of the tester's 591 cancels could never have happened.

I replayed the tester's own rule and fill model (printed trades only) on 1,787 races, letting the cancel see only YES bids that could exist:
- Comeback-leg losses rise from $0.96 to $4.21 per race. On the same races, fills differ by -$2.99/race (se 0.92).
- Net at tester-level credit is -$0.81/race (Oct -$1.52, Sept -$0.28), against +$2.01 with the tester's signal.
- Worst day -$1,398; 17 of 27 days positive.
- Comeback losses are 198% of credit, and still 86-117% at my credit upper bound. The tester's own bar allows at most 60%, so the rule fails in both windows.
- Printed trades understate this: once our offer is 4c on a leg worth 20-50c, more buyers would take it than the tape shows.

What survives is the stats skeptic's guard, set before he saw any data: cancel when the other NO bidders drop 1c below their level at placement, or on our first fill.
- It makes +$1.04/race (se 0.11): Oct +$0.87, Sept +$1.16.
- 26 of 27 days positive; worst day -$60.
- The execution skeptic's 94c cap (chosen after seeing the data) fell to +$0.59/race in September, with a -$754 day.

Limits: it is still a replay, Kalshi has never paid this account NO-side credit, and one order ties up about $950 (82% of the $1,155 bank). So it is $0/day now. At $5,000 it is about $100/day on the tape, $20-50/day realistic.

(1) Crossing share, the number the skeptics split on:

idea.mechanism: Every 15 min: diff the program list by id (the endpoint ignores status/series filters for ended rows), and for each new or large pot read the book, apply the filed walk, and record which side is empty or under target, what size at what price makes the market qualify, our share if we add 1,100 at 1c on each side, and the dump history from trades. test.method: Public GETs only, about 1,105 calls, no auth, no orders. (1) Three radar passes, at 09:40Z (with books), 09:51Z and 10:00Z (top of book only). Each pass pulled every active and upcoming liquidity program (limit 5000), the top of book for all 4,784 live program markets via /markets?tickers= in batches of 100 (yes_bid_size_fp and yes_ask_size_fp give an empty-side census of every market), and full books for a seeded random 560 of the 2,538 non-Treasury markets whose top of book did not prove they qualify (weight 4.53). The filed walk (reference = first level where cumulative size reaches target/5; stop once cumulative size reaches the target; 0.5 per tick below the reference; both sides must hold the target) was applied as found, then again with 1,100 at 1c added wherever that does not cross. A self-test on planted books passes (selftest.py). (2) Full program history: 65 pages, 321,623 programs, for the new_event listing rate and the share paid. (3) 1-minute candles for a seeded 110 new_event markets started since 10-01 (at least 26 h old, at most 3 per event), giving minutes from program start until both sides show a bid. (4) 1-minute candles over each program's life so far (up to 48 h) for all 89 claimable empty sides: how long the side was empty, and whether earlier bids on it ended in a minute with volume (swept) or without (cancelled). (5) 85 settled KXYTVIEWSW and KXSOFRD markets from the last 21 days, hourly candles plus results: does a side that looked dead ever win? Source rank: live books, then candles and tape, then history. No replay.
test.n_markets: 4,784 live program markets in the top-of-book census; 560 full books; 110 new_event markets (candles); 89 claimable sides with their history; 85 settled markets in the dead-side check
test.n_independent_clusters: Claimable sides: 56 of 89 are one KXYTVIEWSW weekly family (about 12 videos, one week) and 3 are one SOFR day; the rest come from about 15 events. 84 sweep episodes across about 25 events. The new_event candle sample covers at least 37 events (capped at 3 per event). Dead-side check: 49 markets in about 4 weekly YouTube events plus 11 SOFR days.
test.result: (a) EMPTY BOOKS. Outside Treasury, 0 markets have both sides empty (census of 4,662). 86-90 markets have one side empty and room for a 1c bid that does not cross, $64-67/hour of pot in total. On 77 of those the other side's best bid is 95c or higher (54 are KXYTVIEWSW); only 9 are at 86-94c, $8/hour (Netflix x2, SOFR x3, YouTube views x2, ERCOT, WNBA MVP). Another 257 markets ($1,027/hour) have an empty side where any bid would cross a 99c stack, so they cannot be claimed at any price. Book sample: 98 of 560 unqualified and 32 claimable by a 1c pair; on 30 of the 32 the other side was at 95c or higher, 2 at 80-94c, 0 under 80c. (b) WHY THEY ARE EMPTY. On the 89 claimable sides, the now-empty side had bids earlier and was empty 58% of observed minutes. 84 of 119 earlier bid episodes ended in a minute with volume of 1,000-2,748 contracts, i.e. whole farmer stacks swept. Sweep rate: 0.079 per stack-hour in the 86-94c group (8 in 101 h) and 0.055 in the 95c+ group (76 in 1,392 h). Break-even for 1,100 at 1c on a half-pot side is 0.5 x pot rate / $11: 0.024/h on KXYTVIEWSW and about 0.040/h on the 86-94c group. Posting on all 89 would earn $33.6/h against an expected sweep loss of $55.9/h, about -$22/h or -$534/day. Settled check: the dead-looking side won 0 of 49 (upper bound 4.6%). (c) NEW LISTINGS. At 09:40Z no new_event program was under 6 h old. Listings cluster at 16-20Z, 00-01Z and 04-05Z, 73-639 a day (median about 320). All 68 checked at 12-24 h old were qualified. In the candle sample, both sides were bid at program start on 56 of 110, within 5 min on 99, within 60 min on 102, and never within 24 h on 4 (all YouTube top-video long shots, again a dead side). Since 10-01, 4,625 of 4,773 ended new_event programs paid out (96.9%). No threshold was fitted, so there is no fit/holdout split; the settled check is a separate test of the dead-side assumption. (d) CORRECTION TO THE IDEA: 'the Miami pot is gone' was a timing artefact. KXTEMPMIAH had 10 active $100 programs at 09:40Z and 09:51Z, had none at 10:00-10:02Z, and the next hour's 10 were listed at 10:02:02Z. Miami programs go straight to active about 2 min after each hour and never appear in upcoming. $8,000 was listed for 10-15 against $10,000 for 10 full hours, so about 2 hours were skipped. That is a gap, not an ending.
test.artefact_checks: (1) 'Ended in a minute with volume' stands in for 'swept'; a cancel that happened to share a minute with an unrelated trade would be miscounted. Against that: the volumes equal the stack sizes (1,000, 1,600, 2,748, 2,459, 2,255, 1,599) on markets that otherwise trade 0-5 contracts a day. Even if half the episodes are reclassified as cancels, the pooled rate (0.028/h) is still above the 0.024 break-even on KXYTVIEWSW. (2) Candles carry top of book only, with no sizes, so 'both sides bid' is a lower bound on time-to-qualify; the 12-24 h cross-section from real books (68 of 68 qualified) covers the other end. (3) One market dominates the 4.53 sample weight: a USD/CAD 15-minute window with 6 minutes left at a $200/hour rate. Without it the weighted gross falls from $504/h to about $51/h, all on dead sides, which is why the unweighted census numbers are the ones quoted. (4) $/hour on short programs (Treasury, 15-min) is the rate while running, so pot-change comparisons were quoted only for daily and weekly series. (5) 0 of 49 cannot rule out the 0.55% dead-side win rate needed to break even; it is reported as zero observed, not as proof. (6) In the 86-94c subset (9 markets, about $4/h of credit) the low end of the 90% sweep-rate range (0.039) touches break-even (0.040), so that subset alone is unresolved. (7) Not measured: whether Kalshi pays a one-account pair (C2-01's gate), how fast farmers re-post after a sweep, and new_event qualification from real books in the first 6 h (none existed during the run).
test.supply_we_would_get: Reward pots, not fills. Right now about 86-90 empty non-Treasury sides could be claimed for half their pot, $32-34/hour gross while we hold them alone, and 94% of them are the losing side of a market priced 95c or higher on the other side. The fills we would get are whole-stack sweeps at about 0.055-0.079 per stack-hour (one every 13-18 h per market), each -$11 at 1,100 contracts. new_event pots have no unclaimed window: about 90% are two-sided within 5 minutes of listing.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0. Running the sniper on every claimable side loses about $530/day (earns $33.6/h, sweeps cost $55.9/h). The best subset (9 sides at 86-94c) is about -$3.8/h (-$90/day) at the measured sweep rate. The radar earns nothing by itself; its value is spotting changes.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Same as now, $0. Capital is not the limit: about $980 covers all 89 sides at $11 each. The sweep rate is the limit, so posting everything loses about $530/day at either bank.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Sweep rate: 84 sweeps over about 1,490 stack-hours, 0.056/h with a 90% range of about 0.047-0.067/h. Break-even is 0.024-0.040/h, so the kill holds unless about half the sweeps are misclassified cancels. 86-94c subset: 8 sweeps in 101 h, range 0.039-0.142/h against a 0.040 break-even; the central estimate is twice break-even but this small subset is unresolved. Settled check: 0 of 49 can only detect a dead-side win rate above about 4.6%. Listing timing: to support 'median unqualified > 12 h', at least 55 of 110 markets would have had to be slow; 4 were.
test.worst_case: As filed, the sniper loses $11 per swept side across about 90 sides, roughly -$1,000 if every stack is hit in one day; about -$530/day is the expected loss at the measured rate, not the tail. The radar costs only API calls: about 55 per full census pass (2 program pages plus 49 market batches), or 2 per pass for a programs-only diff (about 200/day at 15-minute spacing).
test.next_test: None for the sniper; it is killed. For the radar ($0, spotting changes only): keep radar.py and diff.py running as a programs-only diff every 15 min (about 200 calls/day). It writes one line per new series, per pot change over 50% on a daily or weekly series, and per series gap or ending. One rule from this run: an hourly series counts as gone only if it is missing between :05 and :55 in two consecutive hours, because Miami lists about 2 min after each hour and never shows as upcoming. Reopen the sniper only if a census finds 10 or more claimable sides where the other side's best bid is under 80c. Today there were 0 (0 of 32 in the sample), and that is the only population where an empty side would not be explained by sweeps.

idea.name: Covered-ask collateral probe: does a resting YES ask backed by YES we already hold reserve any cash? If not, two-sided reward quoting on longshot markets costs ~$20-60 per 1,000-lot instead of ~$1,000 (WEAK until probed)
idea.lane: kalshi-mechanics-capital x lip-economics / sports weekly pots (capital efficiency)
markets: any liquidity-program market whose one side's reference sits at 90-99c: Trump-approval strikes, Miami hourly safe sides, weekly sports-futures pots, election ladders
idea.mechanism: Two-sided reward quoting needs the target size (usually 1,000) resting on BOTH sides. On a longshot the expensive side is NO: NO bids at 95-99c reserve $950-990 per 1,000, and resting orders reserve cumulatively (proven by the repo's straddle test). A resting YES ask at price p sits on the same book side as a NO bid at 1-p. If Kalshi reserves nothing for an ask that only sells YES we already hold, we buy 1,000 YES at 1-3c (ideally as a maker at the bid, $10-30) and rest 1,000 YES asks at the NO-side reference instead of 1,000 NO bids. Capital per two-sided 1,000-lot drops from ~$1,000 to ~$20-60. If an ask is lifted we sell inventory at the reference (a small profit if it was bought at the bid). Risk bounded: the inventory going to zero.
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi pays the reward pots. The carried 'weekly dead-pot basket' (lip-economics) was rated '$10/day per $1,000 of collateral, capital-limited'; if covered asks reserve nothing, the limit becomes the number of qualifying pots, not cash.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The matching engine treats an ask fully covered by a held YES position as reducing that position and reserves nothing new -- not documented, not measured on our account. (2) Covered asks count as NO-side resting size in the reward score (they sit on that side of the book). (3) Collateral Return/netting being off (all 9 of our subaccount-shard pairs) does not change (1). MERGER NOTE: N2-02 shows ~$650 of the main bank is idle at every close, so below that this probe only matters for scaling to many pots at once.
idea.evidence_so_far: Docs: resting reservation default 'sum reserves all resting-order margin' (target_balance_allocation); 'max' and the new 'none' option (changelog) apply only to the automatic rebalancer. results/FULL_PLAN_FOR_REVIEW.md proved straddles reserve cumulatively and balance_dollars is gross. No test has ever placed a covered ask. How many pots this would unlock: not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 directly. If covered asks reserve nothing, each $100/week pot held alone at near-zero capital is worth ~$14/day before fills (lip and sports lanes' numbers), so the current bank could hold several pots instead of ~one; at $5,000 the cap is pot count, not cash. If covered asks reserve like NO bids: $0, dead in one test. Worst plausible day: the longshot inventory goes to zero, -$10-30 per market-week.
idea.settlements_per_day: weekly / daily pots
idea.test_plan: On the DEMO exchange (demo orders are permitted) or with 1 live contract and sign-off: buy 1 YES at <= 5c, read the shard balance; rest a post-only 1-lot YES ask far above the market; send a second order sized to exactly the remaining balance (the straddle method) -- accepted vs insufficient_balance shows what the ask reserved; cancel. Cost <= $0.05, minutes. Then GET the incentive scoring for that market to see whether the ask is counted on the NO side.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New. The earlier straddle test answered two opposite bids, not an ask covered by held inventory; no ledger row.
idea.worst_case: The longshot never pays off: lose 1-3c x 1,000 = $10-30 per market-week against a $100/week pot.
idea.prior_reason: Five-cent, minutes-long test that could multiply the reward family's capacity; but reward pots carry their own fill cost (the 10-11 coin-race test: paid +$11.04, fills -$12.45) and the money is unmeasured either way.

test.method: Read-only; no order was placed (this run forbids orders, demo included), so question (1), whether a resting ask backed by held YES reserves cash, is NOT measured. What I did measure: (a) Our own Kalshi settlement records (results/kalshi_ledger.json, 1,888 settled markets): 42 markets where we held YES and then bought NO. (b) Our past refused and accepted orders at near-zero shard cash (pinsmoke-20260908T064741Z.jsonl; the 09-07 netting v1 run in HANDOFF_ARCHIVE_2026-09.md:6599-6618). (c) Kalshi docs and the CFTC filing text already saved by earlier lanes, plus the help centre. (d) Whether covered asks would earn anything: a public scan (covered_scan.py, 419 unauthenticated calls, 2026-10-15 09:57Z). It read all 4,823 active reward programs, kept the 4,667 markets whose pots run 20 hours or longer ($126,008/day listed), and read 400 books: the top 260 by pot plus a seeded random 140. Each book was scored with the filing's rules (reference = first level where cumulative size reaches target/5; cutoff at target; 0.5 per tick below the reference; a second counts only when both sides hold at least the target). Each market was priced four ways: join only the cheap side; quote both sides naively; quote both sides with the expensive side covered by held inventory; the expensive side alone, covered. All four honour the no-crossing rule for post-only orders. Inventory carry cost uses the maker-portfolio lane's longshot table, spread over the days to close. Then a greedy capital allocation, with and without covered asks, at $300 / $650 (the idle cash N2-02 measured) / $1,155 / $2,800 / $5,000, for all markets and for quiet ones (24 h volume of 100 contracts or less). Source ranking: own settlement and order records, then live books, then docs. No replay, no tape loss rates.
test.n_markets: 400 books scored (397 on the 1c grid, 395 non-empty) out of 4,667 markets with 20 h+ reward pots; plus 42 of our own hedged settled markets for the netting question
test.n_independent_clusters: 104 series / 137 events in the book scan. KXRT is 183 of the 400 and dominates the top-260, so the random-140 sample is the representative one. One snapshot in time, not a time series.
test.result: 1) THE FAST PATH THIS IDEA NEEDS DOES NOT EXIST. On 395 of 395 non-empty books the expensive (90-99c) side ALREADY holds the full target from other people. Median size already scored there is 24,210 contracts, so our 1,000 would take about 4% of that side's half of the pot. The side that is short is always the CHEAP side (55 markets), and 49 of those cannot be posted at all: the other side's 99c bid makes any 1c bid cross. So 0 of 395 markets need anyone to fill the expensive side for the market to start paying (95% upper bound about 0.8%). 2) Per dollar, the covered expensive side loses to the same market's cheap side in 181 of 208 markets (top) and 82 of 112 (random). Median after inventory carry: covered side -$0.02/day on $140 (top) and +$0.93/day on $145 (random); cheap-side join +$4.62/day on $105 (top) and +$2.01/day on $70 (random). The idea's premise, that a quoter must post both sides, is wrong: once a market counts, each side's share is paid separately, and the cheap side of an already-full market is the cheap slot. There are far more cheap slots than the bank can fill. 3) Extra gross reward from allowing covered asks (greedy, one snapshot, filing formula, before fills, never verified as paid): at $650, +$0.5/day on quiet markets and +$18/day on all markets (top-260); +$4-8/day on the random sample. At $1,155: +$0.5 to +$39/day. At $5,000: +$2 to +$111/day, about 5% on top of the $2,029/day the plain options already reach. The bigger numbers sit on busy KXRT ladders, where the LIP lane measured fills eating the reward (RT -$6/day net at 300 a side). 4) MECHANISM, unmeasured but better evidenced than 'weak': (a) Kalshi nets YES against NO inside one market even with netting OFF. On our 42 both-sides markets, settlement revenue equals the NET position only. KXWTI15M-26SEP181015-15: 5 YES + 10 NO, settled YES, revenue $0. KXBNB15M-26SEP282000-00: 30.3 YES + 60.6 NO, settled NO, revenue $30.30. Kalshi's FIX docs also list 'SingleMarketCollateralReturn: collateral freed from reducing/closing a position in a single market'. So must-be-true (3) holds, and the unofficial-docs claim 'Kalshi doesn't net YES/NO intraday' is contradicted by our data. (b) The 09-07 v1 run accepted a covered post-only ask (0.02 @ 0.30, plain reserve $0.0140) on a shard holding $0.0123. At the time it was waved off as whole-cent rounding down. Our own 09-08 refusal rules that out: 0.01 NO @ 0.992 needs $0.0099 against $0.0026 and was refused insufficient_balance, though rounding down would have made it $0.00. Rounding to the NEAREST cent still explains both, so this is suggestive, not proof. (c) The CFTC filing says 'a yes ask is counted as a bid for no', so must-be-true (2) is documented.
test.artefact_checks: (1) My first pass said covered asks were worth +$1,590-2,885/day. That was an artefact, found and fixed: it ignored the no-crossing rule (a 1c bid against a 99c bid fills at once, the Miami SI04 kill) and compared only against posting both sides. With the cheap one-sided options and the crossing rule added, the extra falls to +$0.5-18/day at $650. (2) Prices come from the *_dollars fields only. Ticks are read per market from price_level_structure (397 linear_cent; the 3 tapered markets were dropped). (3) The first program read returned only 1,000 rows because of the wrong cursor key. Fixed to next_cursor: 4,823 programs, matching the LIP lane's 4,843 on 10-13. (4) One snapshot, so shares move. 'Expensive side always full' is the robust finding (395 of 395); the dollar figures are formula gross, not paid money and not net of fills. (5) The longshot carry cost is a population number from the tape, not our fills. (6) The netting reading rests on Kalshi's settlement 'revenue' field showing net-only payouts. pinledger treats that field as misreported on hedged markets. Final cash is the same either way, but the net-only pattern is what shows single-market netting.
test.supply_we_would_get: Covered-ask slots exist on about 320 of 397 scanned markets: the expensive side of KXRT, AAA gas, EIA crude, snowfall, Trump approval and photo, approval rating, MLB award futures and others. Each is worth about 4% of half the pot, because 10-24k contracts already rest there. No market's payout depends on us supplying that side. Fill exposure on a covered ask is the same as on a plain bid on that side; not measured here.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 to +$5/day at the current bank. Measured formula gross at the ~$650 idle: +$0.5/day on quiet markets, +$18/day if busy KXRT ladders are included before their unmeasured fills. The core mechanism (whether a covered ask reserves cash) is still unmeasured.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: +$2 to +$23/day gross on quiet or random-sample markets; +$111/day gross if busy ladders are counted (about 5% on top of the plain reward options); net of fills not measured
test.smallest_detectable_effect: 0 of 395 books needed the expensive side, so a share of such markets above about 0.8% would have shown (95%, rule of three). The dollar comparisons come from one snapshot of 400 markets; per-market differences under about $1/day are inside snapshot noise and are not claimed.
test.worst_case: If built anyway: the inventory dies worthless. That is 1,000 contracts at 1-3c, -$10-30 per market, about -$15 at the median carry, and -$100-300 for a 10-market basket in a bad week. Covered asks lifted on news cost the same as a plain bid on that side being hit. If covered asks DO reserve cash, every 1,000-lot locks $900-990, the same as today.
test.next_test: Not worth building as a money idea. The 5-cent probe is still worth running ONCE, on demo or with the operator's live sign-off, for a lose-less reason: if position-reducing orders reserve nothing, a stop or hedge stays fundable on a fully deployed account. The 09-07 plan concluded that was impossible, and it matters once bet size outgrows idle cash. Probe: on a fresh shard, buy 0.02 YES at 30c or less; spend free cash down to under 0.3c; post a post_only ask for 0.02 one tick inside the spread, where the plain reserve is at least 1c above the remaining cash; send a control bid AT the best bid, also at least 1c over cash. PASS = treatment accepted AND control refused insufficient_balance, both margins over 1c (rounding then cannot explain it). Then cancel. Cost under $0.05 and minutes. Reopen the money idea only if a later book scan finds markets whose expensive side holds less than the target from others.
