idea.name: First-five-minutes model-conditional maker on the 15-min crypto series (join only the overpriced touch, 600-900 s to close), plus the hourly-ladder extension
merged_from: crypto-15m-new-angles: First-five-minutes one-sided maker (join the touch only where takers overpay the model, 600-900 s to close)
crypto-15m-new-angles: Hourly-ladder cousin of the first-five-minutes maker (same CF 60-s rule, 24 closes/day, deeper books) -- unmeasured extension
idea.mechanism: Every second from the book's first appearance (61-76 s after the open) until 600 s before close, compute the bot's fair Phi((spot-K)/sd), sd = sigma x sqrt(var_factor(tau)) with tau in SECONDS TO CLOSE (pinrun.fair's r argument is only right at tau < 60). When the YES ask >= fair + 2c, rest a post_only SELL-YES at that ask (join the queue; no maker fee on these series); mirror on NO. One side at a time; cancel when the edge drops under 1c or at 600 s; never quote inside 10 min; hold fills to settlement. Run it in its own subaccount (the main bot sizes from cash). Extension: the same rule on the 3 KXBTCD rungs nearest the index in the first minutes after each hourly open.
idea.why_mispriced: Early-window takers are retail, not index-model bots (Burgi-Deng-Whelan 'makers gain, takers lose', confirmed here only 600-900 s out): every maker fill in that band realised +0.84c (fit, t 5.0) / +0.72c (test, t 3.7) per contract, clustered by close; where the taker paid >= 2c over the model +2.2c / +5.9c (fit) and +2.3c / +2.7c (test). Inside 300 s the sign flips (informed takers; makers -3.3 to -3.5c), which is why MAKER_SIM / D17 (quoting at all times, both sides) lost.
idea.must_be_true: Our fills are not the informed subset: the queue at the touch is 40-150 contracts on alts and ~3,000 on BTC, so we fill only when a level is eaten, and big sweeps are the informed fills. MAKER_SIM's own 600-900 s cell with a real queue was -0.10c at L=0, i.e. the queue penalty may eat the class average. The 5c+ overpay edge shrank fit -> test (+5.9c -> +2.7c). Beyond ~8 min the model is over-confident (the market is better calibrated at 8-14 min); the realised-fill measure already includes that. Unchecked: whether the overpay population shrinks when a second model-conditional maker appears; hourly early flow (extension) unmeasured.
idea.evidence_so_far: Trade tape 09-01..09-21 (fit, 16,915 markets) vs 09-22..10-12 (test, 17,131), every 15M trade with a model fair at the trade second, settle check 34,046 of 34,047 against Kalshi's determination; per-close clustered t. 300-600 s: +0.33c fit (t 3.3) but +0.16c test (t 1.5); 5c+ overpay there +4.1c fit, -1.1c test (does not replicate). test.method: SOURCE: this rests on a queue-aware REPLAY of our own tape (rank 4), which per the test plan can kill an idea but never prove one. A trade-tape population companion (rank 2) runs alongside it. (1) mm600.py imports research/makersim.py's Sim unchanged for the queue: an order joins the BACK at landing; fills come from queue, walk-through or a crossing arrival; a cancel needs the ack, so a stale order stays live for L ms. On top of that sits the idea's exact rule. fair = Phi((spot-K)/(sigma*sqrt(var_factor(tau)))), with tau = seconds to close, sigma = trailing 600 s sd of 1-s index increments, spot = the latest index print WE had received (by _rx_ms). Post at the touch when YES ask >= fair+2c (sell YES) or YES bid <= fair-2c (buy YES), one side at a time. Keep while edge >= 1c, follow the touch, cancel on our own clock at 600 s, net cap 3x size per market, hold to Kalshi's own 'determined' result. It streams snapshot + delta + trade + cfbenchmarks_value one hour at a time, only the first 306 s of each quarter, at ~75 MB. The planted-world self-test passes: FIFO fill 5 / LAST 0; the 2c gate blocks a 1.5c edge while an ungated mutant fills; the 600 s cancel blocks a taker at tau 598 while a no-window mutant fills; flee works. (2) Sample: 51 hours (4 a day, rotating through the hours of the day), 10-01..10-13, 9 coins. FIT = 10-01..10-07 (28 h); HOLDOUT = 10-08..10-13 (23 h). Six variants: prorata, behind and last at 300 ms; prorata at 1000 ms; a 1-lot; a 4c entry. A post-hoc sensitivity run on 14 fit hours tried L=50 ms, L=0, flee-3s and a combined version. (3) tapepop.py: every 600-900 s trade in the same hours, same model, maker P&L at settlement with no queue. (4) Extension: btcd.py, KXBTCD via unauthenticated REST. 138 hourly events 10-08..10-13, the 3 rungs nearest BRTI at the hourly open, first 25 min of trades, fair from our BRTI tape. Files: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-03/ (mm600.py, anal.py, anal_full.txt, anal_run2.txt, tapepop.py, tapeanal.txt, btcd.py, btcdanal.txt, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 1,836 fifteen-minute markets (fit 1,008, holdout 828), all with a Kalshi 'determined' result and a lifecycle strike (0 fallbacks); 504 more in the sensitivity run; 402 KXBTCD rungs in 138 hourly events.
test.n_independent_clusters: Clustered by close time: 112 fit + 92 holdout = 204 closes; 56 in the sensitivity run; KXBTCD 67 + 71 events.
test.result: Our simulated fills lose in both halves, in every variant and on 63 of 64 sampled variant-days. Primary variant (prorata, 300 ms, 20-lot): FIT -1.68c per filled contract (t -6.2, 313,732 contracts, 112 closes); HOLDOUT -1.49c (t -5.4, 296,118 contracts, 92 closes). All six variants lose in the holdout (-1.25c to -1.83c, t -2.1 to -7.7). The bar (holdout >= +1.0c) FAILS by 2.5c, about 9 standard errors. The sweep share is 24%, which passes, but that no longer matters. Why: the model edge at our fill was +2.7c, yet the model fair moved 3.1c against us within 5 s (3.6c by 30 s). 78% of filled contracts were stale orders picked off during our cancel round-trip. Optimistic bound (every crossing order post-only, never filling us): fit +0.42c (t 0.4), holdout -0.58c (t -0.5), still a fail. Speed does not save it: L=300 -1.83c, L=50 -1.58c, instant L=0 -0.76c (t -1.2), flee -1.80c, combined -1.72c. Alts-only is worse (holdout -1.68c, t -6.0). Population in the same hours, no queue: taker overpaid 2-5c gave makers +4.4c (t 1.3) fit and +4.5c (t 1.2) holdout. So the hunter's effect exists but belongs to makers already at the front of the queue; joining at the back costs 4-6c per contract. KXBTCD extension, population only: first 10 minutes with overpay >= 2c gave +2.56c (t 0.9) fit and +2.58c (t 1.0) test; all trades +1.27c / +0.06c. Not significant, and on the 15-min books a +4c population turned into -1.5c for our fills.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Signs: the model edge at fill is +2.7c, exactly what the gate requires, while realised P&L is negative, so the loss is selection, not a flipped sign; the self-test books its planted fill at +60c. (2) Settlement: Kalshi 'determined' results for 1,836/1,836 markets; strikes from lifecycle, cross-checked against the previous-window index average (max gap 7e-5, which is rounding). (3) Units: prices parsed from *_dollars strings, never inferred from size; KXBTCD count_fp summed over one rung's life equals its volume_fp exactly (198,549.55). (4) Book consistency: 4,981 of 2.7M prints exceeded the displayed level; 518 delta lines carry a _seq_gap flag. (5) The biggest doubt is CROSS fills (73% of contracts): a post-only crosser would be rejected rather than fill us. But removing every cross fill still leaves the holdout at -0.58c, and instant reaction (6% cross) still loses -0.76c. (6) The tape cannot see takers who would have lifted our stale quote, which biases the replay in our favour. (7) Control: the same model on the tape population comes out positive, so the estimator can find a positive number. The 5 s and 30 s markouts are large and negative, consistent with the loss.
test.supply_we_would_get: 15-min crypto books (Kalshi, 9 coins): a 20-lot rest gets filled about 13,000 contracts an hour (~360 per market per 4-minute window, mostly re-posts after being picked off); a 1-lot about 750 an hour. Supply is not the limit; the sign is. KXBTCD: about 700k contracts a day of taker flow overpaying the model by >= 2c on the 3 near rungs in the first 10 minutes of each hour. That is population flow, not fills we would get.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0, dead. Run as proposed at today's ~$1,155 bank (20-contract rests, alts + ETH), the replay says about -1.7c per filled contract, roughly -$190 an hour. A loss limit would stop it within the first hour.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0, dead. More size only means more contracts at the same -1.5c.
test.worst_case: Replay holdout: about -$237 a day at 1-contract rests on all 9 coins. The proposed 5-lot live test on BTC+XRP+ETH would lose about -$300 a day (scaled from -$76 a day at 1 lot on those three), so its -$20/day kill bar trips on day one. 20-lot alts+ETH: about -$4,500 a day nominal (the loss limit stops it first). Worst single market -$72 at 20-lot.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Holdout primary: se 0.27c per contract over 92 closes, so the smallest detectable effect is ~0.5c (95%, two-sided) or ~0.76c at 80% power. The measured -1.49c sits 9 se below the +1.0c bar. Optimistic no-cross bound: ~3c. KXBTCD population per half: ~5c, so a 2c effect cannot be seen.
test.next_test: Do not run the proposed 5-lot live test: the replay predicts it fails its own +1.0c and -$20/day bars on day one, and even an instant, co-located-speed version loses. The only open thread is the KXBTCD hourly extension, and we do not record its book. Deciding it needs an operator decision to add KXBTCD near rungs to the collector's orderbook_delta subscription (not touched here). Then record 5+ days and run mm600.py over the hourly window. Bar, written now: holdout >= +1.0c per filled contract at L=300 including cross fills, t >= 2 over >= 60 events, sweeps < 60%. The prior is low.

idea.name: In-play momentum-overshoot offer (maker): when a side's price first climbs into 60-80c, rest an offer on that side at its ask and hold to settlement (WEAK-MODERATE; fills and adverse selection unmeasured)
idea.mechanism: 1) Watch the in-play book on one public WebSocket. 2) The first time a side's ask enters 60-80c having been below 55c earlier in the match, with spread <= 3c, post a sell (offer) on that side at the current ask, 20 contracts (free to post on no-maker-fee series). 3) If lifted, hold to settlement; cancel after 2 minutes or if the price moves 5c. Equivalent to buying the trailing side at 20-40c as a maker. Exclude NBA (-10.3c cell).
idea.why_mispriced: Measured at a STOPPING TIME (the first minute the price crossed into the band -- a moment a bot can act on, not a window ending at the real close): the side that just climbed into 60-80c wins less often than its mid says, -4.1c at the mid (se 1.6, 952 events; tight spread -2.9c), both time halves negative (-2.8c, -5.3c). The market over-reacts to the swing (a map won, a break of serve, a goal). A taker cannot harvest it (buying the other side at its ask nets +0.6c, se 1.6 -- spread and fee eat it); a maker selling at the ask can, if the buyers who lift it are momentum buyers rather than people who saw the next point first.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Our offer is lifted by ordinary momentum buyers, not mostly by faster TV/stream watchers -- the adverse-selection cost is unmeasured and is the whole question. (2) The overshoot holds out of sample: t ~2.5 pooled is inside multiple-looks territory (9 sports x 4 bands x 2 directions were looked at). (3) Queue position at the ask is reachable. (4) Minute candles fairly record the displayed book (Kalshi's own bid/ask closes; no depth).
idea.evidence_so_far: grid2.py stopping-time cells (1-minute candles, last ~10 h of 1,417 settled sports events 2026-09-24..10-15, one entry per event, holdout split at 10-11 14:20Z), seller at the ask, gross before adverse selection: pooled +6.5c (952 events); tight spread +3.7c (923 events; halves +2.5c / +5.0c); by sport (tight) esports +7.1c (119 ev), soccer +10.6c (70), cricket +9.6c (49), NHL +5.3c (75), tennis +2.8c (367), MLB +2.9c (75), football +0.2c (103), NBA -10.3c (43). Fade as a taker +0.6c (se 1.6). The same 1,417 events under the old hindsight cut (random minute 5-60 min before the actual close) show the opposite picture, which is why this cell was invisible before. Self-test world (race to 12 points, duration depends on who wins) reproduces the hindsight bias sign; planted +6.6c recovered.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Fill rate unmeasured. If 30% of ~200 qualifying matches/day fill 20 contracts and adverse selection takes half the +3.7c: ~$20/day at $1,155 (collateral 20-40c x 20 per match, minutes to hours); $50-80/day at $5,000. If fills are mostly informed: $0 or negative. Worst plausible day: 15 filled offers at 70c that the climbing side all wins = -$90 against a +$20 expected day.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~200-500 qualifying in-play triggers/day across tennis, esports, soccer, cricket, NHL (952 of 1,417 sampled events triggered)
idea.test_plan: Read-only 2-week recorder on the public WebSocket (orderbook_delta + trade) for esports/tennis/soccer/NHL: at each 60-80c first crossing log the ask depth ahead of us and every later trade at or above our hypothetical offer price; score fills by FIFO queue and by their own settlement (so adverse selection is in the number). Pre-registered bar: >= 150 filled events, net >= +2c per contract after the fills' own outcomes, both weeks positive. Then 5-contract live offers with sign-off.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New and opposite in sign to the carried maker-portfolio '20-40c comeback fader (sell the trailing side in-play)' and to the 'never rest an ask at 60-99c in play' RULE; both rested on hindsight windows. LOSE-LESS IMPLICATION for the carried idea: if the climbing side is rich at 60-80c, the trailing side is cheap at 20-40c, so the comeback fader would sell the cheap side -- it must not go live without a stopping-time re-measure. Only measurable once the stopping-time rule (dropped below as NO-MONEY, evidence kept here) was applied.
idea.worst_case: A filled offer at 70c on 20 contracts that the climbing side wins costs $6; a bad night of 15 such fills is -$90.
idea.prior_reason: Large flow and a stopping-time cell that survives both halves, but t ~2.5 among many looks and the fill/adverse-selection cost -- the thing that kills most maker ideas here -- is entirely unmeasured; two weeks of recording to decide.

test.method: Data sources: the trade tape and 1-minute candles, no replay. (1) I rebuilt the hunter's stopping-time entries exactly from his cached candles (grid2.first_cross, CROSST 60-80, spread <=3c, prior ask <55, >=60 s before close). That gives 923 entries on 1,417 events, with a mid gap of -2.90c and a seller-at-ask gross of +3.64c, the same as his numbers. (2) Fills scored on their own outcomes. I pulled the public trade tape of every entry market for [T-60 s, T+300 s] (923 of 923; 4 truncated at 6 pages). I then simulated a 20-lot sell of the climbing side at its ask, posted at minute-close T, live for 120 s, cancelled if the side printed 5c lower first. No historical sports depth exists, so the queue is bracketed: FRONT (first in queue at the ask), D200/D1000 (that many contracts ahead), THRU (only a print strictly above our price proves the fill, a sure fill), IMPRV (one tick inside the ask when the spread is >=2c, so nobody is ahead). P&L per filled contract = price - 100 x won - maker fee on maker-fee series. Adverse selection = filled events minus all triggered. The self-test passes: hand-built tapes for both sides, cancel and window, plus planted worlds (uninformed buyers recover +4c with about 0 adverse selection; informed buyers give -12.9c). (3) A real holdout. I pulled 1,422 fresh settled events the hunter never saw: the 12 days before his earliest close in each series, same volume >=3,000 filter, same 10 h of 1-minute candles, zero event overlap. The identical rule, unchanged, gives 835 entries. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N2-03/ (entries.py, pull_tr.py, fills_an.py, oos_pull.py, entries_oos.py, oos_more.py; outputs fills.out, entries_oos.out, oos_more.out, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 1,758 entry markets: 923 in the hunter's sample (09-24..10-15) and 835 fresh (09-13..10-14). Trade tapes pulled for all 923 in-sample entries.
test.n_independent_clusters: 1,758 events (one entry per event; cluster = event). On the idea's own sports (tennis, esports, cricket, NHL, soccer): 680 in-sample, 650 fresh.
test.result: The overshoot does not hold on fresh events. Seller-at-ask gross, before adverse selection: hunter's sample +3.64c (se 1.62, 923 events) against fresh events +0.04c (se 1.66, 835). On the idea's own sports: +5.01c (se 1.89, 680) against -1.14c (se 1.87, 650), a drop of 6.2c (z 2.3). On fresh events the climbing side, at a mean ask of 63.5c, won 63.5 times in 100, so it is fairly priced; in-sample it won 59.7 in 100 at 63.3c. By sport, in-sample then fresh: tennis +2.67 then -2.43 (367/366 events), esports +6.99 then -0.96 (119/169), cricket +9.47 then -1.20 (49/59), soccer +10.59 then -2.31 (70/16), NHL +5.24 then +10.47 (75/40, se 7.8), MLB +3.55 then +1.52, football +0.05 then +5.80. The in-sample spread-1c sub-cell (+5.17c, 623 events) flips to -1.84c (487). The two halves of the fresh set are +2.16c and -2.07c. Fills, measured in-sample (the flattering set): 2-minute fill rate 76% FRONT, 66% D200, 63% D1000, 58% THRU. Adverse selection -0.16c (FRONT), -1.14c (D200), -2.06c (D1000), -2.16c (THRU). Net per filled contract +3.07c (se 1.87), +2.19c, +1.41c, +1.27c (se 2.10). Tennis, which is most of the supply, is the worst: adverse selection -2.9c (FRONT) to -4.4c (THRU), and net per filled contract -0.14c and -1.88c even in-sample. IMPRV (one tick inside the ask, 300 eligible events): -2.07c per filled contract (se 3.30). Applying the in-sample adverse selection to the fresh gross gives about -0.2c to -2.2c per filled contract pooled, -1.3c to -3.3c on the idea's sports, and about -5c to -7c on tennis.
test.artefact_checks:
- I reproduced the hunter's entry set exactly before extending it (923 entries, -2.90c mid gap).
- The fresh sample has zero event overlap with his and uses the same selection rule and filters. No parameter was refit.
- The fill model is unit-tested on both sides (NO side price = 100 - yes price), on the cancel rule and on the window. The planted-world self-test recovers a planted +4c and a planted -12.9c adverse selection.
- Trade tapes are complete for 919 of 923 windows; the other 4 are NFL-size, truncated at 6,000 trades.
- Queue depth is NOT measured, because no historical sports book exists. I bracketed it with FRONT vs THRU, and both brackets give the same verdict once the fresh-sample gross is used.
- The trigger fires at the minute close, later than a live WebSocket bot would act. That bias is of unknown sign and small next to a 6c in/out gap.
- Multiple looks: the cell was picked from about 9 sports x 4 bands x 2 directions, and its out-of-sample collapse is what that predicts.
- Recorder liveness: the tape file kalshi_data/trade/20261015T10 was written at 10:12Z (06:12 ET). The collector processes did not show up by name in a read-only process listing; nothing was touched.
- About 1,400 public calls used; scratch folder 5.6 MB; 123 GB disk free.
test.supply_we_would_get: The idea's sports have about 380 settled events a day with volume >= 3,000 (a lower bound: tennis about 300, esports about 60, cricket about 9, NHL about 6, soccer about 3). Of those, 59-65 in 100 trigger, and 58-76 in 100 of the triggers fill within 2 minutes. That is roughly 130-190 filled 20-lot offers a day (about 2,600-3,800 contracts), about 80% of them tennis, the sport with the worst adverse selection.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0, because it should not be run. Run at 20 lots, the central estimate is a loss of about $30 to $70 a day: a fresh-sample gross of -1.1c, minus 0.2-2.2c of adverse selection, on about 2,900 contracts a day. The 95% range is roughly -$170 to +$40 a day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0, do not run. Scaled to about 80 lots, the central loss is roughly $120 to $280 a day, if the books have the depth.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: The fresh sample alone can detect 4.6c per contract pooled (se 1.66, 835 events) and 5.2c on the idea's sports (se 1.87, 650 events), at 80% power. It cannot see a true edge of +1-2c, but it does reject the hunter's +3.6c (pooled, z 2.2) and +5.0c (idea's sports, z 2.3 on the in/out gap).
test.worst_case: Fresh-sample day totals at 20 lots, with every trigger filled: worst day -$118, then -$71 and -$66. The sample covers only part of each day's matches, so a full day of every match would lose more. The hunter's -$90 bad night is an understatement at the measured fill rates.
test.next_test: None for this idea: its own holdout killed it before any recorder was needed. Reusable: fills_an.py scores trade-tape fills against their own outcomes, with FRONT/THRU/inside-ask queue brackets, and is the cheap test to run on any sports maker idea before building a recorder. Lose-less note: the hunter warned that the carried in-play '20-40c comeback fader' sells the cheap side. That is NOT supported out of sample: the climbing side is fair on fresh events (+0.79c outcome-minus-mid, se 1.66, 835 events). The fader still needs its own stopping-time measurement, but this cell is no evidence against it.

test.method: Public GETs only (~525 calls, 16 of them HTTP 429); no orders, no authenticated calls. (1) Pulled every ACTIVE and UPCOMING liquidity program at 2026-10-15 10:07Z (8,289 rows; period_reward /10000 = $). Kept those with a period of 100 h or more: 3,830 markets on 434 series, $66,933/day. Joined to the 10-13 catalogue's 24 h series volume. (2) Took seeded samples. DEAD = 90 markets from the 238 series trading fewer than 50 contracts/day per open market. NAMED = 122 markets of the idea's series: KXCPIYOY all 42, KXAAAGASM all 26, and samples of YTVIEWSW, CPI, CPICORE, STATELEG and HEADLINE. DPZ has no active program today, and the Hormuz pots are 24 h, not weekly. For each market I pulled the full order book, the 14-day trade tape and its metadata. (3) Scored every book with the 2026-07-15 filing walk, with OUR 1,000 inserted: the reference is the first level where cumulative size reaches target/5, the walk stops where cumulative reaches target, and credit halves per tick below the reference. A = join at the reference (as filed). B = the cheapest price that gets at least 95% of the best share (outbid by a tick). C/CA = cheap side only. The self-test has planted books, including a share-exactly-zero case, and passes. (4) Capped time-ordered simulation over the 14-day tape: 1,000 per side, filled pro rata at our score share until gone, either no re-post or re-post daily. refs.strongest_objection:
The idea assumes the quote is almost never filled. That is false once the test does not look ahead. I placed a 1,000-a-side quote at the prices visible at the start of each week and ran the tape forward. On mid-priced strikes (10-90c) it was filled in 40 of 40 market-weeks, and the first fill came within 0.8-4.5 h (median). Ordinary drift runs over the stale side. Two hand-checked cases: CPIYOY-26SEP-T3.6, NO bid at 62c, run over as YES went 37c to 44c in a day: -$592. AAAGASM-26SEP30-4.40, NO bid at 45c, run over as the market went 52c to 79c: -$450. A filled order no longer earns, so the quote collects about $0.8-1.1/day of reward, not $5-7.

The tester's positive numbers rest on two flattering assumptions:
(a) The open-market simulation priced the quote at TODAY's reference and valued fills at TODAY's mid over the PAST 14 days. That is look-ahead, and it makes fills cheap by construction.
(b) Fills were split pro rata at our score share (~25%). But when the market trades THROUGH a price level, every order at that level is filled before deeper ones, so a joined order takes the whole through-quantity, not a quarter of it.

Re-posting daily to keep earning makes it worse: -$14 to -$18.5 per market-day.

Plumbing makes it worse again. These markets sit in cash pool 0, and since v-onepool all main cash is in pool 2. Resting orders reserve cash cumulatively, netting is OFF, and the balance figure pinrun sizes from ignores what resting orders reserve. So in the main account pinrun would size off cash that is already committed. The only idle pool-0 cash is the ~$42 in subaccount 3, enough for about 40 a side: $0.23-0.36/day of reward before fills. 10 of the 26 AAA gas pots can never pay anyone: 99c YES stacks mean any NO bid would cross.

idea.name: AI weekly-dashboard favourite carry: buy the >= 65c side 3 days before the Sunday close on the OpenRouter author-share, Vercel open-weights and Arena-rank weekly markets (SI17 re-measured as a plain price rule)
markets: KXOPENSHARE, KXGOOGSHARE, KXANTHSHARE, KXDEEPSHARE (OpenRouter weekly token share by author, 9 strikes/week each, Sunday close)
KXCHINAAI, KXTECHRANKLISTAICODE (LM Arena rank at a date, weekly)
idea.mechanism: Every Thursday ~12:00 ET read each open fixed-date weekly market. Buy YES at the ask when the YES mid >= 0.65 and ask <= 0.92; buy NO at the NO ask when the YES mid <= 0.25 and NO ask <= 0.92; skip the 0.30-0.60 coin-flip zone. Size 100 contracts or the displayed ask size, whichever is smaller. Taker fee 0.07 x p(1-p) = 0.5-1.3c. Hold to settlement. Exclude release-before-date series (KXGEMINI/GPT/CLAUDE): they settle early on YES and their settled list is survivorship-biased.
idea.why_mispriced: The week's number is a running aggregate: by Thursday 4 of 7 days are already in the total and visible on OpenRouter's public rankings, so the outcome is near-determined while the market still shows 73-90c. Who pays: holders of the other side with stale quotes (books 2-4c wide) and reversal bettors. The loss case is a mid-week model launch that shifts share (KXGOOGSHARE 21.4 in the 10-05 week: NO at 0.80 lost).
idea.must_be_true: (1) Out of sample the favourite side at D-3 loses under ~1 in 8 (break-even for +12c wins vs -80c losses). (2) 50-300 contracts sit on the ask at those prices (per-market volumes 14k-180k say plausible; not read from a live book). (3) Capital ~$800 for 10 positions of 100, locked 3-4 days -- in the MAIN account this cuts the pin bot's bet size (sized from cash), so it must run in a subaccount or after the kalshi-mechanics lane's 'size the main bot on account equity' change.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter pro-desk, calib_slow.py (331 public calls, settled markets + daily candles): fixed-date weekly sci-tech subset 84 markets / 29 events (4-5 weeks). 3 days before close, YES buyer at the ASK by YES-mid bucket: 60-70 2/2 won (+27c), 70-80 2/2 (+18.5c), 80-90 5/5 (+10.4c), 90-100 5/5 (+5.4c) -> 14 of 14 won, ~+12c on asks 0.73-0.95; the one 50-60 case lost; 40-50 YES 3 of 7 (-25c). NO buyer at the NO ask: YES-mid 00-10 19 markets won 19 (+3.4c at 0.97), 10-20 10 of 10 (+7.7c at 0.92), 20-30 5 of 6 (+0.8c). Full sci-tech table at D-3 (calib_slow.out, incl. release series): 60-90c buckets 16 markets / 15 events all YES; 10-40c 24 markets / 21 events realised 0.00-0.20 vs priced 0.14-0.36. N0 arithmetic: if the D-3 ask were fair (~0.83 average), 14 of 14 wins happens ~7 times in 100 (0.83^14), so this is about two-sigma evidence; with ~15 events and 0 losses the 95% upper bound on the loss rate is ~20 per 100, so the sample cannot tell +12c from break-even. Volumes: OPENSHARE median 30k / max 183k contracts per market, ANTHSHARE 22k / 100k, DEEPSHARE 14k / 179k, GOOGSHARE 31k / 92k.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: In-sample ~7 events/week -> ~4 favourite + 2-3 NO buys/week at 100 contracts: ~$67/week = ~$10/day on ~$800 locked 3-4 days. At $5,000: ~$40-50/day if 500-contract asks exist (unmeasured). Worst plausible week: two launch-driven flips at 100 contracts = -$160 (-$800 at 500 lots).
idea.settlements_per_day: ~7 events/week (4 author-share + Vercel + 2 Arena), 9 strikes each; about 1 event/day
idea.test_plan: Paper, 4 weeks, no bot code: first read Thursday 2026-10-16 12:00 ET. Each Thursday pull the open weekly markets' books (public /markets/{t}/orderbook), log the rule's side, ask and displayed size; settle Sunday from /markets. Pre-registered bar: >= 20 entries, <= 1 loss, mean >= +6c after fee, median displayed ask size >= 200. Pass -> $100-200 live in subaccount 1 for 4 more weeks; kill at 2 losses in 20. Companion: on Thursday scrape OpenRouter's per-author weekly table and confirm the running sum sits on the favourite's side of the strike (checks the running-aggregate mechanism directly). Add to results/READS_DUE.json.
idea.prior_reason: ~$10/day at today's bank, liquid books and a fast cheap test that starts tomorrow; but 4-5 weeks of in-sample data, ~15 events, two-sigma at best, and the series are new (Kalshi can re-strike or delist).

SJ42 killed only the reveal RACE on Vercel/RCP, not a 3-day carry. Not in the carried r1 index.

test.method:
Data sources, best first: Kalshi's public hourly candles (the YES bid and ask at the end of each hour) and the settled result from /markets. No replay and none of our own fills were used.
(1) discover.py listed every market in the 7 named series plus 9 sibling AI-dashboard series: the OpenRouter Tencent, Xiaomi, Alibaba, Z-ai and Mistral share series, KXTOKENUSE, and the Arena-type KXTOPMODEL, IMAGEAI and SPEECHAI. That is 1,455 markets.
(2) candles.py pulled hourly quotes for 955 settled markets. That covers every OpenRouter-share market. Rank-type strikes with under 200 lifetime contracts were skipped because they sit at 1c and can never meet the rule.
(3) analyse.py applied the rule exactly as written. Its self-test builds a fair world and a world with a planted bias, and it passes.
- The rule: buy YES at the ask when the YES mid is 0.65 or more and the ask is 0.92 or less. Buy NO when the YES mid is 0.25 or less and the NO ask is 0.92 or less. Taker fee is ceil(0.07 x 100 x p(1-p)) per 100-lot.
- Entry times: the pre-registered one, Thursday 12:00 ET (16:00Z) falling 2 to 7 days before close. Also D3 (close minus 72 h, close to the hunter's own timing), and D1, D2 and D5 to check robustness.
- Clusters: every OpenRouter lab series in a given week settles from one chart, so a week counts as one cluster. Other series cluster by close date. Standard errors are cluster-robust.
- Holdouts: (a) markets not in the hunter's calib_slow sample; (b) the 9 sibling series the rule was never fitted on; (c) early half against late half (closes before, and from, 2026-09-21).
(4) orweeks.py compared OpenRouter's public weekly author chart (52 weeks) with 438 settled strikes. 407 matched exactly, 9 were within 0.05 points (Kalshi rounds to one decimal), and 22 had the lab off the chart, which resolves No. The settlement mapping holds.
(5) book_now.py read the live public order books of all 101 open markets in the 7 series on 2026-10-15 at about 06:20 ET, plus OpenRouter's running share for the current week.
About 1,210 unauthenticated public Kalshi calls in total. Scripts and outputs are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-02/ (analyse.out, book_now.out, discover.out, RESULT.json).

idea.name: Jump-triggered mid-price entry inside the last 60 s (take the stale offer after a >= 4-sigma index print in our favour)
merged_from: crypto-15m-new-angles: Jump-triggered mid-price entry inside the last 60 s (the stale offer after a 4-sigma index print)
idea.mechanism: When a 1-s index print moves >= 4 trailing-600-s sigmas with 10-60 s left, recompute fair with the new print; if fair - ask - fee >= 2c on either side at a MID price (the pin only buys >= 99.5% confidence; the forecaster only from 75c inside 30 s), send an immediate IOC at the displayed ask and hold to settlement 10-60 s later.
idea.why_mispriced: Some resting offers are slow to reprice after a jump: the stale offer is still there 1 s later 78-81 times in 100 and 3 s later 63-65 times in 100, so it is not only a first-100-ms race. Realised P&L of taking the quote 150 ms after our receipt of the print (fresh quotes only, ticker age <= 2 s): test half 321 jump-markets in 20 days +9.7c/contract (t 5.0 clustered by close); at +1 s +5.9c (n 261, t 2.9); fit +15.0c / +6.9c. 60-120 s: +4.6c at 150 ms but +1.4c at +1 s (t 1.3); beyond 120 s negative in the test half.
idea.must_be_true: The offer must be takeable by our ~43 ms warm round trip against faster takers (SJ09/10/42/44 lost first-100-ms races; here the offer survives a full second 4 times in 5). The book already sits nearer the post-jump fair 50 times in 100 BEFORE the print reaches us (the book leads the CF index), and the measured P&L includes those. Our fills are adversely selected on top of the tape number (live pin fills lose ~3 per 100 where the tape says 0.11). Live counter-evidence: the forecaster's own entries with 30+ s left lost 5 of 14 markets (-$12.73, READS_DUE fc-early-skip) -- mid-price buys before 30 s have already lost money live. Overlaps the forecaster inside 30 s.
idea.evidence_so_far: Tape only (population, not ours): .sweep/hunt-2026-10-13/r1-crypto-15m-new-angles/runA|runB2/jumps.csv.gz (130,940 + 124,021 jumps), persist.py, fresh.py; ~16 qualifying jump-markets/day in the 0-60 s band (test); touch size 44-150 contracts.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Tape upper bound at 20 contracts: 16/day x 20 x 6-10c = $19-32/day; realistic with adverse fills $3-10/day at $1,155; $10-40/day at $5,000 (50-100 contracts) if the offers are real for us; could be $0 if the persisting offers are the ones the index then catches up to (the +150 ms -> +1 s decay hints at that). Worst plausible day at 20 contracts: three 70c takes that flip, -$42.
idea.settlements_per_day: 864 markets/day; ~16 triggers/day
idea.test_plan: (1) Free: join the forecaster's live fills (results/forecaster-live-orders.jsonl) and the main bot's fills to >= 4-sigma favourable prints within 1 s before each buy (BRTI and alt indices from C:/kals/kalshi_data/cfbenchmarks_value, read-only); report count and money of jump-triggered fills vs the rest -- if jump-triggered live fills already lose, kill. (2) Then a 1-contract live arm for 14 days with the trigger as the only entry (sign-off: new family); bars fill rate >= 50%, realised >= +3c/contract after fee over >= 150 fills, no day worse than -$10.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: P06 ('index moved >= 3 wobbles AGAINST us', needs-data) and the live --jump-gate are refusals on the bot's own 99.5% entries; this is the mirror (a jump IN FAVOUR as the entry trigger at mid prices) with the offer persistence measured. D25/F17 (exchange-feed lead) are about moves after our entry.
idea.worst_case: A 20-contract take at 70c that flips: -$14; three in a day -$42; at 100 contracts -$70 per event.
idea.prior_reason: Strong tape numbers in both halves (t 5.0 / 2.9) and a cheap free first check, but the tape-to-live gap on this project is large, the forecaster's live 30+ s entries already lost 5 of 14, and the money at today's bank is $3-10/day at best.

test.method: Three read-only measurements. (A) Step 1 of the test plan, OUR LIVE FILLS (source rank 3). livejoin.py joined 137 forecaster fills (110 settled markets, forecaster-live-orders.jsonl) and 912 pin-bot fills that carry t_ms_decide (769 settled markets, pinrun-live-*.jsonl) to the 1-s CF prints in kalshi_data/cfbenchmarks_value (489 hours). For each fill it scored the largest move IN FAVOUR of the side bought, among prints visible in the 2 s before the decision, in trailing-600-s sigmas. Self-test with a planted jump: PASS. (B) Probe of the hunter's data source (probe_ticker.py, hour 20261012T15). The ticker channel is a snapshot sent about once a second per market (median gap 1,002 ms) and 18.9 in 100 trades print THROUGH its displayed quote. The hunter's jumps.csv quotes (bid/ask at 150 ms, 1 s, 3 s) all come from that channel. His jump loop also only covers 45-870 s left (scan15m.py line 369), so the 10-45 s part of the idea was never measured. (C) Re-measurement on the TRUE ORDER BOOK (source rank 2, tape). scan_book.py rebuilds the book from orderbook_snapshot (yes_dollars_fp/no_dollars_fp) plus orderbook_delta in seq order, for every market with a >= 4-sigma 1-s print and 3-120 s left. It ran on 126 randomly drawn UTC hours, 09-02..10-15, with the PC-off gap excluded. 3 hours failed the rebuild check and were dropped. On the 121 kept, the rebuilt top of book matches the ticker at 204,604 of 205,742 ticker timestamps (99.45 in 100), with 0 negative levels and 0 result mismatches. The bot is run as specified: live fair model (scan15m.fair_at with engine.var_factor, effective strike, trailing-600-s sigma); decision on the true book at the moment Kalshi sends the print (sending_ts_ms); IOC limit at that ask; fill only against what is still offered at or below the limit in the book 75 ms later (sensitivity 50 and 150 ms), so faster takers have already taken their share; hold to settlement; taker fee rounded up per order. Cluster = close time. Holdout = the hunter's own split: fit = closes before 2026-09-22 (where 4 sigma / 2c were chosen), test = 09-22 onward. The hunter's ticker method was re-run on the same events for a like-for-like comparison. Files in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-06/: livejoin.py, probe_ticker.py, scan_book.py, analyze_book.py, bytime.py, outputs livejoin.txt, analyze_book.txt, bytime.txt, cand.jsonl, RESULT.json.

The tester's $0/day comes from too small a sample to mean anything. It rests on 26 holdout fills in 21 closes, below the project's 30-close floor. Its own smallest detectable effect was +/-16c, so it could not tell 0 from +7c.

I scanned the full trade tape: 971 hours, all of 09-02..10-15 except the PC-off gap. Results come from Kalshi's public API; 42 of 33,529 disagree with the 60-s mean computed from the index. In the 09-22+ holdout, the offers takers actually bought 40-150 ms after a >=4-sigma print (10-60 s left, >=2c under the post-print fair) made +7.3c a contract after fee at 20 contracts: t 3.9, 439 markets, 331 closes. The fit half made +10.1c. The tester's own pass bar is met on this fill model (holdout >= +3c with t >= 2, fit positive, last 3 weeks +6.7c t 3.5).

The number holds up under every check I ran:
- Taking the last 20 contracts instead of the first gives +6.4c; pro-rata gives +6.7c.
- Arriving later, 250-1000 ms, still gives +5.3c (t 3.2).
- It is positive on every coin and on both YES and NO.
- Leaving out what the pin and forecaster already buy gives +7.2c (t 3.6).
- The clock is sound: the send gap is 3 ms at jump seconds, and there are no duplicate trade ids.
- A random-second control (same rule at ordinary seconds) gives +0.8c (t 0.5) in both halves, so the jump is what pays.
- On the tester's book data, offers nobody took within 1 s were not worse (33 signals).

What still stands against the idea:
1. This is the tape, not our fills. Our share against the bots already doing this is unmeasured; the book shows our price still offered at +75 ms only about 55 times in 100.
2. It is fading. October alone is +4.7c (t 2.1), the week of 10-05 is +1.6c, and the last 9 days were about +$4/day at 20 contracts.
3. It is lumpy: without the best 20 of 331 closes it is +2.8c (t 1.6).
4. The model promised +13.7c a contract and delivered about half, so a 2c margin is thin.
5. The only nearby live evidence is negative but tiny: forecaster entries with 30+ s left lost 5 of 14 markets.

Money: about $5/day now (range $0-15); about $20/day at $5,000. Worst plausible day at 20 contracts: the tape's worst was -$38, so allow about -$50 live. At 98 contracts the tape's worst day was -$196.

idea.name: Collapsed-fill reaction for the residual inside-20-s class: after an entry fills >= 3c under the ask seen, raise that market's insurance line to 0.60 and block its top-up/late add
merged_from: crypto-lose-less-and-forecaster: Collapsed-fill alarm: after an entry fills >= 3c under the ask the bot saw, raise that market's hedge line to 0.60 and block its late add (WEAK)
idea.mechanism: Our IOC sweeps to the 98c limit; a fill far BELOW the ask seen 40-90 ms earlier means the book collapsed during the order's flight (someone dumped our side into us). React at the order reply, seconds before the 1 Hz index shows the move: for that market only, insure at belief < 0.60 instead of 0.40 and do not top up / late-add. A cheap collapsed entry plus insurance can lock a small gain (ZEC 10-10: YES 31c + NO 61c = 92c for a $1 payout).
idea.why_mispriced: n/a -- a lose-less rule; the dumper knows (taker sell share 60-82% in the 3 s before on the losers).
idea.must_be_true: The collapsed class must keep losing several times the base rate AFTER the seller check (--toxic-fresh, being switched back on) has removed what it catches; the earlier insurance must fill better than the 0.40-line one; false-alarm insurance on the winners must cost less than the losses saved. The insurance path must never be blocked.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter (own fills 09-08..10-13, first entry leg): >= 3c under the ask seen 20 mk, 4 lost (20/100), -$21.44 vs 722 mk, 15 lost (2.1/100), +$458. After 10-09: ETH 10-10 09:15 ET -$47.13 (tau 21; the seller check would refuse it) and BTC 10-13 16:15 ET -$32.69 (top-up at tau 28 filled ~55c against 98c sent, sellers 0.82; the check refuses its first buy at 37 s). FINAL_SYNTHESIS 10-09 rejected a collapse rule (TEST group 7 markets, 1 lost, -$1.79) and put 'first fill 2c+ under the ask' on watch with the rule 'live change only after 3 NEW losing markets of the type after 10-09' -- 2 so far (ETH 10-10, BTC 10-13).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: <= $1-2/day at the current bank (~$40 per caught event, ~1 per 2-3 weeks on top of the seller check); about 4x that at $5,000; a worst-market claim. Worst plausible day: 2 extra false-alarm insurance legs, ~-$10.

test.method: Source: our own live fills only (no replay, no tape). Rebuilt every filled entry leg, the per-second hedge_quote records (the model's belief in our side, the opposite ask and touch size), every executed hedge and every settlement from the 33 raw pinrun-live logs, 09-22 12:15Z to 10-15 06:45Z. Money comes from results/kalshi_ledger.json through pinledger.pnl. The counterfactual for each market starts at the order reply of a first entry leg that filled >= 3c under the ask the bot saw. From there it insures every contract held on that side at the first per-second quote with belief < 0.60, priced at that quote's ask plus the slip measured on our 27 real hedge fills. If the real hedge came first or in the same second, the real fill is used. Later same-side entry legs are dropped and the real hedges after the trigger are replaced. The seller check (tau > 20, level age < 500 ms, taker sell share over 3 s > 0.5) is applied as a population filter. Variants: gap 2c or 5c; line 0.50 or 0.70; trigger on any leg; insure only; block only; also block late adds on the flipped side; slip at p90. Control: the 0.60 line on every market. Split at 10-09, the date of the watch rule. A true holdout after 10-14 had 0 collapsed fills. The self-test (a planted world and a null world) passes. Also measured: a lead-time table over all 21 markets with a real hedge, and a side probe of an 'opposite ask jumps' trigger. idea.name: Resting-order hygiene gate for every maker/reward bot: cancel_order_on_pause and expiration_time on every order, decrease-not-cancel, check the book before a post_only re-post, re-post on reactivation, exchange_index on off-shard cancels
idea.lane: lose-less (kalshi-mechanics-capital): protects the live resting-order bots (penny ladder sub 1, coin-race reward filler) and every future maker arm
markets: every resting-order strategy on Kalshi; today: KXBTC15M family (penny ladder, sub 1), KXCRYPTOLEAD15M (racereward)
idea.mechanism: A builder-side self-test that refuses any order body missing these, plus the rules: (1) cancel_order_on_pause = true (default false: GTC orders survive the Thursday 03:00-05:00 ET pause, and during a pause cancels are impossible). (2) expiration_time on every order so expiry happens on the exchange (since 10-01 an amend changing only the expiry keeps queue priority). (3) Shrink with POST .../decrease (keeps FIFO place); a price change or size increase goes to the back. (4) A post_only order that would cross is rejected AND still creates a cancelled record; repeated crossing triggers a temporary rate limit -- check the book before re-posting. (5) Reactivating a market cancels ALL resting orders; re-post on the 'activated' lifecycle event; after close_time every order operation including cancel is rejected. (6) Self-trade prevention applies across subaccounts (taker_at_cross kills the incoming order, maker kills the resting one). (7) Cancels off shard 0 need exchange_index in the query string or they 404 and silently do not cancel. (8) Order groups work per shard only.
idea.why_mispriced: Makers who leave quotes up through pauses are the ones who paid in SJ09: $11,614 was taken from stale <=97c winner-side quotes in decided markets in the first second of 3 Thursday reopens. Nobody pays us; it stops us being that maker.
idea.must_be_true: We run resting-order bots. Merger check 2026-10-15: research/cleanroom/ladder_live.py builds GTC post_only bodies with no expiration and no cancel_order_on_pause (line 243), and its body_ok() REQUIRES time_in_force == good_till_canceled (line 252), so adding the flags means updating that self-test too; grep finds cancel_order_on_pause in 0 files under research/. The ladder placed 13,574 orders (results/ladder-live-orders.jsonl); its sizes are 1-6 contracts at ~2c, so today's exposure is small -- the gate matters most for the larger maker arms this hunt proposes (N2-03, N2-05, reward quoting).
idea.evidence_so_far: Docs saved under r1-kalshi-mechanics-capital/docs/ (maintenance_and_pauses, market_lifecycle, amend-order-v2, decrease-order-v2, order_groups, subaccounts). Lifecycle tape: deactivations are common on props (KXMLBHRR 29,523 deactivations across 38,834 markets; NFL props deactivated/reactivated 100-200 times per series). Own incidents: 10-06 the ladder held 15 contracts against a cap of 10 because a cancel was in flight; 10-11 a racereward cancel returned 404 while the order was still resting (2 tries, +1.3 s).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 directly at today's ladder sizes. Prevents a stale-quote sweep (up to the full resting size x the price gap, each Thursday reopen) and overfills on any larger maker bot; at 200-contract weather bids (N2-05) one stale sweep could cost ~-$196. Worst plausible day without it: one Thursday reopen sweep of every resting quote.
idea.settlements_per_day: n/a

test.method:
This is a check on how we protect resting orders, not a trade. Sources in rank order:
(1) Kalshi public REST: the markets around 3 Thursday pauses for KXBTC15M, KXETH15M, KXSOL15M and KXCRYPTOLEAD15M, plus the trade tape for each tape gap.
(2) Our own tape in C:/kals/kalshi_data: trade and cfbenchmarks_value over 1,156 hours (2026-08-25 to 10-15), and market_lifecycle_v2.
(3) Our own live order logs: results/ladder-live-orders.jsonl (13,656 order sends, 09-28 to 10-15), racereward-live.jsonl (7 orders) and dipsell-live-orders.jsonl (36 sends). Also 9 authenticated GETs of this account's own history: the fills of the 3 reward races, and one order GET with and without exchange_index.
(4) The 2026-10-02 SJ09 exchange-wide reopen trade cache (.sweep/run-2026-10-02/exchange-mechanics/closure_*.json, 3 Thursdays), used for what makers lost at the reopen.
No replay was used.

Code read: ladder_live.py, racereward_live.py, dipsell_live.py and ordercli.py; pinrun and pinracearm send IOC orders only.

Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N2-07/: pause_markets.py, pause_lifecycle.py, ladder_scan.py, cancel_timing.py, ladder_vanish.py, outage_scan.py (its positive control is the Thursday pause itself), gap_rest_check*.py, reopen_maker.py and own_probe.py.

Holdout: nothing is fitted, because this is a rule, not a model. Every incident count below is 0 across the whole window.
test.n_markets:
- Around the pause: 60 listed 15-min markets (4 series x 3 Thursdays, 06:15-09:30Z).
- Ladder: 13,656 orders in about 12,700 markets.
- Reward test: 3 races, 15 of our own fills.
- Dipsell: 32 orders.
- Reopen maker loss: 388 markets traded in the first second across 3 Thursdays.
test.n_independent_clusters:
- 8 Thursday pauses on our tape; 3 of them have exchange-wide reopen trades.
- About 51 days of crypto-shard tape for unscheduled pauses.
- 236 events in the first second after the 3 cached reopens: 131 tennis, 27 weather, 6 crypto.
test.result:
1) NO 15-MINUTE MARKET EVER SPANS THE THURSDAY PAUSE.
- Kalshi lists no 15-min crypto or coin-race market closing inside 07:00-09:00Z. The last close is 07:00:00Z and the next market opens at 09:00:00Z. This held on 10-01, 10-08 and 10-15 for KXBTC15M, KXETH15M, KXSOL15M and KXCRYPTOLEAD15M.
- The lifecycle tape shows 0 crypto 15-min markets created inside the window.
- The ladder's last orders before each pause died with their 07:00 close: the bot's cancels got 409 market_closed at 07:00:00.1-02.4, on all 3 Thursdays.
- So cancel_order_on_pause protects the live ladder and the reward bot by exactly $0.

2) NO UNSCHEDULED PAUSE ON THE CRYPTO SHARD IN 51 DAYS.
- The scan looks for stretches with no 15-min trades while the index keeps printing. Its positive control works: all 8 Thursday pauses were found, about 7,230 s each, and Kalshi's REST tape shows 0 BTC trades 07:00-08:00Z on all 8.
- Every other silence of 120 s or more (64) and every mid-quarter silence of 60-120 s (48) had BTC trades on Kalshi's own tape in its first 30-60 s. All 112 of the 112 checked were our collector missing prints, not exchange pauses.
- 1,661 more 60-120 s lulls start within 90 s of a quarter-hour open, when the ladder rests nothing. Those were not checked.

3) RULE 7 IS ALREADY DONE, AND ITS EVIDENCE WAS MISREAD.
- Both bots send exchange_index=2 on every DELETE (ladder_live.py:447, racereward_live.py:815/863).
- The 10-11 '404 while still resting' cases (3 of 3) each came 0.24 s after a 200 cancel of the same order. A second, redundant cancel, triggered by the lagging resting-order listing, hit an order that was already cancelled. Kalshi then showed it as 'canceled'. This was not an off-shard miss.
- Ladder: 212 cancels got 404 before the close, and all 212 were orders that had fully filled. So there were 0 orders that disappeared without a fill: no self-trade kills and no silent cancel failures.
- 13,277 of 13,673 ladder cancels (97%) are sent at or after the close. Kalshi's docs say every order operation is refused then and the exchange cancels resting orders itself. These are wasted writes with no money effect.

4) RULE 2 (expiry set on the exchange) WOULD HAVE SAVED 0 CONTRACTS.
- All 15 reward-test fills happened at least 62.8 s before the close (latest at 08:58:57.23Z), i.e. before the bot's 60-s exit.
- The ladder's orders already end at the close: they rest a median of 27 s in the last ~30 s.

5) RULES 4, 5 AND 6.
- Rule 4, post-only orders that would cross: 10 of 13,656 ladder sends (0.07%), never more than 2 in a row, and no 429 anywhere in the log. Dipsell had 2 of 36.
- Rule 5, reactivation wipes: they cannot happen on crypto 15-min. The lifecycle tape has 0 deactivated or activated events in about 4,400 markets per coin. They do happen on props and on commodity 15-min markets (KXSILVER15M and KXCOPPER15M, 28 each).
- Rule 6, self-trade prevention kills: 0 (see 3).

6) WHERE THE PAUSE RULE WOULD MATTER (future bots).
- Exchange-wide, makers whose quotes stayed up through the pause lost $28,911 on 605,004 contracts in the first second of 3 reopens: -4.78c a contract, 236 events.
- 92% of that was tennis: -$26,469, 131 events.
- Weather: -$613 on 5,537 contracts (-11.1c), 27 events; $604 of it was on 09-17 alone.
- Crypto markets other than 15-min: +$49 on 1,476 contracts.
- The same markets 60-300 s later, where quotes were posted after the reopen: makers made +1.93c a contract.

NOT MEASURED:
- How Kalshi treats a DELETE sent without exchange_index; testing it needs a write. A GET of a shard-2 order returned 200 whether exchange_index was left out, 2 or 0, so GETs are not shard-routed.
- Whether shrinking an order or changing only its expiry keeps queue position. The amend-order-v2 docs say so; it is untested live.
test.artefact_checks:
- Positive control: the outage scan must find the scheduled pause, and it does. 8 of 8 found, about 7,230 s each, with the index still printing in 93-99% of seconds, and REST shows 0 trades 07:00-08:00Z on all 8.
- Two bugs in earlier versions of the scan were caught and fixed before the run reported here. One under-counted index coverage across multi-hour gaps; the other re-read index files over and over (quadratic slowdown).
- Stretches where the collector was dead (60 gaps where the index also stopped, including the PC-off period 10-14 03:29Z to 10-15 04:39Z) were left out, not counted as 'no pause'.
- Every tape silence of 120 s or more was checked against Kalshi's REST trade tape instead of being trusted.
- Ladder 404s were split by whether they were sent before or after the close, and matched to booked fills: 212 of 212 had filled.
- Reopen maker P&L has a selection effect: settled results exist only for tickers that traded in the first 10 s, so markets with no early print are missing. The 60-300 s window uses the same markets, so it is a matched control. But the event counts per family are small (weather 27, crypto 6), and single outcomes dominate them.
- Units: prices come only from the *_dollars fields, counts from the *_fp fields.
test.supply_we_would_get:
Not applicable: this prevents losses; nobody pays us for it.

Exposure it covers today:
- Only the penny ladder (subaccount 1) rests orders. The reward bot stopped on 10-11 after 3 races, and dipsell stopped on 10-10.
- The ladder's most at rest at once is 9 markets x 6 contracts at 95-98c, about $53. It can never rest across a pause, because no such market exists.

The flag only does something for future maker bots on markets that do span Thursday 07:00-09:00Z: weather daily high/low bids in the last 24 h, sports and tennis, hourly and daily crypto, and reward quoting on long-dated markets.
test.worst_case:
Today: leaving the flag out costs nothing, because no exposure exists.

If a future bot ships without it and rests across Thursday:
- One bad reopen sweep takes its whole resting size, for example 200 x 98c = -$196 on one weather order.
- A tennis or sports resting bot faces the worst family measured: -4.6c a contract on 574k contracts in the first second.

If the flag is added:
- The order is cancelled at 07:00Z and has to be posted again after 09:00Z, which loses its queue place. Makers made money on the reopen flow after the first second: +0.25c a contract at 1-10 s and +1.93c at 60-300 s.
- An unscheduled outage during a 15-min market would now cancel the ladder's bids, and the ladder would not post them again in that market. That is the safe direction.
test.next_test:
No paper test is needed for today's bots.

1) Ship it as a builder rule for NEW maker bots only: weather last-24-h bids, reward quoting, and any good-till-cancelled order on a market whose life covers Thursday 07:00-09:00Z. The self-test refuses any body without cancel_order_on_pause=true and without expiration_time = the earlier of the planned cancel time and the close. Add the same to ordercli.build_reward_order.

2) Do not redeploy the live ladder just for this; it is a measured no-op there. Fold it into the ladder's next change, and at the same time stop sending cancels after the close (97% of its cancels).

3) Optional one-time check on demo (demo orders are allowed):
- Place a resting order carrying both fields, and send a DELETE for a shard-2 order without exchange_index, to settle rule 7's premise. Pass: 201 accepted, and the exchange cancels the order at its expiry.
- Shrink an order, or change only its expiry, and read GET /portfolio/orders/queue_positions before and after. Pass: same position.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k:
$0/day for the same bots at $5,000: at about 4x size the ladder still never rests across a pause.

For a future 200-contract weather bid bot at 97-98c resting over Thursday night: it avoids at most one bad sweep a week, worst case 200 x $0.98 = $196 (the hunter's arithmetic). For context, all weather makers together lost $204 per Thursday on average in the first second after the reopen (3 Thursdays). Our share of that was not measured.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
- Thursday pause, 15-min bots: the exposure is zero because no such market exists. That is a fact about the listings, not a statistical null.
- Unscheduled crypto-shard pauses of 60 s or more mid-market: 0 seen in about 51 days. The 95% upper bound is about 3 per 51 days, roughly 1 every 17 days. The scan cannot see pauses under 60 s, or any inside the 60 stretches where the collector was dead.
- Reopen maker loss by family: weather (27 events) and crypto (6 events) are too few to tell -11c apart from 0 with confidence. Tennis (131 events) is the only family with a clear loss in the first second.

refs.strongest_objection:
It protects $0 today, and parts of the idea are wrong.

Today:
- Nothing rests. I read the account's own resting orders at 11:55Z on 10-15: 0 in the main account, 0 in subaccount 1, 0 in subaccount 2.
- The ladder never holds an order longer than 29.7 s, and never on a market that spans the Thursday pause.

Three claims in the idea are wrong:
1. 'During a pause cancels are impossible' is true only for the rare exchange pause. In the weekly Thursday trading pause, Kalshi's docs say cancels are allowed.
2. The note that repeated post-only crossing triggers a rate limit (changelog 08-22) is about RFQ quoters, not orders. Kalshi's rate-limit page says a 429 has no penalty or cooldown.
3. Rule 7's evidence was a redundant second cancel, not an off-shard miss. Every live DELETE path already sends exchange_index=2.

The tester also said hourly crypto spans the pause. It does not; only the 5 pm ET daily crypto listings do. The decrease rule and rule 7's premise (that a DELETE without exchange_index silently fails) are both untested live.

Why this is not a refutation:
- Rules (1) cancel_order_on_pause and (2) expiration_time are fields in the V2 create-order schema, cost nothing to add, and are the parts that matter.
- They matter for future maker bots on weather, index and daily-crypto markets, which do rest across the pause.

Two small rule-7 gaps worth fixing:
- ordercli.cancel retries without exchange_index (line 305). That retry routes to shard 0, so it can never cancel a shard-2 order.
- goldquote.py cancels with o.get('exchange_index') or 0.

Neither file is on a live order path today.

refs.strongest_objection:
I could not refute it. The tester's numbers come out the same from my own queries. My strongest objection is to the label, not the arithmetic: for every bot running today this rule changes nothing ($0/day, measured). It only has value for future maker bots that leave orders resting across Thursday 03:00-05:00 ET.

My queries turned up two new facts:

(1) "No 15-min market spans the pause" is how Kalshi lists markets now, not a fixed rule.
- 2026-02-19 (winter, pause 08:00-10:00 UTC): Kalshi listed every KXBTC15M quarter-hour market through the pause. The 03:15-05:00 ET markets exist on /historical/markets, each with volume 0.00.
- 03-05 and 03-12: the gap was wider. The 02:45 and 03:00 ET markets were missing too.
- 09-17, 09-24 and 10-15: the gap is exactly 03:15-05:00 ET.
- It is still harmless for 15-min bots, because the pause starts and ends on a quarter hour in ET under both listing patterns (02-19 closes at 08:00 UTC = 03:00 EST). So no 15-min order can rest across the start or end of a pause.
- After the 11-01 clock change the pause moves to 08:00-10:00 UTC, and market names follow ET.
- So the builder self-test should require the flag itself, not rely on the gap in the listings.

(2) The 25 ladder cancels that look like "accepted after close" are a logging artefact. The exchange's own timestamp on each one is 3-120 ms before close. So the rule that every order action is refused after close holds.

Most the missing flag can cost the ladder today is about $0.11/day: unscheduled pauses at most 3 per 51 days (95% upper bound; none seen) x the ladder resting at most 30 s of every 900 s x $58.80 peak exposure. The point estimate is $0.

There was no rate-limit refusal (HTTP 429) on any forecaster or pinrun order send. So the ladder's 13,277 cancels sent after close have cost nothing measurable either.

idea.name: Hourly BTC ladder size-up (0.12 -> 0.5-1.0 x SIZE) with rung re-pick at 120 s and REST re-read on stale books, gated by a base-rate calibration check
markets: KXBTCD (live today at floor(SIZE x 0.12) = 11 contracts)

crypto-hourly-daily-race: Identify-better: calibrate the live bot's hourly-ladder 'fair' against the 30-day base-rate crossing table
idea.mechanism: Same pin as live (last 45 s, buy the safe side of the rung nearest the projection at <= 98c) with three changes: (1) take_n from floor(SIZE x 0.12) toward 0.5-1.0 x SIZE, capped by the offered size; (2) re-pick the 3 watched rungs at tau 120 s with one GET instead of once at tau 900 s; (3) re-read a > 2-s-stale ladder book by REST instead of refusing. Gate first: calibrate the bot's hourly fair against the index-tape base-rate crossing table by vol state; if active-vol bins are over-confident, size up only with an active-state cushion floor.
idea.why_mispriced: The 97-98c near-rung offers come from quoters who do not use the partial 60-s average; the projection error at 30 s is 0.2 bp median. Our 10 live signals 10-10..10-13 saw 450, 907, 859 and 859 contracts at 97-98c in 4 of 10 cases while we took 11.
idea.must_be_true: Fills at ~91 stay near 100% and the loss rate stays well under the 2/100 break-even at 98c. Calibration risk: the bot logged fair 0.9996 for a 2.7 bp cushion at 45 s, while the index tape puts the two-sided crossing rate for > 2 bp at 45 s at 3.0% calm / 16.4% active (> 3 bp 1.2% / 7.5%) -- roughly 0.6-0.8% one-sided at 2.7 bp in calm states (about +1.1c a contract at 98c) and ~3-4% in active states (negative EV). So the bot's 5-min sigma gate must keep it out of active states. The live 46/46 is at 1-11 contracts, mostly calm hours; supply at 91 appeared on only 4 of 10 signals.

test.method:
Read-only, no replay. Sources in rank order: raw index feed, then the trade tape, then our own fills.
(m1) Calibration of the bot's own fair against the raw BRTI tape. The fair was rebuilt exactly as pinrun.fair computes it: live sigma ruler (300 s), partial 60-s average, Phi. It was computed at tau 45, 40 ... 3 on every quarter-hour close from 08-25 to 10-15 (4,536 closes, 1,112 of them hourly), on the KXBTCD $100 rung grid. On each side the money rung is the nearest rung with fair >= 0.995. Outcome = mean of the 60 prints [C-60, C-1]. Fit = first 60% of closes (to 09-25 10:30Z); holdout = last 40%. Vol state = bot sigma above or below the FIT median (0.436 bp per 1-s step).
(m2) Kalshi ledger, per-market money, for KXBTCD and KXBTC15M.
(m3/m6) The live bot's 50 KXBTCD signal closes, 09-25..10-15 (20.8 days): the book logged at the first signal, contracts asked and filled, and the outcome. Money was computed for N = 11 / 49 / 98 / 420 with the live early-leg rules (a third of the size, <= 97c, >= 90c when tau > 30) and the live hit rate.
(m4/m7) Public KXBTCD trades on the 4 rungs around the settle, for 119 more hourly closes (10-07..10-12, 619 public GETs) plus the hunter's 24. Each trade was re-scored with the bot's fair at the trade second. Population: taker buys of the side the bot calls >= 99.5% safe, at <= 98c, tau 3-45.
(m5) Rung selection and stale-book refusals, from the live ladder and refused records.
Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-05/ (m1_calib.py, m1b_table.py, m2_ledger.py, m3_live.py, m4_rungsupply.py, m5_rungs.py, m6_money.py, m6b_early.py, m7_tapefair.py), and the full answer is in RESULT.json there.
test.n_markets:
Live: 50 KXBTCD signal closes, and 42 ledger markets since 09-25 (6 of them at 11 contracts).
Tape: 143 hourly closes, with 20 bot-qualifying rung-markets on 19 closes.
Index: 4,536 closes (1,112 hourly), giving 90,712 close x tau x side rows.
test.n_independent_clusters: Counted as closes: 50 live signal closes over 20.8 days, 143 tape closes over 6 days, 4,536 index closes over 51 days. BTC only, so one index.
test.result:
1) The calibration bar as written FAILS. The bar was: no bin with n >= 30 where the realised rate is more than 2x the promised rate.
- fair 0.995-0.999, holdout, tau 16-30, calm: 2.78% realised vs 0.25% promised (108 rows / 104 closes), 11x.
- Same bin, tau 31-45, calm: 1.85% vs 0.26% (216 / 187), 7x.
- All of fair 0.995-0.999: fit 0.45% (6 / 1,322 rows), holdout 1.27% (10 / 787).
- fair >= 0.9999: 0.012-0.017% realised vs about 0.0001% promised.
These rates are still under break-even: 3.0% at the 96.5c average fill.

2) The fear that busy (high-volatility) hours are dangerous is REFUTED for the trades the bot's gate lets through.
- tau 31-45, fit: active 8 / 8,158 (0.10%), calm 4 / 8,164 (0.05%).
- tau 31-45, holdout: active 0 / 3,832, calm 9 / 7,058 (0.13%).
The idea's 3-4% at a 2.7 bp cushion came from the base rate over all closes, not the closes the bot would trade. The bot's sigma already widens the cushion in busy hours. An active-state cushion floor is not needed; calm hours were the worse group in the holdout.

3) Our own fills:
- KXBTCD: 50 of 50 signal closes won. Ledger since 09-25: 42 markets, 0 lost, +$2.79.
- Same bot on the same index at about 90 contracts, KXBTC15M since 09-25: 137 markets, 5 lost money, -$287.25 total. That is 3.6 per 100 markets, above break-even.

4) Supply:
- At the first signal, >= 98 contracts were offered at <= 98c on 45 of 50 closes (median 1,362).
- In the tape, other takers bought 58,840 bot-qualifying contracts at 90-98c on 18 of 143 closes (median 1,640 per close), with 0 markets lost.

idea.mechanism: 1) Page /incentive_programs?status=active every 30 min (the API ignores series filters) for KXTTSTARMATCH programs. 2) In each window, ONLY while a start/score feed shows no point played, rest 300 YES at 1c and 300 NO at 1c ($6 of collateral per market): a lone poster is its own reference (first level with cumulative size >= Target/5 = 60), so it scores 100% of counted seconds while alone. 3) Cancel at the first point, or when anyone else makes the book two-sided at target. idea.mechanism: 1-3 h before the 21:00Z close, compute every bracket's fair from the live index with an hour-of-day realised-vol curve built from our own 1/s BRTI/ETH tape. (a) Sell YES by hitting bids of 4-9c (asks 6-12c) on brackets >= 2 sd away (taker); (b) buy the 30c+ favourite bracket at the ask when fair > ask + 3c. Hold to settlement. Both legs are one claim: the ladder prices more movement into the last hours than follows (the pin's vol collapse at a 1-3 h horizon).
idea.why_mispriced: Late far-bracket bids come from gamblers chasing a move or stale maker bids; late favourite sellers under-estimate how little can happen in the last hour. On 10-13 the Kalshi-fit sd was 1.11 (BTC) / 1.13 (ETH) x Deribit's at 8.9 h out (the US session -- possibly just seasonality).
idea.must_be_true: Shoulder hit rate must stay under the ~5.3% break-even: 2 of 143 (1.4%) has a 95% upper bound ~4.3% (only +0.7c at the bound). The bids must be there with depth when we arrive (candle-close bids; depth unknown). The favourite cell must survive drift removal (BTC +32% over the Aug 14-Oct 12 sample; the S&P version is -9.3c). The same shoulder sale 6-20 h out LOSES (-0.6 to -4.6c; the bidder knows more), so any edge lives only in the final hours. The Kalshi-vs-Deribit premium must exceed time-of-day seasonality (unmeasured); the lognormal fit is drift-confounded, so only model-free buckets and the index-based fair are trusted.

idea.test_plan: (1) Free, index-first: build the hour-of-day realised-vol curve from our BRTI/ETH 1/s tape (Sep 1..Oct 13) and price every bracket at 3/2/1 h on the 60 events already pulled; score (a) and (b) with fair-based selection, fit Aug 14-Sep 20, hold out Sep 21-Oct 12, plus a drift-neutral split (up days vs down days). Bars: holdout shoulders hit <= 3 per 100 brackets with net >= +2.5c after fee; favourite net >= +3c over >= 30 events with both up- and down-day halves positive. (2) If it passes, record the KXBTC daily book every 60 s in the last 3 h for 2 weeks (~360 public calls/day) for bid depth at 4-9c; bar >= 300 contracts/day; then paper at detection.

test.method: Index-first. (1) Extracted per-minute BRTI/ETHUSD_RTI from our cfbenchmarks_value tape (Aug 25-Oct 15, 1172 hour files, 25 truncated). Checked that the 5 PM settlement = mean of the 60 prints in [close-60s, close): it matched on 46/46 events, exact to the cent. Coinbase 1-min candles fill tape gaps (median |diff| vs BRTI 0.005%). (2) Re-pulled all 60+60 KXBTC/KXETH 5 PM events Aug 16-Oct 14 (batch hourly candles, quote at T-4/3/2/1h, staleness kept). Via /historical/*, pulled 137 older KXBTC events Apr 1-Aug 13 (spot bracket +-1 at each horizon). (3) Fair value: seasonal 5-min vol (weekday/weekend x UTC hour), trailing-72h level, and a scale k plus empirical shape fit ONLY on 21:00Z closes before the scored events (Coinbase 5-min: Aug 2025-Mar 2026 for the older set, Aug 2025-Aug 15 2026 for the recent set). Self-test passes: a fair world shows no edge, and planted rich shoulders are found. (4) Scored the idea's rules, margin variants, mirror controls and first-entry-only versions, clustered by event. The recent set is split train (first 36) / holdout (last 24); the older 137 events are a separate out-of-sample period. (5) Pulled the public trade tape after each entry (~430 GETs) to get real taker prices and sizes. (6) Index-only, month by month: how often the 21Z settle stays in the $250 bracket that held the spot, vs the model. Source ranking: settlement feed (tape) > trade tape > candles. We have no own fills. test.result:
THE IDEA AS WRITTEN:
(a) Shoulder sale is DEAD on supply and on its premise. Bids of 4-9c at >=2 sd from the index appeared on only 3 BTC + 2 ETH brackets in 60 events each (all horizons), and others sold a median 6 contracts at that price. Where 4-9c bids do exist (1-1.5 sd out), the index fair equals the bid (BTC T-3h: bid 4.0c vs fair 4.2c; T-1h: 4.6c vs 5.4c), so there is no edge after fee. The hunter's +3-4c came from an unusually calm stretch: the recent 60 BTC closes had RMS z 0.73-0.82, the bottom decile of 60-close windows in the prior year. At 2 sd and T-3h, 2 of 20 brackets paid.
(b) Fair-model favourite is NOT supported out of sample. On the older 137 events the idea rule (ask>=30c, fair>=ask+fee+3c), first entry, gave 45 brackets / 39 events at +3.3c/contract, per-event +3.8c se 7.0c (April -23.6c, June -6.5c). Recent 60 events: +18.5c (21 events, se 9.9c). ETH: +3.8c (18 events), holdout +1.4c. Brier(mid)-Brier(fair) for BTC is +0.30 se 0.88 (x100): our fair does not beat the market mid.
WHAT SURVIVED (model-free; the hunter's favourite cell made exact): buy YES at the ask on the bracket that holds the index at T-3h/T-2h/T-1h (bid>0, ask 20-99c, each bracket once).
- BTC older Apr 1-Aug 13 (separate holdout, 136 events, 234 brackets): 43% paid vs a 34.7c ask, +6.6c/contract after fee, per-event +11.3c se 4.0c (z 2.8).
- BTC recent Aug 16-Oct 14 (60 events, 100 brackets): 45% paid vs 34.5c, +9.0c/contract, per-event +15.1c se 5.9c (z 2.6).
- By horizon, single entry (older/recent): T-3h +7.2/+5.1c, T-2h +10.2/+15.8c, T-1h +3.1/+10.8c per contract.
- ETH recent 60 events: 79% paid vs 66.0c, +11.4c/contract, per-event +13.5c se 4.0c.
WHY: index-only, from Aug 2025 to Mar 2026 the 21Z settle landed in the spot's $250 bracket 1.00x as often as the model says; since April 2026 it is 1.29x (591 horizon-observations; every month Apr-Sep between 1.20 and 1.46; October so far 1.07). The market still prices the centre as if the old regime held (ask about equal to the old-model fair). So this is a regime the ladder has not adapted to (1-3 h moves more peaked since April), not a model edge.

- Settlement = 60-print BRTI mean, exact on 46/46 events.
- Coinbase vs BRTI: median diff 0.005%, p95 0.017%; 5-min return rms ratio 1.014.
- /historical candles are identical to live batch candles (Aug 15 event checked).
- Every spot-bracket entry had a candle ending exactly at entry time (staleness 0), so there is no stale-ask look-ahead.
- Real prices: other takers' YES-buy VWAP in the 10 min after entry, minus our candle ask, had a median of +0.0c (recent, n 89) and +0.2c (older, n 189). P&L at that VWAP: +11.2c / +6.9c per contract.

- Drift: BTC's +32% over 2 months is about $33 over 2 h, small against a $250 bracket. Trailing-7d up and down splits are both positive.

refs.strongest_objection: Execution is not what limits this; whether the edge lasts is. (1) BTC, the leg with real trade flow, shows no edge on the tester's own holdout split. The last 24 events made +0.6c per contract (per-event se 9.7c) and October made -0.8c (14 events), against +18.7c on the first 36. The tester's index-only monitor fell to 1.07 in October. The decline is not significant against the tester's older Apr-Aug +6.6c (z about 1), so it is a warning, not a kill. (2) The edge is a bet against jumps. Into the 5 PM close, 1-3 h returns are very fat-tailed (kurtosis 4.5-8 for BTC, 18-34 for ETH; the median absolute move is 0.4-0.6x what a normal curve with the same spread implies). The ladder seems to price a normal-shaped spread, so the centre bracket is cheap and its neighbours are dear (neighbour controls lose -1.4 to -12c per contract). Profit therefore depends on how many jump days arrive, which 60-200 events cannot pin down. A jump day also creates up to 3 entries per coin that all miss: the worst observed combined day was -$137 at 98 lots, and all six entries missing would be about -$345 (30% of the bank). (3) The candle ask is sometimes a 1-5 lot order sitting ahead of the maker's deep quote (ETH centre now: 1 lot at 29c, then 30,000 at 33c), so the true 98-lot price is the candle ask plus 0-4c. Large BTC prints after entry paid the candle ask (median +0.0c over 53 entries); ETH has only 6 such entries. Supply is NOT the problem. The tester capped fills by what other takers bought, but the live book holds 20,000-30,000 maker lots at or near the best ask. Depth on the daily ladder at T-3/2/1h itself is not measured.

idea.name: Fixed-close daily-high/low weather 97-98c resting bid (maker) on the near-decided bracket side, 2+ F from the boundary, last 24 h
idea.mechanism: In the last 24 h before a daily-high/low event closes (close time fixed at listing -- checked), rest a 97-98c bid on any bracket side already trading 95c+ when the forecast/observation keeps it 2+ F from the boundary; lottery buyers of the far bracket at 2-3c fill it; hold to settlement. No maker fee on these series (quadratic x1). Cap 200 contracts per bracket.
idea.why_mispriced: Lottery buyers pay 1-3c for ~1-in-100 tails. SJ32 measured the far-bracket loss rate at 8 of 765 (1.05 per 100, upper 1.9) -- selling at 2-3c (= bidding 97-98c) clears that by ~1-2c without paying the taker fee that killed SJ32 at +0.18c.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Fills at 97-98c happen behind competitors' 99c NO bids (SJ32: they exist) -- a 98c bid fills only after the 99c level is eaten, and at 99c the edge is ~0 (break-even 1 per 100 vs 1.05 measured). (2) The 1 F rounding-boundary flips (D01) and whole-Celsius false locks on lows (D05) stay excluded by the 2 F rule. (3) The fills are lottery flow, not informed NO sellers reacting to a forecast update (7 of SJ32's 8 losses sat next to a 10c+ sibling). (4) Capital: with N2-02's finding (~$650 of the main bank is idle at every close) this no longer has to compete with the pin bot.
idea.evidence_so_far: Maker side of every fill on FIXED-close weather series (lasthour2.py, no hindsight): 97-99c 6-24 h before close +1.31c per contract (18 city-day events, 273k contracts, 100% won), 1-6 h +1.01c (18 ev, 66k), 15-60 min +1.02c (13 ev); 95-97c 6-24 h -1.92c (93.7% won -- not safe). MERGER NOTE: 18 events at 100% won cannot see a 1-in-100 tail; the tail rate rests on SJ32's 765 brackets. Dropped legs: KXTRUMPAPPROVE 97-99c 1-6 h -25.2c (4 events, 88k contracts, 72.9% won); KXRAIN and mentions close early when decided, so their last-hours cells are hindsight windows (KXRAIN 6-24 h 90-95c: 56% won).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: ~1c per contract filled. Realistic $2-8/day at $1,155 (~$1,000 locked buys ~1,000 contracts a cycle = ~$10 if fully filled); $10-25/day at $5,000. Worst plausible day: one bracket flip at 98c on 200 contracts = -$196 against ~$2 earned per bracket.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~25 city-day events (daily highs/lows), several brackets each
idea.test_plan: Read-only 3 weeks: once a minute in the last 24 h, poll the books of the 6 series' brackets at 95c+ (~300 calls/week), log depth ahead of a 97c/98c bid and every trade through it; join the NWS climate report for outcomes and the boundary distance. Pre-registered bar: >= 500 contracts/day reachable at 97-98c (not 99c), 0 flips in 60 events at >= 2 F from the boundary, net >= +0.8c after the fills' own outcomes.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SJ32 (taker, dead at +0.18c) and SJ02/SI25 (rain) are the same flow from the taker side or another series; the maker seat on FIXED-close highs/lows with the hindsight-window legs removed is the new part. Distinct from carried maker-portfolio 'Resting favourite BID at 95-99c in-play' (sports) and 'Slow-market longshot ask + favourite bid' (non-weather reward series).
idea.worst_case: One flip at 98c on 200 contracts = -$196.
idea.prior_reason: The tail rate is measured on 765 brackets and the maker seat removes the fee that killed SJ32, but the edge is ~1c, the 99c competitors sit in front, and the downside is 98:1; small dollars at this bank.
