test.method:
Sources, best first: the public trade tape (/markets/trades), settlement results, hourly candles (public batch /markets/candlesticks) and IEM ASOS weather observations. No replay was used.
(1) Pulled hourly candles for all 15,462 settled daily HIGH/LOW temperature markets: 48 series, closes 2026-08-20..10-13, 55 dates, about 2,600 city-days. From these, measured how often a side quoted at 95-99c goes on to lose, sampled every hour from 1 to 24 h before close, split by best-bid band and by what the observations said at the time.
(2) Measured the population of resting-bid fills from a stratified trade tape:
- S1 is all 151 markets where the losing side's hourly best-bid high reached 97c or more in the last 24 h. This stratum holds every losing 97c+ maker fill. Weight 1.
- S2 is a random sample of the remaining markets whose winning side reached 97c: 288 of 1,921 six-series markets and 230 of 12,769 others. Weight N/n.
- Maker side is the opposite of taker_outcome_side. Maker price is that side's print price. P&L is +(100-p) if the side won and -p if it lost. Maker fee is 0: all 49 temperature series are 'quadratic x1'.
- Confidence intervals come from a 1,000-draw bootstrap that resamples city-days, so they carry both the clustering of losses and the S2 sampling noise.
- Holdout: fit = closes before 2026-09-17, test = after. No threshold was fitted; the idea pre-specified the rule (97-98c, last 24 h).
(3) Queue proxy: P&L split by the size of the taker order (a new bid at the back of the queue is reached only by big orders).
(4) One live book snapshot of the six named series, 2026-10-15 07:47 ET.
Total public calls: 1,135. Everything is in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N2-05/ (pop.out, final_an.out, fills_an.out, size_an.py, sweep_an.py, leakcheck.py, books.jsonl, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 15,462 settled markets with candles (quote population). 669 markets with the full last-24 h trade tape: 151 flip markets plus 518 sampled. 368 city-days had 97-98c maker fills.
test.n_independent_clusters: 368 city-days in the fill sample. There were 107 losing market-sides on 35 of the 55 dates. Dates are the coarsest independent unit, because one weather front hits several cities at once.

Six named series: +0.96 [-0.38, +1.86], 1.49 lost per 100 (fit +0.45, test +1.34). By series:

The other 42 series: +1.47 [+0.68, +1.99], positive in both halves.

Back-of-queue proxy: fills from taker orders of 500+ contracts make +0.64c [-1.19, +1.70] and lose 1.77 per 100. Orders under 50 contracts make +1.34c [+0.76, +1.73].

The idea's 2F rule from the boundary does nothing:
- At 97-98c almost no side is locked by observation; locked sides already trade at 99c.
- Open sides 2F or more from the running max make +1.14c, against +1.23c for sides within 1F.

SJ32 adjacency gate:
- Far-bracket NO fills with no adjacent bracket at 10c+ make +1.54c (se 0.41, positive in both halves), against +1.07c when one is adjacent.
- Near-certain YES fills next to a 10c+ bracket make -2.49c (se 3.4). This cut was found after looking.

Quote population (every resting quote on the hourly grid, not just fills): a side bid at 97c loses 1.11 per 100 market-sides (58 of 5,225); at 98c, 0.62 per 100 (39 of 6,244). Fills lose about 1.5 times that per contract. That is the expected sign of being sold to by better-informed traders, but on the tape it does not erase the edge.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) The stratification holds:
- 0 losing 97c+ maker contracts in all 518 S2 markets (4.4M winning contracts).
- 0 prints at 97c+ in 10 randomly pulled markets out of the 614 excluded ones.
(2) Close times are fixed: every event closes at 01:00 local daylight time (00:00 in Phoenix), so there is no window that peeks at the outcome.
(3) IEM join: the observed running high/low at close is within 2F of the CLI settlement value on 98.2% of 15,210 markets.
(4) Units: prices are *_dollars x100. count_fp sums reproduce market volume (pilot B70.5: 82,627 of 86,725 total contracts in the last 24 h).
(5) Self-tests pass: side_status brackets, the fills_an planted world, and the final_an planted 0.00c.
(6) The central number moves with the sample: the all-series estimate went +1.41 -> +1.29 -> +1.12 as S2 grew from 140 to 320 to 518 markets.
(7) The idea's worry that a 98c bid fills only after the 99c queue is eaten is mostly moot. 95% of losing and 94% of winning 97-98c contracts printed with no 99c print in the prior 2 s; the 99c bids had already gone.
(8) This is the tape's maker population, not ours. It includes makers who cancel on news. A slow or back-of-queue bot gets more of the big orders, which carry more of the losses (proxy +0.64c, interval reaching below zero).
test.supply_we_would_get: The tape prints 85,100 contracts/day at 97-98c maker prices across the 48 series (six named 58,500/day; LAX alone about 37,000). One book snapshot (2026-10-15 07:47 ET) of the 12 near-decided sides with a 99c best bid showed 4-5,402 contracts already resting at 98c and 0-1,052 at 97c. Our share of this flow was not measured. Capital limits us before the queue does: about 650 contracts/day at today's ~$650 of idle main-bank cash (N2-02's figure, not measured here), and about 4,000/day at $5,000 (roughly 5% of the printed flow).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $4/day, range -$8 to +$7. 650 contracts/day at +0.64c (back-of-queue proxy) to +1.12c (tape average) gives $4-7 if fully filled every day. The lower 95% bounds (-1.19c and +0.01c) put it at -$8 to $0.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $30/day, range roughly $0-45: about 4,000 contracts/day at +0.64-1.12c. The lower bound is about zero.

test.worst_case: Losses cluster by date: 35 of 55 dates had a losing 97-98c side somewhere. The worst date had 4 losing sides, 2 of them in the six named series. At the 200-contract cap per bracket that is -$390 (2 flips) to -$780 (4 flips) in one day. At today's bank (about 650 contracts at most) a 2-flip day costs -$390, roughly 3 months of the central profit.
test.next_test:
(a) Holdout re-run. Same scripts on markets settling 2026-10-14..11-04: about 1,100 public calls, read around 2026-11-05. Bar: all-series 97-98c maker P&L at least +0.6c with the lower 95% bound above 0, and the 500+ order cut at least +0.3c.
(b) Read-only queue recorder for 21 days. It records WebSocket orderbook_delta and trade for the 48 temperature series; this is a new read-only process, so it needs the operator's OK. It simulates a 200-lot joining at 98c (and separately at 97c) when each side first reaches 95c+:
- queue position = the resting depth at join;
- a fill counts only after the queue ahead is used up by prints at our price (cancellations ahead are ignored, which is conservative);
- held to settlement.
Pass bar: at least 500 simulated contracts/day, net at least +0.5c per contract after the fills' own outcomes, worst simulated day no worse than -$400, and at least 1 losing fill actually reached.
(c) Only after that, a micro-live test: 10-lot bids at 98c on about 20 sides/day for 2 weeks on a subaccount. This is a new strategy family, so it needs the operator's sign-off.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's +1.12c is the TAPE maker population, and a bot with the idea's own 200-contract cap per bracket cannot earn it. On winning sides the tape's 98c maker volume is concentrated: the top 10 of 260 sampled winner sides hold 70% of it, and the median side has 0. A capped bid gets at most 200 on those few sides. On losing sides it gets filled almost fully (196 of 200), because informed sellers sweep through 98c in the afternoon while the high is being set.

My simulation is queue-respecting and runs on my own tapes (780 public calls):
- The bid joins when it can rest at 98c (ask at 99c or more).
- It fills only from real prints: at 98c after the queue ahead is used up. A print below 98c means the level emptied, so that print reaches us.
- Positions are held to settlement; maker fee is 0.

Results:
- Winners fill 70 of 200 on average; losers fill 196.
- Joined sides lose 0.92 times per 100. Break-even needs winners to fill 46% as much as losers; they fill 36%.
- Net per contract at 98c: -0.54c [-1.67, +0.21] at the front of the queue (the most optimistic case), -0.90c [-2.26, +0.03] behind 300.
- Negative in both date halves (-1.27c, -0.66c).
- At 97c: -0.21c with no queue, -0.57c behind 300.

Second error: Kalshi reserves cash for RESTING buy orders, not just for fills (verified on this account 2026-09-06, HANDOFF_ARCHIVE_2026-09.md line 6316). So $650 of idle cash holds only about 3 resting 200-lots, about 4.7 joined sides a day, not 650 fills a day.

The same tapes and weights give +1.60c for the tape population at 98c, so my sample reproduces the tester's sign. The gap comes from the cap and from who fills us.

Limits:
- Cancellations ahead of us are ignored, but the no-queue case (everyone ahead cancelled) is still negative.
- How our presence would change other traders is not modelled.
- A bot that cancels on weather news is a different strategy (it needs a nowcast faster than the sweepers) and was not tested.

Other execution facts:
- Settlement source is The Weather Company, not the NWS report.
- Settlement comes a median 6.2 h after close (one market took 153 h).
- Book snapshot (08:13 ET): where 98c is the best bid, 1-171 contracts rest there; where 99c is best, 98c holds 2-7,427 contracts.
- No weather incentive program in the first 3,200 programs listed.
- Joining only in the last 6 h does not help: -0.06c [-2.08, +1.04].
- The optimistic model, which credits a full 200 fill from any print below 98c, is an upper bound only: +0.07c at 98c, +0.73c at 97c.
refs.independent_number:
Queue-respecting counterfactual: a 200-lot resting bid at 98c in the last 24 h, held to settlement.
- Sample: all 48 temperature series, 32 dates (closes 09-13..10-14); all 98 losing sides whose bid reached 97c or more, plus 260 random winning sides, post-stratified.
- Per contract: -0.54c [-1.67, +0.21] at queue 0; -0.90c [-2.26, +0.03] behind 300.
- Per $650 of cash reserved: -$1.79/day [-5.08, +0.76] at queue 0; -$2.63/day [-6.01, +0.09] behind 300.
- Fill ratio, winners to losers: 70/200 vs 196/200, i.e. 0.36 against a break-even of 0.46.
- Six named series: -0.33c [-2.32, +0.80].
- The same sample's tape maker average is +1.60c.

refs.strongest_objection:
The +1.12c figure has two problems. It comes from a 55-date window that starts one day after the biggest loss in the data. And it measures the tape's volume-weighted maker population, not what a 200-lot bid of ours would get.

Losses are very concentrated. One market, KXHIGHLAX-26AUG18-B81.5, holds 21,141 losing contracts at 97-98c, which is 23% of all losing contracts across 60 dates. The top 10 losing markets hold 69%. Widening the window by 3 days earlier and 2 days later cuts the tape number from +1.12c to about +0.65c a contract (using the tester's own supply of 85,100/day). With my own supply estimate it is +0.1 to +0.2c. The date-clustered interval spans zero.

Per market-side, flips fill a resting 98c bid almost every time (96-100%). Winners fill it only 37-50% of the time on trade evidence. So our seat would lose 2.3-2.9 contracts per 100 filled, against a break-even of 2 per 100. That is -0.1 to -0.9c a contract. It turns positive (+1.0c) only under an upper-bound fill model that counts every winner whose bid dipped below 98c as fully filled, which also counts dips caused by cancellations.

Also not covered by the tester: on CLI day 2026-08-14, settlement moved from the NWS climate report to The Weather Company in all 48 series. The whole usable sample is the first two months of the new source, and its first days carried big losses (DEN on 08-16, LAX on 08-18). 97c bids are worse than 98c in every model.

My own census of losing maker contracts bought at 97-98c in the last 24 h, built from my own pulls:
- Hourly candles for all 16,668 settled temperature markets closing 2026-08-17 to 10-15.
- My own bid-based flip list of 175 markets. It contains all 151 of the tester's.
- The trade tape for all 175.

Result:

- All 60 dates: 91,193 = 1,520/day. The 5 dates outside the tester's window add 29,322 (+47%).

Our-seat counterfactual (200-lot bid at 98c, joins an existing 98c bid queue, never cancelled, held to settlement, 60 dates):

| Fill model | c/contract | 95% CI (by date) |
|---|---|---|
| Front of queue, fills shown by trades | -0.29 | -1.8 to +0.4 |
| 500+ contracts ahead in the queue | -0.75 | -2.8 to +0.2 |
| Upper bound (every bid dip counts as a fill) | +1.01 | +0.70 to +1.26 |

Losers fill 96-100% of the time; winners fill 37-50%.

idea.name: CPI month-vs-year consistency pair (KXCPI x KXCPIYOY, KXCPICORE x KXCPICOREYOY): buy the mispriced two-leg package, best in the 1-7 days after the previous month's print, sell it back at the bids before the print unless it is riskless (U23 PASSED; SI12/SJ57 revived)
markets: KXCPI x KXCPIYOY (headline, same release month)

next windows: the 26NOV ladders from the Nov 10 8:30 AM ET print (the Oct-2026 index, which fixes NSA_{m-1}) to the Dec 10 close; the 26DEC ladders from the Dec 10 print to the Jan 13 close; there is NO 26OCT pair (the Oct-2025 index was never published)
idea.mechanism: Once month m-1 has printed, YoY_m = NSA_{m-1} x r_m x (1 + x/100) / NSA_{m-12} - 1, with x the unrounded seasonally adjusted MoM and r_m the month's seasonal ratio, so 'YoY > T' is exactly 'x >= c_Y(T)' and 'MoM > t' is 'x >= t + 0.05': two ladders pricing almost the same event. For a (T, t) with the two cut-offs within 0.06 pp, one package (YoY YES + MoM NO, or the mirror) pays $1 everywhere except $0 inside the thin band between the cut-offs (P-); the opposite package pays $1 everywhere and $2 in the band (P+, riskless). Steps: (1) re-code the BLS r rebuild (seasonal-factor workbook + relative importances + component indexes; EIA weekly gasoline for motor fuel) and pre-register r_m in results/ before each print; (2) hourly, value every package as P(YoY leg wins) + P(MoM leg wins) - asks - taker fees, with P from the MoM ladder's mids (spread <= 10c, monotone), band probability floored at 4 per pp of MoM and doubled for P-, quotes no older than 2 h, worst case over r +- 0.0001; (3) buy the day's best package (one per release-family per day) when that worst case is > +2c and the package does not change type inside the r band unless it is P+ at both ends; the largest gaps come in the first 1-7 days after the previous month's print, when the YoY ladder has not re-anchored on the new NSA level; (4) sell both legs back at the bids once the ladders converge (1-2 weeks) or 24 h before close at the latest; hold through the print only packages that are P+ at both ends of the r band. Run on a subaccount, never the main pool.
idea.why_mispriced: The YoY and MoM ladders are traded by different crowds and nobody runs the seasonal arithmetic. The YoY ladder's implied r sits 0.0002-0.0004 off the realised r for weeks (8-16c of probability on a central rung) and only converges in the last ~3 days (within 0.00002-0.00011 on all six release-families, cpi_rimpl.out). Right after the previous print the gap is biggest: implied-r error +0.00042 in the first 6 h, +0.00026 at 6-24 h, +0.0002 at 1-7 days, ~0 after 2 weeks (Jul head); Aug head +0.00103 / +0.0005 / +0.00038 / +0.00015 / +0.00008; Sep head -0.00038 / -0.00036 / -0.00034 / -0.00014 (cpi_afterprint.out) -- YoY traders do not re-anchor on the new index level for days. The sign follows the print's surprise, not a bias, so only the arithmetic says which way to lean. The 10-02 refutation (SJ57) inferred r = 0.99922 from the Cleveland Fed nowcast's two-decimal rounding; the realised Sep r was 0.999370 vs the 09-25 model's pre-registered 0.99936 (U23 bar +-0.00007: PASSED). Losers: whoever lifts the expensive side of either ladder.
idea.must_be_true: (a) The BLS r rebuild is re-coded (the 09-25 code is not in the repo) and keeps landing within ~0.0001; one out-of-sample pass so far (Sep +0.00001). The naive 'same month last year' r is NOT good enough: over 67 months its error is median 0.00021, p90 0.00058 headline (core median 0.00014, p90 0.00038), and for Nov 2026 it does not exist (Oct 2025 missing) -- the 2019-2024 Nov history spans 0.99638-0.99712, 0.0007 wide. (b) Size at the touch: candles carry no size; the 09-25/10-02 snapshots showed 263-1,158 pairs; the 26NOV books on 10-15 show 5-21,421 at the central asks (KXCPIYOY-26NOV T3.8 ask 21,421 at 51c, KXCPI-26NOV T0.2 ask 10,185 at 47c) but 1-30 lots on many neighbouring rungs and 1-6 lots on most MoM bids (the exit side). (c) Exit bids exist 1-2 weeks after entry (the exit is a taker sale; fees are in the measurement). (d) The rounding rule holds (232 of 232 settled markets matched round(3-decimal index change, 1), 09-25 sweep). (e) Money sits in a subaccount: 1-4 weeks of lock in the main account would shrink the pin bot's bet size (SI12's objection); moving money between Kalshi subaccounts is not a deposit but is the operator's call.
idea.evidence_so_far: MEASURED 2026-10-15 from Kalshi hourly candles + FRED indexes + Kalshi settled results, 3 releases (Jul/Aug/Sep 2026) x 2 families = 6 independent outcomes (package-days inside a release-family share one print). Hours before the previous month's print excluded (including them was look-ahead and had produced fake 40-80c packages). Merger re-read the code (cpi_pairs3.py, cpi_pairs2_lib.py): density floor, doubled P- band, 2-h quote age and no-flip rule are as stated. cpi_pairs3.out, r = realised +- 0.0001 (stand-in for the rebuild): 50 package-days, conservative expected +$378, realised +$638 held to settlement on $4,463 spent at 100 pairs/day, 0 packages paid $0 (uninformative about the band tail: with 2-8 in 100 band chance per package and 6 outcomes, 0 hits is the expected result); 30 P+ at both ends, 6 P-, 14 changed type inside the band; by release-family +$120 Jul head, +$47 Jul core, +$213 Aug head, +$49 Aug core, +$77 Sep head, +$132 Sep core. Exit at the bids 24 h before close (no print risk): 43 package-days +$281, 38 positive / 5 negative; by family Jul head 16 days +$92 (14 positive), Aug head 11 +$101 (10), Sep head 5 +$29 (5), Sep core 9 +$75 (9), Jul core 1 -$3, Aug core 1 -$13; first days after the Jul print (Aug head entries 08-12, 08-13) worth +33c and +25c a pair at exit; worst package-day -12.7c a pair. Fully ex-ante with the naive r (+-0.00025): 40 package-days, expected +$236, realised +$688, exit +$235 (31 of 33 positive) -- but the naive r was lucky here (errors 0.00001-0.00022 vs p90 0.00058). Sep candles start 3 days after its print, so the first hours are measured only for Jul/Aug; core ladders have almost no quotes in the first week (not measured). Smallest detectable effect: with 6 outcomes, nothing about the band tail; the convergence (exit) result is 4 of 4 families with n >= 5 positive. Correction carried from the hunter: the 10-13 'pair A' (0.94 + 3.4c fees) was -3.4c EV at a 6-in-100 band; it paid $1 but the rule would not have taken it.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: In-sample at 100 pairs/day: ~$125 expected per month across headline + core (~$4/day), realised ~$210/month (~$7/day); exit-before-print ~$90-100/month (~$3/day); money in use up to ~$1,500 per release-family at a time. Current bank (a ~$500 subaccount, ~35 pairs/day): ~$1-1.5/day. At $5,000 (a $2,000 subaccount): ~$4-6/day, capped by depth, not bank. Worst plausible day: holding a P- stack when the print lands in the band -- the whole stack pays $0: about -$500 at 35 pairs/day over ~16 package-days, -$1,500 at 100/day; only the non-P+ package-days carry it (20 of 50 in-sample). The exit variant's worst measured package-day was -$13 per 100 pairs; a mis-built r flips the sign of everything (the worst-case-over-r valuation is the guard).
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 print a month per family (2 families); 5-30 package-days per release-family
idea.test_plan: (1) Re-code the BLS r rebuild and write r_Nov26 (headline and core) into results/ BEFORE the Nov 10 8:30 AM ET print; public fallbacks are not good enough on their own (r_Nov 2024 = 0.99663 head / 0.99772 core; r_Dec naive 0.99682 / 0.99792). (2) Read-only hourly logger of the 26NOV (and from Dec 10 the 26DEC) MoM/YoY books WITH sizes, ~10 unauthenticated GETs an hour, from the Nov 10 print to Dec 10; writer adds a READS_DUE item. (3) Pre-registered bars: GO for a 20-50-pair live test on a subaccount (operator sign-off) if on >= 3 of the first 5 days after the print a package has worst-case value >= +3c with >= 100 pairs at both touches, AND the logged exit value at the bids 7 and 14 days later is above entry cost on >= 70 of 100 package-days; scale only if the realised r lands within +-0.0001 of the pre-registered value. Kill if the logged worst-case value is <= +2c on every day of the first week after the Nov print.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SI12/SJ57 were killed on a wrong r inference; U23 said 'FAIL = dead for good' and it PASSED (+0.00001). New: the first multi-release measurement (cpi_pairs3, cpi_rimpl), the timing structure (gap largest right after the previous print, gone in ~2 weeks), the no-print-risk exit, the look-ahead trap, the naive-r error distribution, the core family and current depth. Not a duplicate of carried econ-nowcast 'CPI upper-tail NO at release' or index-ladders 'CPI-day stale-quote sweep' (different markets and mechanism). Same bot and logger as N1-02.
idea.worst_case: A held P- stack inside the band: the whole stake (-$500 at the current-bank size). An r-model miss larger than the band silently turns a 'riskless' P+ into a P-. Thin exit books force holding into the print, which turns the exit trade into the hold trade with its band tail.
merged_from: r1:revisit / CPI month-vs-year consistency pair, REVIVED and now measured on three releases (SI12/SJ57; U23 bar PASSED)
r1:revisit / CPI after-print convergence trade: the NEXT month's YoY ladder is stale for 1-2 weeks after each print
idea.prior_reason: An exact arithmetic identity, settlement-verified, positive in all 6 release-families held and in 4 of 4 families with n >= 5 on the no-print-risk exit -- the strongest-evidenced idea in this batch. Held back by: n = 3 prints, candle quotes with no size (exit bids are 1-6 lots on many MoM rungs today), the r rebuild not yet re-coded, small money (~$1-1.5/day at the current bank, $4-6/day at $5,000), and a first decision only after the Nov 10 print (~Nov 24).

test.method:
I ran the hunter's rule unchanged on earlier data it was not tuned on (a backward holdout). The rule is the cpi_pairs3 logic: 2c margin, density floor 4 per pp, doubled P- band, quotes no older than 2 h, no-flip rule. I ported it to analyze.py and checked the port against the hunter's own Jul-Sep 2026 run: 51 vs 50 package-days, +$657 vs +$638 held, exit +$293 vs +$281.

New data: Kalshi's public /historical/markets and /historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks endpoints hold every CPI ladder back to 2021. I pulled hourly yes-bid/ask closes and volume for 866 markets: every MoM rung and the in-range YoY rungs of the 2024-01..2026-06 releases (56 release-families, 28 eligible months). 2025-10 and 2025-11 are excluded because the Oct-2025 index does not exist. Each window runs from 1.5 h after the previous print to the close.

r comes from ALFRED first-print vintages, because FRED's current seasonally adjusted series is revised every February and would be look-ahead. r_real is the first print. The ex-ante 'naive' r is the same month a year earlier, in the vintage that was public at the previous print.

Settlement self-check: first-print SA MoM and NSA YoY, rounded to 1 dp, reproduce 2,073 of 2,074 Kalshi results.

P&L is realised from Kalshi results at 100 pairs per package-day, with taker fees 0.07p(1-p) on both legs.

Variants run:
- package choice: the day's best hour (hunter), the first hour that passes (what a bot can actually do), a fixed 11 AM ET daily grid with 24-h quote carry (exogenous)
- quote age 2 h and 24 h
- r bands +-0.00015, +-0.00025 and +-0.0004
- a factor-level r predictor, the only ex-ante r that exists for Nov 2026

Extra checks: the trade tape (/historical/trades) on 40 random package-days, and the implied-r timing across 42-62 release-families.

Data used: candle book quotes (no size), Kalshi results and BLS/ALFRED indexes. No live fills exist for this idea.
test.n_markets: 866 markets pulled out-of-sample (2024-01..2026-06 ladders), plus the hunter's Jul-Sep 2026 candles. 2,074 settled CPI markets used for the settlement self-check.
test.n_independent_clusters: Out-of-sample, the ex-ante naive rule traded in 20 release months (29 release-families) out of 28 eligible months. Headline and core share one print, so the release month is the cluster. In-sample: 3 months.
test.result:
Main version: ex-ante naive r +-0.00025, first hour that passes, 2-h quotes, held to settlement, out-of-sample 2024-01..2026-06.
- 187 package-days, +$2,477 on $16,023 spent at 100 pairs/day.
- 18 of 20 release months positive; mean +$124/month, sd $163 (t 3.39, n 20); worst month -$263.
- 8 package-days paid $0. Seven are 2024-09 core, where the naive r was off by 0.00117 and the 'gap' was the market being right.
- 2024-25: +$1,409 (12 of 14 months positive). 2026H1: +$1,068 on 57 package-days (6 of 6 months positive, none paid $0).

Same data, other variants:
- Hunter's day's-best-hour pick: +$3,076 (18 of 20 months positive).
- Fixed 11 AM ET grid: +$1,341 on 110 package-days (16 of 17 months positive).
- Perfect r (upper bound, real +-0.0001): +$4,925 on 303 (22 of 23).
- Factor-level r +-0.0004 (usable for Nov 2026): +$1,975 on 108, 17 of 17 months positive, none paid $0 out-of-sample. On Jul-Sep 2026 the same predictor made only +$117, with 2 package-days paid $0.

The hunter's no-print-risk exit (sell at the bids 24 h before close) is NOT robust:
- +$408 (77 of 95 positive) with 6-h exit quotes
- -$102 with 24-h exit quotes
- -$48 on the fixed grid

Timing, first-hour rule, P&L per package-day by days since the previous print:
- 0-1 d: $25
- 1-3 d: $20
- 3-7 d: $12
- 7-14 d: $20
- after 14 d: $6 (all 8 packages that paid $0 sit here)

The mechanism holds out-of-sample: the YoY ladder's implied r is off by a median 0.00033-0.00034 in the first 3 days after a print, against 0.00013 after 14 days.
test.artefact_checks:
1. The port reproduces the hunter's in-sample numbers.
2. Settlement arithmetic matches 2,073 of 2,074 results; the one mismatch is a strike-format quirk.
3. Vintage-correct first-print r is used; current-vintage seasonally adjusted data would be look-ahead.
4. The window starts 1.5 h after the previous print.
5. Day's-best-hour selection is a look-ahead inside the day. Replaced by the first hour that passes, P&L falls about 20% and stays positive.
6. The exogenous daily grid is still positive.
7. The exit variant flips sign with the quote-age assumption, so it is rejected.
8. Trade tape, 40 sampled package-days:
   - on 34, at least one leg had NO taker buy at our price or better within +-1-2 h;
   - both legs had 100+ contracts at that price on 1 of 40.
   So the size at the touch is unproven: the quotes are neither contradicted nor confirmed. The thinner leg's 24-h traded volume has a median of 100 contracts (2024-25: 43; 2026H1: 655). With fills capped at that volume, P&L is +$1,656.
9. The naive r band is too narrow about 1 time in 6: 16 of 92 packages rated 'P+ at both ends' were P- at the realised r (2024-25), though none of them landed in the band.
10. Not done: the BLS seasonal-factor r rebuild (needed to approach the +$4,925 bound). Historical book sizes do not exist.

Collectors: both still writing (kalshi_data and feed_data files updated at 08:17 ET). Disk 121.8 GB free. RAM 5.2 GB free. Scratch 4 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get:
Not measured at size. Candles carry no size, and historical books do not exist.

Proxies:
- The thinner leg traded a median 100 contracts in the 24 h before entry (2026H1: 655; 2024-25: 43). A quarter of entries had 0.
- Taker buys at our price on both legs near entry: 6 of 40 sampled package-days.
- The hunter's 10-15 snapshot of the 26NOV books: 10,185-21,421 at the central asks, 1-30 on neighbouring rungs, 1-6 on most MoM bids.

Plausible supply: 20-100 pairs per package-day on central rungs, about 6 package-days per release-family per month (max 24), across 2 families (headline and core).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now:
About $1/day, range $0.6-1.3.

That assumes 30-35 pairs per package-day in a ~$500 subaccount. Money is locked at ~$0.85 per pair for 1-4 weeks, up to ~$700 in the busiest stretch. The out-of-sample rate at 100 pairs is $2.7/day (2026H1: $5.9/day). Scaled by 0.33 for size and by ~0.67 for the volume cap, that gives $0.6-1.3/day.

It is paid in lumps: one print per family per month. The first window opens Nov 10 and settles Dec 10.
test.worst_case:
Measured worst release month: -$263 at 100 pairs, about -$90 at 33 pairs. That was 2024-09 core: the naive r was off by 0.00117, and 7 package-days of 'cheap' YoY NO + MoM YES all paid $0.

Plausible worst: one release-family's whole stack lands in the band. That is up to 24 package-days at ~$0.85 per pair, about -$700 at 33 pairs or -$2,000 at 100.

The failure mode is a wrong r. The biggest gaps are often where our r is wrong, not where the market is.

At today's bank the limit is money, not market depth, and that money is not free. The pin bot sizes from main-account cash (size = bank / 11.76, 98 contracts at $1,155). The CPI pair returns about 0.45% a day on money while it is tied up (Sep-2026 headline: about 11c per pair on about 85c, held about 29 days), so +$1 to $2.20/day on $500. Funded from the main pool it is net NEGATIVE, about -$2 to -$6/day. Only truly idle money avoids that cost: about $42 in the stopped dip-seller and about $55 in the reward-test subaccount, per HANDOFF, not re-measured. About $100 earns about $0.30-0.45/day.

idea.name: Election-night post-decision maker (Nov 3): once a liquid race's side first prints 95c, rest bids on it at 96-97c (= asks at 3-4c on the other side) and hold
markets: SENATETX-26 (26M contracts to date), SENATEME-26 (8.6M), SENATEMI-26 (6.6M), SENATEOHS-26, SENATEIA-26, SENATEAK-26, SENATENC-26, SENATEGA-26
GOVPARTY*-26 (NY, CA, TX, FL and the toss-ups)
KXHOUSERACE (707 markets; only those >= 500k lifetime contracts)
idea.mechanism: 1) On Nov 3 (polls close 19:00-01:00 ET) watch ~40 liquid race markets (>= 500k lifetime contracts). 2) The first time a side prints 95c -- a stopping time, no AP call needed -- wait 60 s, then rest a bid on that side at 96-97c (economically the same as an ask at 3-4c on the other side: a NO bid at 96c on the loser's market = a YES ask at 4c) for a capped size, e.g. 100 contracts per race; these series are fee_type quadratic (no maker fee) -- verify per series. 3) Pull every bid on a race whose price falls under 90c (relapse guard). 4) Hold; the next morning sell into 99c bids where they exist to recycle the cash (settlement is at certification / swearing-in, Dec 2026-Jan 2027); otherwise hold (Kalshi pays 4.05% a year on positions >= $250).
idea.why_mispriced: After the decision, winner-holders cash out early and loser-side lottery buyers keep buying, and the takers mostly SELL the winner into resting bids. Measured on the Aug-Sep 2026 primary tape after the 95c print: OLAR 43,451 contracts sold vs 8,142 bought; RFRY 46,716 vs 20,997; resting winner bids at <= 97c captured ~$3,270 to 99c across the 14 biggest markets vs ~$1,300 for takers. SC special runoff (KXSCRSENS-26-DNOR, 12.0M contracts): 95c -> 99c in 14 min with 1.01M contracts between; 799k at 97-99c and 179k at 95-97c in the last 14 minutes. No wrong-side lock (loser bid >= 90c) in 117 settled election markets, so 'first side to print 95c' won every time measured. Politics takers lose ~1.9c a contract pre-fee at every price (Burgi/Deng/Whelan).
idea.must_be_true: Fills are not adversely selected: relapses under 80c after a 95c print were 6 of 64 in thin FL markets and 12 of 30 in thin TN, 0 of 9 in liquid SC -- hence the >= 500k floor and the 90c guard; our queue share against professional desks on a general-election night (unknown; Nov 2024/2025 are purged from the API, so nothing comparable can be measured); 'takers selling the winner' is not one actor trading with itself; capital turns once per night at this bank, and the pin bot sizes from subaccount-0 cash, so the election cash must be idle or separate funds; a 2020-style count mirage (early vote misleading) is the tail, which the 95c trigger mostly avoids.
idea.evidence_so_far: Kalshi public tape + 1-min candles, Aug-Sep 2026 primaries (r1-election-night scratch: tape_after95.json, decay_rows.jsonl, runoff_candles.json): FL n=64 (58 reached 99c, median 95c -> 99c 6-8 min, 77 market-minutes of <= 97c asks after 95c, 0 after 99c), TN 30, SC 9 + runoff; resting-bid capture upper bound ~$3,270 across 14 markets ($100-230 a market); SC runoff naive ~$6.5k at 95-99c if half the volume hit bids. This run (r1-structural-arb-scan): control vs balance-of-power combo held exactly at the fee boundary for 21 days (0 positive minutes after fees) -- a second Nov 3 recorder item, same night. Our own fills: none.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Nov 3 only, plus ~10 primary nights a year from 2027-28. Capital-bound: ~$800 of idle cash buys ~830 contracts at 97c, +2-3c each = ~$20-30 for the night at the current bank; ~$100-150 at $5,000 (a second turn the next day, if 99c exit bids exist, roughly doubles it). Worst plausible night: one relapse race filled at 97c on the eventual loser = -$97 per 100 contracts; with the 100-a-race cap, -$97 to -$200.
idea.settlements_per_day: One night (~40 liquid races); ~700 race markets settle Nov 2026-Jan 2027; ~10 primary nights a year thereafter
idea.test_plan: (1) Now, free, before the ~60-day API purge: extend tape_after95.json to every Aug-Sep primary market with >= 500k contracts (~150-300 public calls) and replay a 97c bid placed 60 s after the first 95c print -- fills = taker trades at or through 97c on that side after placement, plus relapses and net cents a contract; bar >= +1.5c a contract over >= 15 races, no race worse than -20c. (2) Nov 3: read-only recorder (orderbook_delta + trade) on ~150 election tickers 18:00 ET Nov 3 - 06:00 ET Nov 4 in its own process, never from the crypto watchdog; the WebSocket is signed, so it needs the account key or a research read-only key (operator's OK); disk is now 129 GB free, cap the writer at 0.5 GB; next-morning REST pull of candles/trades. (3) If (1) passes: 2-5 contracts per race live on Nov 3 with sign-off (new strategy family); READS_DUE entry for Nov 4.
idea.prior_reason: Real measured flow on Kalshi's own election tape and a 117-of-117 stopping-time record, but it is one night, against professional queues, and cash turns once per night -- ~$20-30 at this bank; step (1) is cheap and settles the replay sign before Nov 3.

test.method:
Two read-only measurements.

(1) Kalshi primaries. Source: the Kalshi public trade tape (/markets/trades, no auth, 65 calls) plus the hunter's 1-min candles for every settled Aug-Sep 2026 primary market with at least 3k contracts (366 markets). The rule runs exactly as a bot would, with no outcome used:
- Arm at 23:00Z (7 pm ET) on election day. Both side bids must be under 95c at that moment.
- Trigger is the first 1-min candle where one side's bid is 95c or more. Rest a bid on that side at 96c or 97c, 60 s later.
- Fills are later trades where a taker hit our side at or below our price. Optimistic version: we are first in the queue. Conservative version: the price traded strictly below our level.
- Pull the bid after any trade under 90c. Rest at most 12 h. P&L is taken at settlement.
- Maker fee is 0: fee_type 'quadratic' x1 was checked for all 24 target series, and for 1,562 of 1,568 election/politics series in the 10-13 catalogue.
- The TN (Aug 6) trades are now purged from the API, so the hunter's 10-13 pull was used for those markets.
- Also run: an ungated variant (armed all day), and a recycle-exit check (minutes from our first fill to the first 99c trade).

(2) General-election nights, out of sample. Source: Polymarket's public gamma API plus clob prices-history (1-min traded/mid price, NOT a bid). Covered: every resolved 2024 US general-election race market with at least $50k volume (231 candidates), and the Nov 2025 night (406 candidates). Test: the race was contested at 22:00Z on election day; the first side to print 95c is recorded, then whether it won. Clustered by race (the D and R markets of one race count as one race). There is no fit/holdout split because the rule has no fitted parameter, so the general nights are a pure out-of-sample test of the stopping-time claim. Kalshi's own Nov 2024 and Nov 2025 tape is purged, so Polymarket is a different venue standing in for it.

Scripts and rows are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C3-02/ (t1_replay.py, t2_exit.py, p2_poly_night.py, p3_check.py, p4_tally.py, replay_rows_3000_gate.json, poly_rows.json, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: Kalshi primaries: 53 triggered contested markets with the 7 pm gate (79 without it), out of 291 with candles. Of the 53: 20 at 20k+ contracts, 6 at 100k+, and only 2 at the idea's own 500k+ floor. Polymarket: 82 triggered race markets on the 2024 general night and 25 on the Nov 2025 night.
test.n_independent_clusters: Kalshi: 28 events over 4 primary nights (11 events at 20k+). Polymarket: 43 races on the 2024 general night plus 12 races on the Nov 2025 night. The cluster that really matters is the night: 4 primary nights and 2 general nights.
test.result:
Kalshi primaries, gated, 97c bid, 100 contracts a market:
- The trigger side won 53 of 53.
- At 20k+ contracts, 11 of 20 markets filled: 950 contracts (optimistic) or 714 (conservative), worth +$28.51 or +$21.44 over 4 nights. That is about +$5-7 a night, +3c a filled contract.
- Uncapped supply at 97c or below (the upper bound for all makers together) was 34,580 contracts = +$1,037. Two markets (SC RFRY and FL OLAR) hold 76% of it.
- All 14 filled markets reached 99c, median 5.3 min after our first fill.
- Ungated: 78 of 79. The miss is TN-04 D MCOR (11.7k contracts): a 95c bid at 5:41 pm ET before any votes, and it lost.

Polymarket 2024 general night (this is what decides it):
- 43 races triggered; 2 went to the WRONG side after their first 95c print, 2 in 43 = 4.7%.
- Michigan Senate: Rogers went to 95-97.5c between 2:09 and 3:25 am ET on Nov 6, with both the D and R books agreeing. Slotkin won once Detroit's absentee votes came in.
- Wisconsin Senate: Hovde reached 96.5c at 2:09 am ET. Baldwin won after Milwaukee's central count.
- The fills are worst exactly when it matters. 72 of 79 good markets came back to 97c or lower after the trigger, so the bid fills and earns +$3 at 100 contracts. Both wrong races fell straight through 97c, so the fill was certain at -$97 each.
- Break-even wrong-side rate: 3.0% of races if the good races fill fully, about 1.5% at the Kalshi-primary fill rate (47 of 100 contracts).
- Replay at 100 contracts a market: +$216 vs -$291 = -$75. One leg per race: about -$82.
- 40 of 79 good markets also dipped under 90c before winning, so a stop-loss would turn about half the winners into losses.

Nov 2025 night:
- 12 races, 0 wrong side; replay +$72.

Both general nights together:
- Per market: +$288 vs -$291 = -$3. Per race: about -$47.
- Pooled: 2 wrong of 55 races (3.6%).
test.artefact_checks:
(a) The hunter's relapse_under80 flag is True on all 366 rows. That comes from the candle after the market closes (winner bid shows 0), not a real relapse; relapses were recomputed from trades here.
(b) The hunter's 'no wrong-side lock in 117' used candles already flipped into winner terms. Measured side-agnostic, it is 1 of 79 ungated (MCOR, before polls closed).
(c) The MI/WI wrong-side prints were checked by hand:
- Michigan: 10 minute-points at 95c or more over 76 min on the D book, plus 2 on the R book peaking at 97.5c. Two separate books agree, so this is not a stray print.
- Wisconsin: 1 point at 96.5c.
- Both match the well-known 2024 late-count reversal in those two Senate counts.
(d) The Polymarket price is a traded/mid price, so a 95c 'print' there is easier to hit than a resting 95c bid on Kalshi, which could overstate wrong-side triggers. Against that, the MI R book itself traded at 97.5c.
(e) Kalshi units: count_fp is contracts and yes_price_dollars is the price, unit decided once; the side price is 1 - yes for NO-side triggers.
(f) Queue: the true queue depth at 97c cannot be seen on the public tape, so the Kalshi fill numbers are an upper bound.
(g) After the gate, the primary sample cannot show a loss by construction. 0 wrong of 53 is consistent with anything from 0% to 5.7% (rule of three), so it cannot rule out the 1.5-3% break-even.
Also: the newest Kalshi tape file (trade 20261015T12) was still being written at 8:28 am ET, and 121.7 GB of disk is free. The recorders' command lines are not visible to this shell.
test.supply_we_would_get:
Primary nights:
- At 100 contracts a market, about half the triggered markets fill: about 47 contracts per triggered market (optimistic) or 36 (conservative).
- Uncapped supply was 34.6k contracts at 97c or below over 4 nights, mostly in 2 markets. Capital runs out before supply does: about $500-800 of idle cash at the current bank is about 500-800 contracts a turn, with roughly a 5-minute turn to 99c.

Nov 3 Kalshi board (as of 10-13):
- 59 legs with 500k+ lifetime contracts and both sides under 95c, about 28 races (CONTROLH/S, the balance-of-power combo, the Senate and governor races, seat ladders); 133 legs at 100k+.
- Many will not decide on the night: ME and AK count by ranked choice, and House control took 8-11 days in 2022 and 2024.
- Supply and queue on Nov 3 itself: not measured.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: Negative. Nov 3 at 100 contracts a race on ~28 races with a 3.6-4.7% wrong-side rate: about +$73 from good fills vs -$97 to -$128 from wrong ones, net about -$25 to -$57 for the night. Range: no mirage, about +$76; two mirages, about -$123 net. This is a one-night event, not a daily rate: about -$0.1 a day over a year.
test.worst_case: Two count-mirage races on one night, as with MI and WI Senate in 2024, both filled at 97c: -$194 at 100 contracts a race (current bank), -$776 at 400 a race (on a $5k bank). After the night's other fills, about -$123 and -$490. The Nov 3 board has the same setup: SENATEMI-26 (6.6M contracts) and the MI/WI/GA governor races, all in states where big-city absentee votes are counted last. One wrong race costs as much as ~3.4 primary seasons of in-sample gains ($28.51).
test.next_test:
No paper or live test of this rule. Two optional, free, read-only follow-ups:
(1) The already-planned Nov 3 recorder (orderbook_delta + trade on about 150 election tickers, in its own process) would record Kalshi's own wrong-side count and queue depth at 96-98c. Bar to revive: no more than 1 wrong side per 100 races across at least 2 general-election nights, AND at least +1.5c net per filled contract.
(2) Offline variants checked on the same files before anyone builds them: an AP-call trigger, or a 98-99c trigger (MI and WI peaked at 97.5c and 96.5c). Each cuts the margin to 1-2c, so the break-even wrong-side rate drops to about 1-2% and the same sample-size problem comes back.
Polymarket 2020 and 2022 general nights: not measured.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Same sign at 4x size: about -$100 to -$220 for Nov 3 at 400 contracts a race. About +$300 if no mirage happens; two mirages cost -$776 on those races, about -$490 net. Not a daily strategy.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
Wrong-side rate, 95% ranges:
- 2024 night, 2 of 43 races: 0.6%-15.8%.
- Both general nights, 2 of 55: 0.4%-12.5%.
- Adding the 28 Kalshi primary events, 2 of 83: 0.3%-8.4%.
The 1.5-3% break-even sits inside every range, so the data cannot prove an edge, and the two general nights measured net out to about zero or a loss. Proving a rate below 1.5% with 95% confidence would take about 200 general-election races with no misses, which is 5+ general nights. Nov 3 adds about 30 races.

idea.name: Monthly rain ladders: sell the over-bought far strikes and buy the under-priced near ones off month-to-date (NWS CLI) + ensemble + climatology (LAX >1 in, DEN >1 in, HOU >2, CLL >4 NO; MIA >5, NYC >5, SEA >2 YES)
markets: KXRAINCLLM (7-14 strikes each, 'total precipitation at CLIxxx in <month> > K inches', close early when crossed); KXRAINCHIM skipped (no climatology)
idea.mechanism: Month-to-date from the NWS CLI text (IEM AFOS 'MONTH TO DATE' line; the rules name the CLI station) + rest-of-month = Open-Meteo ensemble QPF for days 1-7 (GFS 31 + ECMWF 51 members, free) + a climatological draw for the remaining days from the station's own 30 Octobers. P(YES) = share of the 82 x 30 combinations above K. Buy NO at (1-bid) when (1-P) - (1-bid) - fee >= 5c, YES at the ask likewise, sized to the depth within 3c (cap 300). Hold to Nov 1 (NO legs) or the early close (YES legs).
idea.why_mispriced: Retail over-buys YES on lottery strikes ('rain in LA'): LAX >1 in trades 37-46c on 26k volume while blend 0.14 / climatology 0.13 / raw ensemble 0.11; DEN >1 in 36-42c vs 0.09-0.15. Near strikes in wet cities are under-bought (MIA >5 in 52-59c vs 0.67; NYC >5 in 8-9c vs 0.29 blend / 0.37 climatology). The YES-bid depth at LAX >1 (1,086 contracts within 3c) is the NO buyer's liquidity.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The blend is roughly calibrated for 16-day totals (raw ensembles are under-dispersed; days 8-16 replaced by climatology, days 1-7 still raw). (2) No forecast event the crowd knows that the models give ~10% to. (3) The CLI month-to-date is what Kalshi settles on (a TWC revision is the SJ03-type tail). (4) Depth survives (only LAX>1 1,086, SEA>2 469, DAL/CLL/HOU 74-245 had >= 50 within 3c). (5) Capital ~$500 to Nov 1 must sit in a subaccount: in the main account it would cut the pin bot's cash-based bet size by roughly 40%.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter weather-model, monthly_rain2.out (single snapshot 2026-10-15 ~06Z): 9 cities, MTD from CLI through Oct 14 (LAX 0.23, DEN 0.14, HOU 1.28, MIA 2.27, NYC 2.01, SEA 0.06, DFW 3.84, CLL 3.36 in). Flagged legs at >= 5c edge with depth: LAX>1 NO +22c (depth 1,086), DEN>1 NO +25c (85), HOU>2 NO +14c (136), CLL>4 NO +13c (74), MIA>5 YES +6c (72), SEA>2 YES +8c (469), NYC>5 YES +20c (depth not read), DAL>8 YES +10c (not read). Portfolio at depth-within-3c capped 300/leg: expected +$153 on $496 locked under the blend. Settled history (rainm_candles.json): 10 city-months Aug-Sep; YES strikes priced 20-60c at day 10-15 resolved YES 2 of 17 -- directional only. N0 check: every flagged ticker is the October event (26OCT), not the already-open November set, so a wrong-month artefact is ruled out.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: One-off per month: +$150 expected on ~$500 locked 16 days if the blend is right (~$5-10/day averaged); ~2x at $5,000 (depth-bound). Zero to negative if the market knows a storm. Sources: Kalshi's public hourly candles (the YES bid and ask at the end of each hour) plus settled results for all 1,791 KXYTVIEWSW markets (119 artist-weeks, weeks ending 2026-08-09 to 10-11). ARTEFACT FIXED FIRST: the hunter timed every market from its OWN close_time. But 714 of 963 YES markets close early: Kalshi settles a strike as soon as the week's running maximum crosses it. At "own close - 144 h" only 282 of the 598 YES markets trading at that moment had a candle, against 813 of 813 NO markets. That is survivorship bias toward NO.

How I re-measured:
- Decision time T = the scheduled close (the Sunday that ends the week + 2 days, 14:00Z) minus H. A market counts only if it was open at T. The quote is the last hourly candle at or before T (median age 0 h).
- Second fix: I bucket on the YES BID we would actually hit, not the mid. With no spread cap, a 30-70c bid often sits under an ask of 90c or more (a low-ball bid), and hitting it loses money.
- Bot-shaped rule: scan Wed 14:00Z (H=144) and Thu 14:00Z (H=120), take each market only at its first qualifying scan. Qualifies if the YES bid is 0.30-0.70 and ask minus bid is at most the cap. Buy NO at 1 - bid, pay the taker fee 0.07p(1-p), hold to settlement.
- Statistics: clustered by artist-week (event), cluster-robust SE. TRAIN = weeks ending 08-09 to 09-06, TEST = 09-13 to 10-11. Event-level random-side control.

Scripts t1-t8 are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-07/.

test.method: Queue-aware order-book replay on our own tape (C:\kals\kalshi_data orderbook_snapshot + orderbook_delta + trade, read-only, streamed one hour at a time, peak 127 MB). A virtual 300-lot rests at the favourite's best bid when that bid is 80-95c, which is the same as selling the 5-20c longshot. Each window is scored two ways: (a) exact fills held to settlement, using results from the first tester's public /markets pull (makers pay 0; fee_type 'quadratic' checked on /series for both series), and (b) the reward credit under the 2026-07-15 filing. Reward rule as modelled: a snapshot every second of the 900 s window; the reference is the first level that reaches 60; the walk stops at 300; 0.5 per tick below the reference; a snapshot counts only when both sides reach 300; credit = $20 x our share of our side / 2 / 900. Program terms were checked on a live natgas program: $20, target 300, 5000 bps discount, period = market open to close. Queue rules: we join behind everyone at our price; taker sales at our price eat the queue ahead of us first; any sale through our price fills what we have left; cancels come either from behind us (PESS) or spread over the queue (PROP). Policies: static (the critic's spec: placed at tau 780, pulled at 120 s, also tried pulled at 10 s); late (armed when a side first enters 80-95c); join (moves to the best bid every second); improve (one tick above the best bid when the spread is 2c or more). Fills are capped at 300 per window, with join also run at a 1500 cap. Sample: 52 weekday hours (13-20Z), 2 per day over 26 days. FIT = ET days 09-08..09-30 (12 days with data); HOLDOUT = 10-01..10-13 (9 days). se is clustered by ET day. Source rank: this is a replay of the tape, so a positive result would only be a hypothesis; it is enough to kill because nothing positive survives the split. Files are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-04-RT/: r1_bookreplay.py and r2_agg.py (both have self-tests), r3_checks.py, d1_debug.py, p0_probe.py, r1_windows.jsonl, r2_out.json, r3_out.json, RESULT.json.
test.n_markets: 334 windows scored (natgas 167, copper 167): 11.1 M book deltas and 293 k trades. 3 hours missing from the tape (09-09 15-16Z) were skipped. Coin race was not re-measured: the first tester already killed it (back-of-queue -8.5c per fill, 1 of 38 days positive, consistent with D13).
test.n_independent_clusters: 21 ET days per series (FIT 12 / HOLD 9)
test.result:
The reward cannot be stacked on top of the fills. A 300-lot at the favourite's best bid gets about 243 of its 300 contracts filled per window, so it is live and scoring for only about 81 s of each window (it holds 0.48 of its side while live). Reward credit is $0.43/window on natgas and $0.36 on copper (join, cap 300), and $1.20 at cap 1500. That is about 0.15-0.2c per filled contract, against fill uncertainty of about 2.5-3c (se).

Critic's exact spec (static, placed at tau 780, pulled at 120 s):
- It fires in only 10% of natgas windows, because an up/down window opens near 50c.
- Natgas: -$1.11/window (se 2.33), fills -4.2c/contract, reward $0.04/window.
- Copper: +$1.51/window (se 1.51), FIT +$2.19 (t 2.5) / HOLD +$0.61 (t 0.18), on only about 15 active windows.

Best natgas policy (join, cap 300, PESS): -$0.92/window (se 5.99), fills -0.55c/contract (se 2.46). The sign flips between halves: FIT -3.94c, HOLD +4.24c.
Other cells: natgas late -$4.00/window (pull at 120 s) and -$5.91 (pull at 10 s). Copper join FIT +4.58c / HOLD -5.12c. Copper late HOLD -16.5c/contract (t -3.3).

Pre-registered bar (fills + reward > +$1/window, fills >= -1c/contract, positive in both halves): no natgas policy passes. Copper static is positive in both halves, but its holdout is only $0.61/window (t 0.18) on about 15 active windows.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) I found and fixed a bug in my own replay. Sorting the book snapshot (which only has a receive-time stamp) and the deltas by time dropped deltas, giving crossed books in 94 of 334 windows. After re-ordering by sequence number there are 0 crossed seconds and 0 negative levels in all 334 windows. Fills barely moved because they are driven by trades. The buggy output is kept as r1_windows_tsorder_BUGGY.jsonl.
(2) The queue model does not decide the answer: PESS and PROP differ by 0.5c/contract or less.
(3) Calibration: on natgas windows with fills, the favourite we bought won 127 of 153 times (83%) at about 84-86c paid. That is what no edge looks like.
(4) It agrees with the first tester's tape-only back-of-queue ladder (natgas -0.16c, se 0.68).
(5) Clean-only rerun on the 279 windows whose book snapshot arrived before tau 780: natgas join +$1.53/window (se 7.13), FIT -$6.69 / HOLD +$9.52. Same conclusion.
(6) The self-tests plant queue, trade-through, cancel, cap, reward-walk and empty-world cases.
Not measured: overnight hours (only 13-20Z was sampled); what a real order would actually be paid (formula only; the coin-race live test was paid 90% of formula); other makers reacting to us.
test.supply_we_would_get: Supply is not the limit. On KXNATGAS15M a 300-lot at the favourite's best bid fills about 243 contracts per window, about 23,000 a day at 96 windows; copper fills about 246 per window. The limit is the edge, not the volume.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0, tilted negative. Natgas join is -$0.92/window x 96 windows = about -$88/day, with se of about +-$575/day. The reward adds at most +$41/day gross (0.43 x 96), and that is already inside the figure.
test.worst_case: Worst single window: -$264 (300 favourite contracts at about 88c, lost). Worst sampled 8-window (2-hour) block: -$356 (join) to -$528 (late). A trending full day of 96 windows could plausibly lose $1,000 or more at 300 lots, which is about the whole $1,155 bank.
test.next_test: Nothing further for this idea: fills plus stacked reward is dead, and coin race was already dead. The only leftover is a separate idea: a reward-only order parked k ticks below the best bid so it avoids fills. I did not measure it. The walk stops at 300 and the incumbents rest about 300 at most levels, so a deeper order usually scores 0. To settle it, add a 'deep k' policy to r1_bookreplay.py and run it on the same 52 hours (about 15 min). Bar: credit >= $1/window with fills >= -1c/contract in both halves.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $0. A bigger size (cap 1500) only scales up the coin-flip fills (natgas -2.3c/contract, -$14/window, se $18), while the reward rises only to $1.20/window.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Natgas join: 2 se is about 4.9c per filled contract, or about $12 per window, over 21 days. The reward (about 0.2c per contract) is about 25 times smaller than anything this sample can detect, so it cannot rescue a fill edge that does not show up on its own.

idea.name: Pin the order-book price convention and migrate the deprecated trade/order fields (use_yes_price default flip; taker_side -> taker_outcome_side; V1 action/side/purchased_side) BEFORE Kalshi flips them, plus a changelog watcher
idea.lane: lose-less (kalshi-mechanics-capital): every live bot and every tape analysis
markets: KXBTC15M family (all 12 up/down series the main bot and forecaster read)
the collector tape C:/kals/kalshi_data (orderbook_snapshot, orderbook_delta, trade)
idea.mechanism: Kalshi's docs (getting_started/order_direction, saved under r1-kalshi-mechanics-capital/docs/) say the default of the orderbook subscription flag use_yes_price will flip to true in a future release and the flag will then be removed; after that, NO-side levels in orderbook_snapshot/orderbook_delta move from no-leg pricing (a NO bid at 2c reported 0.02) to yes-leg pricing (reported 0.98). Separately the legacy fields taker_side (trades), action/side/is_yes (orders), purchased_side (fills) are deprecated and 'will not be removed before May 28, 2026' -- that floor has passed, so removal can come in any monthly release. Fix in five steps: (1) every WS subscription passes use_yes_price explicitly and the parsers convert; (2) a per-message convention check (under no-leg, a NO level p must satisfy p + best YES bid <= 1; a stream that breaks it is marked suspect and the bot stands down); (3) livebook reads taker_outcome_side first, taker_side as fallback, and ALARMS when both are missing instead of quietly returning 'no opinion'; (4) tape loaders detect the convention per hour (hard rule 5 applied to book sides); (5) a daily read-only poll of docs.kalshi.com/changelog that alarms on any entry naming use_yes_price, taker_side, purchased_side, is_yes or a removal date -- Kalshi says it will announce concrete dates first, so the real failure mode is nobody reading the announcement.
idea.why_mispriced: Nobody pays; this prevents losses. (a) The main bot's hedge pass computes market_belief from the opposite side's book (our ask = 1 - best NO bid). If the convention flips while our code assumes no-leg, a YES position's ask is read as ~2c instead of ~98c and insurance fires on winning positions whenever the index is stale; entries see fake 2c asks (an IOC at 2c just misses). (b) The toxic-fresh seller check that is being put back on reads only taker_side; if Kalshi removes it, taker_flow returns None and the gate goes silently OFF -- that gate, scored on live fills 10-04..10-13, would have refused 8 of 11 losing markets, so the measured loss class it guards comes straight back. (c) Every tape hour after the flip would be misread by analyses.
idea.must_be_true: Kalshi flips the default or removes the legacy fields while our code still depends on them. Merger checks 2026-10-15: grep of research/ finds use_yes_price in 0 files; research/livebook.py line 605 reads msg.get('taker_side') only (taker_outcome_side appears only in a comment at line 68). Kalshi does carry out removals: the changelog records available_on_brokers removed in the 2026-09-10 release and liquidity_dollars removed in the 2026-10-01 release, each after a deprecation notice. Against urgency: the use_yes_price flip will be announced with dates before it happens, so a watched changelog gives warning.
idea.evidence_so_far: Docs read 2026-10-15 (getting_started__order_direction.md, changelog__index.md). Tape hour 20261015T05 orderbook_delta is still legacy no-leg; trade messages still carry both taker_side and taker_outcome_side. Code audit: use_yes_price 0 files; taker_side read in pinrun.py, livebook.py and sweep/racereward_live.py. Money effect: not measured, because the change has not happened. | CRITIC re-test (see critics.json for the reason)
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 until the change. What it avoids: one or more days of garbage hedges/decisions -- at 98 contracts a misfired insurance order on a winning 97c position costs ~$3-10 per market; a full day of misreads plausibly -$100 to -$500 at the ~$1,155 bank, ~4x that at $5,000; plus every day the toxic-fresh gate is silently off (the losing-market class it blocks). Worst plausible day if NOT done: a silent switch mid-day, -$100 to -$500.
idea.settlements_per_day: n/a (covers every market the bots read: ~900+ 15-min closes/day, 24 KXBTCD closes/day, 96 coin races/day)
idea.test_plan: Read-only paper: open two livebook WS connections on the same 9 markets for 10 minutes, one with use_yes_price:false and one with true; assert the converted books match second by second. Self-test plants both conventions and a mid-stream switch and fails if the detector misses the switch or fires on a clean stream; a second self-test drops taker_side from trade messages and fails if taker_flow returns None without an alarm. Ship the explicit flag + fallback behind a VERSIONS.md entry. Start the changelog poller the same day (1 GET/day).
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New. No ledger row and no repo doc mentions use_yes_price or the legacy-field removal dates; carried crypto-lose-less ideas assume the toxic-fresh gate's input stays present.
idea.worst_case: Doing nothing: a silent convention switch or field removal in the middle of a trading day (-$100 to -$500 at the current bank). Doing it: a conversion bug, caught by the 10-minute two-connection paper test before shipping.
idea.prior_reason: Near-certain to happen eventually (Kalshi removed two deprecated fields in the last 5 weeks; the taker_side floor date has passed), large one-day cost and it silently disables a gate with a measured 8-of-11 loss-market record; but $0 until it happens, and the flip itself will be pre-announced, so expected $/day is a few dollars. Decided in minutes.

refs.strongest_objection:
The guard survives only because it costs almost nothing and cannot lose money. Its dollar case is close to zero, and part of the stated mechanism is wrong.
(1) The headline harm cannot happen: 'insurance fires on winning positions when the book flips.' pinrun.market_belief (line 1308) returns None unless 0 < bid <= ask < 1. On a flipped book, livebook.best() reports yes_ask = the LOWEST real NO bid. So any YES position with a bid over 50c reads as a crossed book: no opinion, no extra trigger.
What a flip really does under today's code:
- NO-held insurance misses. It buys YES at that fake low ask plus 0.10 slip.
- YES entries miss. sweep_limit walks at most 200 tapered ticks up from the fake ask and ends near 92-93c, under the real 95-98c asks (worked out by hand, not run).
- Each YES market burns up to 3 of the 24 order attempts its close shares, so in a close that leans YES some NO entries are blocked too.
(2) A taker_side removal is not silent in the forecaster. bettor_paper's live loop catches the KeyError and writes one 'bad_trade' line per print: about 225,000 lines an hour, about 0.38 GB a day. Its decisions are unaffected: race1_98_r28 uses no flow inputs. But nothing alarms on those lines: watchlive's pattern matches "error", and the line says "err".
(3) The seller check this protects is OFF in the bot running now (start record 04:42Z: toxic_fresh=false). So a removal today costs the main bot $0. On its real live-ON days the gate netted +$1.90 in 6.9 days.
(4) Against refuting it: the migration is an exact rename. Every print checked carries all three side fields, with 0 disagreements. Reading taker_outcome_side first, with an alarm when the field is missing, changes no decision today.
Net: ship the changelog watcher and the fallback-plus-alarm because they are nearly free. Make the alarm one that watchlive matches, and rate-limit the bad_trade lines. Defer the use_yes_price migration until Kalshi posts a dated notice. Do not rank this on dollars.

idea.name: Coin race vs the five 15-min up/down books: an exact cross-family identity (0 violations in 4,459 settled windows) with a 'tick floor' form -- real and book-confirmed but ~$1/day; also explains the coin-race filler's fill cost
idea.lane: structural arbitrage x crypto 15-min x coin race
markets: KXBTC15M / KXETH15M / KXSOL15M / KXXRP15M / KXHYPE15M (same window; tapered tick, 0.1c steps at the tails)
idea.mechanism: The race and the up/down markets use the SAME two 60-s CF averages (race = highest close-TWAP / open-TWAP, 773/773 in RESULTS_coinrace; up/down = close TWAP at least open TWAP). (R1) If X leads and any Y is up, X is up: race-X NO + up/down-X YES + up/down-Y NO pays >= $1 in every outcome. (R2) If X is up and every other coin is down, X leads: race-X YES + up/down-X NO + the other four up/down YES pays >= $1. Buy a package when it costs under $1 after the 3 (or 6) taker fees. The repeatable form is the TICK FLOOR: a dead race leg carries a 1c YES bid (the reward farmers' stacks) while the two up/down legs that prove it dead are offered at 0.1-0.3c; sell the race leg at 1c (buy its NO at 99c) and buy both hedges: +0.6-0.8c a contract riskless. Send the deep, cheap hedges first (if the race bid is then gone, the loss is the 0.2-0.3c hedge premium). A second, fading class: during index jumps one family's book is stale for 1-3 s.
idea.why_mispriced: The race book cannot price below 1c, and the reward program pays farmers to rest 1c bids on legs the up/down books price at 0.1c; the farmer who is hit loses ~0.5-1c a contract (two 500-lot sells into the XRP 1c bid in window 26OCT032100). Lose-less corollary for the carried coin-race 1c filler (lip-mechanics/lip-economics): any displayed 1c YES size on a dead leg is exactly what this arb sells into, so the filler's fill cost grows with the size it displays -- consistent with the 10-11 live burst of ~175 contracts a leg in the last 110 s versus 11 a leg on the tape.
idea.must_be_true: All legs fill inside ~1 s (runs last p10 1.0 s, p50 3.5 s); the farmers keep resting 1c stacks; we never sell into our own race filler's bids (self-trade). Residual identity risk: Kalshi calls ties on 3-decimal % moves and pays 50c per tied leg; a tie AT ~zero return with mixed raw signs could pay R1 only 50c -- ties are 22 in 2,927 races, all two-way, all < 0.58 bp; never seen with a ~0 return (not measured).
idea.evidence_so_far: Own tape, ticker channel (top of book + size), 22.0M messages over 1,012 hour files, 3,966 race windows 09-01..10-15 (gap 10-14 03:29Z..10-15 04:39Z). Positive after fees for >= 300 ms: R1 212 runs in 67 windows (1.7% of windows). Tick-floor class: 139 runs, 69 (window, leg) pairs on 20 of 41 days, edge p50 0.29c, size p50 25 / p90 233 lots, duration p50 3.5 s; valued once per leg: $13 at <= 100 lots, $31 at <= 1,000, $37 at <= 2,000 over 41 days ($0.32 / $0.76 / $0.91 a day). - **Self-trade:** our 1c filler ran live only on 10-11 08:24-09:00Z, and no tick-floor run fell in that time. Our coin-race taker's ceiling is 98c, while 137 of 139 runs needed 99c. So the supply was never our own orders.
- **Valuation:** the hunter's max edge x min size mixes two moments. Re-valued at the touch when each run started; that comes out higher at large caps because sizes at the start exceed the run minimum. Both valuations are under the bar.
- **Absent quotes:** an ask of 0 or a size of 0 is treated as missing, not as a 0c price (covered by the self-test).
- **Timing:** each trade is evaluated against the book as it stood just before its receive time.
- **Data gaps:** 10 hour files unreadable in both channels (09-02T00, 09-02T21, 09-04T07, 09-06T14, 09-09T13, 09-15T13, 09-15T20, 09-23T19, 10-12T03, 10-14T03). Also the PC-off gap 10-14 03:29Z..10-15 04:39Z and a trade-recorder gap 10-11 08:51-09:00Z. Determinations run only to about 10-15 07Z, so later prints are left out of P&L.
- **Hedge-buy signature:** compared against a same-width control window, because the up/down tails trade constantly.
- **Not checked:** book depth beyond the touch (it would raise hedge size, not the race-bid size that binds), our queue position against the competitor, and the tie-at-zero risk.
test.supply_we_would_get: The supply is the 1c YES bids on dead race legs (KXCRYPTOLEAD15M): the reward farmers' stacks, median 1,000 lots when a run starts. The hedges are bought in KXBTC15M/KXETH15M/KXSOL15M/KXXRP15M/KXHYPE15M at 0.1-0.3c; the hedge touch is the binding leg, median 107 lots. There were about 70 usable (window, leg) chances in 41 days, about 1.7 a day, with none on half the days. Another taker already sells into the race bid in 60% of them. Plausibly we would get the ~28 uncontested ones plus a share of the rest: roughly one chance a day at a few hundred lots.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0.4/day. Upper bound $0.62/day on uncontested legs at <= 300 lots; $1.23/day if we won every run. 300 lots ties up about $300 for 1-2 minutes, in the same last minute the pin bot uses.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $1/day: $1.18/day on uncontested legs, $2.61/day best case at <= 1,000 lots. The farmers' bid size and the competitor cap it, not capital.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: This is not a noisy-average question. Each package is riskless by an identity checked on 4,459 settled windows (0 violations) and on 49 proven-dead pairs (0 won). What 41 days can pin down is the supply level. With 70 pairs on 20 days, one burst day moves the 14-day average by about $1.3/day, so the honest result is "well under $5/day", not a precise figure. For the corollary, 1c-maker P&L per contract is resolved to about +-0.2c in the 30-60 s band (72,976 contracts, 1,200 windows) and about +-1.3c in the proven class (9,173 contracts, 40 windows).
test.worst_case:
- **Hedges sent first:** if the hedges fill (0.2-0.6c x size) and the race bid is gone, a miss costs $2-6 at 1,000 lots, so about -$9 to -$18 on a day with 3 misses.
- **Race leg sent first:** an unhedged 99c NO on a proven-dead leg risks 99c x size if the leg later wins. Not seen (0 of 49), but it would be -$990 at 1,000 lots.
- **Tie at about zero return:** -50c a contract. Never observed and not measured.

(5) Two snapshots of all 244 open books (Oct 12-18 week, 2:35-2:50 PM ET), scored with the LIP walk from the 2026-07-15 filing (reference at cumulative 200, cutoff at 1,000, 0.5 per tick). The test was a 200-lot each side at max(best+1c, mid -/+ 5c). Pot: $100 per ~190 h (lip-economics rank_series, 10-13).

test.result:
LOCK-BUYER ARM: dead as specified.
(a) The settlement series cannot be read by a script. All 8 insights calls returned HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; charts_home from the same client returned 200 (366 KB). The recaptcha flag is not set in the page.
(b) Public counters are not the settlement number. Official-video views divided by the settled weekly-max lower bound: TAY 0.48, TAT 0.36, BAD 0.51, DRA 0.34, ARI 0.53, WEE 0.53, JUS 0.55, KEN 0.35, MOR 0.42, OLI 0.41, POS 0.52, FUT 0.40, YE 0.44, YOU 0.60, FUE 0.30. So counters see 30-60% of the number and can only lock a strike in a release spike. kworb's daily history is 12 days long, with repeated (stale) days.
(c) The market learns at fixed times. Of 343 NO markets still undecided at the week end, the decisive collapse came at +19 h (42) or +23 h (84) after the week end, which is Monday 7 PM and 11 PM ET; the rest waited for Kalshi's Tuesday close (+35 h, 92). YES jumps cluster at 7 PM ET (52 of 453) and 11 PM ET (61).
(d) Window between the week end and the move, winner at or below 95c, gross, all takers, both taker sides:
- TRAIN: $38,122 over 5 weeks, of which $30,573 is one market (Bad Bunny Aug 23 week, 28M strike, true value between 27.5M and 28.0M). Counters seeing about half the views cannot resolve a gap that narrow.
- TEST: $3,175 over 5 weeks = $635/week market-wide.
- After the move: about $0 ($159 over 2 weeks, hunter).
(e) The 24 h before any jump, winner at or below 90c: TRAIN $33,040 / 5 weeks, TEST $17,776 / 5 weeks. The top 10 markets are 62% of it. This is an upper bound for a perfectly informed taker, not our supply.
QUOTING ARM (reward plus inside quotes): survives on paper only.
- Pot: $12.63 per market per day; 1,622 of 1,622 ended programs were paid, so farmers collect everything today.
- Live books: 180 of 244 two-sided, median spread 4c (the 70c spreads exist only on quiet strikes). 79 live strikes; on about 33 a 200-lot inside quote takes 90% or more of the score.
- Reward if every live strike were held all day: $616/day on $14,596 capital. Best 5 markets within $1,000: $63/day before fills ($900 capital).
- Tape fills at 10-90c: 7,784 contracts over 23 markets, maker -2.5c per contract on average (-$197). Makers who bought YES lost 18.6c (10-30c, error 1.9c) and 40.8c (30-70c, error 4.1c). Makers who sold YES gained 17.4c and 6.8c (error 21c).
- About 340 mid-priced contracts per market-week, against $88 of reward per market-week.
- One decisive publication per market per week can cost about $90 on a 200-lot left resting, roughly a week's reward.
Holdout: final-day window $38k TRAIN vs $3.2k TEST; outside the one knife-edge market it is $7.5k TRAIN vs $3.2k TEST. The supply shrank in the later half; no threshold was fitted.
test.artefact_checks:
1. Early-closed YES markets first produced negative final-day lags (their last candle came before the week end). Fixed by keeping only markets still open after the week end: YES n fell from 702 to 42.
2. One market (Bad Bunny Aug 23, 28M) is 80% of the TRAIN final-day supply. Reported separately rather than averaged into a per-week number.
3. The candle mean is used as the fill price. Hourly means mix trades, so the supply figures are upper bounds that count every print from both taker sides.
4. The coverage ratio compares one day of official views with a weekly max day. That biases coverage down by the max/typical ratio (about 1.1-1.3), but even corrected it stays under about 0.75, so the conclusion holds.

refs.strongest_objection:
It cannot run today, and the plan's protection does not hold.

(1) The settlement numbers are blocked for a real browser too. I loaded the YouTube Charts artist page twice in a headless Chromium (patchright) at 2:58 and 3:02 PM ET on 10-15: Taylor Swift first, then Bad Bunny after opening the weekly chart page the way a person would. Both times the call that carries 'Global daily views' came back HTTP 429 'rateLimitExceeded' and the artist page drew nothing (0 characters). The weekly chart page loaded fine. That is the tester's own day-1 gate ('if the browser gets a 429, the idea is dead') failing today. Not tried: a signed-in Chrome or a different internet address. This address took about 9 tester calls plus other agents' calls today. With no daily numbers there is no fair price, so the quoting arm would be quoting blind.

(2) Pulling quotes before the 7 PM and 11 PM ET chart posts does not protect them. On my own pull of every trade on 742 settled markets (weeks ending 9-27, 10-04 and 10-11; 48 artist-weeks), the resting side of trades at 30-70c lost 16.3c per contract:
- error 5.5c, over 50,785 contracts on 159 markets;
- 7.9c without the 3 biggest artist-weeks;
- -27.7c, -17.5c, then -1.0c week by week.
70% of that loss ($5,849 of $8,291) came outside 7-9 PM and 11 PM-1 AM ET, and losses appeared in 18 of 24 clock hours. Takers who bought the eventual winner at 70c or less took 200+ contracts within one hour in 41 markets. That is about 0.85 times per artist-week, spread over every weekday and hour, and a resting 200-lot would be first in line for those.

(3) Money. A two-sided 200-lot ties up $116-168 per market, because Kalshi holds the cash behind a resting buy (measured on this account 09-06). These markets sit on exchange 0, while the bot's money is on the Crypto shard (exchange 2), so a transfer is needed. The bet size comes from cash (bank divided by about $11.8). So the $820-900 that 5-6 markets need is 78% of the $1,155 bank, and it would cut the main bot from 98 contracts to about 22 unless the operator overrides that. Those 5-6 markets fall on only 2-3 artists (Tate McRae, Drake, and the YOU ladder). One chart update on those artists, with every quote picked off, costs -$542 to -$586, about half the main bank.

What survives: on the tape, fill losses at 30-70c come to about $11 per market-week against $88 of reward per market-week. But those losses were taken against the farmers' wide quotes. A tight quote gets hit whenever the fair price moves more than the roughly 2c fee, so its losses are not measured and are almost certainly larger. Also not measured: whether the farmers react.

Other own pulls:
- Reward programs: 244 active, each $100 per 190 h = $12.63 per market per day, target 1,000. That is $3,082/day across the series, plus $743/day on KXYTVIEWSHIGH.
- Books (2 snapshots of all 244, 4 min apart): $900 of two-sided 200-lots buys 5-6 markets on 2-3 artists. Gross reward would be $63-66/day if our share held every second, and -$542 to -$586 if all were picked off at once.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's +$10/day assumes resting fills cost about -$6/day for 5 markets (-2.5c a contract, from 7 artist-weeks of the highest-volume markets). I replayed the tester's own quote rule against the public trade tape on my own random sample of 260 settled KXYTVIEWSW markets (70 artist-weeks, Sep 13 - Oct 11). The rule: 200 a side at max(best+1c, mid-5c), refreshed every minute from the 1-minute book, pulled 6:30-8:00 PM and 10:30 PM-midnight ET, stopping at the week end. Fills cost about 1.65x the reward, not a small fraction of it: reward $4,446 vs fills -$7,331 (-18.7c a contract), net -$2,884. 41 of 70 artist-weeks lost money and all 5 weeks were negative. Per market-day quoted: +$10.32 reward (before any farmer response), -$17.01 fills, net -$6.69.

The pull schedule does not protect. Only 2 of 24 YES locks fell inside the pull windows. Fill losses are spread over all 24 ET hours (the top 3 hours hold 38%). The best extra 3-hour pull fitted on Sep 13-27 did nothing on Oct 4-11 (-$792 -> -$748). The takers are informed around the clock, which a once-a-day chart cannot follow. To break even, a chart model would have to cut adverse fills by at least 40% before competition and about 70% after the farmers respond, and a script cannot read the chart today (the tester got HTTP 429 on all 8 tries).

The replay is biased in the strategy's favour. It leaves out informed takers who would trade at our 10c-wide quote but not at the farmers' 70c-wide one, and it leaves out farmers matching our price. The most generous variant counts only trades inside the stale farmer book and drops the sweeps that would hit us first; it reaches only +$15 per artist-week (SE 9.4, not significant). The lock arm is already dead on the tester's own data.
