idea.name: Election carry book: buy the 93-97c side of races rated Solid/Safe by Cook, Sabato and Inside Elections now, exit into 99c bids after Nov 3
markets: KXHOUSERACE (154 legs asked 90-97c; 42 at 97c, 33 at 96c, 13 at 95c)
SENATE*-26 (54 legs; NC-D 0.956, GA-D 0.954 -- NH and NE at 0.90-0.91 are NOT Solid)
idea.mechanism: 1) Join the Kalshi board to the three raters' tables; keep only legs rated Solid/Safe by all three and asked <= 97c. 2) Buy at the ask (taker fee ~0.3c at 95c) or rest 1c under it, spread across >= 20 races, <= 50 contracts each. 3) After the result (Nov 4-5) sell into 99c bids to free the cash (otherwise it is locked to certification / swearing-in, Dec 2026-Jan 2027, earning 4.05% a year on positions >= $250).
idea.why_mispriced: Retail will not lock money for weeks for 3-5c; the counterparty is the lottery buyer of the 3-7c side. Politics YES buyers lose ~1.9c a contract pre-fee at all prices (Burgi/Deng/Whelan Table 8, slope n.s.).
idea.must_be_true: The Solid flip rate among legs still priced <= 97c is under ~1 per 100 (break-even 3 per 100 at 97c, 5 at 95c) -- the market may already price truly Solid seats at 98-99c and leave Likely seats in the 93-97c band, which flip several times per 100 in wave years; 99c exit bids exist on Nov 4-5; the cash does not come out of subaccount 0 (the pin bot sizes from its cash -- the SI30 objection) unless that sizing rule changes; 'sworn in' semantics (death, resignation, contested seating) stay rare.
idea.evidence_so_far: Supply on the 10-13 board: 297 legs at 90-97c, mean 4.7c to 99c, median spread 2.1c. This run (r1-revisit, U17 re-read): the general political carry (93-99c favourites 1-6 weeks out, low-touched fills only) had 0 losses in 5-9 fills per horizon at +4.3 to +5.8c a filled contract -- parked at ~$0.20/day because the population was tiny. Ratings: not retrieved (cookpolitical.com 403; 270toWin and Wikipedia tables truncated). Flip base rate: not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: One-off: ~$800 of idle cash x ~4c net = ~$30 at the current bank over ~3 weeks (about $1.5/day while held); ~$150-200 at $5,000. Each Solid upset costs ~$95 per 100 contracts; worst plausible: two upsets at 50 contracts = -$95 (at $5,000 sizing -$400).
idea.settlements_per_day: Decided Nov 3-4 (~300 legs); settles Dec 2026-Jan 2027
idea.test_plan: (1) Pull the three raters' tables (Wikipedia raw wikitext via its API, or Ballotpedia) and join to a fresh board (~30 public calls): bar >= 30 legs rated Solid by all three and asked <= 97c with >= 50 contracts at the ask. (2) Flip rate of all-three-Solid seats 2018-2024 from the same public tables: bar < 1 per 100. (3) If both pass: a 20-leg paper book to Nov 4, read on Nov 4-5 (READS_DUE); live only with sign-off and from funds that do not shrink the pin bot.
idea.prior_reason: Cheap to decide (one ratings join, outcome on Nov 4) and plausibly positive, but a one-off ~$30 at this bank whose cash competes with the pin bot, and the 93-97c band may be Likely rather than Solid seats.

idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Revives SJ51/U17 (sure-thing political carry, dead/parked) with a different population: one resolution date, ~300 independent races, an external three-rater filter, and an exit into 99c bids the day after rather than rolling 2-6 week expiries.

test.method: Ratings source: Wikipedia raw wikitext through the public API (via curl; python SSL to wikipedia fails on this box), parsed by ratings.py, which has a self-test. 2026 ratings come from the current pages (House: Cook Oct 9, IE Oct 1, Sabato Oct 8). For history, the page revision as it stood at Oct 15 16:00Z of 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024, the same 19-days-out point as today, so ratings that changed later do not leak in. Outcomes: the Result column of each final table, plus the winner of every House district from the main House pages. A House seat missing from Wikipedia's competitive table counts as Safe by every listed rater. Board: fresh public /markets pull (132 calls, 907 legs). Order books for all 73 Solid3 races with entry <= 0.975, plus 12 already-sure seats as a stand-in for exit bids (165 calls). Bot rule, fixed before any outcome was looked at: one leg per race; Cook, IE and Sabato all rate the Kalshi favourite party Safe/Solid; buy at the ask, using whichever is cheaper of the favourite's YES ask and the NO ask on the other party leg; only price levels <= 0.97; at most 13 or 50 contracts per race. Taker fee is rounded up per price level. Exit by selling into the 0.98 or 0.99 bid after the count. A structural check puts each seat on a lean scale: 2 x Cook PVI + the national margin, in points toward the favourite. 2026 uses the VoteHub generic ballot of D+8.4 (Kalshi KXVHGCB). No replay was used and no tape loss rate is quoted. Holdout: the rule has no fitted parameter. Split 2018-20 vs 2022-24: both halves show 0 losses. Scratch: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C3-04-P/ (hist_flip.py, listed_solid.py, pvi_support.py, join.py, books.py, econ.py, scen.py, RESULT.json).

test.artefact_checks: (1) The parser self-test passes. Columns mapped exactly in every table except 3 rows; each year shows 35 Senate rows and 11 or 36 governor rows. (2) The ME/VT 2018 'losses' are a labelling artefact (King and Sanders, independents who caucus with the Democrats, coloured D); counted as wins. (3) Every unlisted seat that changed party was checked by hand: redistricting/new seats (PA-4 2018; IL-3, MI-13, TX-35, TX-38 2022) or territories. (4) Not every district parsed: 2018 GA and ~13 districts in 2022. Listed seats there take their result from the ratings table's own Result column. An unlisted flip hiding in an unparsed row is possible but not observed: every known flip in those years was in the competitive table. (5) The 2026 ratings carry dates of Oct 1-9, and Cook's site returns 403, so they could not be cross-checked. If a rater has since downgraded some of the 82-90c seats, the market may be pricing news the table lacks. Re-pull on entry morning and drop any leg that moved. (6) Prices read from *_dollars fields only. (7) The 7.6/100 'market-implied' figure overstates the market's true upset belief by about 2-3/100, because the money is locked until January. (8) The lean scale is approximate, and D+8.4 is a forecast, not a result. (9) The historical ratings are the Oct 15 revisions, not final ratings, so later rater moves do not leak in. (10) No market prices were found for the 2018-2022 Solid3 seats, so 'markets under-price Solid seats' was not measured directly for those cycles. Only r2's 2024 Polymarket and Kalshi favourites (0.80-0.97, 22 of 22 and 11 of 11 won) support it.

refs.strongest_objection:
At today's bank the money does not exist. The only cash is the pin bot's, and the pin bot sizes from it: size = cash / 11.77, so 99 contracts at $1,164.96 (pinrun-live-size.json, BANK_BRAKE). Its profit grows almost one-for-one with size. 151 of its 179 filled entries this month filled 100%, and none of its 1,329 thin-book refusals would be rescued by a smaller size (all had fewer than 17 contracts offered). Taking the tester's $650-800 out for the ~21 days to settlement drops pin size from 99 to 31-43. At the pin's own Kalshi-ledger rate (+$12.0/day over 10-02..10-13, +$20.9/day over 09-24..10-15, from pinday.py) that costs about $127-271. The carry book earns +$25-52 all-win. Net: roughly -$90 to -$230. The diversion only breaks even if the pin bot's true rate is below about $2.5/day. Subaccounts 1 and 2 are also running live bots, so there is no spare money anywhere.

Second objection: the cheapest 'Solid' legs are not mispriced lottery tickets. Of the 16 Solid3 House legs under 0.90, 14 are rated Lean/Likely/Tossup by 3-6 of the 7 other forecasters on Wikipedia's 2026 ratings page (Economist, Split Ticket, DDHQ, FiftyPlusOne, Fox, Silver, RCP). Examples: NE-01 and NJ-02 at 0.82 (6 of 7 not safe; NJ-02 has a Tossup), NC-09 at 0.84 (6 of 7). The sellers agree with the quant models. The Wikipedia district pages date the Cook/IE/Sabato 'Safe' calls for NE-01 and NJ-02 to Feb-Aug 2025. The tester's lean>=6 rule still keeps several of these (NC-09, TN-09, NC-13, NC-05, AZ-08, NC-14). Its 0-of-119 history counted seats where 'at least one' other rater disagreed, not seats where most of the models did.

In the idea's favour: every 2026 leg pulled (House, MT/NC Senate, TN/NY/CA governor) is 'eligible for accelerated determination after a consensus of media organizations project the winner'. The 2025 VA and NJ governor markets closed and paid about 2 days after election day (2025-11-07 01:01Z and 03:18Z), whereas the 2024 Senate markets, which lacked that clause, waited until Jan 3. So the cash should come back about Nov 5-7 with no need for 99c exit bids. Execution is fine: resting offers, single legs, no naked legs, and the 43 ms send is irrelevant.
refs.independent_number: From my own pulls (2 board calls, 138 order-book calls, Wikipedia's 10-forecaster table): the clean book is 64 House legs with at least 13 contracts at or below 0.97. All are Safe by Cook/IE/Sabato and called not-safe by at most 2 of the other 7 forecasters. That is 37 legs safe by all 10 (mean entry 0.958, 28 R / 9 D) plus 27 more (mean 0.938, all R). At 13 a race: $793 deployed, all-win +$38.82 (4.9%), break-even 4.7 upsets per 100. At 5 a race: $310 for +$14.78. At 50 a race: $2,856 for +$144. Against that, taking $800 of main cash for 21 days costs the pin bot about $156-271, and $300 costs about $58-102 (pin at $12.0-20.9/day, size 99 to 31 or 73). At $5,000, AUTO_SIZE_MAX = 250 leaves about $2,060 of cash truly idle, so the book could run there for about +$60-120 one-off.

refs.strongest_objection: The book is one correlated bet on the national vote, not 67 independent ones: 61 of the 67 cheap legs are Republican seats in a Democratic-wave year. The history behind the 0-losses base rate never had a result that beat the October polls by 4+ points toward the wave party. Kalshi's own national House-vote market (KXHOUSEPOPVOTEMARGIN, normalised mids, 2026-10-15) gives about 13 in 100 to D+12 or more and about 4 in 100 to D+14 or more, against a median near D+8.7. In 2014, the one cycle where the result beat the polls by about 3 points, three seats rated Safe by every rater (NY-25, CA-16, MD-6) held by only 0.5, 1.4 and 1.4 points. So the losses, if they come, come together, in the cheapest legs (the 16 below 0.90 carry 42% of the all-win gain), in roughly a 1-in-8 to 1-in-25 world that a 0-in-2,800 count does not price. The upset rate for 'Safe by all AND priced <= 0.90' is not measured: no historical market prices exist for those seats. With 8 cycles and 0 bad ones, the 95% upper bound on 'a bad cycle' is about 31 per 100. Expected value is still positive under every flip assumption I tried (scenarios, not measured), so this weakens the case but does not refute it. Smaller points: $809 at 13 a leg is ~70% of the main bank, so only the ~$450 lendable plus $97 idle in subaccounts 3/4 should fund it. The tester's 'exit into 99c bids' is conservative: the rules allow accelerated settlement after a media-consensus call. Worst plausible night (D+14-type, ~4/100): about -$300 at 13 a leg and about -$1,150 at 50 a leg (scenario).

Faster bots take the best offers within 25-40 ms of the print. We only ever get what they leave, and in BTC what they leave loses money.

On 09-02..10-15 the frozen band rule gave 462 signals:

- 277 were still there at +40 ms. They won 251 of 277 (91 in 100), +5.2c a contract.

Our fastest path reaches Kalshi a median 38 ms after the print is sent (p90 61 ms); the forecaster takes about 121 ms. So we are always in the left-over group.

BTC is 23 in 100 of band fills. Its left-over lost money at every arrival delay checked: 60 fills at +75 ms, 13 lost, -4.1c a contract; -2.4c at +150 ms; -4.7c at +1 s. The 37 BTC signals the fast bots took won 35 of 37.

I could not refute it:

- The look-ahead validity filter does not inflate it. A filter that uses only ticker checks from before the window gives +10.0c. Running with no filter at all is wrong in the other direction: phantom offers from frozen feeds won 89 of 89.
- Outcomes agree across Kalshi's 'determined' message, fulltape and my computed mean.
- On 116 separate random hours of 09-02..10-14, my code and the frozen code give the same 57 fills: +9.9c (t 2.8 by close, 3.2 by day), and +9.0c at +150 ms (t 2.0).
- The jump beats a clean quiet-second control (same band and model rule, no 2-sigma print in the 5 s before) by about 8c in both separate samples. That is t 1.9 in each, about 2.7 combined, so the trigger seems to matter.

Two cautions remain. A fixed-time model-edge control at 30 or 45 s left earns +7.7c to +9.2c in Sept-Oct, so part of this edge is the forecaster's general model-vs-market edge. And the post-hoc 10-30 s slice is unstable: +14.6c on 11 unseen fills, +4.1c on 7 Sept-Oct fills, while the 46-60 s slice flips the opposite way.

idea.name: Opening-minute taker on the true book (840 s before close, take when model fair - ask - fee >= 3c), plus subscribing each 15-min window at listing so the first 2 minutes are on tape
markets: recorder change also for KXGOLD15M, KXSILVER15M, KXWTI15M, KXNATGAS15M, KXCOPPER15M and the coin race
idea.mechanism: At the CF print 840 s before close compute fair = Phi((spot - K)/(sigma*sqrt(var_factor(839)))), sigma = sd of the trailing 600 one-second increments, mu = spot (NOT tb_scan.fair_at, which is wrong beyond 60 s). If fair - yes_ask - fee per contract >= 3c send an IOC for 20 at that ask (mirror on NO) and hold to settlement. Fill = what is still offered at <= the limit 75 ms after Kalshi sends the print. Enabler: today our recorder's first book for a market arrives 31 s (p10) / 62 s (median) / 114 s (p90) after the open, so only 44 in 100 markets are visible at 840 s; a bot and the collector that subscribe to the next window's markets when they are listed see all of them from second 0 (the collector change is the operator's call: deployment is a copy to C:/kals and a restart costs up to 5 min of tape). Cap the coins fired in one close, since multi-coin fires drive both the result and the worst day.
idea.why_mispriced: At the open the book is a normal 1c-wide market whose mid wanders around the model: on holdout fills the market said 51c for our side, the model 58c, and the side won 62 times in 100. Bets toward and away from 50c were both positive, so it looks like noise in the opening quotes and early taker flow rather than a volatility bias. The other side is the first-minutes makers and takers; the R1 tape already showed takers who pay 5c+ over the model at 600-900 s lose 2.7-5.9c.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The effect is not a handful of closes (it is fragile, see evidence). (2) Our fills are not more adversely selected than the tape's book. (3) The 56 in 100 markets our recorder could not see at 840 s behave like the 44 it could. (4) Markets are listed before their open (check /markets with min_close_ts).
idea.evidence_so_far: TRUE BOOK, pre-registered (PREREG2.txt): every 3rd UTC hour 09-02..10-15 = 327 hours, 11,608 markets; rebuilt book vs ticker 99.97 in 100 (2.2M checks); results vs computed 60-s mean 1 mismatch. Rule at 840 s, 3c, 20 lots, +75 ms: HOLDOUT 09-22..10-15 +8.59c a contract after fee (2SE +/-6.1c, t 2.80; 320 fills, 202 closes); FIT 09-02..09-21 +3.18c (t 0.72; 144 fills, 93 closes) -> the pre-registered bar PASSES. Fragility: the half of the grid run second (159 unseen hours) gives holdout +4.76c (t 1.21), fit +2.08c; dropping the 10 best holdout closes +3.32c (t 1.14; pass 2 alone -1.29c); ONE EQUAL-WEIGHT BET PER CLOSE +1.85c (t 0.68, 295 closes), because multi-coin closes fire all coins the same way (45 of 62 in pass 1) -- this clustered number is the honest one (hard rule 4). Neighbouring seconds weaker: 810 s fit +5.25c / holdout +4.35c (t 1.7-2.0), 780 s +2.2 / +1.6c, first second after our book +3.1 / +3.2c, 870 s negative (n 56). Public trade tape (300 markets, 204,841 trades, first 120 s): first qualifying trade 0-30 s after the open +0.5c (t 0.07, 88 closes), 30-120 s +8.2c (t 1.6, 173 closes). Recorder gap, same 300 markets: 6,452,483 of 10,768,371 contracts (60 in 100) traded in the first 120 s before our recorder had the book; public trades start 0.4 s (p10) / 4.9 s (median) after the open; the R1 fact 'first quote appears 61-76 s after the open' was our subscription lag.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Tape upper bound at 20 lots $61/day on the holdout (only the 44 in 100 visible markets); $21/day without the 10 best closes; realistic $0-15/day at 20 lots (bank $1,155). At 98 lots the holdout tape says $216/day but the fit period $9/day: realistic $0-50/day -- a 'maybe $25/day at $5,000' idea, not proven. Worst UTC day on the tape -$63 at 20 lots; worst plausible about -$60 at 20 lots, -$250 to -$300 at 98 lots (correlated multi-coin closes).
idea.settlements_per_day: 864 markets/day; on the tape 44 fills per scanned day from the 44 in 100 visible markets; a bot subscribed from the open would see about twice that
idea.test_plan: (1) Free, now: score fresh hours with the frozen open_rep.py for 7 days; KILL if the equal-weight-per-close mean is <= 0 after 150 closes (the per-close number is the bar, not per contract); also score a one-coin-per-close variant. Add to READS_DUE. (2) Operator decision: the collector subscribes the next window at listing; after one day check first-snapshot minus open_time (bar median < 2 s) and re-run mw_open_an.py at 900-840 s on all markets. (3) Paper-log the rule inside a process subscribed at listing for 7 days (fill check at the real send time). (4) Only then a small live arm (new family -> sign-off), 5 contracts: >= 300 fills, >= +3c a contract after fee, equal-weight-per-close mean > 0, no day worse than -$15. Scripts in r2-crypto15m-midwindow-taker/ (mw_scan.py, open_rep.py, mw_open_an.py).
idea.prior_reason: Passed its pre-registered bar on the true book, has the largest upside in the batch (~$25/day at $5k) and step (1) decides it for free in a week. But the honest clustered number is weak (one bet per close +1.85c, t 0.68), the replication half is t 1.21 and pass 2 without the best closes is negative, so the chance it is real is about 1 in 4.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Follow-up of 20261015-R1-C1-11 (not-tested this run), which used only the ~1/s ticker snapshot: first true-book test, an independent replication half and a public-trade check of the first 120 s. New ledger fact: our recorder misses 60 in 100 of the contracts traded in a window's first 2 minutes (subscription lag, not an empty market) -- a silent bias in every opening-window number so far.
idea.worst_case: One close where 3-4 coins fire the same way and BTC reverses: -$40 at 20 lots, about -$200 at 98; a trending day of such closes -$250 to -$300 at 98 lots. A collector restart for the subscription change costs up to 5 minutes of tape.

test.method: I re-tested the frozen rule from PREREG2 (3) on EVERY market of the 9 coins from 09-02 to 10-15, not just the 44 in 100 our recorder could see. The rule: at 840 s before close, take either side when fair - ask - fee(20)/20 >= 3c, 20 lots, hold to settlement. Quote source is Kalshi's own 1-min candles from the public batch endpoint /markets/candlesticks?market_tickers=...&period_interval=1 (at most 10,000 market-minutes per call; 558 calls in all). The candle ending at open+60 s is the yes bid/ask at 840 s, and the one at open+120 s is 780 s. Validation: 10 of 10 spot checks matched our rebuilt true book exactly, and 4,809 of 4,892 of the hunter's true-book decisions (98 in 100) came out the same with the candle method. Fair comes from our CF index tape using the hunter's exact formula; my regex loader matched tb_scan.load_index on 32,400 of 32,400 seconds. Strike and result come from /markets; against our own 60-s mean they disagree on 44 of 34,097 markets. I wrote the pre-registration (PREREG_TEST.txt) before pulling any candle. The bar is set on FRESH: the 2 of every 3 hours the hunter never scanned (657 hours, 23,652 markets, 2,628 closes). Fit 09-02..09-21, holdout 09-22..10-15, clustered by close. Fills are assumed at the 840-s quote because candles carry no depth. On the hunter's true-book rows the +75 ms check did not hurt (+5.63c at the quote vs +6.94c at +75 ms), so that assumption is not why the rule fails. Sources: Kalshi's own quote record plus the raw index feed; no replay. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-02/: idx840.py, pull_api.py, an840.py (its self-test plants an edge and a null world: PASS).
test.n_markets: 35,784 markets scored (all 9 coins, every 15-min window 09-02..10-15 that has a candle and our index); the pre-registered FRESH sample is 23,652 markets
test.n_independent_clusters: FRESH: a bet in 1,219 of 2,628 closes (573 fit / 646 holdout). All hours: a bet in 1,842 closes.
test.result: FRESH hours, all markets, 840 s, 3c, 20 lots: FIT +0.94c a contract after fee (t 0.55, 1,027 fills, 573 closes). HOLDOUT -0.54c (t -0.34, 1,138 fills, 646 closes). One bet per close: +0.23c (t 0.19, 1,219 closes). The pre-registered bar FAILS. All hours, all markets: holdout -0.14c (t -0.11, 989 closes); one bet per close +0.72c (t 0.74, 1,842 closes). Must-be-true (3) also FAILS. On the hunter's own hours, the markets his book could NOT see lost -6.51c on the holdout (t -2.04, 161 closes), while the ones it could see made +6.01c (t 2.17, 213 closes). His +8.59c came from which markets the recorder happened to catch. The mechanism fails too: at 840 s the book's own mid predicts the outcome as well as the model or better (holdout Brier 0.2334 for the mid vs 0.2342 for the model over 12,366 markets; fit 0.23458 vs 0.23460). The YES/NO split (+4.26c vs -3.27c, opposite signs) is a trend artefact. Neighbouring settings also fail: 780 s at 3c, FRESH holdout -1.69c (t -1.39); 840 s at 5c, FRESH holdout -1.23c. One of 20 cells looked positive (780 s, 5c, FRESH, one bet per close +2.51c, t 2.07). Its per-contract holdout is only +0.60c (t 0.35), and with 20 looks the chance threshold is near t 3, so it is not a lead.
test.artefact_checks:
- Candle quote equals our true book: 10 of 10 exact, and 98 in 100 identical decisions on 4,892 markets.
- The index loader is byte-equal to the hunter's.
- Strike/result check: 44 of 34,097 mismatches (0.13 in 100), because I left out the half-unit strike rounding.
- 7 damaged gzip index hours were read up to the damage; 1,071 markets with no fair were dropped.
- The +75 ms fill check, measured on the hunter's rows, was not against us.
- This method reproduces the hunter's positive sample (+6.01c holdout on his visible markets), so the full-population null is not a method difference.
- Clustered by close; the multiple-looks threshold is stated.
- The collector is still writing tape (ticker 20261015T19 updated at 3:10 PM ET). I could not see the recorder processes in the process list, so their liveness rests on the tape writes. Free disk 118 GB; scratch folder 15 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: Supply is not the problem; there is no edge to sell into. For scale: the rule fires about 74 times a day across the 9 coins at 20 lots (3,246 bets in 44 days). Candles carry no depth. On the hunter's true book a 20-lot order filled 15.5 contracts on average. First-minute volume is large (for example about 148,000 BTC contracts in one opening minute), so plenty is offered, but it is fairly priced.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0/day. Central estimate: the full-population holdout makes -$2/day at 20 lots with fills at the quote, 2SE about +/-$41/day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0/day
test.smallest_detectable_effect: One bet per close on FRESH has an SE of about 1.2c, so a true edge of about 3.4c a contract would be found 8 times in 10. Per contract on the all-hours holdout, 2SE is +/-2.6c. The hunter's claimed +8.59c would have shown clearly, and so would his +3.18c fit. An edge under 2c cannot be ruled out, but it would not pay for the risk of 98-lot bets.
test.worst_case: Running it: the worst UTC day on the full population was -$275 at 20 lots (all 9 coins). Bets come in correlated bunches: 41 in 100 sit in closes where 3 or more coins fire together. At 98 lots that day would be about -$1,300 if the depth were there (scaled up, not measured). The collector change for subscribe-at-listing would cost up to 5 minutes of tape at restart, and this idea gives no money reason to make it.
test.next_test:
No money test; kill it. Do not start the 7-day open_rep.py watch, because this test already has about 4 times the hunter's closes. Reusable facts for the ledger:
(1) Kalshi's public batch candle endpoint /markets/candlesticks?market_tickers=A,B,...&start_ts&end_ts&period_interval=1 gives every market's top of book at each minute boundary. The limit is markets x minutes <= 10,000 per call, and a request over the limit is refused with HTTP 400. It removes the recorder-subscription bias for any opening-window question at minute resolution, with no collector change.
(2) 15-min crypto markets are created about 31 h before they open (status 'initialized'), so subscribing at listing is possible if sub-second data is ever needed. Whether the WebSocket accepts a subscription before the open was not tested.
(3) At 840 s the book mid is as well calibrated as the CF-index model, so there is no fair-value edge at the open.

idea.name: NFL player-prop maker paid by the CLIFF combo-fee rebate: re-quote at the touch from 6 h to 100 min before kickoff, hard-pull before the inactive list, and a no-quote-in-the-lineup-window rule for every prop maker
markets: rule also for soccer KX*BTTS and every eligible prop leg
idea.mechanism: Kalshi's Sports Prop Combo component-leg program ('CLIFF', help article 17184676) pays 25% of every prop combo's fees monthly as Bonus Credit to the makers of the combo's eligible legs, split by score S = prod(1+F_i) - 1, F_i = our share of that leg's maker volume. Bot: from K-6h to K-100min (K = scheduled kickoff = occurrence_datetime - 3 h, verified) keep a 20-lot bid at the YES bid and a 20-lot offer at the YES ask on NFL player-prop legs, re-quoting as the touch moves; pull everything before K-90 (NFL inactives; K-60 soccer team sheets) and hold fills to settlement. Choose series by the measured rebate per maker contract (equal split, taker-fee pool): PASSTDS 3.05c, PASSYDS 2.54c, RSHYDS 1.33c, RECYDS 1.15c, REC 0.86c, TD 0.69c (90% 0.45-0.98); x1.5 if the combo maker fee counts, x0.54-1.0 after incumbent dilution. Every sports maker decision adds this R to its net (MLB HIT 2.39c, HRR 1.55, KS 1.15, HR 0.12; NHL PTS 0.91, GOAL 0.33; soccer BTTS 1.3-5.3; NCAAF 0.24-0.47; NFL 1H/1Q 0.12-0.59; UFC MOV 0.14; tennis set winners 0.06-0.08; KXNFLFIRSTTD 0.03).
idea.why_mispriced: Nothing in the leg needs to be mispriced: the money is a subsidy out of retail parlay buyers' fees -- combo taker fees $3.09M/day, prop-combo fees $1.23-1.84M/day, CLIFF $308k/day (90% $224-436k) to $461k/day = $9.4-14.0M a month, football 70%; the six NFL prop series drew ~$1.25M/week of CLIFF on 121M maker contracts/week. On top, takers before lineup news are mostly recreational; the informed flow arrives with the inactive list, which is why the rule pulls before it.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The program is live and pays as written: volume counted in contracts not dollars, Bonus Credit usable at face value, and it reaches the subaccount that quoted (the 10-11 coin-race reward landed in main pool 0, not the posting subaccount). The API cannot confirm this. (2) Fill P&L at OUR queue position (a newcomer behind incumbents) is better than about -1.5c a contract, and a re-quoter keeps a meaningful part of the early-window average-maker edge. (3) The late-window loss is driven by news (so pulling avoids it), not noise. (4) Capital turns at least twice per slate (fills lock collateral ~5 h).
idea.evidence_so_far: Pool: 168 hourly 5-s windows of the global trade tape (10-07..10-13; 19,870 combo trades; legs looked up for 82% of combo fee). Static quote at K-90 (fills_an.py; 46 NFL games 09-24..10-13, 6 random ex-ante lines per game, 364 orders): 62% of 20-lot orders filled; gross per filled contract FRONT +0.98c (se 1.99), D200 -1.82c (se 2.74), THRU -6.38c (se 5.16); net of rebate +2.75c / -0.05c / -4.61c. Holdout week 10-07..10-13 (14 games): net FRONT +2.91c (se 3.65), D200 +4.93c (se 5.68), THRU +9.83c (se 10.4); in-sample THRU -11.07c (se 5.46). Smallest detectable effect ~6-8c (FRONT) to ~14c (THRU): it can neither confirm nor reject a +0.5c bar; BAR NOT MET. Window split (average maker over every trade, own outcomes, clustered by game): NFL K-6h..K-100min +8.33c (se 2.84, 20 games, 266k contracts) in-sample and +7.55c (se 14.90, 12 games) holdout, vs K-90..K -1.84c (se 7.75) / -13.03c (se 12.93). Soccer BTTS K-6h..K-70 -3.42c / +1.37c vs K-90..K -14.17c (se 6.9) / -5.73c (se 8.7). A STATIC quote at K-6h earns -0.34c (se 3.01, NFL, 31 games) and -3.30c soccer (70 games) because it cannot follow the touch; quotes 3-10c deeper fill 0-3%. The windows were picked after looking (post hoc) and the RE-QUOTING number is NOT measured. R table: 42 series, CLIFF from the tape sample, maker volume from volume_fp of every settled market 10-07..10-14.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not proven. Static K-90 quoter at a ~$300 sports sleeve (~3,000 contracts/week, NFL days): about -$20 to +$12/day (THRU to FRONT), of which ~$7.6/day is Bonus Credit. Re-quoter, if it kept half the +8c early-window edge on ~2,000 contracts/week: ~+$11/day plus ~$5/day CLIFF at $300; ~$50-80/day at $5,000 (~$1,500 sleeve). Could be $0. Worst plausible: sample worst kickoff day -$27.56 (FRONT) / -$32.71 (THRU) at 6 lines a game and 20 lots; a full-slate quoter 3-5x larger, -$100 to -$170 a Sunday.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~15 NFL games/week (Thu, Sun x3 slots, Mon); ~330 prop markets per game in these six series
idea.test_plan: (1) Payment check first, cheapest: ask Kalshi support (or read the Nov 1-3 statements once any sports maker has run) whether the program is live, contracts vs dollars, and which subaccount is credited. (2) A read-only WS recorder of orderbook_delta + trade on every market of the six series for two Sundays (~5,000 markets, deltas only, < 1 GB) in its own process, output folder outside kalshi_data approved by the operator; replay a re-quote-at-touch simulator with true queue position. Pre-registered bars: D200 bracket net (fill P&L + rebate) >= +0.5c per filled contract on the second Sunday with >= 3,000 contracts at 20-lot clips, AND the K-6h..K-100min re-quoter >= +1c per filled contract before rebate over >= 20 games. (3) Keep the R table current monthly (tape_pull.py + vol_pull.py, ~450 calls). Scripts in r2-sports-maker-cliff/ (fills_an.py, as_pull.py, as_an.py, cliff_an.py). Add the payment read to READS_DUE.
idea.prior_reason: The subsidy is measured and large ($9-14M a month, ~1.8c per maker contract on NFL props), it turns SJ22's -1.35c into roughly break-even, and a pre-lineup re-quoter is the plausible winner that scales to $50-80/day at $5k. Held at 3 because the bar is not met, the re-quoting edge is unmeasured and post hoc, the payment form and destination are unverified, and the test needs a new recorder and two Sundays.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: First measurement of 20261015-R1-N0-16 (not-tested) and literature row 9; ledger SJ22 (pregame NFL prop maker -1.35c) and SI30 never counted the rebate. New: the pool size, the per-series rebate table, the lineup-window split and the pull rule.
idea.worst_case: A late scratch announced before the inactive list (questionable player ruled out at K-3h) with 50 lines up on one game: -$100+; a full-slate Sunday -$100 to -$170.

test.method: I simulated a maker that re-quotes at the best price, running it over the trade tape (requote.py). It passed its self-test: hand-built fills came out right, a planted +4c world was recovered at +3.74c (se 1.16), an empty world gave -1.14c (se 1.16) and an informed-taker world gave -17.6c. The rule was fixed before I opened the fresh data. From K-6h to K-100min (K = occurrence_datetime - 3 h), rest a 20-lot sell-YES at the 1-min candle yes_ask and a 20-lot sell-NO at 100 - yes_bid. Re-post at the back of the queue whenever the best price moves or a clip fills. Cap 100 contracts per side per market and hold to settlement (settlement_value_dollars). No historical sports order-book depth exists, so queue position is bracketed: FRONT / D200 / D1000 / THRU. Speed is bracketed too: SLOW (up to 60 s behind, pick-offs counted) and FAST (dodges any 3c jump). Data: FRESH = NFL weeks 1-3, props closing before 2026-09-24, 3 random markets per series per game among those listed at least 6 h before K, never seen by the hunter. Plus the hunter's 282 markets from 09-24..10-13 (IN and HOLD). Sources: Kalshi public trade tape and 1-min candles (tape, rank 2), and the program terms from Kalshi's CFTC filing of 2026-09-02, Appendix A. Clusters are games; ratio estimator with cluster se. I also split the CLIFF pool by when each combo traded relative to its legs' kickoff, using the hunter's 168-window combo tape, and checked our CLIFF score against the program's 0.01 minimum. Read-only, about 600 public calls. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-03/ (pull.py, requote.py, analyze.py, check_hunter.py, cliff_timing.py, score.py).
test.n_markets: 858 prop markets in 6 NFL series (576 fresh + 282 hunter); 0 truncated tapes
test.n_independent_clusters: 79 games (32 fresh, 32 in-sample, 15 holdout) on 16 kickoff days
test.result:
The pre-registered bar FAILED on the fresh weeks 1-3 (32 games). Re-quoter K-6h..K-100, gross per filled contract: D200 -1.74c (se 2.68, 17,841 contracts) against a +1.0c bar; FRONT (best queue) -0.19c (se 1.91); THRU -6.40c (se 4.18). Adding the hunter's full rebate gives D200 -0.08c against a +0.5c bar. Pooled over 79 games: FRONT -1.70c (se 1.55), D200 -2.98c (se 2.20), THRU -5.37c (se 3.51). No period and no queue model has a positive centre. SLOW and FAST differ by less than 0.1c.

The hunter's +8.33c early-window edge reproduces to the cent, but it comes from a sub-selection: only markets with a quote update within 5 min before K-6h (20 of 32 games). The same window on all 32 in-sample games is -4.86c (se 7.64), and on the fresh games -4.26c (se 3.62).

Rebate: the program terms say that for a Live Event "only the maker volume traded after the scheduled start of the event is eligible", and a participant must score at least 0.01 in a combo to be paid. 29.6% of the six series' CLIFF comes from combos traded after kickoff, and a pre-game quoter gets none of that; under the strict reading it gets nothing from any combo. On the 70% traded before kickoff, our simulated score clears 0.01 on 39% (FRONT), 18% (D200) or 2% (THRU) of the pool. So the reachable rebate is about 0.12-0.27x the hunter's R (roughly 0.2-0.5c a contract), or zero.

Lose-less rule: for capped clips the lineup window is not worse. Fresh LATE K-90..K: FRONT +1.24c, D200 -1.50c, against EARLY -0.19c / -1.74c. Only the volume-weighted average maker is worse late (-12.66c se 8.59 vs -3.62c se 3.17, pooled), which hints that the big late trades are informed; not established.

Side split: buying YES at the bid made +8.87c (t 2.3) in the fresh weeks, but about -2.6c in the 47 later games, so it does not replicate.
test.artefact_checks:
- Taker side checked against the candle prices: 7,753 of 8,392 taker-YES prints were at the previous minute's ask, and 734 of 930 taker-NO prints were at the bid.
- The hunter's +8.33c was reproduced to the cent before I split it apart; it is a sub-selection artefact.
- My first analysis pass ran on 544 of the 576 fresh tapes, because my wait condition matched 'candles done' before the pull finished. I re-ran on the complete set; the final numbers are from that run and moved less than 0.4c.
- Losses are not concentrated: the 5 worst markets are 8-12% of all losses.
- Scalar payouts are handled through settlement_value_dollars.
- The window and the bars were fixed before the fresh data was opened.
- Maker fee is 0 on these series per the hunter's fee_type check; I did not re-check it.

idea.name: Nov 3 election-night guard for the crypto pin bots (19:00-03:00 ET): decide half size, or a 2-minute no-entry after a large index jump, from a loss-multiplier check at the bot's own entries
markets: other 15-min crypto up/down the pin bot trades
idea.mechanism: A scheduled-event guard: results news moves BTC in jumps the trailing-sigma model sees only after the fact. Candidate rules: (a) half bet size 19:00-03:00 ET Nov 3-4; (b) no new entry for 120 s after a 1-s index move >= k sigma that night. Decide before the night with the method that judged the R1 16:00 ET blackout: the guard pays only if the bot's loss rate per entry on such a night is at least B times its ordinary rate (B was 1.85-2.06x for that test).
idea.why_mispriced: Not a mispricing: a loss cap for the live bot on a night with known jump risk.
idea.must_be_true: Last-45-s entries on jump-heavy nights lose at >= B (~2x) the ordinary rate at the bot's own entries. Warning: the R1 16:00 ET blackout was killed because that close was only 1.46x as dangerous (90% 1.14-1.83) against B 1.85-2.06x -- a volatility-scaled model absorbs much of a scheduled event.
idea.evidence_so_far: Coinbase BTC 15-min candles, 19:00-03:00 ET: election-night mean |15-min move| 42.1 bp in 2024 vs a median of 15.9 over the 14 surrounding nights (rank 1 of 15; max 152.5 bp), 28.0 vs 16.4 in 2025 (rank 1), 28.2 vs 21.5 in 2020 (rank 3), 34.0 vs 16.1 in 2022 (rank 4, FTX-collapse week confounds). Not measured: the pin bot's own results on such a night (it has never been live on one) or the loss multiplier at its entries on high-volatility nights.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Costs about half a night's expected profit ($5-15 at current size); saves one $40-90 loss (98 contracts) if a jump lands inside a last-45-s entry. Net not measured; one night a year, so ~$0/day annualised either way; at $5k both sides scale ~4x.
idea.settlements_per_day: One night a year (~96 quarter-hour closes per coin inside the window)
idea.test_plan: Before Nov 3, read-only: reuse refute-tiebreak-20261015-R1-N0-01/tb_ana.py on the raw index at the bot's real entries: rank every night since 08-25 by 19:00-03:00 ET realised 15-min |move| and compute the loss-rate multiplier at the bot's entries on the top-5% volatility nights vs the rest (cluster bootstrap by close). Bar: multiplier lower bound >= B (~2x) -> half size that night; otherwise no guard. After the night: on the Nov 3 recording count windows whose last-45-s index move exceeded the bot's projection distance vs the previous 14 nights. Operator decides the size before the night; add the pre-night read to READS_DUE (due ~Oct 30).
idea.prior_reason: Lose-less ranks first for the operator, the night is under 3 weeks away and a free test on our own entries decides it; but it is one night a year and the closely parallel 16:00 ET blackout was refuted at 1.46x vs ~2x break-even, so the guard may well not pay.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: A different scheduled event from the covered 16:00 ET close blackout (20261015-R1-N0-01, refuted); measured from public BTC data.
idea.worst_case: With the guard: missed profit on a calm night, about -$15. Without it: a jump into one 98-lot 95c entry, about -$93.

test.method: Three sources, best first. (1) The raw index (best source): my own pass, ej_idx.py, read all 1,180 cfbenchmarks_value hour files (25 could not be read) and produced 300,012 rows (one per close, coin and seconds-left) on pinrun's own ruler: the trailing 300-s sigma and var_factor. It is the same ruler as refute-tiebreak tb_idx.py, and the row counts match at every checkpoint. That earlier pass matched Kalshi's avg_60s_data on 49,509 of 49,509 settles. Each row also records (a) the window's move BEFORE the settle minute, which is what ranks the nights, so the last 45 s being scored cannot choose its own nights, and (b) the biggest 1-s move in the last 120 s and in the last 30 s, measured against the sigma just before that move, for all moves and for moves against the favoured side. A night is the closes from 19:15 to 03:00 ET. There are 41 complete nights, 08-27 to 10-12; 10-13 and 10-14 fall in the PC-off gap. I mapped the bot's 1,470 real first non-hedge entries from pinrun-live-*.jsonl onto their own rows. The loss rate implied at those entries is the average, over entries, of the chance that the miss against the bought side at that entry's seconds-left beats its margin, with the misses drawn from the group's own rows. Bootstrap resamples whole NIGHTS. (2) Our money (third-best source): kalshi_ledger.json through pinledger.pnl, 1,541 pin 15-min markets from 08-15 to 10-15, split into the night window and the day. This gives B, the break-even multiple. (3) Past election nights (public data, rough): Coinbase BTC-USD 1-minute candles for the 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025 election nights and the 7 nights either side. For each 15-min window, the last minute's move is divided by the spread of 1-min moves over the previous 5 minutes, a 1-minute version of the bot's miss measured in its own volatility units. 2018 is dropped because most of its minutes show no price change. Holdout: data split at 09-26 00:00Z. Scripts: ej_idx.py, ej_fills.py, ej_ana.py, ej_jump.py, cb_elec.py, cb_pool.py in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-06/.
test.n_markets: Index: 300,012 rows, night windows on 41 nights, and 2,520 night markets in the bot's price zone. Our money: 1,541 pin markets (606 of them in night windows, across 40 nights). Real entries mapped: 1,470. Past election nights: 128 election-night windows vs 1,791 windows on the surrounding nights.
test.n_independent_clusters: 41 nights in total; the most-volatile groups are 3 nights and 5 nights. 435 night closes carry our money. 4 past election nights.
test.result:
THE GUARD DOES NOT PAY. For the whole Nov 3 night it is worth about -$2 to +$5.
(A) Our own tape: on the 3 most volatile nights (BTC moved 16.4-17.3 bp per window on average, 1.6-1.7x the 10.1 bp median), the bot's real entries were only 1.05x as likely to lose as on other nights (90% by night: 0.89-1.25; 0 of 600 bootstrap draws reached 2x). The top 5 nights give 1.04x (0.91-1.18) and the top 10 give 0.92x. Risk does not rise with volatility: the calmest fifth of nights is 1.03x and the wildest fifth 0.88x. Fit half 0.84x; holdout 1.52x (1 night) or 1.32x (3 nights). What the index did in the bot's zone (fair 97-99.99c) on the top 5 nights: 7 of 272 lost vs 38 of 2,248 (1.52x, from only 7 losses). Our money on those 5 nights: 57 markets, 2 lost (3.5 per 100 vs 4.0 on other nights), -$32.43.
(B) Past election nights, after scaling by volatility: the last minute moved more than 3 trailing sds in 7 of 128 windows (5.5 per 100) vs 4.1 per 100 on the nights around them, 1.32x (90% 0.56-2.26). More than 2 sds: 1.12x. More than 4 sds: 2.1x, but from 5 events (0.74-4.20). The volatility-scaled model already prices most of an election night.
(C) The bar is LOW, not ~2x, because the night window barely makes money. 19:00-03:00 ET: 606 markets, 24 lost, +$93.40 (+$0.15 a market). Day: 935 markets, +$817.56 (+$0.87). Since 09-26 nights are -$9.24 on 239 markets. Break-even multiple at night: B = 1.10x (all dates), 0.98x (since 09-26), 1.37x (since 10-04). The measured multiple (1.05 on our tape, 1.32 on the rough election check) sits right on B, and both lower bounds (0.89, 0.56) are below it. The pre-set rule was: lower bound >= B means half size, otherwise no guard. So: no guard. In money at 98 contracts (a loss ~$93, a win ~$4.2, ~12 night markets): half size changes the night's expected result by -$1.1 at 1.05x, +$5.2 at 1.32x, and +$21 only if the multiple were 2x.
(D) Rule (b), no entry for 120 s after a 1-s jump of 6 sigma or more: dead. Index multiple 1.01 (fit) / 1.04 (holdout). It would have refused 586 of our entries, which lost 21 times and still netted +$327, so refusing them would have cost about $327 over 61 days.
SIDE FINDING (found in a scan of 32 cells, not set in advance): entries made within 30 s after a 1-s move of 6 sigma or more AGAINST the bought side. 85 entries, 7 lost in 7 different closes (8.2 per 100 vs 2.7), -$159.63, while the other 1,385 entries made +$1,159.22. Fit half: 51 entries, 2 lost, +$22.58. Holdout: 34 entries, 5 lost, -$182.21. The index population shows no steady excess (0.84x fit, 1.78x holdout), so if this is real, it is about who sells to us right after a jump.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Nights are ranked by the move before the settle minute, so the scored last-45-s miss cannot pick its own nights. (2) Ranking the nights after the fact flatters the guard; even so the multiple is ~1.05. (3) The bootstrap resamples nights, not closes, because 3-5 top nights is the true sample size. (4) Our tape only holds nights up to 1.72x the median volatility. Election night 2024 was 2.70x its own median and about 4x our tape's median in bp. That range is NOT measured on our ruler; the Coinbase check is the only evidence there, and it is rough (1-minute data, one exchange, no 60-s average). (5) On 321 of 1,470 entries, the 1/sec ruler calls the bought side the underdog (same as in the 16:00 tiebreak). It hits both groups equally, so the ratios stand. (6) The B of 25.99 printed for non-top nights since 10-04 comes from two $1.55 losses and is not used. (7) Coinbase 2018 is excluded: its typical move is 0.02-0.03 sds, meaning most minutes had no price change. (8) The side finding is one of 32 cells looked at, and its fit half shows nothing. No loss rate here is called ours unless it comes from the ledger. The recorders' cfbenchmarks_value, ticker, trade and orderbook_delta files were written within 1 s of the check at 15:19 ET. Free disk 118 GB. No process touched; 0 Kalshi API calls.
test.supply_we_would_get: This is not a supply question: the guard only removes or halves our own entries. About 11-15 pin markets fall in the 19:00-03:00 ET window each night (606 over 40 nights; 11.0 per night since 10-04). Rule (b) would have removed 586 of 1,470 entries (40%).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0. It applies to one night a year. Half size on Nov 3 changes that night's expected result by about -$1 to +$5 at 98 contracts: -$1.1 at the measured 1.05x, +$5.2 at the rough 1.32x. Rule (b) would lose about $5 a day (-$327 over 61 days).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0. At $5,000 the night's swing grows ~4.3x, to about -$5 to +$22.
test.worst_case: Without a guard: one loss at 98 contracts costs about $93; two losses (after which the --max-losses 2 brake stops new entries) about $186. With half size: about $47 and $93. Half size on a calm night gives up a few dollars of profit: about $25 of win money, roughly $1 net of the losses it also halves.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Our tape's nights: the 90% band is 0.91-1.18 on 5 nights, so a multiple of about 1.2x or more can be told apart from 1, but only for nights up to 1.7x the median volatility; nothing more volatile is in the tape. Past election nights (128 windows): this can only rule out a multiple of about 2.3x or more at 3 sds. Our money on the top nights (57 markets): only a multiple of about 4x or more would show.
test.next_test: (1) No guard is needed before the night on money grounds. Half size on Nov 3, 19:00-03:00 ET, is purely the operator's risk choice: it costs about $1 in expectation and halves the worst loss. (2) READS_DUE (for the writer agent): a pre-night re-read due 2026-10-30. Re-run ej_idx.py and ej_ana.py with two more weeks of data. Bar: if the lower bound of the multiple on the most volatile nights is at least the night B (now ~1.0-1.4), recommend half size; otherwise no guard. A post-night read due 2026-11-04: the same scripts with the group set to the 2026-11-03 night against the previous 14. Record the multiple, the night's volatility ratio and our ledger P&L that night, so 2028 has a real election-night number on our own ruler. (3) The side finding becomes a paper flag, not a gate. On every live entry, log ja30: the largest 1-s move against the bought side in the last 30 s, divided by the sigma just before it. Threshold set now: k = 6. Read after 60 flagged entries. Bar: in the new data only, flagged entries lose at least 2x as often as unflagged AND the flagged entries net below zero. (4) The night window's weakness needs its own forward test before any night-wide size cut: +$0.15 vs +$0.87 a market; 3.96 vs 2.89 losses per 100, which could easily be chance (p ~0.2). idea.name: NBA player-prop CLIFF maker from the Oct 21 tip-off: pre-registered rebate and fill measurement on week 1, pull before injury news
idea.mechanism: M-03's quoter (re-quote at the touch, 20 lots a side) on NBA player props, collecting the CLIFF rebate (25% of prop-combo fees, split by S = prod(1+F_i) - 1); pull 60 min before tip because NBA injury news lands 30-60 min before. The 82-game season with ~10 games a night is the repeating-market shape the pin bot likes.
idea.why_mispriced: A subsidy, not a mispricing: combo buyers parlay NBA player points heavily; if the leg books stay thin relative to that combo flow, the rebate per maker contract is large (WNBA analogue 4.5c).
idea.must_be_true: (1) NBA leg volume does not grow in step with combo fees. (2) Fill P&L at our queue position >= -2c a contract. (3) The program is live and pays this account (same unknowns as M-03).
idea.evidence_so_far: KXWNBAPTS (WNBA finals week 10-07..10-13, 4 games): CLIFF $26,429/week on 585,546 maker contracts = 4.51c a contract (90% 2.26-7.12; 111 sampled combos). NBA props are not listed yet (the collection holds only game lines). NBA fill P&L not measured. The R1 sports lane flagged NBA as the biggest preseason taker loss. Every other prop-maker fill measured this round is flat to negative (NFL FRONT +0.98c se 1.99; soccer BTTS -1.6c; TDPROT -13.8c).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown until measured. If R ~2-4c and fill P&L ~0: ~$8-15/day at a $300 sleeve (NBA plays nightly), ~$40-75/day at $5,000. Worst plausible: a star scratch after quotes are up, -$50 to -$150 a night at a full slate.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~10-12 NBA games a night from Oct 21 (1,230-game season); ~100+ prop markets a game
idea.test_plan: Oct 28: rerun tape_pull.py (START=2026,10,21, 168 h, ~330 calls), vol_pull.py on the NBA eligible series, and as_pull.py; verify the NBA occurrence_datetime offset against the ESPN schedule first. Pre-registered bar: R >= 1.5c on KXNBAPTS AND FRONT >= 0c AND D200 >= -1.5c gross over >= 40 games, with the second week as holdout. Live only after M-03's payment check confirms the credit. Add READS_DUE 2026-10-28.
idea.prior_reason: Nightly repetition and a measured 4.5c WNBA rebate make it the best CLIFF venue on paper, and a ~330-call read decides the rebate half by Oct 28; but no NBA fill number exists and every other prop-maker fill measured is flat to negative.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New: the NBA regular season was never measured; SJ22/SI30 (dead prop makers) had no rebate.
idea.worst_case: A star scratch after quotes are up: -$50 to -$150 a night at a full slate.
merged_from: r2:sports-maker-cliff: NBA player-prop CLIFF maker from the Oct 21 tip-off (pre-registered measurement)

test.method:
NBA regular-season player props are not listed yet. KXNBAPTS has only 24 settled markets, on 3 preseason games. KXNBAREB/AST/3PT/PRA/BLK/STL have no markets at all, and NBA props drew $0 of CLIFF in the 10-07..10-13 sample. So I measured the closest live analogue: WNBA 2026 player props (KXWNBAPTS/REB/AST/3PT). That is 5,686 settled markets on 105 games, 08-01..10-13, all quadratic x1 with no maker fee. Sources are the trade tape plus Kalshi settlement values; no replay was used.

(1) Clock: K = occurrence_datetime - 3 h. This matched the ESPN scheduled tip on 16 of 16 games (13 WNBA, 3 NBA preseason).

(2) Fill P&L: I reused the lane's as_pull.py and drew one seeded random line per game per series, listed at least 2 h before tip. That gave 416 markets with full tapes K-6h..K (0 truncated) plus 1-minute batch candles. Scoring used fills_an.fill (self-test PASS) in a new as_an_w.py. The quote is 20 lots a side: sell YES at the yes_ask, buy YES at the yes_bid. Windows: quote K-90 and pull at tip (the bar cell); quote K-180 or K-120 and pull K-60 (the idea's pull-before-news rule); K-360 to K-60; K-180 to tip. Queue brackets are FRONT, D200 and THRU. Payout comes from settlement_value_dollars, so did-not-play settles are handled. Clusters are games. In-sample is the regular season (tip before 09-01); holdout is 09-01..10-14 (late season and playoffs).

(3) Rebate: I ran the lane's tape_pull.py and cliff_an.py (self-test PASS, unchanged) on a new regular-season week: 168 hourly 5-second windows of the global tape, 08-10..08-16, lookup cover 0.99, 523 sampled combos carrying a WNBA leg. Dividing by the volume of every WNBA prop market settled that week gives R per maker contract, compared with the lane's finals-week figure.

About 880 public GETs, no auth. Files are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-08/ (as_an_w.py, as_an_wnba.out, p7_raug.out, p8_days.out, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 416 sampled WNBA prop markets (of 5,686 listed) scored for fills. 2,213 WNBA prop markets in the rebate week. NBA regular season: 0 (not listed until Oct 21).
test.n_independent_clusters: 94 games over 37 nights in the K-90 FRONT cell: 56 in-sample, 38 holdout. Rebate: 7 days, with 88 of 168 windows containing a WNBA points leg.
test.result:
REBATE. In a regular-season WNBA week (about 6 games a night) the CLIFF per maker contract is:
- PTS 1.79c (90% 1.31-2.28)
- REB 2.24c (1.46-3.07)
- AST 0.54c (0.18-0.96)
- 3PT 1.20c (0.79-1.68)
- Fill-weighted about 1.4c from the taker-fee pool, or about 2.1c if the combo maker fee (started 08-20) also counts.

The 4.51c the idea rests on came from finals week: one game a night, 111 sampled combos. In the regular season, points-leg volume was 3x higher (1.82M vs 0.59M contracts a week) while the pool attributed to it grew only 24% ($32.7k vs $26.4k a week). A full nightly NBA slate should therefore be expected near 1-2c, not 4.5c.

FILLS (gross, per filled contract, clustered by game):
- Quote K-90, pull at tip: FRONT -0.97c (se 2.06; 94 games, 5,175 contracts; 48% of orders filled), D200 -1.31c (se 3.21), THRU -1.01c (se 3.71).
- The two halves disagree by 8c (about 1.9 se): in-sample (Aug) FRONT -4.19c (se 2.38), D200 -4.77c; holdout (Sep-Oct) FRONT +3.77c (se 3.49), D200 +3.30c.
- The idea's pull-at-K-60 rule (quote K-180, pull K-60): FRONT -1.19c (se 2.79), D200 -1.77c (se 4.32). Fills fall to 37%, and only 10.1% of a prop's lifetime volume trades in that window (22.9% trades in K-90..K, 41.5% in K-6h..K, about 58% in-play).
- Early static quote (K-360, pull K-60): FRONT -4.93c (se 2.50), D200 -10.27c (se 3.38). Stale resting quotes get picked off, so a bot must re-quote; a re-quoting maker is not measured.

NET with the regular-season rebate: K-90 FRONT +0.43c (se 2.06), D200 +0.10c (se 3.22), THRU +0.47c (se 3.72); K-180..K-60 FRONT +0.11c (se 2.79).

Against the idea's own bar (R >= 1.5c on PTS, FRONT >= 0c, D200 >= -1.5c), the analogue lands on a coin flip:
- R passes narrowly (1.79c).
- FRONT fails narrowly (-0.97c).
- D200 passes narrowly (-1.31c).
- None of these is significant.
test.artefact_checks:
- **Tip clock:** K = occ - 3 h verified on 16 of 16 ESPN games. A wrong K would mislabel in-play fills as pre-game.
- **Tapes:** 0 of 416 truncated.
- **Did-not-play markets:** 161 of 5,686 (2.8%) settle at Kalshi's 'fair price' (example: 0.24 against a last trade of 0.23), not 0 or 1. The settlement value is used, so they are scored correctly.
- **Self-tests:** fills_an and cliff_an both PASS.
- **Rebate window:** legs closing 08-10 00:00..08-17 06:00, matching the lane's 7.25-day scale-up. Starting the window at 08-10 06:00 instead gives PTS 1.82c after correcting the day count, so the figure is robust.
- **Maker-fee case:** the 'hi' case is counterfactual for August (the combo maker fee began 08-20), so 'lo' is the measured August figure.
- **Program status:** the rebate formula was applied to August flow. Whether the program existed or paid then is unknown, so this is what the formula would pay, as in the lane.
- **Not measured:** anything NBA (not listed), a re-quoting maker, true queue position, whether CLIFF pays this account, and whether 'maker volume' counts contracts or dollars.
- **Ops:**
  - Recorders are not visible by command-line match and were not touched; kalshi_data/trade/20261015T19 was being written at 19:30Z.
  - 117.9 GB free; scratch folder 4.7 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get:
WNBA analogue: about 52 lines per game are listed at least 2 h before tip. A 20-lot touch quote on both sides of every line at K-90 fills about 8.5 contracts per order (FRONT) or 4.2 (THRU). That is about 900 / 460 maker contracts per game, or about 1,830 / 940 per WNBA night.

NBA (about 10 games a night from Oct 21) would be several times that if lines are listed the same way; not measured.

At our size, capital binds before supply does. Each filled contract locks about 40-60c until the game settles about 3 h after tip, so money turns over once a night and a $300 sleeve holds about 600 contracts a night.

The fills are on the prop leg books (KXNBAPTS etc.). The rebate is paid out of combo buyers' fees (KXMVECROSSCATEGORY).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About +$2 a day central at a $300 sleeve (about 600 filled contracts a night at +0.4c), with roughly +/-$12 a night of noise, so it cannot be told apart from $0. If CLIFF does not pay this account, it is about -$6 a night (-0.97c x 600).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About +$10-15 a day central at a ~$1,500 sleeve (about 3,000 contracts a night), with the same sign uncertainty (+/-$60 a night).
test.smallest_detectable_effect: With se 2.06c per contract on 94 games, the smallest effect this sample can detect at 80% power is about 5.8c. Confirming a +1c edge needs se of about 0.36c, roughly 30 times this sample. The first NBA week (about 60-70 games) can therefore only kill the idea (a fill result of -4c or worse, or R below 1c); it cannot confirm it.
test.worst_case:
Scaled from the WNBA sample with 20 lots on every line (about $900 of collateral a night), the worst nights net of rebate were -$300 to -$560. At a $300 sleeve that is about -$100 to -$190 a night.

A star scratch is less dangerous than the idea assumed. A player who never takes the court settles at a Kalshi 'fair price', not 0 (161 WNBA lines did). The tail comes from ordinary outcomes across many correlated lines on the same player.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's +$2/day credits every maker contract filled BEFORE tip-off with the CLIFF rebate, but Kalshi's own filed terms say otherwise. The CFTC self-certification of 2026-09-02 (Appendix A section 4) and help article 17184676 both say: 'where a given market ... is considered a Live Event, only the maker volume traded after the scheduled start of the event is eligible'. The idea quotes only before tip and pulls 60 min before tip, so it is built on exactly the volume that clause excludes.

- **Literal reading (every game is a Live Event):** the rebate is zero. Net is the bare fill result, about -1c per contract, or about -$6 to -$7 a night at a $300 sleeve.
- **Narrow reading (only combos traded after tip pay only after-tip makers):** the pre-tip quoter still loses those combos' share of the pool. My own sample puts that share at up to about 24%.

Three execution cuts come on top:
- **Queue:** on 133 live prop books, the median resting size at the touch is 669 contracts, and 69% of touches have 200 or more ahead. With a 1-2c spread there is no room to improve the price, so a 20-lot cannot be first in the queue (FRONT). The realistic gross numbers are the tester's D200 -1.31c and THRU -1.01c.
- **Bigger NBA lines:** at 3x to 10x WNBA line volume, the 0.01 minimum score cuts the pre-tip rebate to 0.71x and 0.48x.
- **Big makers on every leg:** a professional maker quoting all legs collects the product bonus, which dilutes our share to 0.63x-0.90x.

Under the narrow reading, net is -0.1c to -0.8c per contract (central about -0.4c, or -$2.5 a night). Under the literal reading it is about -1.2c, or -$7 a night. The best case is about +$1 a night, and it needs the narrow reading, a FRONT queue position and lines no bigger than WNBA's.

The filing also ends the program by Jan 1 2027 at the latest. That covers about 10 NBA weeks, not the 82-game season, and the rebate is paid monthly in arrears as trade credit.

What would revive it: Kalshi confirms the narrow reading in writing, AND the tester's free Oct 28 NBA read shows D200 gross >= +0.5c over at least 40 games.

refs.strongest_objection:
The verdict holds, but its evidence is wrong in both directions.

(1) The rebate is overstated. The lane's R (cliff_an.py line 75, reused unchanged by the tester) splits 25% of each combo's fee over its eligible legs only. The CFTC filing (Appendix A 5.B.ii) scales each combo's pool by eligible/total legs. The live-event clause also gives combos traded after tip only to post-tip maker volume, which a quoter who pulls at tip never has. On my own fresh week (08-17..08-23, 168 hourly windows, 279 combos carrying a WNBA prop leg):
- eligible-leg scaling x0.75 (90% 0.70-0.78)
- pre-game share x0.83 (0.76-0.89)
- together x0.62, so the tester's 1.4c fill-weighted R becomes about 0.9c.
The same correction gives 1.4c in my week, because R itself swings about 1.6x week to week. The 0.01 minimum score then keeps only 9-83% of that for a small sleeve quoting ~5% of lines, depending on fill size (unresolved).

(2) 'NBA props not listed, fills unmeasurable until Oct 28' is false. /historical/markets serves 23,562 KXNBAPTS markets from the 2025-26 season (1,097 games), with /historical/trades and /historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks. NBA can be measured now, and it came out better than the WNBA stand-in, not worse.

(3) Capital is overstated. Resting 20-lot quotes on both sides lock about $18-20 per line. A $300 sleeve rests about 16 lines, about 210-280 filled contracts a night, not 600.

refs.strongest_objection:
Under Kalshi's own filed rules, quoting before tip earns no CLIFF rebate. The tester's +$2/day depends entirely on that rebate (+1.4c a contract covering -0.97c of fill losses), so the idea as specified pays $0 of rebate.

**The rule.** The Sep 2 2026 filing modifies the Aug 11 2026 FOOTBALLSTATS program. I pulled all three Aug 11 versions from cftc.gov (rules08122616003, 08122616002 and 08112615711; the clause is identical in each). They say a participant's score uses "the total maker volume in that market (in the case of a market with a 'live event' such as a sports game, only volume after the scheduled start of that event is considered)".
- A sports game is the filing's own example of a live event.
- The Sep 2 text and help article 17184676 keep the same rule: "For Live Events, only maker volume traded after the scheduled start of the event is eligible", where a Live Event is "an event, such as a sports game ... already started".
- So the "narrow reading" (only combos traded during the game are affected), which the stats skeptic used and the execution skeptic allowed, has no support in the original wording.
- M-08 quotes only before tip and pulls at K-60 (60 minutes before tip). All of its maker volume is the excluded kind.

**A second, separate overstatement.** The lane's cliff_an.py computes `series_cliff[s] += 0.25 * fe / len(el)`. That splits the pool over eligible legs only and never applies the eligible-to-total legs scaling the filing requires (Appendix A 5.B.ii). The stats skeptic measured that factor at x0.75.

**Ruling between the skeptics.** The execution skeptic is right on the decisive point. The stats skeptic is right that NBA history can be measured now. My own NBA sample confirms the fill result is noise:
- Settlement-based P&L, same population as the stats skeptic but a different random sample: my THRU (fill only when the price trades through my quote) is -6.52c (se 5.67). The stats skeptic's is +2.44c (se 4.97).
- Opposite signs, both consistent with zero.

**What is left is a different idea, not M-08.** Plain pregame NBA prop making with no rebate:
- Markout to the price at tip at a realistic queue is +1.2 to +1.5c, but only +0.4 to +0.6c in Feb-Apr.
- Settlement-based P&L at a realistic queue is negative central (-1.3c to -6.5c, se 5-6c).
- 2025-26 books had a median 5c spread at tip. The 2026-27 books may be tighter.

The CLIFF money goes only to makers quoting during the game. That is a separate and much harder idea at our 43 ms speed, and it was not measured.

**Revive M-08 only if** Kalshi says in writing that maker volume traded before the scheduled start counts, or a monthly Bonus Credit statement shows credit on it.

idea.name: Brazil runoff count night (Oct 25): fade the early-count Flavio share/margin rungs and buy the Lula share rungs off the measured TSE drift curve (winner-market trailer and Polymarket lead-lag as paper side-scores)
idea.mechanism: 1) Poll the TSE partials (percent of sections counted f, each candidate's share) every 30 s from poll close (16:00 ET Oct 25). 2) Project Flavio's final share = running share + k x D1(f), D1 = the measured 2026 first-round drift (f=12%: -4.1 pts, 47%: -3.2, 65%: -2.6, 85%: -1.4, 92%: -0.8), k in [0.5, 1.0]. 3) While f is 5-60%, buy NO on Flavio >= X rungs whose X sits >= 0.5 pt above the top of the projection band and buy YES on Lula >= Y rungs >= 0.5 pt below the bottom of Lula's band, only at prices >= 5c better than the band-implied price. 4) Hold to the certified-result settlement. Rules pre-registered in BRAZIL_RUNOFF_PREREG.md. Winner side-score (paper): projected margin = running Flavio-minus-Lula margin + 0.5 x M1(f) (M1: f=12% -8.5, 47% -6.7, 65% -5.5, 85% -3.1, 92% -1.8); 'buy' Lula only if the projection is <= +1.0 pt for Flavio and Lula's ask <= 15c. Lead-lag side-score: Polymarket's same question vs Kalshi at seconds resolution.
idea.why_mispriced: Takers price the running total, but Brazil's count order is systematic: Northeast and late-transmitting sections break for the PT candidate, so the non-PT candidate's early share is inflated in every measured round. On Oct 4 Kalshi takers bought 15,672 'anyone wins outright' YES at 8-27c between 16:40 and 17:30 ET while Flavio's running share was 50-51% with ~12% counted; drift arithmetic put that near zero and it settled NO. Flavio >= 50% YES traded 20-29c (993 contracts, lost); Lula >= 45% was sold down to 6-50c while Lula sat at 41.6-44.2% and settled YES at 45.16%. In the winner market Flavio printed 94-96c at 47% counted with a +8.6 lead, while the drift said +1.9 (final +1.87), i.e. ~75-80%.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The runoff count repeats the drift DIRECTION (3 of 3 measured rounds: 2022 R1 -4.8 pts from ~15% counted, 2022 R2 -2.2 from ~25%, 2026 R1 -4.1 from 12.45%) with a magnitude inside k = 0.5-1.0; a two-candidate runoff can drift less (2022 R2 about half of R1). (2) The R2 ladders carry wrong-side taker flow (R1 ladders were thin: 461-993 contracts a rung on the wrong side; the outright market had 15.7k). (3) For the winner trailer, the crowd prices the running total -- against it, the market already knows the 2022 'virada' and on Oct 4 the 95c Flavio was right.
idea.evidence_so_far: Measured: Kalshi R1 tape (Oct 4: 1-min candles for 15 markets, 4,218 trades on 7 markets) and TSE partials from news (12.45% at 18:00 BRT Flavio 51.09 / Lula 40.71; 47.26% at 18:44 50.20 / 41.63; 64.81% 49.58 / 42.25; 84.96% 48.47 / 43.49; 92.48% at 20:40 47.85 / 44.19; final 47.03 / 45.16): the last 15% of sections broke Lula by 11-20 pts. Structural ladder checks that night: 0 violations after fees in 1,265 quoted minute-pairs. Today's R2 board: Flavio >= 52% 0.64/0.66, >= 53% 0.36/0.38, >= 55% 0.06/0.10; MOV Flavio 3-6% 0.43/0.47. KXBRPRES books (10-15): 2,722-35,039 contracts a level within 4c of the touch (Lula YES bid 0.18 x 109,533). Winner trailer on R1: fired at 17:31 ET (Flavio 92c), Lula ~9c, lost (-10.5c a contract with slippage). Polymarket led Kalshi by ~1 minute on R1 (corr 0.33 at a 1-min lag vs 0.28 same minute, 0.17 the other way); levels within 1-3c all night (21:00Z Poly 0.852 / Kalshi mid 0.865) vs a 1.0-1.2c taker fee -- ~$0. n = 1 Kalshi night.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: One night: about +$30-75 at the current bank (100-300 contracts across 2-3 rungs at a 15-25c average edge if R1 repeats); $100-300 at $5k; annualised ~$0.1-0.8/day, since the shape recurs on Latin American count nights a few times a year. Winner trailer (paper): 300 at 15c = $45 at risk, EV not measurable from one night. Lead-lag ~$0.
idea.settlements_per_day: One night (Oct 25); recurs on Brazilian/Latin American count nights a few times a year
idea.test_plan: Paper exactly per BRAZIL_RUNOFF_PREREG.md (written 2026-10-15, before the night). Recorder: elecnight_record.py (r2-election-night-count-order/; selftest passes) at 5-s top of book of KXBRPRES, KXVOTEBR2, KXBRPRES2MOV, KXBRPRES2MOVD, KXBRRUNOFFSTATES, KXBRPRES2STATEMOVD plus exchange-wide trades every 10 s and TSE partials every 30 s, 15:00-23:59 ET Oct 25 -- this is also the Nov 3 rehearsal; the operator approves an output folder outside kalshi_data (e.g. C:/kals/elec_data) and no other unauthenticated job runs that night (dry run: 2 HTTP 429 in 49 calls with other agents on the IP). Record Polymarket's book alongside for the lead-lag score. Score Oct 26 on settlement. Bar to go live on a later count night: >= +5c a contract net over >= 3 rungs with no rung worse than -50c; for the winner trailer, report whether the projection band contained the final margin at f = 12/25/50/75%. Any live order needs sign-off. Add READS_DUE 2026-10-26.
idea.prior_reason: High chance the drift direction repeats (3 of 3 rounds) and Oct 4's own Kalshi tape shows takers paying for the running total; decided in 10 days on paper for free and it rehearses the Nov 3 recorder. But it is one night, wrong-side ladder flow was thin (461-993 contracts a rung) and the runoff drift may be half of R1's.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Ledger SI35 (needs-data) and U27 (the Oct 4 recording was never made); SJ11 killed a reveal desk on 'siblings lag', not on count order; SJ46 killed settled-question cross-venue arbitrage, not a count-night lead-lag. First measurement of the Brazil drift against Kalshi's own count-night tape; targets share/threshold rungs (near-certain direction) instead of the winner.
idea.worst_case: The drift fails (Flavio's share holds): faded rungs settle YES at about -80c a contract, -$240 at 300 contracts; cap the night at $200 at risk.

test.method: Data, best source first: the Kalshi trade tape and 1-minute candles of the settled first-round count night (Oct 4 2026, 20:00Z-06:00Z). I pulled 18 Flavio/Lula KXVOTEBR1 share rungs fresh (C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-07/f1_fetch.py, 112 unauthenticated GETs, no HTTP 429s) and added the hunter's outright KXBRAZILPRES1R tape. TSE partials come from news: the opovo live blog gives 13 timestamped national partials from 1.23% to 92.48% counted; the 2022 runoff gives 25% counted 51.26, 67.76% 49.99, 85.98% 49.57, 99.5% 49.13, final 49.10. No replay was used, and we have no fills of our own on this market. HOLDOUT: the drift prior is fitted ONLY on the 2022 runoff curve and then replayed on the 2026 first-round night, which it never saw. Two comparisons run alongside: the hunter's own 2026 first-round curve (D1, in-sample) and a zero-drift control. The rule runs as a bot would: it acts on the last TSE partial already published (no look-ahead), trades only while 5-60% is counted, fades Flavio rungs X >= run - d + 0.5, buys Lula rungs Y <= run + d - 0.5, takes model fair = Phi((run - d - X)/1 pt), trades only 5c better than fair, 100 contracts a rung, and pays the taker fee 0.07P(1-P). Taker form: a1_r1_holdout.py. Maker form: a2_r1_maker.py, which rests quotes at fair +/- 5c, fills them from wrong-side takers on the tape at our price, and assumes we are first in queue (an upper bound). a3_sibling_gap.py compares every FBOL-50 taker print with the near-identical deep outright market in the same minute. I also backed the market-implied drift out of the outright mid. Current runoff board: order books, rules and fee type of all 41 KXVOTEBR2 / KXBRPRES2MOV / KXBRPRES2MOVD rungs (r2_books.txt).
test.n_markets: 19 first-round markets replayed (18 share rungs plus the outright); order books of 41 runoff rungs; drift history from 3 count nights (2022 R1, 2022 R2, 2026 R1)
test.n_independent_clusters: 1. It is one Kalshi count night, and every rung settles on the same TSE number. The drift direction repeated in 3 of 3 rounds, but only 1 of those was a runoff.
test.result: (1) TAKER rule on R1 with the 2022-runoff drift (holdout): 0 fires at k = 1.0, 0.5 and 0, so $0. The fade rungs had no YES bid all night (FBOL-50 bid was $0.00 from 17:21 to 01:18 ET), so there was no way to buy NO. The Lula low rungs were offered above the conservative fair. In-sample D1 at k=1.0 fires once: LULA-42 YES at 94c, +5.6c on 100 contracts = +$5.60. (2) MAKER form on R1, holdout drift: 3 rungs, 300 contracts, +$33.01 (11.0c a contract: FBOL-50 +$18.79, FBOL-52 +$5.05, outright +$9.18), assuming we are first in queue. Half the drift: +$5.54 on 1 rung. The ZERO-drift control also made +$8.59 (FBOL-52), so part of the profit needs no drift model at all. In-sample D1: +$40.60 at k=0.5, +$15.32 at k=1.0. (3) Where R1's profit came from: 993 of the 1,044 YES contracts takers bought on FBOL-50 (Flavio >= 50%) paid on average 20.9c MORE than the near-identical deep outright market (Flavio > 50%) was asking in the same minute. Example: 431 contracts at 22c at 18:57 ET while the outright asked 1c. That is a stale thin rung lagging its deep sibling, not an insight from count order. (4) The deep market did NOT price the running total. At 12.45% counted, with Flavio at 51.09% running, the outright YES mid was 12c; pricing the running total would have meant ~80c or more. The remaining drift implied by the outright mid was 1.7-2.6 pts at 5-48% counted assuming a 1-pt spread (3.0-4.6 assuming a 2-pt spread), against a true 3.2-4.2 and a 2022-runoff 1.5-2.2. So the crowd had already priced in at least the 2022-runoff drift. (5) At the same stage of the count, the runoff drift was much smaller than the first-round drift: the 2022 runoff moved 2.16 pts from 25% counted and 0.89 from 67.8%, while the 2026 first round, as a two-candidate share, moved 4.57 from 22% and 2.98 from 64.8% (2022 first round about 2.85 from 70%). That is 0.3-0.5x. The pre-registered band floor (0.5 x D1 = 1.25 pts at 68%) sits ABOVE the only runoff ever measured (0.89). The first-round curve D1 is also in all-valid-vote units, while the runoff rungs are two-candidate shares; the first round's two-candidate drift was 4.64, not 4.06, at 12.45%. (6) Runoff books today: 200-5,000 contracts within 3c of each touch, spreads 2-10c (FBOL-50 0.82/0.91, FBOL-54 0.15/0.24), 0-1,500 contracts a rung traded in the last 24 h. Wrong-side flow on the first-round share rungs over the whole count night was 0-1,044 contracts a rung (FBOL-50 1,044, FBOL-56 655, FBOL-52 595, LULA-45 618, LULA-44 456).
test.artefact_checks: Look-ahead: decisions use the last TSE partial already published (a step function, not interpolation). The partials' times are news-blog stamps accurate to a few minutes, so fills are timed to the minute at best. Holdout: the drift prior never touched 2026 R1, and the D1 runs are labelled in-sample. The zero-drift control also made money (+$8.59), and that is how the stale-thin-rung effect was found; its scale was confirmed by a3. Units: prices read from *_dollars fields, shares in percentage points. Rule text checked: settlement is the certified TSE share of valid votes to 2 decimals; R1 settled 2026-10-05 22:52Z, the next day. Fees: the series charges takers 0.07P(1-P) (multiplier 1). Maker fills are an UPPER bound: first in queue, filled at our price, no lag in repricing, no losses to people polling TSE faster than us. Loosening the margin cannot rescue the taker form on the fade rungs, because there was no YES bid to sell into. Not measured: the runoff night itself, the runoff drift, depth on the R1 ladders (candles carry only the best price), and the Polymarket lead-lag (the hunter's ~1-minute, correlation-0.33 result was not re-run).
test.supply_we_would_get: Taker: about 0 on the fade rungs; on R1 nobody bid on the side we would need to sell into. The only place with taker size is the deep winner market KXBRPRES (2.7k-110k contracts a level). It is the X=50 rung, and the matching deep R1 market already priced the drift. Maker: R1 wrong-side takers trading at prices that met the rule came to 171-179 contracts each on FBOL-50/52 and 6-18k on the outright. The outright has no runoff twin; the nearest is KXBRPRES. If the R1 pattern repeats, a realistic runoff fill is 100-300 contracts across 2-3 thin rungs for the whole night.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: One night only (Oct 25). Taker: about $0. Maker: +$10-35 at 100 contracts a rung if R1's stale-rung flow repeats (the first-in-queue upper bound was $33 on R1 under the holdout drift), and about $0 if the runoff crowd prices the drift the way the deep R1 market did. Spread over a year of such nights: about $0.03-0.10 a day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: One night: maker +$20-60, because the thin rungs cap fills at roughly 175-1,000 wrong-side contracts a rung. About $0.1-0.2 a day spread over a year.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: None, statistically: there is 1 independent night. One night can show only the SIGN of the drift and whether wrong-side flow exists. These fills win 5-19c and lose 81-95c; telling +5c a contract apart from 0 on that payoff needs roughly 20 or more independent count nights.
test.worst_case: The runoff drift comes out near zero or reverses (in 2022 the runoff drift was only 0.3-0.5x the first round's). The faded rungs then settle YES, and each faded contract loses 81-95c: about -$85 a rung, -$255 at 300 contracts at the current bank, and about -$1,000 at $5k (400 a rung x 3). The payoff is the near-certain-side shape, win 5-19c or lose 81-95c, so one wrong rung in six wipes out the night. If it ever goes live, cap the night at $200 at risk.
