Fix the pre-registration BEFORE the night: (a) define the fair as Phi((run - d - X)/1 pt); (b) lower the band floor to the 2022 runoff curve (2.16 at 25% counted or less, 0.89 at 68%) instead of 0.5 x D1, and convert the curve to two-candidate shares; (c) score a MAKER version and a deep-sibling-anchored version side by side. The anchored version takes each rung's fair from KXBRPRES/MOV and ignores drift, because R1's money came from stale thin rungs. Score on Oct 26 (add READS_DUE 2026-10-26): did the 2022-runoff band contain the final at 12/25/50% counted; how many wrong-side taker contracts per rung traded at fair + 5c or better; paper P&L. Bar to go live on a later count night: at least +5c a contract net over at least 3 rungs, no rung worse than -50c, AND at least 500 wrong-side contracts at qualifying prices across the ladder. Any live order needs sign-off. Results saved in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-07/RESULT.json.

refs.strongest_objection:
The count drift is the idea's whole mechanism, and on the Oct 4 first-round night it made no measurable money when tested on data it was not fitted to. Under the 2022-runoff drift the taker rule fired 0 times.

The deep "anyone wins outright" market had already priced about 2 points of drift. From 17:00 to 17:30 ET (12-22% counted, Flavio's running share 51.1%), YES takers bought 8,403 contracts at an average of 11.1c and NO takers 24,733 at 6.6c. The 2022-runoff drift (2.16 pts, 1-pt spread) puts fair at about 14%, so those prices were roughly right. The hunter's "takers paid for the running total" uses the drift curve measured on that same night, which is look-ahead.

All of the first-round profit came from one stale thin rung. Flavio >= 50% lagged its deep sibling by about 20c, and 82% of that wrong-side flow was one burst at a single 22c price, which looks like one buyer. That is one night and in effect one taker.

That staleness needs no count model, and it is on the runoff board today. Thin rungs disagree with their deep twin (KXBRPRES) and with their mirror rungs. The locked-in gaps between them come to at most about $18 after fees, on 2-200 contracts a side.

The runoff drift guess also rests on one runoff: 2022 moved only 0.89 pts from 67.76% counted, below the pre-registered band floor of about 1.3 pts. Faded rungs near the band are coin flips that win 5-19c and lose 81-95c.

Drop the drift fade. What is left is posting quotes on the thin rungs priced off the deep twin and the mirror rungs: a one-off worth tens of dollars.

refs.strongest_objection:
I can't refute it as a free paper night, but the money rests on about 5 taker orders from a single night. On R1, the fills a maker could have had on rungs that also exist in the runoff came to 354 contracts in 5 orders, all in one 40-minute stretch. Whether R2 pays depends on one or two confused buyers turning up again.

Supply on R2 is likely thinner. Today every runoff rung already shows 200-300-lot resting quotes on both sides, while on R1 the FBOL-50 bid was $0.00 all count night. A working market maker would undercut us.

The payoff is lopsided:
- An R1-like night pays about +$24.
- If the drift fails, the loss is about -$255, 22% of the $1,155 bank. Flavio>=X NO and Lula>=100-X YES are the same bet (shares of valid votes, so Flavio + Lula = 100), and every rung settles on one TSE number.

The pre-registered band floor (0.5 x D1) sits above the only runoff drift ever measured (2022 R2: 0.89 pts at 68% counted). The quotes would be priced too aggressively in exactly the spots where people projecting state by state can see it, and that is how our resting orders get picked off.

The drift curve only applies to Brazil, and Brazil has 2 national count nights every 4 years (next in Oct 2030), not "a few times a year".

Other execution checks:
- Fees on KXVOTEBR2, MOV and MOVD: quadratic x1 (taker 0.07P(1-P)).
- Settlement is the certified TSE share, expected expiration 2026-11-25. R1 settled the next day (10-05 22:52Z), so money is probably tied up for about a day, but it could be up to a month.

idea.name: Nov 3 count-order desk: late-D share drift in the five states whose late count kept its sign in every measured race-year (MI, PA, WI, GA, VA), with the count-order trailer rule and its bounce exit as paper side-scores, run off a key-free REST recorder
markets: trailer rule (paper): SENATENC-26, SENATETX-26, SENATEOH-26, SENATEIA-26, GOVPARTYAZ/NV-26
recorder universe ~300 tickers: CONTROLH/S-2026, KXBALANCEPOWERCOMBO, SENATE*-26, GOV*/GOVPARTY*-26, top KXHOUSERACE, seat ladders, KXAPCALL*
idea.mechanism: Poll the NYT/AP race JSON (eevp = expected vote %, D and R totals) every 60-120 s. In MI, PA, WI, GA, VA at eevp 70-85%: projected final D two-party share = counted share + the state's measured shift (2024 value as base, 2020 as upper bound). Buy D-share rungs (or sell R-share / R-margin rungs) sitting >= 1 pt on the wrong side of the projection; buy the D trailer in MI/GA Senate only if R's two-party lead is smaller than the 2024 shift. Hold to settlement (certified share for the ladders). Side-score, paper only: trailer rule v1 (RULE_PREREGISTERED.md, a static late-D / late-R state map written before any test-night price was pulled) -- when a contested race's side first prints >= 90c after 18:00 ET and the leader is the party the late count does NOT favour, buy the trailer, 100 contracts, hold; bounce exit variant max(3x entry, 15c) - 1c. Recorder: unauthenticated GETs only -- GET /markets?tickers=<=100> every 5 s (3 calls), exchange-wide /markets/trades?min_ts= every 10 s, full books for the 30 deepest every 30 s, NYT JSON every 120 s; gzip per stream per hour with a hard size cap; refuses to write under kalshi_data/feed_data/fulltape.
idea.why_mispriced: Running totals in these five states always under-count the D vote at 70-85% counted, and the ladders and winner books are priced off running totals -- the measurable core of the 'blue shift', not the folklore map (wrong in about a third of states). The trailer rule's motivating night: in 2024 Polymarket priced Rogers (MI Senate) to 95-97.5c and Hovde (WI) to 96.5c at 2-3 AM ET while Detroit/Milwaukee absentees were uncounted; both lost.
idea.must_be_true: (1) Institutions unchanged (PA no pre-canvass, WI Milwaukee central count, Detroit, Atlanta metro, VA central absentee precincts) and a midterm shift >= 1 pt. (2) Ladders have wrong-side size on the night (N1-06 saw one grid quoter, 200-lot bids / 5-lot asks today). (3) The market does not already over-price the folklore (2022 AZ governor: Lake bid to 95c on expected late-R ballots; Hobbs won). (4) Recorder: nothing else unauthenticated runs that night (2 HTTP 429 in 49 dry-run calls) and NYT keeps its URL pattern (pages/data/2026-11-03/results-<state>-<office>.json is 404 today).
idea.evidence_so_far: NYT timestamped count histories (179 statewide races, 2020/2024/2025): D two-party share rose from the 80%-expected-vote mark to the final in 15 of 15 race-years in MI, PA, WI, GA, VA (MI +2.0..+3.7 pts, PA +0.6..+4.9, WI +1.3..+2.3, GA +1.5..+4.2, VA +1.0..+2.4); FL and IA fell in 5 of 5; AZ, TX, OH, MN flipped sign between 2020 and 2024; WA/OR/CA late counts leaned R. The folklore map was sign-right only 25/36 (2020) and 26/38 (2024); lean persistence 2020->2024 corr 0.43-0.46 (slope ~0.3). Needle-lite on 2024 Polymarket triggers (post hoc, fit on 2020 only): 6 fires, 2 trailer wins (+$141 per 100 contracts); 6 no-fires, 0 wins (-$45.50). Trailer rule v1, n = races: 2024 Polymarket CLOB (in-sample) 9 fires, 2 wins (+$111 per 100); 2022 Polymarket AMM decoded from Polygon logs (7,140 trades, out of sample) 5 fires, 0 wins (-$49.60); Brazil R1 on Kalshi 1 fire, lost (-$10.50); controls 0 of 20 (2024) and 0 of 18 (2022) non-fire trailers won; pooled 2 of 15 = 13% (95% 1.7-40%) vs ~10% break-even; out of sample alone 0 of 6. Bounce exit: +$21 per 100 over 15 races (~+1.4c a race), worse than holding in-sample. Recorder (10-15): tickers= batch works; exchange-wide trades >1,000 in 60 s with a cursor; 2024 MI Senate NYT file holds 551 snapshots; 60-s dry run on 10 tickers 49 calls, 0.12 MB (projected ~100-150 MB gzipped for 300 tickers x 12 h). Kalshi serves no Nov 2024/2025 tape.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: One night: $10-60 at the current bank if the ladders carry 100-300 contracts of wrong-side size; $40-200 at $5k. Trailer side-score $0-30 expected if the pooled rate holds, negative if the out-of-sample 0 of 6 is the truth; bounce exit $0-10. ~$0/day annualised.
idea.settlements_per_day: One night; ladders settle on certification (weeks), winner markets on the call; 2024 mirages resolved in 2-4 hours (WI Sen D 7.5c at 02:00 ET -> 96c at 06:00)
idea.test_plan: Pre-register before Nov 3: rung choice at the first snapshot with eevp >= 70, projection = counted + 2024 shift; bar >= +5c a contract over >= 5 rungs in >= 3 states (paper only). Recorder elecnight_record.py (r2-election-night-count-order/): rehearse on Oct 25 (Brazil, M-07) and check bytes/hour and the 429 count; run 18:00 ET Nov 3 to 06:00 ET Nov 4; verify the NYT URL pattern the afternoon of Nov 3; operator approves the output folder outside kalshi_data. Trailer rule v1: log every FIRE with the Kalshi ask, score on settlement, KILL if Nov 3 adds >= 5 fires with 0 wins (pooled would fall to 2 of 20); bounce exit scored free on the recording. After the night: pull 1-min candles for every election market before the ~60-day purge and compute R1-N1-06's identities (R House = RR + RD, R Senate = RR + DR; MOV vs vote share vs winner) on every 5-s row. Add READS_DUE Nov 4-6.
idea.prior_reason: The 15-of-15 sign record in five states is the most solid count-order fact found, it is decided on one night under 3 weeks away, and the recorder serves at least five ideas; but it is one night, wrong-side ladder depth is unknown, and the trailer half is a coin flip at 2 of 15 with 0 of 6 out of sample.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Extends 20261015-R1-C3-07 (counting-hour desk, not-tested) and R1-N1-06 (recorder checks) with the first measurement (179 NYT count histories, Polymarket 2022/2024 prices) and narrows it to the 5 states whose shift kept its sign; turns R1-C3-02's mirage killer into a rule tested out of sample (2022 on-chain AMM, Brazil); replaces the WebSocket recorder plan with a REST plan that needs no API key and adds the vote-count stream.
idea.worst_case: A 2026 procedure change kills the shift in one state and the rungs settle against us: about -$100 at the current bank; all trailer fires lose: about -$90 at 100 contracts a race (-$360 at 400 at $5k); recorder runaway disk capped by --max-mb (default 3 GB uncompressed).

test.method:
I ran three measurements, using data that was already on hand plus one new source.

(1) New source: Kalshi's /historical/* endpoints need no login and still serve the settled 2024 and 2025 election markets:
- /historical/markets?series_ticker=|event_ticker= (market list)
- /historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks (1-minute bars with best bid, best ask, last price, volume and open interest)
- /historical/trades?ticker= (each trade with the taker's side, cursor paging)

The cutoff is 2026-08-16. For markets settled before then, /series/.../candlesticks returns 404 and /markets/trades returns 0, which is why the hunter concluded "Kalshi serves no Nov 2024/2025 tape".

What I pulled:
- 1-minute bars from 22:00Z on election day to +24 h for 106 markets: PRESPARTY/SENATE/GOVPARTY<ST>-24 in the map states plus extras, GOVPARTYVA-25 and GOVPARTYNJ-25.
- POPVOTEMOV-24 (18 buckets): hourly bars to Nov 30, plus 1-minute bars for the night.
- The 2024 trade tape for the MI and WI Senate races.

In 2024 Kalshi listed no state vote-share or margin ladders (PRESMOV* and KXVOTEGENERAL return nothing from /historical).

(2) Projection holdout, using the hunter's NYT count histories (lean_table.json):
- Projection = counted D two-party share at the first snapshot with expected vote >= 70% (or 80%) + the same state's shift from the previous cycle. Test pairs: 2020 -> 2024, and 2024 -> VA 2025.
- The rung rule exactly as specified: buy D >= X for every 1-pt two-party rung X with counted < X <= projection - 1 pt. One point of two-party share equals the 2-pt spacing of the KXMIDTERMMOV margin rungs.
- A rung counts as a hit if the final share is >= X.

(3) Trailer rule v1 from RULE_PREREGISTERED.md, scored on Kalshi's own tape:
- Entry at a real ask = min(trailer YES ask, 1 - leader YES bid), plus 1c, plus the taker fee.
- Trigger: the leader's real bid reaches >= 90c. I did not use a last-price trigger, because big market orders sweeping through very wide books set it off. Example: MI Senate R printed 98c on 1,663 contracts at 23:14 ET while the best bid was 41c.
- Bounce exit: sell at the first real trailer bid >= max(3x entry, 15c), minus 1c and the fee.

Sources, best first: Kalshi trade tape and 1-minute book bars, then the NYT count files. No replay was used. Scripts h0-h9 are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-09/.
test.n_markets:
- Kalshi 2024/2025 winner markets: 106 fetched (53 races); 20 races were contested at 18:00 ET and scored by the trailer rule.
- National popular-vote margin ladder POPVOTEMOV-24: 18 buckets.
- NYT projection holdout: 10 core-5 race-years (9 in 2024, plus VA governor 2025).
- Today's board: 12 KXMIDTERMMOV and 16 KXVOTEGENERAL core-5 events (219 rungs, 25 order books).
test.n_independent_clusters: 2 count nights (Nov 5 2024 and Nov 4 2025). All the 2024 races share one national environment, so the trailer and core-5 results are effectively ONE cluster. The national ladder is one market on one night.
test.result:
(a) The projection fails its holdout.
- "Counted + previous-cycle shift" overshot the final D share by 2.47 pts on average at 70% counted (range -7.24 for PA president to +0.70; 10 races), and by 1.75 pts at 80%.
- The rungs the rule would buy settled YES 11 of 30 times at 70% counted (37%) and 12 of 23 at 80% (52%). PA 2024 went 0 of 7.
- The 2026 setup (last cycle as the base) has one test race, VA governor 2025: error -0.67 / +0.19 pts, 2 of 2 rungs.
- The sign held in every race, so the 15/15 fact stands. Only the size is unstable: by state, the 2024 shifts ran 0.05x to 1.4x the 2020 ones.
- Sign-only leftover (buy only the first rung above the count): 6 of 8 at 70%, 8 of 9 at 80%. It only pays if that rung costs under about 82c.
- Caveat: the 2024 presidential finals are NYT snapshots at 94.7-98.8% of expected vote, not certified results. The late drift runs D-ward, so the hit counts are slightly understated (not measured).

(b) The market did not price the running count on the only Kalshi count-night vote-margin ladder with a tape (POPVOTEMOV-24, 3-23M contracts a bucket).
- 00:00 ET Nov 6: the count said Trump +3.73 with 75% of expected vote in; the market's implied average was +1.36.
- 02:00 ET: count +3.98 (83% in); market +1.41, with the bucket that eventually won (Trump 1-1.99%) at 60%.
- That bucket settled YES. The late D drift was priced in from the start.
- One move I can't explain: 07:00-11:00 ET the winning bucket fell to 17-22%, then was back at 65% by 17:00 ET. Our count series stops at 05:25 ET, so it cannot be tied to count order.

(c) Kalshi winner markets in the core-5 states at 80% counted:
- D lost at 3-11c in the MI, WI, GA and PA presidential races, and at 26-32c in PA Senate.
- D won from 9-11c in MI Senate and 25-27c in WI Senate.
- VA governor 2025: D was at 99c from 50% counted, so there was nothing to trade.

(d) Trailer rule v1 on Kalshi 2024/2025:
- Fire class (leader is the party the late count does not favour): 8 races, trailer won 2 (MI and WI Senate), average entry 10.5c, hold to settlement +$110.70 per 100 contracts.
- That is the same night as the hunter's Polymarket in-sample result (+$111, 2 of 9), so it adds no out-of-sample evidence.
- Aligned class: 6 races, 0 wins (-$62.80 per 100). Excluded states: 4 races, 0 wins. NV Senate never triggered.
- Pooled with 2022 (0 of 5) and Brazil (0 of 1): 2 of 14 (14%; true rate anywhere from about 2% to 43%) against a break-even near the 10.5c entry. Out of sample it is still 0 of 6.

(e) Bounce exit on Kalshi 2024: -$8.70 per 100 in the fire class (holding made +$110.70) and -$62.80 in the aligned class. Dead.
test.artefact_checks:
- Trigger artefact, found and fixed: last-price triggers fired on market-order sweeps through very wide early-night Senate books (MI Senate D was 2c bid / 61c ask at 23:04 ET). That put 51-59c "trailer" entries into the fire class. The real-bid trigger removes them.
- The D bid/ask built from two separate books can cross at 1-minute closes because the books don't update in step. Harmless for the expected-vote table.
- The national running margin uses 50 state files and is missing DC. That shifts the margin about 0.2 pt toward Trump, which does not change the 2.5-pt gap between the count and the market.
- The NYT 2024 presidential files end before certification (94.7-98.8% of expected vote), as stated in the result.
- The holdout uses the 2020 presidential shift for the 2024 Senate races too, as the rule itself specifies.
- All 2024 results come from one night. The trailer fire class is in-sample, because the rule was written after seeing the 2024 MI and WI results.

test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now:
$0/day.
- As specified, the ladder rule bought rungs that settled YES only 37-52% of the time in the holdout, and the one Kalshi ladder we can measure had already priced the drift. On that evidence the expected value is not positive.
- The trailer rule is paper-only: +$111 per 100 contracts in-sample, 0 of 6 out of sample.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0/day.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
- Trailer fire class: with 14 pooled races the hit rate is only known to within about +-25 points (2 of 14 means anywhere from 2% to 43%). A 10% break-even cannot be told apart from 0% or 40%. Nov 3 adds about 5-9 fires.
- Projection: 10 races with errors spread about 2.3 pts, so the average error is known to about +-0.7 pt within one night. But all the 2024 races are one cluster, so the real risk (the shift size changing between cycles) rests on effectively 1-2 cycle-to-cycle changes.

- Trailer rule live: every fire that loses costs about 11c a contract (the 2024 losers ran -10.6 to -11.7c). All 8 losing at 100 contracts each is about -$90.

idea.name: Kalshi perp funding-print snipe: hold the receiving side for ~3 minutes across each funding timestamp (funding is paid on contracts held at the snapshot), decided from the public per-second premium
markets: any perp whose WAPI clears the cost
idea.mechanism: At T-150 s before each funding time (crypto 00:00/08:00/16:00 ET; metals daily 10:00 ET; US500/USTECH100 4 PM ET) read GET /margin/funding_rates/estimate, or rebuild the linear-weighted premium WAPI from /funding_rates/premium_index. If |rate| >= live spread + 2 x fee + 1 bp margin (and >= 1.5 bp, so a rate that rounds to zero after entry cannot hurt), open the receiving side (short when the rate is positive) at <= 3x leverage, hold through T, close at T+60 s. Funding is paid on every contract HELD at the funding calculation time (filing text: 'for each Contract held'), times the 60-s VWAP before T.
idea.why_mispriced: Nobody is mispriced in the usual sense: Kalshi's funding is a snapshot payment, not pro-rata, so a position held for 3 minutes collects 8 hours of funding. The payers are persistent US-retail longs (BTC perp premium +1.6 bp on average; BTC funding positive on 49% of prints, negative on 0%). The exchange's Dec-31 rebate makes the round trip nearly free for eligible members.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The operator gets margin access (retail must apply) -- a new venue and product. (2) His fee schedule: at the SCM rebate (crypto taker net 0.3 bp) crypto snipes work; at tier 0 (crypto taker 4 bp) or the older 12 bp only metals/index snipes (taker 0.24 bp) survive. test.method: Public Kalshi perps data only, no auth, 823 GETs, no 429s. (1) All 5,875 funding prints since perps launched on 2026-06-03 (GET /margin/funding_rates/historical). (2) For each of the 751 prints with |rate| >= 1.5 bp, 1-minute candles from 10 min before to 5 min after the funding time (bid close, ask close, open interest). 737 had usable quotes. (3) The bot rule exactly as the idea states it: decide and enter as a taker at the touch 2 minutes before the funding time, using the spread visible then. Enter only if |rate| >= max(1.5 bp, spread + 2 x fee + 1 bp). Take the receiving side (short when the rate is positive; the filing says longs pay shorts). Exit as a taker at the touch 1 minute after. P&L = |rate| + (short: bid_in - ask_out, long: bid_out - ask_in)/mid - 2 x fee. Fees per side: crypto 0.3 bp under the Sep-02 temporary rebate (eligibility not verified, ends 2026-12-31) or 4.0 bp at tier 0 from 2027; metals 0.018 or 0.24 bp; index 0.24 bp. Also scored three other hold windows: 1 min before to 1 min after, 2 min before to 5 min after, and 1 min before to the funding time. (4) Holdout: the rule has no fitted threshold (the 1 bp margin and 1.5 bp floor were fixed beforehand), so I split the qualifying funding timestamps in half at 2026-09-22 (early half / late half). I also chose markets with a positive mean in the early half and scored only those in the late half. (5) Per-second premium index for the 60 qualifying prints still inside its 14-day retention, 30 min either side of the funding time. This gave the prediction error 150 s before the funding time, by exactly inverting the linearly weighted average (1 call per print instead of 8 to 24), and the premium path around the funding time. (6) Open-interest change into and out of the funding time, to see whether other traders already snipe. (7) Six order-book snapshots of the 16 traded perps, 30 s apart, walked for slippage at $100 to $6,000. Dollars computed from the late half (since 2026-09-22): each funding time's notional is split equally across the markets that qualify then; each market is sized at the largest notional whose slippage stays under 1 bp, and pays that slippage. Source ranking: settlement-formula inputs (premium index) and the exchange's own candles. There are no live fills: we have no perps account. Scripts and outputs: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-11/ (probe.py, pull_candles.py, analyze.py, pull_premium.py, recon.py, money.py, money2.py; analyze.json, recon.json, money2.json, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 16 perps traded at least one qualifying print. Scored 737 funding prints with |rate| >= 1.5 bp. 124 qualify under the rebate fee (crypto 88, metals 32, index 4); 33 qualify under tier-0 fees (crypto 4, metals 25, index 4).
test.n_independent_clusters: 94 funding timestamps under the rebate rule (early half 47, late half 47); 26 under tier-0 fees. Crypto prints at the same timestamp share one price shock, so standard errors are clustered by timestamp.
test.result:
REBATE FEES, entry 2 min before / exit 1 min after: +3.64 bp a print (clustered se 1.17; 124 prints / 94 timestamps; positive on 61 of 100).
- Early half +3.12 (se 1.77; 54 prints / 47 timestamps). Late half +4.04 (se 1.55; 70 / 47).
- Markets chosen on the early half (BTC, ETH, HYPE, SOL, XRP) score +4.11 in the late half (se 1.24; 28 prints / 23 timestamps).
- Breakdown: funding received 4.98 bp, minus half-spreads 2.04, minus fees 0.60, plus price move +1.15 (se 1.09, i.e. zero). The near-deterministic part (funding - spread - fee) is +2.3 bp.
- By class: crypto +4.53 (n 88), metals +1.75 (n 32), index -0.79 (n 4; the 4 PM ET equity close moves against it, so drop US500).
- Shorter hold (1 min before to the funding time): +3.16 (se 0.75; 125 / 92; positive on 76 of 100; early +2.02, late +4.00); the variance falls by half.
- Longer hold (exit 5 min after): +1.64 (se 2.41), noise only.

TIER-0 FEES: 33 prints, +2.58 (se 2.10); metals +3.21 (n 25); crypto almost never clears 8 bp of round-trip fee.

PRICE MOVE on all 737 prints >= 1.5 bp: -0.76 bp (se 0.69) for the 3-min hold and -0.14 (se 0.42) for 1 min. Zero-mean within about 1 bp.

PREDICTABILITY: the print estimated 150 s before the funding time was within 0.1 bp on 60 of 60 recent prints (median error 0.007 bp, max 0.059).

PREMIUM PATH (60 prints): the premium on the receiving side sags about 0.45 bp into the funding time and recovers by +3 min. The premium part of the move from 150 s before to 60 s after is +0.71 bp in OUR favour (se 0.24), so nobody is visibly front-running the print.

OPEN INTEREST: no build-up into the funding time (BTC median change -0.002% over the last 2 min, n 96), so there is no sign of competing snipers.

DOLLARS (late half, 23.3 days, 3.0 qualifying prints a day):
- Rebate fees, $500 of perps margin at 3x: $1.06/day measured, $0.66/day with the price move set to zero.
- $1,000 margin: $1.94 / $1.18. $2,000 margin (5k bank): $3.79 / $2.19.
- Tier-0 fees: $0.33, $0.76 and $1.03 a day.
- Contributions at $500 margin over 23 days: SOL +$8.22, UNI +$5.82, platinum +$3.65, BTC +$2.58, gold +$2.35, XRP +$1.29, US500 -$1.13.
- Losing days: 5 of 19 trading days, worst -$1.75.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) Prediction: the backtest uses the final print, not the live estimate. Checked by inverting the weighted average: the estimate 150 s before is within 0.06 bp on 60 of 60, so this is not look-ahead.
(2) Executable prices: candle bid/ask closes are the touch at the minute end. Six current book snapshots show slippage at $1,500 of <= 0.13 bp on BTC, ETH, SOL, gold, platinum, US500 and copper, but 0.4 to 1.4 bp on UNI, VVV, WLD and HYPE; this is charged in the dollar figures. Historical depth is NOT available, so depth at past funding times is a proxy.
(3) The good number was reconciled by hand: 4.98 - 2.04 - 0.60 + 1.15 = 3.49 vs 3.64 reported; the gap is the bid/ask normalisation.
(4) Selection: the rule selects on entry spread only; exit spread and price move are not selected on. The price move on the full 737-print population is zero-mean (-0.76, se 0.69), so qualifying is not picking a favourable drift.
(5) Luck: the measured +3.6 includes a +1.15 bp price move that is noise. Dollars are quoted both as measured and with the move zeroed.
(6) Clustering: se is clustered by funding timestamp, so the 1.3 prints per timestamp are not counted as independent.
(7) NOT VERIFIED, and each would change or kill the result:
- (a) Snapshot payment. The CFTC filing says 'for each Contract held' at the end of the funding calculation interval, and the help pages say you pay or receive 'while your position is open'. Neither says pro-rata, but it was never seen on an account. If payment is pro-rata, a 3-minute hold gets about 0.6% of the funding and every print loses about 2.6 bp.
- (b) Fee eligibility: whether this direct account counts as a Self-Clearing Member for the 0.3 bp rebate.
- (c) The help page describes a 1-minute-candle TWAP, but the per-second linearly weighted formula from the filing is what reproduces the prints (hunter: 5 of 5 to 0.001 bp; here the inversion is consistent on 60).
(8) Adverse selection: our entry time is fixed by the clock, not chosen by someone trading against us, and size <= touch on the deep books, so the usual 'our fills are worse than the tape' gap should be small. It is NOT measured: no perps fills exist.
Housekeeping: the recorders are alive (the cfbenchmarks_value hour file was written 30 s before the end of my work), 117.8 GB free, scratch folder 7.5 MB, no process touched.

refs.strongest_objection:
The per-print edge holds up, but the dollars come from one hot stretch. Of the 71 qualifying prints since 2026-09-22, 56 (79%) fall in the last 10.6 days (10-05..10-15). That is a crypto funding spike: the week of Oct 5 had 94 crypto prints >= 2.5 bp, against 1-22 a week in each of the 18 weeks before it (majors 33 vs 0-8).

Same rule, same fees, $500 margin at 3x, price move set to zero: $0.29/day for 09-22..10-04 vs $1.28/day for 10-05..10-15. So the tester's $0.8/day is the peak of a hot stretch, not a typical day. The crypto part also needs the SCM rebate, which ends 2026-12-31; at tier-0 fees almost only metals qualify.

After the funding time the price moves against the side that receives funding. On all 365 prints >= 1.5 bp: T to T+60 s was -1.37 bp (se 0.78) and T+60 to T+120 s was -1.37 (se 0.94); on the liquid perps, T+60 to T+120 was -0.95 (se 0.82). Any delay in getting out costs about 1 bp a minute. The qualifying set's +1.28 bp favourable move is noise: the liquid-market population over the same hold is 0.00 (se 1.02).

Not refuted, and three structural doubts got weaker:
- Snapshot payment: the API schemas compute funding on "Signed position at funding time" / "Position size at time of funding".
- Rebate eligibility: the rulebook defines a Self-Clearing Member as "a Person, other than an FCM, that has entered into the Self-Clearing Member agreement", so the operator's direct, non-FCM account is most likely eligible. Not confirmed on his own fee-tier endpoint.
- Units: the largest print is exactly 200.00 bp, the 2% clamp, so the rate is a fraction.

Anomaly: 7 nonzero metal/index prints since 10-07 are below the filing's 1 bp deadband. The hunter's 5-of-5 formula match covered crypto only. The tester's "60 of 60 within 0.1 bp" check is close to circular, because under the assumed weighting the last 150 s carry only ~1% by construction.
refs.independent_number: My own pull, 406 public GETs. Since 2026-09-22, rule as stated (enter at the touch at T-120 s, exit at T+60 s, rebate fees): 71 qualifying prints / 48 funding times. Funding minus round-trip half-spreads minus fees = +2.62 bp a print (clustered se 0.28; positive on 96%). Measured net +3.90 bp (se 1.54), which reproduces the tester's +4.04. Deterministic $/day at $500 margin x3: $0.74 over the window, $0.29 for 09-22..10-04, $1.28 for 10-05..10-15; $0.38 at tier-0 fees.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's $0.8/day depends on a fee this account cannot get. It assumes the 0.3 bp crypto fee from the Temporary Perpetual Fee Rebate Program. The filings (09-02, and 09-24, which became a 100% rebate from 10-08) say "Eligible Participants are all Self-Clearing Members of Kalshi" and exclude Kalshi affiliates.

- Kalshi's help centre says Self-Clearing Member status is for institutions that meet "significant financial and operational thresholds". It also says "most retail users on Kalshi trade perpetuals currently through Kalshi Prime, a registered FCM". Kalshi Prime is an affiliate.
- The cheaper 09-22 schedule (crypto 4 bp, metals and index 0.24 bp taker) is scoped to "all self-clearing members of the exchange".
- The 06-24 filing is the last one that names FCM customers. It puts them on 12 bp taker / 5 bp maker at tier 0. This account is tier 0 (about $69.5k of 30-day volume against a $100k threshold).
- The margin API lists separate fee schedules for self_clearing_members, kalshi_prime and fcm.
- Third-party pages dated 09-25 and 10-10 quote 0.12% taker at the retail entry tier, on every asset class.

At 12 bp a side the round trip costs 24 bp in fees alone. Funding prints are a median 2 bp and at most 31 bp, so nothing survives the spread.

Execution points that do not kill it:
- Snapshot payment is fine. The filing says "for each Contract held", and the funding-history API stores "Position size at time of funding".
- The estimate 160 s before the funding time was within 0.071 bp of the final print on all 11 nonzero prints today.

Still unverified:
- Whether a Kalshi Prime retail customer gets API order access at all.
- What the money costs elsewhere: the pin bot sizes from its bank, so moving $500 to perps margin cuts its bet size by about 40%. Not measured.

refs.strongest_objection:
Ruling: the fee question is settled, measured on the operator's own account with read-only GETs and no order.
- GET /margin/enabled returns true, so the account already has perps margin and nothing needs applying for.
- GET /margin/fee_tier_rates returns schedule 'kalshi_prime'. Tier-0 crypto fees are 12 bp taker and 2 bp maker.
- GET /margin/fee_tiers gives the effective rate per market. Every crypto perp and WTI pays 0.0012 taker (12 bp a side). Gold, silver, platinum, palladium, copper, aluminium, US500 and USTECH100 pay 0.000072 taker (0.72 bp) and 0.12 bp maker.
- No SCM rebate shows on this account.

Crypto: the execution skeptic is right. Since 09-22 only 3 crypto prints clear the 24 bp round trip plus 1 bp. All are UNI, and none survives UNI's 11-15 bp spread. Crypto made most of the tester's $0.8/day, and that share is gone.

Metals and index: the execution skeptic is wrong that nothing survives. He applied 12 bp to every asset class; metals and index pay 0.72 bp. From my own pull (5,896 prints, plus 1-minute candles around 54 candidates), the stated rule at this account's fees qualifies 20 metals/index prints at 17 funding times since 09-22.
- Enter at T-120 s, exit at T+60 s: net +3.78 bp a print (se 2.32, not distinguishable from zero). The part that ignores price moves (funding minus half-spreads minus 1.44 bp of fees) is +2.51 bp.
- Shorter hold, T-60 s to T: net +4.23 bp (se 1.11), positive on 20 of 22.
- Money at $500 margin x3 ($1,500 notional), price moves ignored: $0.25/day over 23.8 days. That is $0.11/day for 09-22..10-04 and $0.42/day for 10-05..10-15, the rise coming from metals and index perps listed since 10-06. With measured price moves included: $0.03-0.61/day.

Still unverified:
- Whether a 3-minute holding is paid the full funding (the snapshot rule). A 10-snipe micro test decides it.
- Book depth at past funding times.
- The sample is only 20 prints.

Context, outside this ruling: the Kalshi ledger, all series, averaged -$46/day over 10-01..10-14, so moving $500 out of the predictions bank gives up no measured positive return right now.

refs.strongest_objection:
The NFL +6-7c that kept this idea alive comes from one random draw of lines.

- **A different draw loses.** I ran the same rule on the same 78 regular-season games (weeks 1-5), but drew a different random line per series per game (seed 777, 347 usable lines). BUY-YES FRONT came out -0.63c a contract (se 3.88, 68 games) and D200 -2.42c (49 games), so both fail the idea's own +1c bar. With the tester's 5-min candle window it is -2.20c and -5.20c.
- **It is the draw, not the code.** My code run on the tester's own lines gives +6.61c (they reported +7.27c). The 20 tickers that appear in both draws have identical bids and settlement values.
- **We could not get the fills.** On tonight's TNF books (snapshot at K-4.5 h, one game):
  - The spread is 1c on 189 of 235 lines (80 in 100), so we cannot step in front of the queue without crossing.
  - The queue already sitting at the YES bid has a median of 655 contracts (TD 7,313; the 30-60c band 1,608). Only 29 lines in 100 have 200 or fewer ahead.
  - Over the whole 90-min window, the NO-taker volume printed at the bid has a median of 0-11 contracts per line.
  - 90 in 100 taker contracts in [K-90, K] buy YES (2.10M vs 0.23M), so the YES-bid side is the thin side of the flow.
- **Realistic result is zero.** With the queue drawn from those live books and both draws pooled (634 lines, 78 games): +0.71c a contract (se 3.64 by game, 2.87 by week) on about 420 contracts a week. That is about $0.4 a day with a standard error near $2 a day.
- **Settlement-rule gotcha.** The rules say a player who is active but never takes a snap settles at the fair price before game start (3 of my 347 lines did). Inactive players are not covered. Entry at K-90 is the moment NFL inactives are published. My draw had 0 pre-kickoff crashes, so this risk is structural and not measured as a loss.
- **Soccer:** dead, as the tester found; I did not re-test it.
refs.independent_number: My own draw (seed 777, 347 lines, 78 NFL games, 730 public calls): BUY-YES FRONT -0.63c a contract (se 3.88, 68 games), against the tester's +7.27c on the seed-1015 lines. Live TNF 10-15 queue already at the YES bid: median 655 contracts, against a median of 0-11 NO-taker contracts printed at that bid in the whole 90-min window.

refs.strongest_objection:
Neither mechanism exists in the full population; the NFL +4.37c comes from one random draw.

(1) The tester's mechanism ("YES came in more often than the bid implied"): I pulled EVERY settled NFL prop market (6 series, every rung, every player) for regular-season weeks 1-5. That is 21,461 markets over 79 games. YES at the mid at kickoff-90 min is calibrated: +0.42c (se 0.68 by game). Week means are +1.5, -1.4, +1.7, +0.9, -0.2 (t 0.8 on 4 df). Buying at the bid earns +1.27c (se 0.69), which is half the 1.71c spread plus noise. Scored with my data, the tester's own 304 picks give exactly his +4.37c. Every other market in those same 79 games gives +1.22c. Re-drawing his "one random market per series per game" 2,000 times gives a median of +1.19c, and only 2.7 draws in 100 reach +4.37c.

(2) The idea's mechanism (NO-takers lose, YES-takers don't) fails on my own independent sample: 550 random markets, tapes pulled fresh. The maker made money on BOTH sides. Selling YES at the ask earned +2.16c (se 2.18, 75 games); buying YES at the bid earned +3.90c (se 3.55, 68 games). There is no asymmetry, and the hunter's SELL-YES -2.77c does not replicate.

(3) What is left (a resting bid earns about half the spread) is the generic two-sided prop maker (ledger SJ22 and the separate CLIFF idea). A YES-only rule throws away the other half of the spread for no measured reason.

(4) The forward bar cannot tell edge from no edge. Half-spread alone puts the expected gross at about +1.3c, and a 25-game cell has an se of 5-8c, so "FRONT and D200 both >= +1c" passes about 4 times in 10 with no YES edge at all. The "t >= 2 by week cluster" check uses only 5-7 clusters, where the clustered se is biased low: the tester's own table has the hunter's D200 at t 7.85 by week against 1.28 by game.

Checks that held: fee_type "quadratic" means takers pay and makers pay nothing; result and settlement_value agree on 21,155 markets; kickoff K = occurrence - 3 h re-confirmed. Files: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/refute-stats-20261015-R2-M-12/ (RESULT.json, fullan.out, recon.out, tapes2.out).

idea.name: CPI month-vs-year two-leg package with an ex-ante component-weighted seasonal ratio (Nov 10 window), plus a thin MoM-leg maker variant and a conditional identity hedge for far-strike CPI reward quotes
markets: far-strike KXCPIYOY / KXCPI reward programs (conditional variant)
idea.mechanism: After each CPI print, buy the two-leg package (YoY YES + MoM NO, or YoY NO + MoM YES) whose cut-offs, mapped through r = f(t)/f(t-1), leave no gap where both legs lose, when the package costs <= worst-case value - 2c; hold to the next print. r is computed ex-ante from BLS's published 2026 COMPONENT seasonal factors x the Dec-2025 relative importances updated to t-1 (81 aggregation components), not the aggregate factor a year earlier; band 0.00015; <= 33 pairs to start. Maker variant: where the package passes on the deep YoY touch but the MoM side is thin (YES bids 0-25 on central 26NOV rungs), rest a post-only MoM bid at the price that keeps the package >= +2c and lift the YoY leg the moment it fills (order size <= 33). Conditional variant: only if a non-coin-race reward pot is shown to pay this account (R1-C2-01), quote far-strike CPI reward programs and, when a far YoY bid fills, buy the MoM rung across the r cut-off so the two legs pay >= $1 in every outcome.
idea.why_mispriced: The two ladders are traded by different crowds; the YoY ladder's implied r is off by a median 0.00033 in the first 3 days after a print (R1-N1-01 tester), and nobody on the other side computes r from component factors. They lose on arithmetic, not information.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The component method keeps its accuracy out of sample: first free check Nov 10, pre-registered r_Oct26 = 0.998202 headline / 0.998920 core (bar +-0.00015 / +-0.0001). (2) The 26NOV books refill after the Nov 10 print with >= 33 pairs at both touches. (3) No shutdown or off-identity settlement before Dec 10 (KXCPI-25OCT settled 0.2 on 2025-11-22 with no published index; KXGOVTSHUTDOWN-26DEC12 trades 32/33c, so 26DEC packages wait until it resolves). (4) Maker variant: the YoY leg stays deep for the seconds between fill and lift.
idea.evidence_so_far: Measured. r accuracy (January excluded, 28 months 2024-02..2026-09 vs ALFRED first-print r): headline median |err| 0.00004 (ratio-naive 0.00015, factor-level 0.00021), 27 of 28 within +-0.00015, max 0.00019; core median 0.00001 (naive 0.00013), max 0.00006. Oracle check (true component price moves) reproduces r to < 0.00001 in 27 of 28 months, so the aggregation formula is BLS's. 2024-09 core (naive off 0.00117, the tester's -$263 worst month): component error +0.00001. With a gasoline nowcast (FRED GASREGW, median |err| 0.19% vs CPI motor fuel) headline max error 0.00006. Trade-confirmed P&L (step4 tape code, 10 release months 2025-12..2026-09, first 14 days after each print, both legs bought by takers in the same hour): component r, band 0.00015 = +$122.60 at <= 33 pairs, +$190.11 at <= 100 (naive band 0.00025: +$87.44 / +$179.99); 0 packages paid $0; $0.80/day per $100 locked, average locked only $50 (33 pairs) / $82 (100). Cluster = release month: n = 10. Maker variant NOT measured (supporting facts: YoY central asks 10-22k deep, MoM YES bids 0-25 on the 10-15 snapshot; KXCPI/KXCPIYOY charge makers 0.0175 x p(1-p)). Far-strike hedge NOT measured (R1-C2-10 tiebreak: far strikes +$1.15/market-day, SE 1.88, worst week -$971).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0.40/day at 33 pairs, $0.63/day at 100 (trade-confirmed, first 14 days only); about the same at $5,000 (depth-bound) unless the maker leg adds supply (plausibly doubles it; not measured); far-strike hedge $0-1/day on ~$880 of capital per 1,000-lot market. Worst plausible day about -$150 at 33 pairs (one family's stack in the band; a band miss seen in 1 of 28 headline months, 0 core).
idea.settlements_per_day: 2 releases a month (headline + core families), about 0.07 a day
idea.test_plan: PAPER_BOOK.json (r2-idle-cash-carry-book/): cpi-r-oct26-oos (Nov 10 08:30 ET print; bar +-0.00015 headline / +-0.0001 core vs the pre-registered r -- a FAIL kills the idea); cpi-r-nov26-prereg (record r with Oct weights before flagging); cpi-pair-paper-26nov (hourly book logger with sizes Nov 10-Dec 10; bar >= 3 package-days with >= 50 pairs at both touches and worst-case >= +3c in week 1, held P&L >= 0). Maker variant: from the same logger plus the trade tape, count hours where a resting MoM bid at the passing price would have been hit by a taker sell while the YoY touch had >= 100 offered. Far-strike hedge: only after C2-01 shows a non-coin-race pot pays this account; replay C2-10's s2_sim fills adding the hedge leg at the hourly candle ask. Code: cpi_r.py, cpi_prereg.py, bls_pull.py, step4_tape_pkgs.py. Add the Nov 10 read to READS_DUE.
idea.prior_reason: The most certain money in the batch -- an arithmetic identity, r accurate to 0.00004 over 28 months, trade-confirmed P&L with zero losing packages, and a free pass/fail on Nov 10 -- but depth caps it at $0.4-0.6/day and one off-identity settlement can cost months of profit.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Follow-up of 20261015-R1-N1-01 (needs-data) and ledger SI12/SJ57 (dead because the edge needed a seasonal ratio to 5 decimals that a nowcast put outside the range) and U23 (passed): the component-factor r answers that kill directly (median error ~4x smaller headline, ~10x core), removes the band-miss tail and the 'Nov window is core-only' objection, and replaces the capital-cost kill with a measured $0.80/day per $100. The maker leg and the identity hedge on R1-C2-10 (refuted this run) are new execution variants.
idea.worst_case: A mis-built r or an off-identity settlement hits every package in a family at once: up to -$700 at 33 pairs fully stacked; maker leg risk: a fill followed by a YoY gap leaves a naked MoM leg (capped at 33); unhedged far-strike reward fill -$970 per market (C2-10).

test.method: I tested the frozen rule on the trade tape. Rule: component r from cpi_r.json, band 0.00015, gap-density floor 4 per pp doubled, 2c margin, first passing UTC hour per family-day, first 14 days after the previous print. Size is limited to what takers actually bought at or below the passing price in that hour. Taker fee 0.07p(1-p) per leg, held to settlement, paid from Kalshi results. Steps: (1) Reproduced the hunter's in-sample window (2025-12..2026-09) to the cent. (2) New backward holdout with the rule frozen: 2024-02..2025-09, Januaries excluded, so 19 release months and 38 release-families. Pairs were built from the N1-01 tester's /historical market metadata and ALFRED first-print rel.json; settlement self-check 616 of 616 rungs. I pulled /historical/trades for 501 legs (129,823 trades, 0 truncated, 0 block trades) over the full window, from 1.5 h after the previous print to 6 h before close. (3) Artefact check that both offers existed at the same time: 1-minute candles of both legs, forward-filled, over each flagged hour, counting minutes where both asks together passed. (4) Stricter tape check: both legs bought by takers in the same 5-min or 1-min bucket. (5) Multi-hour variant. (6) Band holdout on r accuracy: band judged on 2024-02..2025-06, tested on 2025-07..2026-09. (7) Maker leg from the tape: a MoM taker trade on the opposite side at or below the highest passing MoM price, with a YoY taker buy of the needed side within the next 300 s. Our fill is at that worst passing price; maker fee 0.0175p(1-p) on KXCPI. (8) Active /incentive_programs scan. Sources: trade tape, 1-minute candles, Kalshi results, BLS/ALFRED first prints. No historical book sizes exist and we have no live fills.

refs.strongest_objection:
This is sold as a sum that cannot lose ('0 packages paid $0 in 84 package-days over 29 months'). The measured profit is not that, for two reasons.

(1) Even at the TRUE seasonal ratio, 18 of 55 in-sample package-days and 4 of 20 holdout ones had a window where the monthly print lands between the two cut-offs and both legs lose. Those package-days carry 41% and 40% of the profit. The monthly ladder's own prices at the flagged hour put the chance of landing in a window at about 1.6 in 100 per package-day. That is 1.17 expected $0 package-days in total, with a 31% chance of seeing none. The expected cost is $17 at 33 pairs (8% of the in-sample profit, 13% of the holdout), and the measured number leaves it out.

(2) The one month in 2024-26 when Kalshi settled the two ladders inconsistently sits OUTSIDE both test windows. In the Oct 2025 shutdown, KXCPI-25OCT settled at 0.2 and KXCPIYOY-25OCT at 3.3; core also settled at 0.2 and 3.3. The published Sep-2025 and Oct-2024 indexes say a 0.2 month means a year figure of 2.84-3.10 headline and 2.76-3.02 core. I ran the frozen rule on that month, using my own trade pull and my own code (it matches the tester's package-days exactly in 12 of 14 in-sample families). It flags 9 package-days and all 9 pay $0: -$73 at 33 pairs and -$124 at 100 (-$22 to -$207 at 33 across r assumptions). One failure of the 'no shutdown' guard wipes out 60% of the in-sample profit. The cheapest-looking packages that month were the YoY ladder pricing a settlement risk that the identity ignores. So 'never in 29 months' comes from which months were picked, not from evidence of zero risk; the guard is the protection, not the data.

(3) The tester's $0.35/day applies the hourly size to every package-day where the best asks passed together for at least one minute. The size at those asks was never seen. Taker buys that pass on both legs within 5 minutes of each other carry only $60 of the $123, and the tester's same-5-minute floor is $35-47 over about 304 days.

Not refuted:
- My own BLS pull gives the true ratio and the unrounded monthly print equal to the tester's in every 2026-02..09 family.
- My own Kalshi results match all 75 package-day payouts.
- The trades show no rival package-taker: passing buys on both legs within 5 s on only 1 of 55 days.
- In months with no shutdown the trade has never lost.

Revised: about $0.20/day at today's bank on idle money. The range is $0.11-0.33/day, and $0.08/day at 2024-25 supply. At $5,000 it is limited by market depth, about $0.3-0.5/day. Worst plausible day is a mismatched settlement on a whole family's stack: measured -$73 at 33 pairs, up to -$207.
refs.independent_number: Oct 2025, the off-identity shutdown month that both test windows leave out. I ran the frozen rule on my own /historical/trades pull of 25 legs (2,774 trades), scored with Kalshi results. It flags 9 package-days; all 9 paid $0, for -$73.21 at up to 33 pairs (-$123.94 at 100). Across r = the pre-registered Oct ratio +-0.0005 and band 0.00015/0.0005, the result ranges from -$22 to -$207 at 33. Second number: at the true r from my own BLS API pull (equal to the tester's to 1e-15), 18 of 55 in-sample package-days ($49.69 of $122.60) and 4 of 20 holdout ones ($21.32 of $52.74) still had a $0 window. The monthly ladder's prices give 0.93 + 0.23 expected $0 package-days, an expected cost of $10.35 + $6.92 at 33 pairs.

refs.strongest_objection:
The calendar takes out most of the trading windows over the next four months, so the 'now' rate is about a third of the tester's $0.35/day. The supply itself held up under every execution check I ran.

(1) There is no window this month. KXCPIYOY-26OCT and KXCPICOREYOY-26OCT return HTTP 404 (not listed), while every month from 2024-01 to 2026-09 had both ladders. The cause: October 2025 CPI was never published (FRED CPIAUCNS 2025-10 is blank), so no 12-month figure for October 2026 can exist. The Oct 14 to Nov 10 window has only the MoM leg.

(2) The 26DEC pair (settles on the Jan 13 print) sits behind KXGOVTSHUTDOWN-26DEC12 at 32/33c. Funding runs to Dec 11, and the rules extend expiry up to six months after a shutdown ends. KXCPI-25OCT settled at 0.2 with no index published. Waiting for the Dec 12 resolution gives up the first two days after the print.

(3) The January window is excluded by design.

So from today to about Feb 11 2027 (~119 days) there is one clean window (26NOV, buying Nov 10-24) plus a shortened Dec window that happens about 2 times in 3. That is about 1.5 windows at ~$11 each ($109 simultaneity-adjusted over 10 in-sample months), roughly $16 in total, or $0.13/day. From Feb 2027: ~11 windows a year, about $0.33/day at 2026 depth and $0.10/day at 2024-25 depth.

Money for it must be idle. Per $100 tied up it earns less than pin does on main-account cash, so funding it from main loses money overall.

Worst day: 33 of the 55 in-sample package-days carry a real zero-pay gap (up to 0.044 pp, so they are not pure identities), and they stack on one rung pair (6 package-days on KXCPIYOY-26JUN-T3.9 / KXCPI-26JUN-T-0.1). A whole family paying $0 costs about $40-115 at 33 pairs, up to the tester's ~$280 for the busiest month. Running it in an isolated subaccount caps this at the subaccount's size.

What I could NOT refute: who gets the supply. Nobody else runs the trade, and the cheap offers sat for minutes to hours (see the number field).
refs.independent_number:
All from my own queries (406 public calls).

(a) Listing: KXCPIYOY-26OCT returns 404. Of the 36 months 2024-01..2026-12, every one has a YoY ladder except 2026-10.

(b) No rival two-ladder bot. My full tapes of the Aug and Sep 2026 headline ladders (76 markets) show opposite-direction cheap no-gap pairs (both legs bought by takers within 3 s, under 98c with fees) 0 times in Aug and 1 in Sep, against 0.0 and 0.6 expected by chance. Same-direction pairs ran 2.7x chance (459 vs 172 within 1 s in Sep): news traders hit both ladders together, which is the leg-race risk for the maker variant.

(c) No flash-price artefact. For all 55 of the hunter's in-sample package-days I pulled both legs' tape from 1 h before to 2 h after the flagged hour. Every trade bounds the needed side's best ask, which gives each cheap offer a maximum lifetime. Every contract the hunter sized on lived 60 s or more, so P&L at <= 33 pairs stays $122.60 (and $190.11 at 100) when only offers lasting 60 s or more are kept. The one flash print I did find (Sep 16 9:37:53 AM ET: YoY T3.0 YES at 14c for 6 ms after a sell sweep, taken by another bot within 6 ms) is outside the hunter's pair filter.

(d) 244 CPI liquidity-reward programs are active (full 41,000-row scan), each $100 per market per ~7-day period with a 1,000-contract target. The deep YoY quotes look reward-driven, not r-aware.

idea.name: Macro-ladder favourite carry: buy the 90-97c side of CPI rungs 14-21 days before the print, extended to payrolls, unemployment and PCE if their history agrees
idea.mechanism: At T-21 and T-14 days before a CPI release, buy the favourite side of any rung whose favourite ask is 0.90-0.97 with a quoted spread <= 5c, at the ask, 50 a leg, and hold to the print. Group cap $250 deployed / $150 max loss per print, shared with M-05 (same print).
idea.why_mispriced: The other side is the 3-10c lottery buyer on far macro rungs three weeks out (Burgi/Deng/Whelan longshot bias; Le 2026 finds favourites under-priced at 1 week to 1 month); the nowcasts that sharpen the market arrive only in the final week, which is exactly where the edge disappears.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The 2024-26 calibration holds (0 losses at 21 days). (2) Asks at those prices have size (the candles carry none). (3) One print is one cluster, so a single surprise can hit several legs. (4) The cached YoY rungs (the 'in-range' ones the R1 tester pulled) are not a selected sample.
idea.evidence_so_far: Measured on the R1-N1-01 tester's cached hourly candles (bid/ask) + Kalshi results, 367 markets, 22 release months 2024-04..2026-06, no API calls (macro_fav.py in r2-idle-cash-carry-book/): T-21, ask 0.90-0.97: 40 legs in 13 months, 0 losses, +6.0c a contract after taker fee (month-clustered +6.0c, se 0.3), halves +5.9 / +6.1c; ask 0.97-0.99: 34 legs, 0 losses, +2.2c. T-14: 56 legs in 17 months, 1 loss (KXCPIYOY-26JUN-T3.6 at 95c), +4.1c a leg, month-clustered +2.8c se 3.0. T-7 and T-3: 4-6 losses per 100, net about 0 or negative. Depth at the ask not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: ~6 legs a month at 50 contracts (~$280 deployed): ~$0.5/day at the measured edge, ~$0.25/day halved ($0.30/day per $100 locked over a 21-day lock); ~$1/day at $5,000 (200 a leg, depth permitting). Worst plausible day: a surprise print flips 2-3 legs at 50 = -$100 to -$140.
idea.settlements_per_day: 4 CPI ladders settle on one print a month (~0.03 clusters a day); payrolls/U3/PCE would add ~3 prints a month
idea.test_plan: Cheapest decision first: run macro_fav.py unchanged on KXPAYROLLS / KXU3 / KXPCE from /historical candles (~400 public GETs, one afternoon); bar 0-1 losses per 30 legs at T-21 and >= +3c month-clustered -- a fail there suggests the CPI result is selection. Then PAPER_BOOK.json cpi-fav-carry-paper-26nov: paper entries 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-26 13:29Z, 50 a leg, log ask depth; month bar losses <= 1 and mean >= +2c; go-live gate after 3 prints: >= 30 legs, <= 2 losses, mean >= +2c, median depth >= 50. Add READS_DUE.
idea.prior_reason: A clean calibration pattern (0 losses in 40 legs at T-21, halves +5.9/+6.1c, edge vanishing in the final week exactly where nowcasts arrive) and a ~400-GET backtest on other macro ladders decides it in a day; but depth at the ask is unmeasured, one print is one cluster, and the money is ~$0.5/day.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New: ledger SJ51/U17 are political carry; the econ-nowcast lane tested model-vs-market bracket picks and median bias, not long-horizon favourite calibration by horizon on macro ladders.
idea.worst_case: Same print as M-05: a 0.2-0.3 pp surprise flips several 90-95c legs and a pair band at once; capped at $150 loss per print by the shared group cap.

test.method: I froze the hunter's rule from macro_fav.py and did not re-tune it (re-implemented in fav_eval.py, scored in summarize.py). At 21/14/7/3/1 days before close, take the last hourly candle in (T-6h, T]. It needs a yes bid and ask with spread <= 5c. The favourite is YES if mid >= 0.5 (pay the YES ask), otherwise NO (pay 1 - YES bid). Hold to settlement. Net = win - ask - the per-order taker fee, ceil(0.07*50*p*(1-p)) cents / 50. Cluster = the print (close date): CPI's 4 ladders share one print, and payrolls + U3 share one. OUT-OF-SAMPLE means new series the hunter never saw, pulled from Kalshi /historical candles plus Kalshi results: KXPAYROLLS 354 markets (2023-03..2026-10), KXU3 312 (strikes within 0.35 pp of the previous print, an ex-ante filter), KXPCECORE 111, and CPI/CPICORE MoM 2022-06..2023-03 194. SELECTION CHECKS on the hunter's own CPI universe: a seeded random 80 of the 211 CPI YoY rungs the R1 cache left out, plus all 44 CPI markets of the 2025 shutdown months that R1 skipped. Significance is computed exactly, as P(losses <= observed | zero edge), two ways: independent legs, and one leg per print. The one-leg-per-print version is the honest one because legs in a print move together. Supply: live order books now on the 26OCT CPI/payrolls/U3 and 26SEP core-PCE ladders, plus the trade tape within +-12 h of 24 sampled CPI rule legs. Source rank: book quotes from candles (no size), real outcomes, trade tape. No live fills exist.
test.n_markets: 1,961 scored: 866 in-sample CPI (R1 cache) + 124 left-out CPI; 971 out-of-sample (payrolls 354, U3 312, core PCE 111, CPI MoM 2022-23 194)
test.n_independent_clusters: Rule legs (21 days out, ask 0.90-0.97): in-sample 40 legs / 13 prints; out-of-sample 47 legs / 19 prints (payrolls 27/15, U3 18/14, PCE 2/2, CPI 2022-23 0); pooled 91 legs / 33 prints
test.result:
IN-SAMPLE CPI, 21 days out, 0.90-0.97: 40 legs, 0 losses, +6.0c. Zero edge implies 2.6 losses here. So 0 losses would happen 8 times in 100 with no edge (independent legs), and 35 in 100 counting one leg per print. The hunter's "se 0.3c" is an artefact: with zero losses it only measures price dispersion. Adding back the rungs R1 left out gives 44 legs, 1 loss (KXCPICOREYOY-25OCT-T3.2, NO at 0.95), +3.7c, and a no-edge chance of 25 in 100.

OUT-OF-SAMPLE, the pre-registered decider (bar: 0-1 losses per 30 legs and >= +3c):
- 21 days out: 47 legs / 19 prints, 4 losses vs 3.0 at break-even, -2.5c a contract (print-clustered -0.8c, se 3.9). FAIL.
- 14 days out: 55 legs, 8 losses vs 3.6, -8.5c. FAIL.
- Payrolls: 21 days 27 legs, 4 losses, -9.0c; 14 days 23 legs, 7 losses, -24c. The Feb-2026 (-92k) and Jul-2026 (-23k) prints each flipped 3-4 favourite legs.
- U3: 21 days 18 legs, 0 losses, +6.1c (no-edge chance 32 in 100); 14 days 22 legs, 1 loss, +1.1c.
- Core PCE: 2 + 8 legs, 0 losses.
- CPI 2022-23: only 3 qualifying legs (wide spreads), so it tells us nothing.
- Halves, 21 days out: earlier +6.1c (9 legs), later -4.6c (38 legs).

POOLED in + out of sample, 21 days out, 0.90-0.97: 91 legs, 5 losses vs 5.8 at break-even, +0.5c a contract (clustered +1.1c, se 2.5). That is zero.

CALIBRATION out of sample (21 + 14 days): favourites priced 0.80-0.97 lost MORE often than their price says. At 0.90-0.93 they lost 17 per 100 against 9 implied; at 0.95-0.97, 8 against 4.5.

Only residual: the 0.97-0.99 bin at 21 days, 102 legs, 0 losses, +1.8c. The no-edge chance of that is 16 in 100 (independent) or 48 in 100 (per print). The same bin at 7/3/1 days has 2-4 losses and nets about 0.
test.artefact_checks: (1) The zero-loss se artefact is replaced by exact break-even probabilities. (2) Selection: the R1 cache dropped 211 YoY rungs and both 2025 shutdown months. Adding back a seeded sample and all the shutdown markets cut in-sample from +6.0c to +3.7c and added a loss. (3) The out-of-sample test used new series with the rule frozen. (4) The payroll losses are checked against Kalshi expiration values (-92,000; -23,000; 119k/178k/172k against NO-favoured rungs). (5) The fee is rounded up per 50-lot order. (6) Rule-risk tail: KXCPICOREYOY-25NOV (shutdown) settled all 9 rungs NO with a blank expiration value, so every YES favourite lost at once. (7) Not done (call budget): GDP, Fed ladders, 2022-23 CPI YoY.
test.supply_we_would_get: Not the binding constraint at 50 a leg. Today (CPI 26 days out, jobs 22, PCE 14), the favourite asks in 0.90-0.97 held 9, 30, 200, 233, 800, 1,820, 2,410, 3,609 and 9,012 contracts at the ask. That is >= 50 on 7 of 9 rungs, median about 800. In the historical tape, takers bought >= 50 at our price or better within +-12 h on 11 of 24 sampled CPI rule legs, and 0 on 8. Signal flow is about 1.4 qualifying CPI legs a month 21 days out (only 13 of ~28 months had any) plus about 1.5 jobs legs a month.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0/day. The pooled measured edge is +0.5c a contract, well inside +-5c of noise. At ~3 legs a month x 50 contracts that is about $0.01/day, and the payroll half is negative.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0/day. Depth would allow 200 a leg on most rungs, but there is no edge to size up.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: With 91 pooled legs at mean ask 0.936 (break-even loss rate 6.0 per 100), the standard error on the loss rate is about 2.5 points. Only an edge of about +6c a contract or more is detectable. The in-sample 40 CPI legs reject break-even only if 0 losses come in roughly 45+ independent legs. Detecting a real +2c edge needs about 770 independent legs (250+ prints).
test.worst_case: One surprise print flips every favourite leg on its ladder. The Feb-2026 payrolls print (-92k) lost 3 legs at 0.92-0.96 under this rule: about -$140 at 50 a leg, and about -$190 with the 14-day legs. The shutdown-month all-NO settlement (Nov 2025 core YoY) has the same shape on CPI.
test.next_test: None worth running. The writer should NOT add the hunter's PAPER_BOOK item cpi-fav-carry-paper-26nov. Three prints of paper cannot move a sample that needs hundreds, and the out-of-sample decider already failed. If the 0.97-0.99 residual is ever revisited, it needs the full 2022-26 history of every macro ladder (about 2,000 more public GETs for GDP/Fed/claims). Bar before any paper arm: >= 300 legs and <= 1 loss per 100.

idea.name: One-touch NO book on BTC monthlies filtered by a Deribit-DVOL barrier model (perp-delta hedge as a variance variant), plus a recorded KXBTCY year-end body gap -- one Deribit-anchored 'Kalshi overprices BTC tails' book
idea.lane: idle-cash-carry-book x crypto long-dated x cross-venue (Deribit)
idea.mechanism: At the ET-day close of day 2 and day 15 of each month, for every strike not yet touched, compute P(touch) with a driftless-GBM first-passage formula on Deribit DVOL; buy NO at 1 - yes_bid when yes_bid - model - fee >= 2c; hold to month end (a touch settles it early as a loss). 50 a leg, ~9 legs a month, ~$370 peak locked, group cap $300 together with the KXBTCY leg (same BTC path). Variance variant: hold a BTC perp position equal to the book's touch delta, re-set daily (needs margin access, see M-11). Record-only leg: the KXBTCY 80-95k body (three central brackets) at 0.332 combined vs a Deribit 25DEC26/26MAR27 smile interpolated to Jan 1 at 0.395, zero fee either side, hold to Jan 1 -- re-measured weekly before any money.
idea.why_mispriced: Touch YES and year-end tails are lottery tickets: on untouched mid-priced strikes Jan-Sep 2026 the realised touch rate was 14.9% (MAX) / 20.3% (MIN) against market mids of 20.5% / 25.7%, and Kalshi's year-end strip carries about twice Deribit's tail mass (below 60k ~0.09 vs 0.047; above 110k ~0.07 vs 0.035). Buyers pay for the story of a big move; the model filter keeps us off strikes that genuinely are close.
idea.must_be_true: (1) 2026's touch over-pricing persists into Nov-Jan. (2) NO depth at decision time >= 50 contracts (today 200-400 within 2 levels on the 92.5k MAX strike). (3) The backtest's fill (1 - the daily candle's yes_bid) was really buyable at that hour. (4) No 15-20% BTC month wipes several same-side legs beyond the group cap. (5) KXBTCY: Deribit's risk-neutral smile is a fair anchor for the Jan 1 BRTI average (6 days past the Dec 25 expiry) and the gap is not a stale book.
idea.evidence_so_far: Measured (ot_bt.py, ot_more.py in r2-idle-cash-carry-book/): Jan-Sep 2026 Kalshi daily candles + results (116 of 179 markets had candles; 7 months scored) vs Deribit DVOL and BTC-PERPETUAL closes: 62 NO legs, 1 loss, +15.5c a contract on a mean NO cost of 0.82, 7 of 7 months positive (t 3.36 by month), Jan-Apr +17.6c / May-Sep +12.1c; day-15 entries alone 36 legs, 0 losses, +11.8c. Blanket NO without the model: +4.0c, 12 losses in 97, t 1.05 -- the model does the work. YES side (buy touches the model calls cheap) MAX -3.0c on 31 legs: do not trade it. Today (16.5 days left) KXBTCMAXMON 92.5k bid 0.17 vs model 0.136 (NO +2.4c after fee). Hedge side only: perp fees 0.3 bp rebated / 4 bp tier 0, BTC touch depth $0.5-1.1k, worst 24-h BTC move 11.5%. KXBTCY measured once (2026-10-15 ~16:00Z): asks 0.137/0.115/0.080 vs model 0.156/0.135/0.104, strip ask sum 0.995, bid sum 0.952, OI 300-360k per body bracket; n = 1 year-end, no backtest possible. Cluster = month: n = 7.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: ~$1.15/day at 50 a leg on a halved edge (~$0.47/day per $100 locked; $0.95 at the measured edge); ~$4/day at $5,000 (200 a leg if depth holds). KXBTCY: model EV +6.3c per 33c package over 77 days (~$0.25/day per $100), +$6 EV / -$33 worst at 100 packages, one-off. The hedge changes variance, not the mean. Worst plausible day: 5 same-side legs touched in one move at 50 a leg = about -$205, on what is also a high-volatility day for the pin bot.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~0.3 legs a day (month-end, or early on a touch); KXBTCY once (Jan 1 2027)
idea.test_plan: Cheap artefact check now: re-score the 62 backtest legs with the HOURLY candle at the decision hour (yes_bid and NO ask both) to confirm the entry price existed with size, and confirm settlement came from the result field, not the index level. Then PAPER_BOOK.json (r2-idle-cash-carry-book/): onetouch-no-paper-oct (one leg, read Nov 1); onetouch-no-paper-nov (decisions 2026-11-03T05:00Z and 2026-11-16T05:00Z, 50 a leg, log NO-ask depth; month bar <= 1 loss per 15 legs and mean >= +3c; go-live gate after Nov-Jan: >= 25 legs, mean >= +5c, 2 of 3 months positive); a paper perp-hedge column (barrier-model delta at each daily mark; bar: P&L variance halved, mean unchanged); kxbtcy-body-record (weekly, ~3 Kalshi + 3 Deribit GETs). Add the Nov 1 read to READS_DUE. Live only with sign-off (new family).
idea.prior_reason: Seven of seven months positive with a model filter that clearly beats the blanket bet is good evidence for a carry idea, but n is 7 months from daily candles, the money is ~$1/day at this bank, the go-live gate needs Nov-Jan, and its worst day lands on the pin bot's worst day.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Extends 20261015-R1-C1-13 (not-tested this run) / U4 / SJ08 (the decided-minute lock is a different trade) with its first backtest (179 markets, 7 months), the MIN side, the day-15 entry and the finding that the model filter, not a blanket NO, carries the edge. KXBTCY extends r1 index #87 / SJ28 (dead zero-fee scalper) with a measured body gap 2-4x the carried '+1c'; SI50 / SJ45 (dead long-dated packages) were structural, not model-vs-market.
idea.worst_case: A 15-20% BTC month hits every NO leg on one side the same day: about -$205 at 50 a leg x 5 legs, plus up to -$33 per 100 KXBTCY packages on the same path; partly offset by the perp hedge if run.

test.method:
I re-ran the hunter's one-touch NO backtest (ot_bt.py, r2-idle-cash-carry-book) with every input taken at the decision time. Sources: Kalshi daily candles, whose end_period_ts falls exactly on ET midnight (verified 14400/18000 s mod 86400), plus Kalshi result and close_time. Deribit HOURLY BTC/ETH-PERPETUAL closes and HOURLY DVOL; the hour used is the one ending at the decision.

Fixes:
(1) True ET offset (EST before 2026-03-08), where the hunter used 04:00Z all year.
(2) Spot and vol from the hour ending at the decision. The hunter keyed Deribit DAILY candles by their START tick, so it read spot 28-52 h and DVOL 20-44 h AFTER the decision.
(3) 'Already touched' comes from Kalshi's own early close_time. The hunter used perp highs/lows through the next UTC day.
(4) The market must have been listed 1 h before the decision.
(5) September included. The hunter had no candles for it (63 markets missing).
(6) Fee: Kalshi per-order roundup at 50 contracts (quadratic, multiplier 1, verified on /series).

Self-test: barrier formula vs Monte Carlo GBM, ET offsets and fee rounding, all passed. Reproduction: fed the hunter's inputs, my pipeline returns exactly its 62 legs / 1 loss / +15.5c.

Rule kept exactly as pre-specified by the hunter: flat DVOL, buy NO when bid - model - fee >= 2c, days 2 and 15. Holdout: Jan-Apr vs May-Sep. ETH run as an out-of-sample asset. idea.name: Pre-market KXINXU stale-quote maker (R1-C2-08) priced off the US500 perp instead of a paid ES feed
idea.mechanism: C2-08's maker on the pre-market KXINXU ladder (04:00-09:30 ET) needs S_hat = ES x SPX_close / ES_16:00, but ES is not free in real time (Yahoo ES=F is 10 min delayed). Replace ES with the US500 perp mid (public REST, 1.2-5 s old): S_hat = perp_mid x S16 / perp_mid_16:00 plus a small calibrated overnight drift; quote C2-08's rungs off S_hat and pull before 08:30 ET releases (the perp lags ES by up to a minute). The US500 reference is the MerQube US Large Cap index (13,596 vs S&P 7,760; ratio 0.5680), so only ratios are used.
idea.why_mispriced: As C2-08: pre-market ladder quotes sit stale while futures move; the perp makes the fair free.
idea.must_be_true: C2-08 itself must pay (unproven: the index-ladders lane saw its sign flip by week); the perp keeps a two-sided pre-market book (it did on all 7 days since its 10-06 launch).
idea.evidence_so_far: 7 trading days 10-07..10-15 (small n): error of the 10:00 ET settle predicted at 08:00 ET -- perp 26.2 pts rms vs ES 25.8; at 09:25 ET perp 11.2 vs ES 9.0; at 09:59 ET 4.5 vs 3.9. Overnight drift ln(perp/ES) 16:00->09:30: mean +3.6 bp, max 7.9 bp (calibratable). Minute-return correlation with ES 0.72-0.98 after launch day (0.32 on day 1); ES leads the perp by one minute (lag corr 0.07-0.12; perp->ES ~0). C2-08's own P&L not measured here.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 by itself; C2-08's lane range was +$300 a close in a good week to -$400 in a bad one at its size (unproven). Same at $5k. Worst: a release-time jump with the perp a minute behind ES picks off stale quotes.
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 pre-market ladder (H1000) per weekday
idea.test_plan: Inside C2-08's paper run: log S_hat from the perp mid every minute 04:00-09:30 ET and, after the fact, from Yahoo ES; 10 trading days; bar: perp-based S_hat within 3 pts of the ES-based one on >= 90% of minutes and C2-08's paper P&L no worse with the perp fair. 1 public GET a minute (premkt.py in r2-perps-venue/).
idea.prior_reason: It removes C2-08's paid-feed blocker for free, but C2-08 is unproven with a sign that flips by week, and the feed comparison rests on 7 days.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New angle on 20261015-R1-C2-08 (not-tested this run): its blocker was the fair-value feed; this measures a free one.
idea.worst_case: A release-time jump with the perp a minute behind ES: stale quotes picked off; prevented only by pulling before 08:30 ET.
merged_from: r2:perps-venue: US500 perp as the free, real-time pre-market S&P fair for the pre-market KXINXU ladder idea (C2-08 enabler)

test.method: Sources: Kalshi public trade tape (rank 2) for every KXINXU H1000 market with pre-market volume (no outcome-based strike selection), 10-06..10-15, prints before 13:30Z, full cursor paging (286 public GETs); US500 perp 1-min bid/ask candles (public margin API, 10 calls); Yahoo ES=F and ^GSPC 1-min (merged r1 file + fresh 8-day pull). S16 = previous KXINXU H1600 settle. Q1: tracking of S_hat_perp = perp_mid*S16/perp16 vs the real-time ES fair ES*S16/ES16, every minute 04:00-09:30 ET, 7 days (10-07..10-15); drift offset fitted on 10-07..10-12, tested on 10-13..10-15. Added a HYBRID a bot can run for free: S_hat = ES(t-10min, Yahoo delayed)*S16/ES16 * perp(t)/perp(t-10min). refs.strongest_objection: The tester's ~$10/day rests on two things. (a) Fills were marked 60-300 s later against the same model fair that set the quotes. By construction that only shows the 2c half-spread we capture; it cannot show whether the model is wrong. (b) A 7-close settlement sim. I ran the tester's own rules on all 47 KXINXU H1000 closes from 08-11 to 10-15: quote round(100f) +/-2c, fill min(print, 20) whenever a taker prints at or through our quote, hold to the 10:00 result, 08:40-09:30 ET. I used a fresh ES fair, at most 60 s old. It loses $510 on the scored subsample. 23 of 47 closes lose, and it is -5.6c a contract pooled over 9,191 contracts. The tester's window (10-07..10-15) is the best of the 41 rolling 7-close windows (+$136, 0 losing closes). The other 40 closes lose $646 (-8.1c a contract), and 68% of 7-close windows lose. Cause: the model's spread is too narrow. Over 45-47 closes the rms z of the 10:00 settle is 1.21-1.54 at every grid time from 06:00 to 09:25 ET. The 10:00 settle lands more than 2 model standard deviations away 8.5-22% of the time, against 4.6% expected. The tester's 0.015%/min sigma floor binds at 55% of grid points. When the model and the market's mid differ by more than 2c, the model is the more extreme one 84% of the time. So 'takers pay 3.7c over fair' is mostly the model being overconfident, not stale quotes. The tester blamed r1's losing week on a stale fair; that does not hold up. With a fresh fair that week still loses $197 on the subsample, and the worst close is -$222 on 09-30. Scaling sigma 1.4x (fitted on the early closes) only gets to break-even: -$52 over all 47 closes, +$39 (se $13) on the later-half holdout. That is with best-case fills: we are first in the queue and no other maker competes. The idea as specified also fails its own feed bar. The perp-based S_hat was within 3 pts of the ES-based one on 67% of 1,862 minutes, against a 90% bar. Daily overnight offsets were 8.3, 5.7, 2.1, 0.0, 3.1 and 2.4 bp, which matches the tester.

idea.name: Short-horizon index momentum term in the forecaster's projection (identify better)
idea.mechanism: After a >= 2-sigma 10-s move the CF index itself keeps going: add E[next 10-60 s move] = beta x the 10-s move to the projection's spot for the forecaster and any mid-window model (negligible at the pin's 99.5c prices).
idea.why_mispriced: The random-walk model assumes no continuation; the composite index has short memory.
idea.must_be_true: The effect is large enough at the prices the forecaster trades (75-98.5c) to change decisions.
idea.evidence_so_far: Model fair continues +0.24c (+10 s) and +0.48c (+30 s) in pass 1, +0.29c (+60 s, t 3.2) pooled, of probability after 2-sigma 10-s moves vs ~0 on random-sign quiet seconds (327 hours, 1,290 closes). No P&L measured.
