test.method:
Sources: the raw settlement index (rank 1) plus Kalshi's own result field. No order book and no replay. One streaming pass with mom_pass.py, which passed its self-test, over C:/kals/kalshi_data/cfbenchmarks_value from 2026-09-01T22 to 10-15T20 UTC, using whole-second prints for the 9 forecaster coins.
(A) For each coin, I regressed the index's future path on its past 1-s, 9-s and 50-s moves. The future path is the sum over the next r prints of log(index/now) for r=1..30, plus the 10/30/60-s moves. Every second was sampled (a fixed grid, not trade arrivals), clustered by UTC hour.
(B) I computed the forecaster's own p at every (market, rel -31..-2) where all window prints are present. It uses bettor_paper.Tables f_sig 'blendvr', s_coef and the TRAIN f_calibrate, imported rather than rewritten. It matches the live bot's logged p_side EXACTLY on all 146 live fills.
I added a momentum term to the projection in three forms: M1 = beta x the 10-s move; M2 = the same but only after |z10|>=2; M3 = three lags. Coefficients were fit per coin on 09-02..09-21 and tested on 09-22..10-15.
Pre-registered bar (PREREG.txt, written before any number was seen): paired log-loss change in the 75-98.5c band, r 1..28, clustered by close; pass if t <= -2, DEAD if t > -1.
I also scored the term on OUR OWN 146 live forecaster fills (subaccount 2, results/forecaster-live-orders.jsonl) and the 446 paper 'real' fills. Strikes and results came from a public pull (48 calls, no auth).
test.n_markets: 36,024 settled 15-min markets read. Where all 60 prints were present (34,866 markets), the settlement computed from our index agrees with Kalshi's result on every one. Forecaster band population: fit 1,349 markets / 12,235 market-seconds; holdout 1,681 markets / 15,721 market-seconds. Own fills: 146 live fills in 115 markets (09-29..10-15), and 446 paper fills in 166 markets.
test.n_independent_clusters: Holdout: 1,002 closes (all coins of one quarter-hour count as one cluster). Fit: 842 closes. Index regressions: 459 fit hours and 534 holdout hours.
test.result:
THE INDEX DOES KEEP GOING, in both halves. Over the next 30 s it continues 7.7% (fit) / 10.4% (holdout) of its last 10-s move, pooled t 10.5 / 16.9. By coin: HYPE 18-19%, XRP 8-9%, BTC 2-4%. Summed over the next 30 prints the coefficient is +1.51 (t 9.9) in the fit and +2.27 (t 23) in the holdout.

BUT IT DOES NOT IMPROVE THE FORECASTER'S FAIR.
- Holdout band log-loss change: M1 -0.00011 (t -0.26), M2 +0.00015 (t +0.87), M3 +0.00020 (t +0.39). Fit period M1 +0.00069 (t +1.15, worse).
- Slope of the outcome surprise on the term's shift: holdout 0.69 +-1.45, fit -0.44 +-1.39. That cannot tell 0 from 1.
- Size of the shift: p moves by >= 1c on 7.9% and >= 2c on 2.7% of holdout band rows (median 0.09c, 99th percentile 3.3c).
- Our 146 live fills: M1 would have refused 6 fills, all WINNERS (-$6.50 of profit given up), and no losers. M3 refused 6: 1 loser (-$7.78 avoided) and 5 winners, net +$6.44. M2 refused none.
- Paper fills (100-lot): M1 refuses 13 fills in 12 markets, 2 of them losers (saves $38 at paper size). M3 refuses 17 fills in 11 markets, 3 of them losing markets (saves $204 at paper size). Three losers is noise, and M3 failed the calibration bar.

UNPROMPTED FINDING (identify better, same data): since 09-22 the forecaster's own p (no momentum) has been UNDER-confident across all band rows.
- The favoured side wins 3.6c more often than p says (2SE 1.0c, 1,002 closes).
- Weekly: +1.4 / +3.4 / +5.5 / +1.8c. 8 of 9 coins are positive; NEAR is -7c.
- Where p said 75-80c, the favourite won 87.4% against 77.5% stated.
- The z-scale with the best log loss is 1.15 in the holdout against 0.95 in the fit, so the sd is about 13% too wide.
- Likely cause: volatility fell after 09-22 (1-s RMS x1e-5: BTC 6.06->5.37, BNB 6.43->4.90, ZEC 19.0->15.2), while f_sig keeps half its weight on the fixed TRAIN (08-25..09-17) global sigma.
- On OUR fills it is the opposite: mean p_side 91.4%, we won 87.8% of 115 markets (14 lost), and paid 81.3% on average. The people selling to us know more, so this is not a licence to trade more.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) Model replication: my index-only p equals the live bot's logged p_side on 146/146 live fills and 427/427 paper fills (max difference < 0.000005).
(2) Settlement from our tape against Kalshi's result: 34,866 agree, 0 disagree.
(3) Self-tests pass: my local sigma equals bettor_paper.Engine.f_local_sigma; a planted AR(1) momentum is recovered (0.199 against 0.200 planted) and a world with none gives ~0; the regex parse equals the json parse on a real hour.
(4) The fit window 09-02..09-21 overlaps the forecaster's TRAIN window (08-25..09-17), so fit-period calibration is partly in-sample. The holdout is clean.
(5) The momentum features use only prints up to the decision second, so there is no lookahead.
(6) Power: if M1 were exactly right, the expected gain is 0.00033 nats per row. The holdout's smallest detectable change is about 0.0012 (2.8 SE). So "dead" here means it cannot be shown to help and cannot pay, not that it is proven wrong.
(7) The PC-off gap (10-14 03:29Z..10-15 04:39Z) has no rows; 54 hour files are missing in the window.
test.supply_we_would_get: n/a (model input). It would have changed 6 of 146 live forecaster fills in 17 days (4 in 100), and all six were winners.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0. M1 would cost about $0.38/day, the 6 refused winners spread over 17 days. For scale, the forecaster itself made +$87.12 in 17 days by its own log, about $5/day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0. The term cannot be shown to help at any size; at most a few tenths of a dollar a day either way.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: In the holdout, the smallest detectable log-loss change is about 0.0012 nats per market-second (2.8 x the clustered SE of 0.00043). That is about 4x the 0.00033 a perfectly right momentum term would deliver. Even seeing it would take about 4x the data: roughly 4,000 band closes, about 3 more months.
test.worst_case: The measurement put no money at risk. Had M1 been deployed, it would have given up 6 winning fills (-$6.50 over 17 days). There is no tail risk.

test.method:
Three measurements.

(1) Upset rate over many cycles. Source: the FiveThirtyEight checking-our-work data (github fivethirtyeight/checking-our-work-data: House, Senate and Governor files), using each year's headline model. For every race I took the favourite party's probability, summed over all of that party's candidates so that same-party top-two races in CA and WA are scored correctly. The forecast was the one issued 0-5 days before T-21, T-18 or T-14 (no look-ahead), and it was scored against the actual outcome. Coverage: Senate 2012-2022, House 2018-2022, Governor 2018 and 2022. Scripts: fte_calib.py and fte_score.py. This is a forecaster's probability, not a market price.

(2) Exit feasibility. Source: Kalshi's own /historical hourly candles from Nov 5 to Nov 25 2024 for the 92 race markets in the hunter's raw file (exit2024.py, 95 unauthenticated calls). For each market I measured how many hours it took for the winning side's bid to reach 0.99 and 0.98.

(3) Today's board. I took the hunter's elec_board.json (2026-10-15), kept the cheapest leg per event, and checked it against public ratings: Inside Elections Senate ratings of Oct 1 2026 (via 270towin) and Cook/Sabato governor ratings (via search).

Holdout: the 0.94-0.96 band was fixed in advance by the hunter. I split the 538 sample into earlier cycles (2012-2018) and later cycles (2020-2022).

Scratch folder: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-13/ (RESULT.json saved there, 3 MB). Source ranking: forecaster calibration plus Kalshi's own historical bids. No replay was used.
test.n_markets:
- 538: 199 race forecasts at 90-98% at T-18 (47 of them at 94-96%), plus 178 at 98-99.5%.
- Kalshi 2024 exit test: 92 race markets (57 presidential-by-state, 10 governor, 24 House, 1 House-margin).
- Today's board: 50 events at 94-96c, 5 of which are 2028 races.
test.n_independent_clusters:
- Senate: 6 cycles (2012-2022). House: 3 cycles (2018-2022). Governor: 2 cycles.
- Market-price evidence covers only one cycle (2024).
- Upsets cluster within a cycle, so the effective sample is far smaller than 199.
test.result:
**How often 538's 90-98% favourites lost (T-18, all offices):** 2 of 199, about 1 in 100 (range 0.3-3.6 in 100). The two losses were Feingold (WI Senate 2016, D, rated 93%) and Kent (WA-3 2022, R, rated 97%).
- 94-96% band: 0 of 47 lost.
- 98-99.5% band: 0 of 178 lost.
- Earlier cycles: 1 of 74. Later cycles: 1 of 125. Both halves say about 1 in 100.
- In the 2018 wave, all 27 Republican favourites at 90-98% held. The wave's losses fell at 80-90% (10 of 95 lost).
- So a careful forecaster's "95%" has meant about 99%.

**Exit on Kalshi 2024 (winning side's bid reaching 0.99):**
- Statewide races got there quickly: presidential-by-state 53 of 57 (median 8 h after the first polls closed), governor 10 of 10 (median 11 h).
- House races did not. Only 12 of 24 reached 0.99 within 20 days; 21 of 24 reached 0.98 (median 148 h), and bids sat at 0.96-0.98 for weeks. Those were competitive seats, so this is a pessimistic read for safe seats.
- Conclusion: the 99c exit works for Senate, Governor and AG legs, not for House legs. House legs should be scored at a 0.98 exit or held to the January 2027 settlement.

**Today's 94-96c band is contaminated:**
- 5 of the 50 events are 2028 races (GOVPARTYNH-28, SENATECO-28, SENATEIN-28, SENATEMD-28, SENATEOK-28), which would lock money for two years.
- North Carolina and Georgia Senate trade at 0.950/0.951 for the Democrat, but Inside Elections rated both Lean D on Oct 1. In the 538 history a race at that level of confidence lost about 10 times in 100. A plain price band therefore buys directional bets along with the safe carry.
- With a Safe/Solid filter, a party-balanced book is available:
  - D legs: Governor CT, MA, ME, MI (not-R), MN, NM (not-R), NY, RI; AG NM; House IL-08.
  - R legs: Senate AR, ID, TN, SD; Governor SC, TN; AG AL, OK; safe House seats such as GA-09 and IN-04.

**Money per 20-contract leg bought at 0.95 (fees included):**

| outcome | per leg |
|---|---|
| exit at 0.99 | +$0.71 |
| exit at 0.98 | +$0.50 |
| hold to January | +$0.93 |
| loss | -$19.07 |

- A 22-leg book (14 legs exit at 0.99, 8 House legs at 0.98) makes +$13.94 if nothing loses.
- At 0.5-1 losses per 100 legs, the expected result is about +$10 one-off on about $420, held about 25 days.
- Break-even loss rate: 3.6 in 100 with a 0.99 exit, 2.6 with a 0.98 exit, 4.7 if held to January.
test.artefact_checks:
- The favourite is picked from the forecast at the time, never from the result. Forecasts are dated on or before the target day, so there is no look-ahead.
- Probabilities are party-level, so same-party top-two races are not counted as upsets.
- The headline model was used per year (classic 2018, deluxe 2020/2022, polls-plus 2016). The deluxe and classic alternatives agree: 0-1 losses at 94-96%.
- Not measured: whether Kalshi's 95c means the same as 538's 95%. That link has not been measured for any cycle. The only market evidence is one cycle (2024: about 33 Kalshi and Polymarket races at 90-97c with 0 losses, already counted by the hunter).
- The 2024 House exit sample is competitive seats only, so it is pessimistic for safe seats.
- 2024 candles are in 1c steps, but the 2026 board quotes 0.1c steps. 2026 exit bids could sit at 0.985-0.995; not measured.
- The hunter's claim that Kalshi pays 4.05% interest on open positions is not verified by me.
- Ratings for the 20 R-favoured House legs could not be fetched (Cook returned 403, the Wikipedia table was missing); not measured.
- The tape was still being written 16 s before my check (C:/kals/kalshi_data, ticker and trade files at 4:22 PM ET). My process query could not see the recorders' command lines. Free disk 117 GB.
test.supply_we_would_get:
- After dropping 2028 races and races rated Lean or Toss-up, about 22 party-balanced legs remain today (11 D, 11 R) at 0.94-0.96.
- Almost all have at least 200 contracts offered at 0.97 or less. Exceptions: KY-04 (17 contracts), SC Governor (223), CT Governor (459).
- 20 contracts a leg is far below the available depth. 100 a leg also fits on all but about 3 legs.
- This is a taker buy of the favourite in the KXHOUSERACE, SENATE<ST>, GOVPARTY<ST> and KXATTYGEN<ST> markets.
- Whoever sells a 95c safe-seat favourite is likely a holder who wants cash, or the other side of a lottery-ticket buyer, so being sold to by someone better informed should be rare. Not measured.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now:
- About +$10 one-off over roughly 25 days (Oct 16 to about Nov 10), so about +$0.40 a day.
- It ties up about $420, which is 36% of the main bank.
- Only worth doing with cash that is genuinely idle. If the locked $420 shrinks the pin bot's bet sizing, it costs more than it makes (pin's daily value was not measured here).
test.worst_case:
- Two Safe-rated legs of the same party lose: -$38 at 20 contracts a leg, -$190 at 100 a leg. This never happened among 90%+ favourites at T-18 in 538's 6 cycles; the most was 1 per cycle.
- Tail case, three legs lose: -$57 at 20 a leg, -$286 at 100 a leg.
- Without the Safe filter, a polling miss toward the Republicans could flip both NC- and GA-type Lean legs bought at 95c together. That is the same -$38, but much more likely.
test.next_test:
Keep the pre-registered paper book election-carry-paper (entries 2026-10-16T16:00Z and 2026-10-20T16:00Z, read 2026-11-06), but change the rule before the first entry:
- (a) Drop any event that does not close in 2026.
- (b) Take only legs rated Safe/Solid by at least one of Cook, Sabato or Inside Elections on entry day. Likely ratings are allowed for Governor and AG legs only.
- (c) Score House legs at a 0.98 exit or held to settlement; score Senate, Governor and AG legs at 0.99.
- (d) Add a read-only hourly order-book logger on the paper legs from 2026-11-03T23:00Z to 2026-11-10 (about 25 GETs an hour) to measure when each leg's bid reaches 0.99 and 0.98 in 2026's price steps.

Bar unchanged: at most 1 loss in the book, and 2 losses in one party's legs raise the correlated-wave flag. The paper book can only catch a disaster (2 or more losses); it cannot show the edge, because expected losses are 0.1-0.25 legs.

Going live needs operator sign-off (new strategy family) and should use idle cash in a separate subaccount only.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k:
- At 100 contracts a leg, 22 legs, about $2,100 locked: about +$50 one-off, roughly +$2 a day over 25 days.
- It only happens once per two-year cycle, plus special elections.
- 2028 races at 94c would lock money for two years at about 3% a year, below the cash interest rate, so skip them.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
- The 538 sample has 0-2 losses in about 200 forecasts. Its upper limit is about 3.6 losses in 100, which is right at the 0.99-exit break-even. So the sample says the edge is probably positive but cannot rule out zero.
- A 25-leg paper book can only detect 2 or more losses.

refs.strongest_objection: The bank has no idle cash, so the +$0.40/day is a gross number that ignores what the cash already earns. The live bot sizes every bet from cash alone: read_bank() in C:/kals-live-0925j/research/pinrun.py reads /portfolio/balance `balance`, which leaves positions out, and size = bank / (4.00 x 3 x ~0.98). Putting $420 of the $1,155 main bank into election contracts for about 25 days cuts every pin bet, and the KXBTCD ladder, by 36% (98 contracts down to about 62). Moving the $420 into a subaccount first causes the same cut. I re-scored our own live fills from 10-04 to 10-15 at 0.636 times the size: 389 markets, pin made +$202.75 by its logs, and Kalshi's books agree to within a few dollars. At the smaller size it would have made $65 to $68 less. That is about $5.5-6/day given up to gain $0.40/day, so the net is about -$5/day, or roughly -$130 over the hold in exchange for a +$10 carry. The carry only comes out ahead if pin's true profit is under about $1.2/day. Pin's 21-day average on Kalshi's books is $21/day (give or take $10.7, counting each day as one data point), so that would take a drop of about 1.9 standard errors. My own board query adds a second problem. Very safe incumbents (Cotton AR 0.949 ask, Risch ID 0.949, Rounds SD 0.957, Healey MA 0.955) trade at the same price as the Lean-D races in NC (Cooper 0.952) and GA (Ossoff 0.953). The price band cannot tell safe from risky, so the whole edge rests on an outside Safe rating that no market sample has ever been filtered on. Kalshi's 2024 data has exactly one non-presidential market at 90-97c three weeks out, and it lost: HOUSEMOV-24-R-B1-5, a House-majority-margin market rather than a race. The 11 presidential-state wins are really one national outcome. Zero losses in about 33 races from one cycle puts the 95% upper bound near 9 losses per 100, against a break-even of 3.6 per 100. Several of the book's legs have also already left the 0.94-0.96 band (MI not-R 0.937, TN Gov R 0.920, NM 0.941). I did not refute the edge itself, a market 95c that really wins about 99 times in 100. It is just worth far less than the same cash earns in pin.
refs.independent_number: Pin profit given up at the smaller size: $5.4-6.2/day. This is my own re-score of 389 live pin markets from 10-04 to 10-15 at 0.636 times the size (bank $735 instead of $1,155). It loses $65.23-$68.09 of +$202.75 over about 11 trading days, after the gap when the PC was off. Script and output: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/refute-stats-20261015-R2-M-13/oppcost.py and oppcost.json. Separately, my own 26-GET board query (board_now.py) confirms all three series checked use the standard quadratic fee x1.

refs.strongest_objection: There is no idle cash; the money would come out of the pin bot's bet size. pinrun.read_bank() sizes off live CASH (/portfolio/balance `balance`), at about bank/11.8 (98 contracts at $1,155). Every other account also auto-sizes off its own pot (the operator's SNOWBALL order). Holding about $420 of election legs, whether in the main account or moved to a subaccount, cuts cash to about $735 and size to about 62. Replaying the October live orders (621 orders, 13 days; only 64% fill in full) with fills capped at 0.636 x requested gives 34.9% fewer pin contracts filled. Kalshi's own ledger (pinday.py) has pin making +$230 over the last 14 ET days, about +$16.5/day (30 days: about +$20/day, daily swing about $70). Forgone: about $5.8/day for the roughly 21-day hold, about $120, against a carry of about +$16. Net about -$5/day. The one way it survives: pin's marginal contracts earn under a third of its average, or pin's true mean is below about $2.2/day. Neither is measured (HANDOFF.md lists 'does pinrun's profit grow with bet size?' as an open lead). On the execution itself the tester was too pessimistic. The 2026 race rules add 'accelerated determination after a consensus of media organizations project the winner'. That clause is absent from the 2024 rules, and the 2024 race markets settled Jan 3-20 2025. Kalshi has used it: NJ and VA governor 2025 and VA AG 2025 settled on 2025-11-07, three days after the vote, and the 2026 CA-34/CA-37/WA-09 top-two House markets settled early. So decided legs should pay $1.00 within days, with no 0.98/0.99 exit and no exit fee. That makes it about +$0.93 per 20-contract leg instead of +$0.50-0.71, and break-even is about 4.6 upsets in 100. Fees checked on /series: quadratic x1 on GOVPARTY, SENATE, KXATTYGEN, KXHOUSERACE. Kalshi's interest accrues on cash plus positions (balance >= $250), so the lockup costs no interest. Depth at <= 0.96 is thin or zero on several 'Safe' legs (CT Gov 0, best ask 0.963; IL-08 0; KY-04 0; SD Sen 73; MN Gov 83; TX-22 127). TN Gov has repriced to 0.92. A resting bid would avoid the taker fee, but it also ties up cash, so the same objection applies.

test.method: I pre-registered the test (PREREG.txt) before scoring any fill: a static pre-game resting quote on NHL player props, scored against the public trade tape using its own fills and Kalshi's settlement values. Source rank is trade tape; no replay was used. Clock: K = occurrence_datetime - 3 h. Before the pull I checked this against ESPN's scheduled puck drop for all 107 games 09-29..10-14: 101 were exactly 3.00 h, 3 were 2.75 h, 1 was 2.67 h and 2 were 4.2 h (both on 10-01; excluded as a check). ESPN marks all 107 as regular season. Sample: every KXNHLPTS / KXNHLGOAL / KXNHLAST game closing 09-29..10-15 (13,007 settled markets). From each game and series I drew 2 markets with seed 1015, among lines listed at least 2 h before K, for 642 markets. For each I pulled 1-min batch candles and the full trade tape over K-6h..K; none was truncated. The rule is M-08's as_an_w.py with NHL constants. At K-S, read yes_bid b and yes_ask a, rest SELL YES at a and BUY YES at b (20 lots each), and pull at K-E. Fills come from fills_an.fill (self-test PASS) under FRONT / D200 / THRU queue brackets. P&L = price - 100 x settlement_value, so scratched-player scalar settlements are handled. There is no maker fee: all three series are fee_type quadratic x1, checked on /series. Windows: (90,0) is the bar cell; (180,60) and (120,60) are the idea's pull-before-lineup/goalie-news rule; (360,60) and (180,0) are extra. Clusters are games. In-sample is K < 10-08 00:00Z; holdout is after that. Variant: carry the standing quote forward up to 60 min. Candles are emitted on quote changes, so this scores every market that had a quote standing. Rebate: I re-attributed the lane's CLIFF combo-tape sample (168 hourly 5-s windows, 10-07..10-13) to NHL legs by scheduled start (nhl_cliff.py). I then computed our CLIFF score S = prod(1+F)-1 from our simulated fills and checked it against the 0.01 minimum (nhl_score.py, M-03's method). Dollars are scaled to every line listed per game (dollars.py). About 915 public no-auth Kalshi GETs (including 429 retries) and about 27 ESPN calls.
test.n_markets: 642 sampled NHL prop markets (214 per series) out of 13,007 settled. 329 had a fresh quote (at most 5 min old) at K-90; the carried-forward variant had 1,086 orders.
test.n_independent_clusters: 107 games on 16 nights. Bar cell (90,0): FRONT filled in 79 games (in-sample 43, holdout 36), D200 in 49. Carried-forward variant: 96 games (FRONT) and 66 (D200).
test.result: The bar failed and the pre-registered kill criterion was met (FRONT below -2c over at least 40 games in (90,0)). Figures below are gross per filled contract. Bar cell (quote K-90, pull at puck drop): FRONT -5.95c (se 3.36, 79 games, 2,611 contracts); D200 -9.86c (se 5.14, 49 games); THRU -7.35c (se 5.69). In-sample FRONT +0.30c and D200 +0.31c; holdout FRONT -16.59c (se 6.48) and D200 -25.80c (se 10.14). The idea's pull rule (quote K-180, pull K-60): FRONT -5.31c (se 3.83, 62 games); D200 -8.36c (se 5.15, 40 games). In-sample -4.95c / -11.03c; holdout -5.92c / -2.89c. Carried-forward quotes: (90,0) FRONT -5.93c (se 2.60, 96 games) and D200 -10.90c (se 4.15); (180,60) FRONT -4.14c (se 2.92, 87 games) and D200 -5.43c. Pooling both halves, 14 of 15 window x queue cells have a negative centre. The one positive cell is THRU K-120..K-60 at +5.94c (se 12.77, 17 games). Both sides lose: at K-90 FRONT, SELL YES -5.29c (73 games) and BUY YES -8.26c (31 games). So this is fills going against us, not an outcome streak. The quote's half-spread is +1.3c, and the fills we actually get earn about 7c less than that. By series (K-90 FRONT): PTS -0.75c, GOAL -7.41c, AST -11.59c. Rebate: about $6,600/day of CLIFF sits on the three series, and 87% of it comes from combos bought before puck drop (lenient reading of the live-event clause; 0 under the strict reading). At K-90 our score clears the 0.01 minimum on 27% (FRONT) / 15% (D200) of that pool. The upper-bound take is about $33/day at a full slate, roughly 1c per filled contract, about a fifth of the fill loss.
test.artefact_checks:
- Clock: the offset was checked on 107 of 107 games before any fill was scored. Dropping the 2 games whose ESPN start was 1.2 h before K gives FRONT -5.14c.
- Tape vs candles: volumes reconcile (229,822 vs 229,724 contracts over K-5.9h..K-1min).
- Empty tapes: all 263 have zero candle volume, so they are quiet markets, not failed pulls. None of the 642 tapes was truncated.
- Concentration: dropping the 3 worst games gives FRONT -3.51c (se 3.18), still negative. The 5 worst fills are only 16% of losing dollars. They are 6-15c longshot YES contracts we sold that then hit (Stamkos, Pastrnak, Hutson).
- Outcome streak ruled out: both quote sides are negative.
- Scalar (did-not-play) settlements: 251 of 13,007 markets, paid at settlement_value.
- Pull restart: I stopped and restarted my own pull processes mid-run, with dedup by ticker; all 642 markets have exactly one tape.
- Not measured: queue position (no historical sports depth exists, hence the brackets); a re-quoting bot (M-03 found re-quoting did not rescue NFL props); whether CLIFF pays this account for pre-game volume.
- Holdout vs in-sample: the holdout is far worse than in-sample. The pooled -6c is t = -1.8 to -2.3, so a small true edge is not excluded, but no cell supports one.
- Ops: the collector was writing (kalshi_data/trade/20261015T20 at 16:33 ET); free disk 117 GB; scratch folder 4.4 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: There are plenty of lines but little flow. About 119 lines per game are listed at least 2 h before puck drop across the 3 series, and there are about 6.7 games a night. The median line trades 259 contracts over its whole life. Only 23.5% of a line's volume trades in the last 90 min before puck drop (43% in the last 6 h); the rest trades in-game. A 20-lot quote at the best price at K-90 fills 25% of orders under FRONT and 12% under D200, about 4 contracts per order. At a full slate that is about 3,100 / 1,800 maker contracts a night, needing about $1,900 / $1,100 of collateral (each contract locks about 61c until settlement, about 3 h after puck drop). Capital is the binding limit: a $300 sleeve holds about 490 contracts a night. The fills are on the NHL prop leg books; the rebate is paid out of combo (KXMVECROSSCATEGORY) fees.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: Negative: about -$28 to -$54 a night at a $300 sleeve, with the rebate already included at its upper bound. The scaled full-slate loss is about -$9.40 per $100 of collateral a night under the pull rule, -$10.75 at K-90 FRONT, and -$13 to -$18 under D200. $0 if not run.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About -$140 to -$270 a night at a $1,500 sleeve, at the same loss per dollar of collateral. The rebate (about 1c a contract) cannot cover the roughly 5-6c a contract lost on fills.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: In the bar cell, se is 3.36c on 79 games, so the test can detect an effect of about 9.4c at 80% power. In the carried-forward variant, se is 2.60c on 96 games, about 7.3c. Confirming a +1c edge would need se around 0.36c, about 85 times this sample (several NHL seasons). More weeks of data can only strengthen the kill, not confirm an edge.
test.worst_case: The worst sampled nights lost 39-56% of that night's collateral under FRONT, and up to 73% under D200 on thin nights. At a $300 sleeve that is about -$120 to -$170 in one night, and 9-13 of the 16 nights lost money. A scratched player is not the tail: that line settles at Kalshi's fair price (251 of 13,007 lines did). The tail is several sold longshot YES contracts hitting on one night, for example a star scoring twice.
test.next_test:
None for this bot. Two keepers for the ledger:
1. NHL props join NFL (M-03) and WNBA (M-08). A static or re-quoted pre-game prop maker loses roughly 1-6c a contract to the people who hit its quotes, more than CLIFF pays back (about 1c, upper bound).
2. The CLIFF score is built from our fraction of each leg, not from contract counts, so thin legs earn more score per contract. Any future CLIFF design should be scored with nhl_score.py's method, not pool divided by volume.
Revisit only with a read-only orderbook recorder on NHL props, which would give queue position and a re-quoting replay. Bar: re-quoter FRONT and D200 gross at least -0.5c over at least 40 unseen games.

test.method: Re-ran the hunter's exact rule with no refit on fresh games. The rule: 90 min before scheduled kickoff (K = occurrence - 3 h), read the 1-minute candle at or just before that moment (no more than 300 s old, two-sided), rest SELL-YES 20 at the ask and BUY-YES 20 at the bid, leave it until kickoff, hold fills to settlement. Fill brackets come from the public trade tape via fills_an.fill, with the self-test passing: FRONT = first in line; D200 / D1000 = 200 / 1,000 contracts ahead of us; THRU = filled only when a print goes through our price. Profit per filled contract = price - 100 x payout. These series charge makers no fee (fee_type quadratic, checked via /series). Games are the clusters. Data, all public and unauthenticated: settled-market listings, batch 1-minute candles and trade tapes K-3h..K. Every NCAAF game the hunter had NOT sampled from 08-27 to 10-14 is included (342 new games, 7 Saturdays, so every game here is out of sample), the hunter's 45 games are kept separately, and KXNCAAF1H / KXNCAAF1HTOTAL (named in the idea, never pulled) were added and are reported apart. Checks: the kickoff clock against the ESPN schedule, and resting depth at the touch now on open markets for Saturday 10-17. Calls: 1,183 Kalshi public, about 100 ESPN, about 52 order-book. Source: trade tape (not our own fills). Files: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-21/ (pull.py, an.py, an.out, days.py, days.json, espn_check.json, depth_now.json, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 1,860 markets drawn: 683 new in the two primary series, 1,087 in the extension series, 90 the hunter's. 883 had a valid two-sided quote at K-90 under the pre-registered rule (1,648 if the candle may be up to 1 h old).
test.n_independent_clusters: Games with at least one fill at K-90 FRONT: 113 new primary, 133 pooled with the hunter's, 214 extension. About 390 distinct games over 7 Saturdays (08-29..10-10) plus weeknights.
test.result:
PRE-REGISTERED BAR (FRONT and D200 both >= +2c gross over >= 40 games): FAILED.

New games only, two primary series, 684 orders, per filled contract:
- FRONT -0.01c (se 2.43, 113 games, 3,497 contracts)
- D200 +2.68c (se 3.09, 96 games)
- D1000 +2.88c (se 3.85)
- THRU -0.36c (se 4.75)

Pooled with the hunter's 20 games: FRONT +0.50c (se 2.18, 133 games), D200 +3.89c (se 2.80). Bootstrapped by game, the chance FRONT is >= +2c is 0.19 (new) and 0.24 (pooled).

Robustness:
- Candles allowed up to 1 h old: new-game FRONT -0.05c (se 2.00, 169 games), D200 +1.37c (se 2.64). Both fail.
- Only ESPN-confirmed kickoffs: FRONT +1.04c (se 3.27).
- K-180: FRONT -1.32c, D200 -2.02c.

Extension series:
- 1H winner: FRONT +2.24c (se 1.84, 190 games), D200 +1.10c.
- 1H total: FRONT -0.36c, D200 -5.75c, D1000 -8.96c, THRU -12.52c.

All four series pooled at 20-lot on the drawn lines: FRONT +1.15c over 10,486 contracts (+$121 over 7 weeks), D200 +1.07c, D1000 +1.66c, THRU -0.65c. 3 of 7 Saturdays were negative at FRONT (-2.3c to +9.1c per contract).

WHY ZERO: the average over ALL quotes placed is +2.10c, exactly half the quoted spread (reconciled by hand). The fills we would actually get give back 1.71c of that to better-informed sellers, leaving about 0.

The hunter's two supporting facts were small-sample noise:
1. The touch fills were +3.69c on 20 games but are -0.01c on 113 new games.
2. The "average maker over every trade loses -14c" became +14.3c (se 5.8) on new games. Big prints (>20 contracts) were not worse for makers than small ones (+14.3c vs +9.0c), so the "sweeps hit deeper makers" mechanism is not there.

The 40-50c-wide-book premise is false before kickoff: 83% of K-90 quotes had spreads under 10c. The rebate adds only +0.24c to +0.47c.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) Half-spread check: the average over all quotes (+2.10c) equals half the median spread, so the scorer is consistent.
(2) Kickoff clock: ESPN start equals K exactly for 495 of 532 matched games. Re-scoring only those changes nothing material.
(3) Place in line: resting size at the touch today on open 10-17 markets has a median of 300 (YES bid) / 1,435 (NO bid) on team totals and 900 / 16 on 1H spreads, so a newcomer's 20-lot usually sits behind hundreds of contracts. FRONT is optimistic; D200/D1000 are the realistic brackets, and they read +2.7c / +2.9c with se 3-4c, which is not different from 0.
(4) One game (26SEP06WSUWASH) carries the new-sample FRONT. Without it the mean is -0.56c.
(5) The 300 s candle filter drops about half the markets (candles are written only when something changes). Relaxing it to 1 h gives the same answer.
(6) Skipping zero-volume tapes was validated: 0 of 84 traded windows missed on the hunter's data.
(7) No tape truncated, no HTTP errors.
(8) About 80 cells were looked at. The best one (1H winner FRONT, t about 1.2) is post hoc and not significant.
Recorders: cfbenchmarks_value and feed_data were still being written at 16:48 ET after the job. Free disk 117 GB. Scratch folder 7.8 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: The supply is on the Kalshi NCAAF pre-game books (team totals, 1H spread, 1H winner, 1H total). About 90-115 games each Saturday, with about 62 eligible lines per game. Quoting just ONE drawn line per series per game at 20-lot filled about 1,400 contracts per Saturday at FRONT, so cash limits a bot, not flow. A $300 sleeve gets about 600-1,200 filled contracts per Saturday. Saturdays only, with about 7 regular-season Saturdays left.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0 per day. The pre-registered cell nets -0.01c per contract. The most generous honest reading (+1c per contract, all four series) on about 1,000 contracts per Saturday is about +$10 per Saturday, or about $1.4 per day, and that is indistinguishable from 0 (range -$15 to +$28 per Saturday).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $0 per day. A $1,500 sleeve (about 5,000 contracts per Saturday) gives a generous reading of about +$50 per Saturday (about $7 per day), with a 95% range of -$75 to +$140 per Saturday.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: With 80% power: about 6.8c per contract for new-game FRONT (se 2.43), about 5.1c pooled (se 1.83), and about 3.1c for all four series on tight books (se 1.10). The 95% upper bound rules out a FRONT edge above about +2.8c to +4.8c. A +1-2c edge, worth about $1-3 per day here, cannot be confirmed or ruled out by any affordable sample.
test.worst_case: Measured on the drawn lines at 20-lot: worst single day -$46 (Thu 09-03 slate). Worst Saturday per contract was -2.3c (FRONT) to -8.6c (THRU, 09-19). At about 1,200 contracts that is -$28 to -$100 on a bad Saturday; at $5,000 it is -$115 to -$430. On top of that, 37 of 532 games' ESPN start differed from K by 1 min to 3 h, so a quote could stay up into live play.
test.next_test: None: drop. The pre-registered bar failed on 113 fresh games, and the hunter's mechanism is not in the data. Only a re-quoting maker with its true place in line could change this. That needs a book recorder (orderbook_delta + trade on all NCAAF eligible markets for 2 Saturdays), with a bar of >= +2c per filled contract over >= 60 games on the second Saturday. It is not worth building for a 0.24-0.47c rebate and about 7 Saturdays left. If a sports book recorder is built for the NFL/NBA prop ideas anyway, add these four series to it at no extra cost.

idea.name: Post-big-move maker bid on the 15-min crypto series: after a >= 3-sigma 10-s index move with 120-600 s left, rest a bid 1c under the mid on the favoured side for 60 s
idea.mechanism: The mid keeps drifting toward the model after big index moves (+1.24c over 60 s after >= 3 sigma, +1.95c after >= 4 sigma, control +0.04c). A resting bid (makers pay no fee on these series) that fills captures part of that drift without the ~3.5c round trip a taker pays; hold to settlement or exit by a resting offer.
idea.why_mispriced: The residual 1-2c of an index move reaches the 15-min book over ~1 minute; a patient bid sits where impatient sellers arrive.
idea.must_be_true: Fills are not concentrated in the cases where the move reverses -- ledger D17: every one of 12 maker variants on these books lost in the queue sim; W16: resting bids filled 100 in 100 losers.
idea.evidence_so_far: Drift on the true book (holdout 09-22..10-15: |z| >= 3, 3,606 rows / 660 closes, mid minus fair +1.24c t 12.5; |z| >= 4, 1,145 rows / 444 closes, +1.95c t 10.1). Maker fill rate and adverse selection NOT measured. The taker version is dead (see dropped: mid-window drift).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not measured; at most a few $/day at 20 lots if fills were neutral, which they probably are not. Worst plausible: 20-lot bids filled into reversals, -$10 each.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~250 >= 3-sigma triggers a day across 9 coins
idea.test_plan: research/makersim.py queue replay at the trigger seconds (can kill, cannot prove); kill if filled bids earn <= 0 after 200 closes.
idea.prior_reason: The drift is real and precise, but every maker variant on these books has lost to adverse selection (D17, W16) and a replay can only kill it.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: D17/W16 tested resting quotes without an index-move trigger; the trigger-conditioned drift is new.
idea.worst_case: Adverse selection makes every fill a loser: -$10 per 20-lot fill.

test.method: Queue replay on the TRUE book (orderbook_snapshot + orderbook_delta rebuilt per market, mw_scan convention) plus the trade channel, C:/kals/kalshi_data read-only, one hour at a time (peak ~137 MB). Source rank: settlement index (trigger, model fair, own 60-print settlement check) + trade tape (taker sells that would hit our bid) -- a replay, so it can kill, not prove. Rule frozen from the idea and pre-registered in PREREG.txt before any tape was read: |10-s index move| >= 3 sigma (trailing-600 1-s sd), 120-600 s to close, 60-s refractory per market; at Kalshi send time of the print + 75 ms (sensitivity 250 ms) rest a 20-lot BUY on the move's side at (side mid - 1c) floored to the tick; mid needs both sides and spread <= 10c; lives 60 s; maker fee 0 (fee_type quadratic = taker-only); hold to settlement. Fill models: PESS (primary: join behind all size at P, queue shrinks only by taker sells printed at P, any taker sell printed below P fills us), OPT (queue also capped by depth left at P), FRONT (first in line), each with/without CROSS (an offer posted at/through P after the other bids at P are gone fills us). Marks: settlement (truth) and model fair at fill second / fill + 60 s (lower-variance index mark). Hours: every 2nd UTC hour 2026-09-02T00..10-15T18 in fixed-seed random order; 83 processed (36 fit < 09-22, 47 holdout >= 09-22), 8 tape-gap hours skipped. Clustered by close time (all 9 coins of one close = 1 cluster). Scripts: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-19/mk_sim.py (self-test PASS), mk_an.py, mk_day.py, mk_outlier.py, validate.py; outputs an_final.txt, mk_orders.jsonl, mk_hours.txt; RESULT.json saved there.
test.n_markets: 4,016 bids placed in 2,245 markets (9 coins); 1,812 bids filled under PESS (959 holdout, 853 fit); 30,352 contracts filled.
test.n_independent_clusters: 330 closes with a bid (fit 143, holdout 187); 318 closes with a PESS fill (fit 140, holdout 178). Below the pre-registered 200 holdout closes needed for a pass.
test.result: PRIMARY (PESS, trades only, 75 ms, settlement): fit +2.09c/contract (2SE +/-2.69, t 1.55, 140 closes); HOLDOUT +0.22c (2SE +/-3.15, t 0.14, 178 closes, +$36 on 16,215 contracts). The pre-registered pass bar (holdout > 0 with t >= 2, fit > 0) FAILS. REALISTIC fill set (PESS + offers that cross a bid left alone): fit -0.68c, HOLDOUT -1.66c (2SE +/-2.62, t -1.27, 181 closes, -$478). That meets the idea's own kill line (filled bids earn <= 0). ADVERSE SELECTION, measured on the index: when a bid is hit, model fair is +2.39c above our price (holdout, t 15); 60 s later it is +0.67c (2SE +/-1.32), so about 72 in 100 of the edge is gone within a minute. Filled bids see the index move 1.48c against them over the order's life, while unfilled bids see it move 1.32c in their favour. Win rate is 62 in 100 filled vs 66 in 100 unfilled at the same ~62c price. If EVERY bid had filled: holdout +1.98c (2SE +/-3.01). The drift is real, but our fills come from the wrong half of it. Queue position does not rescue it: FRONT (first in line) holdout +0.16c and OPT +0.00c, both <= PESS. 250 ms latency: holdout +0.45c (t 0.29), +cross -1.95c. Subsets (diagnostic only, many looks): |z| >= 4 holdout +1.83c (2SE +/-6.62, 91 closes); bids alone above the best bid holdout -5.13c. Dropping 85 orders where model and book disagree by > 25c changes nothing (holdout +0.22c -> +0.22c).
test.artefact_checks: Fill-engine self-test PASS (queue at P, partial fill, sweep below P, wrong taker side ignored, NO-side mirror, cross counted once, 0.1c tick taper, skip rules). Book rebuild: 8 of 8 trigger mids identical to the hunter's mw_drift rows for the same market and second (mw_scan itself agrees with the ticker channel 99.97 in 100). Settlement: Kalshi result vs our own 60-print average, 0 mismatches in 3,922 markets. Prices decoded once from *_dollars strings into 1/10000 units (no magnitude inference). Fill counts look sane: on average 16.8 of 20 contracts filled; fill rate 45 in 100 (PESS) / 68 in 100 (+cross). Edge-at-fill of +2.4c (t 15) confirms bids really sit under model fair when hit, so the decay to ~0 is selection, not a pricing bug. Outlier check (model-book gap > 25c) moves nothing. Every result rests on a REPLAY. It cannot see post-only rejections, our order changing others' behaviour, or live latency. Each of those can only make a maker's real fills worse or rarer, not better, so a replay result of ~0 is a kill. Recorders: trade, cfbenchmarks_value and feed_data/bitstamp files were written within seconds at 20:29Z; free disk 117 GB; scratch 1.5 MB; no process touched.
test.supply_we_would_get: On KXBTC15M/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE/BNB/HYPE/ZEC/NEAR 15-min books: ~1,160 trigger bids a day across 9 coins. PESS fills ~45 in 100 (about 520 filled bids, ~8,800 contracts a day at 20-lot bids); with crossing offers ~68 in 100 (~15,500 contracts a day). 98-lot bids not simulated: fills come from taker sells averaging under 20 contracts per hit, so supply would not scale linearly with size.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0 or worse at 20-lot bids. Holdout is +$19/day if no offer ever crossed our bid (2SE about +/-$261/day), and -$244/day if crossing offers fill us, which is the realistic case unless every seller uses post-only. The fit half was +$197/day (trades only) and did not survive the holdout. 98-lot: not measured.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Not measured beyond 20-lot bids. Per-contract edge is ~0 (trades only) to -1.7c (with crossing offers), so ~$0 or negative at any bank.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Holdout settlement 2SE +/-3.15c a contract (~+/-$261/day at 20-lot bids); index mark at fill + 60 s 2SE +/-1.32c. The sample cannot tell +0.5c from 0. It does rule out capturing the hunter's +1.24c drift net: holdout mark +0.67c, settlement +0.22c.
test.worst_case: At 20-lot bids: worst single close (all coins) -$82 trades-only / -$114 with crossing offers; 5th-percentile close -$29 / -$56. A full day's 1-sd swing is $172 / $278, so a 1-in-100 day is about -$300 (trades-only) to -$835 (with crossing offers). That is far too large for a ~$0 average on a $1,155 bank.
test.next_test: None recommended. Only a live test could overturn a replay, and the replay's friendliest model is already ~0 in the holdout. If someone insists: 1-lot live bids on the exact rule for 5 days (~5,800 bids, ~2,600 fills, worst day ~ -$40). Pass bar: >= +1c a contract at settlement with t >= 2 over >= 300 closes, AND a live fill rate within 10 in 100 of the replay's 45 in 100. Not worth the bank slot versus other leads.

idea.name: Post-goal over-reaction fade in the lower-liquidity soccer leagues: buy NO on the first-goal scorer 60 s after the goal (maker form: rest the scorer's YES ask), forward paper read to Nov 15
markets: big European series (EPL, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, UCL, UEL) as control
idea.mechanism: Taker: 60 s after the first goal, buy NO on the scorer's win at 100 - yes bid and hold to settlement. Maker: for 15 min after the goal, rest the scorer's YES ask (a NO bid) at the touch and hold fills. The maker form suits series with no maker fee (ARG, DIMAYOR, Brasileiro, MLS, Liga MX are 'quadratic'; Ligue 1 charges makers).
idea.why_mispriced: If real, the scorer's price overshoots after a goal in the lower-liquidity leagues (the opposite of the Betfair paper): in the next 15 min the scorer's mid falls back 1.9c pooled and 2.7c in the four lower leagues. The counterparties would be momentum buyers after the goal.
idea.must_be_true: The overshoot is larger than spread plus fee (taker ~2.2c) or than the cost of adverse fills (maker), and the size seen only in October is not noise.
idea.evidence_so_far: Measured, cluster = match. Fade at +60 s in the 12 fully covered leagues (740 goals): -0.08c (se 1.66) -- DEAD pooled; fit half -1.89c, October +6.60c (se 3.68, 158). Four lower leagues back-filled to full coverage (295 goals): fade +2.43c (se 2.68); fit +1.39c (se 3.06), October +5.74c (se 5.57) -- both positive, neither significant. MLS + Liga MX every goal (199 matches): +0.72c (se 2.22). Scorer mid markout +60 s to +15 min: -1.86c (se 0.66, 730) pooled, -2.74c (se 1.05, 301) lower leagues, -1.24c (se 0.86) top-8 (markouts drop one-sided books, a small downward bias is possible). Maker fills NOT measured (no soccer book recording). An earlier -8c 'over-reaction' was a lifetime-volume selection artefact.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Central $0. If the lower-league +2.4c is real: ~5-6 qualifying goals a day x 30 contracts (thin books) x 2.4c = ~$4/day at $1,155; ~$10-15/day at $5,000, limited by book depth (not measured). Worst plausible: 6 of 6 scorers win in a day: about -$60 at 30 lots, -$190 at 98.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~5-7 first goals a day in the 4 lower leagues; ~12.7 across all 12
idea.test_plan: Pre-register now, read 2026-11-15: weekly public pull of 1-min event candles (1 call per match) for every settled match in the 12 leagues, Oct 15-Nov 15 (goal_fade.py, soccer_clean.py in r2-sports-inplay-event-triggers/). Bar: fade at +60 s >= +2c after fee on >= 150 first goals in the 6 non-European leagues AND >= +1c in the top-8; placebo within +-2c. Maker form needs a 1-week order-book recording of 30 matches to count fills at the touch after goals. Add READS_DUE 2026-11-15.
idea.prior_reason: Dead pooled (-0.08c), alive only in a lower-league subset at 0.9 se whose strength sits in October; the forward read is free but takes a month and the books are thin.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New trigger and measurement; its maker form is an instance of the in-play momentum-overshoot offer (20261015-R1-N2-03, dead this run) and gives it its first post-goal markout; ledger SI58 killed the stale-offer speed race, not the slow fade.
idea.worst_case: Each fade risks the NO price (~32c), about $10 at 30 contracts; a day where 6 of 6 scorers win costs about -$60 at 30 lots, -$190 at 98.

test.method:
I ran a backward out-of-sample test and wrote its bars in prereg.txt before computing any number. The hunter's Aug16-Oct14 window starts exactly at the Kalshi /historical cutoff (2026-08-16), so every earlier match was untouched.

Data pulled:
- /historical/markets listed 1,955 settled 3-way games in ARG, DIMAYOR, Brasileiro, Ligue 1, MLS and Liga MX (May 2025 to Aug 15 2026).
- These were matched to ESPN scoreboards (1,844 matched; the result had to agree with ESPN) and to ESPN summary keyEvents for the goal times.
- For each match with a goal: 1 public call for the first scorer's 1-min /historical candles.

The hunter's rule, re-implemented on the scorer's market (fade_holdout.py, self-test passes), reproduces his in-sample four-league number exactly (+2.43c, se 2.68, n 295).
- Fade = buy NO at 100 minus the yes bid, at the first candle close at or after T_trig + 60 s.
- T_trig = the later of the ESPN goal time and the Kalshi candle with a jump of at least 5c.
- Spread at most 4c; hold to settlement; taker fee 0.07p(1-p).

Maker form: I pulled the scorer's public trade tape (/historical/trades) from T_trig + 60 s to + 16 min on the 120 newest holdout matches. Every taker-YES trade is a fill that a resting YES ask would get; each was scored to settlement and at a 15-min markout.

Sources: trade tape and candles (we have no live fills in soccer). Cluster = match, one first goal each.
test.n_markets: Holdout: 735 first goals with a valid +60 s entry (996 built), four lower leagues, May 2025 to Aug 15 2026. Maker trade-tape check: 120 matches. In-sample (hunter's, reproduced): 295.
test.n_independent_clusters: 735 matches (one first goal per match). Maker check: 120 matches.
test.result:
Holdout, four lower leagues (the pre-registered test): the fade at +60 s is -3.37c a contract after fee (se 1.59, n 735); at +300 s it is -2.24c (se 1.50, n 822). In-sample it was +2.43c (se 2.68). The pre-registered dead bar (mean at or below 0) is met with room.

By period, all negative:
- 2025: -4.71c (se 3.65, n 130)
- 2026 Jan-May: -2.25c (se 2.00, n 490)
- 2026 Jun-Aug 15: -6.64c (se 3.78, n 115)

By league: ARG -6.51c (se 3.02), DIMAYOR -5.81c (se 3.49), Ligue 1 -5.33c (se 2.98), Brasileiro +3.22c (se 3.22). One positive league at 1 se is what chance gives across 6 looks.

The result holds when restricted to clean name matches, by goal minute, for underdog or favourite scorers, at spreads of 2c or less, and at higher match volume.

Book check: buying the scorer at +60 s gives -1.01c (se 1.59). Buy plus fade = -4.4c, which is the spread plus two fees, so the post-goal price is about right.

Maker form:
- Scorer's mid move from +60 s to +15 min: holdout -0.70c (se 0.61, n 714) against the hunter's in-sample -2.99c, so the maker's source mostly disappears.
- Maker filled at the ask with no adverse fills: -0.41c (se 1.59).
- Maker on the real post-goal YES-taker flow (120 matches): -3.35c a contract held to settlement (se 3.42); 15-min markout +0.62c (se 1.14), roughly the half-spread.

Combined in-sample plus holdout: four leagues -1.71c (se 1.37, n 1,030); all six non-top leagues -1.37c (se 1.27, n 1,227).
test.artefact_checks:
1. Reproduction: my scorer-only code gives the hunter's +2.43c (se 2.68, n 295) to the cent, so the holdout difference comes from the data, not the code.
2. Price unit was decided from the whole holdout sample: every bid and ask falls between 9 and 99 after multiplying dollars by 100.
3. Timing: 996 of 1,002 holdout matches show the scorer's jump of at least 5c within -3 to +4 min of the ESPN goal time.
4. Consistency: buy plus fade equals minus (spread + 2 fees), as it must.
5. Wrong ESPN pairings: keeping only name similarity of 0.9 or more changes nothing (-2.95c).
6. Maker trade tapes: 21 of 120 hit the 1,000-trade page limit (the newest part is kept). This affects only the maker number.
7. The holdout is earlier in time, with thinner 2025 books. The 2026 Jan-May slice alone (-2.25c, n 490) is the closest comparison and is still negative.
8. Not measured: the MLS + Liga MX 2026 holdout (only 4 matches reached before the call budget ran out). Their in-sample was already about zero (+1.14c, se 3.42).
test.supply_we_would_get: Supply is not what limits this. In the 15 minutes after a first goal, takers bought a median of about 18,700 contracts of the scorer's YES (p25 about 8,500) in these leagues. The spread at +60 s is a median 1c (p90 3c). There are about 5-6 qualifying first goals a day in the four leagues. The offers exist; the edge does not.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 (dead). Traded at 30 contracts it would expect about -$6 a day (-3.4c x 30 x about 6 goals).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0 (dead). At 98 contracts it would expect about -$20 a day.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: The holdout can detect about 3.2c a contract at 2 se (per-goal spread about 43c, n 735). The proposed Oct 15 - Nov 15 forward read would see about 170 lower-league first goals, giving se about 3.3c. It could only detect an edge of about 6.6c or more, so it could not have confirmed the claimed +2.4c even if real.
test.worst_case: Not proposed. If it were traded, a day where all 6 scorers go on to win would cost about -$60 at 30 contracts and -$190 at 98.
test.next_test:
Nothing further for this idea. Record it dead in IDEA_LEDGER with the killing numbers: holdout fade -3.37c (se 1.59) on 735 first goals, and the maker's 15-min markout -0.70c. Do not add the Nov 15 READS_DUE paper read; it has no power.

For later: /historical serves 1-min candles and trades for all soccer before 2026-08-16. Any future in-play soccer idea should be tested on that earlier sample first, using pull_hist.py, fade_holdout.py and maker_trades.py in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-15/.

Housekeeping: 1,300 public Kalshi GETs used, no auth. The recorders' command lines could not be read, but their tape files were being written at 16:58 ET. Free disk is 117 GB. RESULT.json is saved in the scratch folder.

idea.name: Late level-score TIE buyer in soccer: still level at 65' with no goal in the last 3 minutes, buy the tie at the ask (pre-registered forward read)
idea.mechanism: At fixed second-half clock points (60', 65', 70', timed from the 2nd-half kickoff), in a level match with no goal in the previous 3 minutes, buy the TIE at the ask and hold to settlement. Pre-registered decision point: 65'.
idea.why_mispriced: If real, bettors over-weight 'someone will score' late in level games (the mirror of the late longshot bias); counterparties are home/away buyers chasing a winner.
idea.must_be_true: Outside this one sample, the tie wins more often than its ask plus fee at those clock points.
idea.evidence_so_far: Measured on the 8 fully covered series, 0-0 matches included after back-fill. Tie won - mid: 60' +4.58c (se 4.17, 143 matches), 65' +6.97c (se 4.48, 128), 70' +8.70c (se 4.59, 118); buy at ask +2.4 / +4.7 / +6.4c. Random-instant check (level at 0-0, 60'-85', 12 leagues): won - mid +5.15c (se 4.39, 124), buy at ask +2.95c. The instants overlap (same matches), there are 10 clock looks, each 1-1.9 se: none significant. Ledger SJ50 found the opposite sign for a different state (late tie at 8-20c: 5 of 65 won).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Central $0. If +3c held: ~2 qualifying matches a day x 98 x 3c = ~$6/day at $1,155; ~$25/day at $5,000. Worst plausible: 3 tie losses in a day at ~40-48c ~-$135 at 98 lots.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~2 qualifying matches a day in the 8 series
idea.test_plan: Forward read on the same weekly candle pull as M-15 (no extra calls). Bar, pre-registered today: won - ask - fee >= +2c on >= 150 matches at the 65' point. Add READS_DUE with M-15.
idea.prior_reason: Every clock point is 1-1.9 se after 10 looks and a related state (SJ50) went the other way; the forward read is free but needs ~75 days for 150 matches.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New cell (level score, mid second half); SJ50 measured a different state (late tie at 8-20c).
idea.worst_case: Tie at ~40-48c: a loss costs ~$45 at 98 lots; 3 losses in a day ~-$135.

test.method: I wrote down the test and its pass/fail bar before computing any number from the older data (C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-16/prereg.txt). The check looks backward: the hunter formed the idea on 16 Aug-14 Oct 2026, so I tested it on matches from before then. Sample: every settled 3-way match in the 8 series that closed before 2026-08-16, from Kalshi's historical tier. That is the full 2025-26 seasons of EPL, LaLiga, Serie A and Bundesliga, UCL and UEL including the 2026 qualifiers, and MLS and Liga MX from May 2025 to Aug 2026. No volume filter, and 0-0 matches included. I listed 2,739 Kalshi events and matched 2,580 to ESPN scoreboards. I dropped 3 where the result disagreed without extra time; matches that went to extra time or penalties are kept with Kalshi's 90-minute result. Candidates were chosen on in-game score only: level by ESPN's game clock at some minute from 57' to 73'. That gave 1,080 matches, and I pulled ESPN's event timeline and the TIE market's 1-minute historical candles for all of them. The rule is identical to the hunter's ht_diag.py, and before touching the older data I re-ran his own data with my code and got his numbers to the cent (65' +4.69c se 4.48 n 128). The bot looks at minute t, counted from ESPN's second-half kickoff time. It needs the score level, no goal in the previous 3 minutes, a TIE quote no older than 120 s, and a spread of 4c or less. It buys the TIE at the ask, pays the taker fee of 7p(1-p) cents a contract, and holds to settlement. Each match counts once per clock point. Sources: Kalshi 1-minute quote candles plus ESPN. We have no fills of our own in soccer, and no replay was used. Kalshi public calls: 1,404, including retries after rate-limit refusals.
test.n_markets: 630 matches at the pre-registered 65' point (661 at 60', 615 at 70'); 1,080 candidate matches pulled out of 2,580 matched events
test.n_independent_clusters: 630 matches (one decision per match per clock point; different games with independent outcomes)
test.result: At 65', the pre-registered point, the older data says buying the tie at the ask loses 1.77c a contract after fee (se 1.97, 630 matches). The bar was at least +2c, more than 1.5 se, on at least 150 matches, and "dead" if the mean is zero or below, so it is DEAD. Won minus mid is +0.78c (se 1.97): the tie is priced at its fair middle price, so a taker just pays half the 1c spread plus a fee of about 1.7c. Other clock points: 60' -1.99c (se 1.91, 661 matches); 70' -2.07c (se 2.00, 615); 55' +1.39 (1.89, 673); 75' -1.38 (2.05, 571). At 65' by group: the six European series -1.88 (2.28, 468); MLS and Liga MX -1.47 (3.88, 162); 0-0 +0.29 (2.71, 331); level at 1-1 or higher -4.06 (2.86, 299); 2025 second half +1.53 (3.20, 240); 2026 first half -3.29 (2.64, 349). Buying the other side (NO on the tie at 100 minus the bid) loses 3.33c (1.97). Calibration at 65': tie priced 40-49c (avg 45.5c) won 45.7 times in 100 (352 matches); 50-59c (avg 52.7c) won 56.3 times in 100 (183). Pooled with the hunter's in-sample 65' cell: -0.73c (se 1.80, 758 matches). His +4.69c and the -1.77c here differ by 6.5c, which is 1.3 se, so his number was noise. It came almost entirely from September 2026 (+11.2c that month, -5.8c in August).
test.artefact_checks: (1) My TIE-only code reproduced the hunter's in-sample numbers exactly before I used it on the older data. (2) No look-ahead selection: candidates were picked on in-game score only, 0-0 matches were included, and no volume filter was applied. These were the hunter's two measured traps. (3) Stale quotes: allowing a quote up to 600 s old instead of 120 s leaves 65' unchanged at -1.77c. (4) 39 UEFA qualifiers had no second-half kickoff event. I estimated it from the clock times of second-half events, and that estimate was off by a median 1 s (90th percentile 1 s) on the 1,041 matches that did have the event. Adding them back gives 65' -1.55c (se 1.92, 657). (5) Price unit: the historical tier gives dollar strings; 172,334 bid/ask closes, none below a whole cent; all markets are on the 1c tick. (6) Kalshi's settlement is the truth source; ESPN's final score includes extra time. (7) The 77 matches dropped at 65' for a spread over 4c could not be bought at a fair ask anyway; most are thin 2025 books.
test.supply_we_would_get: Not the deciding question, since there is no edge. For the record, on the TIE market of these 8 series: median spread 1c at 65'; median 11,400 contracts traded on the tie in the 10 minutes after 65' (six European series 13,200; MLS and Liga MX 5,700). So 98 contracts would probably fill at the ask, but book depth was NOT measured: there is no soccer book recording, and no match was in play during this run. The holdout averaged about 1.7 qualifying matches a day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 (dead). Run at the measured holdout mean it would lose about 1.8c x 98 contracts x 1.7 matches = about -$3/day at the $1,155 bank.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0 (dead); about -$13/day at the measured mean if run at about 425 contracts.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: 2 se = 3.9c a contract at 65' on 630 matches. The estimate of -1.77c sits 1.9 se below the +2c bar and below zero, which is the pre-registered kill line.
test.worst_case: A tie at about 46c loses about $45 at 98 contracts; three tie losses in one day is about -$135; the expected drift is about -$3/day.
test.next_test: None worth running. Do NOT add a 75-day READS_DUE forward read for M-16: the 630-match backward check already answers the pre-registered question, and the forward read's own bar was only 150 matches. If M-15's weekly candle pull runs anyway, the 65' tie cell can be logged for free, but nothing should be built on it. The only untested version is a maker (a resting bid on the tie). With won minus mid at +0.8c (se 2.0), the most a maker could earn is about half the 1c spread (0.5c), minus the 0.43c maker fee on these fee series, before being filled by sellers who know more. That is not worth building a soccer book recorder.

idea.name: Slow-count House races after Nov 3 (CA, AZ, NV, WA, OR, AK; days 1-21): price uncalled KXHOUSERACE markets off county-level late-ballot leans
idea.mechanism: Counts run for weeks and counties release batches daily; project each uncalled district's final from batch leans measured in 2024 and trade between batches.
idea.why_mispriced: Fewer, slower participants than on election night, and the folklore direction is wrong in the West (statewide WA/OR/CA late counts leaned R in 2020 and 2024), so running-total readers who assume late ballots are D misprice.
idea.must_be_true: District-level 2024 count histories are obtainable (the NYT district JSON was not found at four guessed URL patterns), and KXHOUSERACE books in those districts have size.
idea.evidence_so_far: Statewide only: remainder lean at 80% expected vote WA presidential 2020 -0.150, WA Senate 2024 -0.045, OR 2020 -0.114, CA 2020 -0.053, CA Senate 2024 -0.006. District data not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown; plausibly $0-5/day for 2-3 weeks. Worst: -$20-50 on a wrong district.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~10-20 uncalled districts settle over 1-3 weeks
idea.test_plan: Find a 2024 district batch history (CA SoS update history, Maricopa/Clark/King batch logs); measure lean per batch; check Polymarket 2024 House markets for trailers that came back. Must be done before Nov 4 to be usable.
idea.prior_reason: No district data yet and only statewide leans; plausible but unmeasured, with a hard deadline.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New; needs data.
idea.worst_case: -$20-50 on a wrong district.

test.method: Sources, best first. (1) The raw count feed: NYT/AP timestamped count histories for every 2024 House district in CA/AZ/NV/OR/WA/AK plus CO-8 and NM-2 (84 files), and for 2020 (out-of-sample year) from the 2020 state-page files. URL patterns found here; the hunter had failed to find them: static01.nyt.com/elections-assets/pages/data/2024-11-05/results-<state>-us-house-<N>.json (AK: -us-house-at-large) and .../2020/data/api/2020-11-03/state-page/<state>.json. (2) Polymarket 2024 hourly price for 9 slow-count West districts. This is a traded/midpoint price, not an ask. (3) Kalshi: today's books, open interest and rules for 24 West competitive HOUSE*/KXHOUSERACE series, plus the only Kalshi slow-count tapes still served (AK top-four primary Aug 18 2026 and WA top-two Aug 4 2026). Tests: (a) the hunter's own mechanism, written before seeing outcomes with no fitted parameters: project the final from the D share of the latest batches (~10% of expected vote) times the remaining vote implied by AP's expected-vote %. Scored against the plain running total on every D-vs-R district, one value per district per counted-% bucket. (b) Within-district persistence: does the drift up to 85% counted predict the drift after it? Fit on even-index districts, tested on odd. (c) A state-level drift prior applied at 10 AM ET the morning after: fit on half the 2024 districts, held out on the rest, then applied to 2020 as a true out-of-sample year. (d) Model vs Polymarket on the 9 districts: buy the model side when the gap is at least 10/20/30c, at market +2c + Kalshi taker fee, held to result.
test.n_markets: 2024: 74 completed D-vs-R West districts with full count histories (71 in the persistence test). 9 of them with a Polymarket price path (CA-13, CA-45, CA-27, CA-22, CA-41, CA-47, OR-5, AZ-6, AZ-1). 2020: 69 West districts. Kalshi 2026: 24 West competitive series (48 legs) checked for books.
test.n_independent_clusters: Per district: 74 (2024) and 69 (2020). But the drift that decides money is one shared factor per state per year: about 5 state-years in 2024 and 5 in 2020. For the market test: 9 districts, all in one year, and 6 of them hit by the same CA shift, so roughly 2-3 independent bets.
test.result:
1) THE HUNTER'S MECHANISM LOSES TO DOING NOTHING. Error of the projected final D share (latest-batch extrapolation vs the plain running total), one value per district: at 70-80% counted 1.04 vs 0.76 points (extrapolation better in 21/54 districts); at 80-88% 0.95 vs 0.46 (16/59); at 88-93% 0.43 vs 0.31 (24/53); at 93-97% 0.25 vs 0.15 (25/68). AP's expected-vote % jumps (CA-41 went from 79% to 57% overnight), and recent batches do not represent the rest.
2) NO LATE PERSISTENCE. Drift before 85% counted vs after it: correlation 0.19, fitted slope 0.03. Holdout error 0.36 vs 0.37 points for the running total (better in 15/35). Mean drift after 85% is +0.0001: from there the running total already is the answer.
3) THE STATE PRIOR FLIPS SIGN BY YEAR. 2024, morning after to final: CA drifted D in 42 of 47 districts (mean +1.35 points); AZ drifted R in 7/9; WA R in 7/8. Within 2024 the CA prior holds up on the held-out half (error 0.91 vs 1.53 points, better in 18/24). But 2020 CA drifted R in 43 of 46 districts (mean -1.51 points). Carried into 2020, the 2024 prior makes CA worse: 2.41 vs 1.62 points, better in only 3/46. WA and AZ drifted R both years, but the leader changed in no district there, so there was nothing to trade.
4) MARKET TEST, in-sample, one year. The latest-batch rule at a 10c gap made +$3.69 per contract per signal over 8 districts (37 district-days). That is all one district (CA-45 +$5.10); without it the rule made -$1.41. By district: 3 won, 4 lost, 1 flat. At a 20c gap: +$1.77 (CA-45 +2.58, CA-13 -1.31).
5) WHAT 2024 DID SHOW. The leader changed after 10 AM ET Nov 6 in 6 of 74 districts (four in CA, plus AZ-6 and CO-8). That morning Polymarket priced the four trailing CA Democrats who came back at 22-50c (Tran 0.225, Gray 0.36, Min 0.415, Whitesides 0.50). That is real, but it is one CA-2024 factor, and in 2020 the same factor ran the other way.
6) SIDE FINDING, a different idea. The only Kalshi 'slow' tape served (AK-AL top-four primary, Aug 18 2026) was a withdrawal, not a count. J.B. Williams finished 5th and sat at 1-3c for 8 days. Third-place Schultz had suspended his campaign in July. When he formally withdrew (~Aug 27 ET), Williams went from 2c to 93c, with 188k contracts traded that day. n=1.
test.artefact_checks: Leakage: the latest-batch rule had no fitted parameters and uses only snapshots up to time t. Finals are AP final counts (counted >= 98%). The only fitted things (state drift slope, persistence slope) were fit on even-index districts and tested on odd ones, then on 2020. The within-2024 holdout is not independent; 2020 is the real out-of-sample year. Clustered by district; snapshots were never counted as observations; duplicate snapshots were removed. Units: shares are fractions of the D+R two-party vote. Polymarket 'p' is a traded/midpoint print, not an executable ask; the +2c entry cost is a guess, not measured. AK-AL 2024 has a first-round count only (ranked-choice), so it was excluded from the model. CA districts were redrawn under Prop 50 for 2026, so 2024 district paths do not map to 2026 seats; only a state-level factor would carry over, and that factor flipped between 2020 and 2024. idea.name: NBA in-play leader at 70-90c (first-entry taker or back-of-queue leader bid): forward log of the 2026-27 season, read after 300 games
idea.mechanism: In Q2-Q4 of regulation, at the first minute the leader's ask enters 70-90c, either buy the leader at the ask (taker) or join the leader's bid and keep only fills where the bid was cleared within 5 min (back-of-queue maker). Hold to settlement. Paper only: a free forward log (public candles, 1 call per game, pulled weekly).
idea.why_mispriced: The cross-sport in-play favourite under-pricing (R1: takers at 65-90c win 8-10c); on NBA it appears only in the second half of the 2025-26 season.
idea.must_be_true: Leaders at 70-90c win more often than their price by more than the fee (taker ~1.5c, maker <= 0.44c) in BOTH halves of a season.
idea.evidence_so_far: Measured on 326-330 games: a 1-in-4 systematic sample of 2025-26 KXNBAGAME, historical 1-min candles, ESPN plays for game state; cluster = game; stopping-time estimator (first entry into the band) -- the per-game minute average first used was biased and inflated the result to +6.5c. Won - mid at first entry: 70-80c +3.89c (se 2.47, 280 games), 80-90c +3.56c (se 1.95, 303). Taker at first ask in band: +1.36c (se 2.58) / +1.71c (se 2.03); half 1 (tips before Jan 20) -2.27c / -0.56c; half 2 +5.19c / +3.95c. Back-of-queue maker: +2.51c (se 2.73) / +1.81c (se 2.29); half 1 -0.35 / -0.79; half 2 +5.72 / +4.58. Not concentrated in mismatches or pregame favourites. A cross-fitted lead x clock x spread table's lean flips sign between halves; Kalshi's mid has the best Brier (0.1448 vs table 0.1501, ESPN 0.1519). The bar (>= 1c after maker fee in both halves, >= 300 games) FAILS on half 1. Smallest detectable ~4-5c at 2 se per band.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Oct-Jan (the half that failed): $0 or slightly negative. If the half-2 pattern recurs in Feb-Apr 2027: ~10 games a night x 1 entry x 98 contracts x ~4c = ~$40 a night at $1,155, ~$170 a night at $5,000; depth is not the limit (median 5.5M contracts a game). Worst plausible night: 3 comebacks at 98 lots ~-$235 (about -$1,000 at $5k sizing).
idea.settlements_per_day: ~8-12 NBA games a night from Oct 21 (1,230-game season)
idea.test_plan: Pre-register now a read-only forward log of every 2026-27 game with the same first-entry rule (nba_stop.py logic, public candles, 1 call per game, weekly pull). Read after 300 games (~early January) and again after the February trade deadline. Bar: taker at first ask in band >= +1.5c after fee in each read. Add READS_DUE ~2027-01-10.
idea.prior_reason: Fails its pre-registered bar on season half 1, the free model's lean flips sign and Kalshi beats ESPN on Brier; the forward log is free but cannot speak before January, and the seasonal story (late-season only) is post hoc.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: First NBA regular-season measurement (R1 had NBA in-play net +0.5c on one week); extends the covered NHL leader lean (20261015-R1-C3-01, dead) to NBA and finds the same model-error pattern.
idea.worst_case: A comeback costs the ask (~80c) x size: -$78 a game at 98 lots; 3 in a night about -$235.
