test.method:
Data source: Kalshi's public 1-minute historical candles for the home market (/historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks: yes bid/ask at close, bid low, ask high), joined to ESPN play-by-play for game state (quarter and clock 3 s before each candle closes). No replay was used, and we have no live NBA fills. The rule is exactly the hunter's nba_stop.py (C)/(D). It was pre-registered in PREREG.txt before any hold-out number was seen.
- Minutes kept: regulation Q2-Q4, bid > 0, ask < 100, ask minus bid <= 3c. The leader is the side whose mid is >= 50.
- TAKER: at the first minute the leader's ask is in [70,90) (70-80 and 80-90 also reported), buy at that ask, pay 7*p*(1-p) c, hold to settlement. One entry per game.
- MAKER (back of the queue): at the first minute the leader's mid is in the band, post at the leader's bid. Counted as filled only if the bid is cleared within the next 5 candles. Pay 1.75*p*(1-p) c.
Hold-out sets:
- The 3/4 of 2025-26 KXNBAGAME games the hunter did not use (systematic slices M[1::4], M[2::4], M[3::4]): 987 pulled, 972 with an in-play minute.
- 2024-25 play-in and playoffs (86 games), the only earlier Kalshi NBA season.
Each game is one cluster. Standard errors are also clustered by night as a check. Self-test: a fairly priced world returns -0.15c and a world with a planted +6c under-pricing returns +5.82c. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-14-P/: analyze.py (the pre-registered run), extra_fade.py (one exploratory mirror test), and pull_rest.py, pull_2425.py, espn_2425.py. 1,126 public Kalshi calls were used.
test.n_markets: 2025-26: 1,298 games had an in-play Q2-Q4 minute, and 1,194 had a taker entry at 70-90. That is the hunter's slice (326) plus the hold-out (972). The hold-out had 447 taker entries in the first half of the season and 444 in the second. 2024-25: 86 play-in/playoff games (81 entries). Each game is one settlement (the home and away markets mirror each other).
test.n_independent_clusters: 1,384 games over about 206 + 40 game nights. The night-clustered standard error is within 0.2c of the per-game one (hold-out: 1.40 vs 1.43), so games on the same night are close to independent.
test.result:
The pre-registered bar fails on all three legs.

**P1, hold-out (891 new games), taker at the first ask in 70-90:** -1.91c per contract after fee (se 1.43). The bar was >= +1.5c with t >= 2.
- 70-80: -2.20 (se 1.57); 80-90: -2.52 (se 1.31).
- Back-of-queue maker 70-80: -0.77 (se 1.70, 686 fills); 80-90: -1.28 (se 1.43, 730 fills).
- Won minus mid, before any costs: 70-80 -0.14 (se 1.55); 80-90 -0.54 (se 1.27). The Kalshi mid is calibrated.

**P2, whole 2025-26 season (1,194 games), taker 70-90:** -1.16c (se 1.22).
- First half -3.89 (se 1.80, 599 games); second half +1.59 (se 1.64, 595 games).
- The second-half lean that motivated the forward log shrinks to +0.68 (se 1.94, 444 games) on the hold-out's second-half games, under the +1.5c bar.

**P3, 2024-25 playoffs, taker 70-90:** -5.18 (se 4.97, 81 games). The sign check fails.

**Hunter's slice:** reproduced exactly (taker +1.36 / +1.71, maker +2.51 / +1.81). It was the luckiest of the four 1-in-4 slices: k0 +1.06, k1 -0.65, k2 -1.27, k3 -3.74.

**In counts:** at first entry the leader won 913 of 1,194 games, 76.5 times out of 100, at an average ask of 76.39c. The leader is priced right, so the taker just pays the spread plus fee (about 1.2c).

**Exploratory mirror test** (buy the trailing side at the same minutes):
- At first entry: -2.63 (se 1.22).
- In the last 10 minutes, leader 60-90: -1.64 (se 1.55, 738 games).
- Both sides lose the spread plus fee. The literature's "trailing side is overpriced in the last 10 minutes" (arXiv 2607.14430) does not appear on Kalshi NBA 2025-26: buying the leader in the last 10 minutes at 70-90 gives -3.05 (se 1.52).

**By month:** large swings (Dec -9.39 se 3.40, Mar +3.11 se 2.67, May +16.30 se 4.45 on 31 games), and no pattern that holds outside the hunter's sample.
test.artefact_checks:
1. The hunter's k0 numbers reproduce to the cent, so the hold-out runs the identical rule.
2. Self-test: the fairly priced world gives -0.15c, and a planted +6c is found as +5.82c.
3. Each hold-out slice on its own is below the hunter's slice (-0.65, -1.27, -3.74 vs +1.06). The original lean was sample luck.
4. Entering one minute late gives -1.98 vs -1.91, so this is not a timing artefact.
5. The night-clustered standard error matches the per-game one.
6. Two choices favour the idea, and it still loses: the fee is charged without the per-order round-up, and a maker fill is counted whenever the bid was merely cleared (no queue position, no informed sellers).
7. The mirror test (buying the trailing side) also loses. That fits a fairly priced market minus costs, not a hidden sign error.
8. Price unit: the *_dollars fields were converted x100 once for the whole sample, and the <= 3c spread filter was applied the same way to every slice.
test.supply_we_would_get: Supply is not the limit on KXNBAGAME: volume in the entry minute had a median of 10,223 contracts (10th percentile 1,108), with about 5.8 qualifying games a night. There is plenty of supply, but all of it is fairly priced.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0: do not run it. Run as specified anyway (taker, 98 contracts), it measured an average of -$6.58 a night over 206 nights of 2025-26.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0: do not run it. At $5,000 sizing (about 424 contracts) the same rule would average about -$28 a night, scaled from the 98-contract measurement.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
- Hold-out (891 games): 2 se = 2.9c per contract. Whole season (1,194 games): 2 se = 2.4c.
- The whole season's 95% upper bound on the taker edge is -1.16 + 2.44 = +1.28c, below the +1.5c bar. Last season already rules the bar out.
- A 300-game forward log could only detect an edge of about 5c or more, because each game is roughly a 76/24 coin flip (sd about 43c).
test.worst_case: Measured on 2025-26 at 98 contracts: the worst night lost $316.73, and 5 nights in 100 lost more than $160.19. At $5,000 sizing that is about -$1,370 on the worst night and about -$690 at the 5-in-100 level.
test.next_test:
None recommended. The proposed 2026-27 forward log is free (one public call per game) but cannot plausibly pass. Its +1.5c bar sits above last season's 95% upper bound (+1.28c), and a 300-game read can only resolve about 5c.

If the operator wants it anyway as a cheap watch:
- Use the same rule (analyze.py game_rows / entries) with a weekly pull of public 1-minute candles and ESPN plays.
- Read it after 300 games, around 2027-01-10.
- Pass bar: taker at the first ask in 70-90 >= +1.5c after fee AND t >= 2, on the new games only. A fail ends it.

idea.name: Persistent-funding alt carry: short the Kalshi perp where funding stays positive (UNI, SOL, ZEC, LINK), hedged with Coinbase spot
idea.mechanism: Short the perp at <= 1-2x, buy the same coin on Coinbase spot, collect funding while it stays positive; enter at a 7-day rate >= 30%/yr, unwind when it falls below ~15%/yr. Dominated by M-11 if the snapshot payment is confirmed (the snipe collects the same prints with 3-minute exposure and no spot leg).
idea.why_mispriced: US-retail longs on Kalshi pay a premium that offshore carry desks cannot reach (Kalshi perps are US-only).
idea.must_be_true: Funding stays positive for weeks; Coinbase spot fees (0.4-0.6% a side retail) are paid once; the coin's 24-h moves (UNI worst 10%, ZEC 47%) do not force a liquidation of the short at <= 1-2x.
idea.evidence_so_far: Public funding history: UNI +61%/yr since 09-30 (45 prints, never negative, 49% zero); 7-day annualised SOL 46%, ZEC 54%, LINK 51%, BTC 18%; sign persistence on consecutive nonzero prints ~1.0 but half the prints are zero and the 30-day rates are 13-20%; UNI 7-day already down to 27%/yr. Worst 24-h mark moves: ZEC 46.7%, UNI 10.4%, SOL 13.0%.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: About $0.5-1/day per $1,000 of capital if a 30%/yr rate held a month (after ~1.2% round-trip spot + perp costs and 1.6x capital use); $0 or negative if the regime fades. At $5k: $2-5/day. Worst plausible day: a 20% alt squeeze at 2x eats the perp margin (forced exit, -$100-200 per $1,000, since the spot leg is not cross-margined).
idea.settlements_per_day: 3 funding prints a day
idea.test_plan: Paper only: track the 7-day and 30-day annualised funding per alt daily for 30 days from the public history (funding.py in r2-perps-venue/); bar: the rule 'enter at 7-day >= 30%/yr, exit at < 15%' earns >= 2x the round-trip cost per entry on >= 3 of 5 alts.
idea.prior_reason: The regime is already fading, it needs a margin account plus a Coinbase spot account, and a squeeze can cost a fifth of the capital; M-11 captures the same payer with far less exposure.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New (the critic census gave BTC/ETH means only; BTC/ETH carry itself measured dead this round).
idea.worst_case: -$200 per $1,000 on a squeeze plus a regime flip to negative funding.

test.method: Source: Kalshi's own public perp funding history (/margin/funding_rates/historical, 5,915 prints, all 19 crypto perps, 2026-06-03 to the 2026-10-16 04:00Z print). This is the top-ranked source; no replay and none of our fills. Funding is a fraction of notional per 8-h print, positive = longs pay shorts, and |rate| < 1 bp prints as 0 (r2-perps-venue rebuilt 5 of 5 prints from the premium). final.py runs six tests: (1) monthly annualised funding per perp; (2) walk-forward: every first crossing of trailing-7d >= 15/20/30 %/yr on EVERY crypto perp, then the short's realised funding over the next 7/14/30 days, complete windows only; (3) holdout of the persistence model: fit fwd30 = a + b x tr7 before 2026-08-24, test on the later market-days; (4) the idea's pre-registered rule (enter 30 / exit 15) on fresh data; (5) always-on short per coin; (6) dollars at capital C and perp leverage L (spot leg fully paid, N = C/(1+1/L)), one round trip per 30 days, net of the 4.05% APY Kalshi pays on idle predictions cash. Fee schedules checked today: Binance.US 0% maker / 0.02% taker (lists all 8 candidate coins in USD; spreads 1.1-31 bp), Kraken Pro 0.40/0.80%, Coinbase Advanced US 0.50/0.90%, Kalshi perp 2/4 bp. The short leg's squeeze risk comes from hourly perp candles (squeeze*.py). tail.py measures funding tails and current book depth. Everything is in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-23-P/ (final.py/final.json, carry*.py, squeeze*.py, tail.py, binus.py, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 19 crypto perps and 5,915 funding prints over 134 days. Walk-forward signals: 16 at the 15%/yr bar (7 with a complete 30-day window), 9 at 20% (2 complete), 7 at 30% (1 complete). The persistence fit uses 1,248 market-days.
test.n_independent_clusters: About 4-5. The 7 complete 30-day windows fall in about 4 separate periods: late June, mid-August, late August to early September, and mid-September. October's high funding is ONE crypto-wide cluster: all 6 open episodes started 10-07 to 10-10, and none has a complete 30-day window yet.
test.result:
The funding is real, but it fades fast after a hot week, and the dollars are tiny at either bank size.

Walk-forward after trailing-7d first crosses >= 15%/yr, the short collects:
- next 7 days: 0.446% of notional (23.3%/yr, n 15)
- next 14 days: 0.547% (14.3%/yr, n 9)
- next 30 days: 0.788% (9.6%/yr, n 7)
- At the >= 30% bar, the 30-day forward rate is 7.3%/yr (n 1).

Holdout: the early-half fit (fwd30 = 0.009 + 0.296 x tr7) predicts 7.6%/yr for late market-days with trailing >= 15%. Realised was 9.3%/yr (n 24); the late refit slope is 0.339. About 70% of a hot week's rate is gone within a month, in both halves.

Monthly rates: every alt ran 0-6%/yr from June to September. October jumped (ZEC 37, LINK 31, SOL 28, XRP 25, HYPE 22.5, UNI 54, BTC 16). The newest print (midnight ET 10-16) is 0 bp on all six alts and 2.8 bp on BTC.

Pre-registered rule (enter 30 / exit 15): 1 episode closed (VVV, +0.14% of notional in 6.3 days, a fail). 6 are still open at +0.25% to +1.03% of notional after 5-8 days. The idea's bar (funding per entry >= 2x the round-trip cost on 3 of 5 alts) passes only at the Binance.US floor cost of ~0.10% (6 of 7 so far, all still open). It is 2 of 7 at Kraken maker cost (0.85%) and 0 of 7 at Coinbase cost.

Always-on short with no timing: BTC 8.6%/yr, XRP 6.1, SOL 4.3. The hindsight-best 30-day window on any coin was UNI at 2.51% of notional.

THE KILLING NUMBER: suppose 30%/yr held flat for a whole month. The entire $1,155 at 1x (N $578) would still net only $0.33/day more than that cash earns sitting on Kalshi, and it would take every dollar from the pin bot. At the realistic 9.6%/yr it nets $0.00/day at the floor cost and -$0.04 to -$0.14/day at real alt or Kraken costs. M-11 (the funding snapshot snipe) also beats it: same payer, about $0.8/day on $500, 3-minute hold, no spot leg.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) Units: the funding rate is a fraction per 8-h print (the UNI estimate 0.000124 = 1.24 bp). Prints at 04/12/20Z confirm 3 a day; units were not inferred from magnitudes.
(2) Look-ahead: the test runs on all 19 crypto perps, not just the 4 picked after the fact. The 30/15 thresholds were fixed in the idea before this test.
(3) Zero prints come from the 1-bp deadband, not missing data.
(4) October is one market-wide event, not 6 observations.
(5) The bar's verdict flips with the hedge venue, so today's fee schedules were checked. The idea's 0.4-0.6% Coinbase figure is out of date (now 0.50/0.90%). Binance.US at 0/0.02% is the new cheap angle, and it still does not rescue the dollars.
(6) Opportunity cost: the 4.05% Kalshi APY is charged against the capital. Whether the PERPS balance earns it is NOT VERIFIED; if it does, that adds at most ~$0.06/day at $1,155.
(7) The squeeze numbers come from hourly closes, so they are a lower bound.
(8) The recorders are alive: the 2026-10-16 09Z cfbenchmarks_value and feed_data/coinbase files were written within seconds of the check. Free disk is 114.6 GB.
test.supply_we_would_get:
Supply is not the limit.
- Kalshi perp bids within 25 bp right now: UNI $333k, ZEC $82k, LINK $305k, SOL $1.5M, XRP $1.6M, HYPE $1.6M, BTC $11.6M.
- Binance.US asks within 25 bp: UNI $1.1k, ZEC $3.7k, LINK $21k, SOL $199k, XRP $245k.
- A $578-$2,500 position fits everywhere; taking on UNI/ZEC costs 13-15 bp a side in spread.

Access is the real limit:
- Retail must apply for Kalshi margin access.
- The perps balance is separate from the predictions balance, and API transfers are not available yet.
- A Binance.US account is needed.
- Moving money between venues takes bank days, so the short cannot be topped up quickly before a squeeze.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0.00/day (range -$0.14 to +$0.13), and that assumes ALL $1,155 at 1x at the measured 9.6%/yr forward funding, after Kalshi's 4.05% APY. It also ignores the pin bot's lost earnings, which are far larger. The hindsight ceiling (best 30 days ever, UNI) is $0.34/day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: At 1x (N $2,500): $0.02/day at the floor cost after APY, and -$0.19/day at a real alt round-trip cost. Only a 30%/yr month held flat gives $1.2-1.4/day. At 2x it is $0.21/day, but 2x on alts was liquidated in 18-69% of historical 14-day holds.
test.worst_case:
The funding itself barely hurts: the worst 7 days of funding a short paid on any candidate was -0.51% of notional (XRP), about -$3 at N $578.

The real tail is the short leg's margin, because the spot leg sits on another venue and cannot cover it. Share of 14-day holds whose price rise reached liquidation:
- at 2x: ZEC 69%, HYPE 38%, DOGE 22%, SOL 20%, XRP 19%, LINK 18%
- at 1x: ZEC 27%, XRP 10%, HYPE 6%, SOL/LINK/BTC 0%
The worst 24-h rise was ZEC +50%.

If the short is liquidated, the spot gain roughly offsets the perp loss at that moment, but we are left holding unhedged spot. A 20% retrace then costs ~$115 at N $578 or ~$500 at N $2,500, plus a liquidation penalty (not measured). Limited to SOL/LINK/BTC at 1x, the worst plausible day is about -$5 at the current bank and -$20 at $5k.
test.next_test:
No recorder is needed, because the funding history is public and kept. Re-run final.py around 2026-11-10, when the October signals' 30-day windows complete (one API call).

Pass bar, set now: realised forward 30-day funding of at least 25%/yr on at least 3 coins after trailing-7d first crosses 15%/yr. That is about what $5k at 1x needs to clear $1/day after APY and costs.

Paper-track a 30-day SOL/LINK/BTC 1x carry only if three things all hold: the bar passes, the operator gets margin access, and it beats M-11 per dollar of capital. Otherwise leave this payer to M-11.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Forward 30-day funding after a signal has a standard error of ~0.14% of notional per 30 days (~1.7%/yr). From 7 complete windows the sample can detect a difference of about 3.5%/yr, enough to tell the measured 9.6%/yr from the 25%/yr needed. Whether the October regime persists is NOT measured (no complete 30-day windows yet). The kill does not depend on it: even a flat 30%/yr month is $0.33/day at the current bank.

idea.name: BAND-X: jump-band taker at a 2-sigma trigger -- after a >= 2-sigma favourable CF print with 10-60 s left, take the 70-95c offer outside the pin and forecaster windows (seen ask, 20 lots), co-scored with a calibrated-fair variant; the 98-lot walk to fair - 6c only at a $5,000 bank
idea.mechanism: On every 1-s CF settlement-index print with 10-60 s left: dz = print move / sigma of the trailing 600 one-second moves. If dz >= 2 toward a side, that side's best ask is 70-95c, engine fair (var_factor, the live model) - ask - taker fee(20)/20 >= 2c, and the second is NOT in the pin window (tau <= 45 and fair >= 0.995) or the forecaster window (tau <= 28 and ask >= 0.75): one IOC buy at the seen ask, 20 lots at the $1,155 bank. First qualifying second per market only; hold to settlement 10-60 s later. Own pot (~$150), max 3 entries per close, day stop -$30, run stop -$60; no entries in the weekday 8:30 ET close (inherits M-03). Variant K, scored beside it and traded only if it wins the read: the 2c floor is applied to fair_k = Phi(k x Phi^-1(fair)) with k = 1.50 (10-19 s), 1.16 (20-29 s), 0.90 (30-44 s), 0.78 (45-60 s), fitted by maximum likelihood on 1,332 September markets; it removes the 45-60 s entries where the engine is ~5c too sure. idea.why_mispriced: Offers on the favoured side were posted before the print. After a >= 2-sigma move the book carries most of it but not all (89 in 100 within 75 ms; the rest drifts in over 60-120 s) while part of the 60-s settlement average is already locked. The fastest takers clear 60-70 in 100 of these offers within 260 ms; what they leave is still worth +6-8c a contract. The other side is the slow maker who leaves the offer up. The no-jump control in the same band earns ~0 in October, so the edge is the stale quote after the move, not a general model edge.

refs.strongest_objection:
I found no measurement bug: the tape numbers reproduce exactly from my own code. The weakness is the evidence.

1. **The holdouts are not clean for this family.** The R2 lane had already scored the 4-sigma half of ARM-J (R2-M-01: same 70-95c band, same 10-60 s window, same 2c edge) on both of R3's "unseen" periods, 08-25..09-01 and 09-02..10-15, before R3 pre-registered. Only the 2-4 sigma part is new:
   - October: +7.48c a contract on 42 fills (t 1.41).
   - Aug 25-Sep 1: +6.81c on 48 fills (t 1.53).
   - Neither is significant alone.
   - SEPX shares calendar days with FIT, so it is a fresh sample but not an out-of-time test.
2. **No single period reaches t 2 when clustered by close** (the project's rule): October 1.89, SEPX 1.79, UNSEEN 1.88, FIT 1.81. The tester's "SEPX passes" rests on the t by UTC day. Its standard error comes out 20-35 in 100 smaller than the one clustered by close (bootstrap sd 1.37c by day against 2.10c by close). Only the pooled periods are clearly positive: October + UNSEEN is 159 fills at +6.74c, close-bootstrap 95% range +1.6c to +11.5c, and it is 0 or worse in under 1 draw in 100.
3. **The latest data is flat and shrinking.** W41 without BTC: 25 fills at +0.5c. Fills went from about 7 a day to about 4.
4. **The race is tight.** On our own trade channel, the first other taker to buy the same side at or below the seen ask after our +260 ms slot arrives a median +313 ms after the print. The 25th percentile is +278 ms, so in 1 of 4 fills a rival is within 18 ms of us.

**Checked and not a bias in our favour:** the validity filter. The 76 first-signal markets it threw out (too few ticker messages, or truncated) won 76 of 76, so it lowers the tape edge rather than raising it. Only 5 of 340 October hours were dropped.

I checked real trades by other slow bots: buys of the favoured side 150-1000 ms after Kalshi sent a 2-sigma print, under the same band, edge and window rules. That happened in 44-48 markets a day in weeks 36-37, 22 a day in weeks 40-41, and 13 a day in week 42 (10-12..10-16 06Z). October's first half earned +5.1c a contract (183 markets). Smaller points: losses do not stack much with the pin (the pin lost in only 4 of the 42 losing markets it also traded, -$23.63 in all). idea.name: Overnight 99c dead-strike carry on the gas daily ladders: after 9 PM ET buy the sure side at 99c from others' dead-side 1c stacks on strikes >= 3c from the median, hold to the ~7 AM ET print
idea.mechanism: At 22:01Z 120 dead strikes held dead-side 1c stacks totalling 818,305 contracts; each is a 99c sure-side offer of 1k-40k. After 9 PM ET take them at 99c only on strikes >= 3c from the implied median (skip any state M-06 flags as restoring), cap 300 contracts per strike, hold to the AAA print. Gain: 1c minus the ~0.07c fee per contract, minus flips. This is the sweeper side of M-01, so run it only on strikes M-01 is not claiming.
idea.why_mispriced: The reward farmers post those stacks to qualify for the $100 pots and accept being swept. The sweepers who already take them (1,000-lot bursts) are capital-bound and mostly work the 8 AM listing hour (39% of sweep volume).
idea.must_be_true: The flip rate stays near the measured 0.06% (2 of 3,268 strike-days at 9 PM ET, >= 3c) and 0% (0 of 3,151 at 11 PM ET, >= 3c); no AAA print anomaly (one flip on a 1,000-lot costs -$990, the profit of ~110 clean nights); overnight capital is genuinely idle (R1-N2-02: ~$450 spare at 98 lots, Kalshi pays its 4.05% APY on positions too).
idea.evidence_so_far: Flip table from 67 dates of hourly candles; stack sizes from the 51-ladder top-of-book snapshot at 22:01Z; on the far-strike tape, makers lose 1.17c a contract to sweeps, which is what the sweeper side earns. Print-anomaly check: not run.

Then paper-log the 10 PM ET stacks and outcomes for 7 nights. Bar: 0 flips at >= 3c and paper >= +0.8c a contract. Live only with sign-off, at the 300-per-strike cap.

test.method:
Source: Kalshi's hourly event candles, which record the best bid and ask at the close of each hour (trade-tape tier). They cover 856 gas-daily state-day events with prints 2026-08-10..10-15: national plus 8 big states in Aug-Sep, all ladders in October. Each event was joined to its AAA print (expiration_value). Second source: the M-01 tester's read-only top-of-book recorder of all 51 ladders on 2026-10-15, 9:40-10:28 PM ET (20 rounds, with sizes). No replay was used.

I rebuilt each ladder the way a bot would at 6, 9, 10 and 11 PM ET:
- implied median from the bid/ask mids (the hunter's implied.py);
- dead strike = mid >= 97c or <= 3c;
- the sure-side price a taker pays (YES-sure: yes ask; NO-sure: 1 - yes bid);
- outcome from the print.

What the hunter's table lacked, now added:
1. Kept only strikes whose sure side is actually offered. 84% of dead strike-hours >= 3c from the median at 9-11 PM ET have no offer at all.
2. Safety margin: how far the print landed from the strike.
3. Print error toward the bot's side, plus an exponential-tail fit on FIT.
4. A second anchor: the strike must also be >= 3c from the previous print. This guards against junk medians and stale AAA publishes.
5. 98c offers counted separately (the dead side bid at 2c, above the farmers' 1c level).
6. A nightly simulation: one strike per ladder, 300 contracts a strike, farthest first, capital caps of 450 and 2,000 contracts, fee rounded per order.

The whole edge depends on how often a "sure" strike loses, and the data cannot measure that rate. The strikes we could actually buy are also riskier than the strikes the hunter's flip table was built on.
(1) Too few nights. The guarded rule shows 0 losses in 123 state-days over 26 dates in my own pull. That only proves the loss rate is under 2.4 in 100 state-days, and break-even is 0.94. About 320 clean state-days are needed.
(2) The buyable strikes are riskier. Where someone was selling the sure side at 99c, the price moved at least halfway toward the nearest such strike on 6 of 297 sides (2.0%). Where nobody was selling, it did so on 3 of 600 sides (0.5%) (one-sided Fisher p = 0.04). In price-cycle states, moves of 3c or more toward the strike happened on 4 of 133 sides against 1 of 215. So the hunter's figure of about 0.06% of strikes losing is too kind to us.
(3) Both filters that remove every observed loss and near miss (only exactly-99c offers, and staying 3c away from the previous print) were chosen after seeing those cases. The clean tests are small: 25 TEST state-days on 6 dates, plus 25 state-days the tester never saw.

idea.name: AAA gas daily dead-side reward claim: a 1,100-lot 1c bid on the EMPTY losing side of decided strikes, 6-11:30 PM ET, so the strike scores and we hold about half its $100/day pot (state and national ladders; KXDIESELD and intraday grid-extension strikes as add-ons)
markets: KXAAAGASD<ST> (50 state daily ladders, e.g. KXAAAGASDTX, KXAAAGASDCA, KXAAAGASDOH)
intraday grid-extension strikes on cycle/jump days (WI 4.255-4.275 added 21:50Z 10-15, add-on)
idea.mechanism: 1) Every gas-daily strike has its own liquidity program: $100 per strike-day (period_reward 1,000,000 centi-cents), target 1,000, discount 0.5, running 12:00Z-03:59Z (8 AM-11:59 PM ET). Under the filed walk a second scores only if BOTH sides hold >= 1,000 qualifying contracts. 2) On decided strikes the farmers rest 18k-40k lowball bids on the SURE side (e.g. TX 3.795 YES 18,688 @1c) and the dead side is often empty, so the strike is unqualified and nobody is paid for those seconds. 3) From ~6 PM ET, post_only one 1,100-lot bid at 1c on the dead side (NO on strikes >= 2c below the market-implied median, YES on strikes >= 2c above), only where it rests (sure side's best bid <= 98c, so 1c does not cross a 99c stack), with expiration_time before 03:59Z and cancel-on-pause (R1-N2-07 hygiene). We then hold ~100% of the dead side's score and 0% of the sure side's: ~49-50% of the strike's per-second pot while we sit. 4) A fill (someone buys the sure side at 99c from us) costs 1c a contract; after one sweep on a strike, do not re-post it that evening. A flip (the strike comes alive) pays us. 5) Post from the MAIN account (the 10-11 coin-race credit landed in pool 0, not the posting subaccount). 6) Add-ons on the same code: KXDIESELD dead sides (21 strikes, closes 05:59Z so a longer evening, pots $20-140 per strike-day rotating by day), and any gas strike Kalshi lists after 13:00Z (its own fresh $100 program, born one-sided), found by polling /markets every 5 min. Never join near-money strikes (the simulated gas maker lost 21c a contract to better-informed takers).
idea.why_mispriced: Nobody is paid on the unqualified seconds, so this money is unclaimed rather than taken from another maker. The incumbents farm dead sides only 2-4c from the median (120 stacks, 818,305 contracts at 22:01Z) and leave the deeper strikes empty. The only cost is the 99c sure-side buyer, who earns ~0.9c a contract by lifting a dead-side 1c bid (on the far-strike tape makers lost 1.17c a contract to these sweeps); in the evening that flow is small (249 contracts per strike-evening; 39% of the day's sweep volume is in the 8 AM ET listing hour).
idea.must_be_true: (1) Kalshi pays the dead-side bidder per the filed walk, as it paid the coin-race 1c filler (10-11 live test: 90% of the same /2 formula, to MAIN pool 0). (2) Sweepers do not lift a resting 1,100-lot much faster than the measured population rate once it is there. Break-even sweep hazard for 1,100 at 1c here is ~0.28 per strike-hour (0.5 x $6.25/h / $11); the measured evening rate of >= 1,000-lot bursts is ~0.023 per strike-hour (14 in 100 strike-evenings of ~6 h). But on coin race the tape models UNDERSTATED our live fill cost (live sat between the x99 and latent models, ~47-60% of credit), so latent sellers drawn by our bid are the main risk. (3) Incumbents do not copy onto our strikes within days (if they post 18k at our 1c our share falls to ~5% and the idea is dead). (4) Strikes stay decided: measured flip rate of dead strikes (>= 2c from median, >= 97c) 0.098% at 6 PM, 0.085% at 9 PM, 0.022% at 11 PM ET. (5) Extension add-on only: extensions are frequent and farmers are not first (this run's R1-C2-06 test found new_event pots two-sided within 5 min on 99 of 110, so expect it to be contested).
idea.evidence_so_far: Reward pots (GET /incentive_programs, 12 pages): gas-daily $47.9-53.9k/day on 27 ladders Oct 1-12, $84.8-92.7k/day on 44-51 ladders Oct 13-15 (~40% of the $218.9k/day all-Kalshi active total on 10-13). Candles (Oct, 118,412 strike-hours): one side EMPTY on 27% of strike-hours (US 55%, new states 38%, established 24%), 96% of those the dead side; 11-18% of strike-hours in the morning vs 32-45% from 5 PM ET. Full books (8 ladders, 146 strikes, ~5:45 PM ET): 63 strikes dead, unqualified and claimable with a resting 1c bid, mean pot share 49%; 14 more dead strikes already two-sided (joining would take ~26%). Top of book on all 51 ladders (22:01Z): 382 of 522 dead strikes have an empty dead side, 368 restable. Sweep tape (100 far strike-days, US/TX/OH/CA, Oct 8-15): sure-side buys at >= 97c average 2,182 contracts per strike-day (makers lost 1.17c/contract); 6 PM-midnight ET only 249 per strike-evening, 0.78 bursts per strike-evening, 74 of 100 strike-days had none, median evening burst 6-10 lots, 14 bursts >= 1,000 in 100 strike-evenings. Over 28 minutes this evening the 65 existing dead-side stacks of 500+ were all untouched and total dead-side size grew 446k -> 638k. Caveats: the 'unpaid' share uses candle top of book (a lower bound); paid_out is True on $91,900 of 10-13's $92,700 (only says someone got >= $1 at some second; mornings are mostly two-sided). Contrast with this run's dead R1-C2-06 sniper: dead sides on YouTube/SOFR pots were swept every 13-18 bid-hours, 2.2x faster than a half pot pays, but those pots pay $100 per ~190 h; gas pays $100 per 16 h, ~12x the rate per hour. KXDIESELD: 14 days of programs, all paid; one farmer at exactly 1,000 x 1,000 near the money; empty dead sides; fills not measured. Grid extensions: one observed (WI, 5 strikes, programs from 21:50Z); frequency not measured. critic-r2 found the whole gas-daily family missing from the 10-13 catalogue (national 190k contracts/day, states 10-31k/day each). Our own fills and payment on gas pots: NOT measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: UNVERIFIED until a live test. Per claimed strike-evening (5.5 of 16 program hours): credit ~$15 at 90% paid; sweep cost $3-12 on the tape, up to ~$24 if the coin-race 2x tape-to-live gap repeats; net about -$9 to +$12, central ~+$5. Current bank, 10 strikes (~$110 collateral, MAIN): central ~+$50 an evening, range about -$90 to +$120 (the operation's measured total is +$17.2/day). At $5,000, 40 strikes: central ~+$200 an evening while uncontested (contention, not capital, is the limit). Diesel add-on $5-40/day; extensions $0-30/day. Worst plausible evening: each of 10 strikes swept once at 1,100 = about -$117 before any credit (-$470 at 40 strikes); a strike that flips while we are filled is a gain.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~370-400 claimable strike-evenings across 51 ladders (we would use 10-40); reward accrues per strike-day; each print settles ~7 AM ET
idea.test_plan: (a) Free, read-only, can start any evening: poll top of book for 10 gas ladders + KXDIESELD every 2 min, 6 PM-midnight ET, 3 evenings (~1,800 public calls an evening, sleep >= 0.25 s). Measure by distance from the median: survival time of each existing dead-side 1c stack (the decisive fill-cost number), how often anyone fills or joins an empty dead side, and gas strikes created after 13:00Z (created_time) and who quotes them in their first 10 min. Pre-registered kill: stacks >= 2c out swept at > 0.10 per stack-hour, or incumbents join >= 1/3 of newly claimed dead sides within 24 h. (b) Live micro test, OPERATOR SIGN-OFF FIRST (new family): one post_only 1,100-lot 1c dead-side bid on 3 strikes >= 4c from the median (~$33 collateral), 6-11:30 PM ET, 5 evenings, from MAIN; log every fill; read the credit in MAIN pool 0 the next morning. Bar (pre-registered, summed over the 5 evenings): paid >= 50% of the formula's prediction AND fill cost < 40% of the payout. Then 10 strikes. READS_DUE entries belong to the writer agent.
idea.prior_reason: Largest expected dollars of the round (~$50 an evening central at 10 strikes, about 3x the operation's measured +$17.2/day) on ~$110 of collateral; the payment mechanism is proven on coin race and the measured evening sweep rate is ~12x under break-even. Not 5: our own fill cost and payment on gas pots are unmeasured, the tape understated live cost on coin race, and incumbents can copy within days. Decided in about a week (3 free evenings + 5 micro evenings).

Tester, read-only, public GETs only: about 290 calls this session plus 1,429 from the 10-15 attempt that was cut off. Sources: the trade tape (rank 2), hourly event candles and a top-of-book recorder. No replay was used, and we have no own fills on gas.

1) Reward credit. Computed from the filed walk (results/LIP_FILING_2026-07-15.txt, effective 07-30):

test.result:
Break-even is 281 contracts per stack-hour.

**Cost on the tape, all stack sizes (contracts per stack-hour):**
- FIT: 128 (95% 102-153, 178 strike-days).
- TEST: 197 (156-244, 122 strike-days).
- Fresh evening: 178 (142-217, 135 strike-days).

**Size works against us.**
- Sweeps come as bursts of about 1,000-1,300: 51 of 157 bursts, carrying 91% of all 99c contracts.
- Stacks of 1,000-1,300 (our 1,100) were fully swept 15 times in 81.9 stack-hours = 0.183 per hour (95% 0.10-0.30). Cost 240 per hour = 85% of credit.
- At >= 4c: 5 sweeps in 21 h, 303 per hour = 108% of credit, so net negative.
- At 2.5-4c: 10 sweeps in 60.9 h, 219 per hour = 78% of credit.
- Stacks over 5,000: 0 full sweeps in 64.5 h, but 137 per hour lost to partial takes.
- Recorder (48 min), 1,000-1,300 stacks: 0.31 full sweeps per hour, 332 contracts per hour.

**Net at our size:**
- +$0.41 per stack-hour on the fresh evening across all distances; +$0.62 at 2.5-4c; -$0.22 at >= 4c.
- That is about +$1.4 to +$2.2 per strike-evening at 2.5-4c, stopping after the first sweep.
- The all-size per-strike-evening simulations read higher because they understate cost at our size: October +$6.17 (se 0.54), FIT +$6.85, TEST +$5.17, fresh +$4.43 (se 0.79), fresh >= 4c +$2.01 (se 1.10).

**New angle: sweeps come in passes.**
- Example: 7:41-7:49 PM ET, CA, CO, FL, ID, DE, KY, MD, MN, NV, NM, NY, UT; 20 sweeps, with neighbouring strikes on one ladder hit 2-3 s apart.
- 74% of big sweeps follow another strike's big sweep within 5 min; only 9% follow within 2 s.
- Rule: pull all our stacks on any big sweep and re-post after 3 min of quiet. P was picked on 6-9 PM, where it netted +$1.35 per stack-hour.
- On the held-out 9 PM-midnight half it paused us 35% of the time, dodged 58% of sweep contracts, and netted +$0.82 per stack-hour, against +$0.41 with no rule.

**Why the hunter's central is too high.** The hunter's central (+$5 per strike-evening, +$50 an evening at 10 strikes) used 0.023 sweeps per strike-hour, counted over hours with no stack to sell into. Counted over hours when a stack exists, the rate is 5-8x higher.
test.artefact_checks:
1. **Price convention.** A 99c sure-side taker trade = a sale into the 1c dead bid (YES-sure: taker yes @0.99; NO-sure: taker no, yes_price 0.01). Both branches checked.
2. **Units by field name.** yes_price_dollars and count_fp; period_reward is centi-cents, /10,000 = $100.00 per program, confirmed today.
3. **Tick.** No sub-cent price in 20 rounds x ~900 strikes, so the tick is 1c and a bid below 1c is impossible.
4. **Denominator.** Cost is counted per stack-hour (a stack exists), not per strike-hour. The hunter's 0.023 used the wrong one: hours with an empty dead side show a 0.4-6% chance of any 99c sale, because there is nothing to sell into.
5. **Size.** All-size averages understate cost for a 1,100 stack by about 1.35x, because sweepers take 1,000-1,300 chunks. Our size is reported separately.
6. **Size and distance are tangled.** Every stack over 5,000 sat at 2.5-4c, so "post a huge stack instead" is NOT shown to be cheaper.
7. **Holdout.** Thresholds were fixed before looking. Splits are FIT/TEST by print date, plus one fresh evening never sampled before; the pull rule's P was chosen on the first half of the evening only.
8. **Revealed preference.** The sure-side farmers would earn BOTH halves of a strike's pot by adding a dead-side stack, yet about 170 dead sides stay empty. That fits a thin margin, or a negative one for fresh stacks.
9. **Coverage gap.** The tape was pulled only for strikes that had a stack at an hour start, so stacks posted and swept inside one hour are missed. Cost is slightly understated, and so are the pull rule's triggers.
10. **Housekeeping.** The collector is alive: the cfbenchmarks_value tape file was written 5:29 AM ET 10-16 (process command lines are not readable from this shell). Disk 114.5 GB free; scratch folder 4.2 MB.

idea.name: 8:30 ET data-minute guard for every crypto 15-min bot: on weekdays no new pin, top-up, forecaster or band entry in the window that closes at 8:30:00 ET, and no resting 15-min maker or reward quote across 8:30:00 ET
idea.mechanism: On weekdays, skip the close at 8:30 ET (12:30Z in EDT; 13:30Z after the Nov 1 clock change, so compute it in ET) for every entry in its last 45 s: pin main leg, top-ups, the forecaster's 10-30 s entries and BAND-X (M-02). Cancel any resting 15-min maker or reward quote (coin-race filler, penny ladder) before 8:30:00 ET. Operator option: half size instead of skip. Leave 10:00 ET and every other minute open (measured normal).
idea.why_mispriced: Not a mispricing: a risk the trailing 300-s ruler cannot see. US data (claims, CPI, NFP, PPI, retail sales) prints at 8:30:00 ET exactly, the instant this window settles, and the index whipsaws in the minute before (09-11: +40 to +80 bp 28-25 s before 8:30, then reversed; 10-15: NEAR -15 bp at -25 s, then +13 bp in the last 7 s). Near-certain sides flip far more often than the model predicts and than at any other quarter hour.
idea.must_be_true: The 8:30 ET minute keeps its fat tail (a calendar effect, so it should), and the bots' entries in that minute are not a separately profitable population worth more than the tail they carry; the main bot's live record says they are worth ~$0.
idea.evidence_so_far: INDEX (source 1): 30 weekday 8:30 ET closes x 9 coins, 09-02..10-15, with the live bot's own 300-s ruler at 45 s left: z^2 5.97 vs 1.08 at other weekday closes; |z| > 4 in 5.56 per 100 coin-closes vs 0.57 (10x); states the model called >= 95% sure flipped 7 of 232 (3.0 per 100) vs 83 of 30,924 (0.27 per 100) elsewhere. The 7 come from 2 closes (09-04 NFP; 09-11 with six coins at once), so n is 2 events, not 7. Neighbours are normal: 8:15 ET z^2 0.85, 8:45 ET 1.05, 0 tail flips; 10:00 ET |z| > 4 0.38 per 100; weekday 16:00 ET 0.77 per 100 (why R1-N0-01's 16:00 blackout was refuted and this one is a different claim). LIVE (kalshi_ledger, netted per market): the main bot traded 11 weekday 8:30 ET markets in 62 days, net +$0.20, one loss (KXSOL15M 09-11, -$12.16 at the small size it ran then). Forecaster (forecaster-live.jsonl close_summary forecaster_real, NOT reconciled to the subaccount-2 ledger): 10-15 8:30 ET NEAR -$94.75 on 100 contracts (bought NO at 25 and 21 s left at 0.78-0.96). pinrun.py has no release calendar (its only '8:30' gates are v-nospike's 8:30 PM BTC gates; merger grep). The forecaster's other 8:30 ET entries: not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: About $0 on average for the main bot (it forgoes ~11 markets per 2 months worth +$0.20 in total). Its value is the tail: a 09-11-type minute with the bot in 3 coins at 98 contracts costs about -$270 at today's bank and about -$1,100 at a $5,000 bank (~400 contracts); the forecaster's 10-15 loss alone was -$95 on a ~$109 pot.
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 close per weekday (all 9 coins settle at it)
idea.test_plan: Free and immediate. (1) List every weekday 8:30 ET entry of the main bot, the forecaster and the penny ladder / coin-race filler since each went live, with money netted from kalshi_ledger.json per subaccount (main bot done: 11 markets, +$0.20). (2) Pre-registered forward read: the guard stays if, over the next 20 weekday 8:30 ET closes, the index tail rate (|z| > 4 at 45 s with the 300-s ruler) stays >= 3x the rate at other weekday closes; kill it if the 8:30 ET tail falls to the base rate. Run the same check on 10:00 ET so the guard stays narrow. Deploying it is a live change: a VERSIONS.md entry with its revert and a READS_DUE entry at deploy (writer / live session).
idea.prior_reason: Lose-less, the operator's first priority: it costs ~$0 measured on the main bot, removes a 10x tail minute that cost the forecaster $95 today, is trivial to build and is decided by a free forward read. Not higher because the flip tail rests on 2 events and the average saving beyond that one forecaster loss is unmeasured.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New. Nothing in pinrun.py or the ledger guards the 8:30 ET data minute. A different minute from R1-N0-01 (16:00 ET, refuted at 1.46x vs a ~2x break-even) and R2-M-06 (election-night guard, dead).
idea.worst_case: The forgone 8:30 ET entries (measured +$0.02 a market); at half size instead of skip the tail is halved, not removed.

test.method: I narrowed the hunter's 8:30 ET guard test and extended it back to 2024. (1) Price history 2024-01-02..2026-10-15. Source: Binance spot 1-second klines (public data-api.binance.vision; 7,280 coin-closes, none empty). Coins: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE at every weekday 8:30 ET close. Control: one seeded-random other ET quarter-hour per weekday. The test uses the live bot's own 300-s ruler, copied from volcycle.py: strike = previous 60-s average, then z and the >=95%-sure states at 45, 30 and 10 s left; a flip means the >=95% side lost. I checked the proxy against the real CF index on 150 coin-closes from our tape: z correlation 0.964, mean z^2 5.93 (index) vs 6.19 (proxy), and the discovery-window flips (09-04, 09-11) are reproduced. Release days come from the bls.gov/schedule 2024, 2025 and 2026 pages (Employment Situation, CPI, PPI), not from prices. The post-8:30:00 jump (>6 sd on 65 of 66 NFP/CPI days) confirms those dates. It also shows the release itself lands 1-20 s AFTER the settlement window. refs.strongest_objection:
Two errors drive "viable at $0.25/day".

(1) WRONG CONTROL. The tester's 7x flip effect (p = 0.011) compares NFP/CPI 8:30 ET closes with random quarter-hours across the whole day. But the 8:30 ET slot is already riskier on ordinary weekdays. Across all 662 non-NFP/CPI weekday 8:30 closes, 10 had a >=95%-sure side lose: 1.5 per 100, twice the random-slot rate. Against that same-clock control the release closes show 3 of 62 vs 1.5 per 100. That is 3x on 3 events, one-sided Fisher p = 0.09. In my own seeded sample of 240 such closes it is 7 of 240, p = 0.34. Kalshi's own results (2025-12..2026-08, a separate source) agree: 3 of 17 release closes vs 3 of 72 controls, p = 0.08.

(2) EXPOSURE ERROR IN THE MONEY MODEL. The formula takes the chance that ANY of 5 coins flips at a close (5-8 per 100) and charges a full 98-contract loss for it. The bot holds about 0.4 markets per weekday 8:30 close (ledger: 11 markets in ~28 weekdays since 09-08). A flip hits 1 coin of the ~4-5 that are near-certain. Per coin-market, the >=95% flip rate at release closes is 1.0 per 100 (3 of 307) vs 0.3-0.6 per 100 at same-clock controls. That is about 0.5 per 100 extra loss chance per entry, so the guard is worth roughly 0.4 x 0.005 x $92 = $0.18 per release close, about $4-13 a year.

Three further problems:
- The only live loss cited (09-11 SOL: bought at 59c against a 99.5% fair with 30 s left, a 28c gap) is already refused by the deployed v-cap20 rule, which blocks a gap over 10c with more than 20 s left. pinrun.py's own comment names SOL 09-11 among the cases that rule was built on.
- On Kalshi's own tape, takers buying at 90-98c lost money on release closes only because of one close: 2026-02-11 ETH, which settled 1 bp over its strike and cost takers -$1,776. Without that close they made +2.8c a contract, vs +3.5c on controls. Counted one market at a time, release closes were not worse: 3 of 18 such markets lost vs 8 of 77.
- The pre-registered keep bar is keyed on the |z|>4 tail rate. That rate is already 8x, so the bar cannot fail, and it does not measure money.

What survives: the last 45 s before an NFP/CPI print really are jumpier than the 300-s ruler expects. It does not yet show up as more losses per entry for a near-certain buyer.

"Viable at $0.25/day" does not survive. Three reasons.

(1) Measured against the right comparison and at the bot's own gate, release closes are not clearly worse. I ran my own Binance 1-second query over every weekday 8:30 ET close since 2024-01 (728 closes, 6 coins). It uses the live bot's exact entry gate: 99.5% sure, plus its spike and jump checks, with 3-45 s left.
- Out of sample, a sure side lost at 2 of 62 NFP/CPI closes (3.2 per 100) vs 9 of 634 other weekday 8:30 closes (1.4 per 100). p = 0.26, so the difference could easily be chance.
- Each holdout half on its own: 2024 1 of 24 vs 5 of 237; 2025-26 1 of 38 vs 4 of 397.
- The tester's 7x (p = 0.011) came from comparing with random times of day and using a looser 95% bar.

(2) The one release flip we can replay on the real settlement index and Kalshi's own book (09-11 CPI) would cost today's bot nothing. The deployed gates refuse every losing offer:
- The jump gate refuses DOGE NO at 92c and HYPE NO at 98c. The index had already moved 6-9 times its normal one-second step against NO in the 3 s before those offers appeared (checked to the millisecond).
- The 10c and 15c gap caps refuse SOL NO 70c, XRP NO 77c and BNB NO 86c.

It buys five winners instead (about +$18 at full size, an upper bound). So neither the tester's -$58 nor the execution skeptic's -$175 is what a 09-11 repeat costs today. The execution skeptic's emulation left out the jump gate and the 10c cap. Point (2) rests on a replay of the tape.

(3) The stats skeptic's $0.02 is too low. Live (09-15..10-16), the bot's own model was 99.5%+ sure of a side that then lost at 51 coin-closes. The bot held that losing side for $20 or more in 15 of them (21 counting small legs). That is about 30 in 100, not the ~10 in 100 implied by spreading 0.4 markets over 4-5 coins.

MONEY, built from measured pieces and clustered by close:
- About +$0.09/day, 90% range -$0.06 to +$0.32. There is a 28-in-100 chance the guard is worth nothing or less.
- Out of sample only: +$0.11/day.
- If release closes also hand the bot extra winners, as 09-11 did, it drops to about -$0.02/day.

The guard is cheap insurance with a small, unproven value, not a demonstrated saving. The jumpy-minute effect itself is real: a coin more than 4 ruler-sd off at 45 s left in 15 of 66 release closes vs 21 of 662 (p = 6e-8). It barely reaches the bot's 99.5% gate.

SIDE FINDING (lose less, bigger than this idea): the main bot's 15-min markets since 10-04 (ledger) are 373 markets, net -$429.59.
- 11 losers averaging -$90.45; 361 winners averaging +$1.57.
- It loses 2.9 times in 100 against a break-even of 1.7 in 100.
- The bot holds the losing side in about 30-40 of every 100 cases where its own model is 99.5%+ sure and wrong. That is where the money goes.

idea.name: Worlds 2026 futures liquidity pots ($10.2k/week on 102 markets): one-sided 1,000-lot YES bids at the scoring reference on the 4-10c futures, pulled whenever a Worlds match is live (free lolesports schedule API)
idea.mechanism: 102 Worlds futures carry $100-per-week liquidity programs (started 10-15 17:46-19:01Z, end 10-22; target 1,000, discount 5000 bps). 1) Rest post_only 1,000-lot YES bids at the YES scoring reference on 6-8 cheap futures (4-10c YES, ~$40-100 collateral each) where a new 1,000 takes ~30-45% of the YES side (QUALIFIERS FIN-IG 7c share 0.41, FIN-DK 9c 0.43, FIN-AL 10c 0.44, SSF-LY 9c 0.43, FMVP-KNIGHT 5c 0.31), i.e. about half that share of the market's pot. 2) Poll esports-api.lolesports.com getLive/getSchedule every minute; cancel every resting order while any Worlds match is live and re-post at the new reference after it ends (futures move only on results). 3) Optional with more capital: two-sided 1,000 at the references on a mid-priced qualifier market holding only ~2,000 a side (~50-65% share, approximate walk). 4) Skip longshots stacked at 1c with 12k-20k (share 5-7%). Post from MAIN (credit lands in pool 0); expiration_time and cancel-on-pause on every order (R1-N2-07).
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi pays the pot. Between matches a seller into a 4-10c YES bid is mostly exiting, not informed, because the only real information (match results) arrives on a public schedule and we are pulled then. The pots are one day old, so incumbent size is still ~2,000 a side on many of them.

test.result:
SHARES FELL FAST, THEN HELD.
- The hunter measured a 0.41-0.44 share for a new 1,000 on the named cheap YES sides (22:00Z 10-15, approximate walk, about 4 h after listing).
- By 01:41Z it was 0.15-0.22. At 09:10Z it was 0.14-0.22: FIN-IG 0.219, FIN-DK 0.159, FIN-AL 0.146, SSF-LY 0.152, FMVP-KNIGHT 0.144.

- Holdout (recorder 09:18-09:43Z, 21 cheap sides): a 1,000 joining at the reference held a mean share of 0.138 (median 0.129). One reference moved in 520 side-polls.

IT IS A TICK WAR.
- Under the filing walk, a 1,000-lot one tick above a stack takes 100% of that side, because the walk stops once it reaches 1,000.
- So the stacks keep stepping up. 27 of 47 cheap-side references rose between snapshots a and b with ZERO trades. 1 fell and 19 were unchanged. 8 qualifier markets rose 2c in the same 05Z hour.
- The recorder caught a whole stack jumping from 10c to 12c within 60 s (PENTA-1).
- Bidding one tick above would book $50/week per side on paper, but it is not stable.
- Sum of YES bids across the 19 teams: FIN 1.84 (fair total 2), SF 3.86 (4), QF 7.63 (8). The war has pushed the cheap bids to within 4-8% of fair in aggregate.

FILLS ARE RARE BETWEEN MATCHES.
- Pre-pot (16.9 days): 17 of the 20 qualifier cheap sides had no YES sales at or below today's reference. The other 3 had 14-42 contracts.
- Pot window outside match windows (0.64 day): no hits on any of the 31 candidate sides.
- The idea's reason is wrong, though. Open interest is 0 on 8 of the candidate qualifier markets, so no one is "exiting". Any seller is opening a NO bet.
- Win-Worlds longshots behave differently: sellers hit KXLOL-WORLDS26-LY's 2c bid for 7,515 contracts outside match windows in 15 h.
- In-game props are not safe even with a schedule pull. TEEMO and PENTA-1 traded at 57-93c during or just after the MVK-FUR match (03:01-03:45Z), then fell back to 7-12c.

PULL TIME: 18 of the 152 hours left this week are inside match windows (12%). Swiss weeks are up to 25-29%; the QF/SF week is 11-18%.

MONEY. Assumptions: walk at snapshot-b shares, credit = pot x 0.5 x share, x 0.88 for pull time, x 0.90 for the coin-race payment calibration.
- $300 of collateral covers 8 cheap qualifier/FMVP YES sides: $50/week of credit = $7.2/day gross, $5.7/day after pull and payment, $3.4/day if shares fall another 40%.

idea.name: CLIFF product-score concentration: be the dominant maker on every eligible leg of a few small games
markets: NCAAF 1H / team totals of small games
idea.mechanism: The CLIFF score multiplies across a combo's legs: holding share f on k legs of the same combos scores (1+f)^k - 1, not k*f. A maker who dominates all eligible legs of one game takes a more-than-proportional share of every same-game combo's 25% pool.
idea.why_mispriced: Incumbents already exploit this on the big legs; small games' legs are thin enough for a $300-1,000 maker to hold a large share.
idea.must_be_true: Combos on small games carry enough fees, and fill P&L on thin legs is not as bad as TDPROT's -13.8c.
idea.evidence_so_far: 4,494 sampled prop combos: 26% of the CLIFF comes from combos with ONE eligible leg, 22% two, 11% three, 15% four. A small newcomer on one leg keeps 1.00x / 0.86x / 0.73x / 0.62x / 0.54x of the equal-split rebate when an incumbent holds 0 / 30 / 50 / 70 / 90% of every leg; our own boost f=0.5 on 4 legs = 2.03x the additive score, f=1.0 on 2 legs = 1.5x. Fill P&L on thin legs measured negative (TDPROT -13.8c; soccer BTTS -1.6 to -3.4c FRONT).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown; probably $0, because the thin legs that make concentration possible are the ones where fills lose. WEAK. Worst: -$20 to -$80 per game day at 20-lot clips.
idea.settlements_per_day: Daily (soccer, NHL) or weekly (NCAAF, NFL)
idea.test_plan: Free check first: rank games by (sampled combo fee containing the game's eligible legs) / (sum of those legs' maker volume) from the existing tape sample (combos.jsonl.gz, legvol.json in r2-sports-maker-cliff/), to see whether any game offers > 5c a contract on > 5k contracts. Only then consider a recorder.
idea.prior_reason: It exploits the scoring formula rather than a price, but every thin leg measured loses on fills, and holding most of a leg's volume means holding most of its adverse selection.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New; exploits the program's scoring formula.
idea.worst_case: -$20 to -$80 per game day at 20-lot clips.
merged_from: r2:sports-maker-cliff: Product-score concentration: be the dominant maker on EVERY eligible leg of a few small games

test.method: Sources: trade tape and settlement only (no replay). (A) The product-score boost: r2's 168 hourly 5-s windows of the GLOBAL trade tape 10-07..10-13 (4,494 prop combos with legs), per combo and game/leg-family j = eligible legs held, share = ((1+f)^j-1)/((1+f)^j-1 + j(1-f) + other live legs) with the other makers taken as many small ones (the case MOST favourable to us); BOOST = that take / the additive take; 90% window bootstrap and a time-split (first 84 windows vs last 84) holdout (boost.py, boost_split.py, boost2.py). (B) The free check the idea asked for: per GAME CLIFF per in-play maker contract R_g = pool on the game's eligible legs (0.25 x taker fee x eligible/all legs, LIVE split, filed 0.01 minimum score) / in-play contracts of every market in the game's sampled eligible series-events. In-play volume (after scheduled start K: soccer occ-4h, NHL/NCAAF occ-3h) pulled here from event candlesticks for 489 events (pull_ip.py) + r3's 230 -> 206 complete games (108 soccer, 59 NHL, 39 NCAAF). Robustness: R without the game's single biggest sampled combo; league selection on games before 10-11 00Z, scored on later games; 90% game-cluster bootstrap (games.py). Money at a per-game capacity Q with r3's measured D200 static in-play fill markouts. (C) KXNFLTDPROT (in the idea's market list): every in-play trade of all 182 traded TDPROT markets (r3 tapes, untruncated) + the combo sample; pool with and without r2's unknown-combo fee redistribution (ratio=1 is a lower bound); a concentrator route through the 'cash-out' flow (maker SELLS YES at 98-99c / BUYS YES at 1-2c, settled cost ~1c) modelled leg by leg with the product score (tdprot_conc.py, tdp_ext.py, extremes.py, cashout_tab.py). HOLDOUT: NFL week-7 TNF SEA@DEN, not in the data that formed the idea -- its 44 TDPROT markets, every trade, and 53 fresh hourly 5-s windows of the global tape 10-14 00Z..10-16 05Z (holdout_tnf.py, tnf_ext.py). 1,088 public Kalshi GETs (no auth), 2 web fetches of the CLIFF help article. Recorders checked afterwards: tape and feed files written within seconds; 114 GB free. All files in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R2-M-24-P/ (RESULT.json saved there).

test.result:
THE IDEA AS WRITTEN IS DEAD. The product score does nothing on small games because their combos hold only one of the game's eligible legs. Share of a game's pool that comes from combos holding ONE of its legs: soccer 97%, NCAAF 72-76%, MMA 90%, tennis 98%. BOOST over the additive take at f = 0.1/0.3/0.5: soccer 1.00/1.01/1.01x (fit half 1.00x, hold half 1.00-1.01x), NCAAF 1.01/1.03/1.04x, NHL 1.05/1.09/1.10x (j=2 holds 61%), MMA/tennis 1.00-1.01x. The boost is real only where nobody small can dominate: NFL 1.12-1.41x, MLB 1.08-1.27x, NBA/WNBA 1.10-1.49x, and cross-game leg families 1.10-1.35x at f=0.3. But ONE leg-event there trades a median 326k (NFL), 251k (MLB) or 83k (WNBA) contracts in play, so f = 0.1 needs 25-33k contracts on a single leg-event. We make about 300-800 per leg per game.

FREE CHECK (R_g > 5c on > 5k in-play contracts): 6 of 206 games pass (3 soccer, 3 NHL), but NONE stays above 5c once its single biggest sampled combo is removed. That one combo is 74-80% of the game's pool (ASLSLA 14.0c -> 4.4c, CARCHI 10.5c -> 0.2c). Pooled R per in-play contract: soccer 0.64c (90% 0.49-0.80), NHL 0.94c (0.58-1.40), NCAAF 0.23c (0.14-0.36).

League holdout: no league reaches 5c pooled in the fit period (best Ligue 1 1.58c, Liga MX 1.21c, NHL 1.13c), so nothing is selected. The same leagues in the hold period: Liga MX 1.80c, NHL 0.71c, Ligue 1 0.42c.

Money as a capped in-play maker on all of a game's eligible legs, using measured static-quote fill markouts:
- soccer: +0.08c/contract at Q = 500 a game (+$41/week over 108 games); +0.30c at Q = 2,000. Incumbent dilution of 0.54-0.86x is not yet applied and turns it into -0.07..+0.19c.
- NHL: -3.3c a contract.
- NCAAF: -1.75c a contract.

THE SURVIVING CELL is KXNFLTDPROT, reached through the cash-out flow.
- 72% of its in-play volume (24,975 of 34,701 contracts/week) is cash-out flow on decided legs. That flow cost its makers -0.81c a contract settled (se 0.19, 14 games). The rest of the flow cost -16.0c (se 10.6), and our static quote lost -33c (r3).
- CLIFF per in-play contract: 7.70c on the lower bound (no redistribution; pool $2,672/week) to 17.96c by the r2 method ($6,231/week; 90% window bootstrap 7.8-30.0c).
- 77% of the pool comes from combos with 4+ live TDPROT legs, so the product boost is real here: 1.15x at f=0.1, 1.32x at f=0.25.
- Model, taking a share s of each leg's cash-out flow: s = 0.10 -> net +$147 (lower bound) to +$295/week on 2,498 contracts made (+5.9 to +11.8c a contract); s = 0.25 -> +$393 to +$787/week on 6,244 contracts.

HOLDOUT (TNF SEA@DEN, one game, not used to form the idea): 7,289 in-play contracts, 98% of them cash-out flow, cost -1.02c. Pool $406-800 from 19 sampled combos -> R 5.57-10.98c. s = 0.10 -> +$26 to +$59 for the game; s = 0.25 -> +$66 to +$152 (+3.6 to +8.5c a contract). The sign holds out of sample; the size depends on four unmeasured things (see next_test).
test.artefact_checks:
(1) Per-game R is sampling noise. A game's pool rests on a median of 5-7 sampled 5-s combos, each scaled x720. Every 'R > 5c' game collapses when its biggest combo is removed, so it is reported that way, not as a find.
(2) Dead legs: a leg with zero in-play volume earns nobody anything (LIVE split). r3 already killed the 'sole maker on a dead leg' version ($441/week once two single-combo legs are taken out).
(3) Fee redistribution: r2 scales each window's looked-up combos up by the unknown combos' fee (ratio up to 8.9 in the TDPROT windows). The ratio = 1 figures are a lower bound and are quoted first. Combo maker fees (x1.47) are excluded.
(4) The cash-out cost is settled, not marked. A maker selling YES at 99c on a decided leg loses exactly 1c, and a review reversal makes that side MONEY, so it has no tail. TDPROT prices are whole cents (linear_cent) and 99c is the top tick.
(5) TDPROT markets 'close and expire early if the event occurs' (rules read 10-16), so the cash-out flow lives in the minutes between a touchdown and the early close. The flow exists (23,325 contracts at 99c in the wk6 tapes), but that short window makes queue position decisive.
(6) The boost model assumes the other makers are many small ones, the case most favourable to us. A real incumbent with its own product boost dilutes us more.
(7) In-play only: pre-game volume is excluded, per the article ('only maker volume traded after the scheduled start'). The K offsets were verified by r2/r3 for NFL, NCAAF, NHL and soccer.
(8) This is NOT a loss rate for OUR fills. The cash-out cost is what that flow paid whoever made it; whether WE get any of it is unmeasured.
(9) The CLIFF article (re-read 10-16) does not say whether maker volume is counted in contracts or dollars. It scores the 'fraction of Eligible Maker Volume in each Eligible Component outcome' and excludes Rule 5.17 abusive practices.

TDPROT cash-out route: the whole flow is 24,975 contracts/week in-sample (half of it on one Monday-night game) and 7,130 on the holdout TNF game. Our share s is NOT measured; the 99c YES-offer queue in the minutes after each touchdown sets it. At s = 10-25% that is ~2,500-6,200 contracts/week. Collateral is ~1-2c a contract (under $130/week), so bank size does not bind.

refs.strongest_objection:
We could not get the supply the money model assumes. The tester's take of 10-25% of the KXNFLTDPROT 'cash-out' flow is not available to a newcomer at 99c.

The flow is not free-floating. Takers sweep a queue of 99c sell-YES offers that other makers fill days ahead. My own pull covered 10 NFL games: 31,575 in-play contracts at 2c or less or 98c or more.
- 88% of it arrived in single taker orders that hit 3 or more resting orders at once.
- The same clip sizes recur market after market: 30 x25, 5 x24, 101 x19, 100 x18, 50 x17, 365/367, plus 1,000-3,000 lots.
- Right now all 40 open week-7 TDPROT markets I read already have 232 contracts resting at 99c, about two days before kickoff.
- 53% of the 98c-plus taker-buy flow came in orders that ended partway through a resting order. The taker stopped buying before the 99c queue ran out.

So the tester's design, posting at 99c 2 s after the first 95c-plus print, sits behind the whole ladder and gets nothing from those orders. The only way in is to undercut at 98c. That doubles the settled cost to 2c a contract, and the existing makers can match it.

Three program gates are also unproven:
- (a) All 1,254 TDPROT legs in the 706 combos I scanned picked YES. If Kalshi scores maker volume by the side of the 'Eligible Component outcome', a maker who sells YES at 99c scores nothing. That is 95% of the extreme flow.
- (b) Kalshi's 2026-09-02 CFTC filing still does not say whether volume is counted in contracts or dollars.
- (c) The same filing lets Kalshi revoke eligibility for participation 'inconsistent with the purpose of the Program', which is pricing information. The program also ends no later than 2027-01-01. That leaves at most 11 NFL weeks, and the first credit statement can only be read in early November.

Note: a WebFetch summary claimed volume is in 'dollars' and that volume after an outcome is decided does not count. The verbatim text says neither; do not cite it.

(1) The in-play "cash-out flow" isn't a flow we can take a share of. In both games one fast taker order sweeps a standing stack of resting 99c YES offers (1c NO bids) 0-50 s after the touchdown. The same order sizes (5, 30, 50, 100, 101, 365, 1000, 2000) show up in the same order on all 8 big swept legs across both games, so about 7 incumbents already farm exactly this. Our share is our size against their 2.3-4.2k stack per leg. We only get it by resting BEFORE the TD: 2 of 8 sweeps came within 1 s of the first 95c print, so posting after the TD misses them.

(2) Resting first locks collateral on every leg: X x 1c x 44-57 legs a game. That's about $250 a game at X=500 and about $2,000 for an 8-game Sunday slate, which is more than the $1,155 bank. The tester's "bank does not bind" is wrong for the version that works.

(3) Most of the pool sits on LOSING legs that trade only a few dozen contracts in play, in small 1-2c dumps by sellers, so it can't be bought at size. On SEA@DEN: Smith-Njigba 282c a contract on 135 contracts, Engram 536c on 34, Sutton 3,054c on 1.5.

(4) Kalshi's CFTC filing (2026-08-11, FOOTBALLSTATS Component Legs Liquidity Incentive Program) gives the purpose as increasing order-book liquidity "and thereby enhance pricing efficiency". It lets Kalshi's Chief Regulatory Officer revoke anyone whose participation is "abusive or in any way inconsistent with the purpose". 1c NO bids that fill only on legs already decided do nothing for price efficiency, so revocation is a real risk. The filing also lets the minimum score go as high as 0.2 (the help article says 0.01). It names FOOTBALLSTATS markets, while these combos are KXMVECROSSCATEGORY, so whether they are covered rests on the help article alone. It does confirm the tester's eligible/all-legs scaling.

Not measured: whether takers also sweep OUR added depth (no sports order book is recorded), whether volume is counted in contracts or dollars, and whether only the side the combo picked counts. All 342 sampled TDPROT picks are YES.
