idea.name: Gas price-cycle restoration taker: GasBuddy's live state average (endpoint now found) flags a restoration before noon ET; buy YES on the stale strikes of the cycling-state daily ladders, which learn the jump slowly
idea.mechanism: Midwest and Southeast cycling states jump 5-22c in one print when stations restore prices. Poll GasBuddy's state average every 10 min (POST https://www.gasbuddy.com/graphql, operation LocationBySearchTerm, trends{areaName today todayLow trend}, gbcsrf header scraped from window.gbcsrf on /home, apollo-require-preflight: true; 6 s spacing). When it shows a restoration before noon ET (state average up >= 4c on the day, trend +1), buy YES at the best ask on strikes between the market-implied median and the GasBuddy-implied level and hold to the next AAA print. Use only GasBuddy's CHANGE (its level is rounded to cents and sits ~2.5c below AAA).
idea.why_mispriced: On jump days the morning books are set by makers who are still learning: the implied median carries 36% of the jump by 9 AM ET, 53% by noon, 85% by 3 PM and 95% by 6 PM, and 12 of 84 jumps settled OFF the strike grid. Later in the day the makers are sharp (11 PM ET error 0.10c national, 0.13-0.5c in established states), so only the morning lag is usable.
idea.must_be_true: GasBuddy's day change tracks AAA's next print change to within ~1-2c on jump days; real ask size exists at the stale strikes before noon (books are thin); GasBuddy shows the restoration before the makers' own feed moves the book.
idea.evidence_so_far: Market learning curve: 84 jump state-days on 31 dates (candles). GasBuddy cross-section at ~5:45 PM ET 10-15: corr 0.76 (36 states) between GasBuddy-minus-AAA and the market's implied change for tomorrow, so by evening the makers' information already looks like GasBuddy. Intraday GasBuddy history: NOT measured (no history endpoint found). Forward point: GasBuddy OH 4.10 at ~21:45Z vs AAA 3.9870 and a grid top of 4.075 (the 10-16 print will show it). Public nowcasts without GasBuddy are dead on these ladders (market error 0.62-0.70c vs the best public model's 1.13c; simulated maker -21c a contract).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not measured. Guess $0-50/day at 50-100 contracts on ~1 jump day a day at the current bank; at $5,000 capped by thin morning books (perhaps 2x). Worst day: a GasBuddy false alarm, -$50 to -$100 at 100 contracts across 3 strikes.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~1 cycling-state jump per day (84 jump state-days in 67 dates of the sampled ladders)
idea.test_plan: Run gb_rec.py (written, not started; OH, MI, IN, IL, WI, KY, FL, NC, CO, GA every 10 min) for 3 weeks beside 10-minute public top-of-book snapshots of the same ladders. Score jump days: GasBuddy's day change at 11 AM ET vs the realised print change, and a depth-capped paper taker at the 11 AM best ask. Pre-registered bar: GasBuddy change within 2c of the print change on >= 70% of jump days AND paper P&L > +5c/contract over >= 10 jump days. Starting the recorder is a writer/operator call.
idea.prior_reason: A measured, large morning learning lag in a busy new family plus a free fast feed, but the feed's intraday lead over the makers is unmeasured, morning books are thin, and it takes ~3 weeks to decide.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: A daytime taker on cycle-jump days only. D03 (gas taker, dead) lacked a feed; R1-C2-09 (GasBuddy nightly maker) is a different time and side; the 10-13 lane failed twice to find GasBuddy's data, now found.
idea.worst_case: -$100 on a false-alarm day at 100 contracts.

test.method: Sources, best first. (1) The settlement source itself: the AAA 10-16 print for all 51 states, fetched from gasprices.aaa.com at about 09:40Z 10-16. AAA's TLS certificate reads as expired on this box, so this public page was read without verification. Also Kalshi's settled values. (2) The Kalshi public trade tape, two pulls. t7: the full tape of 376 strikes on 36 up-jump (>=4c) state-days, Sep 1 to Oct 15. t10: an UNCONDITIONAL control, 8 AM-3 PM ET of the listing day, covering the 2-3 strikes just above the prior print on every October state-day (126 state-days, 14 dates, any outcome). (3) Own fills: none exist. (4) Hourly event candles (a replay; the hunter's candles.jsonl, 287 events, 50 dates), used only to price rules at the hour-close ask. GasBuddy: the live GraphQL endpoint (the hunter's 10-15 21:33-21:38Z snapshot of 40 states, plus my 10-16 ~10:00Z read of the 10 states and a field probe). Rules tested: an oracle; CONT (last change x beta, fit on September, tested on October); a no-signal baseline (buy YES above the prior print at the 9-12 ET ask, <=85c); the same rule only after an up-jump print; sweep-following (copy the first >=300-lot, <=90c morning YES sweep); and GBsim, an ASSUMED GasBuddy that knows the print to within 1, 2 or 3c (not a GasBuddy measurement). Forward cross-section: GasBuddy's 5:35 PM ET level vs the 6 PM market vs the 10-16 print. Scripts t1-t15 are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-06/. About 690 public Kalshi GETs, 13 GasBuddy POSTs, 4 AAA GETs, 0 authenticated calls, 0 orders.
test.n_markets: Candles: 287 state-day events (10 states). Jump tape: 376 strikes on 36 up-jump state-days (22 fresh, 14 continuation). Control tape: 262 strikes on 126 state-days. Forward point: 43 state ladders, 35 of them with GasBuddy. GBsim test at 11 ET: 84 strike-takes on 11 state-days.
test.n_independent_clusters: Clustered by date, because cycling states restore together. Candles: 50 dates (35 fit in September, 15 test in October). Up-jump state-days fall on 19 dates, fresh ones on 12 (in October: 12 fresh state-days on 6 dates in 14 days). Control: 14 dates. Forward point: 1 date.
test.result:
1) Forward point 10-16 (measured, 35 states). The 6 PM ET market already had the move: OH implied +9.1c vs a print of +10.0c, which settled above the top strike. Market error averaged 0.60c vs 1.86c for the GasBuddy level (offset-corrected, in-sample). GasBuddy-minus-market vs market error: correlation 0.09, slope 0.04, so by evening GasBuddy adds nothing. GasBuddy's level sits -8c to +1c off AAA depending on the state, so only its CHANGE is usable.
2) Learning curve, split (candles). FRESH jumps (the first print to show the restoration) are priced 8% at 9 AM, 20% at 11, 29% at noon, 59% at 3 PM and 91% at 11 PM. CONTINUATION days are priced 55% at 9 AM, 73% at 11, 69% at noon and 96% at 3 PM. The hunter's pooled 36%/53% curve is partly a grid artefact: the implied median is capped at the top strike (MI 10-09 read +14.5c for 10 hours vs +22.1c printed). On the 10-15 continuation day, OH and WI had no winning-strike ask at or below 90c at any hour from 9 AM.
3) Every no-signal or public-signal rule loses. CONT: -5 to -10c per contract, fit and test. Buying YES above the prior print at the 10-11 AM ask: -26 to -28c per contract over 50 dates (+48c on jump days, -36 to -41c on flat or down days). The same rule only after an up-jump print: -34 to -38c. Sweep-following: -28c per contract, 0 of 6 dates won (8 triggers, only 2 on jump days).
4) Morning YES flow above the prior print, unconditional (control, October, 14 dates): 26,256 contracts at -1.5c per contract (-$386). Big prints (>=50 lots, <=90c) lost -6.8c per contract (-$711). One false alarm, on GA's flat 10-06, cost that sweeper -$1,631 on 1,800 contracts. So the existing morning sweepers are not reliably informed.
5) Supply on fresh jump days (hindsight-selected winning strikes): 44.5k contracts were bought on the YES side at <=90c between 8 AM and noon ET over 22 state-days. That is a median of about 460 per state-day, in sweeps of 1,000-8,000 lots by an existing taker whose first informed sweeps land at about 10:00-11:30 AM ET (OH, 10-14 listing day: 13k contracts at 0.88-0.92 by 10:50 AM).
6) GBsim (assumed GasBuddy, replay-priced, jump days only). Within 2c at 11 AM: +23.7c per contract fit (September, 9 dates, 7 won) and +13.1c test (October, 84 takes, 7 dates, 6 won). Within 3c: +38.7c fit and +12.4c test at 11 AM, +7.9c test at noon. The edge fades by 3-6 PM.
7) Breakeven: a 10-11 AM trigger wins about +48c on a true jump and loses about -38c on a false alarm. So GasBuddy's trigger must be right on more than about 45-55% of the days it fires, against a base rate of 15% of state-days having a >=4c jump.
8) GasBuddy endpoint: the hunter's gb_rec.py home-page GET now returns HTTP 403; adding Accept and Accept-Language headers fixes it. The trends type has a 'yesterday' field, so the day change is one call (OH, 10-16 6 AM ET: today 4.10, yesterday 4.10). GasBuddy's evening 'trend +1' flag was right 1 time in 6: OH printed +10.0c, CO -2.5c, NM and WA fell, IL and IN rose about 1c.
test.artefact_checks: (a) Hindsight: the t7/t8 profits are on WINNING strikes of jump days, so they are positive by construction. The unconditional control (t10/t12) and the no-signal baseline (t14) correct for this, and both show the flow nets to about zero or negative without a real signal. (b) GBsim is not a GasBuddy measurement. It centres the signal on the true print, while GasBuddy's real 11 AM change vs the print is unmeasured: no intraday history exists, and the first print captures 36-82% of a restoration, so the mapping is noisy. (c) A candle ask is the hour-close quote, with size unknown. The tape shows real thousand-lot size executing at stale prices, but by someone else. (d) The grid cap on the implied median (top strike) understates what the market knows on big jumps; strike-level P&L is unaffected. (e) Units: prices in *_dollars, sizes in *_fp, taker fee 0.07p(1-p) per contract; rounding (<=1c per order) ignored. (f) Trade rows that look duplicated (same time, side, price and size) were kept as separate fills. (g) The forward-point offset was corrected with the in-sample median, and covers one date only. (h) 2 control strikes were skipped after repeated HTTP 429s (the shared IP was congested). Recorders kalshi_data and feed_data were still writing at 09:55Z; free disk 114.3 GB; scratch 0.8 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: Markets: winning strikes of KXAAAGASD OH, MI, IN, IL, WI, FL, NC, CO and GA on fresh jump days. There, 44.5k contracts were bought at <=90c before noon ET over 22 state-days (median about 460, mean about 2,000 per state-day), in 1,000-8,000-lot sweeps by an existing taker who starts at about 10:00-11:30 AM ET. Our share depends on whether our GasBuddy poll fires before that taker, which is NOT measured. At 98-300 contracts per strike, supply is not the limit; being first is. Continuation days have almost no stale supply: the market prices them at listing.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: Not measured. The deciding facts (how far GasBuddy's intraday reading leads the existing sweeper, and how often it raises false alarms) have no history. Conditional estimate only: if GasBuddy fires before the sweeper and is right at least 70% of the time, about 300 contracts per fresh jump state-day at roughly +10-15c net, with about 0.86 such state-days a day, gives roughly $25-40/day. If it fires after the sweeper, the leftover asks are worse and false alarms (-38c) dominate, giving $0 or a loss. Every public rule without GasBuddy measured here loses.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Not measured. Only if the recorder test passes: about 1.5-2x the current-bank figure. Supply exists in thousands of lots, but the best prices go to whoever is first.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: GBsim's October test at 11 AM has a per-date standard error of 74c (1 contract per strike) on 7 dates with about 12 takes per date, so the smallest detectable effect is about 15c per contract; the measured +13c sits at that floor. A 3-week recorder (about 18 fresh state-days on about 9 dates) would detect about 13c per contract. The control (14 dates, per-date standard error about $130 on the morning YES flow) cannot detect an edge of a few cents per contract.
test.worst_case: A GasBuddy false alarm, or a restoration that lands mostly in the NEXT print, bought at 10-11 AM: about -38c per contract on the strikes above the prior print. At 3 strikes x 98 contracts that is about -$110 per state, and -$200 to -$400 if two or three Midwest states fire together. Observed analogue: one morning sweeper lost $1,631 on 1,800 contracts at about 0.90 on GA's flat 10-06.

refs.strongest_objection:
The deciding unknown is still how accurate GasBuddy's live reading is before noon, and the one live look at it turned up a false alarm of exactly the size the trigger uses. Colorado's GasBuddy state average (fuelinsights LiveAvg) jumped +4.2c in a single 5-minute update at 06:30 ET 10-16 (4.307 -> 4.349), held for 75 minutes, then fell -4.7c at 07:45 ET. The GraphQL endpoint the idea names showed Colorado at 4.36 with trend +1 from at least 5:38 PM ET 10-15 until 7:14 AM ET 10-16 (Colorado Springs +10c), and back at 4.30 with trend -1 by 8:26 AM. AAA printed Colorado DOWN 2.5c on 10-16. On the 10-16 print, the GraphQL evening reading had a mean abs error of 1.16c over 13 states, worse than the market's 0.60c.

Two artefacts in the tester's numbers. (1) GBsim (+13c a contract) builds in look-ahead: it centres the signal on the true print and runs only on jump days, so false alarms are excluded by construction. Even GasBuddy's END-of-day change (complete information, available only after the market closes) was within 2c of the print on just 4 of 7 fresh jumps (3 dates), and overstated it by 1.3-2.4c on 5 of 7. (2) The pre-registered bar of +8c a contract is below a 3-week recorder's own smallest detectable effect (about 13-15c on about 9 dates). The 60% precision bar on 10-15 fires passes by luck about a quarter of the time at a true 45%. A pass would not prove an edge, so use lower bounds clustered by date.

This is not a kill. The incumbent sweeper's first sweep of 300 or more contracts lands at a median 11:14 ET (15 of 20 fresh listing days, my tape pull), and its timing is not tied to GasBuddy's 5-minute update grid (chi-square p about 0.09). So GasBuddy could still lead it; that is unmeasured. On 3 of 20 fresh days the market already had the jump at listing (zero YES taker flow under 92c on the winning strikes).
refs.independent_number: GasBuddy history exists after all (the hunter and tester said it did not). fuelinsights.gasbuddy.com /api/HighChart/GetHighChartRecords gives the daily state average to 3 decimals (79 of 93 days, Mondays missing), and /api/LiveAvg gives the live state average, updated every 5 minutes. GasBuddy's daily for listing day D-1 is effectively the AAA print D: correlation of daily changes 0.97-1.00 in OH, MI, IN, IL, NC, CO and GA (13-34 state-days each). Slope 0.837, fit on September. October holdout: 81 state-days on 9 dates, mean abs error 0.76c, against 3.12c for assuming no change. This uses the END-of-day value, which is known only after the market closes. On fresh jump days that END-of-day trigger was right on 6 of 8 fires over 3 dates, with 1 outright false alarm (FL, 09-08 print -1.0c after GasBuddy +4.5c). The 95% range is 35-97%, so the precision that decides the idea is not measured. Forward point 10-16 (13 states): slope-corrected GasBuddy END-of-day error 0.50c, GraphQL 5:35 PM reading 1.16c.

refs.strongest_objection:
Not refuted, but the case is much narrower. The morning money that a gas-restoration trigger could take is almost gone where the trigger works best. Where some is left, a bigger and earlier buyer already takes it.

(1) Midwest, October. On the five fresh Speedway-state restoration days (OH, MI, IN and IL on 10-09; OH on 10-15), only 539 contracts traded at 80c or less on the winning morning strikes between 9 AM and noon ET. That was worth $204 to every buyer combined. The first trades on those strikes (08:53-10:31 AM ET) were already at 88-99c. The five September Midwest days had 9,658 contracts worth $4,560.

(2) The rest of October. The whole October morning pool was $15.6k gross over 12 fresh state-days, and 99% of it sat on 3 days: FL 10-06 ($8.0k), WI 10-15 ($6.0k, a single 6,310-lot fill at 4c at 11:39 AM ET) and FL 10-13 ($1.3k). Each was taken in thousand-lot fills at 08:58-11:39 AM ET. For example, on 10-05 someone bought 2,000 at 2c at 08:58 and 7.7k at 15-17c at 10:17-10:22.

(3) The signal is noisy. On a no-news morning, GasBuddy's Colorado average swung between 4.29 and 4.36, so today-minus-yesterday read anywhere from -3c to +3c. That is one cent from a false 4c trigger, so Colorado is unusable. Idaho swung 5c while AAA moved 0.01c (4.8526 to 4.8527).

(4) Access is fragile. After about 155 calls in 85 minutes, GasBuddy put this IP behind a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403 with Cf-Mitigated: challenge). 5 of 34 ten-minute polls failed, 10:59-11:49Z. The proposed recorder (10 states every 2-5 minutes) calls more often than that.

(5) Faster public data exists. GasBuddy also publishes each station's price with its posted time, to the second, and OPIS (AAA's own data source) is sold commercially. The state average is the slowest public view of a restoration.

Live books on 10-16: every ladder opened at 87-99c asks on the far strikes, which then walked down through the morning. At 10-11 AM the median far ask was about 60c, so a trigger must be right about 60% of the time to break even. A perfect, first-in signal at the incumbents' prices would have made about $21-25/day at 98 contracts a strike in October, before any false alarm. No target state restored between 6:19 and 11:49 AM ET today, so the deciding measurement (does GasBuddy fire before the incumbent?) is still not measured. Not measured means plausible-needs-data, not dead.
refs.independent_number: From my own pull (424 strike tapes on 25 fresh up-jump state-days found from my own settled-market download, every strike at or above the prior print that existed before noon ET): October Midwest Speedway restorations (5 state-days) had 539 contracts at 80c or less on winning strikes between 9 AM and noon ET, worth $204 to everyone combined. The same window on 5 September Midwest days had 9,658 contracts and $4,560. 99% of October's $15.6k morning pool sat on 3 state-days (FL 10-06, WI 10-15, FL 10-13).

idea.name: 8:30 ET release-open taker: in the first 0-5 s of the 15-min window that opens at 8:30:00 ET on a US data release, take offers on the jump side when model fair - ask - fee >= 3c (strike known exactly, ~870 s left)
idea.lane: settlement-window-push x macro calendar x crypto 15-min
idea.mechanism: At 8:30:00 ET the next window opens with its strike already fixed (the pre-release 60-s average). The release then moves the index hard in the first 2-8 s. Read an exchange feed (Coinbase/Kraken, or the 5 Hz index if M-08 records it) at 8:30:00.0x, compute fair with K exact and ~870 s left, IOC-take any offer on the jump side where fair - ask - fee >= 3c within the first 5 s, and hold to settlement. Weekdays with an 8:30 release only (~4 weekdays in 5). Compatible with M-03 (which blocks the window that CLOSES at 8:30).
idea.why_mispriced: The opening book is thin and was quoted before the print; makers who have not pulled get run over by the release. The losers are opening makers and slow takers; in the public tape the fast 0-5 s takers are the winners.
idea.must_be_true: Our 43 ms warm send still catches some stale offers the existing fast takers leave, and the 0-5 s winners are not a few lucky days.
idea.evidence_so_far: INDEX: at weekday 8:30 ET closes the mean |move| in the first 10 s after the close is 3.83 sd vs 0.92 at other closes; a >= 4-sd move within 10 s at 19.6 of 100 coin-closes vs 1.3. PUBLIC TRADES (source 2): 150 next-window markets (30 releases x 5 coins), fair from index prints >= 1 s older than each trade: takers with model edge >= 3c in 0-5 s: 52 markets, 91,738 contracts, +21.6c contract-weighted, market-mean +7.0c (se 6.9c); halves +3.1c / +11.2c. All takers in 0-30 s: -1.7c market-mean. Smallest detectable effect ~14c a contract, so a hint, not a result. The general open-burst taker at non-release opens is dead (233 markets, market-mean -4.53c, se 2.93), so the release is the trigger. Our own fills: not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not measured for us. If +7c held on 50-100 contracts in 1-2 coins per release weekday: $4-14 per release weekday at the $1,155 bank, $15-50 at $5,000; $0 if the fast incumbents keep taking it first. Worst: a release that whipsaws inside the first minute (09-11 style) at 100 contracts bought at ~60c: -$60; -$250 at $5,000 sizing.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~5 markets per release weekday (about 4 weekdays in 5)
idea.test_plan: Free: pull public /markets/trades for the next 20 weekday 8:30 ET next-window markets x 5 coins (~100 calls) with our 1/s index and the Coinbase ticker for the sub-second move. Pre-registered bar: fair - price - fee >= 3c using only prints older than the trade; market-mean >= +3c with t >= 2 on >= 40 markets, both halves positive. Then a paper arm logging what our sender would have filled at +43 ms (own-book check). Live only with operator sign-off.
idea.prior_reason: A plausible stale-quote mechanism on a known schedule with a positive public-tape hint, but se 6.9c on 52 markets against a 14c detectable effect, and a race against incumbents who already win it; ~5 weeks to a forward read.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New: keys on the release at a window's OPEN. Different from R2-M-02 (840-s opening-minute taker, dead), M-02 (10-60 s before the close) and the ledger's CPI-day S&P ladder sweep.
idea.worst_case: -$60 per release at 100 contracts; -$250 at $5,000 sizing.

test.method: No replay used; three measurements. (A) RAW PRICE PROCESS (source 1, proxy): Binance spot 1-s klines (public data-api.binance.vision) for the whole 15-min window that opens at 8:30:00 ET on every BLS NFP/CPI/PPI day from 2024-01-05 to 2026-10-15 (98 release days x 5 coins; dates from the bls.gov schedules already copied by test-R3-M-03). Control: one seeded-random non-release, non-Thursday weekday 8:30 open per release day (96 days). Kalshi's rules applied to that series: strike = mean over the 60 s before 8:30:00, settle = mean over the last 60 s. Fair at d s after the open = Phi(ln(S/K)/(m*sig*sqrt(tau-60+20.5))), where sig = the pre-release 1-s sd over 300 s (what a bot has at 8:30:00). Vol multiplier m fitted by max likelihood on 2024-01..2025-11 (66 days), tested on 2025-12..2026-10 (32 days). Proxy check: the Binance outcome matches Kalshi's own result on 135 of 138 scored markets. (B) PUBLIC KALSHI TAPE (source 2): every public trade in the first 60 s of the 8:30-opening KXBTC15M/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE market on those days. Source endpoints: /historical/trades before the 2026-08-17 cutoff, /markets/trades after; 347 unauthenticated calls; trades de-duplicated by trade_id. Strike = Kalshi floor_strike, outcome = Kalshi result. The bot's fast feed = Binance aggTrades (ms) for 8:29:59-8:30:08, ratio-adjusted to Kalshi's strike. Fair uses only prices at least L = 0.10 / 0.25 / 1.0 s older than each trade. The idea's rule: jump side, fair - price - 0.07p(1-p) >= 3c, 0-5 s after the open. Scored per market (contract-weighted inside a market) and per day. OOS = Feb-Aug 2026; DISC = the hunter's 09-02..10-15 window. (C) The hunter's selection reproduced (spot = price at the open second, m=1). Side check: the 8:45 ET close of the same window against the live bot's 300-s ruler. Our own fills: none exist at window opens, so source 3 is not available. Scripts and outputs in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-05/ (calib.py/calib.txt, taker.py/taker.txt, fade.py/fade.txt, close845.py/close845.txt, check_proxy.py, pull_*.py, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: Tape: 131 markets with trades and feed (26 release days, Feb-Oct 2026); 87 of them on 26 days had trades the rule selects (57 OOS, 29 DISC). Dec 2025 and early-Jan 2026 opens had 0-17 trades. Raw feed: 490 release coin-days (330 fit, 160 test) plus 480 control coin-days.
test.n_independent_clusters: 26 release days on the tape (all 5 coins usually resolve the same way, so the day is the unit). Raw feed: 98 release days (66 fit, 32 test) and 96 control days.
test.result:
THE IDEA'S FAIR VALUE IS WRONG BY 15-29c AFTER A RELEASE.
- Raw feed, volatility: in the 5 min after an NFP/CPI/PPI print, price swings are 3.2x the pre-release level (median, 2024-25) and 2.7x (2025-26), vs 1.1x on control days.
- Raw feed, 5 s after the open: with pre-release vol, the model gives the jump side 78.5c, but that side wins 63.9 of 100 (fit, 330 coin-days). In the test period it is 84.3c vs 55.0 of 100. The model is too sure by 14.5c and 29.3c.
- Fitted multiplier m = 3.4 corrects 2024-25 (62.2c vs 63.9 wins). It still misses the test period (64.7c vs 55.0; NFP days won 31 of 100).
- The market already prices it right: on 20 OOS days, the jump-side price 1-5 s after the open sits on the corrected fair, +0.2c on average (se 2.3c).
- Tape, rule exactly as written (m=1, L=0.10 s), 87 markets / 26 days: market-mean -9.2c a contract (se 5.1); day-mean -7.3c (se 8.6). Contract-weighted it is +3.7c, carried by a few big BTC days. OOS -4.1c (se 6.1, 57 markets); DISC -18.9c (se 9.1, 29 markets).
- The model claimed +17.6c of edge on those trades; they realised -9.2c.
- With m = 3.4: -2.8c (se 6.8, 50 markets); OOS -11.6c (se 9.2); DISC +7.5c (se 10.0).
- The jump side lost on about 10 of 26 days, on all coins together. Same picture at L = 0.25 s and 1.0 s.
- Timing: 90% of the rule's contracts traded 1-5 s after the Binance jump and only about 6% inside 500 ms. The offers stayed up because they were not stale.
- The hunter's +7.0c does not reproduce. His spot was the print at the open second, before most of the jump (Binance jump median +0.8 s), so his filter picked the AGAINST-jump side (72% of contracts). On release days that filter scores -3.6c market-mean (se 5.6, 67 markets) and -10.5c contract-weighted.
- FADE variant (buy the against-jump side when it is >= 3c below the corrected fair): market-mean +20.6c (se 6.9, 49 markets / 17 days); OOS +12.6c (se 9.8). But OOS it is -10.3c contract-weighted, and its day-mean is +10.2c (se 12.9, 11 days). The 2024-25 raw feed gives no support: the jump side is fairly priced there, +1.8c gap (se 2.6c). Post-hoc hypothesis only.
- Side check for the live bot: the 8:45 ET close on release days is not riskier for the 300-s ruler. Closes where a 95%-sure side lost with 45 s left: 1 of 66 (2024-25) and 1 of 32 (2026), vs 2 of 66 and 0 of 30 on control days. Keep M-03's guard on the 8:30 close only.
test.artefact_checks:
- Binance-proxy outcome matched Kalshi's result on 135 of 138 markets; the 3 misses were moves under 2.3 bp.
- Kalshi strike / Binance strike-window mean stays within 0.9983-1.0007, so the price gap between the two sources cancels out.
- Self-tests passed:
  - the price lookup never returns a print newer than ts-L;
  - the scorer gives +9.9c on a planted +10c world and about minus the fee on a fair-priced world;
  - calibration fits m ~1.2 on a random-walk world (gap -0.6c) and finds +7.3c in a planted momentum world.
- Trades de-duplicated by trade_id. n is reported in markets and days, never trades. Prices taken from the *_dollars fields, unit decided once. Fee 0.07p(1-p) per contract (order-level roundup is under 0.1c at 98 lots).
- Limits:
  - Binance is a stand-in for the CF index (it is not a constituent).
  - The fills are the public tape's takers, not ours.
  - At the day level the tape alone has se 8.6c. The 98-day raw-feed measurement (overconfidence 3-6x its detection limit) is what makes the verdict decisive.
- The hunter's +7c came from a stale spot (the open-second print), as the reproduction above shows.
test.supply_we_would_get: Plenty is on offer, and that is the problem. The naive rule saw 201k 'edge' contracts in 0-5 s over 26 days (about 20k a day in the DISC window, mostly BTC). 90% of them were still there 1-5 s after the jump, because the market was right and the model was wrong. At 98 contracts the bot would fill whatever it wanted on 1-5 coins and lose about 9c a contract on average. The first-second book cannot be measured from our tape: the collector subscribes to each new window 25-62 s after it opens (checked: +62 s on 09-04, +25 s on 10-15).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 -- the rule loses. As written: about -9c a contract x 98 contracts x 1-5 coins = -$9 to -$45 per release day (about 3 release days a month), roughly -$1 to -$4 a day averaged.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0 (the loss scales about 4x: -$35 to -$180 per release day).
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
- Tape: se 5.1c at the market level on 87 markets (detects about 10c); se 8.6c at the day level on 26 days (detects about 17c).
- Raw feed: se 2.6c on 330 fit coin-days, about 5c at the day level. The measured overconfidence (-14.5c fit, -29.3c test) is 3-6x those limits.
- The fade variant would need about 80 release days (about 2 years) to detect +10c at the day level.
test.worst_case: A reversal day: the jump side lost on every coin together on 10 of 26 days. Holding 98 contracts on each of 5 coins at about 70c costs about -$345 at today's bank, and about -$1,400 at $5,000 sizing.
test.next_test:
None for this rule; do not paper-trade it.

Two reusable facts:
1. Any strategy at a window's OPEN needs a recorder that subscribes to the next window's ticker before 8:30:00 (those markets exist from about 00:01 UTC that day). Our collector misses the first 25-62 s of every window.
2. After a release, pre-release volatility understates the next 5 minutes by about 3x. Any fair value used near the start of a window after 8:30 ET (forecaster, ladder rests) should be checked against that.

The fade variant stays a hypothesis only. Re-running pull_kalshi.py, pull_binance.py and fade.py after each release is free (about 350 Kalshi calls). Pre-registered kill bar: OOS day-mean <= 0 after 20 more release days.

Housekeeping: two of my redundant Binance-history pulls (pull_bn_hist.py pid 386172, pull_rev.py hist pid 400792) were still running at return. They write only to this scratch folder (53 MB now) and will exit on their own; I left them alone per the no-process-touching rule. Both recorders were writing as of 6:27 am ET; 113.8 GB free disk.

idea.name: Quiet-second 70-80c favourite on the 15-min crypto series (no jump, 10-60 s left, model edge >= 2c) -- WEAK, post hoc, fragile to arrival time
idea.mechanism: Buy the 70-80c side at its ask when no print moved >= 2 sigma and the engine fair is >= 2c above ask + fee, outside the pin and forecaster windows; first qualifying second per market; hold to settlement.
idea.why_mispriced: Possibly a favourite-longshot bias at the low end of the band in the last minute (makers shading 70-80c favourites); not established, and the full no-jump band is flat in October.
idea.must_be_true: The +260 ms result is not an artefact of which offers happen to survive to that exact delay.
idea.evidence_so_far: Chosen AFTER looking at the FIT grid (best FIT cell: 250 fills +7.55c). At +260 ms: TEST 176 fills +6.26c (t 2.14, by day 2.38), UNSEEN 175 fills +5.70c. But at our real arrival offsets TEST is +1.06c (163 fills), at +150 ms +3.6c, and the 98-lot walk +1.5c in TEST. Worst UTC day -$92 at 20 lots (08-29/30). The no-jump ARM-ANY control over the whole 70-95c band is +0.25c at +260 ms / -2.07c at real arrival in October. A result that is not monotonic in delay is not trustworthy.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0-5/day at 20 lots at the current bank; nothing claimed at $5,000 until it holds at real arrival times. Worst tape day -$92 at 20 lots.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~13 fills/day
idea.test_plan: Free: score the frozen spec_N.json on new hours at +260 ms AND at real-arrival draws beside M-02; kill if the real-arrival line is <= +2c at 200 new fills.
idea.prior_reason: Post hoc cell whose edge collapses to +1c at our real arrival time; free to keep scoring beside M-02.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: A new cell, flagged post hoc so nobody mistakes it for a pre-registered pass.
idea.worst_case: -$92 tape day at 20 lots.

test.method: Tape only (source rank 2: our own recorder's rebuilt order book). No live or paper fills of this rule exist. I used the hunter's frozen scanner (bx_scan.py, grid_lib.py, bx_grid.py; SHA256 matches PREREG.txt). My streaming evaluator n_eval.py stays under 200 MB and reproduces the hunter's ARM-N exactly: FIT/TEST/UNSEEN signals 521/424/305, +260 ms lines +7.55c/+5.96c/+5.70c. The frozen rule was not changed: quiet second (|dz| < 2), 10-60 s left, ask 70-80c, engine fair minus ask minus fee >= 2c, pin and forecaster windows skipped, first qualifying second per market, IOC at the ask we saw, 20 lots, held to settlement. FRESH data, never scored for this cell: SEPX, the 446 September hours NOT in the hunter's FIT (scanned by the M-02 tester; 17.71 valid days; same calendar days as FIT, hours interleaved), plus 11 new October hours 10-15T21Z..10-16T09Z (I scanned T09; T07 and T08 excluded because their tape is ~4% of normal size). Also the hunter's holdouts TEST (10-01..10-15) and UNSEEN (08-25..09-01). Fills scored at every stored delay +0/75/150/260/500/1000 ms, at the stored real-arrival draw R, and at fixed weighted blends of our 87 measured forecaster arrival times (MIXFC: 68% near 260 ms, 22% near 1 s) and 77 pin arrival times (MIXPIN). Also run: paired per-signal survival analysis (paired.py); week, tau, coin and day tails (weekly.py); controls (edge < 2c, no edge filter, all trigger classes, 80-95c, 65-70c); a short-tau slice (short_tau.py, post hoc); and our own live forecaster fills by price (results/forecaster-live-orders.jsonl). Clustered by close and by UTC day. Everything is in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-14/ (n_eval.txt, n_eval_out.json, paired.txt, weekly.txt, short_tau.txt, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: Fresh (never scored for this cell): 955 signal markets (SEPX 942, new October hours 13). 462 could be filled at +260 ms and 435 at real arrival. All holdouts pooled (UNSEEN + TEST + new hours + SEPX, 38.58 days): 1,684 signal markets, 811 fills at +260, 747 at real arrival. In-sample FIT: 521 signals, 250 fills.
test.n_independent_clusters: Fresh: 378 closes over 30 UTC days at +260 (365 closes at real arrival). All holdouts: 681 closes over 52 days at +260, 648 closes over 53 days at real arrival.
test.result:
Frozen ARM-N, 20 lots, per contract after fee.

- **FIT** (the cell was picked here as the best of ~240): +260 +7.55c on 250 fills (t 3.06 by day).
- **Fresh SEPX** (17.7 days, same September days, hours the hunter never looked at):
  - +260: +0.90c on 460 fills (SE 2.05c, t 0.45 by day).
  - Real arrival R: +0.77c on 431 fills. MIXFC: +1.37c.
  - +150: +1.31c. +75: +3.78c. +0: +3.90c.
  - The 6.65c gap between FIT and SEPX (~2 SE) is the cost of picking the best cell.
- **The idea's own kill bar** ("kill if the real-arrival line is <= +2c at 200 new fills"): the fresh real-arrival line is +0.81c on 435 fills, and the +260 line is +1.04c on 462. KILL FIRES.
- **October** (TEST plus 11 new hours, 14.0 days):
  - +260: +6.26c on 176 fills (t 2.38 by day).
  - But real arrival: +0.76c on 165 fills. +150: +3.98c. +500: +3.47c. +1000: -2.74c.
- **All holdouts pooled:**
  - By delay: +0 +3.24c, +75 +2.92c, +150 +2.22c, +260 +3.11c (t 1.94 by day), +500 +2.15c, +1000 +1.96c.
  - Real arrival: +1.74c on 747 fills (t 1.20). MIXFC: +2.82c.
- **Must-be-true check** (is the +260 line an artefact of which offers survive?):
  - For arrival draws of 205-380 ms, R and +260 agree: 527 holdout signals fill at both, at +2.52c and +2.68c. The R-versus-260 gap is not offers flickering in and out.
  - The gap comes from the ~22% of our real arrivals that land around 1 s. The 87 offers still there at 260 ms but gone by then were winners at +12.45c; what is left at about 1 s earns -1.79c.
  - Offers gone within 75 ms (406 holdout signals) won 83 in 100 at 74c, +9.2c had we been there at +0. Offers still there after 1 s (338) won 73 in 100, -0.8c. Speed decides who gets the good ones.
- **Controls** (holdout, +260):
  - Edge < 2c: -0.52c on 900 fills, against +3.11c with edge >= 2c. The model filter separates about 3.6c.
  - Quiet-second 80-95c: +2.39c over the whole holdout but -1.08c in October.
- **Holdout by ISO week:**
  - +260: +4.0, +5.7, -1.9, +3.6, -3.6, +8.5, +4.6, +3.8c.
  - Real arrival: +5.1, +3.0, +0.1, +1.9, -4.3, +6.2, -1.6, +0.2c.
- **Side finding (post hoc, a hypothesis, not a pass):** the 10-29 s slice of this cell is in effect the forecaster's own window at 70-75c, just under its 75c price floor (MIN_PX 0.75 in forecaster_live.py).
  - It is positive in every period. Holdout: 138 signals; +260 49 fills at +14.3c (t 2.9 by day); real arrival 51 fills at +9.6c (t 2.2).
  - By period: FIT +11.1c, UNSEEN +15.7c, SEPX +8.5c, October +29c on 9 fills.
  - The same slice with edge < 2c loses 11.8c a contract.
  - Our own live forecaster fills in the next bucket up (75-80c): 46 fills in 42 markets, 398 contracts, +$76.36 (+19.2c a contract), 5 losing fills.
  - Supply is about 3.6 signals and 1.3 tape fills a day.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Frozen code hashes match PREREG, and my evaluator reproduces the hunter's counts and lines exactly. (2) SEPX does not overlap FIT (M-02's mk_hours.py asserts it), but it sits on the same calendar days. That makes it a strong test of an edge in the same period and a weak test across time; the October and August holdouts cover the across-time part. (3) Rows are restricted to each source's good hours. 10-16T07 and T08 are excluded: 6.7 MB and 4.9 MB of book deltas against ~175 MB normally. (4) Selection: picking the best of ~240 FIT cells at SE ~2.6c should inflate the winner by about 2.5-3 SE (~7c), which is roughly the whole FIT edge. (5) The pattern across delays is noise around about +2-3c. Holdout signals that fill at every delay (338) run -0.79/+0.39/+1.23/+2.13/+1.92/+3.15c from +0 to +1000 ms in the SAME markets, so 2-4c differences between delays come from contract weighting and price, inside the noise. (6) Rival orders sent in the same millisecond are invisible to the rebuilt book, which only removes faster takers, so every tape number is an upper bound. (7) R is a single stored draw; the MIXFC weighted blend is reported next to it to remove that draw's noise. (8) No tape loss rate is presented as ours.

test.smallest_detectable_effect: Fresh SEPX alone: SE 2.0-2.15c a contract, so about 4-6c is reliably detectable. It rules out the FIT +7.55c (the gap is about 3 SE of SEPX). All holdouts pooled: SE 1.5-1.6c, so about 3-4.5c. The pooled +1.7c (real arrival) to +3.1c (+260) sits at or below that limit.

Add a paper variant identical to the live forecaster except MIN_PX 0.70, so only the 70-75c entries are new, and run it beside the live 75c floor. idea.name: Record Kalshi's 5 Hz CF index channel (BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE at 200 ms) and re-run the pre-print band trigger on the index itself (NEEDS DATA; operator decision)
idea.mechanism: Since 3 Sep 2026 Kalshi streams the CF index at 5 Hz for these five coins (CF methodology: 200 ms effective time). The 800 ms value of second s-1 is the index ~200 ms before the 1-s print, with no exchange-basis noise. Fire the M-02 band IOC when that sub-second value is >= 4 sigma from the last 1-s print and the band offer is >= 2c under the fair priced off it, i.e. before the fast takers who react to the 1-s print.
idea.why_mispriced: The same stale-offer race as M-02, entered 50-200 ms earlier. The Bitstamp-book version of this trigger won 32 of 95 races at +15.6c a contract but died on false triggers (Bitstamp's move vs the composite print); the settlement index itself should not carry that basis error.
idea.must_be_true: The 5 Hz values arrive >= 100 ms before the 1-s print is sent, and the fast bots do not already act on them (they clear offers 0-40 ms AFTER the 1-s print, which suggests most do not).
idea.evidence_so_far: Merger check: our tape hour 2026-10-16T00 (cfbenchmarks_value) holds 3,599 prints per index, all on whole seconds, so the 5 Hz channel is NOT recorded (the brief's '5/sec' line does not match our tape). The Bitstamp pre-print trigger scored without look-ahead (dead, see dropped): FIT 60 fills +8.5c (t 2.39), TEST 40 +3.93c (t 0.84), UNSEEN 33 -7.56c, combined ~-1.3c on 73 fills; triggers whose print came in at 2-4 sigma lost -7.1c in October. The r2 upper bound (book 200 ms before the send) doubled fills at the same per-contract edge. The killed paper arm-5hz (pinrun 10-09..10-13) used the channel only for the pin's projection.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown. Bounded by ~$4-5/day at 20 lots if it captures only the race-winning share without the Bitstamp false triggers; $20-25/day at 98 lots ($5,000 bank). Cost: one recorder.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~3-5 signals/day
idea.test_plan: Operator decision, because the collector is untouchable: record cfbenchmarks_value_5hz for 7 days in a separate read-only recorder (or he adds the channel to the collector), then re-run feed_an.py with the 5 Hz value as v_hat. Bar: >= 60 fills, >= +4c a contract after fee at its own arrival time, both halves > 0.
idea.prior_reason: Cheap to decide (7 days of recording) and it would extend the best-evidenced idea of the round, but it needs an operator call on a new process and its upside is bounded and unmeasured.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: A new use of the 5 Hz channel (an entry trigger for band offers), not the killed arm-5hz projection use. P07/D25/F17 used exchange feeds only as loss gates.
idea.worst_case: $0 plus the recorder's cost if the fast bots already use it; Bitstamp-like false-trigger losses (~-7c a contract) if the 800 ms value is noisy.

test.method: Three measurements, best source first. (1) RAW INDEX FEED, live: rec5hz.py recorded Kalshi's cfbenchmarks_value + cfbenchmarks_value_5hz for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE for 45 min (10-16 10:06-10:51Z, read-only market-data subscription; 13,499 coin-seconds, 67,493 5 Hz frames). rec_an.py measures how far ahead of the 1-s print the 800 ms frame arrives (on Kalshi's send stamps and on our own receipt clock), how much of the 1-s move it already shows, how often a trigger on it is false, and rival trades between the two frames (joined to the collector's trade tape). (2) TRADE TAPE, unfiltered: prescan.py over 417 tape hours 08-25..10-16 (every 2nd hour Aug/Oct, every 4th Sept). For every coin-second with a print it counts taker trades by side in the live 15-min market in windows -600..-400 / -400..-200 / -200..0 / 0..40 / 40..300 ms around the print's Kalshi send, split by coin group (5 Hz coins vs BNB/HYPE/ZEC/NEAR, which have no 5 Hz feed), period (08-25..09-02 is before the 5 Hz channel existed, then Sept, then Oct), print size, and whether the previous second was quiet. t-values are clustered by hour. (3) REAL RIVAL FILLS of the band rule (the refute-execution tester's tt_scan rows, with our own orders and the 8:30 ET closes removed): money per market on the first 20 contracts after fee, clustered by close, by window, coin group, print size and week (preprint*.py, coinsplit.py, coinweek.py, octrobust.py, augsep.py, fastwin.py). Cross-check on r2's book rows (tb_early.py; that file covers only ~10 days, mostly August). No replay used. Holdout: Aug-Sep vs October halves.
test.n_markets: Recording: 13,499 coin-seconds, of which 79 had the 800 ms value >= 4 sigma. Tape scan: 417 hours (about 1.5M quiet and 60k big-move coin-seconds). Real fills: 12,478 band jump-markets; the class this idea targets (5 Hz coins, >= 4 sigma print, a rival filled between -200 and +40 ms) is 260 markets.
test.n_independent_clusters: Target class: 231 closes over 53 days (Aug-Sep 177 closes, Oct 54). Tape scan: 417 hours. Recording: one 45-minute session.
test.result:
The 5 Hz feed itself is good. The 800 ms frame arrives 236 ms before the 1-s print (p10 210 ms) and already carries 80 parts in 100 of that second's move. When it shows >= 4 sigma, the print came in at >= 2 sigma 96 times in 100 (79 cases) and was never against it. So the false triggers that killed the Bitstamp version do not happen here.

What kills the idea is its premise that the fast bots do not trade before the 1-s print. On these five coins, for >= 4 sigma prints after a quiet second, 75 of every 100 taker trades in the 200-600 ms BEFORE the print is sent are already on the side the print will favour (October, t ~30; quiet seconds are 50/50). It was 79 in 100 in August, before Kalshi's 5 Hz channel existed. So these traders work off exchange books and are faster than the 5 Hz frame. In the live recording there was no extra favoured buying between the 5 Hz frame and the 1-s print (18.0 vs 18.5 contracts per 100 ms).

What a 5 Hz trigger could still reach is the gap from about -175 ms to the fast bots that react to the print (0-40 ms). Real rival fills in that gap (-200..+40 ms) on the 5 Hz coins after >= 4 sigma prints earned +3.24c a contract after fee (260 markets, se 2.1c, t 1.5). By half: Aug-Sep +2.65c (200 markets), Oct +5.11c (60 markets). These were picked knowing the print in advance, so a real trigger would do worse, and they sit below the pre-registered +4c bar.

The five coins' band edge in October is about zero overall: +0.72c (191 markets), against +11.43c on BNB/HYPE/ZEC/NEAR (163 markets; difference t 3.3). Those four have no 5 Hz feed, so this idea cannot reach them. Weekly band fills on the 5 Hz coins went W35 +9.1c -> W41 +0.5c -> W42 -0.3c.
test.artefact_checks:
The 5 Hz top-of-second frames equal the 1 Hz prints 13,498 of 13,498 (1 missing), and our 1 Hz prints equal the collector's tape 13,499 of 13,499. The 236 ms lead from Kalshi's send stamps and the 237 ms from our own receipt clock agree, so the laptop clock offset (~475 ms) does not enter.

Pre-print flow: the quiet-second control is flat. Splitting on a quiet previous second rules out reactions to the previous print. 417 of 423 hours passed a send-lag sanity check (6 had missing files). The real-fill rate before the print rises with print size partly because the price filter lets more offers in after a big print, so the claim about who trades when rests on the unfiltered scan, not on that rate.

Real-fill money is picked knowing the true print, which flatters a 5 Hz trigger. r2's book rows (mostly August) agree on supply: early entry on the 5 Hz coins doubled fills (100 vs 47 at +250 ms) at the same edge per contract, but that was in August, before the edge faded.

Recorder health: collector and feed files were written up to 10:52:35Z, and the tape is back to normal size (140 MB of book deltas in 52 min). Free disk 113.6 GB, free RAM 4.3 GB, scratch folder 6.6 MB. No process was touched.
test.supply_we_would_get: Taker orders on BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE 15-min up/down only, 10-60 s left, 70-95c. Markets where anyone was filled in the -200..+40 ms slot after a >= 4 sigma print: 4.9 a day. The 800 ms trigger sees 55-73 in 100 of those prints, so about 3 markets a day at ~18 contracts each at 20 lots. Much of that overlaps what the M-02 band rule already gets at +260 ms.

idea.name: Nov 3 election Solid-race carry in MAKER form: bid one tick above the best bid on the 93-97c side of Solid/Safe race legs, party-balanced, instead of lifting the ask (decide before Oct 20)
markets: KXHOUSERACE / Senate / governor race markets for Nov 3 2026 (the legs of R1-C3-04-P and R2-M-13)
idea.mechanism: Between now and Oct 30, for each Solid/Safe leg the earlier carry ideas would buy at 93-97c, rest a post_only bid one tick above the best bid instead (24 h expiry, re-posted daily); hold the fills to the count; never more than a party-balanced exposure (equal dollars on D-favoured and R-favoured legs) so one national swing cannot flip one side of the book.
idea.why_mispriced: Impatient sellers hit bids weeks out; the taker version gives the edge back in spread and fee. Archive: political favourites at 90-99c earn ~+1c at the ask but ~+3-7c as a one-tick-inside maker.
idea.must_be_true: Bids fill in size before Nov 3 (2024's carry legs had 1-2c spreads, kalshi_hist_carry.py); the national swing does not flip several legs at once (the refuters' objection: 61 of 67 cheap legs were Republican seats in one correlated wave -- party balance is the only answer to it); the fill-conditioned adverse-selection haircut (filled favourites resolve ~3-5 points less often) leaves the maker edge positive.
idea.evidence_so_far: Archive political (Politics+Elections+World) favourites at 90-99c, one leg per driver, the 2024 general election as ONE cluster: at the ask, all periods 77 drivers, 3 losses, +1.01c [-2.89, +4.05]; maker improve+1c with next-day fill 27 drivers, 0 losses, +7.00c [+6.26, +7.74] (test 20 drivers +7.35c); strict traded-through fill 38 drivers, 1 loss, +2.87c [-2.13, +5.86]. r2 2024 race table (49 races): PRES legs 0 losses at 90-99c at T-21/T-14; one House-margin leg lost at 93c. critic-r2: the capital objection used against R1-C3-04-P / R2-M-13 is contradicted by R1-N2-02 (0 of 900 orders failed for cash with ~$450 moved out); the correlated-wave objection stands.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: One-off. If ~500 contracts fill at +3c vs +1c as a taker: ~$15 vs ~$5 on ~$470 locked for ~3 weeks at the current bank. At $5,000 with 3,000 contracts: ~$90 vs ~$30. Worst plausible night: a national-swing miss flips 2-3 legs = ~-$95 each per 100 contracts.
idea.settlements_per_day: one cluster (Nov 3-6)
idea.test_plan: Paper this week, read-only: log every Solid leg's best bid daily and score hypothetical improve+1c fills from /markets/trades prints at or below the price; read on Nov 6 against the taker version. Before Oct 20, the critic's swing check: P(>= 1 and >= 3 legs lose) under a common national-swing model calibrated to 2018/2022/2024 October poll errors, with Kalshi's generic-ballot/House-margin ladders as the swing prior. test.method: Read-only, public endpoints (auth=False), ~830 calls. Universe built fresh 10-16: Safe/Solid race legs with favourite yes bid 0.895-0.970 -- House seats safe by all 10 forecasters (ALL10, 205; 70 pulled = 33 board order + 37 seeded-random, scaled x2.93), House Solid3 with <=2 of 7 other forecasters dissenting (27), refuters' 'disputed' Solid3 (6, apart), Senate/Gov Solid3 (23), and the only election legs with a liquidity program (11 attorney-general, 13 state chambers; full active list of 5,615 programs has none on KXHOUSERACE/SENATE*/GOVPARTY*). Rule fixed before counting (tape.py): each ET day post a 24 h post_only bid one tick (0.1c above 90c) over the prior daily close bid if it does not cross; fill = every trade-tape print of a taker selling the favourite at or below our price that day, summed into one standing order of N per race. Two routes: YES on the favourite leg, NO on the other party's leg (filled by longshot buyers). Robust 'deep' count = prints >=0.5c through our price only. Window 20 ET days 09-26..10-15, halves split 10-06. Improvement = same-moment taker cost (ask + 13-lot fee, quadratic x1 verified on /series; makers 0) minus our price. Adverse-selection proxy: mid change (favourite direction) on fill days minus non-fill days of the same race, clustered by race, incl. drift AFTER the fill day. Money: maker vs taker book on the same races. Swing model for filled House legs: margin = 2 x 2026 PVI + national margin + noise; national t(5) matched to Kalshi's vote-margin ladder (median D+8.7); noise sigma 3/4 (sigma 6 rejected by Solid3 history: predicts 8.1 losses where 0 of 155 occurred). Data rank: tape + daily candles; no replay; no tape loss rate quoted. Scripts and outputs in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-09/ (RESULT.json saved there).
test.n_markets: 150 races pulled (70 of 205 ALL10 House seats, 27 Solid3 House, 6 disputed House, 23 Senate/Governor, 11 attorney general, 13 state chambers), 20 ET days of tape each. MN-05 (D) excluded from all money/improvement numbers: its supply was one news shock (federal search of the member's home 10-12, bids swept to 0.71), 160k of 165k ALL10 YES-route contracts.
test.n_independent_clusters: Supply/markout: 92-102 races with both fill and non-fill days (race = cluster) over 20 days. Outcome: ONE election night and one national environment; filled races R-favoured 87 vs D 42, so the R side is one shared bet on the national vote.
test.result: SUPPLY (both halves): at 13 a race 114 of 150 races fully filled in 20 days (99 at 50, 90 at 100, 67 at 250). Senate/Gov Solid3: 22 of 23 fully filled at 13 and 50 even on sweeps-only. ALL10 House: 48 of 70 full at 13 (sweeps-only 21 of 69). First half 70 races reached >=13, second half 98 (ex MN-05): supply rising into the election. PARTY BALANCE now possible (impossible as taker, 6 cheap D legs): 42 D-favoured races filled vs 87 R. PRICE: improvement over the same-route taker +2.05c per filled contract race-weighted (median +1.83c; +1.10c contract-weighted); NO route +2.33c (+1.00c). MARKOUT: fill days close -0.85c +-0.16c (YES, 91 races) / -0.55c +-0.06c (NO, 101 races) below non-fill days, then the mid RECOVERS +0.50c +-0.19c / +0.21c +-0.08c over the next two days; net 3 closes -0.45c +-0.11c / -0.36c +-0.07c -- impatient sellers moving a thin book, not informed drift. Net maker edge over taker after markout ~+1.6c a filled contract. BOOK at 13 a race over ~232 posted Safe races (ex disputed, ex MN-05): 2,546 contracts filled, all-win +$131 (5.1c/contract) vs taker +$63 (2.5c); at 1 loss per 100 contracts +$105 vs +$38; at 2/100 +$80 vs +$13; at 4/100 +$29 vs -$37. Per dollar tied up over ~21 days: maker 4.6% all-win (3.7% at 1/100) vs taker 2.6% (1.6%) -- ~2x better, positive where taker is negative. CAPITAL DECIDES: full book needs $2,871 reserved (resting buys reserve cash even unfilled); 3.7%/21 days = ~0.18c per dollar per day vs pin bot ~1.6c (tiebreak, Kalshi ledger). REWARDS: only AG ($150/week/market, period ends 10-16 6:46 PM ET, renewal not seen) and state chambers ($100/week, weekly); $1 per-market-per-period floor -> 13-lot earns $0; 100 lots ~$1-3/week on ~8 legs if book held. SWING (85 filled House legs incl. disputed, sigma 3/4): P(>=1 loss) 22/40 in 100, P(>=3) 5/10 in 100; exposed legs are FL/TX/GA/WI/NC R seats at PVI R+7..10 bid 0.90-0.94. Holdout: no fitted parameter; supply and markout hold across halves.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Units from *_dollars/*_fp only; books are tapered_deci_cent so 'one tick better' is +0.1c above 90c, not the archive's +1c. (2) Pennying: touch count assumes nobody steps ahead; sweeps-only (>=0.5c through) halves House ALL10 fills (48 -> 21 of ~70 full at 13) but leaves Senate/Gov at 22 of 23; truth is between. (3) MN-05 outlier excluded and named. (4) ALL10 sample 70 of 205, not chosen by volume or price, scaled x2.93. (5) Daily closes set our price; intraday bid moves not modelled. (6) Markout includes the sell's own impact; the post-fill drift (+0.2 to +0.5c) is the information part and points the benign way, but it is a 3-day horizon, NOT the settlement loss rate of filled races (unmeasured until Nov 4-7). (7) Fractional 0.01 prints counted at face value. (8) Capital fact (THE_PLAN.md, straddle-tested): resting orders reserve cash cumulatively and balance_dollars is GROSS -- a resting election book in the main account lets the pin bot size off cash that is not there (insufficient_balance at a busy close); must live in a separate pool-0 subaccount. (9) Ratings not re-pulled today (10-15 Wikipedia tables from earlier testers). (10) Hit shared-IP 429s from other agents; stopped my own tape.py and resumed on the sampled list (tape2.py, same code).

refs.strongest_objection: The money may not come back for 2-3 months. The tester assumed about 21 days. In 2024 none of the Senate or governor race markets settled early, because those contracts had no early-settlement clause. Every Senate leg settled on swearing-in day, 2025-01-03, 58.9 days after the election, blowouts in FL, TX, MD and OH included. Governors settled 2025-01-10 to 01-20, 66-76 days after. In the meantime, winners that had already been called traded at only 97-98c, so selling early would have given up 2-3c of the roughly 5c a contract earns if every leg wins. The 2025 NJ and VA governor races did settle early (2025-11-07, about 2 days after the vote). The 2026 contracts say they are 'eligible for accelerated determination' once the media project a winner. So a ~21-day hold is likely, but not guaranteed. If Kalshi does not settle early, money is tied up for about 80-95 days and the return per dollar per day falls about 3.5x (0.18c to about 0.05c). That kills any version funded from bot cash and cuts the $5,000-bank estimate to about $0.7-1/day. The idle-$97 version survives. Second objection: on the Senate and governor legs the live version would actually use, bidding one tick above the best bid beats buying at the ask by a median of only 1.29c (range 0.54-2.38c across 20 legs), not the +2.05c headline, which is mostly House races. After the tester's 3-day price drop after fills (-0.36 to -0.45c), bidding beats buying at the ask by about 0.8c a contract, about $0.75 over 91 contracts. Most of the +$3-4 is simply holding near-certain favourites to settlement. Whether filled near-certain legs lose more often cannot be read before the races are called. Supply is not the problem: I confirmed it with my own queries. Gotcha: SENATELA-26-R is titled 'Kentucky Senate winner?' and its rules say Senator of Kentucky, so check each leg's rules before mapping a ticker to a state.
refs.independent_number: My own queries cover the 23 Senate and governor 'Solid' favourite legs over the last 7 ET days (10-09 to 10-16). Our bid was each day's opening bid (from 60-min candles) plus one 0.1c tick. 18 of 23 races would have filled 13 contracts counting only sellers who went at least 0.2c below our price; 19 counting any sale at or below our price, 10 counting only sales at least 0.5c below. All 23 legs are on exchange pool 0. Right now, bidding one tick above the best bid saves a median 1.29c a contract versus buying at the ask with the 13-lot fee (range 0.54-2.38c). Settlement times from /historical/markets settlement_ts: 2024 Senate legs 2025-01-03 (58.9 days after election day), 2024 governors 2025-01-10 to 01-20 (65.7-75.8 days), 2025 GOVPARTYNJ and GOVPARTYVA 2025-11-07 (about 2 days).

refs.strongest_objection:
On the Senate and governor legs the $97 version is built on, the maker part is worth almost nothing. The money is the same unmeasured carry bet that the two refuted taker predecessors made. My own board pull on 10-16 covered 23 legs. Measured against the mid, the maker edge is a median 0.35c a contract (range 0.05-1.1c). Against lifting the ask it saves a median 1.18c. The carry (1 minus our price) is a median 4.6c (range 3.0-8.7c).

The three biggest-carry R legs have 0.1c spreads: SENATEMT 0.913/0.914, SENATEFLS 0.916/0.917, GOVPARTYTN 0.919/0.920, carry 8.1-8.7c. A bid one tick better would cross, so we would join queues of 1,254, 14,415 and 1,303 contracts. We fill only when the level is traded through. Traded-through favourites in the archive won 0.957 of the time (117 drivers, 0.90-0.99 band), not 0.99.

The tester's $0.15/day assumes 1 loss per 100 filled contracts. The same 7-race, 13-lot book priced three ways:
- 1 loss per 100: +$4.82
- archive fill-conditioned win rate 0.957: +$1.82
- market mid is the true chance: +$0.14

A low-carry, mostly-D pick comes out at -$0.23 at 0.957.

Second, payout timing comes from the 2026 rule wording, not from a measurement. Every 2024 Senate market (19) and governor market (10) paid at swearing-in, 59-76 days after the election. Only the 2025 NJ and VA governor markets (n=2) paid in 2.1-2.2 days. The 2026 rules say only 'eligible for accelerated determination'. If the lock is 60 days, the per-day figure falls about 3x.

Not refuted, because supply is real and the outcome cannot be measured before Nov 4-7:
- 19 of 23 legs had 13 or more contracts sold at least 0.2c below our price on at least 1 of the last 7 ET days (FLS 4 of 7 days, TN gov 5, MA 5, NJ 5).
- Trade sides checked: only the (yes,yes,bid) and (no,no,ask) combinations appear, so there is no sign error.
- Fees on all 8 series used are quadratic x1 with makers free.

idea.name: In-play BTTS YES-bid-only maker (the half the CLIFF pays): rest 20-lot YES bids at the touch on soccer BTTS legs from kickoff, never offer YES, cap each game; prove the CLIFF payment with a 10-lot probe
markets: smaller BTTS series (AFC CL, FIFA W, EFL Ch., Serie C) not measured
idea.mechanism: From the scheduled kickoff (K = occurrence - 4 h) to close, every 120 s post or re-post a 20-contract BUY YES at the best YES bid on the game's BTTS market; never rest a YES offer (side guard: offer-YES markout -1.65c at 300 s over 64 games). Hold fills to settlement; cap ~$40 of YES (~100 contracts) per game. It earns (a) the markout -- in-play YES sellers are early and the mid rises after they hit our bid; and (b) the CLIFF prop-combo leg rebate (25% of prop-combo fees), paid ONLY on maker volume after the scheduled start and only if our share of the leg's in-play maker volume clears the 0.01 minimum score. Paid proof first: Oct 17-31, 10-lot bids (cap 40 per game, ~5 games a day) on a subaccount that holds nothing else; Nov 1-5 read every subaccount's and the main account's history for a Bonus Credit line; and ask Kalshi support (a) contracts or dollars for 'maker volume', (b) which account a subaccount's credit lands in, (c) whether Bonus Credit is withdrawable or must be traded through / expires.
idea.why_mispriced: In-play BTTS YES is underpriced as it is pre-game (r2: pre-game YES-bid +9.8c settled); the other side of our bid is the 'it stays 0-0 / one-sided' taker. The CLIFF (~$220k/day after eligible-leg scaling, taker-funded) goes to whoever makes in-play volume on the legs.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The +0.9c 5-minute markout holds forward (a side split of a two-sided quote, measured once, t 1.6). (2) Kalshi pays the CLIFF on these fills as usable money (no public proof; third-party promo pages say Kalshi Bonus Credit must be traded through and may expire in 7 days). (3) Our share clears the 1% minimum: bid-only at D200 reaches F >= 1% on only 16 of 64 markets (25%; 6% with a 100-contract cap), so most of the CLIFF is NOT earned at 20 lots. (4) The D200 queue is not optimistic for these books.
idea.evidence_so_far: Trade tape + 1-minute candles through the game, 64 games 09-24..10-14 (one BTTS market each, 8 leagues), re-posted static 20-lot touch quote, D200 queue. Bid-YES fills: 17,304 contracts in 61 games (284/game). Markout to the mid: +60 s +0.52c (se 0.19), +300 s +0.92c (se 0.57), +900 s +1.85c (se 1.60), settlement +7.63c (se 7.24). Halves at 300 s: fit (28 games) +1.52c (se 0.82), hold (33) +0.38c (se 0.77). FRONT +1.36c (se 0.49). Mirror (offer YES) -1.65c (se 0.60; 900 s -2.99c). Average maker of every in-play BTTS trade at 300 s: -0.09c. CLIFF per in-play maker contract (90% window bootstrap): Liga MX 6.27c (0.48-15.67), UCL 3.13c (0.41-8.22), Serie A ~3.7c, EPL/MLS ~1.4-2.1c; fill-weighted ~2.5c x 0.7 incumbent dilution = +1.75c, x ~25% min-score coverage = ~+0.45c expected. Net ~+1.4c per filled contract (hold half +0.8c); +0.9c without the CLIFF. Smallest effect the markout sample can detect ~1.6c at 80% power. Settled $ per game (uncapped): mean +$21.6, worst -$341; worst UTC day -$591 of 12. No public evidence of any CLIFF payment (help article 17184676; CFTC filings 08112615711 / 08122616002 / 08122616003). Lane rule applied: score sports makers on 1/5/15-min markouts plus an all-market calibration, never on one leg's settlement. Files: r3-sports-inplay-cliff-maker/mo_soc.out, soc_money.out, soc_minscore.out, markout_soc.out, legs_ci.out.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Capped at ~$40 of YES per game: ~$1-3/day at the current bank on a ~$300 pot, worst day about -$120. Uncapped $300 pot: ~$3-8/day (mostly markout) but one 0-0 afternoon can take most of the pot. $5,000 uncapped: ~$20-60/day (5-15 games x ~$4), worst measured day -$591 (12 days). Probe: ~-$2 to +$3 a day.
idea.settlements_per_day: 5-20 BTTS games a day (weekends heavier), each settling at full time or when both teams score
idea.test_plan: Free: re-run pull_inplay.py TAG=soc on the next 3 weeks of BTTS games (plus the smaller BTTS series) and score bid-YES-only at D200 on the 300-s and 900-s markouts; pre-registered bar: pooled >= +0.8c at 300 s over >= 60 new games, both halves > 0. Paid: the 10-lot probe above, OPERATOR SIGN-OFF FIRST; read the early-November statement for a Bonus Credit line (amount vs the formula, which account, withdrawable or not).
idea.prior_reason: The markout edge is under its own detection limit (t 1.6; holdout half +0.38c), the CLIFF is unproven and may be non-cash credit, and at a safe per-game cap it is worth ~$1-3/day; 3 weeks to a free read.

test.method: Trade tape plus 1-minute candles from Kalshi's public API (no auth, 561 calls), on 237 in-play soccer BTTS games the hunter never saw: every settled full-game BTTS market in 29 leagues listed at least 2 h before kickoff, closing 08-17..09-23 (before his window, after the 08-17 historical-trades cutoff) or 10-14 12Z..10-16 (after it). That is 150 seeded-random of 438 games in his 8 leagues before his window, all 27 after it, and 60 seeded-random from the smaller leagues. Rule run exactly as the hunter wrote it, with his fill code (fills_an.fill) unchanged: from kickoff+60 s, every 120 s, rest BUY 20 YES at the 1-minute-candle bid (spread at most 10c) for 120 s, queue FRONT (first in line) or D200 (200 contracts ahead). Pre-registered bar from his test plan: D200 bid-YES markout to the mid at 300 s of at least +0.8c over at least 60 new games, both halves above 0.
