idea.name: Gold / silver 15-minute band bot off a per-second feed (single-print Pyth settlement) -- WEAK, needs a feed check
markets: KXWTI15M (only with a feed that matches Pyth)
idea.mechanism: These settle on the close of the 1-minute Pyth candle at the close vs the open: one print, no average. With a sub-second feed, fair = Phi((spot - K)/(sigma sqrt(tau))). After a >= 2-sigma move with 10-60 s left, take the 70-95c offer the slow makers left: the M-02 template on a second family.
idea.why_mispriced: The same stale-offer mechanism as crypto, if the commodity makers are as slow; unmeasured.
idea.must_be_true: A free real-time feed with < 300 ms latency matches the Pyth print (Pyth Hermes needs a key since 08-26; r2:perps-venue found Kalshi's gold perp reference matched the Pyth up/down outcome on 82 of 82 closes, level diff sd 0.72 bp, silver 80 of 82, while WTI and copper perps sit ~32-34 bp off Pyth); the last-minute quotes are not already tight to that feed.
idea.evidence_so_far: Our tape records the full KXGOLD15M/KXWTI15M books (gold ~28k trades an hour on 10-15T19; one window 1.05M contracts). Fixed-time favourites there earn -1 to +3c (no free bias; gold 60 s 70-80c +3.0c, t 0.9 is the best cell). No feed, no model test. SJ43 killed the commodity PIN (pinned windows 99.8-99.9c).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown; if it matched crypto's +6c on ~3 fills/day at 20 lots, ~$4/day at the current bank, ~$15/day at 98 lots ($5,000).
idea.settlements_per_day: 96 windows/day per series in market hours
idea.test_plan: Free: record Kalshi's gold and silver perp reference prices (public) beside our tape for 3 days, check per-second agreement with the Pyth close prints, then run bx_scan's grid with that feed as the index. Bar as M-02 (>= 100 fills, >= +3c, both halves).
idea.prior_reason: Plausible transfer of the best idea, but no feed is proven and the commodity books show no last-minute bias to start from.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SJ43 killed the commodity pin; SJ23 found no free WTI feed. A mid-band model taker on these books was never measured; the gold perp proxy is a new route around the Hermes key.
idea.worst_case: Unknown; bounded by the same caps as M-02 (-$30 day stop at 20 lots).

test.method: Sources: our recorded KXGOLD15M order book (the tape) plus an outside fast gold price. This is not a replay of our bot. (1) Feeds checked. Pyth's price endpoints (Hermes and benchmarks) all return 401 "unauthorized": a key has been needed since 2026-08-26, with a free trial and then paid plans. Dukascopy's free spot-gold ticks work (median 202 ms apart) but throttled to about one file a minute with 503 errors, so I dropped them. Binance's USD-M XAUUSDT perpetual trade history from its public archive (data.binance.vision) works: 0.4-0.8M trades a day with millisecond timestamps. Live Binance is blocked here (HTTP 451), so it serves only as a research stand-in. Kalshi's perps WebSocket "ticker" carries the Pyth reference price but sends at most one message per second; over REST that reference is a median 1.2 s old. (2) Checked Binance against Kalshi's own settled values on 1,180 closes 09-28..10-15. The error in the 15-minute change has sd 1.01 bp against a typical window move of 12.8 bp, and the up/down result agrees on 973 of 976 moves of 2 bp or more. The settlement print is at the close itself (C-0.5 to C-1 s), not 60 s later. (3) gold_scan.py rebuilt the real KXGOLD15M book (snapshot plus deltas, the same logic as r3 bx_scan) every 100 ms of Kalshi server time over the last 75 s of 1,145 windows: 309 tape hours across 15 UTC days, minus the 10-14 03Z..10-15 04Z gap. The rebuilt top of book matched 99.1 in 100 ticker messages. (4) Three tests. (a) Who moves first: 535 sudden Binance moves (at least 2 standard deviations in one second) in 242 windows that were still in doubt, comparing Kalshi's mid move with the model's fair-value move from -1.5 s to +5 s, and counting how many favoured asks were still at the old price. (b) Does the model know anything the market doesn't: a logistic fit of the outcome on Kalshi's mid plus the model's value at 60/45/30/20/10 s left (458 live markets), fitted on the first half and scored on the second. (c) The bot rule itself: fair = Phi(k*(B(t-L)-B(open))/sqrt(sig^2(tau+L)+(1bp)^2)), with sig from trailing 5-s Binance changes and k fitted on the first half only. Buy on the first moment per market where fair minus the ask is at least 3/5/8/12c, the ask is 65-97c or 70-95c, with or without the 2-sigma jump filter, at feed delays of 0, 300 and 1,200 ms. Fills walk the book at the next 100 ms capture up to the seen ask, 20 and 98 lots, minus the taker fee. Holdout split: first half = closes before 2026-10-08 00Z (715 markets), second half = after (405). Scripts are in the scratch folder: gold_scan.py, bnc.py, validate_bnc.py, gold_lag.py, gold_info.py, gold_ana_main.py, gold_supply.py, gold_daily.py.
test.n_markets: 1,145 KXGOLD15M markets scanned; 1,120 had Binance coverage (first half 715, second half 405). The model-vs-market test used 458 live windows; the who-moves-first test used 535 jump events in 242 windows.
test.n_independent_clusters: 1,120 closes over 15 UTC days (one gold market per close; first half 715, second half 405)
test.result:
The idea needs slow gold makers, and they are not slow: Kalshi's gold book moves with the fast feed, not after it.

Who moves first (535 events): by the time the 100 ms Binance slot holding the jump closes, Kalshi's mid has already made 0.95 of the model's move (first half 0.89, second half 1.04). It has made 0.67 of it 100 ms before that. Only 5 in 100 favoured asks are still at the old price at +0 ms, 6 in 100 at +300 ms and 9 in 100 at +1,000 ms. The model's edge at the ask still showing is -3.2c at +0 ms, -2.8c at +300 ms and -2.5c at +1,000 ms, negative in both halves.

Model vs market: Kalshi's mid predicts the outcome better than the Binance model (lower Brier score) at every time-left point in both halves, even with zero feed delay. Examples: first half, 30 s left, market 0.138 vs model 0.169; second half, 10 s left, 0.160 vs 0.203. Scored on the second half, the error score (log-loss) is 0.4333 for the market alone, 0.4750 for the model alone and 0.4344 for market plus model, so adding the model makes it worse.

The bot rule (48 versions): none meets the bar of at least 100 fills and at least +3c in both halves.
- 300 ms delay, 3c margin, 65-97c: first half +3.3c (57 fills), second half -3.6c (48 fills). Combined +0.05c on 105 fills, which is +$1 at 20 lots over 15 days.
- 1,200 ms delay (the speed of Kalshi's perp reference), 5c margin: first half +3.5c (48 fills), second half +2.3c (36 fills). Combined +2.6c, give or take 4.4c, on 84 fills: indistinguishable from zero, and one of 48 versions tried.
- 11 of 16 versions at 300 ms and 11 of 16 at 1,200 ms lose money in the second half.
- The zero-delay jump versions show +6 to +30c in the second half, but on only 5-20 fills each. They would need a feed faster than Binance with no delay at all, and Binance cannot be reached from the US.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Feed vs settlement: the Binance-vs-Pyth change error has sd 1.0 bp, and outcomes agree on 973 of 976 moves of 2 bp or more. On the analysed markets agreement is 1,047 of 1,079; the misses sit near the strike, where the 65-97c band lives. A real Pyth feed would therefore price better than this stand-in, but the market already beats the stand-in by 0.03-0.04 on the Brier score, which suggests the makers already have Pyth-quality data. (2) Rebuilt book vs ticker messages: 99.1 in 100 agree. (3) Two independent passes reproduce the same dollar totals ($1.00/$51.99, $21.89/$81.86, $48.75/$204.24). (4) Timing uses Binance's matching-engine milliseconds and Kalshi server ts_ms, not our receive times. A clock offset between them was not measured; one of up to 300 ms would not change the verdict, since the edge at the ask is still -2.8c at +300 ms. (5) Settlement timing was checked from -2 s to +60 s; reading the print at C+60 is clearly wrong (error sd 6.7 bp). (6) Many looks: 48 versions times 2 halves, and the few positive second-half cells have 5-20 fills. (7) These are tape quotes, not our fills. The book walk only removes faster takers already in the book; competitors in the same millisecond and people selling to us because they know more would make every number worse. (8) Memory: my first analysis pass held every book in memory and reached about 790 MB, over the 200 MB budget, before I stopped it and rewrote it to stream one market at a time (peak 88 MB). Two earlier analysis scripts used the same all-in-memory loader and were not measured. Both recorders kept writing; their files were seconds old at the check. Free disk 113 GB; scratch folder 25 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: On KXGOLD15M one side is offered at 65-97c in 32 of 100 windows with 60 s left and 11 of 100 with 10 s left. The median size at the best price is 90-1,133 contracts, and takers buy about 8,600 contracts per window at 65-97c in the last 60 s. So the supply is real; the edge on it is not. A realistic rule would fill in about 5-7 windows a day (84-105 fills in 15 days).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0. No rule survives the holdout; the best realistic rule makes +2.6c per contract, give or take 4.4c, which cannot be told apart from zero.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Bot rule: about 8-9c per contract on all fills together (twice the error at 84-105 fills), and about 12-14c on the second half alone (36-48 fills). Who moves first: the 535-event measure is good to about plus or minus 0.05, so stale offers lasting 300 ms on even 1 in 5 jumps would have shown up. What it shows is 5-6 in 100 still stale, with negative edge.
test.worst_case: Run anyway at the Kalshi perp reference's speed (1.2 s delay), the worst replayed day is -$39 at 20 lots and -$192 at 98 lots, with up to 4 losing fills in one day. On the second half the loosest rules expect -1.5 to -6.8c per contract: about -$2 to -$4 a day at 20 lots and -$10 to -$45 a day at 98 lots.
test.next_test: None for gold; it is recorded so nobody re-runs it. Not measured: silver (Binance's silver perp has only about 45k trades a day, too thin to time moves to 100 ms, and Dukascopy's silver files were blocked) and WTI/copper (no free feed matches Pyth). The only thing that could revive this is a feed faster than Binance's gold perp, such as direct CME gold futures or a paid Pyth Pro/Lazer key, followed by a re-run of gold_lag.py showing Kalshi's mid still under half of the move 300 ms after that feed's print. Bar: at least 300 jump events, at least 25 in 100 offers still stale with model edge of +3c or more at +300 ms, in both halves. The cost of such a feed is unknown (Pyth publishes no prices; CME real-time data is not free). Since the gold makers already price as fast as Binance, the odds are low.

idea.name: bo3.gg free API as a CS2 odds anchor (Thunderpick no-vig lines) and match clock: a 1-week read-only lead-lag recorder vs KXCS2GAME -- WEAK
idea.mechanism: Record Kalshi vs Thunderpick no-vig prices on CS2 (match, totals, handicaps) from api.bo3.gg; test who moves first and whether > 2c gaps close toward Kalshi. If Thunderpick leads on tier-2 CS2, take or quote Kalshi toward it.
idea.why_mispriced: No US sportsbook prices tier-2 CS2, so Kalshi's CS2 books may lean on few makers.
idea.must_be_true: Thunderpick is sharper than Kalshi on tier-2 CS2 and gaps persist after fees.
idea.evidence_so_far: api.bo3.gg/api/v1/matches?...filter[matches.status][in]=current answers with no key and includes bet_updates (Thunderpick team_1/team_2, handicaps, total maps, correct scores); /api/v1/games/{id} gives begin_at and game_rounds; the live snapshot endpoint returned not_found for two live matches. Kalshi vs Thunderpick gaps NOT measured. Pregame sports sat within 0.64c of Pinnacle (SI59). 316 of 3,000 CS2 events (10.5%) settled 'scalar' (cancelled at fair price).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown at either bank; a read-only recorder costs $0.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~43 CS2 matches/day
idea.test_plan: 1-week recorder: bo3.gg current/upcoming every 5 min (free) plus Kalshi KXCS2GAME books at the same moments (~300 public GETs/day); bar: gaps > 2c close toward Thunderpick >= 60% of the time over >= 100 matches.
idea.prior_reason: Unmeasured, and the closest analogue (pregame vs Pinnacle) showed no anchor; cheap to check.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New free data source for esports; complements R1-C3-13 (FanDuel lead-lag poller).
idea.worst_case: n/a (read-only recorder).

test.method: I ran a live read-only recorder on 2026-10-16 from 10:57 to 11:50Z (53 min). It polled three sources: (1) the api.bo3.gg list of current and upcoming CS2 matches every 10 s, 315 polls, with Thunderpick odds in bet_updates converted to no-vig odds by the power method; (2) the public Kalshi KXCS2GAME open-market list every 30 s, 105 calls, top of book with both team books merged; (3) Pinnacle's guest API CS2 moneylines every 2 min, 21 polls, as a sharp third reference. I mapped 16 bo3 matches to Kalshi events by schedule and fuzzy team names (15 automatic, 1 by hand). Three measurements: (a) Level: Kalshi mid vs Thunderpick vs Pinnacle at the same moment. (b) Pregame lead-lag: how many times each source moved by 0.5c or more, whether gaps shrank and who moved, and Kalshi's closing line (mid when bo3 flipped the match to live) against the gap at the first poll. (c) In-play lead-lag: for every Thunderpick move of 5c or more, tau is the time we first saw it on bo3; I read Kalshi's public trade tape (last trade, both books merged) from tau-300 s to tau+120 s and took the share of Kalshi's move already done by tau. Extras: a KXCS2TOTALMAPS vs Thunderpick totals snapshot, and Kalshi pregame drift from the hunter's 1-minute candles (582 matches). Sources are the Kalshi trade tape and live public books only; no replay. Holdout: not applicable to the lead-lag, which is a timing measurement with no threshold fitted. The pregame level comparison has no outcome holdout because n is far too small. Scratch folder: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-20/
test.n_markets: 16 CS2 matches recorded (32 KXCS2GAME markets). 13 had a pregame window (522 match-minutes); 7 of those were also priced by Pinnacle. 3 reached their start inside the window, so their closing line was read; 1 of those has settled. In-play: 5 live matches with 59 Thunderpick moves of 5c or more, 27 after removing bo3's back-and-forth flips.
test.n_independent_clusters: Pregame: 13 matches, each one cluster. In-play: 5 live matches; the 27 persistent moves are not independent, so 5 clusters.
test.result:
IN-PLAY (this is what kills it): bo3's Thunderpick numbers trail Kalshi. There were 25 persistent Thunderpick moves that came with a Kalshi move of 2c or more. In the median one, Kalshi had already done 0.91 of its move before the Thunderpick change was visible to us; 20 of 25 were at least half done. The median gap between Thunderpick's new value and Kalshi's price at that moment was 5.4c. bo3 serves two inconsistent caches: 30 of the 59 raw changes flipped A->B->A within 30 s. At the end of a match Thunderpick still showed 6-12% for a team Kalshi had held at 1c for 60+ s. Thunderpick totals said 89% for 'over 2.5 maps' at 1-1, which is a certainty (Kalshi 99c).

PREGAME: Thunderpick is a coarse copy of Pinnacle. Thunderpick vs Pinnacle differed by 0.74c on average (max 1.04c, n=7) at 10:57Z and 0.75c (n=5) at 11:48Z. Kalshi vs Pinnacle differed by 1.49c on average (max 2.68c), then 1.40c. Kalshi vs Thunderpick: 2.48c on average (n=13); 7 of 13 were over 2c and 4 over 3c. Thunderpick's pregame lines moved 0 times in 522 match-minutes (Pinnacle 1, Kalshi 27), so Thunderpick cannot lead Kalshi pregame. In 8 matches the Kalshi-Thunderpick gap was over 1.5c: on 4 Kalshi moved toward Thunderpick and the gap shrank; on the other 4 it grew or stayed (a coin flip; moves of 0.5-2.5c).

Closing line: 2 started matches had a gap over 2c at the first poll, and Kalshi closed away from Thunderpick on both (0 of 2). Taking toward Thunderpick at the first-poll ask plus fee would have finished 3.2c and 2.9c per contract worse than Kalshi's closing price. The one settled match (Voca-HAVU: Thunderpick had Voca at 62.1%, Kalshi at 59%) went to HAVU.

Edge after the taker fee vs Thunderpick at 10:57Z: positive on 7 of 13, but 5 of those were only 0.1-0.6c. The only big ones (5.3c ex-Zero-UNiTY, 3.2c Phantom-HAVU) were on Kalshi books with 9 and 181 contracts of lifetime volume.

Totals: most KXCS2TOTALMAPS books were 30-90c wide. The 3 tight ones sat 1.8-2.9c below Thunderpick, about the size of the fee, and several Thunderpick totals were the 1.85/1.85 default line.

Context: in the last hour before start, Kalshi's CS2 pregame mid moves a median 1.0c, and more than 2c 35% of the time (582 matches). So a 1.5-2.5c gap to an outside book is within normal wander.
test.artefact_checks:
- No-vig method: the proportional method overstates longshots by 1-5c on an 8%-margin book (Phantom-RoundsGG: 85.4% proportional vs 90.6% power). All comparisons use the power method; Shin's method lands within 1c of it, and devig.py's self-test passes.
- Kalshi mid is used only when the merged spread is 6c or less.
- Team mapping was checked by name on every row. Rejected: Unity vs TheChampionGG (Kalshi lists TheChampionGG vs STATE), and 33 vs Just_Players (Thunderpick calls team 1 'BET-M').
- bo3's start_date is wrong for timing (Voca-HAVU went live at 11:06Z; bo3 said 12:00Z, Kalshi 08:00 ET), so the closing line uses the moment bo3 flipped the match to live.
- The in-play study uses last-trade prices, which are noisy (merged books, 1c ticks). The 0.91 is a median over 25 moves, and the reversal filter removes bo3's double counting.
- Pinnacle is itself a low-limit CS2 book, so 'Thunderpick tracks Pinnacle' means Thunderpick copies a feed, not that either is right.
- Kalshi public calls hit one HTTP 429 while the recorder and the candle pull ran together; the call was retried.
- The tape is still being written (C:\kals\kalshi_data\ticker\20261016T11.jsonl.gz updated 11:52Z, and feed_data too); 113 GB disk free; scratch folder 3.8 MB.
- Files: rec.jsonl, pin_rec.jsonl, kmap.json, leadlag_events.json, conv_rows.json, clv_rows.json, RESULT.json.
test.supply_we_would_get: On the 13 mapped matches, Kalshi KXCS2GAME pregame books typically had 100-850 contracts at the best ask (7k-80k on the 3 biggest matches). Pregame volume ran from a few hundred to about 7k contracts per match before start. The big money is in-play (NIP-Liquid traded 227k contracts on one book), and in-play is exactly where Thunderpick is stale. Coverage: bo3 had Thunderpick lines on 32 of 150 listed CS2 matches; 16 of those mapped to Kalshi's 46 open events; Pinnacle priced 11 CS2 matches.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0/day. In-play, the signal arrives after Kalshi has already moved (median 91% done). Pregame, even if Thunderpick's price level were right, the after-fee edge on liquid books is 0.1-0.6c per contract: about 16 mapped matches a day x 98 contracts x ~0.5c on half of them = roughly a $4/day ceiling. The closing-line read (0 of 2 moved toward Thunderpick, 3c worse than the close) points the other way.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0/day, for the same reasons. At $5k the pregame ceiling would be about $10-15/day, and only if Thunderpick's level were right, which nothing measured supports.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Pregame gap-closure share: with n=8 matches the standard error is about 18 percentage points, so 60% vs 50% cannot be told apart. Outcome-level calibration: 1 settled match, and a 1-2c edge needs thousands of matches. In-play lead-lag: 25 persistent moves in 5 matches. The 0.91 median is far from the near-zero a leading signal would show, but 5 clusters (tier-b/c matches, one morning) limit how far it generalises.
test.worst_case: If it were built as a pregame taker anyway: about 5 bets a day x 98 contracts, paying about 1.7c fee each for an edge near zero, costs about $8/day on average. One day's result swings by about $105 either way (one standard deviation), so a bad day is about -$250 at the $1,155 bank.

idea.name: NFL in-play prop maker, side-restricted (WEAK): sell TD YES at the ask through the game (never bid it), quote both sides only at halftime, and route size to the high-CLIFF legs (PASSTDS, RRYDS; NBA PTS from Oct 21)
idea.mechanism: (a) TD arm: from kickoff, every 120 s rest a 20-lot SELL YES at the YES ask on the 1+/2+ TD markets of a game (= buy NO at 100 - ask); never bid YES; no post within 60 s of a scoring play (ESPN wall clock); hold to settlement. (b) Halftime arm: 20-lot bids and offers at the touch on the TD/RECYDS/RSHYDS legs of a game only between the last Q2 play and the first Q3 play, re-posted every 2 min, pulled at the Q3 kickoff. (c) Leg chooser: estimate each leg's CLIFF pool live from the public global trade tape (5-s windows of combo trades + GET /markets?tickers= for mve_selected_legs, ~30 calls an hour) and its in-play volume so far, and send quoting capital to the highest pool-per-volume legs where the side guard allows. Side guards (measured 5-min markouts, in play): never offer YES on RECYDS (-4.16c, se 1.33) or college team totals (-4.40c, se 0.97); never bid YES on RSHYDS (-2.67c, se 0.86) or TD (-0.69c, se 0.23); fills within 60 s of any NFL score -2.39c.
idea.why_mispriced: In-play TD YES buyers chase players, and the mid drifts down after they buy with no adverse selection at 1-5 min. Halftime traders rebalance without field information, so the live-feed makers have no edge there. The CLIFF pays in-play makers and its pool per contract varies ~30x across legs (0.2c UFC MOV to ~6c RRYDS) while makers spread evenly.
idea.must_be_true: The 5-15 min TD markout survives forward and is not cancelled by the slightly LOW mid (YES ~0.65c underpriced at random times); post-TD snipes stay rare (3.9% of filled contracts within 60 s of a score); halftime fills stay benign (injury news at halftime is the risk); high-pool legs are not high-pool because informed money trades them (their markouts are NOT measured); the CLIFF is paid (see M-10); selling 10c YES locks ~90c a contract until the game ends.
idea.evidence_so_far: TD: 47 NFL games 09-24..10-12, one ex-ante random KXNFLTD market per game, in-play tape + candles; D200 sell-YES 11,359 contracts in 37 games; markout +60 s +0.08c (se 0.19), +300 s +0.70c (se 0.20), +900 s +1.99c (se 0.32); halves at 300 s +0.53c (22 games) / +0.94c (15). Settlement +8.06c is NOT trustworthy (2 of the 47 sampled markets won vs an 8.5% base rate). Calibration over every TD market (1,720 markets, 3,885 in-play snapshots): the YES ask is fair (seller at ask +0.18c, se 0.49) and the mid sits 0.65c below the outcome rate. Net +0.05c (300 s + mid bias) to +1.3c (900 s), plus ~+0.66c CLIFF (0.94c x 0.7) = ~+0.7 to +2.0c per filled contract; 37 < 40 games. Halftime (ESPN wall clock): D200 +300 s +0.28c (se 0.25, 29 games, 1,534 contracts; fit +0.04c, hold +0.53c); FRONT +0.51c (se 0.12, 36 games); vs live play -1.07c (se 0.34) and dead-ball -1.01c (se 0.50); ~18 contracts per market per halftime gives F ~0.2%, under the 1% minimum on its own. CLIFF per in-play maker contract (90% CI), from 168 hourly 5-s windows of the global tape (4,494 combos) and 230 leg events: TD 0.94c (0.64-1.27), RECYDS 2.03c (1.43-2.78), PASSYDS 2.68c, RSHYDS 1.74c, REC 1.92c, PASSTDS 4.42c (2.04-7.65), RRYDS 6.28c (1.31-13.6), NHL PTS 5.14c (1.55-10.3), WNBA PTS 4.27c, NCAAF 1HSPREAD 0.88c, TEAMTOTAL 0.74c; pool $220k/day taker-only after the eligible-leg scaling (was $308k unscaled); a both-sided 20-lot at D200 clears F >= 1% on 74% of TD and 81% of RECYDS/RSHYDS markets. Both-sided all-game quoting is dead (see dropped). Files: r3-sports-inplay-cliff-maker/markout_nfl.out, calib_td.out, td_check.out, td_audit.out, legs_ci.out, an_legs.out.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $300 pot at the current bank: TD arm $3-6/day on the 900-s figure (~$0-1 on the conservative 300-s figure); halftime $1-3/day; the leg chooser adds at most +1-4c a contract, not measured. $5,000: TD $10-60/day, halftime $5-15/day. Worst: one TD snipe on a 20-lot -$15 to -$18; worst measured market-game -$196 (D200); a bad Sunday slot at 15 markets -$500 to -$800 at $5,000; a star ruled out at halftime -$15-20 per leg.

idea.test_plan: Free: pull the next 3 NFL weeks (pull_inplay.py TAG=nfl, 3 random TD markets per game, all props at halftime, plus KXNFLPASSTDS/KXNFLRRYDS for the 47 games, ~120 calls) and calib_pull.py SER=KXNFLTD on the same games; NBA week 1 after Oct 28. test.method: Source: Kalshi public trade tape + 1-minute candles (no auth; 1,066 counted GETs + ~20 probes) and ESPN play-by-play wall clocks (80 of 80 games; Kalshi kickoff = occurrence - 3 h matched ESPN to the second on all 80). No replay, no live fills of ours exist in sports. Rule run exactly as the hunter wrote it, with his fill code unchanged (fills_an.fill, an_inplay.touch_at/Espn): from kickoff+60 s, every 120 s, read the 1-minute candle touch (spread <= 10c), rest SELL 20 YES at the ask and BUY 20 YES at the bid for 120 s, queue FRONT (first in line) or D200 (200 contracts ahead); hold to settlement. Marked at the candle mid 1/5/15/30/45 min after each fill and at settlement, split into spread captured vs mid move after the fill, cluster = game. Added: a PHANTOM control (the same quote at every grid time, no fill selection), an all-market calibration of the YES ask (hourly event candles, every TD market of the new games), per-market position caps, and dollars per market-game / per day. One fix to the hunter's mark: a post-close candle with bid 0 / ask 100 read as a 50c mid; after a market's close I mark to settlement (a YES market closes at the touchdown) -- it changes none of his numbers. Samples drawn seeded and ex-ante (listed >= 2 h before kickoff, any volume) BEFORE any new tape was read (plan.py): (1) FORWARD/holdout = the 33 NFL games outside his window (weeks 1-2, 09-09..09-21, plus TNF 10-15), 6 random KXNFLTD markets each (198) + 1 RECYDS + 1 RSHYDS each (66); (2) LUCK CHECK = his own 47 games, 4 other random KXNFLTD markets each (188); (3) HIGH-POOL LEGS = all 80 games, 1 random KXNFLPASSTDS + 1 KXNFLRRYDS each (160). Pre-registered bars from the idea: TD sell-YES >= +0.6c at 300 s over >= 40 new games with both halves > 0; halftime >= +0.3c at 300 s over >= 40 games; high-pool legs' markout no worse than TD's over >= 40 games. Halves = earlier/later kickoff within each set. idea.name: Slow-favourite resting bid book (WEAK): bid one tick above the best bid on the 80-94c favourite of long-dated markets 3-30 days before the event ends, one position per shared driver, hold to settlement
markets: Kalshi long-dated (>= 14-day) markets in Politics, Elections, Economics (non-CPI), Entertainment, Science/Tech, Companies, sports futures/awards -- e.g. KXTRUMPMEET, KXLAGODAYS, KXGOVSHUT*, KXFEDDECISION, KXPAYROLLS/KXU3, KXGDP, KXEGGS, KXRT, KXALBUMSALES, KXOSCAR*/KXGRAM*, KXTOPMODEL, KXLLM1, KXSPACEXCOUNT, KXNFLWINS
idea.mechanism: 1) Once a day (after the 00:00 ET daily candle) list open markets in these series whose event ends in 3-30 days (event end = latest close of any market in the event, or the deadline in a 'before/by <date>' title). 2) Favourite side = YES if mid >= 50c else NO; keep it if its bid is 80-94c and the spread <= 10c. 3) Rest a post_only bid ONE TICK ABOVE the best bid on the favourite, 50-100 contracts, 24 h expiry. 4) If filled, hold to settlement (no exit trade; maker fee only on maker-fee series). 5) At most one open position per shared driver (one election day, FOMC month, shutdown month, jobs report, awards night, league-month of futures). Haircut every read of it by the measured fill-conditioned adverse selection and count a fill only when the price traded THROUGH our level.
idea.why_mispriced: The other side is the taker who sells a weeks-out favourite into the bid (impatience, lottery buyers of the 5-20c side, people freeing capital). On the archive the favourite at an ~88c bid resolves 95.6% when nobody trades through the bid (182 drivers) but 90.7% when the bid IS traded through (108 drivers): the sellers know something (a 4.9-point gap), yet the traded-through fills still win ~3.1 points more often than the 87.6c paid. A taker at the ask gives most of it back in the ~3c spread and 0.7c fee.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The 2025-26 result (+5-6c per filled contract) is not a one-period fluke -- the 2023-24 fit and the post-cutoff live holdout are too small to confirm it and lean flat/negative, as did the ledger's SI23 recent half. (2) A 50-100-lot bid one tick inside fills when the daily candle says the price traded through it (median traded volume on the fill day ~1,000 contracts, p25 ~150, p10 ~40). (3) Losses stay spread across drivers (largest driver 4-5% of profit). (4) Locked cash costs only the 4.05% APY (positions earn it too; R1-N2-02: ~$450 spare).
idea.evidence_so_far: Kalshi /historical + live tier, 296 series, 833 markets candled (one RANDOM market per shared-driver cluster, never chosen by volume or result), daily bid/ask/trade OHLC; deadline clock. Improve+1c, filled only if the next daily candle traded at/through it, first qualifying horizon, one leg per driver: 2025-26 test 92 drivers, 6 losses, +6.06c [90% CI +1.33, +9.91], ~$12 per $100 locked per month, lock 17 days; 2023-24 fit 20 drivers +1.46c [-12.84, +11.90]; live holdout (settled 2026-08-16..10-15) 8 drivers, 2 losses, -10.00c; all periods 119 drivers +4.18c [+0.20, +8.25]. Strict traded-through fill at the plain best bid: test 85 drivers +5.14c [+0.08, +9.00]. Spread <= 5c: all periods 92 drivers +3.11c [-2.63, +7.71], live 6 drivers -17.83c. 90-99c band weaker: test 81 drivers +3.89c, through-filled edge only +1.6c (117 drivers). Haircut rule (same lane): favourite bid 0.80-0.95 traded through 108 drivers win 0.907 (avg bid 0.876, +3.1c) vs not traded through 182 drivers win 0.956 (+6.9c); bid 0.90-0.99 through 117 win 0.957 (+1.6c) vs not 228 win 0.987 (+4.0c); leg-level 'touch' fills +3.7c vs 'through' +2.0c (323 vs 198 legs). First monthly live-tier read (76 drivers settled 08-16..10-15, prereg.json written before it): P1 (90-99c at T-3) 8 drivers, 1 loss, -8.65c; P2 (90-99c at T-7) 13 drivers, 0 losses, +3.74c -- too small to decide. Below the brief's bar (< 150 test events; fit and live do not confirm).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Conservative (+2c a filled contract after adverse selection and the improvement, avg price ~88c, ~16-day lock): ~$4 per $100 locked per month vs the APY's $0.34. At the ~$450 R1-N2-02 says is spare: ~$0.60/day; at the optimistic test-period +6c ~$1.80/day. At $5,000: capacity-bound (~5-15 qualifying drivers a month), ~$1,300-2,200 deployable at 100 lots, ~$2-7/day. Worst plausible day: two or three favourites in one shared driver lose together, ~-$88 each at 100 lots (~-$260); a normal loss -$88 at 100 lots, -$44 at 50.

test.method:
Sources: the trade tape (rank 2) and daily candles. No replay was used.
(1) Re-scored the hunter's S2i rule with independent code, from his score_out.json. The rule: bid 1c above the favourite's best bid, improved bid 0.80-0.95, spread <= 10c, deadline clock, first qualifying horizon (T-30/14/7/3), one leg per driver, hold to settlement. Exact match (2025-26: 92 drivers, +6.06c).
(2) For all 265 of his offered picks, pulled the 24 h trade tape after each quote candle: /historical/trades before the 2026-08-17 cutoff, /markets/trades after. Scored 4 fill rules, pre-registered in prereg.json before any new data was pulled:
- F0: candle fill (his rule)
- F1: any tape print at or through our bid
- F2: >= 50 seller-initiated contracts at or through our bid (PRIMARY)
- F3: >= 50 contracts strictly through our bid
(3) Fresh out-of-sample replication on series the hunter never pulled: the next 315 long-dated series by lifetime volume (Politics 90, Elections 70, Entertainment 70, Economics 30, SciTech 30, Companies 15, World 10; CPI excluded). That gave 6,393 settled markets, 2,907 eligible and 496 new drivers; any driver or event already in his sample was dropped. One random market per driver, then daily candles, scored with his legs_for imported unchanged, and the tape pulled for every offered leg.
(4) Look-ahead check on the clock. Its fallback anchor is the event's ACTUAL latest close, which is after the fact when an outcome triggered the close. Each leg was classed as: title deadline, round-time close (scheduled), or arbitrary-second close (triggered).
Eras: pre-2025, 2025-01..2026-08, and live 2026-08-17..10-15. 1,381 public GETs, no auth. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-12/ (repro.py, tape.py, pull_new.py, fresh.py, anchor2.py, analyze.py, pool.py).

refs.strongest_objection:
Capital, not supply or edge, decides this at today's bank, and the tester's $0.5/day leaves out where the cash comes from.

(1) Pin sizes its bet from subaccount-0 CASH: size = cash / 11.8 (size_for_bank in research/pinrun.py; 100 contracts at $1,187 today). The book is not what limits pin: the project's 09-17 measurement found a median of 433 contracts buyable against a size of 95. So every dollar this book locks up shrinks pin's bet in proportion.
- Pin earned $364.35 (Kalshi ledger, crypto book, ET days 09-25..10-15, 21 calendar days) on a $1,077 average cash bank (from the live logs' bank records). That is $1.61 a day per $100.
- This book earns +3.39c per contract at 87.9c over a ~14-17-day lock, which is $0.23 a day per $100 ($0.31 at the optimistic 2025-26 +4.65c).
- Pin earns 5-7 times more per dollar. Moving the tester's $240 out costs pin about $3.87/day, against this book's +$0.53 to +$0.72/day if the edge is even real. Net: about -$3.2 to -$3.3/day.

(2) Running it inside subaccount 0 is worse. Pin's autosize_tick sees a long-dated purchase as an UNEXPLAINED bank fall (no Kalshi transfer matches it), and that fall counts against the 20% drawdown brake, which is terminal. About $236 locked on a $1,180 high-water mark trips the halt by itself. On a normal bad pin day (-$51 on 10-07, -$105 on 09-27) it trips with much less locked.

(3) Supply is about 100x what the tester assumed, so capital is the only limit.
- In my own live-tier pull, 459 non-sports offers in 174 drivers qualified on Kalshi's day-ago quote.
- In the 24 h to 2026-10-16 ~11:00Z, 27 of those markets in 22 drivers would have filled under the tester's own F2 rule (>= 50 seller-initiated contracts at or through bid+1c).
- Mean time to the deadline anchor for those fills was 14.2 days.
- So $/day = allocated cash x $0.23-0.31 per $100.
- Even under N2-02's proposed equity-sizing change, this book ranks below every other use of the lent cash already measured: forecaster ~$0.7-1.3, rain NO ~$2.1, CPI pair ~$0.8 per $100 a day.

(4) Correlation. 10 of the 22 drivers that filled settle between Nov 1 and Nov 5. Several are midterm-linked Politics events (endorsements, rallies, election emergency, a Trump meeting) that the one-per-driver rule counts as separate drivers. A capital-bound book would hold whichever fills first, which means a cluster on one week. At $240 that is 2-3 positions, so the worst week is about -$176 to -$264.

The edge itself stays unproven (CI includes zero). Reopen only when pin is book-bound, at about a $5,000 bank where size ~424 meets the ~433 median depth, or if N2-02's equity sizing is adopted AND every higher-return sleeve is full. The tester's read-only paper recorder can still run to settle whether the edge is real.

The tester's $0.5/day uses the pooled +3.39c, which includes the hunter's sample where this cell (improve+1c, 80-95c) was chosen as the best of ~40. Only the data that played no part in choosing it counts: the tester's fresh sample plus my own live-tier pull. That comes to 41 fills at +1.1c a contract, 90% CI -6.7 to +8.0. With the look-ahead-free clock (scheduled expiration) it is 39 fills at +3.0c, CI -4.7 to +8.8. Either way the range includes zero.

The edge also fades over time in the tester's own pool: 2025H1 +6.1c (17 fills), 2025H2 +5.9c (31), 2026H1 +2.8c (42), 2026H2 -1.5c (6). My independent read of the live tier (Aug 17 to Oct 16) is -2.5c on 15 fills. Dropping the three series that made most of the profit (KXRT, KXAAAGASM, KXALBUMSALES) leaves +1.9c, CI -3.3 to +6.6.

The proposed forward test cannot decide anything. Detecting +3.4c at a ~0.89 price needs about 330 fills (90% one-sided, 80% power), which is 3.5-6 years at the measured 5-8 fills a month. The tester's bar (60 fills, mean >= +2c, <= 10 losses per 100) passes a zero-edge strategy 33% of the time and a -2c strategy 18% of the time (simulated, 20,000 runs).

I found no artefact: units are dollars, the outcome comes from 'result', there were 0 block trades, and the size-aware fills agree. So the idea is not dead on the evidence, only unproven and effectively untestable at this size. refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's $0.5/day is a gross figure. Once you count where the cash comes from, running this book at today's bank loses money, at every point in the book's own confidence range. The idea assumed locked cash costs only the 4.05% APY (must_be_true 4). Under the live code that is false.

Why: the deployed bot (C:/kals-live-0925j/research/pinrun.py, size_for_bank) sizes every bet from subaccount-0 CASH, size = cash // 11.76, with no ceiling. Equity sizing (R1-N2-02) is not deployed. Pin adopts only positions in its own series, so it never sees a long-dated position. It just reads lower cash and bets smaller, so every dollar parked here comes out of pin's bet.

What a dollar earns in pin, from my own read of Kalshi's books (results/kalshi_ledger.json, crypto 15-min + KXBTCD, ET days 09-25..10-15):
- $362.41 over 21 calendar days on a $1,071.53 average cash bank (192 bank readings in the live logs) = $1.61/day per $100.
- Bank check: +$98 change in the bank plus $221 net moved out to subaccounts (own-account GET) = +$319, against +$389 on the ledger for all books. So the ledger is not inflated by more than about $70.
- Pin is mostly capital-bound at the margin. Of 27,839 entry contracts across 911 live orders since 10-04 (HYPE excluded), 87.7% were bought at the full size the bank set for that leg. Counting only that share, an extra dollar earns about $1.43/day per $100.

What a dollar earns in this book (edge / price / lock, 14.2-day lock; the idea's 16-17 days would look worse):
- Out-of-sample +1.13c: $0.09/day per $100.
- Pooled +3.39c: $0.27.
- Pooled upper 90% bound +7.42c: $0.59.
- Hunter's in-sample best +6.06c: $0.49.
- Cash held by unfilled 24 h resting bids earns nothing on top of that.

So moving the tester's $240 costs pin about $3.4/day and earns $0.22 to $0.65/day: net about -$2.8 to -$3.2/day.

There is also a cost inside subaccount 0. The late-boost room is (cash - 0.8 x high-water mark)/0.98, and a long-dated buy lowers cash without moving the mark. $240 locked removes about 245 contracts of room, which is more than today's ~214. The N2-02 critic measured that boost at about $2.5/day.

Correction to the execution skeptic: the 20% drawdown HALT has been off since 10-06 (--no-drawdown-halt), so a locked purchase does not trip a terminal halt. It only shrinks the bet and the late boost.

Caveats:
- Pin's own 20-day rate is noisy: $1.63/day per $100, 90% CI -0.06 to +3.33. On those numbers the book's dollar beats pin's dollar about 1 time in 10.
- The stats skeptic's power point stands. My own check: about 280 fills to see +3.4c (one-sided 90%, 80% power, 27c spread per contract). At 5-8 fills a month that is years, so no data rescues this at the current bank.
- Reopen only if pin's marginal dollar falls under about $0.5/day per $100 (pin limited by the book, around a $5,000 bank) or equity sizing is deployed. The free read-only paper recorder may still run.

idea.name: Macro-release favourite at 60-80c, 14-30 days before the print (eggs, payrolls, U3, GDP, core PCE, monthly gas) -- WEAK; the 90-97c leg of R2-M-10 is flat on history
idea.mechanism: 14-30 days before a release, on each ladder take the rung whose favourite side is 60-80c and buy it (taker, or the improve+1c bid), hold to the print. One position per release (payrolls and U3 share one report).
idea.why_mispriced: Le 2026's finance slope 1.42 at 1 week-1 month: weeks out, the crowd keeps mid rungs too close to 50c when the release is fairly forecastable (eggs from USDA wholesale, PCE from CPI/PPI, gas from RBOB). The other side is the lottery buyer of the 20-40c rung.
idea.must_be_true: The 2025-26 sign survives; the 2023-24 fit is flat, so this is one period.
idea.evidence_so_far: Economics favourite 60-80c at the ask, first qualifying horizon: 2025-26 test 28 drivers, 4 losses, +14.02c [+3.30, +24.22]; 2023-24 fit 28 drivers +0.26c [-12.13, +14.69]; live holdout 7 drivers +0.67c. Fading it loses: KXEGGS 13 drivers -21.2c, KXPAYROLLS 9 drivers -23.8c, KXGDP 6 -15.5c, KXPCECORE 5 -17.2c. Slope Economics T-30 1.66 [1.20, 2.86], T-14 1.25 [1.00, 1.87], T-7 1.07. For R2-M-10's extension: Economics favourites at 90-99c at the ask, all periods 86 drivers, 5 losses, -0.79c [-5.33, +3.11]; 95-99c 60 drivers, 2 losses, -0.07c -- no carry at the ask on payrolls/U3/PCE/GDP history.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: If +5c held at 50 contracts on ~6 releases a month: ~$15/month (~$0.50/day) at the current bank; ~$2/day at $5,000 (mid-rung depth, not measured, caps it). Worst release: one 70c rung lost = -$35 at 50 lots.

idea.test_plan: Pre-register now on the Nov-Dec 2026 releases (~10-15 events): bar >= +2c a contract after fee on >= 25 events by end of January. Also re-run on the full 2021-24 archive with a second random rung per release (~100 calls) to see whether the fit-period null holds with more n; fold into M-12's monthly holdout read.

test.method:
I re-scored the hunter's rule on every rung of every release ladder. The hunter used one random rung per driver.

**Data**
- Daily candles from Kalshi (/historical plus the live tier, whole life, one call per market) for 822 of the 1,400 eligible markets of KXGDP, KXEGGS, KXAAAGASM, KXPCECORE, KXPAYROLLS and KXU3, 2021-08 to 2026-10.
- Pruning used only what was known at entry: U3 strikes within 0.35 pp of the previous print, and jobs rungs lying beyond a rung that was already at 0.90 or more at T-30.

**Leg logic**
- The hunter's own score.legs_for: clock A (anchor = release time); quote = last daily candle in [entry-2d, entry]; spread at most 10c; favourite chosen by mid; buy at the favourite ask.
- Fee recomputed per 50-lot order and rounded up.

**Rules, frozen from the idea text before scoring**
- R_idea: walk T-30 then T-14. At the first horizon where any rung's favourite ask is in [0.60, 0.80), take the rung closest to 70c. One leg per release date (payrolls and U3 count as one report).
- R_idea21: the same with T-21 added.
- R_hunter: the hunter's T-30/14/7/3 walk.
- ALLRUNGS: every in-band rung at a fixed horizon, averaged per release, with no picking.
- Le's recalibration slope, bootstrapped by release.

**Periods**
- Fit: before 2025-01-01. Test: 2025-01-01 to 2026-08-15 (the hunter's positive period). Live: from 2026-08-16.
- Holdout inside test: first half against second half.

**Cross-check on a second source**
- R2-M-10's and R1-N1-01's hourly candles at T-21 and T-14, with the standing quote carried forward up to 72 h.
- Covers payrolls, U3 and core PCE, plus CPI as a sibling family the hunter never used.

**Supply**
- Today's public order books on the open ladders: 47 rungs with the favourite at 55-85c.

**Source rank**
- Kalshi candles plus Kalshi settlement results: replay-class quotes with no size or queue history.
- No live fills exist for this rule.
- I reproduced the hunter's own number from its score_out.json before scoring.

test.artefact_checks:
1. **Rung lottery and one trend.** The hunter's +14c rested on one random rung per driver, and 11 of its 29 test drivers were KXEGGS: a single 2025 egg-price downtrend whose monthly changes are autocorrelated. Scoring every rung removes the luck of which rung was drawn.
2. **One calendar year.** The 2025 half passes (zero edge would do that well about 3 times in 100). But it is one of about 18 looks (3 rules x 3 sets x 2 halves), and the following 23 releases lost. A 5c spread cap shrinks the 2025 figure to +1.7c.
3. **Fragile pick.** Taking the rung closest to 70c and taking every in-band rung disagree in sign in the test period: +6.5c against -4.4c.
4. **Fees** are charged per 50-lot order and rounded up.
5. **Second source agrees.** The hourly data, including CPI, which the hunter never saw, gives the same sign.
6. **Found and fixed: a sampling bug in an earlier tester.** Kalshi's hourly candles are emitted only when something changes. R2-M-10's "(T-6h, T]" window therefore kept only rungs whose quote had just moved: 159 legs at T-21 where carrying the quote forward finds 293. That tester's sample was selected on recent activity.
7. **Pruning** used only T-30 information. The 60 of about 480 jobs rungs it skipped are covered at T-21 and T-14 by the hourly cross-check.
8. **Coverage gap.** The U3 fit period at T-30 is covered only to 2023-10 because of the call cap. The fit period is not the decider.
9. **Size not observed.** Daily candles carry no size or queue position, so buying at the ask assumes our 50 contracts are there. Today's books say they often are not (see supply).

idea.name: Thin new-state gas ladders (listed 10-01..10-13): be the real two-sided persistence-anchored quote where the 'market' is 1-lot stale orders -- WEAK, paper only
idea.mechanism: Quote a narrow persistence-anchored two-sided market (yesterday's print + 0.61 x yesterday's change) at 20 lots in the thin new-state ladders, 6 PM-midnight ET, and collect the $100/strike pots on strikes we make two-sided.
idea.why_mispriced: No informed maker has set up there: the market-implied median is WORSE than plain persistence (October mean abs error AK 2.65c vs 0.94c, ME 1.15 vs 0.34, MT 1.81 vs 0.29, UT 2.12 vs 1.57, NM 3.46 vs 2.57, HI 1.63 vs 0.75), because the books are 1-lot stale orders 50-90c wide.
idea.must_be_true: The flow in these ladders is uninformed. Against it: the candle taker on new states at 6 PM ET LOST -3.7c a contract (88 signals, 7 dates) and the UT tape showed makers flat (+0.1c over 7,602 contracts), so better-informed traders are present even there.
idea.evidence_so_far: s4_compare (per-state October table), s10_taker (new-state group), UT trade tape (23 strike-days). The established-state model maker is dead (-21c a contract).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0-20/day at the current bank; worst day -$60 (a 3c move against 20 lots on 10 strikes). Not scalable at $5,000 (thin books).
idea.settlements_per_day: ~25 new-state ladders x 17 strikes
idea.test_plan: Paper only: log a persistence-anchored two-sided 20-lot quote in 5 thin states for 14 days against the public tape (fill = a trade through our price) and score 5-min markouts plus settlement. Bar: >= +1c a contract in the 6 PM-midnight window over >= 14 strike-days per state.
idea.prior_reason: The 'error' is mostly a 1-lot-quote artefact and the only measured flows (taker -3.7c, UT makers flat) argue against it.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New ladders; R1-C2-09 targeted the national/weekly books.

test.method: As written (20 lots, narrow quote) the idea is DEAD. The version that survives is the size-corrected one: 200 lots (= 1/5 of the target), quoted +/-15c. Sources: the trade tape (rank 2) and live public order books. None of our own fills exist. (1) Pulled the full public trade tape of every settled strike WITH volume in the 9 named thin ladders (AK ME MT UT NM KS HI MS WY), prints 10-01..10-16: 1,040 of 2,034 settled strikes, 588,251 contracts (t1_pull.py). UT/NM 10-16 were still unsettled at 12:27Z and are excluded. (2) t2_sim.py: fair value exactly as the idea states. mu = yesterday's AAA print + 0.607 x yesterday's change; the 0.607 is the hunter's pooled fit on established states <= 09-30, so it is out of sample here. sd = the state's own rms momentum residual on PRIOR days, or the pooled 9-state residual if under 5 observations. P(print > k) = Phi. A second anchor variant adds 0.765 x the national ladder's implied change. Quote fair -/+ h. A fill is a tape trade THROUGH our price. Capacity is LOT per side per strike per ET hour, in the 6 PM-midnight ET window, scored at settlement, with no maker fee. Grid: sd x {0.75,1,1.5,2} x h {1,2,4,6,10,15c}. Parameters were picked on FIT prints <= 10-09 and scored on TEST prints 10-10..10-16 (7 dates). 8 variants (2 anchors x hour/evening cap x strict/tie fills), each at LOT 20/100/200/1000, clustered by print date. (3) t2b_markout.py: markouts against the next tape trade on the same strike >= 5 and >= 60 min later, with a random-sign control. (4) Reward: t3_reward.py, t4_books.py and t4b_wide.py score our quote with research/lipscan.side_scores. I re-checked that function against the filing text in results/LIP_FILING_2026-07-15.txt and it matches: reference = the first level reaching 1/5 of the 1,000 target, score = 0.5^ticks-below-reference x size, and a second counts only if both sides reach 1,000. Two book sets: (a) the hunter's full-depth EVENING books of ME and UT (10-15 5:49 PM ET); (b) my full-depth MORNING books of all 9 ladders for the 10-17 print (153 strikes, 10-16 8:28 AM ET). Every program on these ladders pays $100 per strike-day (target 1,000, discount 0.5) and started only on 10-13. Payout per strike per 6-h stint = $100 x 6/16 x (our yes share + our no share)/2, with the book held static. Scripts and outputs are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-19/.
test.n_markets: Tape: 1,040 settled strikes with trades (of 2,034 settled) in 9 ladders, 97 state-days, 16 print dates (10-01..10-16). The evening window holds 83 state-days, 14 dates and 220,903 contracts. Holdout TEST 10-10..10-16: 41-43 state-days with fills. Books: 153 strikes (9 ladders, morning 10-16) plus 34 strikes (ME and UT, evening 10-15).
test.n_independent_clusters: 7 test print dates (16 dates in all). All 9 states move with the national price on a given date, so the date is the cluster, not the state-day.
test.result:
FILLS, 20 lots (the idea as written), TEST week. The narrow quote it describes loses. At h 2c: -11.0c a contract (momentum anchor, 4,554 contracts, -$502 = -$72/day) and -10.0c (national-anchored, -$62/day). At h 4c: -9.6c and -8.8c. In every one of the 8 variants, 0 of 24 settings were positive on test, and the loss shrinks steadily as the quote widens, the classic sign of being picked off. The fit always picked the widest setting (h 15c): -2.2c a contract (momentum, -$7.6/day) and -0.3c (national-anchored, -$0.8/day), with 2 standard errors of 8.0c and 4.8c. Bar (>= +1c a contract): FAILED. Markouts on the same fills: -10.7c at +5 min and -16.4c at +60 min, against a random-sign control of -1.6c and -4.8c. In the evening window the population of takers made -0.04c a contract after fees over 220,903 contracts, and makers lost on 9 of 14 dates, so there is no dumb flow to harvest.

REWARD at 20 lots is tiny. 20 is under 200 (1/5 of the target), so the farmers' 1,000-20,000-lot stacks at 4-14c set the reference price and get full credit, leaving us 0-6% of each side. Morning book: $13.5-18.3 per 6-h stint across all 153 strikes. Evening book: ME $0.31 and UT $2.1-3.6. Net at 20 lots: about -$60/day narrow, about +$5 to +$13/day on paper at h 15c, and that needs ~$2,400 collateral for all strikes. Noise-level.

THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS. At 200 lots placed above the farmers, our order becomes the reference price, and the 0.5-per-tick discount wipes out their stacks 10-26 ticks below. We would hold ~100% of both sides; I checked this by hand on KS strikes 3.985-4.000. Static morning book, 200 lots at +/-15c: $2,814 per 6-h stint over 121 qualifying strikes for $23,937 collateral, i.e. $118 per $1,000 of collateral per stint (at 1,000 lots it is $24 per $1,000). Evening book at 250 lots: ME $56 (2 qualifying strikes), UT $138-224. Fills at 200 lots, +/-15c, TEST week: -3.5c a contract (national-anchored, 9,035 contracts, -$45/day over all 153 strikes) and -6.1c (momentum, -$89/day). The worst test date over all strikes was -$229 (national-anchored) and -$481 (momentum). On paper the pot is ~30x the fill cost. Gaps that large have always turned out to be measurement bugs in this project, so the verdict is plausible-needs-data, not viable.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Scoring rule: lipscan.side_scores matches the filing text ('one fifth of the target size', 'Discount Factor taken to the Nth power'). But the case that makes the money, a small order ABOVE the reference beating much larger stacks below it, has NEVER been paid to us live. The 10-11 coin-race test only proved the case where we sit alone on one side. (2) Static book: one morning snapshot of 9 ladders and one evening snapshot of 2. The programs are 3 days old and the farmers quote wide. One UT participant already posts a 250-lot order at the top of the walk (250 @31c over 2,540 @25c), so the trick is known. Incumbents can step ahead of us within minutes, and our share would then fall to a pro-rata split or to zero. (3) The fill model is generous (every trade through our price fills us, no queue), yet it still cannot see the informed flow a tighter quote would ATTRACT, so the fill costs are a lower bound. (4) The fit sample is tiny (6 dates, 13-15 state-days), so the picked parameters are noisy. The dead verdict on the narrow quote does not depend on them: 0/24 settings positive in all 8 variants, with the loss shrinking steadily as the quote widens. (5) For a while two pullers wrote to the same tape file because the child process of my stopped task kept running. That left 205 duplicate lines, removed by ticker; all 1,040 strikes are present and there are 0 bad lines. (6) Price units were decided by field name (*_dollars), never by magnitude. (7) UT/NM 10-16 prints are excluded (unsettled). (8) Collateral assumes Kalshi reserves both resting sides separately; netting was not measured. Housekeeping: ~1,450 unauthenticated GETs, 0 authenticated, 0 orders. The tape file for 12Z was still being written at 12:36Z, so the collector is alive. Free disk 113 GB. Scratch folder 0.6 MB.

Reward pots: $100 per strike-day x ~153 strikes = ~$15,300/day in these 9 ladders, or $37.50 per strike per 6-h stint if we alone hold the top of both sides. In the morning book 121 of 153 strikes qualified (both sides >= 1,000); far fewer did in the evening (ME 2 of 17).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: As written (20 lots, narrow): about -$60/day, measured on the tape. At h 15c about +$5/day, inside noise. Size-corrected (200 lots, +/-15c) at the current bank: collateral is ~$140 per strike, so ~$300 idle in the evening covers 2 strikes. That is at most $75 per 6-h stint on a static book. After cuts for thinner evening books, incumbents stepping ahead and seconds when we are not at the top, the central estimate is ~$15/day (range $0-75). NOT MEASURED. Fills cost ~-$1/day for 2 strikes.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Not measured. With ~$2,000 of collateral free: ~14 strikes, a static-book ceiling of ~$525 per 6-h stint, and with the same cuts roughly $50-150/day until competitors respond. Fills ~-$6/day.
test.worst_case: Per strike: a full 200-lot fill on the wrong side of a +/-15c quote costs up to ~$140-170. Two strikes picked off in one evening: about -$300 at the current bank. For scale, the worst tape-replay test date at 200 lots over ALL 153 strikes was -$229 (national-anchored) and -$481 (momentum). The reward may also simply not be paid at the computed share. Then the fills are the whole result: -3.5 to -6.1c a contract.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Fills: 2 standard errors are ~4.8-8.0c a contract over 7 test dates. That cannot settle the +1c bar, but it does settle the narrow quote's -9 to -11c loss. The reward is not a statistical number: one live stint decides whether the computed share is paid.

refs.strongest_objection: Every dollar is the reward share, and the share is what nobody has measured. Fills do not kill it. The idea as written (20 lots, narrow quote) is dead, as the tester said. The 200-lot version only pays if three things hold. (1) Kalshi pays a small 200-lot order sitting ABOVE the reference price close to 100% of the side. The rule text says it should: I checked the filing and Kalshi's help-center page (help.kalshi.com/en/articles/13823851) and they agree. But that case has never been paid to us live. (2) Incumbents do not join or step ahead of us. In my own 9:08 AM ET snapshot, 41 of 306 book sides (13%) already had a level of 200 lots or more priced above the side's main stack, so the trick is already in use. A farmer who simply joins our price takes half the share at no extra risk to himself. One who steps 1 tick ahead leaves us a third. (3) The book qualifies in the evening (1,000 lots on both sides). The tester's 10-15 evening book had only 2 of 17 Maine strikes qualifying, against 143 of 153 strikes in my morning snapshot. Execution costs the tester did not count: (a) the collateral, ~$140 a strike, comes out of the pin bot's bank. pinrun auto-sizes from /portfolio/balance, so if resting orders reduce that balance (not measured), 2 strikes cut pin's bet ~24% for the stint. (b) Adjacent strikes in one ladder get picked off together. The worst single strike-evening was -$132 under the pessimistic fill model, so a bad evening on 2 strikes is about -$260, 23% of the $1,155 bank, if the reward is not paid.

The reward is at most $37.50 per strike for 6 h, and $35.03 after sides are pulled. A full 200-lot adverse fill costs $44.96 on average. Break-even needs one on 83% of evenings. Observed: 23% of evenings (33% since the program started 10-13). Program terms verified by my own /incentive_programs read: $100 per strike per 16-h period (12:00Z..03:59Z, which is the market's whole open window), target 1,000, discount 0.5, 17 strikes in every one of 52 state ladders plus the national ladder (~$88k/day of pots). My morning book (10-16 13:08Z): our quote would hold more than 90% of both sides on 22 of 41 quotable strikes. Static reward $1,228 per 6 h for $5,669 collateral. Paper net at the current bank (2 strikes, pessimistic fills, full share): about $50 per evening. Central estimate after haircuts for share and competition: ~$15/day, not measured. Scripts and RESULT.json are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/refute-execution-20261015-R3-M-19/.

refs.strongest_objection:
The headline reward comes from a book that stood still, read at 8:28 AM ET, and that is the best moment of the whole day. The big resting stacks ("farmers") are run by programs that keep re-pricing. My own polls of 63 near-money strikes in the thin ladders show it:
- The width of the book at the top fell from 84c (8:42 AM ET) to 62c (9:31), 40c (11:59) and 16c (3:01 PM).
- To take the top of the queue, a 200-lot must sit about 10c above the farmer stack. The median gap between that price and our model fair went +29c, +18c, +12c, then -1c at 3 PM. By then it sits at or above fair.
- Strikes that leave at least 15c of room against the market mid went 56 of 61, 55 of 63, 37 of 63, then 7 of 60.
- The 200-lot +/-15c reward on a still book fell from $1,519 to $630 per 6 hours, and most of the $630 comes from a model fair that the market has already moved past.
- Example: on KS 3.98 the best YES bid went 16c, 32c, 68c, 95c during the day.

So "the book holds still for 6 hours" is false. A top-of-queue order has to keep re-posting, closer to fair each time, which is exactly where the people who sell to us know more than we do.

The case that makes the money, a small order sitting above much bigger stacks, has never been paid to us. On the established ladders, which have had the same $100 pots for 53 days, only 0-3 orders per snapshot do this. Either nobody has found the trick, or those who try get picked off.

The tester's share numbers also use the wrong tick size: the series is 1c ticks throughout, and the tester's tool assumes finer ticks under 10c. That overstates the reward by 4-7%. This is minor.

NOT MEASURED: the 6 PM to midnight ET window itself. The 22:15Z and 23:30Z polls were cancelled and the poller was stopped. Also not measured: the share Kalshi actually pays, and how fast incumbents step in ahead of us. The idea survives only as a hypothesis.

idea.name: Entertainment 60-80c favourite fade, 3-30 days out (buy the contender at its ask, or bid it one tick inside) -- WEAK, post hoc
idea.mechanism: When an Entertainment market's favourite sits at 60-80c 3-30 days before its end, buy the other side at its ask (or rest a bid one tick above its bid) and hold. Optionally only where the R1-N0-09 RT score-drift model or R1-N0-13 album nowcast also puts the favourite <= 60%.
idea.why_mispriced: Attention markets: retail piles onto the obvious favourite (the film everyone expects 'fresh', the album everyone expects to top) while the outcome distribution is wider -- the opposite shape to Economics.
idea.must_be_true: The sign is not a 2025-26 / RT-specific accident (the fit period has < 5 drivers; the live holdout disagrees).
idea.evidence_so_far: Entertainment favourite 60-80c at the ask: test 35 drivers, 18 losses (48.6% win at a 70c ask), -23.26c [-37.32, -9.20]. Fade at the contender's ask: test 35 drivers +16.83c [+2.69, +30.83]; live holdout 9 drivers -3.23c; fit n < 5. Maker form (contender bid 1c inside, next-day fill): all periods 24 fills +15.08c [-1.92, +31.46]. By series: KXRT 25 drivers fade +8.74c [-8.35, +24.37]; KXALBUMSALES 7 drivers +31.2c. Slope Entertainment 0.92-1.20 (no compression).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: At 30 contracts on ~5 events a month and +8c: ~$12/month (~$0.40/day) at the current bank; not scalable past a few hundred dollars, so ~the same at $5,000. Worst event: ~-$10 at 30 lots (contender bought at ~30c).
idea.test_plan: Free: re-score monthly on newly settled KXRT / KXALBUMSALES / chart markets from the live tier (~30-60 calls) inside M-12's monthly read; bar fade >= +5c on >= 30 new drivers.
idea.prior_reason: Post hoc, 90% CIs of +-15c on 35 drivers, live holdout negative, ~$0.40/day.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New cell; the base-rate prior that R1-N0-09 (RT knife-edge) and R1-N0-13 (album nowcast) would start from.
idea.worst_case: Post-hoc noise: a cold month costs ~$30-50.

test.method:
I re-ran the hunter's exact rule, out of sample, on Entertainment drivers he never saw. The bars were written to prereg.json before any new data was pulled. The data is Kalshi's public quote archive (daily candles): exchange quotes, not a replay of our own decisions.

- **Pull:** settled markets from /historical/markets plus the live tier for the 175 Entertainment series the hunter never pulled (the top 150 long-frequency series by lifetime volume, plus the top 25 weekly). That is 36,310 settled markets.
- **Eligibility:** the hunter's rules (result yes/no, volume >= 300, event life >= 14 days, market open >= 3 days). Every event and driver already in his universe was dropped. Up to 3 eligible markets per driver were picked at random with a fixed seed, without looking at outcomes.
- **Candles:** daily candles for 942 markets. Historical-tier markets one call each; live-tier markets through the event-candlesticks endpoint.
- **Scoring:** the hunter's own score.legs_for: clock C, spread <= 10c, horizons 30/14/7/3 days, first qualifying horizon, favourite ask 60-80c. The contender is bought at 1 minus the favourite bid, the taker fee 0.07 x mult x p(1-p) is paid, and the position is held to settlement. One leg per driver.
- **Anchor fix:** the event end is now the outcome-blind scheduled end (expected_expiration_time). The hunter's anchor (latest actual close) lands on the moment a 'reach X during <period>' market resolved YES early, which is look-ahead. Both anchors are reported.
- **Holdout periods:** fit (before 2025), test (2025-01 to 2026-08-15), live tier (settled after 2026-08-16).
- **Checks before real data:** the self-test plants a world where a 70c favourite wins half the time and reads the fade at +17.1c; a calibrated world reads -3.4c. The pipeline also re-derives the hunter's in-sample numbers exactly: 44 drivers +12.72c, test 35 +16.83c, live 9 -3.23c.

Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-15/: s1_pull_markets.py, s2_universe.py, s3b_candles.py, s4_score.py, s5_insample_sched.py, s7_families.py. Outputs: score_sched.out, score_act.out, score_sched_rank0.out, families.out. Total 1,329 public API calls.

test.artefact_checks:
1. **Pipeline:** it reproduces the hunter's numbers to the cent before touching new data.
2. **Look-ahead anchor:** the hunter's latest-actual-close anchor enters early-resolving 'during <period>' markets just before they resolve. I replaced it with the scheduled end. That gives 135 vs 107 drivers and -2.53c vs -0.62c; the artefact did not flatter the fade here.
3. **Prices and units:** favourite plus fade sums to minus the spread and fees (-7.5c), so prices and units are consistent. All candle prices are in dollars on both the historical and live tiers.
4. **Random picks:** seeded, never chosen by volume or result. I confirmed the picks were unchanged after adding the anchor field.
5. **Repeated question:** the 6 Kanye 'BULLY' months (all -34c) were removed as a check; the result is still only +1.38c.
6. **Clustering:** the stricter clusters do not change the sign.
7. **Multiple looks:** the original cell was one of roughly 7 categories x 4 price bands x 3 periods x taker/maker x 3 clocks in the hunter's scan. Its in-sample number (+16.8c on 35 drivers, against a smallest-detectable effect of 21.7c) is what that many looks produce by chance. The in-sample also had zero fit-period drivers.
8. **Housekeeping:** both recorders were writing to kalshi_data and feed_data at 08:54 ET. Scratch folder 28 MB; disk 112.8 GB free.

idea.name: LoL pre-match forward paper book (WEAK): the blue-side team at the ask before each map, and NO on Bo5 'over 4.5 maps' before the match
idea.mechanism: (a) When a map's side is known, buy the blue-side team at the ask at previous close + 2 min (map 1: schedule - 2 min) if the pre-map price ignores the side. (b) A few minutes before a Bo5 starts, buy NO on 'over 4.5 maps' at the ask. Both hold to settlement; both run as a pre-registered paper log first.
idea.why_mispriced: Per-map prices may be copied from the match price with no side adjustment while blue wins ~56% of maps; fans overrate long, close series.
idea.must_be_true: The residuals beat fee + half-spread out of sample, and the side is public before Kalshi reprices (the API's sides for unstarted games 2-5 are placeholders).
idea.evidence_so_far: Blue side: 894 pre-map snapshots, sides from getEventDetails; blue won 55.9% (+5.94c, se 2.04, 724 maps / 308 matches); blue won - price +3.50c (se 1.81); Aug 17-Sep +4.78c (se 1.99, 582 maps); October -1.72c (se 4.23, 142 maps) -- holdout did NOT pass, underpowered (MDE ~8c). Bo5: 139 matches, realised - price -5.8c (se 3.5); Aug 17-Sep -6.8c (107), Oct -2.4c (32); mean spread 3.1c; the market is already 3.4c below an iid-maps model; books ~5k contracts lifetime.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Blue side if +3.5c were real: ~10 maps/day x 50 contracts ~ $10/day, realistically $0-5/day; Bo5 < $2/day (thin books). Same at $5,000 (depth-bound). Worst: -$25 per map at 50 contracts; -$20 per Bo5 at 25.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~25-30 maps/day in season; ~2-3 Bo5/day in playoffs
idea.test_plan: Pre-register now on Worlds Oct 16-Nov 8 plus LCK/LPL 2027: blue-side bar +2c net on >= 150 maps; Bo5 bar +2c net on >= 100 matches; also log when getEventDetails switches a game's side from the placeholder.
