test.method: Neither rule has a fitted threshold, so I tested both on data that played no part in finding them. Sources: Kalshi 1-minute candles (yes bid/ask close) and the official in-game feed for sides. No replay was used. (1) I checked the hunter's side labels against the livestats in-game metadata (gameMetadata.blueTeamMetadata, team found by summoner-name prefix) on 1,257 maps from Aug 17-Oct 15. The getEventDetails sides the hunter used are wrong on 5% of maps (903 of 958 priced maps agree), and the errors cluster in whole matches. (2) NEW independent sample: Kalshi's public /historical/markets archive (markets settled before the 2026-08-16 cutoff) holds 7,308 KXLOLMAP markets back to Oct 2025 and 1,947 KXLOLTOTALMAPS markets. I matched 2,315 maps from Apr 1-Aug 16 to the lolesports schedule (paged back to Jan 2026) and drew 380 matches at random (seed 17). For those I got true sides and game start times from livestats (805 maps), the blue team's archive 1-minute candles (811 maps), and every matched Bo5 'over 4.5 maps' market (160). Rule (a): buy the blue team at the ask at the snapshot (map 1 = schedule - 2 min; map n>=2 = previous map's actual close + 2 min), 50 contracts, taker fee roundup(0.07*C*P*(1-P)). Dataset A pays min(ask, 1 - other book's bid); dataset B pays the blue book's ask only. Rule (b): buy NO on over-4.5 at 1 - yes bid at schedule - 2 min, 25 contracts. Also measured: price drift from snapshot to 1 min before game start, the side-free 'previous-map loser' rule, quote age, and contracts traded before the snapshot. Clustered by match. About 1,190 public Kalshi calls; the rest went to lolesports. Recorders confirmed still writing (kalshi_data and feed_data files updated 09:08 ET). Scripts and output are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-17/ (truesides.py, sched_hist.py, match_hist.py, details_hist.py, candles_hist.py, analysis.py, analysis.out, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: Blue side: 1,296 priced maps = 726 maps from Aug 17-Oct 15 (hunter set, true sides) + 570 archive maps from Apr 1-Aug 16. Out-of-sample (Oct 1-15 + archive): 714 maps. Bo5: 250 matches = 139 hunter + 111 archive (Jan-Aug 16); out-of-sample 143.
test.n_independent_clusters: Blue side: 309 matches (A) + 313 matches (B); out-of-sample pooled 370 matches. Bo5: 250 matches, 143 out-of-sample.
test.result: BLUE SIDE: the lean is real but smaller than the cost of buying it. In-sample (Aug 17-Sep, where it was found, true sides): blue won - mid +4.47c (se 1.96, 582 maps / 252 matches), but NET at the ask after fee only +1.45c (se 1.97). Oct 1-15 holdout: net -5.67c (se 4.13, 144 maps / 57 matches). NEW archive, Apr 1-Aug 16: blue won 57.0%, blue won - mid +4.34c (se 2.05), net at the ask +0.86c (se 2.05, 570 maps / 313 matches). Out-of-sample pooled: mid residual +2.88c (se 1.85) but NET -0.46c (se 1.84, 714 maps / 370 matches). Map 1 -0.55c, maps 2+ -0.38c. Buying costs about 3.3-3.8c a contract (half-spread 1.5-2.0c + fee ~1.76c), and the ~3c lean never covers it. The price barely moves toward blue as the draft reveals the side: +0.28c (se 0.10) from snapshot to 1 min before game start. So this is a small steady lean, not a lag a fast bot can catch. The side-free 'buy the previous map's loser' rule is worse: net -6.99c out-of-sample (se 2.24, 415 maps). Its mirror, the previous winner, is about +3.2c at the mid and about -0.4c after costs. The pre-registered bar (+2c net on >= 150 maps) fails in every out-of-sample cut. BO5 OVER 4.5 NO: did not replicate. Archive realized - yes mid -0.42c (se 4.16, 111 Bo5s; a fifth map was played in 32 of 111 at a 29c average price); NO net at the ask -3.34c (se 4.17). Out-of-sample pooled net -2.75c (se 3.62, 143 matches). The hunter's -6.8c in-sample gap was noise.
test.artefact_checks: 1) Side labels: the API sides are wrong on 5.0% of A maps and 4.8% of B maps. Switching to in-game sides moved the in-sample mid residual from +4.78c to +4.47c; all results use true sides. Game 1 follows 'first-listed team is blue' on 331 of 347 maps (95%), so the side is knowable before the match; side secrecy is not why this fails. 2) Mid vs what we pay: the hunter quoted won - MID, but the trade pays the ask plus fee. That alone takes +4.5c down to +1.5c in-sample. 3) Stale quotes: median quote age at the snapshot is 21 s (90th pct 120 s). Keeping only quotes <= 10 min old changes nothing (out-of-sample -0.41c). 4) Dataset B pays the blue book's ask only (half-spread 2.0c, vs 1.5c in A, where the cheaper of the two books is used). Giving B the A spread lifts B net to about +1.4c and the out-of-sample pool to about 0c: still under the bar and not significant. 5) Selection: B is a seeded random draw of 380 of 1,071 archive matches. 572 of 811 maps had a usable two-sided quote (spread <= 10c); the rest could not be traded anyway. 6) Timing: the game starts a median 13.6 min after the snapshot (10th-90th pct 7.5-21.7 min). Using the price 1 min before game start gives the same answer (out-of-sample +2.75c at the mid, se 1.99). 7) Multiple looks: about 5 cuts x 2 rules. The one positive cut (archive maps 2+, +2.5c, se 2.66) has t < 1 and was not pre-registered. 8) No replay was used, and no tape loss rate is quoted as ours.
test.supply_we_would_get: KXLOLMAP, taking at the ask: about 24 Kalshi-listed maps/day Aug 17-Sep, 16/day in October, roughly 8-12/day through Worlds (to Nov 8), then near zero until mid-January (the archive shows 0 maps in Dec 2025 and ~220 in Jan 2026). Contracts traded in the 30 min before the snapshot: median 800 across both books (A), 305 on the blue book alone (B), under 100 for the bottom quarter. So 50 contracts fits most maps. KXLOLTOTALMAPS over-4.5: about 1-3 Bo5s a day in playoff weeks, with books around 5k contracts lifetime.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0: do not run. If run anyway at 50 contracts on ~16 maps/day, the central estimate is about -$4/day (-0.46c x 50 x 16), with a 95% range of roughly -$33 to +$26/day. The Bo5 leg is about -$1 to -$2/day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0. More size cannot fix a negative edge per contract, and depth would cap it near 100-150 contracts a map anyway.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Blue side, out-of-sample: about 5.2c a contract (2.8 x se 1.84 on 714 maps / 370 matches). That is enough to see the +3.5-4.5c the hunter hoped for, and the measured net is -0.5c. Bo5 out-of-sample: about 10c (143 matches).
test.worst_case: One map at 50 contracts near 54c loses about $27 including fee. A bad 16-map day winning only 5 (about 4 days in 100 at the measured 56.6% blue win rate) costs about $195; a typical losing day costs $30-60. Bo5 leg: -$19 per match at 25 contracts.
test.next_test: None for the taker rule: kill it. Ledger line: out-of-sample net -0.46c +- 1.84 on 714 maps / 370 matches; the ~3c lean at the mid is smaller than half-spread + fee (~3.4c). The only variant left is low prior and NOT measured here. It would rest a maker bid (LoL maker fee is 0) on the blue team or the previous-map winner, from previous close + 2 min until game start, so it earns the half-spread instead of paying it. The catch: fills would come from people watching the draft and selling into us, the classic trap of being sold to by someone who knows more. Deciding it needs an order-book-delta recorder on KXLOLMAP through Worlds (Oct 16-Nov 8, ~150-250 maps), paper only. Bar: filled-bid net >= +2c a contract on >= 150 FILLED maps, clustered by match. Bo5 totals: dead, no further test.

idea.name: Opening-30-s BTC maker: rest small model quotes from each window's open (strike known exactly), pulled 2 s before any weekday 8:30 ET open -- WEAK
idea.mechanism: Be resting at the open of each BTC window (strike = previous settle, known exactly) with small two-sided quotes around model fair; cancel them 2 s before any scheduled release open (8:30 ET weekdays), and let the opening takers hit us. Requires subscribing each window at listing (the recorder joins 31-114 s late).
idea.why_mispriced: Opening takers lose on average: in BTC's first 30 s takers lose -2.73c a contract (market-mean, se 1.30c) on a median 91,000 contracts per market. Makers collect that, before adverse selection on our own fills.
idea.must_be_true: Our fills are not the adversely selected slice (the 8:30 ET result shows the 0-5 s fast takers can win big), and the 1.6-1.85x post-close variance burst does not run over our quotes.
idea.evidence_so_far: PUBLIC TRADES, 100 BTC markets 10-02..10-13, first 30 s: all takers -2.78c contract-weighted, -2.73c market-mean (se 1.30c), on 9.24M contracts. ETH/SOL/XRP takers -0.3 to -2.2c (not significant). The model-edge taker in the same 30 s is dead (233 markets, -4.53c), so the opening model is the stale one. Our own maker fills: NOT measured. Its parent R1-C1-03 (600-900 s model-conditional maker) is dead.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not measured. Catching 1% of the opening flow (~900 contracts a window) at +1c after adverse selection would be ~$9 a window; realistic $0-20/day at the current bank, maker capital the cap. Worst: quotes run over by a jump during the burst: 200 contracts x 30c = -$60 a window.
idea.settlements_per_day: 96 BTC windows
idea.test_plan: Before any order: score would-be resting fills at 0-30 s (weekday 8:30 ET opens excluded) from the public tape against the next-second index move, to measure adverse selection on the fills a resting quote would actually get. Bar: post-fill 5-s markout >= +0.5c over >= 200 windows, both halves.
idea.prior_reason: A population-average taker loss (-2.7c) is not our maker gain; every 15-min crypto maker tested this run (R1-C1-03, R2-M-19) died on adverse selection.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Extension of the dead R1-C1-03 to the 0-30 s slice with the measured opening-taker loss and a release exclusion.
idea.worst_case: -$60 a window when run over.

test.method: SOURCE RANK: trade tape (public /markets/trades, unauthenticated) for each window's first 31 s + our raw BRTI 1/s feed (cfbenchmarks_value, READ-ONLY) for fair and index marks + Kalshi's own result/floor_strike for truth + our ticker tape (READ-ONLY) for the market's own YES mid at 120 s and 300 s after the open. No book exists on our tape for 0-30 s (recorder joins 36-69 s late, checked), so fills are inferred from prints: a queue-free REPLAY, which can kill, never prove. RULE as a bot would run it (PREREG.txt, frozen before scoring): K = floor_strike; spot = latest BRTI print whose Kalshi received_at + D <= T (D = 0.25 s, sensitivity 1.0 s); sigma = sd of 1-s $ increments over the 600 s before the open; fair = Phi((spot-K)/(sigma*sqrt(tau-60+20.5))); YES bid = fair-h floored to tick, ask = fair+h ceiled (tapered tick), Q = 20 a side (100 secondary), quotes from T=D to 30 s, hold to settlement, maker fee 0 (KXBTC15M fee_type quadratic). Weekday 8:30 ET opens excluded. Fill sets CONS (taker print strictly through our price; post-only reject if the other side printed at/through it in the prior 1 s), REAL (primary: + offers that would have crossed our live quote), OPT (+ prints at our price). Marks: settlement, model fair at T+0/1/5/30/60 s, and model-free market mid at t0+120/300 s. Grid h in {0.5,1,2,3,4,6}c x D x Q x fill set. HOLDOUT: 495 windows by open time, FIT 09-18..10-03 (247) vs TEST 10-04..10-16 (248), h chosen on FIT; then a second pre-registered CONFIRMATION sample (PREREG2.txt, written before its pull): 178 new windows. Self-test PASSES (planted uninformed-taker world +1.38c, planted informed world -3.19c, fill-rule/reject/Q-cap/tick/unit checks). Files: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-16/ (mo_sim.py, mo_mark.py, mo_diag.py, conc.py, conf.py, mark_mid.py, extract_idx.py, pull_trades*.py; outputs mo_out.txt, mo_mark.txt, mo_diag.txt, conc.txt, conf_main.txt, conf_confirm.txt, mo_release.txt; PREREG.txt, PREREG2.txt; RESULT.json). ~1,100-1,300 public API calls (IP shared with other agents' pollers: 134 429s).
test.n_markets: 673 KXBTC15M windows (495 main: 100 reused from the hunter's cache + 395 new, after dropping 1 truncated and 3 weekday-8:30-ET windows; 178 confirmation), 2026-09-18..2026-10-16, ~41.8M public contracts traded in the main sample's first 30 s; plus 18 weekday 8:30 ET windows scored separately.
test.n_independent_clusters: 673 windows (one BTC market per close, each its own cluster; window-clustered ratio-estimator SEs); 29 calendar days in the main sample.
test.result: DEAD. (1) The quotes that actually trade lose against the market's own price 2 minutes later, in every sample: REAL, D=0.25 s, 20-lot, fair +/- 2c: -1.42c a contract FIT (t -2.8), -0.84c TEST (t -1.7), -1.31c CONFIRMATION (t -2.2); pooled main -1.12c (se 0.35, t -3.2) on 13,146 contracts / 453 windows; settlement -1.19c main, -2.21c confirmation. +/- 0.5c and 1c: -1.3c to -1.9c in both halves (t -3.3 to -4.8). Every h <= 3c cell, both D values, CONS and REAL, negative on the market mark in both halves. (2) Adverse selection is immediate: at +/- 2c the index moves 2.1-2.3c against our fills within 1 s and stays (edge at fill +1.97c -> 5-s model markout -0.24c FIT / -0.76c TEST). (3) The only positive-looking width failed its pre-registered confirmation: +/- 6c (picked by the FIT rule on model 5-s markout, +1.50c FIT / +1.51c TEST) marks to the 120-s mid at -1.31c FIT, +3.34c TEST, -1.85c CONFIRMATION (bar >= +1.0c: FAIL); combined ~+0.16c on ~8 contracts a window; settlement -9.32c / +11.42c / +1.82c (noise). PREREG1 alone would have said plausible-needs-data (182 < 200 fill-windows); PREREG2 decides it. (4) The premise fails: the hunter's -2.73c opening-taker loss is mostly the TAKER FEE (~1.4-1.7c), which makers never get. Population makers (every print 0-30 s) earn only +0.24c FIT / +0.40c TEST against the 120-s mid (t 1.1/1.5) and -0.07c / -0.25c at settlement; our model-anchored quotes get a worse slice. (5) The market beats the index-only model at the open even with a zero-lag index: Brier 0.2419 market vs 0.2443 model (495 windows); outcome on both: market coef 2.40 (se 0.91), model -1.20 (se 0.81). So the idea's own yardstick (model 5-s markout) is biased in our favour by ~0.6-1.3c (confirmation +/- 6c: model +2.00c t 3.8 vs market mark -1.85c). (6) The 8:30 ET exclusion is right: 18 release opens settle -6.48c (h=1c), -4.29c (h=2c).
test.artefact_checks: Strike: Kalshi floor_strike vs our 60-print BRTI mean, median gap $0.0025, max $0.0050 on all 673 windows. Units: prices parsed once from *_dollars strings to 1/10000 $; tapered tick; self-test unit checks. Clocks: trade created_time and index received_at both Kalshi clock (our PC runs ~100-160 ms behind, unused). Backward companion: same loader reproduces the hunter's sign (takers 0-30 s -1.72c market-mean, se 0.61, 495 windows vs hunter -2.73c, se 1.30, 100); population maker positive on the model mark (+0.87c/+0.68c, t 9), so the estimator can find a positive; our fills' negative is selection. Market mark found for 499/499 and 178/178 windows, median lag 0.3 s, median spread 1c. Concentration: +/- 2c loss survives trimming the 5 best/5 worst windows (-1.13c), 11 of 29 days positive; +/- 6c flips sign by sample. trade_id dedupe dropped 0 rows; 1 capped hunter market excluded. Replay biases all favour us (unseen cancelled crossing orders, our order changing behaviour, exact post-only rejects), so negative replay = kill. Recorders alive: cfbenchmarks_value, trade, feed_data/coinbase and gemini written 11 s before the last check (09:08 ET); free disk 112.7 GB; scratch 20.8 MB; no process touched except my own pullers.
test.supply_we_would_get: Plenty, but the wrong kind. In KXBTC15M's first 30 s (~82-87k public contracts per window), a 20-lot two-sided quote at fair +/- 2c fills in 453 of 495 windows (26.6 contracts a window); +/- 1c ~30; a 100-lot ~128-148 a window; +/- 6c only 182 of 495 windows (7.9 a window). The fills come from takers about 1 s ahead of the index.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0, dead. Run as specified (20-lot, +/- 2c) it would LOSE about $30 a day at the current bank (main: -$0.32 a window x 95; confirmation: -$55 a day). The 6c-wide version comes to about $0-1 a day, which can't be told apart from zero.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0. At 100-lot the per-contract loss has the same sign (+/- 2c, Q=100: settlement -2.17c FIT / -0.55c TEST; model 5-s -0.15c / -0.85c) on ~5x the contracts, so roughly -$100 to -$150 a day if run.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Market-mid mark: 2 se = 0.7c a contract for +/- 2c (pooled main), 2.0c for +/- 6c. Settlement: 2 se = 2.3c (+/- 2c), 6.4c (+/- 6c). The idea's 'catch 1% at +1c' would have shown at +/- 2c; it came out -1.1c instead.
test.worst_case: 20-lot at +/- 2c: average -$30 a day, day-to-day swing about $66 (95 windows), so a bad day is about -$160. One window run over costs up to ~$10 (20 x 50c). +/- 6c: a bad day is about -$110. At $5,000 sizing, roughly 5x.
test.next_test: Nothing more for this idea. Any revived opening maker has to be a NEW idea: anchor quotes on an exchange-feed nowcast (feed_data/coinbase leads the CF index by about a second, which matches the adverse move measured here), not on the index. Free decisive test: rerun mo_sim.py with fair from Coinbase mids on the same 673 windows and mark to the 120-s market mid. Bar: >= +0.5c a contract with t >= 2 on FIT, TEST and confirmation separately, >= 300 fill-windows. Only after that, a 1-lot probe.

idea.name: Evening rain model-vs-market taker on KXRAIN (~7-10 PM local the night before, scored with the 18Z NBM run) -- the lane's '4 AM overnight +7.7c' was a look-ahead; clean +6.3c in-sample, 0.0c on the October holdout (WEAK)
markets: KXRAIN (30-35 cities/day; close_time ~1 AM local the NEXT day: TTN 05Z, SATX 06Z, SEA/SFO 08Z; only DTW closes 14Z)
idea.mechanism: At H=30 before Kalshi's close (23Z-02Z, i.e. 7-10 PM local the evening BEFORE the target day) compute P(rain on the target day) = 1 - prod(1 - p06) over the four 6-h periods ending 12Z D, 18Z D, 00Z D+1, 06Z D+1, from the 18Z NBS run of D-1 (public ~19-20Z), or for western cities the 00Z run once it is public (~01:15Z, log the issue time). Buy YES at the ask when P - ask - fee >= 10c; buy NO at (1 - bid) when (1-P) - (1-bid) - fee >= 10c. Size min(50, depth within 5c). Hold to settlement.
idea.why_mispriced: The evening book is thin and set by resting orders and reward farmers; in September it had not absorbed the afternoon NBM run (slope of outcome-minus-market on model-minus-market 0.43 with the clean run). By ~3 AM local it has (slope -0.005). Who pays: whoever rests the stale evening quote.
idea.must_be_true: (1) The clean September edge (+6.3c, se 3.5, t ~1.8) is not noise and returns after a null October (0.0c, se 5.0). (2) The NBS 18Z text is public before the quote (IEM archive gives run times, not issue times; NBM text normally lands ~1 h after the cycle). (3) Fills at 20-50 lots in the evening book (unmeasured; the lane's one live read was at 06:12Z = ~3 AM local, the regime the backtest calls dead). (4) Mountain-zone legs lost in September (-12.9c, se 7.8) -- not a pre-registered exclusion.
idea.evidence_so_far: N0 re-check (C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/merge-N0/rain_clean.py, rain_clean.out; no API calls; reuses the lane's MOS file and the r1-revisit candle cache): Kalshi /markets confirms close_time 2026-10-01T05:00Z for KXRAIN-26SEP30-TTN and 06Z for SATX, so the lane's 'H=30 = 4 AM local' snapshot really sits at 22Z-02Z (quote hours in the data: 22-02Z) and was scored with the 00Z and 06Z runs of the target day, issued ~0-3 h and ~5-8 h AFTER the quote. Reproduced the lane's number exactly (H=30 + 06Z run, 10c margin: 145 trades, 33 dates, +7.7c se 3.0). Clean pairings at the 10c margin -- H=30 + 18Z D-1 run: Sept 128 trades / 29 dates +6.3c (se 3.5), YES legs +3.2c n103, NO legs +10.9c n25; October holdout (10-01..10-13) 59 / 13 +0.0c (se 5.0); 5c margin Sept +3.2c (se 2.3), Oct +4.6c (se 3.9); 20c margin Sept +4.0c, Oct -9.2c. test.method:
Source: Kalshi's own hourly candle history (closing yes bid/ask each hour) for every settled KXRAIN city-day market with target dates 2026-07-27..2026-10-15. That is the r1-revisit cache plus 68 markets for 10-14/10-15, pulled without login. It was scored against the NBM short-range text (NBS) forecast archive. This is quote history plus a forecast archive: not our fills, and not pinsim. The trade tape was read on top of it to measure supply.

Rule, exactly as N0 pre-registered it:
- Quote = the last hourly candle at or before close minus 30 h, i.e. 6-10 PM local the evening before.
- P = 1 - prod(1 - p06) over the 6-h periods ending 12Z D through 06Z D+1.
- Buy YES at the ask, or NO at 1 - bid, when edge minus fee >= 10c. Hold to settlement.
- Fee rounded up to the cent at 50 lots.

Two models:
- (A) The 18Z D-1 run, N0's clean cell. Source is the IEM archive, which I pulled back to 07-24 to cover the new August sample.
- (B) The newest run provably public at the quote. This is what the idea's own paper-test plan specifies. NBS text is issued EVERY hour, about 36-48 min after the cycle (NOMADS listing on 10-15; AWS NBM bucket Last-Modified on each file). I pulled the 21Z D-1 NBS text for all 81 days from the NOAA AWS bucket: streamed, parsed for 34 stations, and the parser matched IEM on 48 of 48 values. It is used, or the 00Z D run for 02Z quotes, only if its upload time + 5 min <= the quote time. 34 markets were dropped by that gate.

Samples:
- AUG 07-27..08-28: a new backward holdout that nobody had scored.
- SEP 08-29..09-30: the in-sample the rule was chosen on. N0's +6.3c reproduced exactly.
- OCT 10-01..10-15: forward holdout.

Clustering is by target date. Means are per contract, with date-clustered se and a bootstrap over dates. N0's per-date average is also shown.

Controls:
- Placebos: the model shuffled across dates, and shuffled across cities (200 draws each).
- Opposite side of every leg.
- Leave out each month and each time zone; remove the best 3 dates.
- Leg-by-leg comparison of the 18Z run against the newest run.
- close_time against outcome (these markets 'close early if it rains').
- Trade tape +-1 h around every holdout leg: 361 leg reads, using /historical/trades for Jul-Aug.
- Cost of walking the book for 20 and 50 lots, from the lane's 10-15 06:12Z full-depth snapshot.

test.artefact_checks:
PASSED:
1. N0's +6.3c / 128 legs reproduced exactly from the 10-02 file.
2. No look-ahead: every run is used only after its own upload time (AWS Last-Modified) + 5 min. 21Z files land 21:42-21:48Z and 00Z files 01:14-01:18Z; one 00Z file uploaded at 14:17Z, and the time gate kept it out of every quote it postdated. NOMADS shows the 18Z text public at 18:43Z on 10-15, so N0's 18Z cell is clean too.
3. KXRAIN 'closes early if it rains', but the recorded close_time is end of the local day for YES and NO markets alike (all 1,925 checked, by month). So close minus 30 h does not depend on the outcome.
4. Placebos: model shuffled across dates (same city) gives median -3.6c, max -0.5c in 200 draws, against the real +11.5c. Shuffled across cities (same date): median -1.9c, max +0.5c. The opposite side of the same legs loses -16.6c.
5. Concentration: the best 3 dates are 41% of holdout P&L, and without them it is still +7.8c. Leaving out August gives +8.1c; leaving out October gives +14.5c. On the holdout, Eastern +16.8c, Central +9.7c, Mountain +3.9c, Pacific +3.2c, so the result does not rest on one zone.
6. Phantom quotes: legs where no other taker bought our side at our price within +-1 h still made +5.9c (33 legs), against +13.0c where >= 20 contracts traded (105 legs). The edge is not built on tiny fractional offers.
7. Rounding the fee at a real 50-lot order changes the result by less than 0.1c.

NOT RESOLVED:
- Candles carry the best price but not its size.
- Book-walk cost for 50 lots was measured only at about 2-3 AM local (median 0.4c, mean 0.66c, 90th percentile 2.1c). Depth in the 6-10 PM book is NOT measured.
- Legs whose quote hour had zero volume lost in Sept and Oct (-9.8c n18, -7.3c n13).
- Mountain lost in Sept (-12.9c) and over the whole sample on the newest run (-7.5c, 45 legs). It was not excluded, because that exclusion was not pre-registered.
- Several versions were tried: 2 models x 3 margins, plus a calibrated variant. Model B was named in the idea's test plan before this run.
- One season only, summer thunderstorms into early autumn; winter is unmeasured.
- Under the operator's rule this is replay-class evidence (quote history), not our fills.

KXRAIN, 30-34 cities a day. Each market closes about 1 AM local the next day, so the quote window is 22Z-02Z.

- About 4.1 qualifying legs per target date at the 10c margin. 73 of 79 dates had at least one; the most was 14.

We would be competing with those other takers for the same stale offers. Our real fill rate is not measured.

The money comes back within ~30 h. Regime risk: the edge was biggest in the August thunderstorm season (+14.5c) and smaller in September (+4.2c); winter is unmeasured.

At 80% power and 5% two-sided (2.8 x cluster se):

refs.strongest_objection: Nothing in execution kills it: the 1-minute book reproduces the price, the edge holds 5-60 min after the quote time, and nobody races for the offers. The problem is SIZE in the 6-10 PM book, which is still not measured, and the richest legs are the thinnest. NO legs earn +19.3c a contract (54 legs) and are ~40% of the fixed-30-lot profit ($299 of $720), but other takers found a median of only 8 contracts at our price before it moved (16 of 54 found none). If fills are capped at the size the tape proves was there, the money drops from $8.47 to $4.62 a day all-sample. September, the period the rule was chosen on, is +4.2c (se 3.5), which is $3.83 a day at 30 lots. Second: the stale makers are paid to be there. Every KXRAIN market carries a series_lip liquidity reward of $100 a period (period_reward 1,000,000 centi-cents, target 1,000 contracts, active on the 10-16 and 10-17 markets), which explains why stale quotes last a median 36 min. If Kalshi drops that program, the supply may go with it. Third: YES legs bought under 10c lose (-1.5c, 49 legs), the same overpriced-longshot effect SJ02 bets against; excluding them was not pre-registered. One summer-to-autumn season only; winter is not measured.

idea.name: Pre-market S&P/Nasdaq hourly ladders vs ES futures: stale-quote maker 04:00-09:30 ET and the 08:30 release sweep
markets: KXINXU (all 7 hourly ladders list at 20:00Z the day before; H1000 carries 70-90% of pre-market volume)
idea.mechanism: Maker: 04:00-09:30 ET rest two-sided quotes at fair +/- 2-3c on the 8-10 rungs within +/- 30 pts of the ES-implied S&P (S_hat = ES x yesterday's SPX close / ES at 16:00 ET), 5-20 contracts a rung, no maker fee; refresh every minute; pull 5 min before 08:30 ET releases and at 09:25 ET. Taker: at 08:30:00 ET on CPI/jobs/retail-sales mornings take every rung whose ask sits > 8c below the post-release ES fair in the first seconds.
idea.why_mispriced: Pre-market touches are 10-18c wide and refreshed on a minute scale (07:44 ET read 10-13: K7800 51/69 vs an ES fair of 57c; K7810 25/41 vs 40c); in the in-sample week 63% of pre-market contracts traded > 10c from the ES fair and takers lost 13.9c a contract (se 6.2, 23 closes, 147k contracts).
idea.must_be_true: Pre-market taker flow must be uninformed on average -- it is not reliably: the previous week flips the sign (H1000 takers +10.9c; whales posting 20-40k clips at 20c that won). A real-time futures/SPY source is needed (Yahoo ES=F is ~10 min delayed; nothing free and real-time found). The resident 35-48-lot quoter must not undercut to zero. Taker leg: the quoter must not pull within ~1 s of the print (first-100-ms races on reveals are dead: SJ09/10/42/44).
idea.evidence_so_far: In-sample week 10-06..10-12 (1-min ES bars): H1000 maker at fair +/- 2c +$1,601 over 4 closes (0 losing; 7,602 capped fills, +21c/contract); +$1,324 with the fair lagged 10 min; all 7 ladders +$1,698 over 18 closes (6 losing, worst -$138). Holdout Sep 29-Oct 5 (5-min bars): H1000 -$2,174 over 5 closes (3 losing, worst -$1,933), H1600 +$449. Net over 10 H1000 closes about -$900 at 20-lot fills. The sim fills at our quote whenever a print crossed it (assumes queue priority, ignores the resident quoter) = an UPPER bound. Release leg: nothing measured (the 10-14 CPI recording was lost: the PC was off 10-14 03:29Z .. 10-15 04:39Z).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: About $0 expected: +$75 / -$100 a morning at 5 lots; the release leg unknown ($0 if quotes are pulled at the print), ~8 releases a month. Worst plausible day: a trend morning runs over 10 rungs for 30-80c each, -$480 at 5 lots (-$1,933 measured at 20 lots in the holdout); at $5,000 and 50 lots -$4,800.
idea.settlements_per_day: 7 closes a weekday (H1000 the one with pre-market volume); ~8 release mornings a month
idea.test_plan: Two-week read-only forward paper: poll the H1000 ladder book 04:00-09:30 ET plus the best free futures quote; credit a fill only when a print crosses our quote AND our quote was at the touch at that second. Bar: >= +3c/contract over >= 10 closes, no close worse than -$50 at 5 lots, release minutes excluded; kill if either week is negative. Release leg: record the H1000 book 08:29-08:33 ET on the next two release mornings plus a per-second SPY/futures source; bar >= $50 of asks > 8c below the post-print fair surviving >= 500 ms on both days.
idea.prior_reason: A new, deep area (150k-2M contracts a week pre-market) with measured staleness, but the only replay is an upper bound whose sign flipped on the holdout; a free two-week forward paper is the honest next step.

test.method: Data sources, best first: the trade tape plus 1-minute ES futures and S&P index bars. No book history exists for KXINXU, and this does not replay our own bot. (1) Pulled the pre-market trade tape of the 10am S&P ladder, KXINXU-<D>H1000, from its 20:00Z open to 13:30Z, for all 20 trading mornings 2026-09-18..10-15 (pull.py, 574 public GETs): 498 rungs, 12,557 trades, 2.23M contracts. Rungs were chosen from the ES-implied path +-45 pts. The 10-13 hunter chose them within 0.4% of the SETTLE, which looks at the outcome and drops the rungs a trend morning runs over. (2) 29 days of 1-minute Yahoo ES=F and ^GSPC bars, pulled in 6-day chunks; Yahoo keeps 1-minute bars for about 30 days, not 7. Fair = Phi(ln(S_hat/K)/sd), where S_hat = ES x (previous H1600 settle / ES at 16:00 ET). sd^2 = the per-minute-of-day ES variance summed to 10:00 ET, so the 08:30 release and the 09:30 open are inside it, plus basis noise. It was fitted on the early 10 mornings only. (3) Maker sim. Quotes run 04:00-09:25 ET, with 08:25-08:35 blacked out every day, on rungs within 30 pts of S_hat. Quote = round(fair) +- w, refreshed once a minute. Fill model A is the hunter's: any print at or through our price fills, 20 a print, so it is an upper bound. Fill model B fills only on a print strictly through our price, so the resident order was worse than ours and the taker must have hit us first, and caps fills at q a rung a side a minute. The fair was either 0-60 s stale (best case for a real-time feed) or 10 min stale (what free Yahoo ES gives a live bot). Width w was picked on the fit half and read on the test half (10-02..10-15). The self-test passes: takers at fair give 0 fills, uninformed takers 6c through fair give +2.5c/contract, informed takers give -41.6c, and synthetic calibration rms z is 0.8-1.15. (4) Checks that lean less on the model: center.py (the market-implied level vs the ES-implied level vs the settle, per morning); align.py (|price - fair(ES at t+k)| over time shifts k); who_right (P&L of following the ES fair at the trade price, by |price - fair|, clustered by morning). (5) Release minute: the H1000 tape 0-120 s after 08:30:00 ET on the 4 big-move mornings, plus the Kalshi US500 perp trade tape from the public margin API. idea.name: Nov 3 election-night structural checks for the recorder: House/Senate control vs the 4-leg balance-of-power combo, and margin-of-victory ladders vs vote-share ladders vs race winners (both consistent today)
idea.mechanism: (A) Control vs combo: R House = RR + RD, R Senate = RR + DR (same Feb-1-2027 question). Package A: a control NO + its two combo legs YES pays exactly $1; package B: control YES + its two combo legs NO pays exactly $2; the four combo legs pay exactly $1 (all YES) or $3 (all NO). (B) Margin vs vote share vs winner on one race: {opponent >= d%} and {P margin >= m} cannot both win when m > 100 - 2d (buy both NO); P margin >= m implies P wins and implies P's share >= (100 + m - t)/2 (t = third-party share). On Nov 3 the marginals, the combo, the MOV/vote grids and the deep winner books are repriced by different crowds second by second as counts and calls land; buy any package that costs less than its payout after the 2-4 taker fees for >= 2 s with size, and after a call buy MOV rungs far below the running margin that the grid's 5-lot asks still offer under 95c.
idea.why_mispriced: Today nothing is: an arbitrageur holds every control/combo package inside the 3-leg fee band, and one grid quoter prices the MOV/vote ladders 8c wide (200-lot bids, 5-lot asks) consistently with the deep winner books. The only hope is that on election night one side lags by more than the fee band for longer than our send time.
idea.must_be_true: A lag > 2-4c lasting > 2 s with >= 200 lots (control/combo) or >= $200 of 5-lot MOV asks under 95c surviving 10 s after calls. MOV settles on CERTIFIED margins, so a rung below the called running margin is near-sure only when far below it. Riskless MOV/vote pairs need party identity per vote ladder (not in the API), a third-party cap (Kansas Libertarian 4.9% in 2020) and no ranked-choice state (Alaska). The carried 'decided-side taker sweeper after the AP call' was measured DEAD on primary nights (supply swept in seconds), the strongest prior against the MOV follow-on.
idea.evidence_so_far: Control/combo: live read 07:15Z 10-15 (8 GETs; inside the Thursday maintenance window, quotes resting): packages POSITIVE before fees (B on R House +0.5c, B on R Senate +0.8c, all-NO +0.4c) and negative after (-0.8c, -2.9c, -3.4c); 1-minute candles for all 8 legs, 21 days, 26,160 minutes with all 8 quoted (95 GETs): 0 positive minutes after fees for any of the 10 packages, best B on R House -0.12c. MOV/vote/winner snapshot 06:00Z, 29 races with all three series and 512 MOV races: 1,734 exclusive pairs 0 positive after fees (best -3.75c); 3,479 MOV-vs-winner pairs 0 positive (best -1.13c); 16 'positive' nests all needing a third-party share <= 3% (KS Senate +10.6c on 5 lots, MS Senate +8c on 11 lots) or Alaska RCV -> not riskless, ~$1-2 total; buy-both positives were party-mapping artefacts. MOV rung width p10/50/90 = 4.0/7.8/9.0c; median bid size 200, ask size 5.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 until Nov 3. Nov 3, not measured: if a 3c lag on 500 lots appeared 3 times (control/combo) ~$45 once; if 5-lot MOV asks survived 10 s after calls on 200 races at 5c each, ~$50 once. Same at the current bank and at $5,000 (size is the book's). Capital: control/combo settles Feb 2027 unless unwound (Kalshi pays 4.05% on positions >= $250). Worst plausible night: a 3-leg package half filled while calls land -- a naked control or race position, up to -$1 a set (-$50-100 at a few hundred lots).
idea.settlements_per_day: 0 until Nov 3; then 4,902 MOV markets settle on certification (Nov-Dec); control/combo in Feb 2027
idea.test_plan: Add the 8 control/combo tickers and the MOV ladders of the ~40 biggest races to the carried 'Nov 3 election-night recorder' (read-only). Log every second the 10 control/combo package costs with touch sizes, and at each AP call the MOV asks below the running margin for 60 s. Pre-registered bars: control/combo >= 3 crosses after fees of >= 1c on >= 200 lots lasting >= 2 s during the night; MOV >= $200 of resting asks under 95c surviving 10 s, rungs at least 5 points below the running margin. Fail both = dead for 2028.

Extends the carried 'Election margin-of-victory ladders as a running-count pin -- NOT MEASURED properly' with a measurement; no new trade until Nov 3.

test.method:
Three read-only measurements, all from Kalshi public 1-minute candles (the best bid and ask at the close of each minute, carried forward) plus the trade tape where it is still served; about 560 GETs. Kalshi keeps no order-book history, so there are no sizes. The tape ranks above any replay here, and no replay was used.
(A) Control vs the balance-of-power combo: the hunter's 10 packages plus the 2-way control sets on all 8 legs, extended from 21 to 45 days (2026-09-01..10-16, 51,394 minutes with all 8 legs quoted). Added: the minutes when a control price moved fast, and a check of how stale each leg's quote was at every positive minute (s5_bop.py, s14_bop_diag.py).
(B) As the stand-in for Nov 3, the only count nights the API still serves:
- (B1) Brazil first round, 2026-10-04: 90 markets in 6 linked series (first-round winner, margin buckets, vote-share ladders, outright win, advance, 2nd place). 280 packages that each pay a fixed minimum (identity, nested, exclusive and partition packages). Self-test: every package's actual payout at settlement was at least its stated minimum, PASS. The one cross was checked against the tape (s7_brazil.py, s8_verify_br.py).
- (B2) The Aug-Sep 2026 primary nights: every settled KXPRIMARYMOV / KXPRIMARYMOVD margin ladder (288 markets, 29 ladders, 11 poll-close times), from 3 hours before poll close to 21 hours after. Three tests:
  - In-ladder partition and nested-rung packages: 448 packages, self-test PASS (s11_mov_struct.py).
  - The idea's follow-on as a rule with no hindsight: once some bucket in the ladder is bid at least 50c and at least 30 minutes have passed since poll close, buy the favoured side of each leg the first minute its ask falls in a price band, and hold to certification. Fit on nights before Aug 15, holdout from Aug 15; t-stat taken across events (s10_calib.py; tight-spread version s13_calib_tight.py).
  - A hindsight ceiling on near-sure supply after the market had found the final margin (s6_mov_analyse.py, self-test PASS).
Nov 3 itself, and the Nov 2024 and Nov 2025 nights, cannot be measured (the API has purged them). Both recorders were writing at the end of the run (tape and feed files updated within seconds); 113 GB disk free; scratch folder 855 KB.

test.result:
FOLLOW-ON (the idea's money leg) LOSES. Buying the favoured side at 75-95c after the count had settled the ladder:
- 107 legs: won 72% (30 lost) against an average price paid of 87.8c, so -16.5c per contract.
- Average per event -16.7c (se 5.9c, t -2.84, 25 events). Fit -24.0c (9 events); holdout -12.6c (16 events).
- The opposite side also loses (-11.4c), because the average spread at those minutes was about 26c.
- Tight spreads only (6c or less): 23 legs in 12 events, won 87% against 90.2c paid, -3.8c per contract; average per event +4.1c +/- 5.1c. Fit -19.2c vs holdout +10.3c (12 of 12 won): the sign flips, it is not significant, and it is about 1 leg per night.
- Hindsight ceiling: after the market had found the final margin, 36 legs at least 5 points from the final margin, in 9 of 23 events, still offered the near-sure side at 95c or less. Only 10,337 contracts traded in those minutes in total (both sides), which is under about $30 per night even with perfect foresight.

STRUCTURAL PACKAGES:
- Control/combo: package B_RH (buy R-House YES + combo RR NO + combo RD NO, pays exactly $2) WAS positive after fees on 1,610 minute-updates across 8 days, Sep 9-21. The cause: the RR bid (Republican House AND Senate) at 0.16 sat above the R-House ask at 0.15. 76 runs, the longest 7.6 hours. Typical edge +0.38c to +0.56c per $2 set; best +1.52c (Sep 9, 16:01-16:51 UTC).
  - Only 90 of those minutes had all 3 legs refreshed within 2 minutes (best +0.59c).
  - None since Sep 21, which is why the hunter's 21-day window found none.
  - In the 260 minutes when a control price moved 1c or more, the best package was +0.59c.
- Brazil count night: 1 of 112 packages with quotes on every leg went positive, for one minute: +1.43c after fees on 5 legs, 26 minutes after polls closed, while the first-round winner's price ran from 33c to 62c in 15 minutes. The next minute the R1 bid had fallen from 41c to 38c.
- Primary nights: 6 of 391 such packages went positive, in 4 of 29 ladders, all during the fastest repricing:
  - Michigan Democratic Senate primary, 13-leg bucket set: asks summed to 0.87 at 01:04 UTC on Aug 5, worth +9c to +14.5c after fees for about 2 minutes.
  - FL-25 nested rungs: +5.4c and +2.6c, one minute each.
  - South Carolina first round: +2.6c.
  - Two more under +1c.
- Sizes cannot be measured: there are no historical order books, and the early-August trade tape has been purged.
test.artefact_checks:
- Self-tests: every package's actual payout at settlement was at least its stated minimum (Brazil 280 packages, primaries 448), PASS. Every leg flagged as near-sure in hindsight settled on its near-sure side, PASS.
- The Brazil cross was confirmed on the tape: trades printed at the crossed asks within that minute.
- The control/combo positives all trace to one quote pattern (RR bid 0.16 above the R-House ask 0.15) that sat unchanged for days. The oldest leg's quote was typically 23 minutes old, so most of those minutes are quotes nobody refreshed, not fresh crosses; only 90 were fresh.

- Fees: 0.07 x p x (1-p) per contract (standard fee, multiplier 1, on every series checked), unrounded, which is exact for 100-lot orders.
- The large negative follow-on number is partly a wide-spread effect (about 26c average spread at entry). The tight-spread subset is the fair test, and it shows no edge.
- Candles give only the end-of-minute quote: a cross inside a minute is invisible, and a cross at the end of a minute may have no size behind it.

idea.name: CPI index-level ladder vs YoY ladder (KXCPINDEX x KXCPIYOY): an exact, model-free pair -- hold to settlement only; depth unknown
markets: no index ladder is listed on 10-15; the Sep one was listed 08-16 for the 09-11 release (~4 weeks ahead)
idea.mechanism: 'YoY > T' is exactly 'NSA_m >= NSA_{m-12} x (1 + (T + 0.05)/100)', and NSA_{m-12} is public a year ahead: no seasonal ratio, no previous print needed, valid for the whole life of both ladders. Pair each YoY rung with the index rung within 0.15 points of its cut-off (the 0.05 grid keeps the band <= 0.025 points, ~1-3 in 100); value and buy exactly as N1-01 (worst-case value > +2c after both taker fees), take the thin index leg first, hold to settlement (selling back loses: see evidence).
idea.why_mispriced: The index ladder is a sleepy series (24 h volume 0 in the catalogue, OI 5,643) whose quotes nobody ties to the busy YoY ladder. Losers: whoever rests or lifts the index ladder's stale quotes.
idea.must_be_true: Size on the index side (unknown; thin). Held to settlement, the band (0.002-0.12 index points in-sample) must stay small enough that the per-pair edge covers it. The ladder keeps being listed (it was absent on 10-15).
idea.evidence_so_far: MEASURED (cpindex_pairs.out; 38 index rungs' hourly candles, Kalshi settled results): 38 package-days over Jul/Aug/Sep, conservative expected +$355, realised held to settlement +$437 on $3,363 spent at 100 pairs/day, 0 packages lost (says nothing about the band tail: 3 outcomes); by release: Jul 13 days +$195 held, Aug 19 days +$160, Sep 6 days +$82; e.g. 07-16 'YoY>3.4 NO 0.53 + index>334.2 YES 0.16' all-in 0.717 on a 0.008-point band; Sep 'YoY>3.6 YES + index>336.650 NO' all-in 0.86 on a 0.004-point band. Selling back 24 h before close: -$160 in total (Jul +$56, 10 of 13 positive; Aug -$147, 3 of 16; Sep -$69, 0 of 6) -- the index ladder's bids are too thin to exit. Candles carry no size; index-side depth is not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Depth-limited and unmeasured. If 100 pairs a day were really there: ~$140/month = ~$4.5/day; realistic on a thin index book $0.5-2/day at the current bank (a few hundred dollars in a subaccount) and about the same at $5,000 (depth, not bank, binds). Worst plausible day: the NSA print lands inside a 0.01-0.03-point band and the stack pays $0: -$100 to -$900 per release at 100 pairs/day.
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 print a month
idea.test_plan: Once a day, 1 unauthenticated call: GET /events?series_ticker=KXCPINDEX&status=open; when the next ladder lists, add its book WITH sizes to N1-01's hourly logger against KXCPIYOY. Pre-registered GO: >= 50 pairs at both touches with all-in <= 0.92 on a <= 0.03-point band on >= 3 days; then a 20-pair live test on the same subaccount as N1-01 with sign-off.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Not in the ledger or the carried index; SJ40's consistency scan covered same-family ladders, not this cross-series identity; the 09-25 sweep listed the index rungs as a watch item only.
idea.worst_case: A held stack inside the band pays $0 (the whole stake); a thin index leg filling without its YoY partner leaves a naked bet (take the thin leg first).

test.method:
Sources, best first: the Kalshi trade tape (/markets/trades plus /historical/trades), then hourly candles. No replay used.
(1) Checked the identity on every settled rung. 'YoY > T' holds exactly when NSA_m >= NSA_{m-12} x (1+(T+0.05)/100). Index 'above L' holds exactly when NSA_m >= L+0.001. The KXCPINDEX rules text confirms NSA (not seasonally adjusted). The YoY rules use the BLS one-decimal 12-month change.
(2) Pulled the full-life trade tape of all 76 rungs on the 3 settled index ladders: KXCPINDEX-26AUG12, 26SEP11 and 26OCT14 (the Jul, Aug and Sep 2026 prints). Also pulled the open Oct ladder. July trades sit behind the 2026-08-17 historical cutoff: /markets/trades returned only 49 of 1,012 of them, so they came from /historical/trades. Contracts now reconcile exactly to each market's volume_fp.
(3) Paired every index print with the complementary YoY leg on every YoY rung whose cut-off is within 0.15 index points.
- TAKER supply: someone bought our side; we could have bought it first.
- MAKER supply: someone sold our side into a resting bid. KXCPINDEX makers pay 0.
- The YoY leg is priced from the last hourly candle that closed before the print, so there is no look-ahead. It was then re-priced from the YoY trade tape (100 windows; nearest same-side trade within 15 min).
- A package qualifies at all-in <= 0.85, 0.90 or 0.95 (both prices plus taker fees), and must be P+ or have a P- band <= 0.03 points.
- Sweeps were split off and excluded. A sweep is a print >= 30c from the same rung's print within 5 min: a market order eating stale far offers.
- Positions are held to settlement and scored on Kalshi results, with per-day caps of 25 to 500 contracts.
- Holdout: the rule was set in advance (cap 0.90, band <= 0.03, hold); Sep is read out of sample.
(4) Competitor check: was the partner YoY side bought within 120 s after a qualifying index print?
(5) Live: pulled books with sizes on the open Oct index ladder and the Nov YoY ladder, and checked whether October has a YoY partner at all.
test.n_markets:
- 76 settled index rungs (18 Jul, 25 Aug, 33 Sep) plus 25 open Oct rungs.
- 144 rungs identity-checked (76 index + 68 YoY).
- 1,925 index prints (207,478 contracts) on the tape.
- 245 qualifying index prints at cap 0.95.
- 100 YoY tape windows.
test.n_independent_clusters: 3 releases (the Jul, Aug and Sep 2026 prints), so 3 outcomes. Supply is spread over 29 active days at cap 0.90.
test.result:
IDENTITY: 0 mismatches in 144 settled rungs.

EDGE (prices measured on the tape):
- Qualifying packages cost 0.62-0.90 all-in for a $1 floor.
- They realised 14-34c per contract.
- Every release was positive, including the Sep holdout.

SUPPLY other people actually traded at qualifying prices (cap 0.90, sweeps excluded):
- Jul: 476 taker + 2,115 maker contracts.
- Aug: 3,748 taker + 452 maker.
- Sep: 972 taker + 200 maker.

MONEY if we had captured 100% of that supply:
- Capped at <= 100 contracts/day: 29 active days, $1,628 spent, realised +$437 (expected +$409 after band risk), Jul 14 to Oct 14. That is $4.76 per calendar day (Jul +$107, Aug +$206, Sep +$124 holdout).
- Capped at <= 500/day: +$945, or $10.28/day.
- Riskless P+ only: cap 0.90 at <= 100/day +$167 ($1.81/day); cap 0.95 at <= 100/day +$243 ($2.64/day).
- Sweeps excluded from all of this: 3,981 contracts, +$2,284, almost all from August market orders. Buyers paid 0.90 and 0.45 for index YES on rungs the YoY ladder priced near 6c. That is a one-off windfall for whoever had far offers resting, not supply that repeats.

DECISIVE NEW FACTS:
(a) The open Oct-2026 index ladder (KXCPINDEX-26NOV10) has no YoY partner. KXCPIYOY-26OCT returns 404 because the Oct-2025 index was never published (FRED has no 2025-10). So nothing can be traded until the Nov-2026 index ladder lists. Recent ladders opened on the day of the previous print or a few days after it, so expect about Nov 10-11, running about 4 weeks to the Dec 10 print.
(b) A competitor has appeared. After 7 of 12 qualifying Sep index prints, someone bought the partner YoY side within 120 s in matching size. Example: 10-09 22:45 UTC, index NO x100, then YoY T3.6 YES x100.
(c) Index ladder volume fell from 96,539 contracts (Jul) and 101,509 (Aug) to 9,430 (Sep). The open Oct ladder now has a market maker quoting thousands at 1c spreads on the wing rungs. The central rungs, where the pairs sit, show only 1-2 contracts at the best price.
test.artefact_checks:
- Units: prices read from *_dollars fields, never inferred from magnitude.
- Identity: 0 of 144 mismatches. NSA confirmed in the rules text; the YoY one-decimal rule confirmed.
- Tape completeness: the July tape was 95% missing on /markets/trades (historical cutoff 2026-08-17). Fixed with /historical/trades; totals now reconcile exactly to volume_fp on all 76 rungs.
- YoY leg pricing: re-priced on its own tape, tape minus candle has median -1c (10th/90th percentile -4c/+1c), so the candle price is not flattering. Only 74 of 245 qualifying prints had a same-side YoY trade within 15 min; the rest use the candle close.
- No look-ahead: the YoY quote comes from the candle closed before each index print.
- Sweeps (market orders eating stale offers) were separated; left in, they would have tripled August.
- No double counting: each index print counted once, with its cheapest partner.
- Not checkable: resting index offers that never traded do not appear on the tape. The hunter's candles show cheap offers sat for days, sizes unknown. So the tape number is a floor on offered supply but a ceiling on what we would get, because every contract counted was taken by someone else.
test.supply_we_would_get:
The thin leg is KXCPINDEX; the deep leg is same-month KXCPIYOY (hundreds to thousands of contracts at the best price).

Over 3 releases, others took about 1,200-4,200 qualifying contracts per release at cap 0.90 (sweeps excluded). At <= 100/day that is about 550 contracts per release.

Our share is NOT measured. An automated arb was visibly active in Sep, and maker fills need queue priority. Assuming 30-50% capture: about 150-300 contracts per release at 10-20c each, or roughly $30-80 per release. 11 of the next 12 months can be paired; October 2026 cannot.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 until about Nov 10-11, because the open Oct ladder has no partner. Averaged over a year after that: about $1.5-2.5/day central. That is $4.76/day at 100% capture of the measured <= 100/day supply, times 30-50% capture, times 11/12 pairable months. Riskless P+ only: about $0.6-1.2/day. Needs about $300-800 locked for 2-4 weeks per release in a subaccount.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $3-5/day: <= 500/day measured $10.28/day at 100% capture, times 30-50%, times 11/12. Depth, not bank, is the limit. Peak capital lock is about $2,000.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
The edge comes straight from both legs' traded or quoted prices, not from outcomes, so it does not need many settlements. Realised edge was 14-34c per contract, within 0-7% of the expected value after band risk.

What 3 outcomes cannot detect is how often a print lands in the band. 0 losses in 3 is consistent with a rate as high as about 63% (95% bound). That risk rests instead on the exact identity plus print density: about 1.5 per index point times bands of 0.004-0.028 points, or about 0.6-4% per P- release.
test.worst_case:
The main risk is one print landing inside a P- band, which zeroes that pair's stake. Measured P- stakes at <= 100/day:
- Jul: $282 (band 0.008)
- Aug: $441 (bands 0.022-0.028)
- Sep: $300 (band 0.004)

So the worst plausible release loses about $300-450 (roughly 1-4 releases in 100), against the +$107 to +$206 a release earns. Restricting to P+ (riskless) packages removes the band loss entirely, at about half the money.

Smaller risks:
- Legging: the index leg fills and the YoY ladder moves before the hedge. Small at 43 ms on a deep YoY book.
- Resting index bids get picked off when the YoY ladder jumps; the bot must re-quote on every YoY move.
- Capital is tied up 2-4 weeks.
- The competitor takes the cheap offers first. That means zero fills, not a loss.
test.next_test:
Recorder, no money.
- Trigger: once a day, call GET /events?series_ticker=KXCPINDEX&status=open. When KXCPINDEX-26DEC10 (the Nov-2026 index) lists, expected about Nov 10-11 ET, start recording.
- What to record: both ladders' books with sizes, until the Dec 10 8:30 AM ET print. That is the ~25 index rungs plus the ~6 KXCPIYOY-26NOV rungs whose cut-offs fall inside the index strike range (base is the Nov-2025 NSA, 324.122). Use the WebSocket orderbook_delta feed, or REST every 60 s.
- Pre-registered GO: >= 500 contracts of qualifying packages that stayed on the book >= 2 s, on >= 5 distinct days. A package qualifies at all-in <= 0.90 after both taker fees, and must be P+ or have a P- band <= 0.03 points. Size is the smaller of the two legs' displayed sizes. Also count how often packages vanish within 2 s (the competitor).
- If GO: a micro-live test of 20-50 pairs on a subaccount with sign-off, P+ only first, index leg first, then the YoY leg.
- If under 200 contracts: dead on depth.
- Add it to results/READS_DUE.json, due 2026-12-10.

refs.strongest_objection:
I could not refute it on supply or competition. On those points my own data is better for the idea than the tester's 30-50% capture assumption. It has two execution problems the tester did not price.

(1) THE TWO LEGS SETTLE UNDER DIFFERENT RULES IF THE RELEASE IS DELAYED.
- KXCPINDEX, under its ECONSTAT terms, expires at the latest 7 days after the scheduled date (KXCPINDEX-26NOV10: 2026-11-17) and has no shutdown clause. If no value can be determined, 'Kalshi has the right to determine payouts' (Rule 6.3(b)), with Trading Economics as the fallback source.
- KXCPIYOY instead waits up to 6 months after a shutdown ends (KXCPIYOY-26NOV latest expiration 2027-03-11).
- Government funding runs only to 2026-12-11. The Nov window (Dec 10 print) is inside that. The Dec-data window (Jan 13 print) is not: a funding lapse during December data collection would repeat Oct 2025, when the index was never published.
- In that case the index leg settles at Kalshi's discretion within a week while the YoY leg waits. The exact identity breaks, and an 'index YES + YoY NO' package becomes a naked YoY bet.
- So a riskless P+ package is riskless only while BLS publishes on time, and the tester's '11 of 12 months pairable' overstates it.

(2) AT TODAY'S BANK, MONEY IS THE LIMIT, NOT DEPTH OR COMPETITION, AND IT EARNS NO MORE PER DOLLAR THAN THE MAIN ACCOUNT.
- With $300-400 tied up per release, the tape gives Sep +$117-129 (1.1-1.3% per dollar per day held) and Aug +$43-58 (0.6%).
- The main account made +$220 over 10-01..10-16 ET in the Kalshi ledger (about $14/day on about $1,150, about 1.2%/day).
- Taking $300-400 out of the main pool shrinks pin's bet size (bank/11.76). If pin scales with the bank, that costs about $4-5/day, as much as or more than the pair earns.
- So the trade only adds money if it is funded with new or idle cash. Whether pin's P&L scales with the bank is not measured.

Sep (the holdout) qualifying taker packages at all-in <= 0.90: 822 contracts, $658 cost, +$164 realised. Maker-side supply added 200 contracts, +$34.

DECISIVE: every Sep qualifying package had sat on the book at <= 0.90 on both legs for 412-874 minutes before anyone took it. In Aug the wait was 0-564 minutes, median about 147. So there is no speed race; checking once a minute would have seen all of it.

In the 1-10 minutes after a print the YoY ask moved 0c on average in Sep and -0.15 to +0.07c in Aug, so the risk of being left with one leg filled is negligible.

refs.strongest_objection:
Not refuted, because the edge is real. I checked the rule linking the two ladders myself: 0 of 144 settled rungs broke it. I also re-priced the YoY leg from my own 1-minute candles, using the price at the minute of each index trade instead of an hourly candle up to 2 h old. The packages were still there at almost the same prices.

There are two weaknesses.

(1) The tester's starting number is about 25% too high: $409 expected, or $4.76/day at 100% capture, against my $336, or $3.66/day.
- Their 100-a-day limit is filled cheapest-first, which uses hindsight.
- Their filter for one-off market orders (sweeps) is looser.
- They quote realised money, which includes luck, rather than expected money.

(2) Everything rests on 3 releases, and the trend is down.
- Index ladder volume fell from about 100,000 contracts in Jul and Aug to 9,430 in Sep.
- An arb bot is now visible. In Sep, after 3 of 8 qualifying taker trades, someone bought the matching YoY side within 120 s; at nearby control times that happens 2 times in 100. In Jul the same happened after 8 of 20 maker fills (control: also 2 in 100).
- A market maker now quotes the open Oct ladder.
- Index-side depth beyond what others traded is not measured, so our share is unmeasured.
- Nothing can trade until the Nov-2026 index ladder lists, about Nov 10-11 ET.

idea.name: Opening-minute taker on the 15-min crypto series (at 840 s to close, take when fair - ask - fee >= 3c)
merged_from: crypto-15m-new-angles: Opening-minute taker: the first displayed book versus the index move since the strike
idea.mechanism: The strike is the previous settle and the first book appears a median 61-76 s after the open (90th pct 114 s), by which time the index has moved a median 6.5 sigma from the strike. At 60 s after the open (840 s to close) take YES when fair - ask - fee >= 3c (mirror on NO), hold to settlement.
idea.why_mispriced: WEAK: opening quotes may come from slow default quoters, but the book leads the CF index half the time.
idea.must_be_true: The opening quotes must be posted by slow quoters, not makers who see exchange spot first. Best of ~70 cells; fresh-quote t 1.2-1.6; the take at the very first quote shows nothing (+0.6c fit, -1.3c test). The model is over-confident beyond ~8 min (fair 0.868 realises less at 780 s), which works against a model-based taker at 840 s.
idea.evidence_so_far: Tape: grid.csv.gz at tau 840/870 both halves; YES 3c edge fit +4.7c on 296 markets (t 1.5), test +6.8c on 418 (t 2.8); fresh quotes only at 2c +3.1c / +3.3c (t 1.2 / 1.6); NO 2c +3.4c / +1.1c; by coin pooled 2c: BNB +9.6c (142 mk), DOGE +6.4c, NEAR +5.4c, SOL +4.8c, HYPE -2.2c, ZEC -0.5c, XRP 0, BTC +1.1c; touch 37-40 contracts; 25-35 firings/day. Taker rules on the model at 60-300 s FAIL the holdout at every threshold.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Tape upper bound 30/day x 20 contracts x 3c = $18/day; realistic $0-5/day at $1,155; ~$0-15 at $5,000. Worst day at 20 contracts: five full losses, -$60.
idea.settlements_per_day: 864 markets/day; ~30 firings/day
idea.test_plan: Re-score on the next 3 weeks of tape (scan15m.py, fresh quotes only, cell frozen as YES/NO >= 3c at 840 s): bar >= +2c/contract with t >= 2 on markets not used to choose it; only then a 1-contract live arm 14 days (fill >= 50%, >= +2c over >= 150 fills, kill at -$15).
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No ledger row looks at the window open; the 61-76 s no-book fact is new.
idea.worst_case: At 20 contracts five full losses in a day, -$60; at 1 contract -$3.

test.method: Holdout on tape no one had looked at. The hunter picked the cell (840 s to close, fresh quote <= 2 s old, take YES/NO when model fair beats the touch by >= 3c after fee, hold to settlement) from about 70 cells on 09-01..10-12. I re-scanned 2026-10-13T00Z..2026-10-16T13Z (the PC was off 10-14 03Z..10-15 04Z) with open840.py. It subclasses the hunter's scan15m.py, so the same live-model fair (engine.var_factor, 600 s trailing sigma, effective strike) comes from imported code, and its self-test passed. It also records the quote 250 ms and 1 s later and when our collector first saw each market. score840.py (planted-answer self-test passes) scores the frozen rule clustered by close. It also fits the whole-population regression (y - mid) = a + b(fair - mid) over every market quoted at 840 s, which has far more power than the firings alone. diag840.py: within-close regression, the rule with other coins' same-close move removed (drift check), neighbouring taus. subsplit.py: split by our subscription time. Source: the trade tape and quote tape (ticker channel) plus the 1/sec CF index; no replay, no live fills (nothing of ours ever traded at 840 s). Files: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-11/ (RESULT.json, score840.txt, diag840.txt, subsplit.txt, new/open840.csv.gz).
test.n_markets: Holdout: 1,753 markets quoted at 840 s, 212 fired. In-sample (hunter's 09-01..10-12): 14,597 quoted, 1,510 fired.
test.n_independent_clusters: Holdout: 228 closes (103 with a firing). In-sample: 2,072 closes (914 with a firing). The 9 coins share each close, so the close is the cluster.
test.result: FROZEN RULE, holdout 10-13..10-16: -6.17c per contract, t -1.75, n 212 markets / 103 closes. YES side +1.71c (t 0.34, n 94); NO side -12.45c (t -2.57, n 118). Every holdout day was negative (avg per firing): 10-13 -0.8c over 103, 10-14 (3 h) -8.0c over 17, 10-15 -10.5c over 45, 10-16 -13.1c over 47. In-sample, same code: fit +4.93c t 2.21 (590); test +4.08c t 2.37 (920); pooled +4.41c t 3.23 (1,510 / 914 closes). The holdout sits 2.8 standard errors below the in-sample number. Pre-registered bar (>= +2c with t >= 2 on unseen markets): FAILED. Other thresholds in the holdout: 0c -3.2c, 1c -1.1c, 2c -2.4c, 5c -6.9c, 8c -3.9c; all negative. By coin, 8 of 9 negative. Neighbouring times, holdout: 810 s -3.4c (n 287), 780 s -1.9c (n 350), 870 s -22.7c (n 18). POPULATION REGRESSION (every quoted market): in-sample b = +0.56 (se 0.15, t 3.75; within-close +0.49, t 4.25), meaning the model's disagreement with the book carried about half-weight information. Holdout b = -0.16 (se 0.43) and within-close -0.25 (se 0.34): no information. The in-sample b implies only about +2.0c per contract for this rule, not +4.4c, so the selected cell was inflated about 2x even before the holdout.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Pipeline: open840.py reproduces the hunter's runB2 grid exactly on 1,346 overlapping markets (10-11..10-12): fair, bid, ask, result and firing all agree, with the same +5.09c on that window. So the holdout used the in-sample measurement, unchanged. (2) Settlement: our computed settle agrees with Kalshi's 'determined' result on 2,058 of 2,058 holdout markets. (3) The idea's mechanism is FALSE. 'First book appears 61-76 s after open' comes from OUR collector: it polls REST every 30 s and only then subscribes. On 10-15 12Z the first ticker message and the orderbook_snapshot arrive together at 25-27 s or 56-58 s after open, at that cadence. The market has a book before we subscribe. (4) Is the in-sample gain a subscription-snapshot artefact? No: it shows in every first-seen bucket (0-20 s +8.8c, 20-35 s +2.3c, 35-50 s +4.7c, 50-56 s +3.7c, 56-60 s +7.0c), and the holdout is negative in every bucket. (5) Drift: the holdout had a broad up-move. Across all markets, y - mid averaged +4.0c to +5.7c on every holdout day, against a median -1.3c on in-sample days. With the other coins' same-close move removed, the rule is -7.8c, t -3.57. Drift does not explain the failure. (6) Fill-ability: 207 of 212 fired quotes were still at that price 250 ms later and 155 of 212 one second later; median touch 61 contracts. Execution is not the problem; the price is. Recorders were still writing at 14:25Z; disk 112 GB free.

Sources: the live order books and the public trade tape (rank 1-2 for this question, because the money is a reward paid on resting size, so the book is the primary source). test.result:
THE MONEY IS REAL AND MUCH BIGGER THAN THE IDEA SAID, BUT BIG STACKS ALREADY HOLD IT, AND IT IS A ONE-WEEK ONE-OFF.
(a) Pots (measured). Dec rungs: $160 each for 10-15 17:51Z..10-23 03:59Z = $21.56/day a rung. Jan rungs: $80 each for 10-15 18:01Z..10-18 04:00Z = $33.1/day a rung. The first Jan period ($160 a rung, 10-13 23:02Z..10-15 17:48Z) shows paid_out=true, so these programs do pay. Total $273/day on the series, and one side can earn at most half. Target 1,000 a side, discount 0.5 a tick. No later period is listed (0 upcoming).
(b) Who holds the share now. On 9 of 10 rungs one NO stack at the best NO price takes 100% of the NO side: Dec T1000 42,761 at 1c, T1500 23,561 at 3c, T1750 9,460 at 6c; Jan T1000 14,896 at 3c, T1500 10,000 at 4c; 3,415-7,053 on the near rungs. These stacks were built overnight: Dec T1000 NO went from 3,741 (21:43Z 10-15) to 42,761 (12:37Z 10-16), and Dec T1500 from 500 to 23,561. On the YES side a two-sided market maker with 1,620-2,713-lot bids holds 93-100%.
(c) Static value of stepping 1c above the cheap-side stack with 1,000 contracts (the walk then stops at our level and the stack scores 0): $10.78/day per Dec rung, $16.56/day per Jan rung. The 6 far NO sides (T1000/T1500/T1750 on both dates) = $82/day on $300 of collateral, $290 over the rest of the programs. The 3 cheapest (Dec T1000 at 2c, Dec T1500 at 4c, Jan T1000 at 4c) = $38/day on $100, $167 in total. Joining the stack at its price instead gets only 2-10% of a side ($0.25-1.51/day a rung).
(d) The deciding unknown is how fast incumbents react, and the record points both ways.
- Slow: the far-rung NO stacks did not move in the whole 116-minute record, and Jan T1000 NO has sat at 3c since 10-14 00:58Z. A natural experiment on Jan T1750: at 12:53-12:56Z the market maker grew its 7c NO from 735.71 to 1,091.98, just over the 1,000 target, which cut the 36,000-lot stack at 4c to zero share. That stack did not respond for at least 97 minutes.
- Fast: the near rungs do step up. At 14:08-14:13Z new orders of 5,150 at 11c (Dec T2000) and 4,700 at 20c (Dec T2250) appeared 1c above the old 10c/19c stacks, with zero trades. The market maker rescaled all its Jan quotes by about 35% within one 3-minute window. On the LoL Worlds new-listing pots (tester R3-M-04), stacks stepped up within 60 s.
(e) If an incumbent re-joins our price with its full stack, our share falls to 2-10%. The 3 cheapest sides then earn $7.6 in total (re-join after 1 h), $12 (after 4 h), $24 (12 h) or $43 (24 h). The 6 sides earn $19 / $29 / $55 / $93.
(f) Fills. Since listing (2.6 days) there have been 13 organic trades, 65 contracts, across all 10 rungs; 20 of those contracts were buyers taking YES on far rungs. There were ZERO trades on any rung from 10-16 00:00Z to 14:35Z. The other 250,500 contracts are three 83,500 blocks at 19:45Z 10-15, printed at 44c/60c/76c YES, far below the book at that time: a negotiated block, not book flow. Fees: the series is quadratic, so makers pay 0.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Units: period_reward /10000 = dollars (1,600,000 = $160.00); target_size_fp read directly (the hunter's 'target None' came from reading the wrong field name). (2) The walk was self-tested on 6 planted books, covering the stop-at-target, the target/5 reference and the excluded-side cases. A hand-check of Jan T1750 (735.71 x1 + 50 x0.25 + 36,000 x0.125, giving shares of 14.0% / 0.2% / 85.7%) matches the script. (3) The 'counted seconds' condition (both sides >= 1,000 in total) holds on all 10 rungs only because of 1c filler orders (1,100-2,113 YES at 1c, 1,200 NO at 1c). If those are pulled, YES sides such as Dec T1750 (only 491 contracts above 1c) fall under target and every second is excluded for everyone. That is a real risk to any credit and is not modelled. (4) The idea's '250k volume' is three negotiated 83,500 blocks, not book supply. (5) 'paid_out=true' shows the period was paid to someone; it does not show how much or to whom. (6) The static shares assume nobody reacts; they are an upper bound and are labelled that way everywhere. (7) Fair NO for the far rungs is NOT measured (SMM is paywalled); the fill-cost range (0-5c a contract over fair) is an assumption. (8) The 36,000-lot stack's non-reaction is one observation (n = 1), not a distribution of reaction times. (9) Recorders: C:/kals/kalshi_data/ticker and C:/kals/feed_data/bitstamp were still being written at 13:18Z (last write 9:18:40 AM ET, about 2 minutes before the check). Basis: the 3 cheapest far NO sides (Dec T1000 at 2c, Dec T1500 at 4c, Jan T1000 at 4c; $100 collateral) with an incumbent re-joining after about 12 hours = $24 in total. If they re-join within 1 hour: $8 in total (about $1/day). If they never re-join: $167 (the upper bound, about $26/day). Cash does not bind at the current bank (tester R1-N2-02), so the 6-side version ($300 collateral) is also possible: $55 in total at a 12-hour re-join (about $8/day).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $8/day for the remaining week: the 6 far NO sides ($300 collateral) at a 12-hour re-join = $55 in total. A bigger bank does not help much, because the binding limit is the incumbents' size and speed, not our cash. The YES side is not counted: joining the market maker's best bid with 1,000 would get about 95% of that side on a static book ($10-16/day a rung), but it needs $730-960 of collateral a rung and faces a market maker that rescales its quotes within minutes.
test.worst_case: A deliberate buyer takes our whole 1,000 NO on a far rung and APT does not crash: we lose that rung's collateral, $20 (Dec T1000 at 2c) to $80 (Jan T1750 at 8c). The expected cost of a full fill is smaller (fair NO is maybe 0.3-7c, not measured). Worst plausible day: -$40 (one $40 side filled, no credit received yet). All six filled at once: -$300, which is implausible since nobody has bought YES on a far rung since 10-14. Separate risk: if the 1c filler orders that keep both sides at 1,000 are pulled, every second is excluded and the credit is $0 while our collateral still sits there.

Timing matters: the Dec period ends 10-23 03:59Z (10-22 11:59 PM ET) and the Jan one ends 10-18 04:00Z.
(1) FREE, start now: a 1-minute read-only recorder of all 10 KXAPTROT books (10 GETs/min) until 10-23 04:00Z. test.smallest_detectable_effect: The shares and pot dollars are exact under the filed rule (the same walk matched a real payment to 98.5-98.9%). What is still open is reaction time. The 5-minute recorder could not see a re-join faster than 5 minutes, and the one natural experiment (n = 1) only says that one stack took at least 97 minutes. A micro-live credit is read to the cent, so a single period can tell getting 50% of the model's credit apart from getting 5%.

refs.strongest_objection:
The $4/day is not a measurement. It is the 12-hour point on a curve that runs from $0.5/day to $25/day, and one unmeasured parameter sets where we land: how fast a far-rung NO stack reacts once someone bids above it. Three problems.

(1) The tester's PASS bar ('median far-rung re-join >= 4 h' from a passive recorder) depends on an event that almost never happens. On the far rungs someone bid above a standing stack once in 2.6 days (Jan T1000 at 4c, 10-15 10:28Z-19:46Z, 9 h 18 min, and the 3c stack never re-joined), and not since 10-15 19:46Z; my 42-minute 1-minute recorder saw 0 such events. The incumbents that did lose their share never responded: Jan T1750 4c x36,000 for >= 143 min, Dec T2000 10c x5,112 and Dec T2250 19c x4,111 for >= 66 min. So a recorder only produces '>=' times, never a median, before the programs end. Only the micro-live test can measure this.

(2) The rational answer to us is not re-joining with the whole stack (which leaves us 2.3-6.3%). It is 1,000 contracts one tick above us ($30 of collateral on Dec T1000), which leaves us 0. That makes the 12 h case $20.16, not $24.31.

(3) Fill cost is set to about 0, but the project's only live far-side reward quote (09-26 KXTENCENTSHARE, 1,000 at 1c) was filled after 1 h 40 min for -$10. Here a full fill costs nearly the whole collateral, because public APT prints are $2,500-3,250/mtu against strikes of $1,000/$1,500. That is -$20 to -$40 a side, which wipes out 2-10 days of the realistic credit.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's $4/day assumes the stack holder takes about 12 h to answer and then only re-joins our price, so we keep 2-10%. My own data point the other way.

(1) How fast others answer. In the first Jan period (pot then $45/day a side), the best NO bid on the Jan rungs was stepped 1c->2c->3c->4c in batches across all rungs, 72 then 25 minutes apart (my 1-minute candles, 10-13 23:45Z..10-14 01:23Z). Today the market maker keeps its Jan T1750 7c NO at 1,082-1,092, just over the 1,000 target, and topped it back up within 6 minutes (15:01Z->15:07Z). At 14:10Z a farmer cancelled about 1,941 at 10c and 1,127 at 19c and re-posted 5,150 at 11c and 4,700 at 20c. Both of them understand the reward rule.

(2) Someone who understands the rule does not re-join. They step one tick above us with 1,000 or more, and our share goes to 0. Add the $1.00 minimum payout per market per period and the 0.9 payment calibration, and a hold under about 2.5 h earns $0 on that rung.

(3) Resting exactly 1,000 breaks easily. The only YES buying on the far rungs since listing came in about $10 lots (Jan T1000: 2 x 10.09 at 97c on 10-14). A 10-contract fill drops our share from 100% to 4.4% (Dec T1000) or 7.8% (Dec T1500), because the reward count then runs on into the big stack one tick below at half weight. Our bid is above fair, so buying 11 contracts from us to knock us out is profitable for anyone. Fix: rest 1,200 or more and top back up.

(4) Timing. The Jan programs end 10-18 04:00Z (Sat 10-17 midnight ET), 37 h after my pull. After sign-off and a build, little of Jan is left, so only the Dec rungs count.

(5) Kalshi changes pots. The first Jan period ended at 17:48:09Z 10-15, minutes before a half-size $80 period replaced it. Whether that was an early cut is not known.

What still argues for the idea. No far-rung NO price has moved in 19 h (since 10-15 19:46Z). Stacks that someone outbid at the top have stayed put: the 36,000 at 4c on Jan T1750 has not answered for at least 2 h 33 min, and the 10c and 19c stacks have not answered the 14:10Z step-up for at least 79 min. The market maker does not quote NO on Dec T1000 or T1500, so to step over us there it would have to price above its own fair value. So how fast the far rungs answer is still not measured. Only a micro-live probe can measure it, with these fixes: rest 1,200 not 1,000, top back up after any fill, and drop the Jan rungs.

idea.name: VoteHub generic-ballot daily ladder (KXVHGCB): buy the 'unchanged from yesterday' bucket in the first hours after listing (WEAK, 10 days)
markets: KXVHGCB (VoteHub D-R generic ballot margin, exact 0.1-point buckets, ~8k contracts/day)
idea.mechanism: Each day's KXVHGCB ladder lists 14:01Z (10:01 AM ET) and closes 21:04Z the next day (fixed close: exp - close = 0.02 h on all 178 markets, no early closes). In the first 1-6 h, if the bucket equal to yesterday's settled value is offered at <= 35c, buy it (taker, fee <= 1.6c) up to the depth shown; hold to settlement.
idea.why_mispriced: The new day's book starts as 1c/2c seed quotes for 1-3 h, then 10-27c wide with ~1.6% of the day's volume in the first 6 h; whoever posts the early asks prices a change that usually does not happen (the time-weighted average moves only when new polls land).
idea.must_be_true: (1) Persistence >= 55% through the midterm run-in (more polls = more changes). (2) Real depth at <= 35c -- the 1-2c asks were 1-3 contracts, and those seed asks supply most of the +24c average. (3) The fixed close holds (checked).
idea.evidence_so_far: 10 consecutive days 10-04..10-14: the unchanged bucket won 6 of 10; open-hour asks 2, 2, 2, 23, 34, 88, 99, 99, 2, 2c; asks 12 h later 28-78c; taker P&L at the open ask +24c per contract on average; the market's implied median beat 'same as yesterday' on 0 of 9 days (miss 0.146 vs 0.078 points). Hourly candles only, no depth. KXTRUMPAPPROVE same test: 4 of 11, +0.8c = nothing.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $10-40/day if 50-200 contracts are really offered at <= 35c and persistence holds; ~$0 if the depth is the 1-3 seed contracts. Same at $5,000 (depth-capped). Worst plausible day: 200 contracts at 30c lost = -$60 (cap risk at $60/day until 20 days logged). After Nov 3 the series may lose interest.
idea.test_plan: 20 days read-only: GET the KXVHGCB orderbook at listing +1 h, +3 h, +6 h (3 calls/day); log ask depth on yesterday's bucket and the result. Pre-registered bar: persistence >= 55%, mean fillable ask <= 40c with >= 50 contracts, net >= +10c per contract.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No ledger row measured the VoteHub opening-hours mispricing; carried lip-economics proposed quoting the Trump-approval ATM strike for the reward pot, a different series and mechanism.
idea.worst_case: A poll-heavy week: -$60 a day at 200 contracts.
idea.prior_reason: n=10 days, the headline +24c is mostly 1-3-contract seed asks, one settlement a day so 20 days to decide, and the series may die after Nov 3.

(2) Full public Kalshi trade tape of all 196 KXVHGCB markets (22 events, 21 settled, 09-25..10-15, 12,521 prints). Rules tested: (a) the idea as written: buy 'yesterday's value' at <=35c in the first 1-6 h after listing; (b) the same with no lookahead (bucket = the value readable at listing +1 h); (c) the fixable version: buy the unchanged bucket after yesterday settles, filtered by weekday, with weekday rates fit on VoteHub Jan-Jul 2026 and tested on Aug-Oct 2026 (holdout), then scored on the tape; (d) a check of the repricing bursts.
