test.result:
1) THE IDEA'S CHEAP OPENING ASKS ARE DUST. Live book of the new 26OCT17 ladder: at +3 and +15 min every strike is 1c bid / 99c ask. At +35 min the 'yes ask 2-3c' on every strike is a 0.01-contract order; the next real ask on the unchanged bucket (E8.1) is 94c for 10 contracts, then 98c. Tape: in the first hour after listing, 52 contracts traded at <=35c on the unchanged bucket over 19 days (8 of them at <=5c).
2) THE IDEA LOOKS AHEAD. Since 10-03 the ladder lists at 10:01 AM ET and yesterday settles at 5:04 PM ET, 7 h later. So 'yesterday's settled value' is not public in the 1-6 h window. On 6 of 18 days the bucket the market favoured at listing +1 h was not that value.
3) NO-LOOKAHEAD OPENING RULE: bucket won 9/18 days. 2,657 contracts traded at <=35c in listing +1..6 h, +35.8c per contract weighted by contracts. But 7,100c and 6,400c of the ~+12,800c (at a 100/day cap) came from 10-08 and 10-10, both inside the one calm run. The days before the hunter's window (09-26..10-03) are a holdout: 1 day with fills, which lost (501 contracts, -6c).
4) BASE RATE FROM THE FEED: in 2026 the 0.1-rounded margin was the same as the day before 46.2% of days (Jan-Jul, n 212, se 3.4) and 45.5% in the holdout (Aug-Oct, n 77). In 2025 it was 76%, so polls are now more frequent. The Kalshi window ran luckier: 10/19 = 53%. The market prices the unchanged bucket at about 37-46c (average price over each window after yesterday settles), so a no-filter buyer's expected edge is about 0 to +5c, minus a 1.7c fee.
5) WEEKDAY EFFECT IS REAL IN THE FEED: days settling Sat/Sun/Mon stay the same 59% (fit) / 61% (holdout, n 33); Tue-Fri 37% / 34% (n 44). On the KXVHGCB tape, weekend days priced 39-46c on average (won 5 of 8). But at the bar (<=54c), the cheap supply came mostly on losing days: 5 weekend days had fills, 2 won and 3 lost, about -$46 net at a 100/day cap.
6) A DEEPER MARKET ALREADY PRICES IT: on KXTRUMPAPPROVE (50x the volume) the Saturday unchanged bucket trades 66-72c (won 5/6) and Thu/Fri 16-22c (won 1/7, 1/6). Buying the unchanged bucket every day: -2.5c (se 7.1, 41 days) and -4.0c (se 7.0, 43 days). The weekday rule on the holdout half: -18.6c (8 days) and -10.6c (9 days).
7) KXVHGCB buy-every-day at the average price after settlement: +14.3c (se 10.8, 17 days) and +18.4c (se 12.2, 14 days). Neither is significant; both are consistent with the calm run and the feed's 46%.
8) Adjacent, not this idea: buying after a repricing jump (<50c to >=70c; 22 jumps on 11 days) made +8.5c in the first 2 min, -1.1c at 2-10 min, +9.0c at 10-30 min. That is noise; 6 of the 22 jumps reversed.
test.artefact_checks: Lookahead: the hunter's 'unchanged' bucket uses a value that settles 7 h after the window. Re-measured with the value readable at the time; the edge falls into one calm run. Dust quotes: the live book shows the 2-3c asks are 0.01 contracts, so the hunter's '+24c at the open ask' (from hourly candles) is an artefact of dust quotes. Winner selection: the first burst count used only eventual winners (+43.7c); without that selection it falls to +8.5c / -1.1c. Feed revisions: VoteHub's daily series disagrees with Kalshi's 5:05 PM ET settled value on 2 of 20 days (09-25, 09-30), either revision or end-of-day timing, so the feed's 46% is approximate (the tape-only figure is 53%, n 19). VoteHub's public poll API (api.votehub.com/polls) is incomplete (4 polls since 09-10) and was not used. A scratch file named inspect.py shadowed the standard library and broke kauth; it was renamed and rerun, and no results changed. Self-tests in analyze.py and analyze2.py pass. Price unit taken from the yes_price_dollars field name (x100), never from magnitude.

Tape: 52 contracts at <=35c in the first hour over 19 days (about 3 a day), and 2,657 in +1..6 h, mostly on 2 days. Fixable weekend version after settlement at <=54c: 5 of 8 weekend days had any fill, sizes 4-1,118 contracts, mostly on days it lost. The series likely ends Nov 3 (VoteHub's generic-ballot average lists end_date 2026-11-03), so at most 9 more weekend settlement days.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0. The opening-hours rule has nothing real to buy, and its paper edge needs data that is not public yet. Best case for the weekend version, if VoteHub's 60% holds and the market keeps charging about 42c: about 100 contracts x 16c x 3 days a week = about $7/day average, only until Nov 3. Not measured as real; the tape's weekend fills lost money (about -$46 on 5 days) and the deeper RCP ladder shows the effect gets priced.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0. Depth, not cash, is the limit; a bigger bank changes nothing.

KXTRUMPAPPROVE (43 days): about 14c. Feed persistence rate: about 7 points (fit) and 11 points (holdout). A 15c weekend edge would need about 44 weekend days (about 15 weeks). idea.name: XRP/BNB photo-finish entry guard: refuse an entry when the projected settle is within 2 rounding steps of the strike (insurance unaffected)
merged_from: crypto-15m-new-angles: XRP/BNB photo-finish guard (R16 measured): treat a projected settle within 2 rounding steps of the strike as a coin flip
idea.mechanism: When the projected settle (locked prints + spot) is within 2 rounding steps of the strike (XRP step $0.0001, BNB $0.01), refuse the entry; insurance stays allowed (standing rule). Money = losses avoided where the 60-s mean lands on the strike's rounding boundary.
idea.why_mispriced: n/a -- lose-less. The settle lands within ONE rounding step of the strike in 0.8 of 100 markets overall, but 4.9 of 100 XRP markets (94 of 1,908) and BNB 1.4/100; BTC, SOL, HYPE, ZEC never. XRP's 1-s index sigma is only 5-9 steps.
idea.must_be_true: The losses in the class must be visible at ENTRY (R10, dead: a 1/2/3-tick margin floor removed 0 of 20 measured losses 09-09..09-27; all had >= 5.9 ticks projected at entry). At the live gate the class is small (17 of 16,202 markets with model >= 99.5% at 20 s ended within 1 step; 1 lost on the tape).
idea.evidence_so_far: photofinish.py over the index + lifecycle channels 09-22..10-12 (17,172 markets; computed settle = Kalshi's on 34,046 of 34,047; the one miss a DOGE tie at the 7th digit); pf/photofinish.jsonl. Named live loss: XRP 09-30 19:15 ET, Kalshi money -$42.60 net of insurance (the hunter's -$84.65 is the bet leg): C1 read of live_markets -- full leg at tau 20, ask seen 88c, 89 filled at 94.76c (sweep), strike 1.4890, spot 1.48927 = 2.7 steps above at the send, logged fair 1.0, sellers 56%; insurance 89 NO at 51c at belief 0.39 (also F19's dump-then-buy case). Whether its projection (not spot) was within 2 steps is not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Lose-less only: at most one $40-85 loss avoided a month at current size (~$1-2/day ceiling), $0 if the class is invisible at entry as R10 found; skipped-win cost ~$1-2/month. Worst day: none in money (code risk only).
idea.settlements_per_day: 192 XRP+BNB markets/day; the rule would fire on ~1-2
idea.test_plan: Free, index only: for every XRP/BNB live entry 09-22..10-15 compute the projected settle in rounding steps from the strike at the send second (locked prints from cfbenchmarks_value + spot); count losers and winners within 2 steps; deploy (paper arm vs twin for 2 weeks first) only if it catches >= 1 loser a month at a skipped-win cost under one loss a month.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: R16 (needs-data) is answered as an XRP/BNB problem; R10 is the dead general version; the XRP/BNB restriction and the 09-30 loss are new.
idea.worst_case: None in money; a gate must never block insurance.
idea.prior_reason: Free test, but R10 found no loss visible at entry and the named loss sat 2.7 steps from the strike at fair 1.0; ~$1-2/day ceiling.

test.method:
Sources: live fills and the raw settlement index only, no replay.

1. gather.py collected every live 15-min crypto entry fill in results/pinrun-live-*.jsonl from 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-16: 965 entry fills on 820 markets. Each fill carries the signal that fired it (strike, round digits, logged spot, logged sigma, logged fair). Money per market comes from results/kalshi_ledger.json via pinledger.pnl, which pays result x contracts held and does not use the revenue field.
2. proj.py (self-test PASS on a planted XRP world) rebuilt pinrun.projection() at each send from C:/kals/kalshi_data/cfbenchmarks_value. The projection is (locked prints from close-60 to the newest held print + r x newest print) / 60. The newest held print is found by matching the bot's own logged spot.
3. Margins are in rounding steps (10^-round_digits) and measured two ways: on our side to the exchange boundary K = strike - step/2, and as the idea's literal |mu - strike|/step. The 60-print settle is put on the same scale.
4. analyze.py works per market (cluster). It counts losers, winners and Kalshi net inside bands of 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 and 20 steps, for XRP+BNB, NEAR+ETH and all coins.
5. Holdout by ET close day: H1 is 09-21..10-02, H2 is 10-03..10-16. The idea set the 2-step bar in advance; it was not fitted.
test.n_markets: 793 live markets rebuilt (933 of 965 entries). XRP+BNB: 212 markets, 3 lost. NEAR+ETH: 177 markets, 3 lost. All 9 coins: 16 lost.
test.n_independent_clusters: 793 markets over 25 ET days, of which 212 are XRP+BNB. 16 losing markets in total, 3 of them on XRP/BNB.
test.result:
**The guard catches zero losers.**

Entry margin on our side, in rounding steps, for every live losing market:
- XRP 09-30 19:15 ET: 3.2 steps. |mu-strike| was 2.7 and the model width was 0.7 step, so the entry sat 4.7 widths deep. It settled at -0.09. Kalshi net -$42.60 including insurance.
- BNB 09-28: 4.1 steps.
- ETH 10-10: 4.8 steps.
- XRP 10-10: 5.5 steps.
- The other 12: from 11.9 to 6,694 steps.

No loser on any coin had a margin under 3.2 steps.

**XRP+BNB inside 2 steps (our side):** 34 markets would be refused, 0 lost. Their Kalshi net is +$91.93: H1 13 markets +$34.36, H2 21 markets +$57.57. So the guard costs about $92 over 25 days, and both halves are negative. With the literal |mu-strike| <= 2 rule it is 38 markets, 0 lost, +$111.32 given up.

**Wider bands never turn positive:**
- <= 3 steps catches the XRP 09-30 loss (-$42.60) but refuses $126.42 of winners, net -$84.
- <= 5 steps refuses $149 of winners to avoid $51.52 of losses.
- All coins at <= 2 steps: 35 markets, 0 lost, +$120 given up.
- NEAR+ETH at <= 2 steps fires once, on a winner.

**Why:** XRP's model width is a median 1.6 rounding steps (BNB 3.9). Entries 0.2 to 2 steps from the boundary are routinely 2.6 to 7 widths deep, and they win. All 34 in-band markets settled on our side.

Of our 28 markets whose settle really landed within 1 step, 27 won. The one loser (XRP 09-30) was 3.2 steps clear at entry and was lost to a fast move after entry. That matches R10, now confirmed on XRP/BNB with 2.5 more weeks of data.

**The only photo-finish money cost found is not an entry problem.** On BNB 09-26 10:30 ET the bet won (the settle landed 0.06 step on our side), but insurance fired at 57.8c and lost, for a Kalshi net of -$20.29. That is a hedge-trigger problem (ledger W02).
test.artefact_checks:
1. **Projection rebuild vs the bot's own logged fair** (using its logged sigma): within 0.1c on 899 of 933 entries and within 0.5c on 932 of 933. The outlier is one BTC entry that used the receipt-time fallback. The logged spot matched a tape print exactly on 932 of 933.
2. **Settle side:** the tape's settle side equals Kalshi's market_result on 932 of 932.
3. **Money bug caught in my own first pass.** Using revenue - costs gave -$131.60 for XRP 09-30 and -$118.29 for BNB 09-26. Kalshi's revenue field reads 0 when both sides are held, so the $1-per-pair payout was missing. Switching to pinledger.pnl gives -$42.60 and -$20.29, which match the bot's own settled pnl_c legs.
4. **Rounding step** comes from the bot's logged round_digits on each signal (XRP 4, BNB 2, DOGE 7, BTC/ETH 2, others 4). It is never inferred from the size of the price.
5. **Entries not rebuilt:** 32, because of tape gaps on 09-22/23 and the 10-16 hour still being written. The only loser among them is BTC 09-23, hundreds of steps from any strike, so no XRP/BNB loser is missing.
6. **Counting rule:** a market counts as refused if ANY of its entries is in band, which is the count most generous to the guard. Counting only first entries also gives 0 losers.
7. **Recorders:** I could not see their process command lines, but cfbenchmarks_value was still being written at 14:38Z. Free disk is 112 GB.
test.supply_we_would_get: Not applicable: this is a lose-less gate on our own KXXRP15M/KXBNB15M entries. It would fire on about 1.4 XRP/BNB markets a day (34 of 212 in 25 days, about 16 in 100 of the XRP/BNB markets we trade), and every one of those won.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: If deployed: about -$3.70/day from winners given up ($92 over 25 days; H2, closest to current size, is -$4.10/day). It avoids $0 of losses. Not deploying = $0.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: If deployed: roughly -$10 to -$16/day, assuming fills scale with size (not measured). The benefit is $0.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
To break even, the guard must stop at least $92 of losses per 25 days inside its band. That is about 2 XRP/BNB losses of ~$42-47 each (net of insurance) among its 34 markets, an in-band loss rate of about 6 in 100.

- **What the in-band count shows:** 0 of 34 lost. The 95% upper bound is about 8.5 in 100, so the in-band rate alone cannot rule out break-even.
- **What settles it:** 0 of the 16 live losers sit inside 3.2 steps (95% upper bound: at most about 17 in 100 losers in band), and the one named loss is outside the band at 2.7-3.2 steps.
test.worst_case: Deployed as written, it blocks about 1.4 winning XRP/BNB markets a day (about $4/day at today's size) and stops no loss. The code would be a risk only if it ever touched insurance, which it must not.
test.next_test:
None for the entry guard: kill it.

The photo-finish money that does exist is insurance firing on a market that then settles our way (BNB 09-26, -$20.29 on a winning bet). That belongs to ledger W02 (hedge only when the projection is at least 2 rounding steps through the strike). W02's pre-registered read needs about 5 alarms where the projection is only just through the strike (~17 days) from the live bot's own hedge records; no new recorder is needed.

To re-run with more days, use these scripts in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-10/: gather.py, then proj.py, then analyze.py. The result is saved in RESULT.json in the same folder.

idea.name: Saturday half-size for the live pin bot (loss concentration by ET weekday on live money) -- pre-registered forward read
merged_from: crypto-15m-new-angles: Saturday half-size for the live pin bot (loss concentration by weekday, live records)
idea.mechanism: On Saturdays (ET) the bot runs at half its auto-size; nothing else changes. Money = avoided Saturday losses minus half of Saturday wins.
idea.why_mispriced: Not a payer; a calendar lose-less gate. Proposed mechanism: the weekend index is half as volatile (BTC 1-s sigma 2.1 vs 4.3-5.1 x 1e-5 on weekdays, every coin similar), so the model reaches 99.5% on a thinner dollar cushion and cheap weekend offers are sold to us where a burst in a quiet tape flips the settle. The model's own tape miss rate is not clearly higher on Saturdays (0.17/100 vs 0.06-0.12 Mon-Thu, 0.31 Fri), so it would be a fills effect.
idea.must_be_true: It must hold forward and on money, not only on counts. One look among 7 weekdays and 24 hours (post hoc). FINAL_SYNTHESIS 10-09 already rejected weekday/Saturday rules as 'not stable across halves'.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter (settled records since 09-08): Saturday 332 mk, 20 lost (6.0/100) vs 2.6/100 on other days, z +2.86. C1 re-read on Kalshi money (results/kalshi_ledger.json main account, KX*15M, 09-08..10-15, 1,526 markets, insurance pairs counted; C1/weekday_ledger.py): Saturday 283 mk (211 closes), 17 lost (6.0/100), -$144.12 (-0.95c per $ bet) vs other days 1,243 mk, 37 lost (3.0/100), +$1,064 (+1.87c/$). By period the Saturday loss rate is higher every time -- 09-08..09-21 7.1 vs 2.8/100 (money -$185 vs +$667), 09-22..10-08 3.5 vs 2.7 (+$19 vs +$201), 10-08..10-15 (one Saturday) 7.1 vs 1.5 (+$22 vs +$196) -- but Saturday money was positive in the last two periods. Each Saturday: 09-12 6 lost +$38; 09-19 6 lost -$223; 09-26 1 lost +$47; 10-03 2 lost -$28; 10-10 2 lost +$22. Halving Saturday size would have gained ~+$93 in the first period and cost ~-$9 and ~-$11 since. The seller check removes 19 of 86 Saturday markets 09-22..10-08 and none of the 3 Saturday losers.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: ~$0-2/day either way at $1,155 (halving saves half the Saturday losses, gives up half the Saturday wins); at $5,000 ~4x. Its real value is the worst Saturday (09-19, -$223 -> ~-$110). If noise, halving costs ~$10-30 per Saturday.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~30-100 live markets per Saturday
idea.test_plan: Pre-register now, change nothing: the next 4 Saturdays at live size. Bar: >= 6 losing markets in the first ~130 Saturday markets (4.5/100) AND Saturday money per $ bet below the other days' over the same 4 weeks -> halve Saturday auto-size (VERSIONS entry, operator's OK); <= 3 losses or Saturday per-$ money >= the other days' -> drop. Zero cost.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No ledger row tests a weekday effect on the live loss population; FINAL_SYNTHESIS 10-09 rejected it on money across halves. New: Kalshi-money re-check by period (counts consistent, money not) and the weekend-sigma mechanism.
idea.worst_case: If noise, halving gives up ~$10-30 of Saturday wins per Saturday at current size.
idea.prior_reason: Loss counts are consistently higher on Saturdays, but money says ~$0 since 09-22 and the 10-09 synthesis already rejected it; slow (4 Saturdays).

test.method:
Data sources, best first: the raw CF Benchmarks 1/sec settlement index (rank 1), used for the volatility mechanism, and our own live fills, with money taken from Kalshi's own per-market settlement ledger (results/kalshi_ledger.json, main account, KX*15M crypto up/down only; insurance pairs credited $1). No replay was used, and no loss rate comes from the tape. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-09/:
- satgate.py: weekday tables; a day-level permutation test with a 7-weekday correction; a date holdout (fit up to 09-30, test 10-01..10-16); terciles of index sigma; overlap with the seller check; simulated power of the forward bar. Its self-test plants a Saturday effect and also runs a world with nothing planted.
- idxvol.py: streams 909 hourly index files from 09-07 to 10-16, read-only, into 5-minute buckets of 1-s log-return sd and largest move. Its self-test plants a known sigma and a gap. 7 truncated hours were skipped.
- satmoney.py: what a Saturday loss is made of; a day-level bootstrap of Saturday money per $ bet; the rule's value at today's size.
- jumpgate.py: tests pre-entry index jumpiness as a gate that does not depend on the calendar, with cuts fit on the first half.
- satbar.py: power of the forward bar, and how many Saturdays the money question needs.

Definitions: a 'model miss' means the side of our first live signal settled against us. A 'right-call loss' means our call was right but the market still lost money because the insurance cost more than the win.
test.n_markets: 1,560 live 15-minute crypto markets with Kalshi money, 09-08..10-16 ET: 283 on Saturdays, 1,277 on other days
test.n_independent_clusters: 38 ET dates, of which 5 are Saturdays (09-12, 09-19, 09-26, 10-03, 10-10). 1,173 closes, 211 of them on Saturdays. A calendar rule acts on whole days, so the n that decides this is 5 Saturdays.
test.result:
The loss COUNT effect holds. The MONEY effect does not.

(1) Losing-market counts. Saturday: 17 of 283 lost (6.0 per 100). Other days: 32 of 1,277 (2.5 per 100). Day-level permutation p = 0.006, or 0.038 after allowing for 7 weekdays. The hunter also looked at 24 hours, so the true correction is larger than that. Without 09-19, p = 0.13. The count replicates in the holdout: Saturday 6.0 vs 2.5 per 100 in the fit half, and 6.2 vs 2.5 per 100 in the test half (4 of 65).

(2) Money per $ bet. Saturday -0.95c vs +1.77c on other days, but the 7-weekday p is 0.32. Without 09-19 (-$223), Saturdays made +0.95c per $ (p 0.96). Each Saturday in turn: +2.30, -3.32, +1.84, -1.09, +1.36 c/$.
- Test half: Saturday -0.13c/$ (-$5.24). Halving Saturdays there would have made +$2.62 over 15 days (+$0.17/day).
- Day bootstrap of Saturday money: -0.95c/$ pooled, 90% range -2.47 to +1.77c/$, a 69% chance it is below zero.
- Telling -0.95c/$ apart from zero needs about 39 Saturdays (9 months).

(3) What the Saturday excess is made of:
- Model misses: 3.18 vs 2.04 per 100 (9 markets, -$456, vs 25 markets, -$930).
- Right-call insurance losses: 2.12 vs 0.47 per 100 (6 markets, -$148, vs 6 markets, -$88). By half: 5 vs 4 in the fit half, 1 vs 2 in the test half.

(4) The proposed mechanism (a quiet weekend index) is FALSIFIED on the raw index.
- Saturday is the quietest day for every coin: BTC's 1-s sd is 0.46x its median, the other coins 0.58-0.74x, Sunday 0.74-0.89x.
- But quiet windows on other days do not lose more. Non-Saturday quietest third: 2.5 lost per 100 (+1.61c/$). Middle third: 3.4 (+1.44c/$). Busiest third: 1.7 (+2.70c/$).
- Saturday loses more in every third, including the busiest.
- Pre-entry jumpiness does not explain it either: the smoothest Saturdays lose the most (4 misses in 59).

(5) Overlap with the seller check. On Saturdays it refuses 19 of 114 markets with 0 losers among them, giving up +$23.72. After the check, Saturdays still run 5.3 lost per 100 at +0.29c/$, against 2.3 per 100 at +2.03c/$ on other days. The two rules catch different markets.
test.artefact_checks:
- Money: recomputed from Kalshi's ledger, not from the bot's own pnl. Insurance pairs credited $1 (C1 hand-checked BNB 10-06 and ETH 10-10).
- Tiny markets: the 'lost' count includes them. 09-12's six losers total -$34, and three of them are under $1.10. So I also counted model misses and losses over $10 (Saturday 11 of 283 vs 23 of 1,277). Same direction, smaller gap.
- One burst? No: Saturday's 17 losers sit on 16 different closes, at most 2 at any one close.
- Bet size changed a lot: per Saturday market it was $17 on 09-12, $92 on 09-19 and is $46 now. So money is compared per $ bet and rescaled to today's size. The -$144 Saturday total is mostly 09-19, run at the biggest size ever.
- Weekday: ET weekday taken from the ticker's ET close.
- Index sigma: whole-second prints and consecutive seconds only. Windows with under 600 of 900 returns were dropped, leaving 1,526 of 1,560 markets.
- Bar power: simulated by resampling whole days, so clustering within a day is kept.
- Recorders: alive. Files under kalshi_data and feed_data were written within seconds of the end of the run. Process command lines are hidden from this shell, so this was checked by file writes. Free disk is 111.8 GB; the scratch folder is 9 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: No new supply. This is a size change on the pin bot's existing Saturday fills: 28-49 markets per Saturday recently, about $1,750 bet per Saturday at today's size ($46 per market, measured since 10-11).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now:
About $0.
- Holdout realised: +$0.17/day.
- Central: +$1.19/day (+$8.34 per Saturday), if Saturdays really run -0.95c/$. 90% range -$2.21 to +$3.08/day.
- If Saturdays are as positive as they were without 09-19, halving costs about $1.2/day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $0. If Saturday fills scale with the bank (not measured; the bot is limited by how many offers there are), roughly 4x the range above: -$9 to +$12/day.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
- Loss counts: about 3 extra losing markets per 100 Saturday markets (the day-to-day spread is 2.55 per 100). The observed +3.5 is just above that.
- Money: with 5 Saturdays, only about -3c per $ is detectable, which is about -$52 per Saturday at today's size. The observed -0.95c/$ would need about 39 Saturdays.
test.worst_case: If Saturdays are net winners, halving gives up half of every good Saturday: about $20 on the best one seen (+2.30c/$ x $1,748) and about $8 on a typical one. The tail it would trim: a Saturday at 09-19's rate (-3.32c/$) costs -$58 at today's size, and halving makes that -$29.
test.next_test:
Drop the calendar rule.

The bar as pre-registered (>= 6 losers in ~130 Saturday markets AND Saturday money per $ below the other days') is not safe. It would order the half-size change in 50 of 100 runs even if Saturdays win money, as they did without 09-19. If Saturday is no different, it fires in 7 of 100.

If a free read is still wanted, change the money half of the bar to 'Saturday money per $ below ZERO'. Under that bar: false alarms 3 of 100; it fires 9 of 100 in the world without 09-19, and 48 of 100 if Saturdays look like all five so far.

Better uses of the same question:
(a) Right-call insurance losses (2.3 vs 0.5 per 100 in the fit half, 1.5 vs 0.5 in the test half). Read the bot's hedge records by weekday over the next 4 Saturdays (10-17, 10-24, 10-31, 11-07). Bar: Saturday hedge firings on calls that end right reach >= 2x the weekday rate AND their net cost is over $20. If it passes, look at the insurance trigger, not the bet size.
(b) A side lead from jumpgate.py, not a rule. On non-Saturdays, the jumpiest third of pre-entry windows had more model misses in both halves (3.2 vs 1.9 per 100 for the smoothest third in the fit half; 3.4 vs 1.1 in the test half). But that third still made money (+0.94 and +0.62c/$), so jumpiness could feed the model's volatility estimate rather than refuse trades.

idea.name: Rotten Tomatoes knife-edge: a score-drift model for strikes within 1 point of the live Tomatometer (the slow part, not the dead SI32 sniper)
markets: KXMC (all close 14:00Z = 10:00 AM ET on the settlement date)
idea.mechanism: 1) Log every open KXRT title's Tomatometer and review count every 10 minutes (free page scrape). 2) Fit P(score at the 10:00 AM ET snapshot > K | current score, review count, hours left, time since embargo). 3) On strikes within +-1 point of the live score, trade only when the model differs from the market by > 8c, as a maker where possible.
idea.why_mispriced: The settlement is a 10 AM snapshot of a number that moves 1 point every few reviews; 23 of 27 films still had a knife-edge strike 24 h before close; of 28 markets mid-priced (10-90c) at 24 h, 19 settled within +-1 point (6 exactly on it) and YES won 50% -- the crowd is coin-flipping. ~42k mid-priced contracts/week trade in the last 24 h.
idea.must_be_true: Review arrival is predictable enough to beat 50/50 on +-1-point strikes (reviews cluster at embargo lifts, previews, release day); a 10-minute logger sees moves before the market; the 10:00 AM snapshot timing is exact.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter slow-source, candles on 418 markets / 27 films (63 days): at 1 h before close the 85-95c bucket lost 1 of 5 (103,694 contracts in that hour); at 6 h 70-85c won 1 of 3; at 24 h 50-70c resolved YES 29% (7), 30-50c 60% (5). RT median 22.6k contracts/market; 72% of volume 48-168 h before close (4.8M mid-priced contracts). No score history was available, so no model was fitted.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Not measurable yet. Pot ~42k mid-priced contracts/week in the last day: a 5c edge on 5% of it = ~$100/week = ~$15/day at the current bank, more at $5,000 only if depth allows; $0 if review arrival is unpredictable. Worst plausible day: -$95 per 98 contracts on one wrong knife-edge.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~6-7 markets/day (418 over 63 days)
idea.test_plan: 4-week read-only RT logger (score + review count every 10 min for every open KXRT title) joined to Kalshi 1-minute candles; fit on weeks 1-2, test on 3-4. Pass: >= 60% directional accuracy on >= 30 knife-edge markets with a >= 8c model-vs-market gap. One scraper, no Kalshi API load. Add to results/READS_DUE.json.
idea.prior_reason: Large, coin-flipping knife-edge volume and a free logger; but no model exists yet and review timing may simply be unpredictable.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SI32 killed the review-burst SNIPER (speed race lost in the first second); the carried lip-economics lane killed RT reward quoting. Modelling where the score lands days later is a different, slow trade.
idea.worst_case: A late review batch flips the score by 2 points after entry: -$95 per 98 contracts; a mis-timed snapshot is the systematic risk.
merged_from: slow-source-settlement-lag #3

test.method: First real Rotten Tomatoes score history for this idea. Rebuilt the Tomatometer (exact liked/total review counts) for 76 settled KXRT films (Jan 26 to Oct 12 2026) from 602 Wayback Machine captures, fetched with curl because Wayback answers Python urllib with HTTP 429. RT's own reviews API returns 401 (Akamai bot wall). All 484 page scores equal round-half-up(100*liked/total), including 9 exact .5 cases. Kalshi: all 1,229 settled KXRT markets (883 from /historical/markets, which serves markets settled before 08-17 that /markets no longer returns; 346 live). Event settlement_sources give each film's RT URL. Hourly candles for every strike within 7 points of the settled score (/historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks), then 1-minute quotes 2-5 min after each capture. Model, fitted on TRAIN only (42 films closing before 2026-07-01): future reviews = current count x a growth ratio resampled from TRAIN captures with similar hours left; each new review is fresh with probability (current fresh rate + delta); P(YES) = P(final rounded score > K). Fitted delta = -0.015 (new reviews come in 1.5 points less fresh), no extra spread. Median review growth to close: +0.4% with 0-6 h left, +4% at 6-24 h, +9% at 24-48 h, +36% at 48-96 h. HOLDOUT = 35 films closing 07-06..10-12. The bar was written to PREREG.txt before any test number: knife-edge strike within 1 point of the live score, 10+ reviews, 0-96 h left; buy at the taker price when model minus price minus fee >= 8c; first signal per market; held to settlement. Sources: Wayback captures of the settlement page (raw source, archived) > trade tape > candles. No live fills exist. Scripts are s1_markets.py .. s9_quote1m.py and t9/t10 in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-09/.
test.n_markets: Holdout: 255 knife-edge observations on 78 markets (219 obs / 71 markets with a 1-minute quote); 35 signalled markets at the hourly quote, 28 at the 1-minute quote. Train: 204 obs / 96 markets. Pooled: 395 obs, 66 signalled markets.
test.n_independent_clusters: Holdout 30 films (27 with 1-minute quotes); signals came from 23 films (19 at 1-minute quotes). Pooled 66 films, 44 of them with signals. Strikes on one film share one number, so the film is the cluster.
test.result: PRE-REGISTERED VERDICT: KILL. (a) passed: 35 markets from 23 films signalled. (b) FAILED: the model's side won 15 of 35 (43%) against a 60% bar; with the more realistic 1-minute quote it won 14 of 28 (50%), which also fails (a). (c) +5.4c per contract per film, t 0.74, both halves positive (+4.8c and +4.4c), but not significant. (d) model Brier 0.1184 vs market 0.1194, a difference of 0.001 that is noise (per-film t 0.24). TRAIN in-sample, hourly quote: 43 markets, won 42%, -2.0c per film (t -0.29). 1-minute quotes, holdout: Brier model 0.1211 vs market 0.1234, CI on the difference [-0.023, +0.014]; +6.0c per film, t 0.68. POOLED 66 films (1-minute quotes): the model's disagreement with the price does carry some information (slope +0.69, film-bootstrap CI [+0.19, +1.10]). But it does not turn into tradeable money: the 50/50 blend beats the market Brier by 0.0048, CI [-0.0117, +0.0010]; the 8c-edge signals made 66 markets / 44 films, won 32 (48%), +4.4c per contract per film, sd 38c, t 0.78. Raising the edge bar does not rescue it (pooled 12c: +12.3c, t 1.52, 38 markets; 15c: +4.3c, t 0.53). The idea's premise that the crowd is coin-flipping is false. The market is calibrated on knife-edges: holdout YES rate tracks the mid within noise in every bucket, and the one apparent bias, the 30-50c bucket, flips sign between halves (train 39c mid -> 53-59% YES; test 39c -> 22-30% YES). POST-HOC LEAD, not pre-registered, one of 3 slices: signals within 24 h of a market's LISTING made 8 markets / 7 films, won 6, +37.6c per film, t 2.54. Example: KXRT-OTH-18 was listed 10-09 17:00Z with reviews already out; at 8/47 = 17% it bid 0.81 YES for about an hour while takers bought NO at 0.19; it settled NO. That is about one case a month.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Per-film P&L sd is about 35-38c per contract. With 23-44 signalling films the smallest edge this sample could detect (2 standard errors) is about 11-15c per contract. Edges of 0-6c, which is where every point estimate sits, cannot be told from zero here; proving them would take about 150+ films, roughly 1.5 years at 2.1 films a week. Brier-difference resolution is about +-0.01.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Rounding: 484 of 484 page scores equal integer round-half-up of liked/total (9 exact .5 cases). (2) Wayback captures against settlement: captures within 3 h of close matched the settled score 8 of 9 times. The miss (KXRT-RES, 197/206 = 96 at 1.4 h, settled 95) is one late rotten review. In the OTH-18 case, taker flow at the capture time agreed with the captured count, so the capture was not stale. (3) Look-ahead in strike selection: candles were pulled for strikes within 7 points of the final score. Only 3 of 476 knife-edge (capture, strike) pairs fell outside that band or had no candles. (4) Quote timing: the hourly close 5-65 min after the capture (conservative) and the 1-minute quote 2-5 min after give the same verdict. (5) Parameter leakage: delta and the arrival pool come from TRAIN only. A naive model (delta 0) gives holdout Brier 0.1246, worse than the market's 0.1194. (6) Two holdout signals with 0.9 h left (HEA-87, DIG-50, NO at 1c) are artefacts: the arrival pool is too thin near close, with only 6 TRAIN captures under 6 h. They cost 1c each. (7) The 1-minute check moved several signals: the hourly quote mispriced some entries by 5-30c (END-84 edge 9c -> 4c; INS-60 13c -> 2c; OTH-18 NO 0.55 -> 0.19). That is why the 1-minute version is the decisive one. (8) Units: candle prices are dollars (historical field 'close', live field 'close_dollars'), checked against trades. (9) Recorders still writing at the end (kalshi_data and feed_data files updated 14:55Z). Disk 112 GB free.
test.supply_we_would_get: On KXRT (Rotten Tomatoes score markets), about 1.8 signals a week (66 in about 37 weeks). After each holdout signal, the contracts others took at or better than our price within 2 h: median 92, 25th percentile 7, zero on 5 of 35 signals, at least 98 on 17 of 35. The live books on 2026-10-16 for the 4 films closing 10-19 (SENS, STRA, WHA, YOUC) show 2.5 to 529 contracts at the best price on knife-edge strikes. So a 98-contract order fills fully about half the time.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 central: no edge was shown. Even if the unproven +4.4c per contract held: 98 contracts x 4.4c x about 1.8 signals a week x about 50% fill = about $0.55 a day. The post-hoc listing-day slice, if real: 98 x about 37c x 8 signals in 37 weeks = about $1 a day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $0-2 a day. Depth caps size: the median 92 contracts at or better in 2 h means 400-contract orders mostly do not fill, so the ceiling grows far less than the bank.
test.worst_case: One knife-edge strike flipping by a single late review: 98 contracts x about 60c = about -$59. Two correlated strikes on one film: about -$100. The holdout already showed it, KXRT-END-84 NO at 0.76 (-77c) and END-83 NO at 0.50 (-52c) on the same film the same weekend. The worst plausible weekend with 3 films is about -$150 at the current bank.
test.next_test: None for the drift model: killed by its own pre-registered bar, and capped near $1 a day even if a small edge exists. The only lead is the listing-day mispricing (8 markets, t 2.54, post-hoc). A cheap way to decide it: a read-only watcher that, when a new KXRT event lists while RT reviews already exist (OTH-type), logs the RT count every 10 min and the book on knife-edge strikes for the first 24 h. Pre-register now: at least 15 listings from at least 10 films, model side wins at least 65%, and at least +10c per contract per film after fee at the quote 2-5 min after the read. At about one case a month this takes about a year. With a ceiling of about $1 a day it is not worth a bot unless it generalises to other newly listed slow markets. If built, add it to results/READS_DUE.json. Free re-runs: s2_wayback.py + s5_eval.py + s9_quote1m.py on new films as they settle. idea.name: Exchange-side fill cap for the coin-race reward filler: one order group per race (rolling 15-s contract limit across all legs) -- DOWNGRADED: on the 3 live races nearly all fills came after v2's 110-120 s exit
idea.lane: kalshi-mechanics-capital x lip-mechanics (lose less on the reward family)
markets: KXCRYPTOLEAD15M (coin race, reward per leg per window)
idea.mechanism: A Kalshi order group cancels every resting order in the group once filled contracts exceed a limit within a rolling 15 s, and blocks new orders until reset -- on the exchange, with no 0.2-2 s client cancel in flight. Put each race's 1c YES bids (all legs) in one group, limit ~100 contracts. When informed sellers start hitting one dead leg (a coin coming alive), the group pulls the other legs before they are swept too.
idea.why_mispriced: The reward is real (Kalshi paid +$11.04, 90% of expected, on 10-11) but fills cost more (-$12.45) and arrive in bursts across legs; a client-side cancel is too slow (one cancel on 10-11 returned 404 while the order was still resting, 2 tries, +1.3 s).
idea.must_be_true: (1) Order groups work on shard 2 (groups are per exchange instance; every coin-race leg lives on shard 2). (2) Bursts happen BEFORE the bot's planned exit. MERGER CHECK of results/racereward-live.jsonl (fills are cumulative per order): race 1 ETH 62 + SOL 203 at 108-81 s left; race 2 ETH 222 + BTC 185, of which all but 8 contracts at 107-90 s left; race 3 HYPE 289 + BTC 284, of which all but ~9 contracts at 117-59 s left. Fills with > 120 s left totalled ~17 contracts ($0.17). The carried v2 filler exits at 110-120 s, which by itself avoids nearly all of the $12.45; the hunter's '$6.1 saved' was computed against the exit-60 run, so the order group's saving ON TOP of v2 on these races is ~$0.1-0.2.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter replay of the 16 live fill events (3 races, 10-11) with a 100-contract/15-s group vs the exit-60 run: ~$6.1 of $12.45 fill cost avoided, ~$1.5 of $12.23 expected credit given up; net -$1.41 -> ~+$3.2 over 3 races. Merger re-read above: nearly all of that overlap is already captured by v2's earlier exit. n = 3 races.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: On top of v2: ~$0 on the measured races; only insurance against a coin coming alive earlier than the exit (unmeasured). Same at $5,000 (reward does not scale with bank). Worst plausible day: the group triggers on harmless noise and gives up ~10-20% of the credit.
idea.settlements_per_day: 96 races/day
idea.test_plan: Ride along with the next v2 live reward test (operator sign-off per the reward lanes' plan): attach every leg's order to one group per race (POST /portfolio/order_groups, limit 100), log triggers from the order_group_updates WS channel. Bar: over >= 20 races, count fills that arrived > 120 s before close and the cost the group avoided; keep it only if avoided cost > credit given up.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: New angle on SI05/SJ36 and carried lip-mechanics 'Coin-race 1c filler v2 (exit 110-120 s, expiration_ts ...)' / lip-economics 'exit at 120 s', which cut fill cost by exiting earlier; nobody proposed the exchange's own kill switch -- but the earlier exit already does most of its job.
idea.worst_case: The group triggers on noise and gives up 10-20% of the credit; or Kalshi rejects grouped post-only orders (cheap to find out).
idea.prior_reason: The live fill log shows the bursts sit inside the window v2 already vacates, so its incremental money is about zero on the only data there is; kept as cheap insurance to bolt onto the v2 test.
merged_from: r1:kalshi-mechanics-capital: Server-side fill cap for the coin-race reward filler

test.method:
Replayed the coin-race 1c reward filler v2 on the C2-02 tester's rebuilt books, reusing their files and rule unchanged (.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C2-02/legs_*.jsonl.gz and v99/). The v2 settings: exit at 115 s on Kalshi's side, $1.25 floor, size 1,100. Added one Kalshi order group per race across all legs. Per Kalshi's docs, a group counts filled contracts over a rolling 15 s; once the count passes the limit, every resting order in the group is cancelled and new orders are refused until a reset.

Two simulators:
- sim_group.py: fills counted per second.
- sim_group_ms.py: fills taken from the trade tape's individual taker orders at millisecond time (same ticker plus same ts_ms = one taker order), so the group can stop the rest of a second. x99 NO-99c crossers are placed at mid-second.

Grid:
- limit: 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 / 300 contracts
- cancel delay: 0 ms (exchange group; other legs' orders in the same ms are stopped, the best case), 1 ms, 300 ms (a fast cap the bot could run itself), 2,000 ms
- reset: none (the idea as proposed), 1 s, 15 s, 30 s, re-posting a fresh 1,100 only if the leg still passes the v2 rule

Fill models: low / mid / high queue models on the tape's 1c sales (551 races, 10-07..10-15). x99 = high plus NO bids added at 99c that would have crossed our bid (277 races, 10-10..10-15); C2-02 found x99 closest to our only live run. Cost is counted as 1c per filled contract (conservative). The no-group baselines reproduce C2-02's numbers exactly.

Holdout: first half of races vs second half. Standard errors are clustered by race (se_group.py). trade_bursts.py measured the millisecond structure of every 1c YES sale on coin-race legs, 10-08..10-16 (179 hour files, 684 races).

Sources: trade tape plus book deltas (rank 2), checked against our 10-11 live fills (rank 3) through C2-02's calibration. No pinsim replay. The order-group API was read from Kalshi's docs and not exercised.
test.n_markets: 1,104 placed leg-windows in 551 races (main); 552 placed leg-windows in 277 races (x99 cut)
test.n_independent_clusters: 551 races (main, full ET days 10-08..10-13 plus partial days); 277 races for x99 (3 full days). The race is the cluster: its 5 legs share one outcome and one group.
test.result:
As proposed (one group per race, no re-post) it loses money in every fill model.
- Limit 100, per race: -$0.08 (low), -$0.18 (mid), -$0.32 (high), -$0.21 (x99), standard error $0.03-0.10.
- Negative in both the fit half and the holdout half (high: fit -$79, holdout -$96; x99: fit -$22, holdout -$38).
- It does cut fill cost (high: -$70 of $539; x99: -$87 of $378), but gives up more credit because it pulls every leg in the race (high: -$246; x99: -$147).
- Limit 200: -$0.02 to -$0.08 per race; x99 +$0.02 (SE $0.065), i.e. zero.
- Limit 50: -$0.16 to -$0.46 per race.

The exchange-side speed is worth about $0.01 a race. The same rule with a 300 ms bot-side cancel instead of the group:
- high: -$0.331 vs -$0.318 per race
- mid: -$0.187 vs -$0.179
- low: -$0.087 vs -$0.081
- x99: -$0.225 vs -$0.214

The gap is $0.006-0.013 per race, about $0.5-1.3 a day.

Why the group can't help: 66% of the 1c YES contracts sold 360-115 s before close arrive in single taker orders of 100 or more, and 30% in single orders of 500 or more (13 orders of 1,100+ carried 34,503 contracts). A single sweep fills before any group can trigger. Spill-over onto other legs within 0.5 s of a burst of 50+ is 10,924 contracts, against 149,952 in the bursts themselves (7%). On our 3 live races only about 16 contracts filled before the 115 s exit, so the group would never have fired ($0).

Side finding (not this idea): the same trigger followed by a fresh re-post 1 s later, gated by the v2 rule, is positive in every model.
- Limit 100, per race: +$0.09 (low), +$0.16 (mid), +$0.23 (high), +$0.39 (x99), SE $0.03-0.09.
- Holdout positive in every model.
- Nearly all of the gain comes from two things: re-posting restores our size above the 1,000 target after a partial fill, and the v2 rule blocks re-posts while a 99c NO bid rests.
- A bot-side version earns the same within $0.01 a race, so no order group is needed.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) The no-group baselines reproduce C2-02's sim3 no-rail rows to the cent (high: paid $1,625.63, cost $539.22; mid: $1,714.29 / $337.15; low: $1,776.94 / $147.02). The millisecond simulator matches the per-second one exactly at baseline.
(2) Moving from per-second to per-millisecond changed the no-re-post result by less than $0.02 a race.
(3) Delay 0 stops other legs' orders in the same millisecond, the most generous reading of the matching engine. The group still loses.
(4) The re-post gain is a size-refresh effect. Re-posting after 1 s or after 15 s gives the same result within $0.01-0.03 a race, so the pause (the group's actual job) adds about nothing. The gain is untested against sellers drawn in by our own bid (the latent model cannot run per event).
(5) The best setting was picked on the fit half. At limit 100 the no-re-post rows are negative in both halves for every model.
(6) Units decided by field name: count_fp is contracts, yes_price_dollars is dollars. Only yes <= $0.0101 with taker_side 'no' was kept.
(7) The x99 cut covers only 3 full days.
(8) Creating an order group defaults to exchange_index 0, but every coin-race leg is on shard 2. A group created without exchange_index=2 would not cover the orders. Not exercised.
(9) The trade and cfbenchmarks_value hour files were written at 10:57:15 local, seconds before the check. The recorder command lines are not visible to the process query; 39 python processes were running. Free disk 111.8 GB; scratch 0.3 MB. 0 Kalshi API calls, 0 orders, 1 docs page fetched.
test.supply_we_would_get: Same as the v2 filler it would ride on: KXCRYPTOLEAD15M only, about 2 postable dead legs per race, about 190 leg-windows a day. At limit 100 the group changes the outcome on 46-102 of 551 races; at limit 200, on 13-38. The $20 pot per leg-window caps it, not the bank.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0 to -$20 a day as proposed. Limit 100 without re-post: -$0.21 a race (x99) x 96 races = -$20 a day before the bot's $30 day rail. That rail lets only about 15-50% of legs post, so about -$3 to -$10 a day as run. Limit 200: about $0. The exchange-side part (vs doing the same in the bot) is worth about +$1 a day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Same as now: the pot caps the filler, not the bank. The group itself is about $0 (limit 200) to -$20 a day (limit 100); exchange-side speed adds about +$1 a day.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: The race-clustered standard error is $0.03-0.10 a race over 551 races (277 for x99). So the sample detects about +/-$0.07-0.20 a race (2 SE), i.e. +/-$7-19 a day at 96 races. The $0.01-a-race exchange-vs-bot difference is far below what any live test could see. The spread between fill models (low vs x99) is bigger than the sampling error.
test.worst_case: With limit 50 and no re-post, the group fires on ordinary small fills and pulls every leg: -$0.46 a race in the high model, about -$45 a day of credit given up at 96 races. In practice the $30 rail caps it. Creating the group without exchange_index=2 would silently protect nothing.
test.next_test:
None for the order group. It is dead: as proposed it gives up more credit than it saves, and the exchange-side speed is worth about $1 a day.

Pass the side finding to the planned v2 live test instead, as a rule pre-registered before the test: "after any fill that leaves our YES side under 1,000, cancel and re-post a fresh 1,100 if the leg still passes the v2 rule (best NO <= 98c etc.)". The tape models say +$0.09 to +$0.39 a race.

Bar for that rule: over at least 20 live races, log per leg the credit lost to under-1,000 seconds after fills, and the fills on re-posted orders. Keep it only if fills on re-posted orders cost less than 50% of the credit they add.

If the filler ever runs unattended, a group with limit about 1,100 on exchange_index 2 is a cheap backstop in case the bot crashes (not measured).

idea.name: Rain 11-20c YES in autumn: the inverse of the dead U10 tail-NO desk (October fronts rained 6 of 21 at 11-20c) -- post hoc, pre-register November
markets: KXRAIN daily city rain, the 11-20c YES rung ~22 h before close
idea.mechanism: Buy YES at the ask on the 11-20c rung ~22 h before close (taker, 25 lots), hold to settlement, only from November onward and only if the pre-registered November read passes.
idea.why_mispriced: In October the summer dry-day lottery supply collapsed and the 11-20c rung is where autumn fronts actually rain: 29 per 100 realised against ~15 priced. Losers: NO buyers / YES sellers anchored on the summer base rate.
idea.must_be_true: The October excess rain rate at 11-20c repeats in November on fresh data (post hoc, n = 21 markets on 13 days, ~6 rain events).
idea.evidence_so_far: MEASURED 10-15 (rain_rerun2.out, Kalshi candles, settled markets): October 11-20c rung rained 6 of 21 (28.6 per 100); the NO side lost -14.3c a contract, so YES made ~+14c a contract ($75 at 25 lots over 13 days) -- found while scoring the dead U10 desk, i.e. post hoc. Not measured: depth at the 11-20c asks, any other month.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: If real: ~1.6 markets/day x 25 lots x ~14c = ~$5/day at the current bank (capital ~$4 a market); ~$5-10/day at $5,000 (depth binds). Worst plausible day: a dry spell -- every fill loses ~15c a contract, ~-$6 a day; a dry November ~-$100.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~30 cities/day, ~1-2 at the rung
idea.test_plan: Pre-register now (writer, in results/): 'November 11-20c rung: >= 25 markets, rain rate >= 22 per 100, YES net >= +5c a contract at the 25-lot ask fill', read from the same weekly rain_candles.py run already scheduled to the 11-15 U10 decision (0 extra GETs). Cross-check against the weather-model lane's overnight NBM rain taker (another new lane): if that model already buys these markets, this row folds into it.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: U10/SJ02 sold the 3-10c rung; the 11-20c autumn YES inverse is new. Overlaps the new weather-model lane's NBM rain taker (not a carried idea).
idea.worst_case: A dry November: ~-15c a contract on every fill.
merged_from: r1:revisit / Rain tail NO desk (U10/SJ02): failing its own bar -- the WEAK inverse angle only
idea.prior_reason: Post hoc on 21 markets / ~6 rain events; free to pre-register and read in November, small if real.

test.method: Data: Kalshi's own hourly candles for every settled KXRAIN daily market from 2026-07-26 to 2026-10-15 (1,944 markets on 82 dates). I seeded the cache from r1-revisit and fetched the 68 markets that settled on 10-14 and 10-15 through the public API (77 GETs). The rule is run the way a bot would: at close-22h, take the last hourly candle's YES bid and ask; buy YES at the ASK when the ask is 11-20c; pay the taker fee ceil(0.07*P*(1-P)*25) on each 25-lot order; hold to settlement and score with the result field. I also ran the idea's own definition (rung set by the YES BID, but we pay the ask) and an upper bound filled at the bid. Results are clustered by DATE, because one weather system rains on several cities. Splits: Jul-Sep (before); Oct 01-13 (where the idea was found, after the fact); Oct 14-15 (settled after the idea was written, so a fresh holdout). Extra checks: calibration across all rungs by month, neighbouring rungs, decision hour (H=30/26/22/18/14), a multiple-looks null (24 month x rung cells, outcome drawn from the candle mid, rain correlated within a date at rho 0-0.5), and a live order-book snapshot of depth at the YES ask (70 GETs). Source rank: Kalshi candles plus settlement results (trade-tape grade); no replay used. Scratch folder: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N1-07/ (fetch.py, analyse.py -> analyse.out, looks.py -> looks.out, books.py -> books.out, worst.py, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 190 markets with a YES ask of 11-20c at close-22h (162 in Jul-Sep, 20 in Oct 01-13, 8 in Oct 14-15), out of 1,937 markets with a usable quote. The idea's bid-defined rung has 181 (155 / 21 / 5).
test.n_independent_clusters: 76 trade-dates (64 in Jul-Sep, 10 in Oct 01-13, 2 in Oct 14-15). Rain at the rung fell on only 17 dates in total, and on 3 dates in Oct 01-13 when the rung is set by the ask (4 when set by the bid).
test.result:
I reproduced the hunter's number: in Oct 01-13, with the rung set by the YES BID at 11-20c, 6 of 21 markets rained. But a buyer pays the ASK, and 3 of those 6 rains (HOU 10-05, PIT 10-10, OKC 10-13) had a 21c ask, so they were outside the rung.

Rung set by the ASK (what the bot actually sees):
- Oct 01-13: 3 of 20 rained (15 per 100) against 15.2 priced; YES lost 1.06c a contract.
- Fresh Oct 14-15: 1 of 8 rained; -3.14c.
- All of October: 4 of 28 (14 per 100); -1.66c pooled (date-mean +1.2c, se 9.4).

Idea's bid definition, paid at the ask:
- Oct 01-13: +10.8c (date-mean +7.4c, se 11.5), resting on 4 rain dates.
- Fresh Oct 14-15: 1 of 5 rained; date-mean -5.2c.

The summer baseline is not neutral; YES LOST in it. Jul-Sep at ask 11-20c: 15 of 162 rained (9.3 per 100, 95% range 5.7-14.7) against 15.4 priced. That is -7.05c a contract pooled, date-mean -5.9c (se 3.2, 64 dates), or -$285 at 25 lots. Every 14-day block was negative except the last (Oct 04-17: +1.6c, n 23, se 11).

Across all rungs: in Jul-Sep the market priced rain about 4.2 per 100 too high (se 0.7, 1,469 markets). October came out calibrated (+0.4 per 100, se 1.6, 468 markets). So what happened in October is that the NO side's edge vanished; YES did not become cheap. A YES taker who pays the spread plus the fee loses about 1-2c a contract.

Noise checks:
- In October, ask 11-15c rained 3 of 10; ask 16-20c rained 0 of 10.
- Moving the decision hour swings October from +20.9c (H=30, 9 rains on 4 dates) to -6.3c (H=18). Jul-Sep is negative at every hour tested (-2.4c to -11.5c).
- If every market were priced right, the best of the hunter's 24 month x rung cells would show +10.8c or more by luck 18% of the time (rain independent) to 30% (rho 0.5).
test.artefact_checks:
1. Rung-boundary artefact found: the +14c depends on setting the rung by the bid. By the price actually paid it is -1.1c, because 3 of the 6 rains had 21c asks.
2. After-the-fact month selection: August and September at the same rung lost about 7c a contract each. October is the one positive month of three, and the multiple-looks null puts the chance of this by luck at 18-30%.
3. Clustering: the 6 rains fall on 4 dates, and two of those dates carry 4 of them (10-10 SEA+PIT, 10-13 OKC+MIN). The real sample is about 4 weather systems.
4. Fresh holdout (10-14 and 10-15, never seen by the hunter): with the rung set by the ask, 1 of 8 rained and YES lost 3.1c.
5. Calibration across every rung shows October calibrated at the mid, not YES underpriced. The Jul-Sep market over-priced rain (the old NO-desk edge).
6. The hunter's 6 of 21 reproduced exactly, so the data path is not the problem.
7. Limits: candle closes are hourly quote snapshots, not fills. Depth at exactly close-22h was not observed; the book snapshot was taken 15-40 h before close.
test.supply_we_would_get: About 2.3 markets a day reached a YES ask of 11-20c at close-22h over Jul-Oct (10 on the busiest day); October was about 1.9 a day. Book snapshot at 10:56 ET on 2026-10-16: 3 of 57 open KXRAIN markets had a YES ask of 11-20c. Contracts available at the ask were 1, 29 and 71; within +2c they were 58, 115 and 731. So 25 lots usually fill within 1-2c, and each extra cent costs 1c a contract. The supply is on KXRAIN daily city markets. The sellers we would buy from are the NO-side tail sellers, who were right in Jul-Sep.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: Negative. Over all 82 measured days at 25 lots it is about -$3.60 a day (-6.25c a contract on ~2.3 markets a day); October alone is about -$0.80 a day (-1.7c). Central realistic figure: $0, because the bot should not run.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Same sign. Depth at the ask is tens of contracts, which caps size near 25-75 lots, so at $5,000 it would lose about $4-10 a day if run. Not worth running.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: October's 28 markets at the rung can only detect a true rain rate of about 34 per 100 against 15 priced (80% power, before allowing for clustering). The Jul-Sep sample of 162 detects about 8 per 100, and it measured rain 6 per 100 BELOW the price. To detect the claimed 29-vs-15 effect takes about 48 markets if they were independent, about 75-95 once dates are clustered, which is roughly 35-45 days of supply.
test.worst_case: A dry stretch like Aug 23 - Sep 5: 1 rain in 41 markets, -14c a contract, -$144 over two weeks at 25 lots. The worst single day measured was -$30 (08-16: 7 markets, all dry). A November like August or September would cost about $100-150 a month at 25 lots.
test.next_test: None for this row: the ask-defined measurement and the negative Jul-Sep baseline kill it. If the writer still wants the free November read from the weekly rain_candles.py run (0 extra GETs), pre-register it on the ASK-defined rung: at least 60 markets, and YES net at the ask of at least +3c a contract with a date-clustered t of at least 2. The idea's own bar (25 markets, rain at least 22 per 100) would pass by luck about 16-17% of the time on a correctly priced 15c rung. Any real rain-YES edge belongs to the MOS/NBM model taker being tested in test-20261015-R1-N0-06, not to a price-only rung rule.

Third: the offer ends Oct 20 2026 11:59 AM ET (4 days away), and each $20 expires ONE day after it is credited, not 7 days as the idea said.

For the record, if he WERE eligible: FanDuel's fee is 2c per $1 of payout, so $20 buys 20/(p+0.02) contracts. test.method: Source: Kalshi's public trade record (rank 2; no replay). Every taker trade between 20 h and 30 min before the 4 PM ET close, from /markets/trades and /historical/trades (data before 2026-08-17 sits in /historical), on 1,303 KXINX daily brackets in 150 events, 2025-03-07..2026-10-15. Brackets were chosen ONLY by lifetime volume >= 25 contracts and their distance from the previous close (>= 0.4 trailing sd); nothing outcome-based. A maker's fill = a taker buying YES at that price (taker_outcome_side), held to the market's result. Maker fee 0 (series fee type quadratic x1). Pre-registered rule = the idea's own: 6-12c, 6-12 h out (4-10 AM ET), 1c inside, cap 100 per bracket. Holdout: earlier 75 events vs later 75. Second test, live period only: an ES-futures fair value (Yahoo 5-min ES=F minus the prior close's ES-SPX gap; spread of outcomes fit on the early half; the Sep-14 contract-roll day skipped), and the rule 'sell only if fair <= price - margin', with the margin picked on the early half and scored on the late half. Self-tests pass (planted edge found, null not found, cap logic). Scripts and outputs are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-12/ (analyze_tape.py/.out, analyze2.py/.out, esfair.py/.out, esmoney.py, sidecells.py, checks.py, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 1,303 brackets / 150 events. The idea's cell: 226 brackets with a taker YES buy at 6-12c in 6-12 h, in 107 events; 50,531 contracts.
test.n_independent_clusters: 107 events with fills, out of 150 sampled (one S&P close per event; all brackets of an event share it). ES test: 38 events.
test.result: THE IDEA FAILS ITS OWN BAR. Brackets where takers actually bought YES at 6-12c, 6-12 h out, paid 18 of 226 times (8 per 100; the bar was <= 3) at an average price of about 9.3c. So the price was fair. P&L: at the taker's price +2.29c/contract, se 2.94, 50,531 contracts. 1c inside with a 100 cap: -0.68c/contract, se 2.16, 12,847 contracts = 86 per event, -$0.58 per event. Early half -1.19c, late half -0.07c (75 events each). Upper 95% about +3.6c, still under the +4c bar. Adverse selection is the cause: quoted 6-12c asks that sat unfilled at 12 h paid 0 of 106 (hunter's candles), but the ones takers actually lifted paid 8 of 100. Worst events (taker price, no cap): 2026-06-22 -$916, 2026-04-08 -$385. A distance-from-close filter picked on the early half gives -0.07c on the late half at cap 100. ES-FILTERED VARIANT (new hypothesis; 2026-08-11..10-15 only): price minus ES fair at the moment takers bought had a median of +3.7c. Brackets where ES said fair >= price: 2 paid of 15. Gap 0-4c: 3 of 15. Gap > 4c: 0 of 36. Rule fair <= price - 4c, 1c inside, cap 100: 1,513 contracts in 47 trading days (32 a day), +8.4c, $126.66 = $2.69 per trading day. Margin picked on the early half (5c), scored on the late half: +7.96c on 1,260 contracts, 8 events, 0 losing. Cap 500: $5.95 per trading day (supply-limited). Zero hits in 36 brackets can't rule out a true hit rate up to about 8 per 100, which would erase it. SIDE CELLS (found by looking at a 25-cell grid, so they are only hypotheses; both halves agree): selling YES at 1-3c 6-12 h out +2.2c/+2.2c (1 hit in 89 brackets), $0.47/trading day at cap 100; 6-12c 12-20 h +7.8/+8.8c, $1.23/day; 3-6c in the last 0.5-1 h +5.1/+5.4c, $0.67/day; 1-3c 1-3 h +2.8/+2.2c, $1.02/day. Mirror image: buying YES at 1-6c loses 2-4c/contract (t -2 to -3.6). Cheap S&P tails are overpriced, but only by pennies of money a day.
test.artefact_checks: Units: *_dollars fields; every trade price lies in 0.01-0.99; direction from taker_outcome_side (taker_side is deprecated). Every event has exactly one YES bracket; results only yes/no. No bracket needed a second page (max 1), so nothing was cut off. Duplicate lines from a briefly doubled puller (my own orphaned process, stopped) are removed by keying on ticker. The volume >= 25 exclusion dropped 280 low-volume brackets (0 paid, 2,507 contracts). Even if all of them were winning sales, the result is +0.74c, not +4c. Dropping the one partly-pulled event changes nothing (-0.68c). The ES fair uses only the 5-min bar closed before each trade, plus the previous close's gap. The sd was fit on the early half. Historical Yahoo bars are not delayed, but the free live Yahoo ES=F is about 10 min late, so the ES test is OPTIMISTIC for a live bot. The ES test's '0 hits' is a calm Aug-Oct 2026 window (8-11% annual vol). Only 3 of 21 April-2025 crash days are in the sample. Calls used about 1,550 (slightly over the 1,500 guide), all public GETs. Both recorders were still writing at 11:30 ET (tape and feed files updated that minute; their command lines are not readable from this shell). Disk 111.5 GB free; scratch 3.6 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: KXINX daily only (KXNASDAQ100 not measured; the catalogue showed 567 contracts in 24 h). Taker YES buys at 6-12c in 6-12 h: 337 contracts per event uncapped, very lumpy: in Aug-Oct 2026 the top 5 trades were 79% of contracts (one 9,965-lot); the median trade was 9 contracts. At cap 100 we would get at most 86 per event, or 32 per day with the ES filter, assuming we sit 1c inside the 100,000-lot incumbent and it does not follow us down.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 for the rule as proposed (central -$0.58 per trading day). The ES-filtered variant, if its zero-hit run held up: about $1.30-2.70 per trading day at 100 lots, not established.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0 as proposed. ES-filtered at cap 500: about $4-6 per trading day if it held; capped by taker flow, not by bank.

test.worst_case: Only one bracket pays per event, so the worst day is about one sold bracket paying: -$91 per 100 contracts sold at 9c, -$455 at cap 500. Worst event seen at cap 100: -$90 (several). Uncapped, the incumbent's worst was -$916 (2026-06-22). A crash regime like April 2025 is barely sampled (3 days), so its rate of hits is not measured.
test.next_test: Do not build the 6-12c/6-12h rule. Only if a cheap REAL-TIME ES or SPX-futures feed is available (the free Yahoo one is about 10 min late): a paper recorder on the KXINX daily ladder. Every 60 s from 4 AM to 4 PM ET, record the book and live ES. Paper-sell YES 1c inside the best ask on any bracket at 1-12c whose ES fair <= ask - 4c, cap 100. test.method: I pulled every KXJOBLESSCLAIMS event Kalshi still serves: 61 events, 600 markets, Jun 2025 to Oct 2026. Markets settled before the 2026-08-17 cutoff came from /historical/markets, /historical/trades and /historical/.../candlesticks. The 10-13 hunter only had 10 events. For each market I took hourly candles (yes bid/ask) for its whole life and the full trade tape: 1,340 unauthenticated GETs, no auth, no orders. First prints come from Kalshi expiration_value and agree with the Nasdaq calendar 'actual' on 52 of 52 events. The Nasdaq calendar (api.nasdaq.com/api/calendar/economicevents?date=D+1; the date shifts by one day) also gives survey consensus and the revised prior week. Model, as a bot would see it: next first print ~ Normal(last FIRST print + 310, sd 10,062). A second version adds mean reversion: -0.379 x (last - 4-week average), sd 9,654. Parameters were fit on FRED ICSA 2023-01..2025-05, before the first Kalshi event, so the whole Kalshi sample is out of sample for the model. Decision times: R + h hours, where R is the prior release (previous close + 5 min); h = 2..166. Quote = the last hourly candle closed at or before t. Rule as pre-registered by the hunter: take when model edge > fee (10-lot rounding) + 5c. Two holdouts. (a) Time: train = 30 events Jun 2025-Mar 2026, test = 29 events Apr-Oct 2026. (b) Design: the 49 events the rule was NOT designed on, against the hunter's 10. Fill checks: did the quote survive to the next hourly candle, and did tape takers trade the same side at that price within 1 h. Live book read of the open OCT22 ladder. Maker variant: tape population, resting at model +/- 3/6/10c. Source rank: trade tape plus Kalshi candles; no replay; no fills of our own exist on this series. Self-test: profit in an efficient world fails, a missed planted edge fails; passed. test.result: TIME HOLDOUT. Persistence rule, margin 5c. R+24h (= the hunter's 'H=144 before close', Friday 08:30 ET, not the Thursday open): train +9.7c/leg (59 legs, 16 events, se 6.8) vs TEST -2.0c/leg (50 legs, 16 events, se 7.2). R+48h: +9.7 vs +0.4. R+96h: +12.5 (se 4.9) vs -1.8 (se 4.9). R+144h: +5.9 vs -7.1. R+156h: +8.4 vs -12.5. The mean-reversion version is the same: test +0.7c at R+24h, -1.8c at R+96h. DESIGN HOLDOUT. The hunter's 10 events reproduce after fixing his look-ahead: +11.2c/leg, 22 legs. The other 19 test-half events (Apr-Jul 2026 + Oct 15): -12.4c/leg at R+24h (28 legs, 9 events) and -8.0c/leg at R+96h (60 legs, 16 events). Pooled over all 59 events: R+24h +4.3c/leg (se 5.0), R+96h +5.6c/leg (se 3.6); neither is significant. MECHANISM. The profit was one directional bias: the market ladder (and the survey consensus, mean error -3.0k over 59 weeks) priced claims too high. At R+24h, NO legs made +9.8c/leg (79) and YES legs lost -10.2c/leg (30). The market median sat above the actual print by +3.97k in train and +2.66k in test, so the bias shrank. NO-only: train +18.1c/leg vs test +1.8c (R+24h); +18.7 vs -1.8 (R+96h). FORECAST ACCURACY. Mean miss on the print at R+24h (n=48 events): market median 7.47k, persistence 7.28k, consensus 7.02k, a tie. At R+156h the market wins: 6.50k vs persistence 7.97k. FILLS. 84% of triggered quotes were still there an hour later. Those legs paid +6.4c pooled at R+24h (train +9.6, test +1.9). The quotes that vanished were the good ones: at R+6h they would have paid +26.7c vs +3.8c for the ones that stayed. MAKER VARIANT (tape population, not our fills). On the 49 unseen events, contract-weighted results are -15c (R+0-24h), -14c (24-96h) and -17c (96h-close) per contract at a 3c offset, and -9 to -16c at a 6-10c offset.

(8) Candle-close quotes can be stale or tiny. Checked with next-hour survival and the tape; surviving quotes pay less. (9) A live book read showed what the candles imply for recent weeks: no maker early in the week.

test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0/day. Book-capped, not bank-capped; the bank size does not matter here.

test.worst_case: Worst single week at 10 lots a leg: -$20.34 (R+24h rule) or -$19.17 (R+48h), from a 5-7 leg directional stack on one print (e.g. 2025-09-18: last print 263k, actual 231k; 2026-04-09: 202k to 219k). At 20 lots that is about -$40 a week. The legs of one event all lose together.
test.next_test: None worth a bot. A zero-cost watcher could decide a revival: every Friday at R+24h for 8 weeks, read the KXJOBLESSCLAIMS ladder (number of two-sided strikes, ATM spread, market median minus last first print). Revive only if, over those 8 weeks, at least 5 strikes are two-sided with an ATM spread of 10c or less AND the market median sits at least +3k above the last print on average (the train-half bias). Even then it is a directional regime bet (fading the market's high-side lean), not a model edge; re-run analyze.py out of sample before any money. idea.name: Election counting-hour projection desk: a county-baseline model of the running count vs Kalshi's winner markets and margin-of-victory ladders, Nov 3 (paper first)
markets: SENATETX-26, SENATEME-26, SENATEMI-26, SENATEOHS-26, SENATEIA-26, SENATEAK-26, GOVPARTY*-26
KXMIDTERMMOV-<race>-P<n> (4,902 open, 4,532 two-sided; one grid quoter, rungs ~8c wide, median bid 200 lots, ask 5 lots)
KXHOUSERACE toss-ups (CO04, NY21, FL14, SC01, AL02, OH07, VA05)
idea.mechanism: 1) Before Nov 3 build county baselines for 3 races (2024/2022 county results, expected vote, early/mail split). 2) On the night poll free county feeds (state SoS pages) every 30-60 s and compute a projected margin and its uncertainty. 3) Winner markets: rest quotes at fair +- margin, take only when fair beats the market by >= 5c with small count uncertainty, stop at any contradiction (relapse guard). 4) MOV ladders: once the projected margin is tight, sell rungs far above it into the 200-lot bids and buy decided rungs below it if 5-lot asks survive.
idea.why_mispriced: The crowd trades off raw running totals and TV: SC runoff 57c at poll close, 85c +11 min, 91c +20, 96c +46, 99c +60 min with 3.75M contracts in that hour (1.45M at 80-90c). The MOV grid quoter's 8c-wide ladders may lag the count. Politics takers lose ~1.9c a contract pre-fee.
idea.must_be_true: Our model beats the crowd by minutes, not seconds -- and the crowd has the free NYT needle and paid DDHQ/AP feeds (free county feeds lag AP by 1-5 min); the count does not reverse (relapses after 95c: 6 of 64 thin, 0 of 9 liquid); the 80-90c runoff volume was not two informed sides trading each other; MOV rungs actually trade during the count (the 10-13 window landed on certification days: 0 night volume in 21 markets). Capacity on MOV is tiny (5-lot asks).
idea.evidence_so_far: Price paths only, no model built: KXSCRSENS-26-DNOR runoff (12.0M contracts) 57c -> 99c in 60 min; FL-25 D 95c at +6 min, 99c at +14-16 min (~30k contracts). This run (r1-structural-arb-scan): MOV x vote-share x winner ladders measured consistent after fees (0 positive in 1,734 exclusive pairs and 3,479 MOV-vs-winner pairs; nest 'positives' need a third party <= 3% or ranked choice). Model edge vs market: not measured (n = 0).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Nov 3: $0 (paper). If the model leads by 3c+ on the recording: tens of dollars a night at the current bank (deep winner books, 5-lot MOV asks), a few hundred at $5,000, about 10 nights a year. Worst plausible live night: a mirage fills 85-90c bids on the eventual loser = -$85-90 per 100 contracts (cap 2 contracts a race on the first live night).
idea.settlements_per_day: One night (Nov 3) plus primaries/specials (~10 nights a year)
idea.test_plan: (1) URGENT, free: before the purge (~60 days after settlement; Aug 6-11 primaries are due now), re-pull 1-min candles and trades for the 40 biggest KXPRIMARYMOV markets windowed on the primary NIGHT, not the certification close (~80 public calls): do MOV rungs trade during the count and how stale is the grid? (2) Build baselines for TX, ME and the OH special; on Nov 3 run read-only and log fair value per minute (uses C3-02's recorder). Bars: fair leads the Kalshi mid by >= 3c for >= 5 consecutive minutes in >= 2 of 3 races, never on the wrong side by > 5c after 20% counted; MOV: >= $200 of resting asks under 95c on rungs below the reported margin surviving 10 s after calls. Fail = drop the lane until 2028.
idea.prior_reason: A real build (county baselines in 19 days) for one night against a crowd that watches the free NYT needle and paid feeds; Kalshi already beat ESPN's free model on football (the sports lane's ESPN kill), so a free-feed model edge is unlikely; MOV capacity is 5-lot asks.

test.method:
Read-only. About 540 unauthenticated Kalshi GETs plus about 50 NYT files. NEW SOURCE: Kalshi's /historical archive still serves the Nov 5-6 2024 and Nov 4 2025 election nights. It has 1-minute candles (yes bid/ask/trade open-high-low-close) at /historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks?period_interval=1 and the full taker-sided trade tape at /historical/trades?ticker=&min_ts=&max_ts=. The r1 FACT that 'Nov 2024/2025 nights cannot be measured' is wrong. Source rank: Kalshi's own 1-min tape (2), plus NYT/AP timestamped state count histories (eevp, D, R).

(A) Winner markets. 253 markets pulled (PRESPARTY<ST>-24, SENATE<ST>-24, GOVPARTY<ST>-24, GOVPARTYVA/NJ-25, POPVOTEMOV<ST>, KXELECTIONMOVVAGOV/NJGOV). D-win bid/ask was built from both legs (D yes, R no), minute-close carried forward. The model is exactly what a bot would run from a free count feed:
- inputs: running two-party share s; eevp gives the remaining fraction f.
- M0: proj = s.
- M1h / M1f: proj = s + 0.5 or 1.0 x the previous election's state late lean x f.
- sd(f) was FITTED ON 2020 ONLY (79 races).
- fair = Phi((proj-0.5)/sd).
- The bot acts on a snapshot 0, 2 or 5 min after its AP timestamp.
- Take rule: take when fair - ask - 0.07p(1-p) - 1c >= 5c. First entry per race per side, 100 contracts, held to Kalshi settlement.
- Arming at eevp >= 5/30/50/70/85.
The rule was pre-registered in prereg.json before any 2024 price was read. The hindsight ORACLE ceiling uses the true lean of the remaining vote. Holdout: the 2025 VA/NJ night, with sd refit on 2020+2024. Self-tests pass: a planted 10-min market lag gives +10c/entry and a better model Brier score; a market equal to the model gives 0 entries.

(B) MOV ladders. 10 ladders: 8 swing-state 2024 president-margin ladders and the 2025 VA/NJ governor ladders. Same projection mapped to margin, P(rung) from Phi, same take rule. Also measured: night volume and supply on 'far' rungs.

(C) Supply in the mirage windows, from /historical/trades.

(D) Today's Nov 3 books: SENATE*-26 and KXMIDTERMMOV TX/MI.

test.result:
WINNER MARKETS, Kalshi 2024 night. 46 contested races, 2020-fit model, 2-min data lag. Dollars are at 100 contracts an entry.
- M0 (running count), all eevp: -$418 (44 entries, 7 won). Brier score: model 0.120 vs Kalshi mid 0.0275; the model was better in 3 of 43 races.
- Armed only at >= 70% of expected vote counted: M0 -$95 (20 entries, 4 won); M1h -$59; M1f +$28 (18 entries, 5 won).
- Armed only at >= 85%: M0 -$170; M1h -$7; M1f +$59 (11 entries, 3 won).
- Every positive M1f dollar is a Senate trailer in MI, WI or NV (Slotkin 17-25c, Baldwin 27c, Rosen 40-49c). The same rule lost on PA, GA, MI and WI president and on PA Senate. This is r2's already-measured trailer lottery (pooled 2 of 15), not a model edge, and M1f's Brier score is the worst of all (0.12-0.15).
- Lag 0 vs 2 vs 5 min moves results by under $45: the model is wrong in level, not late.
- With 2024's own tighter sd (in-sample, optimistic), M0 at >= 70% loses -$125. Its Brier score is better in 19 of 27 races, but the mean is 0.059 vs 0.030 because it is confidently wrong in the mirage races.
- The idea's own bar, 'never on the wrong side by more than 5c after 20% counted', failed in 36-38 of 46 races for M0/M1, and in 9-10 races even for the hindsight oracle.
- CEILING: the oracle that knows the true lean of the uncounted vote makes +$162 to +$271 for the whole night (7-33 entries).
- 2025 holdout: the VA and NJ winners were at 90-99c before polls closed. One entry, lost 8.5c; no real test was possible.

MOV LADDERS (10 ladders), M0 rule:
- all eevp: -$134 (120 entries)
- >= 70% counted: -$241 (81 entries)
- >= 85% counted: -$267 (63 entries)
- MOV rungs DO trade during the count when liquid: 0.23-3.0M contracts per ladder on the night, 15-22% of lifetime volume.
- 'Far' rungs (at least 3 points from the running margin with <= 20% still out, near-sure side offered at <= 95c): 65 minutes on 5 rungs. The near-sure side won only 41 of those 65 minutes; a Michigan rung lost (the mirage again).
- Step (1) of the test plan, on primary MOV nights, was already done by N1-06: following the favourite lost -16.5c a contract over 25 events.
test.artefact_checks:
1. Units: every candle price is <= 1.0 (asserted over all 253 markets), so prices are dollars.
2. NYT 2024 histories are truncated in some states; Michigan president ends at 94.68% counted, at 05:43 ET Nov 6. Outcomes therefore come only from Kalshi results, never from NYT. The oracle's 'final' is the last NYT snapshot, which is why even the oracle loses on PA Senate.
3. The 2020 sd is about 1.7x 2024's (2020 had big COVID mail shifts). The in-sample 2024 sd variant also loses, so the loss is not only a too-wide sd.
4. The D and R legs were combined as complements. NE Senate (no Democrat) is excluded by the NYT party filter.
5. Quotes are minute-close, so sub-minute crosses are invisible. The intra-minute check (s9) found the Wisconsin Senate Democrat offered at 4c (a 96c bid on the eventual loser) at 01:14 ET Nov 6.
6. Self-tests pass for both estimators.
7. The positive M1f cells were traced race by race, not taken at face value.
8. The 2024 fee schedule was not verified; today's 0.07p(1-p) was used, which is the cost going forward.

idea.name: FanDuel-vs-Kalshi lead-lag poller (free, read-only): does the sportsbook move first, and do > 1.5c gaps close toward Kalshi or FanDuel?

If FanDuel leads, shade resting Kalshi quotes toward FanDuel's new price inside the 1c spread (maker fee 0.44c); if Kalshi leads, a manual FanDuel bet when its price beats Kalshi's fair by more than the fee.
idea.why_mispriced: A sportsbook line moves on its own trader's hand and sharp action, Kalshi's on its own flow; SI59's 0.64c average gap to Pinnacle says nothing about the minutes after a move.
idea.must_be_true: A one-directional lead of >= 1-2 minutes; > 30 gap events a week; fills on the shaded quote are not the informed flow that caused the move (the trap that killed D17 and SI43).
idea.evidence_so_far: One snapshot: 42 sides, median |FD no-vig - Kalshi mid| 0.73c, p90 1.83c, max 2.81c; 1 side of 42 with FD's raw price below Kalshi's mid. No time series.

idea.test_plan: Read-only poller, 7 days, 60-s cadence (~2,000 FD + ~2,000 Kalshi public GETs a day -- run it when no other agent shares the public limit). Bar written now: >= 30 gap events >= 1.5c and the follower moves within 5 min in >= 70% of them; otherwise dead.
