test.method: Instead of a 7-day live poller, I rebuilt the history after the fact. FanDuel side: sportsbookreview.com line-history pages (free, public; /betting-odds/<league>/line-history/<gameId>/ __NEXT_DATA__). They list every pregame moneyline change for 8 US books (fanduel, draftkings, betmgm, bet365, caesars, fanatics, betrivers, hardrock), timed to the second. I checked SBR's FanDuel times against my own direct FanDuel VA poll (30-s cadence, 2026-10-16 15:36-15:57Z): all 4 matched changes were stamped 30-45 s BEFORE my poll saw them, so SBR's times are good to under a minute. Kalshi side: public 1-minute candles of the home-team market over the last 36 h before start; mid used only when spread <= 3c. 316 games matched by date and both team names (NHL 109 analysed, NFL 80, MLB 72, NBA preseason 54), 2026-09-10..10-16. Tests: (a) the pre-registered bar: starts of a |FanDuel no-vig - Kalshi mid| gap >= 1.5c, and whether either side closes half of it within 5 min; (b) event studies around FanDuel moves >= 1c (flicker filtered) and Kalshi 1-minute jumps >= 1.5c; (c) a regression of how much of the gap 24h/6h/1h/15min out each venue closes by the start; (d) the taker rule a bot would run: after a FanDuel move, buy Kalshi at the ask (or 1-bid) one minute later if FanDuel no-vig beats it by fee (0.07p(1-p), MLB x0.5) plus a margin of 0/0.5/1c. Valued at Kalshi mid +15/30/60 min, at Kalshi's pregame close, and at the other 7 books' closing no-vig; (e) the bet-at-FanDuel form: FanDuel's own price (vig included) better than Kalshi mid by >= 0.5c, valued against FanDuel's own closing price. Every average is clustered by game. Holdout split at 2026-10-08 (early vs late). Also re-run with each game's typical FanDuel-Kalshi offset removed. Self-test with planted FanDuel-leads and Kalshi-leads worlds: PASS before real data. Sources: SBR history plus Kalshi candles (tape-grade). No replay used. Settlement outcomes appear only as noise checks. Scripts and outputs in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C3-13/ (leadlag.py, sbr_pull.py, sbr_pull_wk.py, match_pull.py, k_list.py, calib.py, fd_poll.py; leadlag_*.json, calib.json, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 316 games (one home-team market each; the away market is its mirror): NHL 109, NFL 80, MLB 72, NBA preseason 54. Within them: 802 FanDuel moves >= 1c, 886 gap events >= 1.5c, 122 qualifying taker trades, 296 FanDuel-bet signals.
test.n_independent_clusters: 316 games (each settles once). 225 games had a gap event, 67 a taker trade, 105 a FanDuel-bet signal.
test.result:
THE BAR FAILS. Gap events are plentiful: 886 in 225 games, and NHL alone had 240 in 15 days, far above 30 a week. But they don't close within 5 minutes. Kalshi closed half the gap in 48 (5%), FanDuel in 111 (13%), both in 2, and NEITHER in 725 (82%); the bar needed one side at >= 70%. At 30 minutes neither had still closed it in 544 of 812 (67%). Holdout halves: neither 83% early, 81% late. With each game's typical offset removed: 692 events, neither 74% at 5 min.

WHO MOVES FIRST: there is no clean one-way lead of several minutes. FanDuel's moves (average 1.8c) are mostly catch-ups: just before moving, FanDuel sat 1.08c (se 0.06) behind Kalshi in the direction it then moved. Kalshi moved 0.68c the same way in the 30 min before a FanDuel move and 0.81c (se 0.09) in the 30 min after, so both are reacting to the same news. After a Kalshi jump >= 1.5c (214 jumps, 84 games), FanDuel followed: +0.96c within 2 min, +1.45c within 5, +1.77c (se 0.29) within 30. Of the gap 1 h before start, FanDuel closes 38% (se 8%) by the start and Kalshi 9% (se 9%); 15 min out, FanDuel 32% (se 4%) and Kalshi -1% (se 4%). In the last hour Kalshi leads and FanDuel follows, which is the opposite of the premise that we shade Kalshi toward FanDuel.

MONEY, TAKER ON KALSHI: at margin 0, 122 trades in 67 games. Value per contract: -1.19c 30 min later (se 0.18), -0.69c at Kalshi's pregame close (se 0.51), -0.58c against the other books' close (se 0.49). At 30 min the halves are -1.05c early and -1.32c late. At margin 1c, 39 trades: -0.73c at 30 min and +1.28c at the close (se 1.24). That splits into +2.25c early (se 2.09, 21 trades) and +0.14c on the holdout (se 1.08, 18 trades), and is -0.82c with the offset removed. Nothing survives.

MONEY, BET AT FANDUEL: 296 signals in 105 games (2% of minutes). The apparent edge is 1.2c when the signal fires. Against FanDuel's own closing price it is worth -0.01c (se 0.43); against Kalshi's close +0.26c (se 0.45). Halves: -0.56c early, +0.46c late. Settlement return is -17.9% per dollar staked (se 11.6), which is noise.

MAKER FORM: not measured (the candles carry no queue data). Kalshi pregame books are 1c wide with thousands of contracts at the best price, so there is no room to post inside the spread. Kalshi drifts only 0.47c in the 5 min after a FanDuel move, against a maker fee of about 0.44c at 50c.

So SBR is not a slow copy that could fake a Kalshi lead, and the result over several hours doesn't depend on minute timing anyway. 2) Self-test: in the planted FanDuel-leads world, Kalshi moved +2.05c after FanDuel moves and closed 867 of 889 gaps. In the planted Kalshi-leads world, FanDuel closed 881 of 900. PASS before touching real data. 3) No-vig method bias (the multiplicative split leans toward favourites): re-ran with each game's median FanDuel-Kalshi offset removed. The bar still fails (74% neither) and the 1c-margin taker is -0.82c at the close. 4) Kalshi mid is used only when spread <= 3c. The candles include zero-volume bars, so quote changes without trades are captured. 5) Flicker filter: a FanDuel change reverted within 3 min is skipped. 6) Matching is by date plus both team names: 0 NHL games since 10-01 went unmatched. 17 MLB events and 35 NHL preseason events were skipped (unmatched, or outside the SBR pull). 7) Every number has the 2026-10-08 holdout split. 8) Settlement-outcome P&L is shown only as a noise check; n is far too small for it. 9) NOT checked: timing finer than one minute (1-min candles); NBA regular season (only preseason, where rest news makes lines jumpier); spreads and totals (moneyline only); per-order taker fee rounding (<= 1c per 98-lot order, ignored). Both recorders were writing at 2026-10-16 15:59Z (newest kalshi_data/ticker and feed_data files). Their command lines are hidden from this shell, so this is a file-freshness check, not a process check. Disk 112 GB free; scratch 5.2 MB; about 400 Kalshi public GETs, about 310 SBR GETs, about 230 FanDuel GETs.

The taker rule fires about 3.4 times a day across the 4 leagues (122 in about 36 days, mostly NBA preseason and NHL). idea.name: Album-units nowcast from kworb's Spotify daily charts against the Luminate-settled album ladders (WEAK, model needed)
markets: KXPUREALBUMS (Luminate week Fri-Thu, close Sun 14:00Z, ~11 rungs per album, 4-5 albums/week)
idea.mechanism: Each morning (kworb US daily chart posts ~04-06Z, dated D-2) sum the album's track streams, scale by a fitted Spotify-to-Luminate ratio to total streams and album-equivalent units; on days 2-4 of the tracking week trade rungs where the projection differs from the market by > 8c; close out before Saturday night.
idea.why_mispriced: Decisions arrive progressively (median decision-to-close 114-135 h; decision hours cluster at the daily data drops); 30-50c rungs 48 h out resolved 56% YES (9), 5-15c rungs 12.5% (24). But the final 24 h trades only at 1-5c and 95-99c, i.e. the market already has a Luminate-grade source (SJN6).
idea.must_be_true: A Spotify-only nowcast beats the market's own source on days 2-4 for new releases; physical sales (vinyl, bundles) do not swamp it.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter slow-source: hourly candles on 456 + 309 + 397 settled markets (102 album-weeks, 08-09..10-11): decision-hour histograms and calibration at 1/6/24/48/96 h; kworb's US daily page confirmed scrapeable. No model built. Pro-desk: KXALBUMEQUIV 2 days out, YES ask 0.50-0.89 on 50-80c mids: 5 markets / 4 events, 4 won; KXALBUMSTREAMS asks empty on almost every strike.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Pot ~58k contracts/week at 5-95c within 48 h of close; a 5c edge on 5% of it ~$150/week = ~$20/day; $0 if the market's source is faster (SJN6 says it is). Worst plausible day: -$50 to -$90 per 98 contracts on a rung the projection missed.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~15-20 markets/day equivalent (all close Sunday 14:00Z)
idea.test_plan: 4 weeks read-only: log kworb daily sums for every album with open rungs, the Kalshi book at 14:00Z daily, and the settled units; fit the ratio on weeks 1-2, test on 3-4. Pass: projection error under 3% by day 4 and a >= 5c average edge vs the market on >= 20 rungs in the test weeks.
idea.prior_reason: SJN6 already showed the market has a Luminate-grade source; a Spotify-only input is unlikely to beat it.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SJN6 used HITS' Friday projection (6 of 13 wrong side); the daily-stream nowcast is an earlier, different input.
idea.worst_case: A physical-sales surprise Spotify cannot see: -$50-90 per 98 contracts on the affected rungs.

test.method: Sources: (1) Kalshi trade tape as hourly candles (hunter's r1-slow-source-settlement-lag/candles: 456 KXALBUMEQUIV + 309 KXALBUMSTREAMS + 397 KXPUREALBUMS settled markets, closes 08-09..10-11) and settled Luminate values (expiration_value); (2) kworb.net Spotify data (raw public charts): US daily top-200 page, US/global daily pages, and 723 track pages (US weekly table = Spotify week Fri-Thu = the Luminate tracking week; daily table = last ~31 chart days only). No replay. Steps: t2 calibration/Brier of the ladder at d1..d9 18Z (d0 = release Friday); t6 the market's own implied median (monotone PAVA ladder, log-strike interpolation) and its error vs the settled value by tracking day; t8 the BEST CASE of the idea: the whole tracking week of Spotify US streams for the album's new tracks (weekly table, daily when it covers the week), ratio Luminate/Spotify fitted on the earlier half of events, tested on the later half, compared with the market's own error on the same events; the US top-200 cutoff (#200 = 293k streams/day on the 10-14 chart); the US share of Spotify streams across 78 artists on both the US and global charts (the spread a global-count nowcast would carry). Spin-off (t5/t9): the ladder's own calibration on days 2-4 with executable candle quotes (spread <= 8c), event-clustered, first/second-half holdout, 4 snapshot hours. Open-book snapshot (t7, 27 public calls). Holdout = earlier vs later close dates. Scripts and outputs in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-13/ (t1-t9 *.py/*.out, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 1,162 settled album-ladder markets (456 EQUIV, 309 STREAMS, 397 PURE). Spotify-linked: 7 STREAMS events and 9 EQUIV events have any Spotify-visible album track (of 26 and 40).
test.n_independent_clusters: 102 album-weeks (40 EQUIV, 26 STREAMS, 36 PURE events); nowcast holdout 4 STREAMS + 5 EQUIV events; spin-off 22-28 EQUIV events per snapshot hour
test.result: KILL: the idea's input cannot see what it is meant to nowcast. The US Spotify chart lists only tracks above 293k US streams a day. Visible US Spotify streams in the tracking week as a share of the Luminate total: Rod Wave 1.9M of 108.6M (1.8%), Alex Warren 0.46M of 24.1M (1.9%), Quavo 0.32M of 20.3M (1.6%), Yeat 0.96M of 15.2M (6%), Miley 0.77M of 16.2M (5%), Jhene Aiko 3.4M of 79.7M (4%), ADELA 7.9M of 27.9M (28%, one #1 single). The Luminate/visible ratio runs from 3.5x to 63x (sd of log 1.0 on STREAMS, 1.34 on EQUIV). Holdout: even with the FULL week of Spotify known, the fitted-ratio nowcast's median error is a factor of 2.5 (|log err| 0.905 STREAMS, 0.853 EQUIV), and it beat the market's day-3 price on 0 of 5 holdout events. The market's own median error (implied median vs settled value): EQUIV 9.1% at d2, 7.5% d3, 8.4% d4, 3.6% d6; STREAMS 20.5% d2, 9.6% d3, 5.9% d4. This week's three most-traded ladders (Troye Sivan, Remi Wolf, Dominic Fike; 101k contracts lifetime) have ZERO new-album tracks on the US chart on day 6. A global all-track input does exist (kworb album pages, e.g. Troye's 'She's the Best' at 31.5M global by 10-14). But the US share of an artist's streams varies with sd 0.27 in log (p10 17%, p90 35%) even on the friendliest sample (78 artists on both charts). That alone is 3x the market's d3-d4 error, before Spotify's unknown share of all US platforms. The market already reacts when Spotify posts (d1 16-19Z carry 41% of that day's EQUIV price movement). SPIN-OFF (not the idea, found after looking): on KXALBUMEQUIV days 2-4 the YES favourite (ask 65-95c, spread <= 8c, first qualifying snapshot) won at every snapshot hour. 18Z: 40 markets/22 events, 0 losing events, +13.1c a contract (se 1.05c; chance of 0 losing events if the asks were fair 0.035). 12Z: +8.3c (47/24, 2 losing events). 00Z: +11.9c (34/22, 1). 06Z: +3.3c, se 4.9c (56/28, 4). The holdout half is +9 to +13c at all four hours. The NO-side mirror LOSES (-6.3c at 18Z, 16 losses in 78), so the effect is 'the ladder under-calls units on days 2-4', not favourite-longshot. KXALBUMSTREAMS under the same rule has 2-4 markets per hour, too few to judge; KXPUREALBUMS is negative. About 24 looks were taken (4 hours x 2 sides x 3 bands x 3 series), so this is a hypothesis, not a finding.
test.artefact_checks: (1) The first pass bought the candle yes_ask with no spread filter and showed big losses at 0.96-0.97 asks on rungs that settled NO. Those were one-sided ghost asks on wide books (bid 0.01-0.02); with spread <= 8c the losses vanish, and every reported spin-off number uses the filter. (2) kworb's daily table keeps only the last ~31 chart days, so long-running hits lose their release week there. For those the weekly table (full run) was used; daily data only when it covers the whole week. (3) Album tracks are matched by kworb primary artist and a first chart date within 120 days, so features credited to another lead artist are missed. That can undercount visible streams by maybe 1.5-2x, not the 4-60x gap. (4) Week labels: kworb weekly '2026/09/10' = Fri 09-04..Thu 09-10, confirmed on PRIMA (released 09-04). (5) The implied-median error uses a PAVA-monotone ladder; events whose ladder never brackets 50c are left out (n 12-30 per day). The d9 18Z snapshot is after the 14Z close and is not used. (6) Spin-off: candles give the quote at the hour end, not the size at the touch. The same events appear at all four hours, so the hours are not independent confirmations. Recorders checked after the jobs: kalshi_data/ticker and feed_data files written within the last minute; disk 111 GB free; scratch folder 5.8 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: Idea: none, because there is no usable signal to trade. For reference, KXALBUMEQUIV trades ~21k contracts/day and KXALBUMSTREAMS ~20k/day series-wide (catalogue 24 h). Open EQUIV books show ~100 contracts at the touch per rung (one maker posting 100-lots about 4c either side). STREAMS books carry 4-7k resting contracts (reward farmers; KXALBUMSTREAMS pays $282 per 7 days of liquidity rewards over 49 markets). Spin-off: ~5 qualifying EQUIV markets a week, with a median 133 contracts traded at or below the snapshot ask within 24 h per market (an upper bound, not our fills).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 for the Spotify nowcast. The spin-off is not measured on fills: the upper bound is ~5 markets/week x 100 contracts x +13c = ~$9/day; at a more cautious +5c it is ~$3.5/day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0 for the nowcast (no edge to scale). The spin-off is capped by the ~100-contract touch, not the bank, so it is about the same $3-9/day at $5k.
test.worst_case: Nowcast, if traded anyway: rungs missed by a factor of 2 cost -$50 to -$90 per 98 contracts per rung, with several rungs of one album on the same side. Spin-off: one 85c YES favourite that misses costs -$85 per 100 contracts; a whole album under-delivering hits 2-3 rungs at once, -$170 to -$250 that day.
test.next_test: Nowcast: no further test. It is dead on what the input can see (US chart cutoff 293k/day; 1.6-6% of the Luminate total visible on 6 of 7 STREAMS events) and on the US-share spread (sd 0.27 in log) of any global-count substitute, against a market that is already 6-10% accurate by days 3-4. Spin-off (KXALBUMEQUIV YES favourite, days 2-4): run a read-only paper logger for 6 weeks. Each day at 18Z, record every open EQUIV rung on tracking days 2-4 with yes ask 65-95c and spread <= 8c (the first time it qualifies), plus the displayed ask size; score at settlement with the taker fee. Pre-registered bar: >= 25 markets over >= 15 album-weeks, net >= +4c a contract, at most 2 losing album-weeks, positive in both 3-week halves. Only then a 10-contract live test, with the operator's sign-off.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Nowcast vs market: with 4-5 holdout events, only an error gap of about 2x is detectable. The measured gap runs the other way and is larger (nowcast off by 2.5x against the market's 6-25%). Spin-off: with 22 events and an event-level sd of ~5c (18Z: se 1.05c), about +2-3c a contract is detectable at one hour; across the 24 looks the bar is about +4c.

idea.name: Daily-high weather big-print follower: after a top-2% sweep at 20-80c on a fixed-close daily-high market, buy the same side (WEAK, 9-14 events)
idea.mechanism: Watch the public trade feed on daily-high markets; when one sweep >= the series' 98th-percentile size buys a side at 20-80c with > 5 min to close, buy the same side at the next price (within 2c of the sweep's); hold to settlement.
idea.why_mispriced: The sweeps look like a forecast-model bot acting on a model run: the price keeps moving their way for 30 minutes, so the resting quotes were stale against the update and stay partly stale for a minute. The stale resting quotes pay.
idea.must_be_true: (1) 9-14 events become 40+ with the same sign. (2) The follower's price within 2c of the sweep's. (3) The measured clip pool also contained KXRAIN, which closes early on determination (a hindsight window) -- the re-measure must use fixed-close daily highs only.
idea.evidence_so_far: Weather clips at 20-80c: 30-min continuation +10.2c (se 1.1, 14 events) vs small-print control -3.4c (10 events) -- unlike sports, size matters here; clip's own P&L to settlement +7.65c (se 3.9, 14 ev); follower at the next same-side trade +5.5c (se 6.0, 9 ev).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: If +5c held on 20 contracts and 5 events/day: ~$5/day at $1,155; ~$10-15/day at $5,000 (depth-capped). Worst plausible day: -$50 (a 50c follow losing 20 contracts = -$10, five of them).
idea.settlements_per_day: ~25 daily-high events, perhaps 3-8 qualifying sweeps
idea.test_plan: Three weeks of public trades on the 5 series (~150 calls/week), daily highs only: pre-registered bar 40+ events, follower >= +3c net after fee, both halves positive.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Weather rows (D01, D05, T04, SJ02, SJ32) are model-vs-market or lottery-side; following the informed sweep needs no model. Carried index-ladders 'Follow the whale' (S&P, ~$0) and the sports clip-follow (dead, below) are the same shape on other families.
idea.worst_case: -$50 on a bad day at 20 contracts.
idea.prior_reason: 9-14 events with se 6.0 on the follower's own P&L, pool contaminated by an early-close series, ~$5/day ceiling at this bank.

test.method: Source: Kalshi public trade tape (rank 2) plus Kalshi's own 1-minute event candlesticks; no replay, no model. Pulled with full cursor paging (no auth): 762 settled daily-high markets, 128 city-day events, 27 dates spread over 2026-08-10..2026-10-15 (every 4th date, shuffled order, so the budget cut leaves an even spread), 5 series KXHIGHNY/LAX/MIA/CHI/TPHX, fixed-close daily highs only (KXRAIN removed), 995,320 trades, 1,467 pages, 0 HTTP errors. The rule is coded exactly as a bot would run it. A print is consecutive same-side taker trades within 1 s. A clip is a print of at least max(100, the series' 98th-percentile print size), with the bought side at 20-80c and more than 5 min to close. The thresholds were fit on the FIT half only: NY 461, LAX 935, MIA 468, CHI 407, PHX 367 contracts. The follower buys 20 contracts at the first same-side public trade 1-60 s later, only if that trade is <= the sweep's VWAP + 2c. Taker fee is roundup(0.07*C*P*(1-P)) per order; the position is held to settlement (the result field). Cluster = event, with a date-cluster check. Holdout: FIT = 13 dates 08-10..09-14, TEST = 14 dates 09-15..10-15. Three fill-price models: (a) the tape's next same-side trade (the hunter's method), at a 1, 2 or 5 s delay; (b) the same fills marked to the VWAP 30 min and 2 h later (lower variance; assumes later prices are unbiased); (c) NO tape selection: the bought side's best ask from the 1-min candles 5-65 s after the sweep, for 283 clips in 241 windows. Controls: a small-print follower, a fade (buy the other side), and the average taker. Self-test: plants +37c in one series and finds it; the null series reads -0.5c (se 4.0). Scripts and outputs are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N2-10/ (pull.py, analyse.py -> analyse.out, candles.py -> candles.out, daily.py, RESULT.json). Calls used: 1,965 public GETs, over the ~1,500 guideline because each daily-high event needs about 12 tape pages.
test.n_markets: 762 settled markets (5 series); 924 in-band clips; 434 followed by the tape rule; 283 priced from candles
test.n_independent_clusters: 128 events on 27 dates; tape-follower cell 90 events (44 FIT / 46 TEST); candle-ask cell 107 events; date-clustered se 2.64 on 26 dates vs event-clustered 2.62
test.result: The pre-registered bar FAILS (40+ events, follower >= +3c net, both halves positive). Tape follower (1 s, 2c cap): +2.05c/contract (se 2.62, 90 events); FIT +3.45 (se 3.96), TEST +0.58 (se 3.37). First clip per market only: +0.38c (se 4.82, 72 ev). No cap (the hunter's version): +0.75c (se 2.15, 103 ev). 5 s delay: +1.39c, TEST -0.53c. Without the hunter's 6 events: +1.82c, TEST -0.14c. Marked to the 30-min-later price: -0.29c (se 0.75, 89 ev; FIT -0.24, TEST -0.33); 2 h later: +1.81c (se 1.28). No-selection candle ask 5-65 s after the sweep: -1.34c (se 2.94, 107 ev; FIT -2.79, TEST +0.21); with the 2c cap -2.39c (FIT -2.74, TEST -1.91); first per market -2.74c. What IS real: the hunter's 30-min continuation reproduces, +9.94c (se 1.37, 114 ev, FIT +9.75 / TEST +10.17), vs +0.72c after small prints. But it runs from the PRE-sweep price, and the sweep itself takes it: the next offer is already about fair. The sweeper's own P&L to settlement is +1.81c (se 2.92; FIT +5.8, TEST -2.9). The fade loses -6.5c (se 1.8). The small-print follower loses -3.4c (se 1.6) = the spread+fee a follower pays with no signal; the clip signal wins back only about that much. No series is reliably positive (5 looks; MIA +6.7c on 16 events, PHX +18c on 9 events, both inside noise). Clips peak 1-3 PM ET (afternoon heating, i.e. driven by observations), with a small excess at :50-:59 past the hour (hourly METAR release), not at model-run times.
test.artefact_checks: Prices: yes_price_dollars x100; all 762 markets are price_level_structure linear_cent (the unit is decided from the field, not from magnitude). Sizes: count_fp (fractional counts exist, e.g. 33333.33). Side: taker_outcome_side. Outcome: result -- 127 yes / 635 no across 128 events = one winning bracket per event (one event was cut by the budget). Fee: rounded up to the cent per 20-lot order. Full cursor paging, no truncated tapes (the hunter's sample was 8-10 truncated markets per series). The early-close KXRAIN contamination is removed. Thresholds were fit on FIT only. The hunter's events were excluded in a separate pass. Date clustering gives the same se. The hunter's continuation reproduces (+9.9c vs his +10.2c), so the data agrees. The tape follower's selection ('someone else also bought within 60 s', 47% of clips) was removed with the candle asks; those are guarded against stale quotes (<= 2 min). Ask minus sweep VWAP at 5-65 s: median +0.3c, p10 -3.9c, p90 +7.0c. Recorders checked after the job: kalshi_data and feed_data both wrote files at 12:02 PM ET. Free disk 111 GB; scratch 11.5 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: On KXHIGH* daily-high brackets: about 34 in-band clips/day across the 5 cities. The tape rule finds a same-side offer <= the cap within 60 s on 47% of them = 16 follows/day at 20 contracts (3.7/day if only the first clip per market). Median 42 (p25 11) same-side contracts printed at <= the cap within 60 s: that is the depth we would race other followers for.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 (dead). Point estimates at 20 contracts per follow: tape fill +$6.6/day (daily sd ~$45, so se ~$8.7/day; the TEST half alone +$1.6/day); marked to 30 min -$0.9/day; candle ask -$4.3/day on all clips, -$2.0/day first-per-market.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0. Even if it worked, the depth caps it near 40 contracts per follow.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Settlement P&L: se 2.6c -> about 7c/contract detectable (80% power, 5% two-sided). Marked to 30 min: se 0.75c -> about 2.1c detectable. A true +3c edge would have shown as t ~ 4 in the marked measure; we read -0.29c (upper 95% bound +1.2c).
test.worst_case: Worst sampled day -$81 (all clips, 20 contracts each, 34 follows, $350 committed); first-per-market worst day -$39. Out of 27 days: 11 losing, 15 winning, 1 flat.
test.next_test: None. It fails the pre-registered bar, and two independent fill-price models (marked-to-market and the no-selection candle ask) both read zero or negative in both halves. Do not build the paper bot. The only angle left untested is sub-second following (buying within 0.1-0.3 s, before makers reprice). That needs the public trade + orderbook WebSocket recorded on KXHIGH* for about 2 weeks, with a bar of >= +3c net on 40+ events at the recorded best ask 0.3 s after the sweep. Prior is low: the ask 5-65 s later sits at the sweep's own VWAP (median +0.3c), and the sweeper itself nets only +1.8c.

idea.name: Rain model as a one-sided MAKER inside the KXRAIN liquidity pot (N0-06 x the reward family) -- conditional on N0-06 passing
markets: KXRAIN (each market carries a $100 liquidity program per ~2-day period, target 1,000, 99.3% of pots paid = contested)
idea.mechanism: Instead of taking, rest one-sided toward the model in the evening: a YES bid at (model P - 8c) where the market is below the model, a NO bid where above, 100-500 contracts, pulled when the market has caught up (by ~3 AM local per N0-06's timing). Earns the spread instead of paying it and scores the pot on the quoted side.
idea.why_mispriced: Same stale evening book as N0-06; the lip-economics lane measured a blind two-sided 300 quote on rain at $18 credit vs $21 of fills per day -- the fills were the adverse half; a one-sided model-informed quote keeps only the side the model favours.
idea.must_be_true: N0-06's lead is real (currently +6.3c Sept / 0.0c Oct, unproven); the resting side fills before the price moves (unmeasured); a one-sided quote scores only one side of the pot (both sides must hold >= 1,000 for the second to count).
idea.evidence_so_far: None beyond N0-06's numbers and the carried lip-economics rain pot figures ($18 credit vs $21 fills per day). Not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown; bounded by N0-06 (~$8/day if it held) plus a few dollars of pot share. Worst plausible morning: -$60 per 100-lot YES bid at 60c on a wet day.
idea.test_plan: Only after N0-06 passes its 20-date paper bar: 5 evenings of a 100-lot one-sided rest in a side account; bar >= 50% of rests filled and net >= N0-06's taker net + 2c.
idea.prior_reason: Conditional on a parent that just lost most of its evidence to a look-ahead.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: The lip rows (SI15/SI16, carried lip-economics 'rain $18 vs $21') are blind two-sided quotes; a model-directed one-sided rest is new.
idea.worst_case: The quote is the adverse side on a wet morning: -$60 per 100-lot YES bid at 60c.

test.method: Source: Kalshi's own trade tape (rank 2), not our fills and not pinsim. The rule is the idea's own, written into select_rests.py before any fill was simulated. Quote time and model come from the parent N0-06 tester (newest NBS run public before the quote, at close-30 h = 6-10 PM local the evening before). Side = YES if model P > book mid, else NO. Bid at b = min(P_side - 8c, ask_side - 1c), only where that beats the current best bid (we become the best bid). Rest 8 h, then cancel. Hold fills to settlement. Makers pay no fee on KXRAIN (fee_type quadratic = taker only, from /series/KXRAIN). Fills simulated from the full 8 h trade tape for all 460 markets that rest at the 5c margin (506 unauthenticated calls). Model A: every trade at a side price <= b fills us. Model B: only takers who SOLD our side. Sizes tested: 100, 250, 500. Also run: 5c/12c margins and a 3 h window. Controls: opposite side at best+1c; same side at best+1c; same bid filled in full at the quote (no selection); the parent's taker on the same markets; best-3-dates removal; per month. Holdout = Jul-Aug + Oct, because the parent's rule was chosen on September. Liquidity reward: /incentive_programs read (every KXRAIN market has $100 per ~43.7 h period, open ~09:16Z D-1 to close, target 1,000, 0.5 per tick; 1,891 programs since mid-July, 99.3% paid). Historical book depth is not recorded anywhere, so our reward share uses TODAY's full-depth books (69 open markets, read 10-16 ~12:30 PM ET) as a stand-in, applying the filed formula (self-tested) and the $1.00 per-market-period payout floor. Scripts and outputs in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-12/: dump_fresh.py, select_rests.py, pull_tr.py, sim.py (sim.out), control.py (control.out), books_lip.py, lip_apply.py (lip_apply.out), RESULT.json. ~575 unauthenticated GETs, 0 authenticated, 0 orders.
test.n_markets: 1,754 settled KXRAIN city-day markets scored. 319 rests at the 8c rule (460 at 5c, 210 at 12c), each with its full 8 h trade tape. Plus 69 open markets' full books read today.
test.n_independent_clusters: 75 target dates with a rest (Jul-Aug 34, Sep 29, Oct 12) out of 79 calendar dates. Every city on a date shares the weather, so the dates are the clusters.
test.result: 100-lot rests, 8c rule, 8 h: 90% of rests got a fill (86% under the stricter model B), first fill after a median 29 min. Profit per filled contract: ALL +4.4c (model A, se 2.8, 95% -0.8..+9.7) / +2.3c (model B, se 2.9). September, the month the parent's rule was chosen on: -0.1c / -3.5c. HOLDOUT Jul-Aug+Oct: +9.0c (95% +1.2..+16.1) / +8.6c (+1.1..+16.5). October alone +28c on 12 dates. Best 3 dates = 54% of the profit; without them +2.2c (95% -2.9..+7.3). Being picked by sellers costs 2-4c a contract: the same bids filled in full at the quote would make +6.4c. Opposite-side control loses -7.1c (95% -12.1..-1.9), so the model carries real information. Against the parent's taker on the SAME markets, the taker makes +4.9c a contract. The maker is NOT better per contract, which FAILS the idea's own bar (maker >= taker + 2c). It does get more contracts: 90% of rests fill at 100 lots, against a taker capped by a thin ask. Structural: in 148 of the parent's 296 taker legs the spread is 1c, so a maker cannot get in front. The maker only covers the wide-spread half. Reward (stand-in from today's books): all 23 active two-sided books already hold >= 1,000 a side (YES side median 2,701, NO side median 3,288 -- a farmer's ladder). Our share of a side: ~11% at 100 lots (199 of 319 rests fall under the $1 payout floor -> about $3-4/day), 32-37% at 250 (about $14-18/day), 81-84% at 500 (about $26-28/day). Money per calendar day (79 days), fills + reward: 100 lots +$16.7 (A) / +$10.5 (B); September -$3..+$4/day. 250 lots +$43.8 / +$28.4; September +$6 / -$19. 500 lots +$75.8 / +$44.0, but it needs $805-2,095 posted per evening.
test.artefact_checks: PASSED: (1) Self-tests on the rule, the fill model, payout floor arithmetic and the reward-share walk (planted books). (2) The model carries information: opposite side -7.1c vs ours +4.4c on the same markets. (3) Selection cost measured, not assumed: +6.4c with no selection vs +4.4/+2.3c on fills. (4) Two fill models; the stricter one (sellers only) is shown alongside. (5) The reward program existed across the whole sample (from ISO week 29, 140-223 programs a week) and paid 99.3%. Its units are verified (1,000,000 centi-cents = $100; target 1,000). NOT RESOLVED: (a) historical book depth is unknown, so the reward share is today's books applied to past nights; the farmer may react when we take the top; (b) the tape fill model assumes the same flow would come with our bid present; (c) it is concentrated (best 3 dates 54%; October's +28c rests on 12 dates); (d) several looks: 3 margins x 3 sizes x 2 windows x 2 fill models. The 8c / 8 h / 100-lot cell was named by the idea before the run; (e) rests at best+1c (no model price) did better (+6.8c A, holdout +13.5c), but that was not pre-registered, so it is a hint only; (f) a live bot would re-price when the 00Z run lands inside the window; not simulated (static bid = conservative); (g) one season, summer into autumn; winter is not measured; (h) the parent N0-06 has not yet passed its own paper test.
test.supply_we_would_get: KXRAIN, about 4 rests per evening (319 over 75 of 79 dates; October books are tighter, 28 rests in 15 days). At 100 lots: 90% of rests fill something, 70% fill in full, ~308 contracts a day filled (model A; 265 under B). At 250 lots ~490-650 contracts a day. The flow comes from takers selling through our price on the tape. Reward supply: $100 per market per ~43.7 h period, about $18 of it inside our 8 h window per market, half to each side.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $7/day central at 100 lots (range -$9 to +$17). Fills shrunk to ~+2c a contract (best-3-dates removed / stricter model) x ~280 contracts = ~$5.6, plus ~$3 of reward after the $1 floor. Capital: median $161 posted per evening (p90 $419). Filled contracts stay locked ~36 h, so two nights overlap: needs a ~$400-600 side account, not the main bot's money. A September-like month nets about -$9 to +$3 a day.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $20/day central at 250 lots (range -$20 to +$44): fills $10-29/day (models B/A, all months; September -$8 to -$39) plus reward $14-18/day if our 32-37% share holds. 500 lots would add reward (~$26-28/day) but posts $805-2,095 an evening.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Fill profit per contract: all-sample se 2.8c -> about 8c at 80% power, 5% two-sided. Holdout se 3.8c -> about 11c. So the likely +2-4c a contract cannot be confirmed by this sample, and a 20-evening test (se ~5-7c) cannot confirm it either. The reward credit is the part a short live test CAN measure (paid vs formula).
test.worst_case: Observed worst evening on fills: -$255 at 100 lots (2026-09-06; -$213 on 09-10), -$583 at 250 lots, -$1,142 at 500 lots (09-10). The reward on those dates was only +$4 to +$61. 31 of 75 dates lost money on fills. Plausible bad day at 100 lots: about -$250, with the money back within ~36 h. Regime risk: a month like September (the rule's own month) is zero to negative.
test.next_test: 1) Zero risk, add to the N0-06 paper recorder that starts tonight. At each evening rest, every 10 min for 8 h, log both sides' full depth (our would-be reward share at 100/250 lots by the filed formula, and whether both sides hold >= 1,000) plus the trade tape (fills under models A/B). Bar after 20 evenings (~80 rests): median share at 250 lots >= 25%, seconds counted >= 80%, model-B fill profit >= 0c a contract. Kill if model B is <= -3c after 20 evenings. 2) Only if 1) and N0-06 both pass: micro-live in a new ~$300 subaccount for 10 evenings at 250 lots on the 2 best rests a night (clears the $1 floor), cancel at +8 h. Bar: reward paid >= 70% of the formula (credited to main pool 0 after each market closes), >= 50% of rests filled, fills + reward >= +$5 an evening. Kill at -$150 cumulative. Writer: add both to results/READS_DUE.json. Ledger notes: KXRAIN's reward farmer keeps ~2,700/3,300 contracts a side on every active book; half of the parent's taker legs have a 1c spread, so no maker can improve them; this is the first rain-reward version whose fills are not negative (blind two-sided quoting was $18 of credit vs $21 of fill losses).

refs.strongest_objection: Execution does not kill it, but it turns it into a reward farm whose trading half is a coin flip. In the season a bot would trade from now (Sep+Oct, 41 dates, 172 rests), the 100-lot fills make +0.4c a contract (se 3.8), which is +$1.17 a day. At 250 lots they lose: -0.8c, or -$4.70 a day. September alone is -3.5c. About three quarters of the income is the liquidity reward ($3.26 a day at 100 lots, $15.28 at 250), and it is measured only on midday books, because the 6-10 PM book is not recorded anywhere. The worst observed fill day is -$237 at 100 lots (-$583 at 250), against under $10 of reward that day. YES bids under 10c lose on every cut (-5.6c, se 0.8, 29 rests). That is the longshot effect the SJ02 desk bets against, so the two desks would sit on opposite sides of the same markets. Attempts to refute on execution that failed: (1) Queue position. 241 of 319 rests sit at the ask minus 1c, so nobody can get in front without crossing. Counting only trade-through fills gives +2.1c vs +2.3c. (2) The big resting order (the 'farmer') does not chase the best price: it moved with the best bid on only 7 of 81 best-bid changes. A 100-lot bid does not move the reward reference level either, so the share is unchanged if the farmer joins us (26.0% vs 25.9%); at 250 lots it costs about 10%. (3) Someone else sold above our bid within 10 minutes of the quote on only 17 of 319 rests.

refs.strongest_objection: This is a statistics problem, not a bug: the maker's fills have no edge outside 12 October dates. From July to September, under the stricter fill model (only sellers fill us), the rests make +0.2c a contract over 63 dates (se 3.0; 95% -5.9..+5.7). That is about $0.70 a day. October alone carries the result: +23.7c, se 6.9. October's no-selection figure, +21.9c, is about 3 times the parent taker's October +6.6c, so it looks like 12 lucky dates rather than a stable edge. The tester's 'holdout' (Jul-Aug + Oct) looks good only because it contains October; Jul-Aug on its own is +5.2c with se 4.2. The whole sample spans just 12 ISO weeks, so the smallest effect it can detect is about 8-9c a contract, while the likely true effect is 0-4c. Neither the 20-evening paper test nor the 10-evening micro-live can settle the fill edge. Two parts are solid. The reward pays $1-3 a day at 100 lots. Adverse selection is measured, not assumed: rests whose offer never came down to our bid would have made +13.5c, against +5.0c for the rests that did get filled. Bids under 10c lose 5.6c a contract. Worst evening at 100 lots: -$237 to -$264 (09-06). 30-36 of the 75 dates lost money.

idea.name: AAA gas ladders as a maker: replicate the makers' station feed (GasBuddy nightly for daily/weekly; RBOB pass-through for the monthly)
markets: KXAAAGASD (230-370k contracts/day, 17 strikes at 0.5c, closes 23:59 ET the night before the AAA print)
KXAAAGASM (monthly, maker-fee series; $300 reward pot x 26 markets active 10-15)
idea.mechanism: The weekly market knows Monday's AAA value to +/- 1c on Sunday night (market-implied mean MAE 0.8c at 24 h, 1.7c at 96 h, n=8 weeks) and the daily market priced every >= 80c strike right (D03, 217/217): its makers hold station-level data (OPIS, which AAA aggregates). If GasBuddy's free live national average at 23:00 ET predicts the next-morning AAA print to +/- 0.3c, quote the 0.5c ladder as a third maker instead of taking. Monthly arm: a wholesale (NY Harbor RBOB) pass-through model at 2-4 weeks, before station data can know the answer.
idea.why_mispriced: Takers on the daily ladder are uninformed retail and lose ~$800/day (D03: $9,800 in 12 days) to 2-3 makers with the station feed; whether that feed is replicable for free was never tested.
idea.must_be_true: GasBuddy's daily CHANGE must track AAA's within 0.25-0.3c on most days (different station sets and methods -- doubtful); its data endpoint must be found (fuelinsights is a JS app; 2 probes failed); the maker side must not be crowded. Monthly: the model must beat a market that already beat it 6 days out (market MAE 4.6c vs model 5.3c vs no-change 6.9c, n=8); maker fee 0.44c at 50c; only 2 settled monthly events exist.
idea.evidence_so_far: Market side only: a Sunday-night nowcast from AAA's own daily series lost -4.6c/contract (1 win in 40 legs, 4 weeks); market MAE 0.8c at 24 h vs no-change 6.9c; RBOB model 1-week RMSE 10.8c vs 13.4c no-change on the 2026 holdout. Feed tracking: not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 if the feed does not track; $20-80/day as a third maker on $1-2k of collateral if it does (needs the $5,000 bank); monthly arm $0-2/day. Worst plausible day: a 2c AAA jump against a 0.5c grid takes the whole quoted side, -$100 to -$300 at 20 lots a strike.
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 daily + 1 weekly + 20 state dailies; 1 monthly
idea.test_plan: 14 nights read-only: record GasBuddy's US average at 23:00 ET (browser XHR once found) and the next AAA print (from the daily market's settlement). Bar: |GasBuddy change - AAA change| <= 0.3c on >= 11 of 14 nights; FAIL = the family stays dead (D03). Monthly: log the model's distribution vs the KXAAAGASM ladder at each month start for 6 months.
idea.prior_reason: The pot is real, but the edge needs a free crowd-sourced average to match a professional station feed to a third of a cent, which is unlikely, and the endpoint is not found; cheap to rule out.

test.method:
Feed first, no replay. (1) Found GasBuddy's free data API on fuelinsights.gasbuddy.com by reading /App/viewmodels/backend.js:
- POST /api/HighChart/GetHighChartRecords/ with {regionID:[500000 US | 300001-300051 states], fuelType:3, timeWindow:[6], frequency:1} returns one year of daily regular-gas averages to 3 decimals for the US and every state.
- GET /api/LiveAvg/?id=&countryID=500000 returns the live average, which ticks every 5 minutes.
- GET /api/HeatMap/GetMapData?regionID=500000&subRegionType=4&fuelType=3&timeType=1&masterRegionType=6&masterRegionIDForRanking=500000&calculationType=1 returns all 50 states in one call.
- About 200 calls at 1.5-2 s spacing drew no rate limiting.
(2) The real AAA number = Kalshi expiration_value for every settled KXAAAGASD* event: the r3 lane's realised.json plus today's 51 prints.
(3) The market's own estimate = the middle of each ladder's price spread at 09/12/15/18/23 ET, from hourly candles (r3 candles.jsonl).
(4) Rules a bot would use: tomorrow's AAA = today's AAA + b x (GasBuddy change), with GasBuddy taken from the same day or one day earlier, plus a market-plus-GasBuddy blend. Everything was fitted on print dates up to 09-30 and scored on October, grouped by print date. The self-tests (a planted-lead world, a pure-noise world, a stale-market world, a sharp-market world, and a check for gains from shrinking the market's number alone) all pass.
(5) Look-ahead check: read the history's 'today' value and the live average at 12:05, 12:12 and 12:15 ET.
(6) Forward snapshot of 15 cycling-state ladders for the 10-17 print against a fair value built from GasBuddy's live number, saved before the result is known (snap_now_20261016T161836Z.json).
test.n_markets: National ladder: 67 prints since 08-10, of which 9-10 October nights have GasBuddy data for scoring. States: 50 ladders, 321-331 October state-days in the head-to-head. Cycling-state group (15 states): 111-129 October state-days per clock time.
test.n_independent_clusters: 9 October print dates in the scored half (19-20 dates in the fitting half). All states on one date share that date's news, so the honest count is about 9 dates.
test.result:
THE IDEA (resting quotes overnight using GasBuddy): dead.
- National: the GasBuddy forecast of the next AAA print missed by 1.03c on average over 9 October nights. The market's own 23 ET price missed by 0.115c, about 9 times closer. GasBuddy was closer on 1 night of 9.
- The idea's own bar (GasBuddy change within 0.3c of AAA's change on at least 11 of 14 nights) was met on only 3 of 10 October days (2 of 10 using the same day's GasBuddy).
- GasBuddy's national series dips about 5c on Sundays (10-04 4.302, 10-11 4.299), so it is not measuring the same thing AAA measures.
- States at 23 ET: adding GasBuddy to the market's number shrinks the market's miss from 0.562c to 0.536c in cycling states (128 state-days) and from 0.783c to 0.746c elsewhere. GasBuddy's weight in the blend is 0.05 / 0.02, effectively zero.
- Buying when the blend disagreed with the 23 ET market lost 5.1c per contract in cycling states (2 of 8 dates up) and 3.6c per date elsewhere (4 of 9 up).
- Using GasBuddy data that is definitely known by the trade time (one more day old), it adds nothing at any hour.

MONTHLY ARM: KXAAAGASM settles on the same AAA national print as the daily ladder on the month's last night. Only 2 events have settled (Aug 31, Sep 30), so the 2-4-week market cannot be scored. The market already beat the wholesale-gasoline (RBOB) model 6 days out (4.6c vs 5.3c miss, 8 weekly events, r1 lane). Not measured beyond that; dead for lack of data.

SPIN-OFF (not this idea, flagged for the hunt): AAA runs about a day behind GasBuddy.
- GasBuddy's state change on one day tracks AAA's change the next day: pooled correlation 0.92, slope 0.78; 0.97-0.99 for OH/MI/NC/CO/IL/GA in October.
- At 9 ET in cycling states this beat the market's 9 ET price (0.60c vs 1.29c miss in October). Buying off it made +12.8c per contract, +10.0c per date, up on 9 of 9 dates (231 contracts). The fitting half gave +9.1c, up on 17 of 19.
- BUT THIS NUMBER IS CONTAMINATED BY LOOK-AHEAD. GasBuddy's stored daily value is the live average, which keeps changing all day (US 4.313 at 12:00, 4.312 at 12:10, 4.311 at 12:15 ET today). So at 9 ET a bot sees only part of the move that the backtest used.
- Supply is also unproven: at the flagged strikes, the median number of contracts traded in the 3 hours after a 9 ET signal was 0 (6 after noon).
test.artefact_checks:
(a) Look-ahead: three readings (12:05-12:15 ET) prove the history's same-day value is the live, still-moving average. So every result using that day's value before about 23 ET is contaminated. Re-running everything with GasBuddy one day older (definitely known in time) removes the edge.
(b) The 0.67 correlation between "GasBuddy minus market" and the market's miss is built in, because both numbers contain the market's own error. I replaced it with a fit-then-score test against a market-only baseline; the self-test caught the naive version.
(c) "GasBuddy beats the market at 9 ET" in non-cycling states (0.69c vs 1.14c miss) comes from thin new ladders whose prices are stale 1-contract quotes (r3). Trading there gave only 8 scored contracts at -8.5c, so it is not tradable.
(d) I ran 10 combinations of clock time and state group. The one positive late case (non-cycling states, 18 ET, +4.6c per date with an error band of 3.3c) gives GasBuddy a weight of only 0.045 and is within chance for 10 tries.
(e) The candle prices carry no size, so how many contracts we could actually have bought is not measured from history.
(f) Units: candle bid/ask and Kalshi values come from *_dollars fields; GasBuddy is dollars per gallon to 3 decimals; all errors are in cents.

idea.name: CLIFF: Kalshi's Sports Prop Combo leg-maker rebate (25% of prop-combo fees to the legs' makers, monthly Bonus Credit) as a kicker for the sports maker ideas (NEEDS DATA)
markets: MLB/NBA/NHL/tennis/esports prop legs listed in the program
idea.mechanism: Rest maker orders in prop legs that retail combos use. Monthly, Kalshi pools 25% of the fees of every settled sports-prop combo and splits it among makers of its legs by score S = (1+F1)(1+F2)...(1+Fn) - 1, Fi = our share of total maker volume in leg i (in-play legs: only post-start volume counts); minimum score 0.01; paid as Bonus Credit; no opt-in.
idea.why_mispriced: Parlay buyers pay the fee; Kalshi hands a quarter of it to leg makers on top of any maker edge, in proportion to maker-volume share -- so a small book's share is tiny unless it concentrates in thin legs.
idea.must_be_true: Prop-combo fee pools per leg are large relative to that leg's total maker volume (unknown) and our maker fills there are not adversely selected (the carried maker-portfolio rule: never rest a 60-99c ask in play).
idea.evidence_so_far: Help article 17184676 (fetched 10-15): rules as stated. Kalshi parlay maker fees totalled $26M in the 4 weeks after 2026-08-20 and exceed $1M/day on NFL weekends (news.bitcoin.com) -- all combos; the sports-prop share and the per-leg pot are NOT published and NOT measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown; plausibly $0-5/day at our size, paid as trade credit, not cash. Worst plausible day: the maker fills, not the rebate -- a -10c adverse fill on 5-contract legs, ~-$5.

refs.strongest_objection: The per-league CLIFF rates the tester priced the kicker with are inflated by a selection bug. r3's pull_legs.py measured in-play volume only for the events with the biggest sampled combo pools (top-N by pool plus 60 random), so each league's rate is its luckiest legs' pool divided by only those legs' volume (Liga MX: the top 4 of 9 legs; UCL: the single top leg of 9; Serie A: the top leg plus one random). Counting every leg in the denominator (my own pull of all 81 BTTS legs, games 10-08..10-13), the rates drop to 0.16-0.60x on 7 of 8 leagues and rise 3x on Saudi. This does not kill the ~$1/day, for two reasons. (1) A capped quote only clears the 1% minimum on thin legs (under 10k contracts in play), and thin legs carry more pool per contract (3.98c, 90% range 1.93-6.61c). (2) The filed rule scores per combo (S = product over legs), so when we quote every BTTS leg, combos holding several of our legs clear the minimum even when no single leg does; that roughly doubles what clears at ~90 contracts a leg. Net capped kicker: $0.08-0.89 a game across rate models and samples (tester $0.12). Separately, the capped vehicle's own 5-minute markout does not replicate on my fresh games (+0.03c a contract, se 0.47, vs tester +0.94c). The uncapped one does (+1.05c, se 0.54), and its edge sits in fills more than ~60 min after kickoff. The payment itself (paid at all, which account, trade credit) is still unproven, so the verdict stays needs-data.

refs.strongest_objection:
I could not kill it. The best objection is real, but it is more than offset by a mistake that cuts the other way.
(1) The per-league CLIFF table the tester used (from r3) is 2x to 16x too high for 6 of the 8 leagues. My own combo sample (09-04..09-21, no overlap with r3's 10-07..10-13 windows) gives the linear pool per in-play maker contract as: Liga MX 0.39c (r3: 6.27c), Serie A 0.44c (3.69c), LaLiga 0.47c (2.0c), Bundesliga 0.67c (2.0c), EPL 0.91c (1.86c), UCL 1.28c (3.13c), MLS 1.43c (2.81c), Saudi 1.92c (0.41c). All 8 together: 0.80c. So the leagues picked for the tester's probe (Liga MX, UCL, LaLiga) are the wrong ones, and quoting only those three halves the kicker: at a 300-contract cap it falls from 0.29-0.63c to 0.12-0.21c per contract.
(2) The tester's minimum-score rule is too harsh: it paid nothing on any leg where our share was under 1%. Combos holding a target BTTS leg hold 2.53 of them on average (pool-weighted, 474 combos). A bot quoting every BTTS leg therefore scores the SUM of its shares and clears 0.01 at 0.4-0.8% per leg. Under the filed product-score rule, with an incumbent maker on every eligible leg (one maker at 30-90%, or three makers sharing 90%), a 100-contract cap pays 0.22-0.43c per filled contract. That is $0.19-0.38 a game, or $1.5-3.0/day at 8 games a day, against the tester's 0.13c and $1/day.
(3) The queue does not kill supply. Behind a real queue, fills come mostly from sweeps: 79% of fills with 200 contracts ahead, 92% with 1,000 ahead, 100% with 10,000 ahead. Fills drop only from 351 to 277 contracts a game between 200 and 10,000 ahead (64 games). Swept fills marked out at +1.67c over 5 minutes (se 0.62, 62 games), so being swept is not adverse here.
Still unproven: whether Kalshi pays the CLIFF at all, which account it lands in, and whether 'maker volume' means contracts, dollars or one side only. I found no public record of any payment. The program ends by 2027-01-01, so about 76 days are left: about $150 in total at the 100 cap, paid monthly as trade credit.

test.method: Source: Kalshi's own trade tape (which side the taker was on is given) and Kalshi's settled results. No replay. (1) SETTLED one-date House races Kalshi still serves, pulled from /historical/markets + /historical/trades and from /markets/trades after the 2026-08-16 archive cutoff. The archive DOES hold the 2024 House district markets; the 10-13 lane thought Nov 2024 was gone because it only tried the live tier. Population: the 2024 general (24 races, 49 legs; these markets opened only on 2024-10-31, 5 days before the vote), the House specials FL-1/FL-6 (Apr 2025), VA-11 (Sep 2025), TN-7 (Dec 2025) and NJ-11 (Apr 2026), and the 2026 House-district primaries Aug 4 - Sep 8 (legs with >= 5,000 contracts). I pulled 179 of 296 legs: 96% of their volume, 83 races, 12 election dates. The missing legs are the thinnest primary legs, cut because the shared rate limit slowed the pull to a crawl. The rule, run as a bot would: rest orders on both sides from listing until 24 h before the state's first poll close (window W1), then hold to settlement. Fill model: rows with the same timestamp and side are one taker order. Each order fills min(Q, its size) of our resting order at 1c better than the price it actually paid. This is the optimistic '1c inside' assumption, run at Q = 10/50/200/all. A 'join the back of the queue' variant fills us only from the part of an order beyond 300 or 1,000 contracts, at the touch. Each fill is scored two ways: against the settled result, and against the price 24 h before poll close (the mid from the last YES-taker and NO-taker prints, at most 2 days old). The second removes the coin-flip noise of outcomes. Unit = race (event); the honest unit = election date. Halves: before vs after 2026-08-15. (2) LIVE target, KXHOUSERACE 2026: the board now (707 legs), plus the tape since 2026-08-16 for the 60 most-traded contested legs (mid 10-90c, 33 races). Each taker order is scored against the price 7 days later and against the price now. Self-tests (analyse.py --selftest): a planted world where takers overpay 3c gives -3.01c; a null world gives +0.36c (noise). In a random-walk world with a 2c book, takers who know nothing score -1.00c against the later price (expected -1) and informed takers score +0.97c. About 650 public calls, no auth. test.result: DEAD. The resting maker LOSES money, and takers in pre-election House flow do not lose. Settled races, strategy window (listing to 24 h before polls close), 10-lot maker 1c inside: -3.34c a contract per race (se 1.12, 83 races) and -2.82c per election date (se 2.23, positive on 4 of 12 dates); pooled -1.33c on 294k contracts. Against the price 24 h before close, with no outcome noise: -1.47c per date (se 0.38, positive on 3 of 11) and -2.64c per race (se 0.49). BOTH halves are negative: before Aug 15 -1.33c per date over 8 dates; after, -1.84c over 3 dates, none positive. Bigger quotes lose more (per date, against the later price): Q=50 -1.30c, Q=200 -1.54c, all -1.69c. Joining the back of a 300-lot queue at the touch instead gives -0.58c per date against the later price (se 0.92), +1.00c settle-scored (se 1.96) and -0.14c pooled: no edge either way. Takers in the window made +2.27c per race (se 1.47) and -0.19c per date, so they did not lose. Whelan's politics figure (-1.9c) does not appear in this population. Takers lose only in totals weighted by contract count, which big orders dominate: -3.7c in 2024 and -4.3c in the specials. A 10-lot quote cannot collect that. Final 24 h (not part of the strategy): -0.88c per date. LIVE 2026 KXHOUSERACE (Aug 16 - Oct 16, 33 races): a 10-lot maker 1c inside scores -0.85c per race against the price 7 days later (se 0.13), positive in 3 of 33 races; against the price now, -0.98c (se 0.23). Takers buying the D side (+0.18c) and the R side (+1.01c) both gained. So the flow itself moves prices; it is not just the national swing. The idea's own bar (takers lose >= 1.5c on >= 50 markets AND the maker is positive 1c inside in both halves) FAILS on both parts. This agrees with the dead sibling SI23 (-0.07 to -0.20c).
test.artefact_checks: Taker-side convention checked against the data: a YES-taker print sits above the opposite NO-taker print within 10 min in 15,038 cases vs 1,021 below (2,066 equal). Prices come from the *_dollars fields x100, so the unit is taken from the field name, never from the number's size. Self-tests pass: the planted edge is recovered, the null world reads near zero, and the later-price scorer is unbiased in a random-walk world and catches informed flow. The window is cut at the state's FIRST poll close, so no election-night counting leaks into W1. Results are clustered by race and by election date, with the 24 Nov-2024 races counted as one date. The fill model is on the OPTIMISTIC side: every order hands us its first Q contracts at 1c better, with no other maker ahead of us. The true maker result is therefore at or below these numbers. A few trades may be double-counted at the 2026-08-16 archive boundary (negligible). The mid from prints can be up to 2 days stale, but the settle-scored numbers, which need no mid, give the same sign. 2024 covers only 5 pre-vote days, because Kalshi listed those districts on Oct 31.
test.supply_we_would_get: On KXHOUSERACE (no maker fee) today there are 97 contested legs (mid 10-90c). 70 of them already sit at a 1c spread, 16 at 2c and 11 wider, so 'rest 1c inside' cannot even be placed on about 7 in 10. Median volume is 100 contracts per leg per day, and 20 legs traded nothing in 24 h. The median front-of-book queue is 255 (bid) / 353 (ask) contracts across all contested legs, and 565 / 1,639 on the 60 busiest. Upper bound, if we were alone 1c inside on the 60 busiest legs with 10-lot quotes: about 1,130 contracts a day, every one losing about 1c on average. The fills would come from takers hitting resting orders in the 3 weeks before Nov 3, and that is the flow that moves the price after it trades.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 (dead). Running it at 10 lots across the 60 busiest legs would have cost about -$10 to -$18 a day on the 2026 tape (marked to later prices), with the capital locked until the January swearing-in.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0 (dead). At 50-lot quotes the same fills cost about -$64 a day on the 2026 tape. More size makes it worse, because the bigger orders are the better-informed ones.
test.worst_case: Live 2026 tape, 10 lots on 60 legs: worst fill day -$55 marked to later prices (9 of 62 days positive); at 50 lots, -$197. Settled history, 10 lots on every leg, scored at settlement: worst fill day -$747 (a primary-scale day across ~60 legs), mean -$10.64 a day over 368 fill days. Capital is tied up until Jan 2027.
test.next_test: None for this maker; no paper bot is warranted. One free post-hoc check: when KXHOUSERACE settles (Dec 2026 - Jan 2027), run house26.py with /historical/trades and analyse.py on the settled legs (~200 calls). Revive the idea ONLY if a 10-lot quote 1c inside scores >= +1c a contract per race on >= 50 races AND >= 0 against the price 24 h before polls close. The later-price results measured here say it will not. test.method:
Re-measured on the scheduled clock using public Kalshi data only: 1,550 unauthenticated GETs, 0 authenticated, 0 orders.
(1) Listed every settled market from 2026-09-18 to 10-16 in 30 sports series: the 17 named in the idea plus 13 extended. UFC was dropped because fight order on a card is unknown, so there is no honest start time.
(2) Scheduled start S:
- From the rules text or event ticker (ET start) for cricket, esports, MLB, MLB HR and Euroleague. exp - S is then constant per series: T20/LoL/CS2/Dota/Valorant 4 h, ODI 8 h, MLB/NHL/Euroleague 3 h.
- Date-only series use exp - 3 h. NHL was checked 74/74 against the league schedule. Soccer close - S is 1.8-2.1 h on every league.
- NFL uses exp - 6 h (Sunday 1 PM ET games close 20:00-20:30Z).
- A guard S_used = min(S, close - minimum game length) keeps the window pre-game where the date-only offset is mixed (NCAAF).
(3) Quote calibration on an exogenous grid (hourly candles at S-10h, S-6h, S-3h): every outcome whose best offer was under 15c, sold at that offer. 2-way events are counted once, at the lower of the two books' offers. Payout comes from settlement_value_dollars, so cricket no-result (50c) and esports fair-price cancellations settle honestly.
(4) Fill P&L from the trade tape, pulled with min_ts/max_ts = [S-12h, S-2h], so there is no newest-first truncation. Every taker buy of a side priced 5-15c is a fill a resting longshot offer would have got. Maker net = price - payout - maker fee. Capture models: first 20 contracts per book (front of queue), the same with a 1c undercut, and first 100 per book.
Cluster = event. Holdout = H1 (scheduled before 2026-10-02 12Z) vs H2. Self-tests (planted fair, overpriced and informed worlds) pass in grid.py and tape.py, and win counts were checked by hand against price-implied wins (reconcile.py).
Source rank: trade tape and candles. No replay, no own fills.
Files: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C3-10/ (grid.out, tape.out, RESULT.json, scripts).
test.n_markets: 9,533 settled markets with pre-game candles (3,628 events). 1,054 markets with a pre-game-window tape: everything planned except about 280 NCAAF markets cut by the call budget and 2 skipped on HTTP 429.
test.n_independent_clusters: Grid at S-6h: 475 events had an offer under 15c (named series 227, esports 139). Fills, 20-lot model: 367 events over 29 scheduled days (named series 214, esports 176, cricket 53, soccer 69, MLB HR 45 games, US team sports 24).
test.result:
THE NAMED IDEA FAILS.
- Quote calibration, named series, S-6h, selling at the offer: -0.52c a contract (se 0.80, 227 events; H1 -1.82c, H2 +1.00c). At the mid: -1.66c.
- Fills, named series, 20-lot front of queue: +2.60c (se 1.63, 214 events; H1 +1.40c, H2 +3.47c). 1c undercut: +1.60c. Losing events: 23 of 214 (1 in 9).

By leg (20-lot fills; outright longshot wins vs wins the prices imply):
- Cricket: -0.48c; 4 vs 5.3, plus 4 no-result 50c settles.
- Soccer: +0.46c; 9 vs 7.2.
- NHL: only 3 events in 28 days had a pre-game side under 15c, so supply is zero.
- MLB HR (postseason only, ends about Oct 31): grid -0.88c at the offer (73 games) and -2.86c at the mid; fills +6.07c on 45 games, 2 vs 4.9 (P=0.13). Grid and fills disagree, so not trusted.
- The carried +4.69c on 148 events does not reproduce on the scheduled clock outside esports. Everything outside esports pooled: 16 wins vs 19.8 implied, no edge.

SURVIVOR: ESPORTS (LoL was named; CS2 and Dota 2 were found here).
- Grid at S-6h, selling at the offer: +5.64c (se 1.48, 139 events; H1 +5.83c, H2 +5.37c). At the mid: +5.08c. Longshots won 4 vs 12.7 price-implied (Poisson P=0.005).
- Fills, 20-lot: +4.25c (se 1.85, 176 events; H1 +5.31c, H2 +2.77c with se 3.33). 1c undercut: +3.25c. 100-lot: +4.22c.
- Outright longshot wins: 7 vs 18.9 implied (P=0.0016; about 0.008 after allowing for the 5 families looked at).
- By title: CS2 3 vs 9.7 (86 events), Dota 0 vs 3.2 (28), LoL 3 vs 5.7 (60).
- 14 of the 176 esports events settled at a fair price (cancellations). They are counted and have a small P&L effect.

Against the pre-registered bar, esports gets:
- +3c: passes.
- At most 1 losing market per 25: passes on outright wins (7 in 176). It fails if fair-price settles are counted as losses (21 in 176).
- Both halves positive: passes.
- At least 60 events: passes.
But esports was chosen after the data was seen.
test.artefact_checks:
1) Hindsight clock removed: windows are anchored on the scheduled start, not the actual close. An NFL offset error was found through close - S and fixed: exp - 3 h would have put 1 h of in-play trading inside the window. A guard caps S at close - minimum game length.
2) Truncation removed: trades were pulled by min_ts/max_ts window.
3) Whale prints: contract-weighted cells are dominated by single 10k-31k contract prints (for example 31,033 at 13c on an ODI). The decision therefore rests on the 20-lot capture model and event-equal means.
4) Unit: prices were read from *_dollars x 100. All these series use a 1c tick (linear_cent).
5) Settlement value used, not result (50c no-result, esports fair-price).
6) Two-way double counting removed in the grid.
7) Hand reconciliation: the all-families 20-lot model has a mean fill price of 10.16c and 23 wins vs 38.7 implied; the rebuilt +3.03c equals the reported figure.
8) Post-hoc selection: esports was picked after looking at 5 families. The grid and the tape share events, so they do not independently confirm each other; a forward holdout is needed.
9) Not measurable from the tape: our queue position, and whether our stale offer gets picked off on roster or stand-in news. The makers already in the book took those fills, and we would be slower than them.
test.supply_we_would_get: All on esports (LoL, CS2, Dota). Pre-game taker buys (S-12h to S-2h) of sides under 15c come to about 19,000 contracts/day across 6.2 events/day, shared by all makers. A 20-lot offer per book at the front of the queue would have filled about 169 contracts/day (about $152/day of collateral turned over, each lot locked 12 h at most). A 100-lot offer: about 726 contracts/day. Our real share depends on queue position, which was not measured.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now:
Esports only, 20 lots per book:

Named legs (cricket, soccer, NHL, MLB HR): $0.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Esports, 100 lots per book with a 1c undercut: about $23/day at the front of the queue (726 contracts/day x about 3.2c), about $10/day central with partial queue share. This is limited by flow, not by bank size.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Under a fair-price null the per-event sd is about 30c (one outcome at about 10c per event). Esports, 176 events: se about 2.3c, so the 80%-power MDE is about 6.3c a contract. Named series, 214 events: MDE about 5.7c. The +3c bar was below what this sample can detect at 80% power; the exact win-count test (7 vs 18.9) is the sharper evidence.
test.worst_case: Measured worst day at 20 lots: -$57.70 for esports, -$53 for all families. At 100 lots, about -$290. Unmeasured tail: an offer left up through a roster or stand-in announcement is picked off by informed takers, or several underdogs win on the same day (each 20-lot loss is about -$18).

On the 38 earlier days (08-10..09-17), which the tester never looked at, the same fill model makes nothing. Events whose longshot only dipped briefly into 5-15c lost -10.6c (17 wins vs 10.1 implied, 78 events), and those are exactly the fills a resting offer gets. The esports survivor does not hold up in an earlier period the tester never looked at, once we are made to undercut by 1c, which we have to.
- Holdout 2026-08-07 to 09-17 (38 days, my own tape pull, scheduled clock only, 20 lots per book at 1c under the best offer): +1.22c a contract (event-equal +1.56c, se 2.09, 172 events). That is below the tester's own +2c bar, and the first half of that period is negative (-1.20c).

The best price did not move over about 25 minutes. Pre-game taker longshot flow is a median of 207 contracts per book over 10 hours, so an order that joins the best fills on only 101 of 360 books.

idea.mechanism: When a sportsbook app shows a token, bet it on side A; rest a Kalshi order on NOT-A sized so both branches pay the same (K = stake + boosted profit for a boost; K = profit + stake - 0.7 x stake for a no-sweat bet). test.method:
Source ranking: no outcome data is needed, because a matched bet's locked amount is arithmetic on live prices. Inputs:
(a) A fresh read-only snapshot at 2026-10-16 17:05Z. FanDuel Virginia's public moneyline JSON (the hunter's endpoint) was joined to Kalshi game books at depth 10, no auth, 202 calls (snap.py).
(b) The hunter's 2026-10-13 snapshot (fd_vs_kalshi.json, top-of-book prices), used as the FIT half.
(c) FanDuel's own public page of existing-user promos, plus one token's terms page, for supply.
(d) Kalshi rules_secondary for all 5 game series.

lock.py, per side at odds -200 or longer:
- A $25 token on that side at FanDuel's real price.
- Hedged with a whole number of Kalshi contracts that pay if that side does not win: NO on it, or YES on the other team, whichever book is cheaper when walked level by level.
- Taker fee rounded up to the cent at each level; MLB fee multiplier 0.5.
- Token types: profit boosts of 25/30/50/100%; no-sweat (bonus bet back, converted at the measured 0.611); and the conversion of a bonus bet whose stake is not returned.
- Maker version: rest at the best bid and pay the maker fee. The fill is ASSUMED, so this is an upper bound; fill rate not measured.

Tax cases:
- T1: taxed at 22% on net profit.
- T2: sportsbook wins taxed, sportsbook cash losses not deductible (standard deduction), Kalshi netted against his other Kalshi results.
- T3: T2 plus Kalshi losses also not deductible (gambling treatment).
- Closed forms: T2 adds 22% x (1-p) x stake; T3 also adds 22% x p x hedge cost.

Holdout: the odds band for each token type was fitted on 10-13 and tested on 10-16. One NFL row was checked by hand and matched the script to the cent.
test.n_markets: Fresh 10-16 snapshot: 129 sides on 93 games (NCAAF 71, NBA 26, NFL 20, NHL 10, MLB 2), all at odds -200 or longer. Of these, 68 are liquid sides (Kalshi spread 1c or less, odds -200 to +200). Fit half: 43 sides on about 21 games (10-13). Supply: 12 days of FanDuel's listed promos (Oct 2-13).
test.n_independent_clusters: 114 games on two dates. A locked amount does not depend on how the game ends, so the game count only limits the sample of price gaps. The dollar uncertainty comes from token supply and tax treatment, and neither is a sampling question.
test.result:
Per $25 token, Kalshi leg taken, liquid sides (n=68):

| Token | Before tax | Taxed on net (T1) | Standard deduction (T2) | Gambling both legs (T3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50% boost | median $3.21 (p90 $4.60) | $2.50 | -$0.25 (p90 +$0.61) | median -$3.45 |
| 100% boost | about $7.8-10.4 | not computed | +$4.12 | not computed |
| No-sweat | $5.2-7.5 | not computed | +$1.70 | not computed |
| 25% boost | $0.33-0.50 | not computed | negative | not computed |
| 30% boost | $0.85-1.32 | not computed | negative | not computed |

A resting Kalshi hedge would add about $1.5-2.5 per 50% token if it filled. The fill is not measured.

Why T2 kills the 25-50% boosts:
- The FanDuel side loses its $25 cash stake about 4-6 times in 10.
- Without itemizing, that loss cannot be deducted, while the matching Kalshi win is taxed.
- That costs about 22% x $25 x (1-p) = $2.75-3.40 per token, which is the boost's whole value.
- Virginia's 5.75% state tax makes it about $1 worse again per token.

Hedge leg and prices:
- Kalshi median spread is 1c in all 5 leagues. It is 1c or less on 100% of NFL, 92% of NHL, 90% of NBA and 65% of NCAAF sides.
- FanDuel's price sits a median 2.3c worse than Kalshi's mid on the side bet (p10 0.6c, p90 3.8c).
- A bonus bet whose stake is not returned converts at median 0.611 and best 0.756 (43 sides at +200 or longer).

Holdout:
- The best band on 10-13 (+200 to +400, n=4) was overfit. 50% boost: $5.94 in-sample, $3.49 on 10-16 (n=26). 25% boost: +$1.72 in-sample, -$0.26 on 10-16.
- The robust band is +100 to +200. 50% boost: $3.67 (n=17), then $3.83 (n=37).
- Synthetic -110 check: 50% boost $3.16 against the hunter's $3.21. 25% boost $0.30 against $0.50; the gap comes from whole contracts and per-level fee rounding.
test.artefact_checks:
1. A team mis-match would show as a large gap between FanDuel and Kalshi. None of 129 sides is off by more than 8c; the largest gap is 5.5c.
2. One NFL row was recomputed by hand: Jaguars, decimal odds 1.704, 51 contracts, all-in NO price 0.4573 (0.44 ask plus 1.7c fee), lock $2.68. It matches the script.
3. The synthetic -110 case matches the hunter within $0.20.
4. Choosing the odds band in-sample overfit on n=4, and the holdout caught it. The reported numbers use the liquid +100 to +200 band.
5. FanDuel prices come from the public Virginia API, not his logged-in app. The token's max wager is not public ("log in for more details"), so every dollar figure is per $25 and scales linearly.
6. Maker numbers assume a fill. Kalshi queues at the best price hold 10^5-10^6 contracts on NFL and MLB, so a resting hedge may not fill before the game starts. This is not measured and is not used in the central figure.
7. Kalshi rules, read today: an NFL tie resolves at $0.50 per team, while books push a two-way moneyline. A postponed game stays open 48 hours (MLB: two days), then settles at "fair price".
8. Recorders: process command lines could not be read from this shell. kalshi_data cfbenchmarks_value 20261016T17 was written at 17:10Z and feed_data at 17:11Z, so both are writing. Free disk 110.7 GB; scratch 0.75 MB.

FanDuel's own public promo page, Oct 2-13 (12 days):
- 6 single-game "any wager" 50% profit-boost tokens: CFB 10-02, NFL 10-05, MLB 10-06, MLB 10-07, NFL 10-08, MLB 10-13.
- One 25% token (WNBA 10-07).

Terms: Virginia is in the eligible-state list on the 10-13 token; minimum odds -200; max wager not public.

DraftKings: not measured. Its pages return 403, and listings describe profit-boost and no-sweat tokens, many of them same-game-parlay or parlay-only.

Whether these tokens appear in HIS app: not measured.

The Kalshi side is never the limit: 10^5+ contracts sit at the best price on NFL and MLB against the 40-175 needed, and hedge capital is $23-67 per token.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now:
FanDuel only, 3.5 x 50% tokens a week at $25:
- Before tax: about $1.6/day.
- Taxed on net profit: $1.25/day. If he itemizes, the 2026 rule that allows only 90% of gambling losses leaks about $0.3 a token.
- Standard deduction: about $0/day from 50% tokens. Only 100% and no-sweat tokens pay, about $4.1 and $1.7 each, and about one or fewer a week has been seen. That gives about $0.2-0.6/day.
- Adding DraftKings at a similar rate would roughly double each figure (not measured).
- Central estimate: about $0.3/day.

It is manual: about 5 minutes of his time per token. It is not a bot; the most that can be automated is a helper that sizes the Kalshi leg.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: The same as now, because the cap is the book's token size, not the bank. $0-1.25/day with FanDuel only, $0-2.5/day with DraftKings added; central about $0.3/day.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: The locked amount per token is known to about +/-$0.30: it is the median of 68 liquid sides, and the two dates agree within $0.16 on the robust band. Three things cannot be measured here, and each moves the daily figure by a factor of 0 to 4: how many tokens a week his app shows, the max wager per token, and his tax treatment.
test.worst_case:
- NFL tie on a longshot token: Kalshi pays 50c per team while the book refunds the bet. A 50% token at +200 (100 contracts at about 69c) loses about $19; at +400 (175 contracts at about 81c) about $54. Avoid NFL underdogs, or accept the roughly 0.3% chance of a tie.
- The book voids or re-prices the boosted bet after the hedge is on: the hedge is left uncovered, -$25 to -$70.
- A game postponed outside the book's window but inside Kalshi's 48 hours: exit the hedge at about 2c a contract, -$1 to -$3.
- Worst plausible day: about -$55, and only on an NFL longshot.
- The book limiting the account or removing its promos ends the income, with no loss.
- Hedging from the main account shrinks the pin bot's size by about 2-6% for a few hours, roughly $0.1-0.3 per token. A subaccount avoids this.
test.next_test:
No recorder or paper bot can decide this; two answers from the operator do.

1. Tax: does he itemize, or take the standard deduction? If standard deduction, use ONLY 100% boosts and no-sweat tokens and skip 25-50% boosts, which net about -$0.25 each.
2. Supply: screenshot the FanDuel and DraftKings Promotions tabs on 3 days over one week, about 2 minutes each. Count single-game "any wager" tokens, the boost %, and the max wager.

Pass bar: at least 3 hedgeable tokens a week with a max wager of $25 or more, AND either he itemizes or there is at least one 100% or no-sweat token a week.

If it passes, hedge one token:
- Use a liquid NBA, NHL or MLB game at +100 to +200, never an NFL underdog.
- Take the Kalshi leg from a subaccount within a minute of the FanDuel bet.
- Read: the locked amount should be within $1 of lock.py's figure.

Kill if there are fewer than 2 hedgeable tokens a week over 2 weeks, or if he takes the standard deduction and gets no 100% or no-sweat tokens.

refs.strongest_objection:
The arithmetic holds, but the dollar figure rests on three inputs nobody has measured, and each can push the result to zero.

(1) The max wager is set per customer. FanDuel's own token pages say "There is a maximum wager associated with YOUR Profit Boost Token. Log in for more details." No public page gives a dollar figure. He has used FanDuel and DraftKings before, so his cap could be well under $25.

(2) His tax treatment and tax bracket.
- Standard deduction at 22% federal: a 50% token nets -$0.27.
- Adding Virginia's 5.75% makes it about -$1.
- In the 12% bracket the same token nets about +$1.1.
- If both legs count as gambling, even a 100% token nets about $0.

(3) Whether his account still gets the "Claim Now" tokens: not measured.

Also, FanDuel's promo index shows no new token pages for 10-14 to 10-16 (3 days, read 17:20Z).

This is not a refutation. The locked amount is arithmetic on live prices, and it reproduces.
