refs.strongest_objection:
Not refuted, but three execution facts cut it down.

1. The Kalshi resting (maker) hedge in the idea's title does not fill on NFL.
   - The resting price we would join holds 0.95 to 3.9 million contracts on most Week-7 NFL sides. Taker flow into it was 2k to 95k contracts over 12 hours.
   - At that pace the median wait to reach the front is about 960 hours. Only 3 of 22 NFL sides would fill before kickoff (NBA 9 of 24, NHL 5 of 16, MLB 0 of 2).
   - This ignores cancellations by orders ahead of us, so the real wait could be shorter.
   - Only the taken hedge is real: the hunter's +$4.29 resting figure for a 50% boost is not available; about $3.3 taken is.

2. Tax with Virginia added makes the main token type lose money.
   - Assumes 22% federal plus Virginia's 5.75%, and the standard deduction (sportsbook cash losses not deductible).
   - A 50% boost then nets a median -$1.03 per $25 token (40 liquid sides, 23 games).
   - Only 100% boosts (+$2.95) and no-sweat tokens pay, and at most about one of those a week has been seen.
   - If he itemizes, the 50% boosts come back to about +$2.15 each.

3. FanDuel's max wager is per user and hidden until the bet slip ("log in for more details").
   - So the FanDuel bet has to go first and the Kalshi leg second; hedging first risks being over-hedged.
   - The gap between the two legs costs nothing on average but adds noise: pregame NFL prices move about 1.1c in 5 minutes (typical size), about +/-$0.70 per token.

Worst plausible day is still an NFL tie on an underdog token: -$19 to -$54. A voided FanDuel bet can be exited by selling the Kalshi leg back for about $2-3. That is far smaller than the -$25 to -$70 the tester gave for holding it unhedged.

idea.name: Two-book locking bid in thin tennis (ITF singles 2-3c wide, ITF/Challenger doubles 25-37c): rest a bid on one player that is pre-hedged by the other player's ask -- WEAK, decidable for free on the existing 31-minute recording
idea.mechanism: Each player's YES is its own book. Rest a bid on player A at 1 - ask(B) - fee(B) - 1c (and symmetrically on B). If it is hit, lift B at its ask: the pair costs under $1 and pays exactly $1. Resting on both books doubles the fill chances versus quoting one side. ITF fee_type is quadratic: no maker fee on the resting leg; the hedge leg pays the taker fee.
idea.why_mispriced: Retail sells into thin ITF books; the resident quotes are 2-3c wide in singles and 25-37c in doubles, so a bid 1c inside the best bid can still lock >= 0 against the other player's ask. Against it: in play the seller who hits our bid often knows a point has just been won, and B's ask is then lifted or repriced -- the lock fails exactly when it is needed.
idea.must_be_true: Someone sells into our improving bid (fill rate unmeasured); the other leg's ask is still there ~1 s after our fill (unmeasured); ~$1 per pair locked for 1-3 h is acceptable.
idea.evidence_so_far: Snapshot 06:00Z 10-15: sets where a locking bid can improve the best bid by >= 1c: ITF W singles 13 of 50, ITF M 13 of 42, ITF W doubles 10 of 15, ITF M doubles 11 of 12, Challenger doubles yes; NFL 0 of 28, NHL 0 of 24, NBA 0 of 18, UFC 0 of 21, NCAAF 4 of 103. Median possible improvement: singles mostly the 1c minimum, doubles +12..+19c (books 60-70c wide on the bid side). Same books, from the revisit lane's 31-minute WebSocket recording 06:02-06:33Z (149 markets, 881,962 book frames, tennis_ws.jsonl.gz): a 15-lot behind the displayed queue at 3-5c filled on 3 markets counting only taker buys at our price (7 if every size drop is ahead of us); after a fill the trailer's bid rose above our price within 300 s on 0 of 9 -- some ITF flow is not instantly informed. Recording bug found and fixed (float size residues left phantom crossed books; use a 1e-9 or 0.01 threshold). Not measured: locking-bid fills, survival of the other ask.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: Unknown; bounded by tennis maker economics: probably $0-3/day at the current bank (15 contracts a pair, ~$15 locked per open pair), little more at $5,000 (flow, not bank, binds). Worst plausible day: several hits with the other ask gone, each a naked in-play position: -50c x 15 = -$7.50 a pair, ~-$20 a bad day.
idea.settlements_per_day: ~360 ITF singles + ~60 doubles markets a day
idea.test_plan: 0 GETs: replay C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/r1-revisit/tennis_ws.jsonl.gz (rounding sizes to 0.01 and deleting at <= 0): at every frame compute the locking bid for each two-player set; count trades at or through it and whether B's ask (same size) still stood 1 s later. Then fold into the carried in-play longshot seller's recorder (maker-portfolio / sports lanes) when it runs. Bar: >= 20 locked pairs a day at >= 1c net, projected from >= 3 hours of recording; kill if the other ask is gone on > 1 in 3 fills.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SJ18/U12 and the carried in-play longshot sellers sell one side unhedged; the two-book lock (hedge available by construction) is not in the ledger or the carried index. SJ41 found tennis sibling books move together at the book level, which is the main reason this is weak.
idea.worst_case: Hit on A, B's ask gone: a naked in-play position, -50c a contract on 15 contracts = -$7.50 a pair; capped by size.

test.method:
SINGLES (this decides it; the source is the raw exchange book feed, the best kind we have): a second-by-second replay of all three tennis WebSocket book+trade recordings already on disk. A = 2026-10-15 06:02-06:33Z, 149 markets. B = 2026-10-03 08:00-08:45Z, 93 markets. C = 2026-10-03 06:39-07:34Z, 62 markets. Together that is 131 min, 127 two-player match-recordings and 36,527 taker orders on paired books. The replay script lock_replay.py has a self-test: a planted lock is found and priced, a failed lock comes out negative, mirrored books give nothing, the queue blocks a fill, and the NO side works.
How the replay works: at every taker order that sold a contract on one player's book, it asks whether a resting locking bid priced off the other player's ask would have been hit. Two bid prices were tried: best bid + 1c, and the maximum price that still locks. The bid size is capped by the hedge depth, so the whole hedge still nets >= 1c after the taker fee (and after the 0.0175 maker fee on ATP/WTA main tour). After a fill it walks the other book L_h seconds later to get the real hedge cost. The quote is built from the books as they were L_q earlier, and after a fill our order is gone for one re-post cycle.
Latencies tried (L_q/L_h): 0.05/0.05 (faster than co-located), 0.1/0.15 (our 43 ms warm send), 0.25/0.5 and 0.5/1.0. Variants: IMP1, MAX, and QUIET (quote only when both relevant books had been still for 30 s). Holdout: the margin threshold was fit on 10-03 (B+C) and tested on 10-15 (A).
DOUBLES: no book recording exists, and an unauthenticated WebSocket returns 401, so I did not record. Instead I used the public trade tape plus Kalshi 1-minute candles for 145 of the 441 doubles events settled in 4 days: the top 95 by volume, plus a seeded random 50 of the 301 ranked below the top 140. I also tested a rule with no look-ahead, QUIET1 (quote only if the hedge ask was flat for the whole previous minute), on a seeded 60 of those events. The candle method was calibrated against the WebSocket on the 10-15 singles minutes, and I read best-level depth on 36 open doubles books. About 1,620 unauthenticated GETs in total, a little over the ~1,500 guide. The collector and feed files were still being written at 17:15Z.
test.n_markets: Singles: 254 paired markets (127 match-recordings) across 131 recorded minutes. Doubles: 290 markets (145 events) out of 441 events settled 2026-10-12..16; 60 of those events used for the no-look-ahead test.
test.n_independent_clusters: Singles: the fills landed on 11-16 matches, depending on latency. Doubles QUIET1: 70 fills on 22 events.
test.result:
SINGLES at our speed (0.1/0.15 s): 25 fills on 11 matches, 200 contracts. Planned +$3.29, realised -$3.53, which is -1.8c a contract (match-bootstrap 90% range -2.8c to -0.65c). 12 of the 25 locks failed (48%); the wins added up to +$1.54 and the losses to -$5.07.
Other latencies:
- Faster than co-located (0.05/0.05): 27 fills, -$4.58, 13 failed.
- 0.25/0.5: -$5.28 (-2.4c a contract), 17 of 27 failed (63%).
- 0.5/1.0: -$6.20, 19 of 27 failed (70%).
It is negative in all 3 recordings, at every latency, for both variants.
Holdout (fit on 10-03, tested on 10-15), by margin threshold:
- margin >= 1c: fit -$2.60, test -$0.93
- margin >= 2c: fit -$0.63, test -$0.18
- margin >= 3c: fit -$0.58, test 0 fills
No threshold turns it positive. The QUIET filter gave 1 fill in 131 min (+$0.02). A lock quote exists only 0.5-5% of market-side seconds.
The failure is the one predicted: the other player's ask is lifted or pulled in the same 50-500 ms that our bid is hit. In recording B, on 5 of the 9 fills where the hedge ask moved, it had already moved at the instant of our fill.
DOUBLES: the only positive subset (+$12.50/day at 15 lots, 66 fills, 0 negative) is fills where the hedge ask happened to stay flat all minute. That subset is picked by its outcome (look-ahead), so a bot cannot trade it. Without look-ahead (QUIET1): 70 fills on 22 events, planned +$25.63, and the hedge ask rose above plan inside the fill's minute on 49 of 70 (70%). Hedging at the minute's high gives -$30.40, at its low +$28.04 (scaled, about -$34 to +$42/day). That range straddles zero and cannot be decided at 1-second resolution, but it shows the same pattern as singles.
test.artefact_checks:
- Book rebuild rounds sizes and deletes levels at <= 0.005 (the float-residue bug). Recording A has 0 crossed-book seconds and 3 sequence gaps. There are 0 duplicate trade ids in 82,505 prints.
- My own first run priced the hedge at the top ask only and showed 16 fills with 12 failed. That was wrong, because a 15-lot hedge walks the book; I fixed it by capping the quote size at the hedge depth, which gave the numbers above.
- Re-fill double counting removed (one re-post cycle after each fill).
- Candle fidelity against the WebSocket on 2,153 singles market-minutes: 1,541 candle-flat vs 1,543 WS-flat; 0 candle-flat minutes moved on the WS; the candle high was below the WS max on 26 (1.2%).
- The optimistic candle bound is not evidence: on the same 31 minutes it said +$101, while the WebSocket truth is -$1.80.
- The doubles flat-minute profit was identified as look-ahead.
- Rules checked: a walkover or cancellation before a ball is played settles all markets at $0.50, so a pair still pays $1. A withdrawal after the start settles that player No.
- Fees verified on /series: quadratic x1 for ITF, Challenger and doubles; quadratic_with_maker_fees for ATP/WTA main tour, and that maker fee is charged in the model.
- Depth on open doubles books: best levels median 45 contracts; 64% hold >= 15.
test.supply_we_would_get: Singles: about 12 fills an hour across all live tennis, roughly 90 contracts an hour (each fill capped at 15). Most are on ITF men's and women's singles, the rest on ATP/WTA main tour. The fills that do arrive are mostly the ones where the other book is repricing at that moment. Doubles: about 110 events a day; 70 fills under the no-look-ahead rule on 22 of 60 sampled events over 4 days; depth usually covers a 15-lot.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: Dead. Run at our speed, it measured about -$1.60 per hour of live tennis (-1.8c a contract). That is roughly -$25 a day if run all day, but this is a projection from 131 minutes, not a day measured. Recommended: $0 (do not build).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Same loss per contract. The bank is not what limits it (fills are limited by who sells into the bid), so $5,000 changes nothing. Recommended $0.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Singles: about 1.7c a contract (2.5 match-clustered standard errors on 200 contracts across 11 matches). The measured -1.8c (90% range -2.8c to -0.65c) rules out the +1c to +3c the plan needed. Doubles: 1-minute candles cannot decide it (the range straddles zero).
test.worst_case:
- Worst single fill measured: -$0.98 (15 contracts; the hedge ask jumped from 24c to 32c within 150 ms).
- Worst recorded stretch: -$3.76 in 45 minutes (recording B at 0.5/1.0 s).
- A bad full day if it were run, projected and not measured: -$40 to -$60 at 15 lots.
A failed lock is still hedged, so it is a locked loss of a few cents a contract, not a naked position, unless the other book empties.

idea.name: Esports map markets with empty books: be the only quote, priced off the same series' match price

idea.mechanism: Post two-sided quotes 15-20c wide around a fair derived from the match-winner market (map win probability for the favourite ~ a shaded match price, with map-order effects); no maker fee; widen or pull when a map turns one-sided.

test.n_independent_clusters:
Clusters are matches.
- Calibration, map 1: 1,137 maps on 1,137 matches (holdout 394).
- Calibration, map 2: 1,059 maps (holdout 368).
- Trade-tape simulation: 155 fit maps (Sep 9-30, about 79 matches) and 82 holdout maps (Oct 1-15, about 40 matches).
test.result:
THE BOOK IS NOT EMPTY WHEN ANYONE TRADES. The 92c-wide books are maps listed days ahead, with no match running.

Where the volume prints. Of 40.7M contracts printed on CS2 map books (Sep 9-Oct 15):
- 77-78% printed while the incumbent's spread was 5c or less, and about 92% while it was 10c or less;
- only 3.0-3.9% printed while it was wider than 20c, the only place a 15-20c quote would be best;
- before the scheduled start only 0.75M (map 1) and 0.94M (map 2) printed, 87-90% of it at spreads of 10c or less.
Contracts printed per played map while the incumbent was wider than 20c:
- map 1 before start: 34 (median 0);
- map 1 in play: 562 (median 97);
- map 2 before start: 49;
- map 2 in play: 498 (median 1).
Volume is bigger than the idea assumed: median 1,865 and mean 7,877 contracts per market, about 1.08M a day.

The fair. Before the match, the fair taken from the match price is accurate:
- map 1 holdout: won minus fair +1.11c (se 2.39, 394 maps);
- map 2 holdout: -0.01c (se 2.40, 368 maps).
But the incumbent beats it on map 2 (Brier 0.2047 vs 0.2125 on 448 maps; map 1 is a tie, 0.2201 vs 0.2210). In play, our fair sits a median 3.7-5.8c from the incumbent's mid (p75 6.7-10.5c).

The quote, as the idea describes it (ONLY, in play, h = 7.5c, i.e. 15c wide):

| Sample | Stale bracket | Ahead bracket |
|---|---|---|
| Fit, h 7.5c | -13.31c a contract (se 5.49; 24,577 contracts / 64 matches) | -9.49c (se 7.41) |
| Holdout, h 7.5c | -13.01c (se 6.43; 9,209 contracts / 25 matches) | -10.69c (se 8.04) |
| Fit, h 10c | -12.39c | -8.10c |
| Holdout, h 10c | -25.55c | -16.99c |

All 12 in-play ONLY cells (3 widths x 2 brackets x 2 halves) are negative.

Quoting only before the start (PRE, ONLY):
- fit: -33.7c a contract (se 9.1; 4,700 contracts / 28 matches);
- holdout: -15.9c (se 24.1; 792 contracts / 8 matches).
Most of that loss is map 2 quoted at the iid fair while map 1 is still being played: -36.8c on 6,927 contracts in the last 20 min before map 1 closed (fit). The incumbent prices which team picked map 2; the iid fair does not.
Map 1 strictly before the scheduled start is about 33 contracts a match. Pooled it is roughly +8c, but se is about 15-20c on about 22 matches and the sign flips between time buckets, so it is effectively unmeasured.

Quoting all the time like an ordinary maker (ALL, h = 7.5c):
- fit: -10.60c (stale), -6.53c (ahead);
- holdout: -7.71c (stale), +3.30c (ahead, se 5.25).
It is not positive in the fit half even with up to a minute of look-ahead.

Dota 2 has the same shape: 85-91% of map volume prints while the incumbent is 10c wide or less, and only 2.6% of map volume prints before the start.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) A bug in my own first simulation was found and fixed. p was fixed at schedule minus 5 min and applied to earlier prints, so one match that started early (K27UPG, Oct 2) got F = 0.99 and dominated the pre-start loss. sim3 uses a fair built only from prices available at the time, plus the pull rule; in-play results moved by less than 1c.
(2) How stale the match price is was bracketed both ways: the previous minute's close, and the same minute's close with look-ahead. The idea fails under both.
(3) Sign and unit sanity check: in the holdout, takers' own P&L in tight in-play books (5c or less) is -0.02c (se 1.45, 1.98M contracts), so no convention is flipped. Prints on team B's book were converted to team A terms (price 1-p, direction flipped).
(4) The fill model is generous to us: nobody queued ahead of us, and any print beyond our price fills up to 50 contracts. Real results would be worse.
(5) With 1-minute candles, the incumbent's spread is the previous minute's close, so a print just after the incumbent re-quotes can be put in the wrong bucket. That blurs the ONLY/ALL split; it does not change the sign.
(6) Every sample was chosen by schedule (every match, or every 10th match in schedule order), never by volume.
(7) Exclusions and assumptions: 546 of 6,000 map markets settled 'scalar' (unplayed or cancelled) and were left out; map 3 is not listed; CS2 matches with 2 map events were treated as best-of-3.
(8) In the Dota calibration, both the fair and the incumbent showed won minus fair of about -11c for the first-listed team on 80 maps. Same sign for both and a small sample, so it was not used.
(9) Both recorders were still writing at the end (kalshi_data ticker and feed_data bitstamp files updated 13:38 ET). Disk 110 GB free; scratch folder 23 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: Market-wide, CS2 map books print about 39k contracts a day while the incumbent is wider than 20c, across about 68 played maps a day. That is all a 15-20c-wide quote could ever be first in line for, and it is the toxic part: the incumbent's quote is missing because a round or map just swung. Before the start only (the 'empty book' case), it is about 30-50 contracts a map, or about 1-3k contracts a day market-wide. Dota adds about 14 maps a day with the same shape.

At the current bank, quoting 50 contracts on every map: about -10c to -13c per contract filled, about 50 filled per map, about 68 maps a day, which is roughly -$340 to -$440 a day from in-play fills. test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Negative: the same loss per contract, and bigger size only scales it. $0 if not built.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Quote simulation: se is 5-8c a contract in each half, so the smallest effect it can detect is about 11-16c (2 se). The in-play ONLY cells, -9c to -26c, sit about 1.5-4 se below zero in each half, and all 12 are negative. Fair calibration: se 2.4c on about 380 holdout maps, so about 4.8c is detectable.
test.worst_case: If built: the incumbent pulls its quote at a round swing and a stream watcher takes our 50-lot, about -$35 to -$45 a map. With dozens of such fills a day, that is a day worse than -$400 at the current bank.

test.method:
New data source, found in this run: Robinhood's public prediction-market pages need no login. They are robinhood.com/us/en/prediction-markets/<category>/ and /events/<slug>/. They carry live quotes for every venue Robinhood routes to, each tagged with its exchange: Kalshi, Rothera (Robinhood plus Susquehanna), ForecastEx or CDNA. The event pages also show quote sizes, venue timestamps, volume and open interest. That let me automate the operator's "2-minute quote check" for Rothera and CDNA.

How I measured:
- xmatch.py (self-tested) read 7 category pages a round and matched each Rothera or CDNA contract to its Kalshi twin. Rothera copies Kalshi's ticker scheme (ECUSFED->KXFEDDECISION, SENRACE->SENATE, GOVRACE->GOVPARTY, HOURACE->KXHOUSERACE, NFLGAME->KXNFLGAME). Nominees were matched by name, and MLB totals and spreads by strike.
- It read Kalshi's top of book with sizes from public /markets?tickers=.
- It computed the locked profit for buying the same question on both venues, in both directions. A lock is the other venue's bid minus Kalshi's ask, minus Kalshi's taker fee 0.07p(1-p), minus a 1c Robinhood commission (its published cap).
- 7 rounds, 2026-10-16 17:31-17:58Z.
- For each positive lock, lockdepth.py walked Kalshi's whole order book against Rothera's displayed size.
- I also pulled Kalshi hourly candles and trades for the far Fed meetings, and compared the rules text (Rothera's FOMC terms against Kalshi's rules).

Source rank: venue quotes, which work like a feed but run 1-6 min late, plus Kalshi's live book. No replay was used.

Not measured:
- CME event contracts and FanDuel Predicts: cmegroup.com returns 403 to Python and WebFetch timed out; predicts.fanduel.com redirects to fanduel.com and has no feed.
- DraftKings Predictions: returns 403.
- ForecastEx S&P/Nasdaq daily ladders: read via Robinhood but not compared to Kalshi, because they settle on futures and Kalshi settles on the cash index. They are 10-11c wide near the money and were last updated about 35 min before the read, so they are no use as an anchor.

Scratch folder: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C3-12/ (xmatch.py, lockdepth.py, persist.py, analyze.py, rounds.jsonl, lockdepth.json, fed_depth.json, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 516 Rothera/CDNA contracts matched to a Kalshi twin, read in 7 rounds = 3,608 records. 292 Rothera contracts stayed unmatched: mostly NHL season futures, plus a few races and the 4 'control of Congress' combos.

test.result:
On the same question, Rothera copies Kalshi:
- The typical gap between the two venues' middle prices is 0.5c (90th percentile 1.6c).
- Rothera's typical spread is 3c against Kalshi's 1c, so Kalshi is the better book on nearly everything.
- A lock paid after fees on 7-10 of 152 events. Every one lasted all 7 rounds (about 40 min).

Walking the real order books, everything lockable at 1:58 PM ET came to about $52, once:
- **Fed, January 2027, "no change": $41.31.** Rothera offers 56c x 1,000. Kalshi's bids are 66c x 1.7, 63c x 769 and 62c x 1,003. That is 4.1c a pair on 1,000 pairs. Each pair costs about 96c and is held to Jan 27 2027 (about 104 days), roughly 15% a year.
- **Texas governor: $7.20.** 0.7c x 1,000, which is below Kalshi's 4.05% interest. The rules also differ: Kalshi pays on "inaugurated", Rothera on "win".
- **Florida governor: $3.15** (1.8c x 172).
- **Fed July 2027 rungs: $0.71.** Rothera's sizes there are only 5-11.
- **Louisiana Senate: $0.10.**

Why the one real gap exists: between 7 and 8 AM ET, Kalshi's Jan-2027 "no change" jumped from 54/55 to 70/72. That hour traded 5,456 contracts, with prints up to 81c, and someone bought 50,000 'hike 25' contracts on the same meeting at 7:37 AM ET. Kalshi then settled at 64-67. Rothera's far-meeting quotes did not follow: it re-posted its 56c ask at 9:00 AM ET, with the bid at 55. The near meetings (October, December) agreed within 1c, so the lag is specific to far, thin Fed meetings.

No holdout was possible in one afternoon. How often these gaps reappear after other releases is not measured.
test.artefact_checks:
1. My own mapping bug, found and fixed. Rothera's MLB total or spread "N" means over N.5; Kalshi's "N" means over (N-1).5 (checked: KXMLBTOTAL-...-5 is 'Over 4.5', KXMLBSPREAD-...-TB2 is 'over 1.5'). Round 1 showed fake 4-11c locks on 16 MLB rows. After the fix they sit 0-1c apart.
2. CDNA 'Washington' was matched to Washington State, a fake 27c lock. Fixed by requiring both team names to match.
3. Delay. Robinhood pages are cached (CloudFront, s-maxage 60, stale-while-revalidate 300). The newest quote on a freshly rebuilt page was 6 min old, so these quotes cannot feed a bot. The Fed gap is 10c and has stood since 9:00 AM ET by Rothera's own venue timestamps, so a few minutes of delay cannot create it; it held in all 7 rounds.
4. Units. Both venues quote in dollars, and the October Fed quotes are identical on both (87/88), which confirms the scale.
5. Kalshi's book was walked level by level, not just the 1.7-contract top.
6. Rules, Fed: both settle on the change the FOMC announces at that meeting, and both pay "no change" if the meeting is cancelled. Rothera adds settlement at "fair market value" if the release comes after expiry, a small tail risk. Rules, elections: Kalshi pays on 'inaugurated/sworn in', Rothera on 'win'. That is a real difference.
7. The Robinhood fee was taken at its 1c cap, which is conservative.

test.worst_case:
- Placing the Robinhood leg by hand while Kalshi moves: a 5c move on 300 pairs costs $15.
- Rule split (Rothera's 'fair market value' clause if the FOMC release is delayed; 'win' vs 'inaugurated' on races): loses up to the full pair cost, about $290 on 300 pairs. Unlikely, but that is the tail.

refs.strongest_objection:
Everything rests on one 1,000-contract Rothera offer at 56c. Nobody has taken it in 5 hours while Kalshi bid 63-72c, and the venue is co-owned by Susquehanna, a top Kalshi market maker. Whether a retail Robinhood account would actually be filled there is the untested crux. It cannot be tested without opening and funding an account, and deposits are forbidden by default.

Fee correction: Robinhood's published all-in cost is 1c commission plus 1c exchange fee, not 1c. That makes the lock about $33 per 1,000 pairs, not $41, and about $12 at a bank-sized 300 pairs.

Rule split, refined from Kalshi's own rules text: Kalshi pays 'maintain' YES if the meeting does not happen on Jan 27 2027. Rothera settles on the actual decision until its Jan 29 16:00Z expiry, and at fair market value after that. So a 1-2 day postponement followed by a hike or cut loses both legs, about $290 on 300 pairs. Very unlikely.

The gap came from one Kalshi burst: 5,456 contracts in one hour, 85 since. How often a gap like this recurs is not measured. Not refuted on the arithmetic: if the Rothera offer fills, it is a real lock.

test.method: Sources, best first: (1) VoteHub's own API, which is the settlement source. polling.votehub.com/site/polls?...&in_averages_only=true shows each poll's current weight in the average (average_weights). /averages shows last_updated and enop. /averages/generic_ballot_2026/values gives the daily series. Two live cache-busted loggers ran from 1:31 to 2:16 PM ET on 10-16: vhlog.py logged the value and the KXVHGCB-26OCT16 quotes once a minute; vhlog2.py compared the raw and in-average poll lists every 30 s. (2) The full public KXVHGCB trade tape from sibling test N2-08: 196 markets, 21 settled days 09-25..10-15, 739,864 contracts. (3) Pollster release times from the pollsters' own pages (Fox News, AP-NORC, Focaldata) and from dated URLs. No replay. Measured: (a) recon.py: does sum(w x pct)/sum(w) with VoteHub's own weights reproduce the page? (b) kernel2.py, kernel3.py: fit a recency kernel to today's weights and backcast Sep 20-Oct 16 against the daily series; those days are not in the fit. (c) sens.py, grades.py: how a guessed weight for a poll not yet entered moves the bucket. (d) pool.py, fine.py: 58 repricing events (>=30c move in <=15 min) and second-by-second taking after each trigger print; the self-test recovers a planted jump and fires nothing on a flat tape. (e) phase.py: do triggers line up with VoteHub's 10-minute recompute cycle (chi-square against uniform)? (f) prize.py: the cheap supply on the winning bucket before its first >=70c print, capped at 100 contracts a day, which is the ceiling for a bot that knows the value early. (g) Release time vs VoteHub entry vs market move for the polls with a public timestamp. All scratch is in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-14/ (RESULT.json is saved there).
test.n_markets: 196 KXVHGCB markets (21 settled days, 739,864 contracts); 58 repricing events on 18 days; 77 weighted polls in today's VoteHub average; 27 backcast days; 2 polls with a checked release time (Fox 10-14 6:00 PM ET, Focaldata 10-11), plus 6 more with a dated release
test.n_independent_clusters: 21 settlement days; 18 days with a repricing; 2 fully traced release->entry->market episodes. Two cases are anecdotes, not a rate.
test.result:
1) THE FORMULA REPRODUCES TODAY'S VALUE EXACTLY. Using VoteHub's own weights, the weighted mean is D 49.397 / R 41.291 against the page's 49.4 / 41.3, and the weights sum to 9.509 against VoteHub's published enop of 9.511. No house-effect adjustment is applied to the number shown.
2) IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE ANY OTHER DAY, OR A NEW POLL. A kernel fitted to today's weights backcasts the right 0.1 bucket on only 4 of 27 days (median error 0.16 points; within 0.1 on 9 of 27). The weight a new poll will get cannot be read in advance: same-age polls carry 0.27 to 0.91, and VoteHub's pollster grade does not predict it (grade D pollsters get 0.36-0.57, grade B YouGov 0.27, grade A Fox/Beacon 0.91). On the 10-15 entry (Fox + AP-NORC), a guess of 0.5-0.8 for each gives the right bucket (8.1); 0.85-0.9 gives 8.2 and 0.3-0.4 gives 8.0.
3) VOTEHUB RECOMPUTES ABOUT EVERY 10 MINUTES. Seen live at 1:30:51, 1:41:20, 1:51:19, 2:00:55 and 2:10:53 PM ET, i.e. 50-80 s past each 10-minute mark. Normal readers get a copy up to 5 minutes old; a cache-buster gets a fresh one.
4) THE MARKET MOVES WHEN VOTEHUB'S PAGE MOVES, NOT WHEN THE POLL COMES OUT. Repricing triggers pile up in the first 2 minutes of the 10-minute cycle: 25 of 58 against 11.6 expected at random, and 17 of the 33 big ones against 6.6 (chi-square 21.0 and 26.7, against 16.9 at the 5% level). Fox case: the poll went public at 6:00 PM ET on 10-14. VoteHub entered it on 10-15 and the market jumped at 11:41-11:54 AM ET, 17.7 h later. From 10-14's settlement to that jump, the winning bucket E8.1 traded at 18-36c: 1,297 contracts bought from asks and 2,926 sold into bids at <=40c. Focaldata case: published 10-11, entered and repriced 12:45-12:51 PM ET on 10-12. The winner E8.4 traded at 11-17c overnight (3,305 + 1,343 contracts at <=40c). But one buyer took about 2,450 at 12-13c at 6:02 PM ET on 10-11, so at least one front-runner already exists. Of 8 polls with a dated release, 7 were entered 1-2 days later; AP-NORC went in the same day.
5) ONCE THE PAGE MOVES, FASTER BOTS ARE ALREADY THERE. 11,676 of the 32,362 contracts traded in the jump direction went within 10 s of the trigger print. Net +$663: +$2,348 on jumps that proved right, -$1,685 on jumps that proved wrong; 33 of the 58 jumps went the wrong way. From 1 to 15 min after the trigger, 18,239 contracts traded, +$1,842 to all takers over 21 days.
6) THIS LADDER PAYS TAKERS. All takers together netted +$12,264 over 21 days, about +$584/day or +1.7c per contract, so the makers are being picked off.
7) CEILING: a bot that knew the 5:05 PM value before the first >=70c print, buying the cheapest winning supply at <=40c and capped at 100 contracts/day, would have made $1,094 over 21 days = $52/day (14 of 21 days had such supply). A real bot often picks the wrong 0.1 bucket (point 2), so its share is well below that; not measured.
8) CALENDAR: VoteHub's generic-ballot average ends 2026-11-03, so about 18 settlement days are left. During the live logging (1:31-2:16 PM ET 10-16) no new poll was entered. The value stayed 8.1; E8.1 was quoted 45-49c bid / 60-63c ask.
test.artefact_checks: Winner selection: the jump pool counts every bucket that jumped, winner or not; the 33 of 58 wrong jumps are netted in. The prize is labelled as a perfect-foresight ceiling, not a strategy result. Lookahead: the settled value is used only to score; trigger timing uses tape timestamps only. Recompute phase: measured on one afternoon (5 stamps, 52-81 s past the mark). If the phase drifts from day to day, the timing test is weaker than shown, but a drifting phase would push the result toward uniform, not create a pile-up. Release times: only 2 of the 8 have a time of day (Fox from its own page; Focaldata has a date only); 'entered the next day' comes from created_at, which is a date only. Snapshot match: D, R and the weight sum all matched, three independent checks. Units: prices are yes_price_dollars x100; weights and percentages as VoteHub publishes them, never inferred from magnitude. Taker fee 0.07 x P x (1-P) per contract (series multiplier x1; no maker fee). Self-tests in pool.py pass. A dead path checked: the raw api.votehub.com list has no weights and a date-only created_at, and 129 raw rows are excluded from the average (mostly adults-only duplicates); whether a new poll shows up there before the recompute was not observed, because no poll was entered during logging.
test.supply_we_would_get: On KXVHGCB itself, not a proxy. Before VoteHub entered the poll, the winning bucket had cheap supply (<=40c) on 14 of 21 days, usually hundreds to a few thousand contracts a day (4,223 on 10-15, 4,648 on 10-12). It came both as resting asks to take and as sellers hitting a resting bid. At our size (about 100 contracts) depth is not the limit; picking the right 0.1 bucket is. After the page moves, the first 10 s go to faster bots; 1-15 min later about 870 contracts a day still trade in the jump direction (all takers, right and wrong jumps mixed).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: Not measured. With perfect foresight at 100 contracts a day the ceiling is $52/day. With the bucket guessed from a weight we cannot read in advance (right about half the time in the one case checked), plausibly $0-20/day, and only for the roughly 18 settlement days left before Nov 3: a total upside of roughly $0-300.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: Not measured. There is depth for about 300 contracts a day on the cheap side (perfect-foresight ceiling about $100-150/day). Realistic is plausibly $0-40/day, with the same Nov 3 end.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: A 100-contract set swings about +/-$45 per event. With the 8-12 entry events left before Nov 3, the standard error is about $14, so only an edge of about $28 per event (about +28c per contract) could be told apart from zero. Timing test: with 58 triggers, a doubling of the first-2-minute rate is detectable (and was seen); a 30% excess would not be.
test.worst_case: Buy the predicted bucket and both neighbours for about 65c combined, 100 sets; a second poll entered the same afternoon moves the value outside all three: -$65 that day. A 200-contract single-bucket bet at 30c that misses: -$60. 10-12 shows the trap: the market jumped to the wrong bucket (8.7) twice before 8.4 landed, and the 4,500 contracts bought on those jumps lost $1,098.
test.next_test:
Start today, read-only, no orders.
(1) A VoteHub recorder: poll /averages (25 KB) every 15 s with a cache-buster. Whenever last_updated changes, save the in-average poll list with weights and the value. Also poll the raw api.votehub.com list every 60 s, to see whether a new poll appears there before the 10-minute recompute.
(2) A release log: the RealClearPolling generic-ballot table every 5 min, giving the time each poll becomes public.
(3) Pull the public KXVHGCB tape daily.
Paper rule, fixed in advance: when a poll is public but not yet in VoteHub, predict VoteHub's margin from the weights VoteHub shows plus that pollster's last fresh weight from the recorder. Paper-buy the predicted bucket and both neighbours at the live ask if the three cost <= 65c, 100 sets, scored at 5:05 PM ET. Read on 2026-10-27, after 8 trading days.
Pass bar: >= 6 events, paper net >= +$150, >= 4 of 6 sets paid, and a median release-to-entry gap of >= 3 h.
Kill: on 3 of the first 5 events the market moves >= 30c toward the right bucket before VoteHub enters the poll (someone else already front-runs), or there are fewer than 4 events.
Even a pass leaves only about one week (10-28..11-03) to trade, so the operator should decide whether roughly $0-300 is worth the build. The lesson that carries over: these Kalshi markets moved on the aggregator's recompute, not on the poll's release. Check it on any later VoteHub-settled ladder (Trump approval) and on KXTRUMPAPPROVE (RCP, 50x the volume), where SI34 found the opposite.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's only evidence that a bot can pick the bucket before VoteHub enters a poll is sens.py: on the 10-15 Fox+AP-NORC entry, a guessed weight of 0.5-0.8 for each poll gives the right bucket, 8.1. That check used TODAY's post-entry weights for the old polls, which a bot cannot see before the entry, so it is lookahead.

My own redo without lookahead (naive.py) starts from VoteHub's published pre-entry value (10-14: D 49.2 / R 41.1). It allows any pre-entry weight total from 7.81 to 9.51 and new-poll weights anywhere in the observed 0.27-0.91 range. Only 16% of those inputs land on the true 8.1 bucket; 60% give 8.2 and 23% give 8.3. With Fox alone, which is all that was public at 6 PM ET 10-14, the split is 41% 8.1 and 50% 8.2.

My peel test (peel.py) removes the newest polls from today's weight list and compares the result with VoteHub's published value for the day before. It matches on 0 of 12 dates. The errors run from -0.1 to -0.5 points, plus one of +1.0; the one-day cut is off by -0.2, which is 2 buckets. So VoteHub reweights the old polls between days by about as much as a new poll moves the average. The tester's log shows weights fixed within a day, so the shift happens at day boundaries or at entries; I cannot separate the two. Other traders already trade on it: at 00:32-00:50 ET on 10-15, E8.1 was sold from 27c to 18c and 'below 7.9' was bought from 4c to 35c, with 7,543 contracts traded in that hour.

So betting a single bucket has no support. Only 3-bucket or tail sets survive, and they carry four execution costs:
- (a) Late entry. If VoteHub enters the poll after 5:05 PM, a set that leaves out the no-change bucket loses everything. On 10-12, buyers paid an average of 47c for the no-change bucket E8.7 before the entry.
- (b) Thin neighbour buckets. On 10-15 before the entry, only 15 contracts of E8.0 and 52 of E8.3 were bought from asks. In today's book E8.0 shows 2 lots at the best ask and 65 within 10c; buying 100 averages 48.8c against a 41c best ask. The best asks on the 26OCT16 ladder add up to at least 140c.
- (c) Front-runners already exist. Someone bought 2,462 E8.4 at 11-13c at 6:02 PM ET on 10-11, 18.5 h before VoteHub entered the poll. Before the 10-13 entry, 1,763 'below 8.4' were bought from asks at 14c.
- (d) Time is short. VoteHub's average ends on 2026-11-03 (my own /averages query), so 18 settlement days are left, and the 10-27 paper read leaves about a week to trade.

I could not get it to dead. A naive model without lookahead, betting sets, would have found cheap winning supply big enough for 100 contracts before the entry on all three traced days:
- 10-12: 3,304 E8.4 bought from asks at an average of 14.0c.
- 10-13: 1,763 'below 8.4' at 14.4c. The naive model's range of 8.16-8.38 falls entirely inside that one bucket.
- 10-15: 1,279 E8.1 at 31.0c.

These are three days picked after the fact, and most of the polls' release times are unknown, so they are anecdotes, not a rate. Verdict: still plausible-needs-data, and only the set version, not the single-bucket version.

refs.strongest_objection:
Look-ahead in the key support. The tester's sens.py builds the pre-entry base by deleting the two 10-15 polls from TODAY's (post-entry) weight list. That base is D 49.103 / R 41.191, shown as 7.9. The page before entry actually showed 49.2 / 41.1 = 8.1. So when VoteHub enters a poll it also re-weights the old ones, and on 10-15 that moved the old set by about -0.19 points, about the same size as the new polls' own pull (about +0.16 to +0.2). Neither the tester's kernel (right on 4 of 27 days) nor my no-kernel backcast (right on 4 of 20) reproduces that re-weighting.

The paper rule ("VoteHub's shown weights plus the pollster's last fresh weight") is exactly the plain add-the-poll update. It picks the wrong bucket on the tester's own showcase case even when given the true weights.

Replay of the 3-bucket rule on the 8 entry days 10-05..10-15 (hourly asks from candlesticks, buy when the set costs <= 65c). This replay already knows the weights, so it is a hypothesis only. At 10 AM ET it trades 4 times and is right on 2: -26c, +75c, +35c, -38c a set. That is about +$45 at 100 sets over 11 days, with a standard error of about +/-$100: zero.

VoteHub's average ends 11-03, so at most about 8-12 entries are left. The tester's own smallest detectable edge is about 28c a contract; the replay suggests about 11c a set, so the edge can never be confirmed before the series expires.

Other checks:
- Phase test: it counted buckets that jumped together as independent. 58 bucket jumps are 48 recompute episodes, and chi-square drops from 21.0 to 8.7, not significant (5% bar 16.9). The first-2-minute excess survives, weaker: 17 against 9.6 expected, P 0.009.
- Reproduced exactly on my own pull: all takers +$12,264.34 on 739,864 contracts. The $1,094 ceiling splits into $773 over the 11 days the value changed and $321 over the 10 days it did not. Those 10 days belong to the other lane's 'yesterday's bucket' idea, not to poll front-running.

The page before entry showed D 49.2 / R 41.1 = 8.1 (my own pull of VoteHub's values series; Kalshi settled 10-14 at 8.1). Adding both polls (D+9 each) with their TRUE weights (0.789, 0.91) shows 8.2-8.4 on 603 of 605 grid points (the whole D/R rounding range, with the old polls' total weight scaled 0.8x to 1.25x). It settled 8.1. The tester's 'right bucket' came from a post-entry base of 7.9. refs.strongest_objection:
Both skeptics agree that betting a single bucket has no support. They split on whether the 3-bucket set is still alive. It is not.

I measured it on all 14 entry days (not on 3 days picked afterwards), with no look-ahead:
- The model's 3-bucket set caught the settled value on 8 of 14 days.
- The free bet "yesterday's value +-0.1" was right on 11 of 14.
- Even when given each poll's true weight, the model was right on only 10 of 14.

So the model knows nothing the market does not. The cause is the one the stats skeptic found: when VoteHub enters a new poll, it also re-weights the old ones, and that moves the value about as much as the new poll does. Nobody outside VoteHub can model it.

The paper rule's own filter (buy only when the set costs <= 65c) picks out the days when the model is wrong. At 10 AM ET it bought on 6 days and won once: -$156 at 100 sets.

The execution skeptic's "cheap winning supply existed on 3 traced days" is a perfect-hindsight count picked afterwards. A model without look-ahead would not have bought it.

The sample is small. There were 6 trades, with a spread of about 33-52c a set, so the loss on its own is only about 1.3 standard errors from zero. What decides it is the hit-rate comparison plus the calendar. VoteHub's average ends 2026-11-03: 18 settlement days and about 10-12 entries are left, which is too few to ever detect an edge.

Caveats that do not change the ruling:
- created_at is a date only, so a poll entered after 5:05 PM ET is counted on the wrong day.
- Polls that have since dropped out of the average are missing from today's list.
- Hourly candle closes are not depth we could actually trade.

What carries over is a separate idea: the market moves on VoteHub's 10-minute recompute. Test that on KXTRUMPVH, which does not expire, and record the weights before and after each entry.

idea.name: Endorsement-count lock (KXTRUMPENDORSEMENTS) with an image-reading counter -- the text counter is dead; the in-burst supply is large (WEAK)
markets: KXTRUMPENDORSEMENTS ('at least N endorsements on Truth Social, Sat-Fri', ~7 markets/week)
idea.mechanism: Count endorsement posts in real time, reading the GRAPHICS (OCR or an image classifier on the post images, since most endorsements are images whose text is not in the archive HTML), dedupe per Kalshi's rule (one person once per week; slates count each name), and buy 'At least N' YES the moment the Nth lands, during the burst while the crossing strike still trades 55-90c.
idea.why_mispriced: Endorsements arrive in bursts of 10-30 posts in an hour; during the burst the crossing strike trades from 5c to 99c (08-13: 'At least 50' 11,802 contracts at an average 59c in one hour; 08-17: 'At least 20/25' 4,366 + 4,381 at 87c; 09-01: 'At least 15' 2,557 at 63c). Whoever counts exactly and fast takes it.
idea.must_be_true: An image-reading counter matches Kalshi's count in 9 of 10 historical weeks; the burst lasts long enough (an hour, observed) that a laptop counter is not out-raced; post images are retrievable from a public archive.
idea.evidence_so_far: Hunter politics-entertainment-tech: the TEXT regex matched Kalshi's settled range in 3 of 10 weeks (counts 2,2,3,3,0,4,3,1,16,3 vs ranges 50+, 50+, 25-49, 5-9, 3-4, 10-14, 20-24, 0-2, 15-19, 3-4); where a lock was found, winner <= 90c after it = $544 gross / 10 weeks with 0 false locks. Final-day winner <= 90c for the family $8,948 / 10 weeks.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0 as a text bot (measured). With an image counter: unknown; in-burst supply $500-5,000 per burst hour for all takers, speed-shared. Worst plausible week: a miscount buys a strike that settles NO, -$100 to -$300.
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 ladder (7 markets) per week
idea.test_plan: Only if an image counter is built: replay the 10 weeks' bursts (archive timestamps vs tape), require the counter in-range 9 of 10 weeks before any paper lock, then measure supply at +2 s / +10 s / +60 s after each lock as I33 did.
idea.prior_reason: Real supply, but the exact count is the whole trade and nothing shows an image counter can match Kalshi's rule; build cost before any test.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: Not in the ledger (SJ14/SI52 are 'says' word markets).
idea.worst_case: A miscount: full stake on that strike, -$100 to -$300 at our size.

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's arithmetic reproduces, but the edge is untested where the money actually is.

1. One market carries almost all the supply. Of the tester's "realistic" +2 min supply ($743), $702 comes from SEP04-A20. $530 of that (2,023 contracts) was bought 6 hours to 3 days after our lock, at 59-79c. All that time the market priced the strike at about 70%, and NO buyers kept paying 22-34c. This is money from disagreeing with the market, not from being fast.

2. The post behind it was ambiguous. It was a disaster-aid announcement that mentions "Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick, Ken Paxton ... and the entire ticket of Republican Candidates, who have my Complete and Total Endorsement". It took the count to exactly the strike: 20, in a 20-24 range. It settled YES, but only once.

3. The false-lock bound uses the wrong count. The tester's "0 false locks in 34, so at most about 9%" includes 31 locks the market agreed with within seconds, and those carry about $0. Count only the contested locks (market below 90c for more than an hour after our lock):
   - 1 settled exact-strike slate lock: the 95% upper bound on the false-lock rate is 95%.
   - 3 if the two Sunday-open At-least-3 locks are added: the bound is 63%.
   - Break-even is a false-lock rate of 25-30% for entries at 70-75c, so the sample cannot tell a winning strategy from a losing one.

4. The counter was tuned in-sample. Its rules were set while looking at all 10 weeks. It sits at the bottom of Kalshi's range in 4 of 8 in-range weeks and under the range in 2. Undercounting protects YES buys, but it can also hide a name the counter wrongly credits. The open week (counter 10, At-least-15 at 61-64c) may be a third undercount.

5. Kalshi's rules partly back the tester. rules_secondary says slates count per name ("all will be counted") and reaffirmations count. It also counts "Vote for X" and "I support X", which the strict counter ignores.

So I found no measurement bug. But the profit rests on a rule-reading bet with one settled case.

refs.strongest_objection:
The money left after the first 2 minutes is not supply that slow bots leave behind. It exists when the market disputes the count, and for that group of locks the 0-of-34 false-lock record is the wrong denominator. Every settled event with real supply locked AT the strike or one above it:
- SEP04-A20: the counter's final week count is 20 against a strike of 20, and the slate rule that produced the count was written after looking at that week.
- OCT09-A3: count 3 at the Sunday open.
- AUG21-A3: count 4 at the open.
- OCT16-A10: exactly 10, still pending.

Any one name credited wrongly turns such a lock into a total loss. The market held 58-84c on these for minutes to days. The SEP04-A20 ask sat at 92-95c from +5 min to +3.5 h after the lock, then drifted to 60-68c over Wed-Fri, so the supply after +1 h was a 3-day disagreement, not slow takers. That one event is 55% of all the >=2-minute supply ($702 of $1,283). The sample that matters is 4 settled wins, all in-sample: the 95% upper bound on the false-lock rate is about 53%, against a break-even of about 19% at 80c entries.

The tester's planned source, the trumpstruth.org archive, lagged 22-32 min (measured below), so it fails the tester's own pass bar of a median under 60 s. A buyer who trades in lots of 200 contracts shows up in every event, sometimes 8-11 s after the post, sometimes 3 h later. Capital also binds at the current bank, against the tester's claim that only supply does: the SEP04 3-day drift was about 2,000 contracts, roughly $1,400 at about 70c, while the pin bot needs up to about $285 of the $1,155.

It is not dead:
- Kalshi's rules (own GET) count slates, 'Vote for X', 'I support X' and Saturday posts made before the Sunday open, so the strict counter is a lower bound. Kalshi's range was at or above it in all 10 weeks.
- Disputed offers stood 25-55 min (OCT16-A10 at 0.73-0.84; OCT09-A3 at 0.81-0.84).
- The direct Truth Social API works from this machine, against the tester's 403.

The tester's ~$4/day is about 2x too high: it skips the false-lock haircut and leans on one event.

idea.name: Polymarket US futures/politics maker quoted off Kalshi's same-question mid, collecting Poly's maker rebate
markets: Polymarket US futures (4,641 sports, 1,006 politics of 6,000+ open; e.g. aachc-cfb-wins, tec-nfl-mvp, paccc-usho-midterms, ewc-usgub-*)
Kalshi season wins / awards / midterm / governor markets (anchor and hedge)
idea.mechanism: Rest two-sided quotes on Poly US futures 1-2c outside Kalshi's mid on the identical question; each fill earns the spread plus the maker rebate (0.0125 x C x p x (1-p): 0.31c at 50c, 0.09c at 10c); hedge on Kalshi only when net exposure passes a cap.
idea.why_mispriced: Polymarket US subsidises makers and its futures books are thin.
idea.must_be_true: Retail actually hits quotes on Poly US futures (volume and depth unmeasured: outcomePrices is a string of two prices, not a book); identical resolution text on both venues (SJ46: 20 'big gaps' were different questions); capital: the Poly pot is $60, so anything more needs his deposit.
idea.evidence_so_far: Listing via the operator's read-only key: 6,000+ open markets, 'futures' 5,994, tick 0.01; fee schedule from docs.polymarket.us. Depth and trade rate: not measured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0-2/day on the $60 pot; maybe $5-15/day after a ~$1,000 Poly deposit IF fills reach 50+ contracts a day (a guess). Worst plausible: an informed fill on an awards/election market before the hedge, -$20 to -$60.
idea.settlements_per_day: Futures settle at season/event end; fills would be the daily flow
idea.test_plan: Run the repo's scan_poly_ws.py read-only for 48 h on 50 shared markets: trades, depth, and how often Poly's best price crosses Kalshi's mid by >= 2c. Bar: >= 100 contracts a day traded by others within 2c of Kalshi's mid.
idea.prior_reason: Capped by a $60 pot without a deposit, unmeasured volume, and the same-question trap that emptied SJ46.
merged_from: cross-venue: Polymarket US season-futures/politics maker (idea 5)
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SJ46 killed the taker locks and SI43 the BTC maker; the futures/politics maker with the rebate priced, on a 6,000-market listing, is new.
idea.worst_case: -$20 to -$60 on an informed fill at the current pot.

test.method:
Read-only, 2026-10-16 17:00-18:30Z, no orders placed.
(1) Pulled the Polymarket US open listing: 200 GETs, capped at 20,000 markets (it was 6,000 on 10-13). Matched each Poly market to the Kalshi market asking the same question, by name, state or district: 1,061 pairs (KXHOUSERACE 688, SENATE* 66, GOVPARTY* 64, KXNCAAF 48, KXNFLMVP 43, KXHEISMAN 35, KXSB 32, KXNFLCOTY 32, KXNBA 30, KXNFLNFCCHAMP 16, KXMLB 3, CONTROLH/S 4). 283 are 'quotable': Kalshi has both a bid and an ask, and its mid is between 5c and 95c.
(2) Snapshotted both venues at t0 and t1: Poly /v1/markets/{slug}/bbo, which includes cumulative sharesTraded, and the public Kalshi /markets.
(3) Recorded the Polymarket US WebSocket (TRADE + MARKET_DATA) on all 1,061 slugs for 45-50 minutes over three connections. A connection allows only 10 subscriptions; I found the cap and split the slugs across connections.
(4) Pulled 14 days of hourly history for the 283 quotable pairs: Poly public price-history (gateway, no auth) and Kalshi 60-minute candles. I measured that a Poly hourly label is the price at the END of that hour, so I shifted the Poly series back 1 hour to line up with Kalshi. On that history I ran four tests:
- Lead-lag: when the two mids differ by 1c or more, which venue closes the gap within 24 h.
- Touch-through maker fills: a quote at Kalshi mid -/+ h counts as filled when Poly's opposite touch reaches it. Fit on the first 7 days, holdout on the last 7, clustered by market and by market-day.
- A round trip that exits with a resting order at the Kalshi mid from entry time.
- A placebo that anchors on Poly's own mid instead of Kalshi's.
(5) Read the fee and rebate schedule at docs.polymarket.us/fees.
(6) Adjacent check: pulled Poly US /v1/incentives and the full order books on 64 matched markets to price a small maker's share of the liquidity reward pools.
Sources, best first: the Poly WebSocket trade tape and both venues' live books, then the book-derived hourly display prices. No replay was used, and our own fill rates are not measured.
test.n_markets: 1,061 matched pairs, 283 quotable. Hourly test: 261-267 markets. Valid-book round trips: 41 markets in the fit half, 42 in the holdout. Live WebSocket: 201 trades on 55 markets; 9 of those markets had trades 1.5c or more beyond Kalshi's mid.
test.n_independent_clusters: Round trips: 41 + 42 market clusters. House, Senate and Governor legs all move with the same national environment, so there are roughly 30-40 truly independent events. Live window: 9 markets, about 5 events; a single Maine Senate burst supplied 71% of the contracts that traded off Kalshi's price.
test.result:
The rebate leg is dead. docs.polymarket.us/fees: the flat maker rebate (-0.0125 x C x p(1-p)) ends Oct 18. From Oct 19 2026 1 PM ET, accounts with under $10M of maker volume in the prior calendar month get 'No maker rebate' (tier 1). It would have averaged only 0.15c/contract on our fills anyway.

Book structure at t0: both venues have a 1c median spread, and the two mids differ by a median 0-1c. A quote at Kalshi mid -/+1.5c would be at the front of Poly's book on 81 of 566 sides (14%); at -/+2c on 57 (10%); at -/+1c on 183 (32%).

Lead-lag (14 days): when the mids differ by 1c or more, Poly closes a median 46% (fit) / 37% (holdout) of the gap within 24 h; Kalshi closes 3% / 6%. Kalshi is the anchor.

Touch-through fills:
- Naive: +1.0c/contract (fit) and +0.6c (holdout) at h=1c, marked to Kalshi's mid 24 h later. But 28% of these fills came from Poly displays showing a 0c or negative spread, which a live book cannot have.
- Valid 1-4c books only, h=1.5c round trip: fit -0.32c/contract (market-cluster mean -0.69c, se 1.45; 49 trips on 41 markets; worst -49c). Holdout +0.66c (se 0.26; 42 trips on 42 markets; worst -5.5c).
- Valid books, h=2c: fit +1.37c (se 1.35; 26 trips; worst -30.5c). Holdout +0.91c (se 0.47; 16 trips).
- Frequency: about 6-7 entries/day at 1.5c and 2-4/day at 2c. Median hold 58-74 h.
- The big losses are sports event jumps: MLB playoff games moved Milwaukee from 16c to 45c, and a Heisman leg went from 25c to 38c.
- Marked to Poly's own later price instead of Kalshi's: about 0 at +24 h (-0.36c, se 0.43 / +0.29c, se 0.27); +1.1c / +0.8c at +72 h.
- Placebo anchored on Poly's own mid: -11c to -19c per fill.

Live 45-minute WebSocket window: 201 trades, 31,695 contracts. The WebSocket quantity equals Poly's sharesTraded change to the contract on 9 of the top 10 markets. 6,069 contracts on 9 markets traded 1.5c or more beyond Kalshi's mid in the taker's direction, and Kalshi's mid had not moved 30 minutes later (+1.5c markout over 30 trades; one window, no holdout). About 26,000 contracts traded within 2c of Kalshi's mid, so the hunter's bar of 100/day is cleared more than 100x, but that bar says nothing about profit.

Adjacent finding (not this idea): all 64 matched markets checked carry an active Poly US liquidity pool.
- Pools per period: midterm toss-ups $560 (target 25,000 contracts, discount 0.3), competitive governor races $315, NBA champion $150, MLB postseason $75, CFB futures $36, NFL futures $22, House races $5.
- 100 contracts resting at the best price would earn $0.2-2.3/day on toss-up and control books, and $0.1-0.5/day on NBA and MLB.
- On thin-touch legs (NFL coach of the year and MVP, CFB champion and Heisman) it would be $4-14/day IF the pool is per market. If it is per event and shared across the event's 30-50 legs, divide those by 30-50. This is not resolved.
test.artefact_checks:
(1) Poly's hourly price-history label is the price at the end of the hour: 78 of 78 hours with a price change matched minute 59 and none matched minute 0. Shifted Poly back 1 h; the result did not change.
(2) Locked or crossed Poly displays (0c or negative spread) produced 28% of the naive fills. Removing them took the fit-half edge from +1.0c to -0.3c.
(3) The placebo anchored on Poly's own mid loses 11-19c per fill, so the Kalshi-anchored result is not a generic artefact of the fill model.
(4) Marked to Poly's own later price, the edge is about 0 at 24 h. So the edge is 'Kalshi is right and Poly comes back to it within about 3 days'. It is realised only through a second maker fill or at settlement (Nov 2026 - Feb 2027).
(5) The WebSocket quantity unit is contracts: it matches the sharesTraded changes.
(6) Same-question trap: chamber control first matched the 2028 Kalshi markets, which showed a fake 15c gap; fixed to 2026. Poly's election legs are named candidates while Kalshi's are parties ('sworn in' / 'inaugurated'): nearly the same question, not identical.
(7) Kalshi candle closes and Poly labels are aligned to the same real time. Noise in Kalshi's mid biases AGAINST the strategy, because quotes set off a noisy mid are worse.
(8) Liquidity pool scope (per market vs per event) and the per-side split are the classic unit trap and are NOT resolved.
test.supply_we_would_get: On Polymarket US (the venue we would quote on), matched futures and politics markets. At Kalshi mid -/+1.5c we would be first in Poly's queue on about 14% of quotable sides today. On valid books that gives about 6-7 touch-through fills per day. Live, 6,069 contracts traded 1.5c or more beyond Kalshi's mid on 9 markets in 45 minutes. That is far more than the $60 Poly pot can hold (about 98 contracts at a median $0.61) and more than a $2,000 Poly balance could hold (about 3,300 contracts). Not measured: our place in the queue behind Poly's existing makers when we quote a tied price.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0.10/day (range -$0.10 to +$0.25). The $60 Poly pot holds about 98 contracts; the edge is -0.3c to +0.7c per contract (fit vs holdout) per 2.5-4 day turnover. The rebate is worth about $0.15 once before Oct 19, then $0. A liquidity-pool share with $60 in one thin market is $0.1 to $10/day depending on the unresolved pool scope; not counted.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: If about $2,000 of a $5,000 bank sat on Poly (his deposit decision): about 3,300 contracts of inventory, worth about $1-4/day if the holdout's +0.66c holds and about $0 if the fit half is right. A liquidity-pool share could add more; unmeasured, and its scope is unresolved.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Holdout se 0.26c, so about 0.5c/contract at 2 se. Fit se 1.45c, so about 2.9c. Pooled about 1c. The 45-minute live window cannot resolve anything under about 1.5c.
test.worst_case: An event jumps on inventory filled just before it. Observed losses were 13c to 49c per contract on sports futures (MLB playoff games, a Heisman leg after a game). At the $60 pot that is -$20 to -$48 in a day. Unhedged election legs settle at 0 or 1 on Nov 3, so the whole $60 is at risk that night. With $2,000 on Poly: -$300 to -$600 on a correlated election move or a bad sports night.
test.next_test:
A. Read-only 7-day recorder, no orders.
- Record the Poly WebSocket (TRADE + MARKET_DATA) on the 283 quotable pairs (3 connections x 10 subscriptions) and Kalshi books every 10 s.
- Simulate quotes at Kalshi mid -/+1.5c and -/+2c with real queue position: a tied price joins behind existing size.
- Fill only from actual Poly trades; exit with a resting order at Kalshi's mid; pull sports-futures quotes during games.
- Mark to Kalshi's and Poly's mids at +72 h.
- Pre-registered pass bar: at least +0.5c/contract on at least 60 round trips across at least 30 markets, no single loss above 25c, and at least 300 contracts/day where we would have been first in line.

B. Liquidity-pool scope, which decides whether a thin market is worth $0.2 or $10/day.
- With his per-instance sign-off, rest 50 contracts (about $10) at the best price on one thin-touch qualifying leg for 2 days.
- Read GET /v1/incentives/earnings once paid, within 7 business days.
- Bar: at least $1/day per $50 resting, net of fills marked to Kalshi.

Either way it only pays if he moves money onto Poly; at the $60 pot it is about $0.1/day. Scratch: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C3-14/ (23 MB; RESULT.json saved there). The collector and feed recorder were still writing at 18:28Z, and 110 GB of disk is free.

refs.strongest_objection:
The statistics survive, but the fill model has not been tested. In both sims, every fill and every exit is a 'touch-through' read off hourly snapshots of Poly's displayed best price. None of them is an observed trade. Poly US has a post-only order flag: per docs.polymarket.us/api-reference/orders/create-order, participateDontInitiate means 'Order will be rejected if it would immediately match'. So a Poly maker re-quoting down through our bid would be rejected and would not fill us. Poly US also has no public trade history (every trade route returns 404), so nobody has shown that these displayed moves were real sellers hitting a resting bid.

The edge is entirely in House races. My number for them is +1.57c per contract, against +0.16c (zero) for everything else on about 20 independent events. House markets are thin: a median of 56 contracts a day per market over their life, and 0.054 touch events per market-day, which is about 6 a day across all House markets. They also settle on Nov 3, 18 days from now. After that nothing measurable is left. The $60 Poly pot caps the money at cents a day either way.

Checks I ran that failed to refute it:
- Price-history semantics: the last minute matched the live book on 60 of 60 markets.
- Hour label: 128 of 128 changed hours match minute 59, so the tester's 1-hour shift is right and there is no look-ahead.
- Dust at the touch: 13 of 560 sides under 1 contract; median size 1,740.
- End-of-sample censoring: a fixed 7-day mark gives +0.90c, higher than the tester's censored +0.66c.
- Survivorship: 430 pairs that are not quotable now gave +0.73c, no worse than the quotable set.
- Clustering: errors clustered by market, district and day all give similar se, and all four weekly blocks are positive.
refs.independent_number:
Own 30-day hourly pull: Poly public gateway plus Kalshi public 60-minute candles, 709 matched pairs, including 430 not quotable now. Each fill is scored at a fixed 7-day horizon, with no end-of-sample censoring, strict valid books, and quotes at Kalshi mid -/+1.5c.
- House races: +1.57c/contract on 106 round trips, 90 markets, 74 districts. se 0.17 clustered by market, 0.16 by entry day. First half +1.78c, second half +1.43c. Worst trip -5.5c.
- All other families: +0.16c on 97 trips, 20 events, se 0.22-0.41. Halves +0.47c and -0.30c.
- At a 24-hour mark the edge is -0.14c (se 0.24-0.28). It only appears over several days.
- The tester's censored 7+7-day split reproduced on my data: fit -0.23c, holdout +0.63c (se 0.25), against their -0.32c and +0.66c.

refs.strongest_objection:
Live Poly books leave no room to be first in line. My own match covers 115 pairs (66 politics, 49 sports futures). Across 4 live snapshots (2026-10-16 18:40-19:42Z), 0 of 230 sides would let a quote at Kalshi mid -/+1.5c sit strictly inside Poly's spread. 16-17 sides would cross Poly's book, which is a taker trade (the dead SJ46 lock), not a maker quote. The rest join the back of a queue with a median ~37,000 contracts ahead. The tester's '14% at the front' counted those crossing sides as front.

The openings do happen, but briefly. In 6 days of minute-level history they appeared in 0.58% of market-minutes, with a median length of 3 minutes, and 39 of 51 fills landed within 5 minutes of an opening. So a bot has to react within seconds when Poly's book widens.

15 of the 66 fills at 1.5c came from a single Poly book wipe-and-rebuild on 10-15, 11:40-12:15Z (books like 0.04/0.98). Those were makers re-posting, not takers selling. Of the 51 fills left, 47 are on thin sports-futures legs. The most-filled ones (NFL coach of the year) traded 0 contracts in my 53-minute flow window, so fill size is not measured.

What survives is +0.55c/contract on the round trip (se 0.51) and +0.82c against Kalshi's mid 24 h later (se 0.70). Neither can be told apart from zero.

Capital: the $60.52 pot is a $50 bonus hold plus $10.52 cash. At 10 contracts per fill it is fully locked in unexited inventory by day 2-4: 21 of 51 fills never exited inside 6 days. Those legs settle Dec 2026-Jun 2027 (sports) or Jan-Feb 2027 (elections).

The rebate is gone for this account from Oct 19, 1 PM ET (tier 1 gets no rebate). A Kalshi taker hedge costs a median 1.35c/contract on politics and 1.08c on sports, against a 1.5c edge, and Kalshi's sports futures also charge makers. research/polyorder.py cannot rest an order longer than 60 s or trade non-BTC slugs, so a new order path would be needed.

idea.name: Payroll wings: buy both far wings when the market's payroll ladder is tighter than the consensus-error history
idea.mechanism: The night before the jobs report, buy both far wings at 2-5c when the market's central 90% band is narrower than the historical consensus-error sd (~75k).
idea.why_mispriced: In all 3 settled releases (Jul, Aug, Sep 2026) the realised number fell in a bucket the market priced at 2-6c (Aug 150-175k vs a 50k median; Jul negative vs 80k; Sep 20-30k vs 90k); the Fed/NBER study (Diercks, Katz & Wright 2026) found CPI/U3 well calibrated but did not test payrolls.
idea.must_be_true: n=3 is not evidence; needs 12+ releases; each wing must win more than ~8 times in 100 to pay at 2-5c.
idea.evidence_so_far: 3 of 3 payroll releases outside the market's central band at close; CPI 0 of 2 and U3 1 of 3 (calibrated-looking).
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $0-5/day averaged (one release a month) at either bank; worst month -$10 at 100 contracts of wings.
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 per month
idea.test_plan: Pull Kalshi payroll ladders at close for every release since 2023 (older series or the study's replication repo github WillBtK/macro_kalshi); count realised-outside-90%-band. Bar >= 25% of releases (10% if calibrated).
idea.prior_reason: Three data points and a few dollars a month; the historical pull is cheap, which is the only reason to keep it.
merged_from: econ-nowcast: Payroll wings: the market's payroll ladder may be too tight
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No payroll-calibration row; SI07 is the post-print race.
idea.worst_case: -$10 a month.

test.method:
The idea as stated (buy both far wings at 2-5c) is DEAD. A variant on the same thesis survives only as a hypothesis: in months when the payroll ladder is narrow (implied sd under 75k), buy the 8-30c shoulder rungs on both sides.

Data, best source first: exchange candles and the trade tape, plus Kalshi's own settlement. No replay and no model of our fills. All pulls read-only and unauthenticated:
- Every settled KXPAYROLLS/PAYROLLS/PROLLS release from Mar 2023 to Sep 2026, from /historical/markets plus the live tier: 43 events, 396 strike markets.
- The realised first print (expiration_value). It never disagreed with the strike results.
- Hourly candles (best bid/ask close) for every strike over the last 50 h before close.

Written in prereg.json before any P&L was computed:
- Snapshot at close minus 12 h (about 8:30 pm ET the evening before).
- High wing: the lowest strike with YES ask at or under 5c. Low wing: the highest strike with YES bid at or over 95c.
- 100-lot taker at the candle quote, fee ceil(0.07*C*P*(1-P)) with fee_multiplier 1. Settled on Kalshi's result field.
- Fit = closes before 2025-01-01 (21 releases); test = 2025-01-01 onward (21). One release = one cluster. 25OCT excluded (report cancelled).

Calibration: a probit fit of the monotone (PAVA) mid ladder gives the market's mean mu and sd sigma_mkt. z = (realised - mu)/sigma_mkt, and lambda = sqrt(mean z^2): 1 means calibrated, above 1 means the market is too tight. Robustness runs: snapshots at 1 h and 36 h, wing caps 3c and 10c.

Post hoc, labelled hypothesis: a shoulder rule. Fair value = N(mu_mkt, sigma_fair), with sigma_fair = the fit-period RMSE of the miss (85,745 jobs). Buy the best rung per side when fair minus price minus fee is at least 3c and price is at most 30c, scored on test. Also a model-free baseline that buys every 8-30c shoulder.

test.method:
Sources: Kalshi's own quote history (hourly and 1-minute candles, yes bid/ask close). This is not our fills and not pinsim. It is scored against the NBM text archive: NBS 6-h PoP from IEM and the NOAA AWS bucket, and NBE 12-h PoP streamed from AWS for every 21Z cycle 07-24..10-14 (parser checked against a hand-read file). Every forecast run counts only from its AWS upload time + 5 min, and only if that is at or before the quote.

FACT that reshaped the idea: a daily KXRAIN market for day D is listed at 09:10Z on D-1 (5:10 AM ET) and closes ~05-08Z D+1. So no day-after-tomorrow market ever exists. The longest-lead daily book is the D-1 morning one, right after listing.

Three parts:
(A) KXRAINWKND (Sat+Sun rain, 23 cities, listed Mon 09:10Z). 8 settled weekends 08-22..10-10, 173 scorable markets; WPB dropped (no NBS station). Quote is Friday 8 PM ET with the 21Z Friday NBS. Model = 1-prod(1-p06) over the 8 weekend periods, logistic-recalibrated ONLY on weekday pseudo-weekends (rain on D or D+1, D = Mon..Thu, 1,091 pairs), so no weekend outcome enters the fit.
(C) Same with the NBE at Wednesday and Thursday 8 PM ET. P12, the two edge periods half-weighted, recalibrated the same way at the same lead.
(B) Daily KXRAIN at listing. The parent's rule (10c margin, 50-lot fee, both sides, hold to settle) with the 06Z D-1 NBS run. Entry at listing +5..+170 min from 1-minute candles, carried forward. Trade tape from listing to +6 h for supply, plus overlap with the parent's evening legs.

Holdout: the at-listing rule was found on the live tier (target dates 08-16..10-15). Listing+30 min was then pre-registered in hist_test.py and scored on the untouched historical tier 07-27..08-15.

Clusters: weekends (A, C); target dates (B).

Scripts and outputs (*.out) in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-10/: probe.py, pull_wk.py, wk_test.py, pull_nbe.py, wk_nbe.py, pull_daily.py, daily_morning.py, pull_open.py, open_analysis.py, pull_hist.py, hist_test.py, trend.py, extra_checks.py, phantom.py. The median such trade comes 28 min after listing, so being first at +5..+15 min is the whole game. (5) The weekend part rests on 7-8 weekends, and its fill size was never measured.
refs.independent_number: My own pipeline (NBS 06Z text streamed from NOAA AWS with my own parser, gated on Last-Modified + 5 min, plus my own Kalshi 1-min event candles and results, 30 target dates 09-16..10-15) reproduces October at listing+30 exactly: 73 legs over 14 dates, +8.9c a contract (date-clustered se 3.8), date-mean +1.9c. That matches the tester to the decimal, so there is no code or look-ahead bug; re-clustering by week does not widen the se. My own trade-tape pull (176 markets), each leg capped at 30 contracts, gives October $1.99 a date at +15 (se 3.27) vs $7.27 at +30 (se 5.31). On the newest listings (10-16/10-17), the model is +4.3c above the ask on 80%+ books, vs +14.3c in late September.

refs.strongest_objection: Execution does not kill the daily at-listing leg. The prices are real, nobody else trades at our price before about 09:45Z (5:45 AM ET), and a 30-lot order costs about 0c more than the quoted price. What the tape does show is that the October money rests on one or two dates. At 30 lots with fills capped at what the tape proves was there, the median October date makes $0 at every entry minute. The entry minute alone moves October from $1.65 to $9.09 a date (+30 min is the best of the four, and it was picked by looking). Dropping the single best date takes October to between -$2.23 and +$4.84 a date. The window is also closing. Competing takers show up between +30 and +50 min after listing (median 25 contracts at our price before a +50 entry, 0 before +30). That fits bots acting on the 09Z NBS run, which uploads at ~09:45Z. A live bot must be filled by ~09:40Z, and at +50 October is +6.2c a contract with a date-mean of -1.0c. The weekend half is overstated by the candle price: the best weekend quote is usually 1-5 lots, and 30 lots walk ~4c, which turns Friday's +6.3c into ~+2.5c. Only Thursday clearly clears fee plus walk, on 7 weekends. The paid market makers on the other side (liquidity reward, $100 a period per market) were already paid on every KXRAIN date back to at least 09-07. So the decay is not explained by a reward-program change, and nothing says it stops.
