idea.name: One-touch monthlies vs a Deribit-anchored barrier model (sell touch YES where the bid > model + fee + 2c), from the Nov 1 relisting
merged_from: vol-relative-value: One-touch monthlies vs barrier model carry (sell Kalshi touch YES where bid > 2 x Deribit P(beyond) + fee + 2c) -- WEAK
idea.mechanism: Price each one-touch with the reflection principle (P(touch) ~ 2 x P(terminal beyond), driftless) from the Deribit smile interpolated to month end; sell YES at the bid where it exceeds the model by fee + 2c; hold. Kalshi monitors a per-minute 20% trimmed mean (SJ08), so the continuous-monitoring model over-states the touch probability -- conservative for the seller.
idea.why_mispriced: Retail buys 'ETH hits 3000 this month' lottery tickets; the gap on a 20% move in 18 days is a few cents.
idea.must_be_true: Deribit's driftless smile must be close to the physical touch rate (it embeds a vol premium; SI46 found Kalshi crypto longshots came true 2-3x more often than history); n = 1 snapshot.
idea.evidence_so_far: One snapshot 10-13: 3 of 31 strikes +2.2..+3.5c after fee (ETHMAXMON 3000 bid 12c vs model 7.8%; BTCMINMON 75k/77.5k); the other 28 within +-2c of the model.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: 3.5c on 88c of collateral over 18 days: $0.20-2/day on $90-900 deployed; $1-10/day at $5,000. Worst: -$88 per 100 lots on a 20% month (ETH did +14.6% in one day on Aug 19).
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 per month per series (4 series)
idea.test_plan: Price the Aug and Sep settled one-touch strikes at mid-month from their candles with a DVOL-based model and count touches vs model; at the Nov 1 relisting take daily snapshots (2 calls/day) alongside the SJ08/U4 watcher. Year-long collection; no decision soon.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: SJ08/U4 is the decided-minute lock; SI50/SJ45 are nested pairs and the Poly basis; Deribit-anchored barrier pricing of the touch itself is new.
idea.worst_case: -$88 per 100 lots when ETH rallies 20% inside the month.
idea.prior_reason: One snapshot, $0.20-2/day, one settlement a month: too slow to decide and too small to matter at this bank.

test.method:
Sources, best first: Kalshi's own settled outcomes and candles, then Coinbase and Deribit public history. No replay was used.

(1) Kalshi has a /historical tier: GET /historical/markets?series_ticker= and /historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks, with a cutoff of market_settled_ts 2026-08-17. It serves Jan-Jul 2026, so the test covers 9 settled months (Jan-Sep 2026) x 4 series = 36 events. I pulled 339 markets and hourly candles for all of them (376 public GETs).

(2) Snapshot once a day at 16:00 UTC per live market: 7,409 market-days over 307 markets.
- Bid and ask come from the last hourly candle (median age 0 h).
- Spot is the Coinbase hourly close; sigma is the Deribit DVOL hourly close.
- Touch probability uses the exact continuous-monitoring driftless-GBM touch formula (Monte Carlo self-test PASS).
- The rule is exactly the idea's: sell YES at the bid as a taker (fee 0.07p(1-p)) when bid - model - fee > 2c, first fire per market, hold to settlement.
- Results are clustered by event. Holdout: Jan-May vs Jun-Sep.

(3) Physical check of the model, with no Kalshi data:
- Every UTC day 2021-03..2026-09, BTC and ETH, barriers at 0.3-3.0 sd. A touch is the Coinbase daily high/low reaching the barrier before month end. That gives 134 coin-month clusters.
- Wick bias, measured on our own BRTI/ETH RTI tape over 180 sampled hours: the Coinbase hourly high sits above Kalshi's per-minute 20%-trimmed mean by a median of 2.6 bp (BTC) and 3.6 bp (ETH), p99 15-46 bp. That is negligible against barriers 5-30% away.
- The map from model to real touch rate was fitted on 2021-04..2024-06 and applied to the 2026 Kalshi fires as a clean holdout. Estimator self-test PASS: simulated sigma_true = model gives a ratio of 0.94; 0.75x gives 0.47.

(4) Live books for the open Oct markets (29 GETs).

Scratch: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C1-13/ (kalshi_test.out, long_calib.out, calib_rule.out, regime.out, sens.out, stale.out, zone5.out, supply_now.out, wick.out, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: 339 BTC/ETH monthly one-touch markets pulled (Jan-Oct 2026), 307 of them with snapshots. The rule fired on 114 (110 with bid <= 30c; 48 in the refined model >= 5% version).
test.n_independent_clusters: 36 settled events in 9 months; the fires land in 30-32 of them. BTC and ETH months move together, so there are only about 9-12 truly independent months. The physical check has 134 coin-months (67 per coin), 2021-03..2026-09.
test.result:
Kalshi overall is about fair: selling every 3-60c YES at its first snapshot = -0.8c/contract (145 markets, 37 events).

The idea's rule (bid <= 30c):
- 110 fires in 30 events, 5 touched. Realised +3.82 per contract-set (+3.5c/contract), +- 3.21 event-cluster SE (t about 1.2). The model said +3.71.
- Holdout halves (all bids): Jan-May -0.01, Jun-Sep +3.29.
- Without January: +7.22 +- 1.47. January alone (a crash; 5 MIN strikes touched) cost -$374 per 100 lots per fire. Every other month made +$57 to +$118.
- Fresh-quote subset (candle <= 2 h old and the bid still there the next hour): 99 fires, +2.40 +- 3.19.

Physical check:
- The DVOL model over-states touches in the 10-35% zone (touched/model 0.66-0.78).
- It under-states the far tails: where the model says < 2%, touches came 2.5-2.9x as often in 2021-26, and 5.9x in 2026.
- In the rule zone (model 0.5-30%) the ratio was 0.79 on the fit years, 0.81 on 2024-07..2026-09, and 1.01 in 2026 alone. The volatility premium that favours the seller disappeared in 2026.

Expected value of the rule's 110 fires, depending on which years' touch rates are used:

| Touch rates from | Expected per contract |
|---|---|
| 2021-24 (clean holdout) | +2.4c |
| 2024-26 | +3.0c |
| 2026 only | +0.9c |
| All years | +2.6c |

Fires where the model says 1.5-5% are worth about nothing (+0.2 of the +2.6).

Refinement (model >= 5%, bid <= 30c): 48 fires in 22 events, realised +2.50 +- 2.56, physical-expected +2.08 (about 4.3c/contract). Collateral is 41c per fire-set instead of $1.01.

Sensitivity: vol x0.9 gives +0.58 +- 6.79 (25 touched); vol x1.1 gives +2.33 +- 2.49.

Right now (2026-10-16 19:00Z, 15 days left), no Oct market fires. The closest are BTC 92.5k MAX, bid 10c vs model 7.6% (+1.8c), and ETH 3000 MAX, bid 5c vs model 2.9% (+1.8c, but that is in the zone worth about nothing physically).
test.artefact_checks:
(a) Stale quotes: candle age at fire was median 0.0 h, max 3 h. The bid was still there in the next 3 h on 100 of 110 fires, and the fresh-only subset keeps the sign (+2.40).
(b) Look-ahead: spot, DVOL and the Kalshi bid are all taken at the same hour end; the long history uses the DVOL daily OPEN.
(c) Strikes come from floor_strike/cap_strike, not the ticker. The Feb BTC MIN 45k/50k/55k tickers read 225000/250000/275000.
(d) Wick bias between Coinbase and Kalshi's trimmed-minute BRTI: measured at 3-5 bp median.
(e) Price units are dollars in both candle tiers; the historical tier names fields close/high, the live tier close_dollars.
(f) DVOL is divided by 100 and annualised on a 365-day year; checked by the Monte Carlo self-test.
(g) Not checked:
- The per-strike Deribit smile. DVOL was used flat; the physical map absorbs the overall level but not month-to-month skew changes.
- Historical bid SIZE. Only traded volume and today's books were available.
test.supply_we_would_get:
Markets: Kalshi KXBTCMAXMON, KXBTCMINMON, KXETHMAXMON and KXETHMINMON.
- About 12 fires a month (110 in 9.5 months); about 5 a month in the model >= 5% version.
- Contracts traded on a fired market in the 24 h after the fire: median 5,321 (p25 1,223); 83 of 100 fires saw >= 1,000.
- Today's books show 200-10,000 contracts at the best bid. Examples: BTC MAX 90k has 220 at 18c and 5,850 within 2c; ETH MAX 3000 has 863 at 5c.

So 100 lots per fire is available. Capital, not offers, is the limit.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: About $0.35/day (range $0.15-0.50). That is the refined rule at 50 lots per fire (about 4.3c expected per contract, about 5 fires a month), tying up a peak of about $300 of the $1,155 main bank. The full rule at 100 lots per fire would make about $0.95/day (realised in 2026: $1.20/day), but it needs $730-1,814 of collateral at the monthly peak, which is more than the bank can take away from pin.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: About $1.8/day (range $0.7-2.4), at about 250 lots per fire on the refined rule (peak collateral about $1,500-2,000). Collateral and the crash tail limit it, not offers.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: Clustered by event, the per-contract SE is 2.9c, so the smallest effect the 9 Kalshi months can detect (80% power) is about 8c per contract. The claimed edge is 2-4c, so Kalshi outcomes alone would need about 10x the data, roughly 8 years of monthlies. The 5.5-year physical check pins the model's bias to within about 1c per bucket, but shows that bias shifts with the market regime (ratio 0.79 vs 1.01).
test.worst_case:
One crash month. January 2026 cost -$374 per 100 lots per fire (5 strikes touched: BTC MIN -$241, ETH MIN -$150), wiping out about 4 normal months.
- At 50 lots on the refined rule: worst month about -$130; a single crash day that touches every same-side strike about -$150-200.
- At 250 lots ($5k bank): about -$650 for the month, about -$800-1,000 for the day.

The losing days are big-move crypto days, which may also be pin's bad days. That correlation was not measured.
test.next_test:
No live or paper test can settle this within a year, because each market settles once a month. The cheapest useful step is a read-only daily logger from the Nov 1 relisting, run alongside the SJ08/U4 watcher. It would make one book GET per strike per day (about 30 calls/day) and record the bid, bid size, DVOL model, the 2021-24 physical-map probability, the fire flag and the outcome.

Pass bar, written now: after 6 settled months, the refined rule (model >= 5%, bid <= 30c, margin 2c) must show realised >= +1.5c per contract across >= 25 fires, and no single month may lose more than 3 months of average gains. Otherwise drop it. It is only worth sizing above 50 lots once the bank is >= $3-5k and pin is not limited by bank.

refs.strongest_objection:
What is refuted is the +$0.35/day "now" figure, not the idea itself. At today's $1,155 bank the money has to come out of pin, and pin's marginal dollar earns 4-7x more than this idea's.

Pin's size follows the cash balance (size = bank/11.79, giving 98).

Cost to pin, from our own logs (10-08..10-16, 164 filled 15-min markets, 8,177 contracts):
- In 52 of those markets pin filled its full bank-set size, so cash limits it.
- With cash lower by $150, pin would have bought 7.9% fewer contracts. With $300 lower, 16.3% fewer.
- Pin's 15-min money in kalshi_ledger.json is $16.50/day over 30 days ($11.73 over 14 days, $30.13 over 9).
- So the idea's cash costs pin about $1.3/day at a $150 average lock and about $2.7/day at the tester's $300 peak. The idea earns +$0.35/day.
- Funded now, the net is about -$0.9/day (range -$0.6 to -$2.0).

Second problem: how the risk is valued moves the price by more than the claimed 2-4c edge.
- The tested rule uses one flat volatility (DVOL). The idea's own stated anchor is Deribit's full option price curve (the smile). On the strikes where the rule fires, the two disagree by 4-11 points of probability, in opposite directions.
- Today: BTC MIN 70k is 6.0% flat vs 16.8% on the smile, bid 8c. ETH MIN 2000 is 8.5% vs 17.3%, bid 8c. BTC MAX 90k is 18.2% vs 14.1%, bid 18c.
- On the smile, the crash-side (MIN) strikes are buys, not sales. So the tested rule is selling crash insurance the options market prices higher, and that is exactly what lost January (-$374 per 100 lots per fire).
- The tester's own version using real-world touch rates (calib_rule.out (b), margin 2c) expected +6.26 and realised -0.55 +- 7.65 over 151 fires. The flat-DVOL rule's +3.29 +- 3.47 is about one standard error from zero.

What survives:
- The read-only daily logger, which needs no money.
- Spare cash at a bigger bank. Pin stops growing at 250 contracts, which it reaches at about a $2,950 bank, so cash above that costs pin nothing.
refs.independent_number:
Three checks of my own; none reuse the tester's files.

1. Our pin logs and ledger: with $300 less cash, pin would have bought 16.3% fewer contracts (1,332 of 8,177) over 10-08..10-16; with $150 less, 7.9% fewer. At pin's 30-day $16.50/day that costs -$2.7/day and -$1.3/day, against the idea's +$0.35/day.

2. 53 public Kalshi requests plus Coinbase spot and Deribit volatility, about 19:20Z on 10-16:
- No market fires today under the refined rule. The biggest edge is ETH MAX 3000: bid 6c vs 3.4% model, +2.23c, but the model is under 5%.
- Contracts offered at or near the best bid: BTC MIN 70k has 200 at 8c (4,938 within 2c). ETH MAX 3000 has 200 at 6c (785 within 2c). BTC MAX 92.5k has 269 at 10c (292 within 2c). So 50 lots fit; 100 lots on the thinner strikes means selling part of the order 1-2c lower.
- None of the 4 series has a liquidity-reward program, and all 4 charge the standard taker fee (multiplier 1).

3. 39 days of pin results against daily crypto moves: correlation +0.10. Pin's 6 worst days fell on days with a 1.0-6.1% range, so its losses and a crash month did not stack in this sample. But the sample has no crash day (biggest range 9.6%).

refs.strongest_objection:
The tester's Kalshi evidence (realised +3.82 vs model +3.71; refined rule +2.50, i.e. +5.2c per contract) rests on checking ONCE A DAY at 16:00 UTC. A bot checks continuously. I re-ran the same rule on my own pull, checked every hour, over the same 9 months:
- Refined rule: 89 fires; 14 touched where the model expected 9.5; realised -1.7c per contract.
- Full rule: 177 fires; 16 touched where the model expected 9.6; realised +0.1c per contract.

The result falls steadily as checks get more frequent. Refined rule: 24 h +5.8c, 12 h +4.2c, 8 h +2.9c, 6 h +2.2c, 4 h +1.2c, 3 h +0.1c, 2 h -0.4c, 1 h -1.7c. So the moment a Kalshi bid first rises above the model is followed by touches 1.5-1.7x as often as the model says, about 2x the physical map.

The tester's +4.3c expected value assumes that Kalshi pricing above the model tells you nothing. This is the only direct test of that assumption, and it points the wrong way. The 7.5c swing between check schedules is bigger than the claimed 4.3c edge. Filters chosen after seeing the data (skip the listing day, spread <= 3c) only reach -0.1c to +1.2c, against the physical map's +5-6c.

Nothing on Kalshi is significant either way: month-clustered SE is about 7c per contract over 9 months. The general option-implied overpricing is real (my own check: touched/model 0.73 in the 5-30% zone, below 1 in every year 2021-26). But the money case needs that premium to survive being selected by Kalshi richness, and that is unverified.

Two practical problems:
- pinrun's read_bank sizes pin from CASH. Locking $300-420 here on the main account cuts pin's bet size by roughly a quarter to a third, and pin earned about 2.5% of bank a day in September (SI46; not re-measured).
- The logger the tester proposes snapshots once a day, which is exactly the schedule that flatters the result.

Minor: the Feb BTC MIN 45k/50k/55k markets (tickers 225000/250000/275000) have rules that literally say "below $NA"; they added +0.44 of the +3.82. There are 38 settled events, not 36 (there is no ETH MIN March event).
refs.independent_number:
My own pull: 382 Kalshi GETs (339 markets including the historical tier, hourly candles), plus Coinbase hourly closes and Deribit DVOL hourly closes. Same rule (sell YES at the bid when bid - model - fee > 2c, bid <= 30c, fee at 50 lots), checked EVERY HOUR:
- Refined (model >= 5%): 89 fires in 30 events over 9 months. 14 touched vs 9.5 expected by the model. Realised -1.54 per contract-set = -1.7c per contract (month-cluster SE about 7c per contract).
- Full: 177 fires, 16 touched vs 9.6 expected, +0.1c per contract.

Checked once a day at any one of the 24 UTC hours instead:
- Refined: +2.6 to +9.6c per contract (mean +5.8c).
- Full: +0.1 to +3.6c (mean +2.3c).
- My 16:00 UTC run reproduces the tester: 110 fires, 5 touched, +3.81.

Own physical check (Coinbase daily, DVOL daily open, 2021-03 to 2026-09, 134 coin-months), refined zone touched/model:

| Year | Ratio |
|---|---|
| 2021 | 0.60 |
| 2022 | 0.79 |
| 2023 | 0.69 |
| 2024 | 0.74 |
| 2025 | 0.72 |
| 2026 | 0.83 |
| All | 0.73 (touched - model = -0.040, SE 0.010) |

How often a whole side gets taken out: in 30 of 264 coin-month-sides, 3 or more strikes that were in the zone on the 1st all touched. 18 of 66 months had at least one such event.

idea.name: Kalshi refer-a-friend: $25 to the referrer per new account that trades $25 in 7 days (cap 40 = $1,000)
markets: Kalshi account level (no market); not available in AZ, IL, MA, MD, MI, MT, NV, OH, WA; VA fine
idea.mechanism: He shares his referral link; each genuinely new friend who passes KYC and trades $25 within 7 days credits $25 to both. The referrer needs 100 completed trades (he has thousands).
idea.why_mispriced: Kalshi pays for customer acquisition.
idea.must_be_true: Friends genuinely new to Kalshi; the credit is usable/withdrawable (terms say 'bonus credit reflected in their balance' -- not verified); terms current (read only on affiliate pages).
idea.evidence_so_far: Terms read on RotoWire, Covers, SportsHandle and casino.org pages; nothing primary; nothing on the account.

merged_from: cross-venue: Kalshi refer-a-friend (idea 2)
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No ledger row covers Kalshi's own referral program (SI08 covered other venues' sign-ups).

test.method: Source rank: Kalshi's own pages and Kalshi's public API (no replay, no tape). (1) Referral terms: fetched Kalshi's own Help Center article 13823783 'Kalshi Referral Program FAQ' read-only on 2026-10-16 (fetch.py; text saved in the scratch folder), plus its Programs & Promotions collection and the 'Perps Promotions, Bonuses & Credits' article (16071412). kalshi.com/referral and kalshi.com/legal/referral-program-terms are 404; the per-offer terms live only inside the app (Explore > menu > Your rewards > Offers). The API docs mirror has no referral endpoint, so the account's own referral status cannot be read by API. (2) Referrer eligibility: counted this account's settled markets in results/kalshi_ledger.json (ledger_count.py). (3) New angle found in the same Kalshi collection and measured: the Kalshi Market Bug Bounty (help article 13823852, dated 2026-04-21: $25-$100 for most bugs, $100-$250 moderate, $250-$1,000+ severe, first reporter only, Kalshi's discretion; categories include broken variables, rules-vs-title contradictions, wrong dates, typos). Built bugscan.py (self-test plants each of 9 bug types in a synthetic market plus one clean market; must flag every plant and nothing on the clean one; passes) and ran it over EVERY open non-combo market via 156 unauthenticated GETs of /markets?status=open&mve_filter=exclude (2026-10-16 ~19:45Z). Then read every strong-check hit by hand (showv2.py; getm.py for full market records). No holdout applies: these are eligibility facts and a census, not a fitted threshold. Scratch: C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-C3-15/ (RESULT.json, bugscan.py, flags_v2.json, scan_summary.json).
test.n_markets: Referral: 1 Kalshi primary FAQ + 2 related primary articles; this account's 1,931 settled markets (2026-08-15..2026-10-16). Bug-bounty census: 144,786 open markets, 16,163 events, 4,935 series.
test.n_independent_clusters: Referral: 1 program, paid per genuinely new friend (one-off each). Bug census: about 5 distinct reportable issues (each is one template bug repeated across 1-100 markets), hand-classified from 30 strong-check flag groups.
test.result:
REFERRAL. Kalshi's own FAQ no longer states the affiliate-page numbers ($25 each side, trade $25 in 7 days, cap 40 = $1,000, excluded-state list, 100-trade referrer bar). Verbatim: 'Amounts vary by offer and may differ between the person referring a friend and the person signing up'; 'Limits vary by program'; 'Referral rewards may be issued as trading credits with withdrawal restrictions. Some require you to trade the credited amount on an eligible product before it becomes withdrawable'; 'Unused credits may expire'. Some bonuses must be claimed by tapping 'Unlock bonus', and friends may add a code within 72 hours of opening the account. So the $25/$1,000 figures are unverified, and the credit is probably a trading credit, not cash. For this account the trade-through requirement costs nothing: the bot already settles about 46 markets a day (1,931 in 42 days), far past any 100-trade referrer bar. The perps referral (article 16071412) is different and recurring: a share of the friend's perps trading fees, paid weekly. But perps credits land in the perps account, cannot be moved to predictions, cannot be withdrawn (only winnings can), and may expire in 7 days; self-referrals and accounts that already existed never qualify. Money: $25 x number of genuinely new friends, once each; no friend count is knowable from here.

BUG BOUNTY (new angle, measured). Of 144,786 open markets, the strong checks flagged 30 series groups. By hand, about 5 distinct issues look reportable:
(a) Float garbage in the rules of a company-results template, 7 series (KXUBER, KXDASHA, KXFUTU, KXFUTUA, KXFA, KXLYFTA, KXETOR; created 2026-06-09..08-07; largest open interest 2,313 contracts on KXFA). Title 'Above 4.1 billion' vs rules 'reports Above 4099999999.9999995 total trips'. idea.name: KXTORNADO October count: YES on '>50' at 87-89c (one-off, barely measured)
idea.mechanism: Read SPC's preliminary tornado count month-to-date; with 48 raw reports through Oct 14 and 17 days left, '>50' at 89c needs only a few more if the de-duplicated preliminary count is near the raw sum, paying +9c after fee.
idea.why_mispriced: Thin, retail-priced monthly count market (~6k contracts on the strike); the running count is public but nobody updates the price daily.
idea.must_be_true: The market's 'preliminary number' (SPC monthly page, JS-driven, unread) is close to the raw report count; raw local-storm reports over-count the filtered number by 10-30%, so the real count could be ~35-43, needing 8-16 more in 17 days. Depth at 89c unmeasured.
idea.rough_dollars_per_day: $5-15 one-off (100-200 contracts x 9c) if right; nothing repeatable. Worst case -$89 per 100 contracts.
idea.settlements_per_day: 1 per month
idea.test_plan: Operator (2 minutes): open spc.noaa.gov/climo/online/monthly/newm.html and read October's preliminary count; if >= 45, a $50-100 YES at <= 90c with per-order sign-off; otherwise drop.
idea.prior_reason: One-off, a few dollars, hinges on one unread number.
idea.novelty_vs_ledger: No ledger row.
idea.worst_case: -$89 per 100 contracts if October stays quiet and the de-duplicated count is far below the raw sum.
merged_from: weather-model #5

test.method: Settlement feed first. (1) Read the actual settlement number. SPC's monthly page runs on JavaScript, but its data files are public: https://www.spc.noaa.gov/climo/summary/2026/ruf/NAT/NAT_OCT.json (total plus daily counts) and NAT_OCT_TORN.png. The PNG carries the 'Storm Reports Legend' that the rules name; the map was updated 10:08 ET Oct 16. Validated this source against Kalshi by comparing the expiration_value of all 38 settled KXTORNADO/TORNADO monthly events (/historical/markets) with the SPC archive totals. (2) Forecast: SPC Day 1, 2, 3 and Day 4-8 outlook text, Oct 16. (3) Climatology of the count still to come: SPC preliminary daily counts for every month 2004-2026 (274 monthly JSONs), plus the final SPC tornado database 1950-2025, streamed and not saved. (4) Market: the live book and full trade tape for KXTORNADO-26OCT-50/75/100 and for Aug/Sep 2026, plus daily candles over the whole life of all 365 tornado markets. (5) Backtest of the general rule a bot would run. Model p = P(preliminary count still to come >= need), using the same month in strictly earlier years (2004..Y-1), so it is a holdout by construction. Month-to-date count = days <= X-2 at each daily close, so no partial day is used. Quotes are daily-close yes bid/ask; fee 0.07p(1-p); outcome is the Kalshi result; one entry per market; P&L clustered by monthly event. Fit = Jul 2023-Jun 2025 (23 events); holdout = Jul 2025-Sep 2026 (15 events). Source rank: SPC feed > tape/candles > replay; we have no fills of our own here. Scripts and outputs are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R1-N0-15/ (spc5.py, spc7.py, clim.py, clim2.py, final_db.py, pull1-5.py, tape_an.py, bt.py..bt4.py, RESULT.json).
test.n_markets: The idea itself: 1 market (KXTORNADO-26OCT-50). General-rule backtest: 348 settled strike markets (308 with quotes on both sides) across 38 monthly events, Jul 2023 - Sep 2026.
test.n_independent_clusters: 38 monthly events (fit 23, holdout 15). The Oct 2026 bet is 1 cluster (one settlement, Nov 1).
test.result:
PREMISE WRONG. The settlement number (the SPC preliminary legend, updated 10:08 ET Oct 16) is 37, not about 48. The hunter added up raw reports; the preliminary database removes duplicates (Oct 10: 25 raw -> 17; Oct 11: 21 -> 15; Oct 14: 1 -> 3). '>50' needs 14 more from Oct 16-31.

FORECAST: SPC Day 1 (Oct 16) is a slight risk with 'a tornado or two'. Days 2-3 show no severe weather, and Days 4-8 (Oct 19-23) carry no severe probabilities, so the realistic window is Oct 24-31.

CLIMATOLOGY (SPC preliminary, 22 Octobers 2004-25):
- P(>=14 in Oct 16-31) = 15/22 = 0.68 [95% 0.47-0.84].
- P(>=11..13 in Oct 24-31) = 10-11/22 = 0.45-0.50 [0.27-0.69].
- Final database 1990-2025: P(>=13 in Oct 24-31) = 19/36 = 0.53.
- So fair YES on '>50' is about 0.45-0.55.

MARKET ALREADY REPRICED: bid 87 / ask 89 on Oct 15 became bid 64 / ask 79 on Oct 16, last trade 63. Sellers hit bids from 9 ET Oct 16 onward. Buying YES at 87-89 would have meant about -30 to -40c per contract expected.

SETTLEMENT LAG: Kalshi settles on a snapshot that sits 0-55 below SPC's later archive (Dec 2024 90 vs 145, Sep 2024 61 vs 73, Jun 2026 383 vs 399, Oct 2024 50 vs 53). Tornadoes late in a month partly miss settlement.

THE OPPOSITE TRADE (NO on '>50' at 36-43c, which the model now signals) IS NOT SUPPORTED. In the backtest, signals where the model said NO was cheap lost money:
- Threshold 0.10, pooled: -6.1c/market (122 markets, 29 events, t -1.10); fit -9.6c, holdout -0.6c.
- Threshold 0.20 with the real-time-count proxy: fit -3.0c, holdout -4.8c.
- The market beats the climatology model on Brier score (0.136 vs 0.149, event-clustered t 1.38).

SIDE FINDING (a different idea): signals where the model said YES was cheap (p - ask - fee >= 0.20) made money, but the case is weak.
- +15.7c/market pooled (80 markets, 27 events, t 1.99); fit +17.4c, holdout +13.7c.
- With the real-time-count proxy: +17.7c, t 2.17.
- This is borderline after about 24 looks and is carried by big months (Apr 2024, Jun 2026).
- The archive's month-to-date counts include reports added later. That is look-ahead, and it cannot be removed without real-time snapshots.
- Calibration: when the model said 0.8-1.0, YES settled 92-96 times in 100 while the market mid sat at 83-87c.

No current signal on any Oct 2026 strike: '>75' ask 37 vs model <=0.45; '>100' ask 21 vs model 0.14.
test.artefact_checks: (1) Source/unit: the settlement number was read from the exact legend the rules name (PNG viewed) and from the JSON behind it; both say 37. (2) Source checked on history: Kalshi expiration_value vs the SPC archive for 38 months. The archive is always >= the settlement snapshot (0 to +55), so archive month-to-date counts carry look-ahead. Re-ran with a known*S/A proxy: the YES-side result survives and the NO-side result stays negative. (3) No look-ahead in the climatology: only years strictly before the event year are used. (4) No partial-day information is used (count through day X-2 only). (5) Clustered by monthly event; n is reported as markets/events, never trades. (6) Fee is charged at the quoted price, one entry per market. (7) Candle closes can be 1-contract quotes; depth at the signal price was NOT measured. (8) The hunter's own warning that raw reports over-count was right: raw over-counted by 11 (30%).
test.supply_we_would_get: KXTORNADO-26OCT-50 book now: YES bids 64x1, 63x46, 62x17, 59x100, 58x25, 57x100. That is 289 contracts of NO available at <=43c, average 40.9c. YES asks are thin: 79x7, then 84x1, 85x15. Lifetime volume 6,609 contracts, 151 in the last 24 h. For the YES-side variant, the rule fires about 1.8 times a month across all strikes; depth at the signal price was not measured (daily candles only).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0 - the idea is dead: the count was wrong and the price has already moved. The unproven YES-side variant would make about 1.8 signals/month x <=100 contracts x ~15c = ~$25-30/month, about $1/day, before adverse fills.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0 for this idea. The variant is capped by thin books: about $1-2/day at most, not measured.
test.smallest_detectable_effect: One-off bet: none - a single settlement cannot tell a 15c edge from luck. Backtest: with 25-38 monthly clusters and an event-level spread of about 1.0-1.5 dollars per contract, the smallest mean it can detect at 95% is about +/-0.4-0.5 dollars per event, roughly +/-12-15c per market traded.
test.worst_case: As proposed: 100 YES at 89c settles NO for -$89, and with fair value near 0.5 that is close to a coin flip. The opposite side, 100 NO at about 38c, loses -$38. Variant: a full YES position bought at 60-80c can go to zero in a month, -$60-80 per 100 contracts per strike, and several strikes in the same month move together (one cluster).
test.next_test: No bet on Oct 2026, either side. The variant is low priority (about $1/day). If it is pursued: a recorder that snapshots SPC NAT_<MON>.json every hour, which gives the true real-time count and removes the archive look-ahead, plus a daily KXTORNADO orderbook snapshot for depth. Then a paper bot runs the YES-side rule (strictly-prior-year climatology, p - ask - fee >= 0.20) for about 6 months. Pass bar: >= +8c/contract over >= 15 paper fills spanning >= 6 monthly events, with >= 50 contracts of recorded depth at the signal price.

RTH chain: not read.

test.method:
Live market-hours reads on 2026-10-16, a down day (S&P -1.3%, Nasdaq-100 -2.8%). Four snapshots between 15:08 and 15:51 ET, taken with snap.py. Each snapshot holds: the free CBOE option chains (15 minutes delayed), keeping only the SPXW and NDXP 2026-12-31 PM-settled options, which settle on the same 4pm Dec-31 close as Kalshi; the full public Kalshi orderbook for every open market in KXINXY, KXINXDIRY, KXINXPOS, KXNASDAQ100Y and KXNASDAQ100POS; and Yahoo 1-minute ^GSPC/^NDX. Yahoo was checked to be real-time against the chain's own delayed spot.

Synchronous scoring: each Kalshi book was compared with the chain fetched 12-15 minutes later, whose quotes date from the book's time (pairs s1:s2, s2:s3, s3:s4, plus s4 same-time with a spot shift).

Fair value (analyse.py; its self-test passes, recovering a planted digital to 0.08c and flagging a planted 6c mispricing). Forward and discount come from a put-call parity fit (S&P 183 strikes). P(close > K) is taken from mid-price call spreads K±50 points (S&P) or ±500 (NDX), with strict bid/ask bounds. Fees are taken per series. Kalshi pays about 4% APY on open positions, so the fair is used undiscounted.

Two real-world yardsticks, so a risk premium is not mistaken for mispricing:
- pmeas.py: the option-implied distribution tilted to a 5% and a 10% equity premium.
- hist.py: Yahoo daily closes, ^GSPC 1950-2026 (19,208 overlapping 52-trading-day windows, about 369 independent) and ^NDX 1985-2026 (about 197 independent), both raw and scaled to today's implied vol.

Supply: public trade tapes 10-08..10-16 (571,367 contracts), plus all 6,887 incentive programs. No replay was used. About 730 public Kalshi GETs. Holdout: three cross-time synchronous pairs, plus the hunter's 10-13 pre-market read.
test.n_markets: 76 Kalshi markets settle on the Dec-31-2026 close: KXINXY 27, KXINXDIRY 17, KXINXPOS 1, KXNASDAQ100Y 30, KXNASDAQ100POS 1. In each of the 4 reads, 8 S&P brackets and 13-14 Nasdaq brackets were two-sided with a fair value between 3c and 97c.
test.n_independent_clusters: 1. Every market settles on the same 4pm 2026-12-31 close, and S&P and Nasdaq move together, so any position is one outcome. The 4 reads are 45 minutes of one afternoon.
test.result:
The bar was a bracket more than 5c off a fair whose bounds are within 3c. No S&P bracket met it in any of the 4 reads.

S&P yearly brackets (KXINXY):
- Kalshi mid minus option fair: mean -0.72c to -0.78c; largest gap 2.8c to 3.5c. Brackets more than 5c off with tight bounds: 0 of 8, every read.
- Today's 46,751 KXINXY contracts traded at a contract-weighted +0.02c from the option fair, so takers and makers both broke even against options.
- The gaps that exist point the way a risk premium would (Kalshi slightly more bullish than options):
  - B7900 (7800-7999): ask 20c x 403. Options say 22.3-22.9c, the tilt says 23.7c, but 76 years of history say 18.0c, so buying at 20c loses by history.
  - B8100: bid 18c. Options say 16.2-16.9c, but the tilt says 18.2c.
- No bracket clears fee plus 1c on all three yardsticks with more than 3 contracts behind it.

Nasdaq:
- T33000 (Nasdaq-100 at or above 33000) bid 12c x 57, against an option fair of 7.0-7.4c (bounds 4.3-9.7). It is the only market that passes the 5c bar. History puts it at 9.8c (vol-scaled) to 13.6c (raw), and 57 contracts are worth $2.40 at the option fair.
- Large cheap downside asks: B26750 at 2c x 28,287 and B27750 at 3c x 24,682. NDXP bounds there are 0-18c wide, and history puts B26750 at 2.7-2.8c, so buying at 2c is +0.6c, inside the ±1.2c error.

Reward programs on the whole family: none of 6,887.

test.method: Sources, best first: Kalshi's public trade tape and 1-minute quote candles, timed against the raw public livestats feed. No replay was used. Sample: 69 thin-league KXLOLMAP maps (TCL 25, LCP 24, VCS 12, LJL 8; 32 matches, 2026-08-11 to 10-11). Maps were picked in md5-of-ticker order, not by volume; the only maps left out were ones cancelled and settled at fair price. For each map I pulled every 10-s livestats window, the full trade tape of both team markets, and 1-min candles with full open/low/high/close of yes_bid and yes_ask. Candles are emitted for minutes where only the quote changed, so a missing minute means the quote did not change. Triggers were fixed before looking at any price: a net swing of 2+ kills within 20 s, a baron, an inhibitor, or an elder dragon, with a 45-s gap between triggers. That gave 419 triggers. Our receive time R = floor10(T) + 32 s, using the 21-31 s publication delay the lane measured live on 2026-10-15. Cost of the helped team = min(own yes_ask, 1 - other yes_bid), in dollars (unit taken from the *_dollars field name). PRE = cost at the minute boundary just before the first kill or objective, minus 5 s. At R, a quote counts as proven STALE if the candle high <= PRE + 1c. It counts as proven REPRICED if the candle low >= PRE + 3c, or if a trade buying the helped side at >= that book's own PRE + 3c printed between the first kill and R. A 'big' event is one where the cost rose 4c+ by R + 180 s. The tradable rule tested was 'take the quote if it is still stale at R'. It was scored by settlement (win - cost_hi - 0.07p(1-p)) and by the change versus the helped team's mid at R + 180 s. Placebo: random times and sides under the same rose-4c-later condition. Control: random time and random team. Holdout: maps before 2026-09-01 used for fitting, maps on or after that date for testing. All results are clustered by map. Scripts are in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-21/ (thinfetch.py, thinan.py, bykind.py, spreads.py); output is in thinan_final.out and RESULT.json.
test.n_markets: 69 maps (138 team markets), 419 triggers, 161 big events
test.n_independent_clusters: 69 maps in 32 matches (one settlement per map)
test.result:
The bar fails by a wide margin.

- **Staleness on big events:** of 161, the quote was still stale when our feed frame arrived in only 15 (9%). It was proven already repriced or consumed in 124 (77%).
- **How early the market moves:** the first trade buying the helped side at the old ask + 3c or more came a median 21 s BEFORE our receive time. That is about 5-10 s after the game event, the same speed as the major leagues.
- **Placebo:** with the same condition, 32% showed the repriced proof and 30% were stale. So the early repricing is caused by the event; the 'rose 4c later' condition does not create it.
- **The tradable rule (take any quote still stale at R):** 124 takes on 47 maps. By settlement it made -3.3c per contract (se 4.0). Against the mid 3 min later it made -10.3c (se 1.8, 42 maps).
- **Fit vs holdout:**
  - Fit (Aug, 49 maps): 77% repriced, 9% stale; stale takes -8.9c vs mid (se 2.3).
  - Holdout (Sep-Oct, 20 maps): 77% repriced, 11% stale; stale takes -13.4c vs mid (se 2.9).
- **By league (big events repriced before R / stale-take result vs mid):**
  - LCP: 84% / -4.1c (se 3.1)
  - TCL: 73% / -7.2c (se 2.6)
  - VCS: 74% / -14.8c (se 3.2)
  - LJL: 64% / -21.3c (se 5.4)
- **Two kinds of book:**
  - TCL and LCP have an in-game cost of 4-5c (median) to buy both sides, and they reprice before we see the event.
  - VCS and LJL cost 20-25c (median; single maps up to 50c). Their quotes are often stale, but the stale ask sits 10-25c above fair, so nothing is worth taking.
- **By trigger:**
  - Kills: 78% repriced.
  - Barons: 68% repriced. The 16 stale baron takes made +2.7c by settlement (se 1.7, 15 maps). That is 1.6 se in one of about 20 cells looked at, so it is not a pass.
  - Inhibitors: 83% repriced.

The earlier finding that thin leagues lag 30-55 s came from the last trade on 1-3 games. Across 69 maps, the first informed trade comes about 20 s before our frame.
test.artefact_checks:
1. **Placebo:** random times with the same 'rose 4c+ later' condition show 32% repriced before R against 77% for events, and 30% stale against 9%. The difference comes from the event, not the conditioning.
2. **Each book judged against its own price:** the trade proof uses each book's OWN pre-event level, so a trade in the dearer of the two books cannot fake a move. The first pass mixed the two books; this was fixed.
3. **Units:** taken from the *_dollars field names, never from magnitude.
4. **Candle gaps:** I checked that candles are emitted for minutes where only the quote changed (volume-0 rows), so the last close is exact through a missing minute. Inside a minute only low/high are known, which leaves about 45% of all triggers ambiguous; the trade proof settles most of the big ones.
5. **Selection:** schedule-blind (md5 of ticker), not by volume, which avoids the lane's volume-selection trap.
6. **Receive delay not measured here:** R comes from the live Worlds measurement, not from a thin-league game. If thin-league feeds published faster, the result could change. But the median informed trade lands 21 s before R, so the feed would have to be about 20 s faster just to tie.
7. **Depth not measured:** there is no historical order book for these markets. Contracts traded at stale prices after R: median 0.
8. **Fetch runs:** two copies of my own fetch script turned out to be running in parallel (the earlier TaskStop only killed the shell). I stopped both by PID once 69 maps were in; partly written files were checked and removed. About 290 public Kalshi calls in total, well under the cap.
9. **Collector:** I checked only that the collector's output is current; the process itself was not checked. kalshi_data/ticker/20261016T20.jsonl.gz was being written at 16:03 local. Disk free 109 GB; scratch folder 1.5 MB.
test.supply_we_would_get: None worth taking. On events that matter, the offer is gone about 20 s before our frame arrives (77% of big events). Where quotes are still stale (the wide VCS and LJL books), they sit 10-25c above fair. Median contracts traded at stale prices after our receive time: 0. Books trade about 2-15k contracts per map over their life (median VCS 2.2k, TCL 5.3k, LCP 14.8k).
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_now: $0/day at the ~$1,155 bank. No positive-EV supply exists at our feed speed; the taker rule loses about 10c per contract against the price 3 minutes later.
test.realistic_dollars_per_day_5k: $0/day at $5,000. The limit is feed speed, not capital.
test.smallest_detectable_effect:
- **Stale share of big events:** 15/161 = 9% (se about 3 points after clustering), so the 50% bar sits more than 10 se away.
- **Stale-take result vs mid:** se 1.8c, so a true +3.6c effect (2 se) would have shown; about 5c at 80% power.
- **Settlement-scored EV:** noisier, se 4.0c.
test.worst_case: If built anyway, stale takes average about -10c per contract against the price 3 minutes later. At 20 contracts and about 4 thin-league events a day in season, that is about -$8/day. A bad day, with several takes on the wrong side of a throw, is about -$30. There is no exposure now: these leagues are off until about January 2027.
test.next_test:
Nothing more is needed to kill this. Optional cheap confirmation (recorder only, no money): run the lane's live_rec.py, which reads the public feed and polls the order book right after each event, on two events:
- LCP Promotion/Relegation, Nov 10-13 (5 matches; whether Kalshi lists them is not yet checked).
- SK Gaming Avarosa vs Mental Rush, listed on Kalshi now for Oct 19 16:00Z (12:00 ET), book 4c/93c. Only if lolesports serves livestats for it; that is not confirmed, as the match is missing from the lolesports schedule pull.

The bar stays the same: the ask is unchanged at our receive time on at least half of big events, with 20+ contracts at that ask. Expected to fail (historically 9%). Re-open only with a sub-second data source (GRID, paid).

idea.name: Late taker pin on the hourly S&P and Nasdaq-100 ladders off a per-second index feed
idea.mechanism: Settlement is the index print at the exact listed ET time and equals Yahoo's 1-minute bar close to the cent (median 0.00 pts, n=347; NDX +0.3 median). With <= 30 s left take the winning side at <= 97c on rungs where the live index is >= 4 pts (>= 4 one-second sds) from the strike, as pinrun does on crypto.
idea.why_mispriced: Retail resting orders left on rungs the index has already moved past; a per-second feed beats them.
idea.must_be_true: Cheap decided supply must exist at the moment it is decided. By the 1-minute bar it looks like 5,437 contracts / $997 over 5 closes, but the within-minute index shows nearly all of it was a strike +/- 0.4-2 pt coin flip (10-09 H1200 T7800: NO bought at 44-95c with 0.9 s left while the fresh index sat 0.38 pts below). The one real-looking case: 10-09 H1600 T7815, 996 contracts at 95-97c with 6 s left and the index 3.9 pts away. A real-time index source is needed; Nasdaq rungs are finer than a 1-minute sd, so 'decided' is rarer there.
idea.evidence_so_far: S&P 35 closes 10-06..10-12 (44k RTH trades): decided winner supply by the fresh bar ~1,000 contracts over 35 closes (~$50 gross); loser side bought >= 95c in the last 5 min: 770 contracts in 2 closes (flips are real). refs.strongest_objection:
The capital rescue holds. The $2.2 is still a tail bet that the data can bound but not measure, and it depends on a code change.

(1) Capital, confirmed by a second method. I set Kalshi's ledger cost per close against the bot's own last bank read before that close.
- With $450 parked, 0 of 435 closes since 10-01 could have refused anything.
- The first close that could needs $805.62 parked. Since 10-10 that is $887.21; overnight since 10-10, $917.31.
- Orders are immediate-or-cancel, so no resting order holds cash.

(2) Equity sizing has to cover every safety limit, not just the bet size.
- The late boost is capped by (cash - 0.8 x the bank's high-water mark) / 0.98. With $450 of cash parked and the high-water mark unchanged, that cap goes negative, so the boost is off overnight.
- The boost fired 34 of its 63 times overnight since 09-19, but only 3 times in the last 7 days, so this costs about $0-0.5 a night today.
- The day loss cap ($224) is smaller than one flip ($297). The carry's money must be kept out of pin's loss limits, or one flip stops pin for the day.

(3) The money is a tail rate.
- Without the offer filters: dead strikes at least 3c past both the 9 PM median and the previous print lost on 2 of 696 state-day sides. That is 0.29%, with a one-sided 95% upper bound of 0.90%, just under the 0.93% break-even. Sides on the same date are not fully independent.
- Both losses were in September: AZ 09-22 (not offered) and FL 09-23 (offered at 98c).
- On the sides the rule actually buys (offered at exactly 99c): 0 losses in 140, upper bound 2.12%.
- The exactly-99c filter was chosen after seeing the FL loss. Offers below 99c lost 1 of 16.

(4) Big misses happen, but the market flagged them.
- The print beat both the median and the previous print by at least 3c on 8 of 829 state-days (0.97%), all in price-cycle or brand-new ladders.
- 7 of the 8 printed past the end of the strike grid. 6 of the 8 had no dead strike on that side.
- AAA state prints move a lot: 14% of 1,235 daily changes are 3c or more, and 3.2% are 8c or more (MI +22c on 10-09).
- So the protection comes from the market's own dead pricing, not from the previous-print guard.

(5) The tester's "both ideas together do not fit" pools the low-bank 10-01..10-09 period.
- At today's bank, $900 parked overnight refuses 0 of 79 overnight closes since 10-10 on my bound.
- By design, though, $900 parked leaves cash for exactly one worst close ($300 at a bet of 102) and nothing more.

Not refuted. The capital re-test holds when I check it a different way, and the supply showed up tonight. What is left are conditions, not a kill.
(1) The +$2.2 a night exists only after a code change to the live bot, and the change has to go in at read_bank (cash plus the carry's positions), not only size_for_bank. one_coin_cap's room is (bank - 0.8 x high-water mark) / 0.98. With $450 parked it goes negative every night (about $743 against 0.8 x $1,190), so the late boost and one-coin depth switch off. On pinrun's own records (not the ledger, small sample), 14 boosted overnight markets since 10-01 earned $18.23 on the contracts above the base size: about $1.15 a night lost with a size-only patch. Under today's cash sizing the carry stays about -$1.3 a night.
(2) Competing sweepers are real and fast. Tonight one taker bought 29,244 NO at 99c on IL 4.725 at 7:51:47 PM ET (about $29k). Others took AZ at 7:47 PM and WY at 7:59 PM, then cleared IN 3.81 and 3.815 at 9:07:54 and 9:08:29 PM (1,520 each) and CO at 9:06 PM. Of the seven 9 PM picks, only 2 were left at 9:10. The farmers re-post, so this only hurts a bot that is not polling at 9:00:00.
(3) The supply left after them sits mostly in price-cycle states: tonight's 9 PM set was IN x8, NM x7, plus CO, FL, NE, UT and WY. Today takers bought 2,012 dead-side YES at 2c on CO, betting on a price restoration. At the 450 cap the rule picks only YES-sure strikes below the median (NM, IN), the safe direction. At the 2,000 cap it also picks NO-sure strikes in cycling states (CO, NE), which is the jump direction of the one measured flip (FL 09-23). The rule should skip NO-sure strikes in cycling states.
(4) Gas trades in pool 0. Pinrun's bank read counts pool-0 cash, but pool-2 orders cannot spend it, so the $450 must sit in pool 0 permanently. That leaves about $743 in pool 2 all day, which the measured headroom covers.

test.method: This re-tests the MAKER form at the critic's request. The 10-15 tester killed only the taker. Data, in source rank order: the Kalshi public trade tape (taker_side, yes price, count). It came from /markets/trades after the 2026-08-17 archive cutoff and /historical/trades before it; the cutoff was read live from /historical/cutoff. Also 1-minute candles for the quote at snap, plus livestats in-game sides and game-start times reused from the 10-15 tester (truesides.json, details_hist.json). No replay. The critic fixed the rule before any number was seen. At snap (map 1 = scheduled start - 2 min; map n>=2 = previous map's close + 2 min), rest a 50-lot YES bid on the blue team's own KXLOLMAP market at its best bid (candle close at snap), and cancel at game start. Maker fee is 0 (fee_type 'quadratic', checked live on /series/KXLOLMAP). Fills come from every print in (snap, game start]. Seller-initiated means taker_side 'no'; checked on this sample: in the same minute, 'yes'-taker prints sit +2.2c above 'no'-taker prints on 90% of 971 map-minutes. Four fill rules: (1) the critic's: >= 50 seller contracts at or through our bid (ignores the queue); (2) conservative: any seller print strictly below our bid (our level was certainly cleared); (3) queue sensitivity: >= 350, assuming 300 queued ahead; (4) queue-honest: bid 1c above the best bid where the spread is >= 2c, filled if >= 50 seller contracts printed at <= the old bid. Outcome is the map result, one leg per map, clustered by match. FIT = Aug 17-Sep 30 (dataset A, where the lean was found). HOLDOUT = Oct 1-15 (A) plus the Apr 1-Aug 16 archive (B). 1,215 maps had a usable two-sided quote on the blue book (spread <= 10c) and a known game start. All 1,215 tapes were pulled with 0 errors, using 1,383 public GETs. Scripts in C:/kals-repo/.sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/test-20261015-R3-M-17-RT2/: build_items.py, pull_trades.py, pull_rev.py, pull_slice.py, score.py (full output in score.out), checks.py.
test.n_markets: 1,215 maps, one blue-book market each. FIT: 534 maps / 246 matches. HOLDOUT: 681 maps / 362 matches (Oct 133 / 53; archive 548 / 309). Filled under the critic's rule: FIT 130 maps, HOLDOUT 179 maps (Oct 27, archive 152).
test.n_independent_clusters: 608 matches overall. Filled maps fall in 91 matches (FIT) and 138 matches (HOLDOUT).
test.result:
FAILS the bar (>= +2c per filled contract on >= 150 filled maps, both halves > 0).

Critic's rule:
- FIT: +5.15c per filled contract (se 4.33, 130 maps / 91 matches).
- HOLDOUT: -3.28c (se 3.40, 179 maps / 138 matches). Both pieces are negative: Oct -2.85c (27 maps), archive -3.36c (152 maps).
- All 1,215 maps pooled: +0.27c (se 2.71, 309 filled maps).

Other fill rules, HOLDOUT:
- Conservative: -0.21c (se 3.72, 151 maps).
- Queue-300: -1.07c (se 5.64, 68 maps).
- Queue-honest +1c bid: -4.17c (se 4.02, 127 maps).
- Partial fills: -3.25c per contract (10,469 contracts / 250 maps).

WHY: the lean is real, but it sits on the maps where nobody sells to us.
- Blue won - bid across EVERY map is +4.94c in the holdout (+5.72c all). That is what a bid filled 100% of the time would earn.
- On filled maps blue wins 50.3%, against 58.6% on unfilled maps (holdout). The 8.3-point gap is larger than the whole +4.9c edge. All maps: 51.5% vs 57.5%.
- Per contract in the holdout: filled -3.28c vs unfilled +7.88c, a difference of about 11c, roughly 2.7 standard errors.
- Maps where no seller reached our price: +7.62c (783 maps). Maps where any seller did: +2.28c (432 maps).
- Markout to 1 min before game start: on filled maps the mid ends +1.0c above our bid, against +2.7c on unfilled maps. The price moves against us after we are hit.
- No sign that late-draft fills are worse than early ones: filled <= 5 min before start +1.16c vs earlier -0.55c (all maps, both se ~3.7). So the bid is not hit only by people watching the draft. The sellers are whoever prices the map below the lean, and they are right often enough to erase it.

CS2 / Valorant: NOT measured.
- CS2 has no fixed per-map side because teams swap at half. The nearest equivalent, the team that picked the map, is in neither the Kalshi archive nor bo3.gg's match and game records (probed one finished match).
- Valorant map markets showed 0 contracts traded in 24 h in the 10-13 catalogue.
test.artefact_checks:
1) Queue optimism. The critic's rule assumes nobody is ahead of us at our price. Two rules that remove that assumption also fail in the holdout: conservative -0.21c (a print strictly below our bid, which can only happen after our whole level is gone) and queue-honest +1c -4.17c. Neither comes near +2c, so the failure is not a queue artefact.
2) taker_side meaning was checked on this sample: yes-taker prints sit 2.2c above no-taker prints in the same minute on 90% of 971 map-minutes.
3) Quote at snap: the first seller print sits at the snap bid at the median (25th-75th percentile: 0 to +2c). The candle-close bid is not systematically stale against us.
4) Sides come from the livestats in-game metadata; the API's sides are wrong on about 5% of maps.
5) The only positive half is the in-sample window where the lean was found (+5.15c, about 1.2 standard errors), and it does not survive either holdout piece.
6) 783 of 1,215 maps (64%) saw no seller at our bid at all, and those are exactly the maps where the lean pays.
7) No replay was used, and no tape loss rate is quoted as ours. Fills here are inferred from the tape; real fills would be at least this adversely selected, because a real bid also shows its size.
8) Multiple looks: 4 fill rules x 3 periods, and none passes in the holdout.
9) Recorders: C:\kals\kalshi_data and C:\kals\feed_data were both still being written at 23:01Z (7:01 PM ET, 10-16). Free disk 108 GB; scratch folder 2.4 MB.

idea.name: Pre-market KXINXU stale-quote maker (R1-C2-08) priced off the US500 perp instead of a paid ES feed
idea.mechanism: C2-08's maker on the pre-market KXINXU ladder (04:00-09:30 ET) needs S_hat = ES x SPX_close / ES_16:00, but ES is not free in real time (Yahoo ES=F is 10 min delayed). Replace ES with the US500 perp mid (public REST, 1.2-5 s old): S_hat = perp_mid x S16 / perp_mid_16:00 plus a small calibrated overnight drift; quote C2-08's rungs off S_hat and pull before 08:30 ET releases (the perp lags ES by up to a minute). The US500 reference is the MerQube US Large Cap index (13,596 vs S&P 7,760; ratio 0.5680), so only ratios are used.
idea.why_mispriced: As C2-08: pre-market ladder quotes sit stale while futures move; the perp makes the fair free.
idea.must_be_true: C2-08 itself must pay (unproven: the index-ladders lane saw its sign flip by week); the perp keeps a two-sided pre-market book (it did on all 7 days since its 10-06 launch).
idea.evidence_so_far: 7 trading days 10-07..10-15 (small n): error of the 10:00 ET settle predicted at 08:00 ET -- perp 26.2 pts rms vs ES 25.8; at 09:25 ET perp 11.2 vs ES 9.0; at 09:59 ET 4.5 vs 3.9. Overnight drift ln(perp/ES) 16:00->09:30: mean +3.6 bp, max 7.9 bp (calibratable). Minute-return correlation with ES 0.72-0.98 after launch day (0.32 on day 1); ES leads the perp by one minute (lag corr 0.07-0.12; perp->ES ~0). C2-08's own P&L not measured here.

idea.test_plan: Inside C2-08's paper run: log S_hat from the perp mid every minute 04:00-09:30 ET and, after the fact, from Yahoo ES; 10 trading days; bar: perp-based S_hat within 3 pts of the ES-based one on >= 90% of minutes and C2-08's paper P&L no worse with the perp fair. 1 public GET a minute (premkt.py in r2-perps-venue/).

test.method:
Critic re-test of the pre-market KXINXU 10am-ladder maker (R2-M-18 / R1-C2-08). I re-ran the refuter's sim on ALL prints, using a sigma frozen before any holdout was scored. Sources, ranked:
- Kalshi public trade tape (rank 2), 08:40-09:30 ET.
- Settlement results from the result field.
- Fair-value feeds: Dukascopy USA500 cash-CFD ticks at 1-second resolution, used as the real-time S&P fair. It is free and historical, 464 hour-files. Checked against Yahoo ES 1-min: within 3 pts on 99% of 1,122 minutes; daily offset 0.1-2.9 pts.
- Yahoo ES=F 1-min (09-16 on).
- The free hybrid: 10-min-delayed ES level x KXUS500PERP 1-min change. It only exists from 10-07, because the perp did not trade 10-06 pre-market.
- VIX1D daily close.
No replay and no live fills involved.

Rule exactly as the tester's:
- quote round(100f) +-2c, with f = Phi(ln(S_hat/K)/sd);
- S_hat = feed x prior H1600 settle / feed at 16:00;
- fills only on prints STRICTLY through our price;
- one fill per taker order (prints sharing created_time and side), capped at 5 or 20;
- 1 s refill after a fill;
- held to the 10:00 result; maker fee 0 (verified /series/KXINXU: quadratic x1).

Sigma rules, all frozen:
- A: trailing-60-min realised x1.4 (the refuter's Brier fit on 08-11..09-11), plus my refit on <=10-01, which gave 1.3;
- B: realised variance for the pre-market minutes plus (kB x VIX1D_prev)^2 for the 30 RTH minutes to 10:00, kB=0.8 fitted on <=10-01.

Pre-registered primary, written in sim.py before scoring: real-time fair, k=1.4, cap 5. Bar (the critic's): >= +1c a contract, t >= 2 by close, no close < -$100.

Holdouts:
- forward: closes 10-02..10-16, 11 closes including the new 10-16 close;
- backward, added because the forward one is 7/11 the tester's known-good window: 68 closes 05-04..08-10 pulled via /historical/markets and /historical/trades. No parameter was fitted on them.

test.result:
The sigma fix is real, but it only brings the strategy to break-even.

1) The fix works out of sample.
- Calibration: rms z of the 10:00 settle went from 1.12-1.51 to 0.80-1.08 (Aug-Oct) with k=1.4, and from 1.54-2.22 to 1.10-1.59 (May-Aug). Rule B: 0.90-1.03 and 1.15-1.41.
- Money, paired per close, k=1.4 minus k=1.0: +$19.1 (se 6.8) on the 48 closes; +$11.6 (se 2.9, t 4.0) on the 68 backward closes. Rule B minus k=1.0: +$16.4 (se 3.7) backward.

2) The fixed rule does not make money. Cap 5, real-time fair:
- Forward holdout, 11 closes: +$114, +$10.4/close, se $16.9, t 0.61, +4.7c/contract, 4 losing, worst -$96. All of it comes from the tester's 10-07..10-15 window (+$254). 10-02..10-06 lost -$128 and the new 10-16 close -$11. FAILS t >= 2.
- Backward holdout, fully out of sample, 66 closes: k=1.4 -$326 (-$4.9/close, se $9.1, t -0.54, -2.3c/contract, 31 losing, worst -$229). With the 2 anchor-excluded closes back in: -$398 (t -0.66). Rule B: -$1 (t 0.00); -$71 including all 68.
- All 114 closes: k=1.4 +$236 (+$2.1/close, se $7.1, t 0.29, +0.8c/contract, 51 losing); Rule B +$906 (+$7.9/close, se $8.0, t 0.99, +3.1c/contract); refit k=1.3 -$45. Without the fix (k=1.0): -$1,448 (t -1.84).
- Cap 20: k=1.4 +$787 (t 0.32, worst -$675); B +$2,616 (t 0.93, worst -$761).
- By month, k=1.4 cap 5: May +110, Jun -48, Jul -448, Aug +547, Sep -21, Oct +97.

3) Free hybrid fair vs real-time fair, same 8 closes 10-07..10-16: +$257 vs +$242 (k=1.4). The free feed costs nothing; there is simply no edge for it to keep.

4) Model vs the market's own mid (Brier score at fixed 5-min grid times, 47 closes): k=1.4 better by 0.0031 (se 0.0042); B better by 0.0055 (se 0.0039). Not significant: the fixed model forecasts no better than the market.

5) Robustness:
- one extra minute of fair staleness halves the forward holdout (+$114 to +$59);
- wider half-spreads w=3 and w=4 (exploratory) do not rescue it (+$584 and +$579 on 48 closes);
- per-print fills instead of per-order are within noise.

The critic's bar (t >= 2 and no close below -$100) fails on every rule and on both holdouts.

idea.name: Quiet-second 70-80c favourite on the 15-min crypto series (no jump, 10-60 s left, model edge >= 2c) -- WEAK, post hoc, fragile to arrival time

test.one_line: Speed is real money in this market, but it does not rescue the M-14 cell: at a fixable ~50 ms arrival the October line is +1.09c a contract on 309 fills with the Oct 9-16 half at -2.95c. The bigger find is that our live forecaster waits 1.26 s by design (a paper fill rule copied into execution), and the offers it loses by waiting were +3.2c winners.
test.method: Source rank 2 (our recorder's rebuilt true book) for fills; live logs for latency. (1) latdecomp.py / inbound.py / lateprobe.py split every live order's time on one clock, or as a difference in which the clock offset cancels. (2) bx_scan2.py = the frozen bx_scan.py with 4 extra arrival delays (+25/+50/+100/+125 ms) and nothing else changed. It reproduces the frozen output on 441/441 shared (row, delay) pairs on 10-16T09. It was run on ALL 334 October hours, 12 new hours (10-16T10..T21) and 301 of 421 SEPX hours, and the October rescan gives the identical stored +75 line (238 fills +2.39c). (3) rt2_eval.py scores frozen ARM-N and ARM-J (first qualifying second per market, IOC at the seen ask, 20 and 98 lots, hold to settlement) at each delay. It also scores a rival-adjusted line, where contracts that a taker also took within 25 ms after our arrival are counted at half, and an event-driven laptop arrival mix: measured inbound p50 22 ms + 2 ms compute + half the measured warm round trip, giving arrival p10/p50/p90 44/52/78 ms. Clustered by close and by UTC day; chronological halves. (4) fc_optreal.py: the live forecaster's own paper engine logs every decision both 'opt' (filled at the decision instant) and 'real' (only if still there 1 s later).

latency_split.forecaster: THE FORECASTER'S IOC REACHES KALSHI 1,215 / 1,259 / 1,296 ms (p10/p50/p90, 117 October orders, Kalshi clock both ends) AFTER KALSHI SENT THE PRINT IT DECIDED ON. The earlier 276 ms (lat_real.py) was measured from the NEXT print: in 106 of 133 orders the newest print before our send was the one after the decision print. Pieces: about 22 ms inbound; about 110 ms waiting, because bettor_paper.py DECIDE_OFFSET = 0.2 s makes the engine decide 200 ms after the print's own second; 1,000-1,041 ms more, because SURVIVE_S = 1.0 s is the paper's 'real' fill rule and forecaster_live.py sends the live IOC only when that paper fill books; then about 100 ms outbound, because ordercli.send opens a fresh urllib/TLS connection per order (the pin's warm connection is 48 ms round trip). So the ~1 s tails are not network: a conservative PAPER fill test was copied into live EXECUTION.
latency_split.pin: Pin, 300 live orders 10-10..10-16. Decide minus local receipt of the latest print: p10 41 / p50 403 / p90 1,063 ms. Decide-to-send 2 ms; warm round trip p50 48 ms (81 ms over all connections). index_age_s at send: p50 0.32 s, p90 1.04 s. 119 of 300 orders were decided more than 600 ms after the latest print arrived, spread across every leg (early 58, full 45, topup 15). The universe refresh is NOT it: it is deferred inside 60 s of a close (UNI_NEAR_TAU_S). Slow passes (> 200 ms) inside the last 60 s were 602 over 161 closes, and 467 of them are the tau-0 close pass. Likely mechanism (a HYPOTHESIS, not verified line by line): the 20 Hz scan fires on integer-second tau gates read from time.time(), so many entries open at the wall-clock second boundary, about 90 ms BEFORE that second's print arrives, and trade on a print about 1 s old.
latency_split.laptop_clock: OPS: the laptop clock drifts by up to about 0.6 s. Laptop receipt minus Kalshi send of index prints (median, normally about 20 ms) was -261 ms at 10-15T06Z, +467..+637 ms from 10-16T09Z to T16Z (05:00-12:00 ET), and -20 ms by T21Z. The forecaster's health lag_ms (receipt minus CF stamp) shows the same climb to 667 ms. Anything comparing local time to exchange time inherits this, including pin's index_age_s gate (MAX_INDEX_AGE_S = 2 s) and LATE_S / STALE_S in the forecaster. Money impact not measured.
latency_split.recorder_stalls: On about 1 second in 5 (18-22% of seconds in clock-good hours), the collector receives index prints AND book deltas 0.3-2 s late together: in those seconds 83 in 100 deltas are late, against 4 in 100 otherwise. The Bitstamp feed on the same box is unaffected (rx minus exchange p50 80 / p90 92 ms in both), and the live forecaster's own socket shows lag p99 77-88 ms. So the stall is in the collector's Kalshi connection or process, not the laptop's network. Book rebuilds use Kalshi ts_ms, so tape fills are unaffected, but any study that uses collector _rx_ms as 'when we knew' inherits a fake 1-s tail.

wrongful_kills.why: Killed by its own bar at 'our real arrival'. That arrival time comes from our own code, not from the market, and the code can be fixed. The r3 lane measured it (lat_real.py, 87 October forecaster IOCs, Kalshi's own order stamps): from Kalshi sending the print to our order reaching Kalshi took p10 225 / p50 276 / p90 1,275 ms. Only about 26 ms of that is the inbound network. The forecaster waits about 141 ms after the print arrives, then takes about 100 ms more to reach Kalshi. The live pin is slower: my read of its 161 latest order records (critic-final/pinlat.py) gives index_age_s at send p50 0.32 s and p90 1.04 s, while its warm order round trip is only 48 ms (p50). The round-1 drop 'Universe-pass overrun near the close' (pin pass p50 ~0.93 s; dropped as NO-MONEY, unpriced) is the same delay, and the tape now puts a price on it. On the frozen ARM-N rule, the fresh SEPX sample made +3.90c a contract at +0 ms and +3.78c at +75 ms, against +0.77c at real arrival. Across all holdouts, +260 ms made +3.11c (811 fills, t 1.94 by day) against +1.74c at real arrival. The tester's own paired check: offers still there at 260 ms but gone by ~1 s were +12.45c winners, and the ~22 in 100 of our arrivals that land ~1 s late get the -1.8c leftovers. The same speed would add fills to the M-02 survivor: 208 fills at +75 ms against 136 at real arrival (T+U), at a similar edge a contract.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: (1) Use the live logs to split each order's time into print sent, our receipt, decision, send and Kalshi's stamp. Sources: pinrun-live order records (index_age_s, t_ms_decide, t_ms_send, latency_ms); forecaster-live decision lag_ms and order client-id ms against Kalshi ts_ms. Name the code step behind the ~1 s tails and the pin's ~320 ms median wait. (2) Score the frozen spec_N.json (n_eval.py) and ARM-J (ana2.py) on every tape hour after 10-16T09Z at +50/+75/+100 ms and at the measured mix. Overturn if the <= 100 ms line makes >= +2c a contract after fee on >= 200 new fills with both halves > 0 (the idea's own bar), after halving for rivals sending in the same millisecond. Money if it passes: tape about $3-7/day at 20 lots on October supply, about 4-5x that at 98 lots. Tape worst day -$54 to -$92 at 20 lots.

wrongful_kills.why: It was killed as a TAKER only. The blue-side lean holds out of sample: blue won minus mid was +4.34c on the new Apr-Aug archive (se 2.05) and +2.88c pooled out of sample (714 maps / 370 matches). It is smaller than half-spread plus fee (~3.3-3.8c), so buying at the ask loses (-0.46c). LoL makers pay no fee. A resting bid on the blue team keeps the 1.5-2c half-spread instead of paying it, roughly +4.5c a contract before adverse selection. The tester also found the price barely moves as the draft reveals sides (+0.28c from snap to game start), so the people selling into our bid may know little. The tester wrote the maker off as 'not measured, needs a recorder'. It does not need one: the public trade tape with taker_side (the fill rule the R3-M-12 tester used) can score it now on the same 714 maps.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Rule: rest a 50-lot bid at the blue team's best bid from previous map close + 2 min to game start. Count a fill only when >= 50 seller-initiated contracts trade at or through our price. Outcome from the map result, one leg per map, clustered by match. FIT Aug 17-Sep; holdout = the Apr 1-Aug 16 archive plus October. Bar: >= +2c per filled contract on >= 150 filled maps, both halves > 0. Also check whether filled maps' blue win rate falls below unfilled maps' by more than the edge. Then the same on CS2 map side and Valorant if the archive holds them. Window: Worlds runs to Nov 8 (8-12 maps a day), then near zero until mid-January. Money if it passes: about $5-15/day at 50 lots during Worlds. Not measured.
