wrongful_kills.why: R1-C2-08 is covered by the same point. The pre-market KXINXU maker was killed because its model was over-confident: rms z was 1.21-1.54 over 47 closes, and when the model and the market differed by more than 2c, the model was the more extreme one 84% of the time. That is an input that can be fixed, not proof of no edge. The stats refuter's own fix (sigma x1.4, fitted on the early closes) made +$39 (se $13, about 3 se) on the later-half holdout of a 1-in-5 print subsample, with a fresh fair and best-case fills. It was reported as 'break-even overall' only because the fit half was included, and it was never tested as the main rule. The money in the window is real. Pre-market makers as a group made +22.7c a contract (r1 flows lane, 33 events, 123k contracts). Takers pay ~3.7c over the ES fair. The free hybrid fair (delayed ES level plus the perp's change) is within 1 pt on 91% of minutes.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Re-run the refuter's 47-close sim (refute-stats-20261015-R2-M-18) on all prints, with sigma frozen in advance (x1.4, or scaled by VIX1D/VIX). Run it twice: once on the real-time ES fair and once on the free hybrid. Fills only on prints strictly through our price, 08:40-09:30 ET. Holdout: closes after 10-01 plus every new close. Bar: >= +1c a contract, t >= 2 by close, no close below -$100 at cap 5. Money if it passes: about $2 a weekday at cap 5, about $8 at cap 20. Worst close without the fix: -$373 at cap 5.

weak_survivors.problem: Refuted, correctly. But the numbers its refuters left behind are wrong and must not reach the operator. live_830.py, tb_ledger830.py and ledger830.py compute money as revenue/100 - costs - fee. That is the trap pinledger.payout documents: revenue reads 0 when both sides were held, which is every insured market. The tiebreak's 'side finding' claims the main bot lost -$429.59 on 373 markets since 10-04: losers averaged -$90, and it lost 2.9 times in 100 against a break-even of 1.7. That is false. pinledger.pnl on the same ledger (critic-final/pinpnl2.py) gives +$233.19 on 380 markets. The 11 losers averaged -$31.80, winners +$1.58, and break-even is 4.73 losses per 100. The revenue-only formula reproduces -$418 on my run, which confirms the bug. Because the real loss size is ~$32, not ~$90, each refuter's guard value falls to about a third, so the kill stands even more firmly. About 20 other scripts in this hunt compute pin money the same way (e.g. refute-execution-20261015-R3-M-07/q2_ledger.py, refute-execution-20261015-R1-C1-13/pin_daily.py, refute-tiebreak-20261015-R1-N0-17/t5_pinday.py). Each understates the main account's 15-min money by about $50/day ($651 over 13 ET days). Where that was used to argue pin's cash is valuable, the objection is conservative, not wrong. Any figure saying pin is losing, such as the R2-M-11 tiebreak's -$46/day, is this bug.

The best-evidenced survivor, but weak in three measured ways. (1) Its October edge is on the four coins with no 5 Hz feed. In real rival fills (R3-M-08 tester), BNB/HYPE/ZEC/NEAR made +11.43c on 163 markets and BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE made +0.72c on 191 (difference t 3.3). The 5 Hz coins fell from +9.1c in W35 to -0.3c in W42, because rivals now trade before the print off exchange books: 75 in 100 taker trades in the 200-600 ms before a >= 4-sigma print are on its side. (2) The holdouts are not clean: R2 had already scored the 4-sigma half on both 'unseen' periods, and no single period reaches t 2 by close. (3) Supply is shrinking. Real slow-rival fills fell from 44-48 markets a day (W36-37) to 13 (W42), and October's second half made -0.03c. Pre-register the read split by coin group, with a drop rule for the whole 5 Hz group (not just BTC) and the supply stop (< 10 slow fills a day for a week).

Every surviving reward idea rests on a payment nobody has seen: a weekly or daily non-coin-race pot paid to THIS account, split pro rata with the farmers. The only cash proof is the coin race, paid at 90% to main pool 0 for 100% of an EMPTY side. Shares do not hold. LoL fell from 0.41 to 0.14-0.22 within hours, with 27 of 47 references ratcheting up with no trades. Aspen fell from 15.5% to 10.3% in 1 h 42 min. M-22's $4/day is one point on a $0.5-25/day curve set by how fast rivals react (unmeasured), and they stepped bids up 1c->4c in the previous period. M-19's narrow quote loses -11c, and its 200-lot share was read on a still book at 8:28 AM ET, the best moment of the day. Non-crypto pots settle in pool 0, which holds $0 since v-onepool, so any probe needs the operator to fund a subaccount. One written question to Kalshi support, then one ~$150-290 probe on a single weekly pot, decides the whole family. Until then each of these is $0.

The CLIFF combo rebate. The idea as written is dead. In play, the score-concentration boost is only 1.0-1.35x (1.9-3.7c a contract; dropped r3 #122). A one-off 20-lot fill falls under the 1% minimum score on 2,186 of 2,559 legs. The per-league CLIFF rates used were 2-16x too high for 6 of 8 leagues, because the pull took only the biggest pools. Pre-game volume earns nothing. Above all, how it pays is unknown: cash or bonus credit, counted in contracts or dollars, paid to the subaccount or to pool 0. The reopen clauses of R3-M-10/M-11 hinge on the same question. One written support answer settles all four; until then they are $0.

On the Senate and governor legs its $97 version is built on, the maker part measured a median 0.35c a contract against the mid. The rest is the same unmeasured carry bet that the two refuted taker versions (R1-C3-04-P, R2-M-13) made. In 2024 those legs had no early settlement: they paid on 2025-01-03, 59 days after the election, so the cash is locked into January. Most cheap legs are one party's seats, so a single national swing hits them together.

The trigger feed is unproven. GasBuddy's Colorado live average jumped +4.2c in one 5-minute update at 06:30 ET 10-16, which is a false alarm exactly the size of the trigger. On the five fresh Midwest restoration days most of the morning money was already gone, and a bigger, earlier buyer takes what is left. By 6 PM ET the market already holds the move (error 0.60c vs GasBuddy 1.86c). The $3/day has not been measured on a live feed.

All three KXRAIN survivors fade going into October. N0-10 (buy at listing) made +20.9c in Jul/Aug, +15.3c in Sep and +3.2c on Oct 1-8, and its October money rests on 1-2 dates. N0-06 (evening): Sep+Oct is +4.8c with a date-clustered 95% CI of -1.5..+10.6. Its own kill line (per-date net <= 0 after 15 dates) is already met for the 18Z version in October, and the 6-10 PM book depth is unmeasured. N0-12 (maker): Jul-Sep made +0.2c a contract under the strict fill model (se 3.0); everything comes from 12 October dates, and it loses at 250 lots. All three share one weather driver per date, so they are one bet, not three.

The strongest non-crypto survivor (0 identity breaks in 144 rungs, every release positive), with three gaps. (1) If a release is delayed, the two legs settle under different rules; KXCPI-25OCT already settled off the identity. (2) Government funding runs only to Dec 11, so the next prints face shutdown risk. (3) There is one print a month, and the money figure assumes we capture 100% of the supply others traded. Price the delayed-release tail before any paper run.

These cross-venue survivors are worth about $0 recurring. Matched betting (C3-09): under the standard deduction, the likely case for a retail filer, a 50% boost token nets -$0.25 per $25 (p90 +$0.61). Only 100% boosts (+$4.12) and no-sweat bets (+$1.70) survive, the maximum wager is set per customer and unknown, and the resting Kalshi hedge does not fill on NFL (0.95-3.9M contracts ahead). Poly maker (C3-14): the rebate ends Oct 18. 0 of 230 live sides allow a quote strictly inside Poly's spread, the fills are inferred from hourly snapshots and never seen in trades, and it needs a Poly deposit. Rothera (C3-12): a one-off ~$52 resting on one 1,000-lot offer at 56c. Nobody has taken it in 5 h, the venue is co-owned by Susquehanna, Rothera's own ~0.5c fee is left out, and it recurs far less than weekly.

Each rests on one episode. Endorsements: one market (SEP04-A20) carries $702 of the $743 two-minute supply. The rest exists only when the market disputes the count, and there 0-of-34 false locks is the wrong denominator. Payroll wings: the whole effect is 2026, driven by shutdown-delayed releases, and only 24 of 47 shoulder legs had >= 100 contracts printed at the quote within 2 h.

next_lanes.brief:
Price and cut our own decision delay on the 15-min crypto books; the tape now shows speed is money (wrongful kill R3-M-14). Measured facts:
- Forecaster: Kalshi sends the print -> our order reaches Kalshi p10 225 / p50 276 / p90 1,275 ms. About 26 ms of that is the inbound network, about 141 ms waiting, about 100 ms to reach Kalshi (r3 lat_real.py).
- Pin: index_age_s at send p50 0.32 s / p90 1.04 s on 161 recent orders, but a warm round trip of only 48 ms p50 (critic-final/pinlat.py). Its universe pass takes p50 ~0.93 s (dropped r1 C1 item).
- Network: laptop -> Kalshi round trip ~29 ms; an Ohio VM ~1 ms (results/VM_PLAN_2026-09-24.md).
Steps:
(1) From the live logs, split every live order into print sent -> receipt -> decision -> send -> Kalshi stamp, and name the code steps behind the 1 s tails.
(2) On the rebuilt book, replay each bot's OWN live decisions moved to +50/+100/+150 ms after the print. fillcheck.py matches our IOCs 160 of 163. Measure extra contracts fillable at or under the limit and the price improvement, per market. This is a book question, not a loss rate. Reuse the existing ARM-J/ARM-N +0/+75/+150/+260 lines.
(3) Money = extra fills x the measured edge a contract, clustered by close. Compare an event-driven rewrite (free) with an Ohio Lightsail VM ($84-124/month).
Bar: >= $5/day at today's size, both halves.
Read-only. Stream one delta hour at a time under 200 MB; never load_quotes; never touch the live processes.

Rivals beat the 1-s print using exchange books, not Kalshi's 5 Hz feed. 75 in 100 taker trades in the 200-600 ms before a >= 4-sigma print are already on its side, and it was 79 in 100 in August, before the 5 Hz channel existed (test-20261015-R3-M-08). Our feed_data has constituent books only for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE. The band edge still alive in October is on the coins we do not record: BNB/HYPE/ZEC/NEAR +11.43c on 163 markets, against +0.72c on 191 for the 5 Hz coins.
(1) Free first: re-run R3-M-16's mo_sim.py with the fair taken from feed_data/coinbase mids instead of BRTI, on the same 673 BTC windows, marked to the 120-s market mid. This is the opening-maker test the tester named but never ran. Bar: >= +0.5c a contract, t >= 2 in FIT, TEST and confirmation separately, >= 300 fill-windows.
(2) From CF Benchmarks' published methodology, list the constituent exchanges of the BNB/HYPE/ZEC/NEAR indices. Measure rivals' pre-print share on those four coins with prescan.py.
(3) Operator decision: run a new read-only recorder (never the collector) of those exchanges' public trade/book WebSockets for 7 days. Score the composite nowcast two ways: (a) as a pre-print band trigger at -200..0 ms on the rebuilt book; (b) as a pin loss gate on those coins' live losers (ledger via pinledger.pnl, NOT the revenue field).
Bars: pre-print >= +4c a contract at our own arrival on >= 60 fills, both halves. The gate must refuse >= 3 losers and net >= +$3/day.

Golf has about 100 Kalshi series and none has ever been tested. KXDPWORLDTOUR (winner) traded 494,877 contracts in 24 h and KXPGATOUR 128,311 (catalogue 10-13). There are also top-5/10/20/40, make-cut, H2H, 3-ball, round-leader, LIV and LPGA series. The only ledger rows died for lack of data: SJN5 ('Kalshi serves only 6-7 settled events') and SJ20 (decided top-20). /historical now serves them. My probe (capped at 4 pages, critic-final/hist_probe.json), Feb-Aug 2026: KXPGATOUR >= 34 events, KXPGATOP10 >= 33, KXPGAMAKECUT >= 30, KXDPWORLDTOUR 19, KXPGAH2H 1,183 head-to-head events; plus the live tier since 08-16. Free data: ESPN golf scoreboard/leaderboard JSON (hole by hole) and PGA Tour / DP World Tour results.
(1) Calibrate on a fixed clock (before R1, and at the end of R1/R2/R3), one leg per event. Cover winner and top-N favourites and longshots. Price H2H (two players, one round or the tournament) against a simple model: current score difference plus holes left x per-hole spread from past rounds. Fit Feb-May; test Jun-Aug plus the live tier.
(2) Test a maker on the thin H2H and top-N legs. Read fee_type per series (KXPGATOUR charges maker fees).
Bar: >= +2c a contract after fee on >= 150 test events, both halves, and no event > 25% of profit. Season: PGA fall events and the DP World Tour run through November, then January. ~1,200 public calls.

The Mentions category (76 series, ~190k contracts/day) was left out of the r3 archive lane. SJ17 (earnings words) died on n = 6 because 'banks have zero settled markets', which /historical now overturns. My probe (critic-final/hist_probe.json): KXTRUMPMENTION >= 143 settled events since 2025-11 (pull capped); KXEARNINGSMENTIONJPM and GS have 4 events and 49-60 word-markets each since 2025-10; KXWORLDNEWSMENTION has 28 events. Bank earnings are this week and big tech is late October. Reward pots are large: KXWORLDNEWSMENTION ~$6.6k/day while active, KXTRUMPMENTION 107 active programs (critic-final/incent_rate.txt, incent_types.json).
(1) Pull every settled mention market (all KX*MENTION* and KXTRUMPSAY) from /historical plus the live tier, with daily and hourly candles. Take the YES price at T-7d, T-1d and 1 h before the event. One market per word per event, clustered by event.
(2) Base rates: for earnings words, the word count in the company's last 4-8 call transcripts (free on investor-relations sites); for Trump and news words, the event type. Test the YES-overpricing bias and compare model and market Brier scores. Watch the trap: early-YES settlements are listed first.
(3) Maker: cheap-side NO joins inside the reward pots, with fills scored on the trade tape (F2 rule).
Bar: >= +2c a contract on >= 150 test events. Fit 2025; test 2026.

KXTESTMATCH is Kalshi's 2nd-biggest sports series by 24h volume (1,722,831 contracts on 10-13); KXODIMATCH traded 252,909 and KXT20MATCH 148,333. Cricket was only touched as one leg of the C3-10 pregame longshot seller (-0.48c, with 4 no-result settles at 50c), and U21 (washout convexity) is still unread. /historical (critic-final/hist_probe.json): KXT20MATCH 1,046 settled events Feb-Aug 2026, KXODIMATCH 111, KXTESTMATCH 30. Free data: ESPNcricinfo/Cricbuzz ball-by-ball JSON, and Open-Meteo hourly venue forecasts and history.
(1) Read each series' rules for draw, tie, no result and abandonment.
(2) T20/ODI: compare the trailing side's price with the chance of no result from the venue rain forecast. When rain interrupts, compare with the DLS par score. Calibrate at fixed points (end of powerplay, innings break, 10 overs left).
(3) Tests: calibrate draw/result at the start of days 4 and 5 (lead, overs left, weather).
(4) Run the feed-lag gate first (the esports rule): free ball-by-ball delay against Kalshi's repricing lag; stop if the feed is later.
Cluster by match; hold out by date. Bar: >= +2c a contract after fee on >= 150 matches, both halves.

Kalshi runs its own live sports feed and nobody examined it; round 1 only fetched the docs (r1-kalshi-mechanics-capital/docs/api-reference__live-data__get-game-stats.md). GET /live_data/milestone/{milestone_id}/game_stats serves public, Sportradar-sourced play-by-play for NFL, NCAAF, NBA, NCAAB, WNBA, soccer, NHL and MLB. Every in-play idea in this hunt died because Kalshi reprices 0-10 s after the event, ahead of ESPN and other public feeds. The in-play prop makers died at about 0 net: NFL D200 markout -0.99c plus +0.96c CLIFF. Fills within 60 s of a score cost -1.81c to -2.39c.
(1) Map milestones to events (milestone and structured-target endpoints). Poll game_stats once a second for NFL Sunday 10-18, NBA from 10-21 and the World Series. For each scoring or possession play, line up when it appears in the feed with Kalshi's first trade that moves the mid >= 2c.
(2) If the feed leads Kalshi by >= 2 s on >= 50 of 100 scoring plays, re-run the R3-M-10/M-11 maker scripts (test-20261015-R3-M-10, -M-11) with a pull-quotes-on-event guard driven by this feed. Bar: in-play D200 300-s markout >= +0.5c over >= 40 games, both halves, before any CLIFF.
If the feed trails Kalshi, report that and stop. Read-only; <= 1,500 public calls.

wrongful_kills.id: capital-cost kill reason: 20261015-R1-N1-01 (execution objection), 20261015-R1-C2-07, 20261015-R1-C2-10 (tiebreak dollars), 20261015-R1-N0-07 (execution), 20261015-R1-N2-05 (dump flow 'capital-bound'), SI25 rain half, SI30, SI12
wrongful_kills.why: These kills and haircuts all rest on one claim: the locked cash comes out of the bank the pin bot sizes from, so it costs pin's ~1.6%/day. This round's own N2-02 test measured that this is false at today's bank. 0 of 900 orders and 0 of 20 hedges failed for cash. Worst concurrent cash need was ~$390 of $1,155 (p99 $2.31 per contract of bet). pinrun keeps SIZE at 98 while ~$450 is moved out (--bank-brake 2.44, --loss-cap-frac 0.306). Another $97 already sits idle in stopped subaccounts 3 and 4. Kalshi pays APY on cash AND positions on balances >= $250 (SJ47). So for the first ~$450, a slow trade's opportunity cost is about the APY, not pin's return. The execution skeptic's finding that the CPI pair is net -$2 to -$6/day is entirely this cost.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Re-score each of these at an opportunity cost of ~4%/yr for the first ~$450 locked, and at pin's marginal return beyond that. Use trade-confirmed supply, not candles. The condition is N2-02's weekly capital_need.py read: per-contract p99 <= $2.50 and max <= $2.94. To revive any one: positive held P&L per month after fees on its own holdout, and worst plausible loss <= the $216 day stop.

wrongful_kills.id: D08 + 'Kalshi lists no perpetuals' (results/BRIEF_FOR_OPERATOR.md l.59) + kills that cited no per-second index feed or Pyth now needing a key (index-ladders hourly maker 're-opens only with a sub-second index feed'; DJI hourly; C2-03 execution objection; the daily-commodity 5 PM pin pointer)
wrongful_kills.why: I measured this on 2026-10-15 with public GETs (critic-r1/perp_census.json). Kalshi runs 29 perpetual futures on a separate margin API (https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/margin; market data needs no auth). They trade $979M/day of notional with $56M open interest: BTC $415M/day at 1.95 bp, ETH $377M, gold $48M, silver $39M, a US500 index perp $11M at 0.07 bp, WTI, USTECH100, and the same alt coins as our 15-min binaries. Every market carries a reference_price and a mark price with millisecond stamps. The Temporary Perpetual Fee Rebate (to 2026-12-31: makers NET +0.3 bp, takers pay 0.3 bp) removes D08's fee half ('fees 449x a binary hedge'). D08's size half (the hedge size explodes near 50c) still stands. The feed-based kills may reopen if the perp references track the binaries' settlement sources; that is NOT measured.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Over 2 weeks of hourly closes, compare the perp reference/mark at the close second with the settled value (expiration_value) of: KXINXU and KXNASDAQ100U (US500 and USTECH100 perps); the Pyth-settled KXGOLDH, KXSILVERH and KXWTIH; and the 15-min gold, silver, copper, platinum and palladium markets (metal perps). Bar: >= 99 closes in 100 on the correct side of every strike within 1 tick, and update latency <= 1 s. Separately, compare the KXBTCPERP, ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE references with our CF BRTI tape second by second: equal, lagging or leading?

wrongful_kills.why: It was killed as a naive fill strategy, but the idea as filed also stacked the natgas $20/window reward, and that half was never measured (the result says 'Reward overlay not measured'). The tester's own leftover is the best natgas fact of the round. A favourite-side bid at 80-95c from tau 780 to 120 s costs ~0 at the back of the queue; only the last 120 s cost -5.5c. That makes natgas the better first market for the C2-03 reward share grab, not 'commodities only after' FX. In FX the tape cost is ~0 only on average, and the risk of being the stale order is unmeasured.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Run a queue-aware orderbook_delta replay on ~20 untouched natgas hours, streaming one hour at a time (~150 MB/hour). Simulate a one-sided 300-lot at the favourite's best bid when it is 80-95c, placed at tau 780 and pulled at tau 120. Score exact fills plus the filed reward score: reference walk to 1/5 of target, 0.5 discount per tick, normalised per side. Bar: fills + reward > +$1/window, fills no worse than -1c/contract, positive in both halves.

wrongful_kills.why: It was refuted on a $/day stake that was itself computed with the revenue-0 ledger bug. The fix's value is avoiding a rare bad day, not a daily rate. The tester measured in real code what a silent taker_side removal does: it switches the seller check (toxic-fresh) off with no alarm, and the forecaster's engine raises KeyError on every print. A silent book flip blinds the stale-index hedge belief on YES-favourite markets. Kalshi has given 0-7 days notice on past field removals. Refuting the daily $ does not refute shipping a cheap guard.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: (1) The corrected-ledger loss per day (netting credit included) of the markets the toxic-fresh check refuses, with the check off, over 10-04..10-15. That is the cost of one silent-removal day. (2) From the last 12 months of the Kalshi changelog: how many breaking field or default changes there were, and how many days of notice each got. Expected loss avoided = rate x days to notice x (1). Ship regardless if (1) exceeds the guard's build cost. Also run the ws_flag_test.py delta check (>= 1,000 deltas, 0 mismatches) after a non-pause hour.

wrongful_kills.id: SJ51 / U17 (political carry) and the untested 20261015-R1-C3-04 (election Solid carry)
wrongful_kills.why: SJ51 was killed on 10-02, but its critic re-check was positive at 4 of 5 horizons, with resting-bid adverse selection unmeasured. Le 2026 (64.7M Kalshi trades) measured politics favourites UNDER-priced at 1 week to 1 month (recalibration slope 1.83). This round's pro-desk lane measured politics only at 1-7 days. The Nov 3 board is the last chance this cycle. With idle cash costing ~APY (wrongful kill 1), the carry has a lower bar to clear than when it was killed.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Use Polymarket 2022 and 2024 House/Senate/Governor race markets (gamma + clob prices-history, free; C3-02's scripts) at T-21 and T-14 days. Take sides priced 90-97c and compare realised win rate with price, clustered by race. Bar: >= +2c a contract after fees on >= 150 races, and <= 1 loss per 100 at >= 95c. Then list today's Kalshi legs at 93-97c with their ask depth, plus a post-Nov-3 exit at 99c bids.

wrongful_kills.id: SI51 team-sport leg / maker-portfolio in-play sellers (killed by the stopping-time audit's generalisation)
wrongful_kills.why: The audit concluded 'most of their edge is the hindsight window; NHL/MLB are the exceptions'. C3-01 then measured NHL only at 85-98c leader prices in periods 2-3. NBA was never measured on an exogenous clock, though it supplied 13.0M of the 23M trades behind the arXiv 2607.14430 step-function result, and the season starts Oct 21. Last season's tape is reachable through the /historical endpoints (historical/markets, historical/trades, historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks, already used by the N1-01 and C2-10 testers), so 'no data' is not a reason.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Compare KXNBAGAME 2025-26 from /historical against a model-free history table built from NBA cdn play-by-play (lead x seconds left x possession x home), using C3-01's method on an every-minute grid. Measure leader ask minus history, and maker bid-fill quality at the back of the queue (fills that clear the level). Bar: a lean >= 1c a contract after maker fee at back-of-queue quality, in both halves of the season, over >= 300 games.

weak_survivors.problem: The only positive part is the reward credit ($228/day at 300, $110 at 100). It was polled 04:17-04:37 ET on Thursday, inside the 03:00-05:00 ET exchange pause, on a static book, so it is not a trading-hours number. Fills cost -$114/day (se $38; 15 of 20 days lose; worst -$421), and 13% of fills carry 95% of the loss. Treat as dead unless credit measured in open hours beats the fill cost.

The lottery leg is dead (October flow is 10x below September). A farmer's 2c piles set the reward share minute by minute and cut any 1c bid's share to zero. The tape contradicts the 'lenient' +$7.9/day: 1c levels sold into with >= 100 contracts emptied 45 times out of 45.

The hunters' key number was an artefact; across all far strikes the net is -$3.48 per strike-hour. The surviving 6-8 bp band (+$3.88) assumes a constant sweep rate. That rate was measured on other farmers' stacks, which are pulled before sweeps, and one sweeper bot hits all five tenors in the same hour.

$0/day now. One 1,000-lot NO at ~95c reserves ~$950 (82% of the bank), and this account has never been paid NO-side credit. The filed variant (a) fails once the cancel signal is valid (-$0.81/race); only the guard variant survives, and only in a replay (+$1.04/race).

Narrowed to far-strike CPI quotes at +$1.15/market-day (SE 1.88, within noise). Mid strikes lose -$7.43 (2.9 SE below zero). The worst week was -$970 on one market, and every candidate rides the same monthly print.

The rule as written fails its own t >= 2 bar on the full rebuilt book, and it lost -7.0c/contract over the last 9 days. Only a post-hoc 70-95c limit band survives (holdout +8.84c, 77 fills), and it needs a pre-registered forward read.

Its own calibration bar FAILS: at fair 0.995-0.999, tau 16-30, calm, losses ran 2.78% against 0.25% promised (11x). The size-up's extra contracts would be bought at 98c, where the only full-size test shows losses above break-even. The $2/day was read off a table at an assumed loss rate.
The edge comes from one calm regime: Jan-Mar 2026 gives +0.7c/contract, BTC's own holdout gives +0.6c (last 24 events), and October gives -0.8c. The shoulder-sale half is dead on supply.
Only the NO side survives, and it was chosen after YES failed. Without May 2026 it is +3.0c at t 0.84, clustered by calendar month, on ~7 NO legs a month.
The forward rate being scaled (+10-13% per $) comes from the 11 days since r28; the same rules on 09-30..10-03 earn far less. A 40-close step test can only catch a collapse, not a halving.

Still the only survivor with t > 3 (20 release months), but four problems. Trade-confirmed supply is about a quarter of the candle claim (median 10 pairs; $0.29/day at 33 pairs). The factor-level headline r was biased 4 months running in 2026, so the first window (Nov 10) is core-only on the named r. Kalshi settled KXCPI-25OCT and KXCPIYOY-25OCT off-identity when that index was never published. Government funding runs only to Dec 11. Realistic ~$0.3-1/day.

All the profit is the reward. The one cost that decides it, how often the slow, stale order at the touch gets run over, is invisible on the tape. Pyth's free endpoints now return 401, so the bot would quote without a live fair price. Natgas is the better first market (see wrongful kill C1-04).

The most decision-ready of the reward family, but its cost at the 115 s exit is unmeasured on our fills. The tape puts it at 33-50% of credit, and the 18% figure is only a floor from 15-s polling. The only live evidence is 3 races, and the reward is paid to pool 0, not to the posting subaccount.
Viable as a rule but protects $0 today: nothing rests across the Thursday pause and no 15-minute market spans it. It only has value for future resting-order bots.

Refuted by their skeptics or tiebreaks, yet still labelled plausible-needs-data. N0-01: weekday 16:00 ET is only 1.46x as dangerous on our entries, against a ~2x break-even. N2-05: the +1.12c is the tape's whole maker population, which a 200-lot capped bid cannot earn, measured in a window that starts the day after the biggest loss. N0-07: it rests on a 20c spread filter chosen after the literal rule lost. Record all three as dead unless new data arrives.

next_lanes.brief: Kalshi perpetual futures: a live Kalshi product on a separate margin API that the project has never examined (base https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/margin). Market data needs no auth: /markets, /exchange/status, /funding_rates/historical?ticker=, /markets/{t}/orderbook, /markets/{t}/candlesticks and trades; see docs.kalshi.com/margin-rest/*. Critic census 2026-10-15 (critic-r1/perp_census.json; reuse perp_census.py): 29 markets, $979M/day notional, $56M OI. Keep searching the 15-minute books, the best-shaped market we have. Sports is 27M contracts/day and every in-play taker idea this round died. The literature consistently finds that makers earn, but our maker tests die on adverse selection. One structural subsidy was never measured: the Sports Prop Combo component-leg program (help.kalshi.com article 17184676; map literature row 9; N0-16). It pays 25% of every prop combo's fees monthly, as Bonus Credit, to makers of the combo's legs. Score S = prod(1+Fi) - 1 over a combo's legs; no cap, no opt-in. Read-only, public:
(1) Pull one week of settled prop combos via the multivariate endpoints (docs.kalshi.com api-reference/multivariate: multivariate events and event collections; /markets?mve_filter=only). From legs, contracts and prices, compute fees per combo (verify the combo fee formula and fee_type), then the rebate pool per leg per day and the monthly total.
(2) Total maker volume per leg (one maker per trade, from /markets/trades), giving rebate per maker contract per leg and the boost from being a maker on several legs of the same popular combos.
(3) Adverse selection of a resting quote on those legs, using fills_an.py (test-20261015-R1-N2-03: trade-tape fill + own-outcome scoring, FRONT/THRU queue brackets), for NFL TD props, college football props, and NBA props from Oct 21, pre-game on the SCHEDULED clock. Net = rebate + spread capture - adverse selection - maker fee (most prop series are fee-free; check).
Bar: net >= +0.5c per filled contract on a holdout week, with >= 200 fills/day available at our size. Report the monthly pool even if the bar fails, so the operator knows the prize.

Published in-play effects never measured on Kalshi. Each is triggered by an event or a fixed clock grid, so the hindsight/close-type trap that killed most sports ideas does not apply.
(a) Soccer first goal (Angelini, De Angelis & Singleton, Betfair EPL): the home side is under-priced from 20 s to 5 min after a home first goal; flat-stake ROI 10-12% at 1-5 min (text in hunt-2026-10-13/map-literature/angelini_inplay.txt). Markets: KXEPLGAME, KXLALIGAGAME, KXMLSGAME, KXUCLGAME, KXFIFAWGAME and the other soccer game series (14M contracts/day, 1-5c spreads). Goal wallclock from ESPN soccer summaries or the Kalshi price jump. Fair price from a model-free history table (win probability by minute x score x home, built from football-data.co.uk or past ESPN seasons). Enter at the ask 60 s and 300 s after the goal. Older trades via /historical/trades and /historical/markets/{t}/candlesticks. Fit on Aug-Sep, test on October. Bar: >= +2c a contract after taker fee on >= 150 goals, both halves positive, and a random-goal-time placebo near 0.
(b) NBA, before the Oct 21 start: last season's KXNBAGAME from the /historical endpoints against a history table from NBA cdn play-by-play (lead x seconds left x possession x home), using C3-01's method (test-20261015-R1-C3-01/*.py) on an every-minute grid. Score maker bid fills at back-of-queue quality. Bar: a lean >= 1c after maker fee, in both season halves, over >= 300 games.
(c) Cheap add-on, tennis 'buzz' (Ramirez, Reade & Singleton 2022): use each player's Wikimedia pageview surge against their own baseline to predict (result - Kalshi pregame price) on ATP/WTA/Challenger, over 60 days of settled matches. Bar: >= 3c after fee in the top-buzz decile, holdout by date.
Cluster by match or game, and state the smallest detectable effect.

Nov 3 is the biggest one-night liquidity event on Kalshi (election series trade 7.8M contracts/day while open; ~18,000 markets), and nothing is built for it. C3-02 killed the 95c post-decision maker because 2 of 43 races on the 2024 general night reversed after the leader printed 95-97.5c: MI and WI Senate, the 'red mirage' undone by Detroit and Milwaukee absentees counted last. If that pattern is predictable it is an opportunity: a count-order rule that buys the 3-10c trailer only where the uncounted vote is known to lean its way.
(1) Write the rule BEFORE looking at prices. Per state: what is counted last (mail/absentee pre-processing law from the NCSL table; late-arriving mail in NV/CA/WA/AK; central-count cities), and which side the remaining vote favours (2020/2022/2024 county reporting order from public results).
(2) Test it on the Polymarket 2022 and 2024 general nights and the Nov 2025 night, with C3-02's gamma + prices-history scripts (test-20261015-R1-C3-02). Take every race where a side first printed >= 90c while the rule said the remainder leaned the other way. Report hit rate, price paid, P&L per 100 contracts, number of races and false alarms. n is small, so report the interval, and treat Nov 3 as paper unless the past nights are decisive.
(3) Confirm or specify a read-only Nov 3 recorder: books + trades for ~300 race, control and seat-ladder tickers, in its own process, 18:00 ET Nov 3 to 06:00 ET Nov 4, never the crypto collector. Add a timestamped vote-count poller (state SOS pages; AP via NYT/DDHQ JSON) so the night can be scored afterwards; Kalshi does not serve its own Nov 2024/2025 tapes.
(4) Run the N1-06 structural checks on that recording: control vs the balance-of-power combo; margin-of-victory vs vote-share vs winner ladders.
This is money for one night only; any live trading needs operator sign-off.

wrongful_kills.id: r2 sports-maker-cliff: NFL 'Protected' TD legs (KXNFLTDPROT), dropped in merge-M2 as HUNTER-DEAD with its re-look pushed to after NFL week 10. Every CLIFF rebate figure this round has the same problem.
wrongful_kills.why: Every CLIFF number this round spread the combo pool over ALL maker volume. Kalshi's filed rule (refute-tiebreak-20261015-R2-M-08) pays only on maker volume traded after the scheduled start, so the whole $308-461k/day pool goes to makers who quote during the game. I measured the in-play share of traded contracts from hourly candles on random settled markets: KXNFLTDPROT 42.9% (35 markets), NFL props 49.6% (59), NCAAF 83.6% (39), soccer BTTS 68.8% (39). The lane's own trade tapes stop at kickoff, so they show 0% in-play. That turns TDPROT's 7.55c all-volume rebate into about 7.55 x 0.75 (eligible-leg scaling) / 0.43 = about 13c per in-play maker contract. The only in-play cell ever measured was -5.28c gross on one week (se about 5), which nets to roughly +8c, not +2.27c. The idea was set aside because of the pre-game number (-20.64c), and pre-game volume earns no rebate at all.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Run tdprot.py now on all settled KXNFLTDPROT markets from NFL weeks 6-7 (76+ markets); do not wait for week 10. Measure in-play average maker P&L per contract (the maker gets minus the taker's P&L, settled at the result), plus the FRONT and D200 queue positions, clustered by game. Compute the CLIFF paid per in-play maker contract from combos.jsonl.gz and legvol.json, counting only in-play volume in each maker's share and applying the 0.75 scaling. Bar: in-play gross >= -4c and net >= +1c per filled contract over >= 40 games, with both halves passing. Then do the same for KXNFLTD, RECYDS, RSHYDS, the NCAAF first-half and team-total markets, KXUFCMOV and tennis set winners.

wrongful_kills.why: Both rest on the live endpoints keeping only about two months of data ('Kalshi's retained (since ~Aug 2026) tape'; 'only 5-20 favoured entries per horizon'). Two published effects have never been checked on Kalshi's own archive: the Bartlett-O'Hara single-name NO book, and Le 2026's finding that long-dated favourites are underpriced (politics slope 1.73-1.83 at one week and beyond; sports 1.74 and crypto 1.36 at one month and beyond).
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: Rerun the calib_slow.py / carry2 logic on /historical settled markets from 2023-01 to 2026-08, plus those settled live since then. Cover Politics, World, Economics (except CPI), Entertainment, Sci/Tech, Companies and sports futures/awards, keeping markets that were open for at least 14 days. Use the result, one leg per event, fit on 2023-24 and test on 2025-26, and treat the whole 2024 presidential complex as one cluster. Bar: >= +2c a contract after fee on >= 150 test events, <= 1 loss per 100 at >= 95c, and no single event > 25% of profit.

wrongful_kills.id: 20261015-R1-C3-04-P and 20261015-R2-M-13 (refuted because 'there is no idle cash; every dollar moved shrinks the pin bot's bet; pin earns 5-10x more')
wrongful_kills.why: The refuters described how the code sizes bets today; they did not measure a cost. 20261015-R1-N2-02 measured that 0 of 900 orders and 0 of 20 hedges failed for cash, that the most cash any close needed was $226 at the 99th percentile ($284 max) at 98 contracts, and that the bet stays at 98 with about $450 moved out once --bank-brake is lowered. Kalshi also pays its 4.05% APY on positions as well as cash (accounts >= $250). The round-1 critic flagged this kill reason, and round 2 used it again on two ideas. One number used against them, '-$46/day' (R2-M-11 tiebreak), is contradicted by pinday: all books made +$223.07 over 10-01..10-13, +$17.2/day. The verdicts may still stand on other grounds: 61 of the 67 cheap election legs are Republican seats that would fall together in one wave, and the gain is small (about $40 per $1,000, one-off). They do not stand on capital.
wrongful_kills.what_to_measure: (1) Rerun N2-02's capital_need.py over 10-01..10-15 with $300, $450 and $600 held in non-pin positions, adjusting the brake and the high-water-mark logic (one_coin_cap uses bank - 0.8 x hwm). Count the orders that would have been cut or refused. If none are at a given amount, the hurdle for any carry or maker book up to that amount is the APY, not pin's return. (2) For the election carry only: estimate the chance that at least 1, and at least 3, of the cheap legs lose under a common national swing. Calibrate the swing to October poll errors in 2018, 2022 and 2024, and use Kalshi's own generic-ballot and House-margin ladders as the starting estimate. Compare the carry's gain with that expected loss at the size step (1) allows. Decide before Oct 20, or drop it for this election.

weak_survivors.problem: This is the best evidence in the hunt, but it is still tape fills, not ours. At our real decision delay (+150 to +260 ms), the unseen-tape edge is +8.0c with t 1.69 by close and 1.33 by day. $72 of the $99 came from two days, 08-30 and 08-31. In BTC, the offers left for us lose (-4.1c over 60 fills). Much of the edge is the forecaster's general model-vs-market edge: the no-jump fixed 30-s and 45-s controls made +9.2c and +7.7c in Sept-Oct but only +0.6c and +2.7c on the unseen August tape. Two band losses would trip the forecaster's $27.42 day stop.

It makes $0.25-0.42/day at this account's measured fees. Crypto perps cost this account 12 bp a side as taker, so every crypto print fails; only metals and index at 0.72 bp qualify, and that is 20 prints. 79% of the qualifying prints fall in one 10-day crypto funding spike. Whether a short hold is paid the full funding is unverified. After each print the price drifts about 1 bp a minute against the side that receives funding.

The holdout makes $0.09-0.12/day at 33 pairs. There is no October window (KXCPIYOY-26OCT returns 404). On 18 of 55 in-sample package-days the print could land between the two legs, so the pair is not riskless. Every package rides one shared monthly print, and funding only runs to Dec 11.

On the held-out drift curve the taker rule fired 0 times. The maker's +$33 assumes we are first in queue. The zero-drift control also made money, so the profit is not coming from the drift. The whole case rests on one night of about 5 confused taker orders.

The forward rate it scales (+10-13% per dollar bet) comes from the 11 days since r28; the same rules earn far less on 09-30..10-03. It should feed the crypto15m-model-band-expansion sizing test, not justify moving money on its own.

This is the most decision-ready reward idea, but its cost at the 115 s exit has never been measured on our own fills. The tape says 33-50% of credit, and the 18% figure is only a floor from polling every 15 s. There are just 3 live races, and the reward is paid to the main account (pool 0), not the subaccount that posts.

All of the profit is reward. The one cost that decides it is how often a slow, stale order at the best price gets run over, and the tape cannot show that. There is no free per-second fair price either (Pyth returns 401).

Its only positive part, the reward credit, was measured during the Thursday 03:00-05:00 ET exchange pause, on a book that was not moving. Fills cost -$114/day, and 15 of 20 days lose. Treat it as dead unless credit measured in open hours beats the fill cost.

In these reward ideas the cost side contradicts the case. Treasury far strikes net -$3.48 per strike-hour because one sweeper bot clears them. On ERCOT, other reward collectors' 2c piles cut a 1c bid's reward to zero. Far-strike CPI quotes make +$1.15 per market-day, which is inside noise, with a -$970 worst week.

It fails its own calibration bar: in the fair 0.995-0.999 bin, tau 16-30, calm hours, losses ran 2.78% against 0.25% promised. The extra contracts from the size-up are bought at 98c, where losses run above break-even. The $2/day was read off a table at an assumed loss rate.
It comes from one calm regime: Jan-Mar 2026 made +0.7c, BTC's own holdout +0.6c, and October -0.8c.
Only the NO side survives, and it was chosen after YES failed. Without May 2026 it makes +3.0c at t 0.84, from about 7 NO legs a month.
It earns $0 on its own, yet the refuters of every carry idea ignore what it measured. It needs the single sizing run in wrongful kill 3 so the capital question stops being re-argued.

Their skeptics or tiebreaks refuted them, but they are still labelled plausible-needs-data. The reasons: 16:00 ET closes are only 1.46x as risky against a break-even of about 2x; the weather 97-98c edge belongs to the whole tape's makers and a capped bid cannot earn it; the YouTube rule depends on a 20c spread filter chosen after the literal rule lost; the YouTube settlement numbers are blocked even for a real browser; the coin-race variant (a) fails once post-only rejects are counted. Record them as dead unless new data appears.
These are viable housekeeping rules measured at about $0/day. Keep them as rules, not as money found.
It already fails its pre-registered bar on season half 1, and a free forward log cannot say anything before January. Keep it only as a READS_DUE log.
Superseded. Because only in-play maker volume counts, the score-concentration trick matters only during games; fold it into sports-inplay-cliff-maker.
M-11 covers the same payments with less exposure, and the fees now kill it: this account pays 12 bp as taker on crypto perps. It also needs a second account at Coinbase.

The CLIFF combo rebate ($308-461k/day, $9-14M/month; see the r2-sports-maker-cliff facts) is paid only on maker volume traded after the scheduled start (filed text, refute-tiebreak-20261015-R2-M-08). So all of it goes to in-play makers, and every pre-game test this round used a rebate that does not exist. In-play share of traded contracts, measured by this critic: KXNFLTDPROT 42.9%, NFL props 49.6%, NCAAF first-half/team totals 83.6%, soccer BTTS 68.8% (critic-r2/inplay_share2.json, tdprot_share.json). So the rebate per in-play maker contract = the all-volume figure x 0.75 eligible scaling / in-play share: about 13c on TDPROT and about 1-4c on NFL props. (1) Recompute the CLIFF per in-play maker contract by series with cliff_an.py, counting only in-play volume in each maker's share and applying the 0.75 scaling (combos.jsonl.gz, legvol.json; pull fresh combos for Sunday 10-18). (2) Measure in-play maker P&L by series from the public trade tape, pulled THROUGH the game (the lane's tapes stop at kickoff). Each trade's maker gets minus the taker's P&L, settled at the result. Use the FRONT and D200 queue positions with fills_an.py on 1-minute candles. Split by game phase and by seconds since the last scoring or possession play (ESPN play-by-play with wall-clock times, free) to find quiet windows. Priority markets: KXNFLTDPROT weeks 6-7 now (tdprot.py; the in-play cell was -5.28c gross on one week), KXNFLTD/RECYDS/RSHYDS, KXNCAAF1HSPREAD/TEAMTOTAL, KXUFCMOV (13M contracts a week, 1c wide during fights), KXATPSETWINNER and KXWTASETWINNER (17M and 12.7M a week), KXNHLGOAL/PTS (missing from the catalogue, about 320k/day), and soccer BTTS and corners. (3) Test the score-concentration trick (R2-M-24) in play, on the same-game legs of small games. (4) Find proof of payment: any public evidence that September's CLIFF credit was paid (a help-article revision, Kalshi announcements, X or Discord), what form it takes (withdrawable cash or bonus), and whether it lands in the posting subaccount or the main account (pool 0). Bar: rebate + in-play markout >= +1c per filled contract at D200 over >= 40 games, both halves > 0, and >= 2,000 fillable contracts a day at 20-lot orders. Give money for a $300 pot and at $5,000, and the worst night (a TD-prop maker caught by a score at 20 lots on 10 legs is about -$150). Read-only; <= 1,500 public calls; scratch under 100 MB.

This is the biggest family no lane ever saw: the catalogue is missing the AAA DAILY gas ladders. The national ladder KXAAAGASD trades 190k contracts a day (14.6M settled since 08-22). The 50 state ladders KXAAAGASD<ST> trade about 1M a day together. CA, FL, IL, TX, NY, NC, GA and MI have each settled 1.3-2.4M contracts since late August, and 25 states were listed after 09-24. Each ladder has 17 strikes 0.5c apart, pays the normal taker fee with no maker fee, settles on the gasprices.aaa.com state average, and closes at 23:59 ET the night before the print (critic-r2/gas_probe.json, catalogue_gap.json). It has the pin shape: 51 markets a day, an exact public settlement number, and tomorrow's AAA value is mostly today's station prices. specs.bot_name: v-sidefield (live-bot change) + kdrift.py (read-only Kalshi API drift watcher) -- not a new trading bot
specs.what_it_does: Makes the live bots keep working, and say so loudly, when Kalshi deletes the old 'which side did the taker buy' field (taker_side) or flips how the order book reports NO prices (use_yes_price). Today our code reads only taker_side, so its removal would silently switch off the seller check and flood the forecaster log; a book flip would make YES entries miss and NO-position insurance be priced wrong. A small watcher reads Kalshi's changelog every 6 hours and our own tape every hour, and pushes an alarm the moment either change is announced or appears.
specs.data_feeds: No new market data. (1) The bots' existing WebSocket trade and orderbook_delta channels (fields taker_outcome_side, taker_side, taker_book_side; yes_dollars_fp / no_dollars_fp snapshot levels; price_dollars deltas). (2) Public docs, 3 GETs per poll every 6 h: docs.kalshi.com/changelog/index.md, /changelog/rss.xml, /getting_started/order_direction.md (not the trading API, so no shared rate limit). (3) Read-only tape: newest complete hour of C:/kals/kalshi_data/orderbook_snapshot (~42 KB/hour) and the first 20,000 prints of the newest complete trade hour (measured < 0.2 s each). Today: 20,000 of 20,000 prints carry all three side fields (2026-10-17T01Z), 64 of 64 two-sided snapshots legacy in each of 10-16T23Z..10-17T01Z (sentinel_probe.json); earlier 2,287,061 of 2,287,061 prints and 75,771 of 75,771 snapshots (test folders).
specs.decision_rule: A. Side of a trade = taker_outcome_side if yes/no, else taker_side if yes/no, else taker_book_side (bid=yes, ask=no, per Kalshi's docs), else None. Rolling 60 s window of prints per connection: >= 10 prints and >= 90% with no side -> feed_alarm 'side_missing' (those prints dropped; the seller gate reads None and stands down = today's behaviour; NO trading halt); >= 10 prints and taker_side absent on >= 90% while taker_outcome_side present -> feed_change 'taker_side_removed' (fallback carrying it); >= 10 prints and > 1% disagreeing -> feed_alarm 'side_disagree' (outcome side wins). Each at most once per 600 s, via livebook's existing _trade_event queue; pinrun writes feed_alarm / feed_change records; watchlive alerts on them; pinphone pushes them. Forecaster engine: same helper, a None side skips the print, bad_trade lines rate-limited to 5 then 1 per 60 s. ordercli.order_collateral: outcome_side/book_side first, then legacy action/side, unknown -> count x $1.00 (never the cheap side). B. Snapshot class: legacy if maxYES + maxNO <= 1 and not (minNO > maxYES); yesleg if minNO > maxYES and not legacy; else ambiguous / one_sided / neither. Entry gate crossed_book: refuse an ENTRY (never a hedge) when yes_bid >= yes_ask; placed below the hedge pass, above toxic_fresh. book_convention alarm: >= 2 snapshots decisively of the unexpected class on this connection, or 1 plus >= 3 markets crossed within 10 s -> feed_alarm + halt record; refuse every NEW entry for the rest of the run, keep the hedge pass running; operator restarts flat with the right --book-convention. C. --book-convention legacy (default, subscribe frames byte-identical) | yesleg (send use_yes_price:true, store NO price p as 1-p before keying; if the subscribe is refused naming the flag, resubscribe once without it and keep converting); built now, armed only on Kalshi's dated notice or a convention alarm. K. kdrift: new changelog block (sha1 not seen) that is not Margin-only and matches the ALARM regex (a field/flag/channel/endpoint our code reads) AND the CHANGE regex (remov|deprecat|no longer|breaking|renam|default|will be|stops|instead of|replac|returns an error|HTTP 4xx|semantic) -> ALARM; CHANGE only on a Predictions/WebSocket/REST entry -> NOTICE; any change of order_direction.md -> ALARM; tape: snapshot verdict yesleg or MIXED, taker_side present < 99%, none-of-three > 0.1%, or disagree > 0.1% -> ALARM; a failed GET is an error record (never 'no change'); 3 failed polls in a row -> 'watcher_blind'. Back-test of these exact rules on 315 changelog entries of the last 12 months: 11 of 11 changes that touched a bot like ours flagged (8 ALARM, 3 NOTICE), 104 flagged entries a year (~2 a week), and the 2026-05-06 taker_side deprecation is flagged ALARM (watch_backtest.json).
specs.sizing_and_limits: Places no orders and changes no size. Main bot (~$1,155, 98 contracts) sizes are untouched; the only new refusals are crossed_book (measured 0 crossed books in 7,556,823 healthy two-sided book states and 0 of 1,140 decision-window samples) and the convention halt (cannot fire on a legacy feed: 0 decisive yes-leg snapshots in ~76,800). Money: $0 income; expected loss avoided ~$0.005-0.06/day now and ~4x at $5,000, and $0 to the main bot while --toxic-fresh stays OFF (live start record 10-15 04:42Z). Worst plausible day if NOT done: seller gate back ON and taker_side removed silently -> about -$72 at today's bank (worst measured day of that class, 10-07), about -$310 at $5,000; a silent book flip -> -$90 to -$190 (one or two unhedged 98-contract NO losers; an estimate, not measured), about 4x at $5,000. Worst plausible day CAUSED by the change: the halt or crossed gate firing on a healthy feed -> that day's entry income, about $19/day net at today's bank (+$190.73 over 10-04..10-13), about $80/day at $5,000; expected cost ~$0 at the measured false-fire rate. Watcher limits: 3 docs GETs per 6 h, read-only tape streaming, < 1 MB/month of logs, stop file results/kdrift.stop, never writes under C:/kals. Forecaster log flood (~0.38 GB/day if taker_side vanished) capped to < 1 MB/day.
specs.paper_mode: N1 tape NULL: replay three complete tape hours (a US afternoon such as 2026-10-15T18Z, an overnight hour, a weekend hour; one hour at a time, < 200 MB) through the old and new livebook on_frame; sample taker_flow(tk, side, 3 s) and best() for every ticker and side each second. Pass = identical on 100% of samples, 0 alarms, 0 crossed. Planted controls on the same hours: strip taker_side -> identical taker_flow and one taker_side_removed; strip all three -> side_missing within 60 s of tape time; NO prices at 1-p -> book_convention on the first two new-market snapshots and crossed on >= 99% of YES-favourite states (refute-stats measured 781,765 of 781,765). N2 live shadow, 1 hour, read-only: new and old LiveBook side by side, each on its own WebSocket, on the main bot's 10-20 markets; compare best()/taker_flow() at 1 Hz; pass = 0 mismatches over >= 3,000 market-seconds and >= 2 quarter-hour closes, 0 alarms (check the account's connection limit first). N3 pinrun paper startup with the exact live argv across one 15-min and one hourly close: self-test PASS, start record has livebook_sha and book_convention, 0 error, 0 feed_alarm, 0 crossed_book, signals carry sell_share_3s. N4 (gates arming part C only): ws_flag_test2.py re-pointed at two real LiveBook instances (legacy vs yesleg), >= 30 min, >= 2 closes, >= 100,000 aligned deltas, 0 mismatches of the internal book and best/rungs/buyable. kdrift: --once immediately from a session (no restart), then --loop with the operator's yes. Self-tests (each must FAIL with its fix reverted, checked from a scratch copy): livebook +~12, pinrun +~8, bettor_paper/fc_variants +~4, ordercli +3, watchlive +4, kdrift +~10, listed in SPEC.md section 3.

L1 v-sidefield live (READS_DUE sidefield-live, due deploy + 7 ET days, every settled main-bot market in them, expected ~300-400 markets and ~41-74 signals a day): KEEP if 0 feed_alarm while kdrift's tape check shows the fields present and the feed legacy, 0 crossed_book refusals on a legacy feed, sell_share_3s non-null on >= 98% of signal records (baseline 340 of 341 = 99.7%, 10-09..10-16), 0 new error records from livebook or the event loop, trade_feed events still only 'subscribed' (baseline 33 in 8 days, all subscribed). REVERT at once on any of those, or if a spot-check of 20 orders shows any order or hedge different from what the old build would send on the same book. If Kalshi removes taker_side inside the window: pass needs a feed_change within 60 s and sell_share_3s non-null >= 98% afterwards. L2 kdrift (READS_DUE kdrift-14d, due start + 14 days): pass = >= 95% of scheduled polls (4 docs + 24 tape a day) logged without error, every changelog entry of the 14 days logged within 6 h of its RSS date (hand-checked on day 14), every ALARM read to the operator and acked, 0 tape alarms on a healthy tape; kill = one missed Predictions/WebSocket removal or default change, or > 10 false tape alarms. L3 part C arming (READS_DUE bookconv-arm, opened by the first kdrift ALARM naming use_yes_price or a dated flip): N4 pass, deploy --book-convention yesleg while flat BEFORE Kalshi's posted flip date; keep if 1 ET day shows 100% yesleg snapshot classes, 0 book_convention alarms, 0 crossed_book refusals. Pre-deploy gates: N1 100% identical on 3 hours; N3 clean.

specs.risks_and_open_questions: For the operator: (1) build v-sidefield into the next main-bot restart (ladderboost + this), before --toxic-fresh goes back on? (2) on a book-convention alarm, halt new entries until a restart (this spec) or keep NO-side entries running (their prices stay right under a flip; only NO-position insurance is mispriced)? (3) may kdrift --loop run always-on and push alarms to his phone through pinphone? For the builder: (4) watchlive -- this agent measured that it matches none of the 582 alarm-like side-bot records in the last 30 MB of the forecaster, forecaster-orders, ladder and pinracepenny logs (they key records by 'ev', and pinracepenny writes 'live_halt'); the fix alerts on (kind|ev) in {halt, live_halt, stop, stop_file, exit, error, feed_alarm, feed_change, hedge...}; whether ws_error/rest_error (113 + 167 in the forecaster log) should alert or only be counted is open. Not measured: the yearly chance Kalshi removes taker_side; how long a silent removal would go unnoticed today; the money cost of a flip day (reasoned from code only); the forecaster and ladder books under a flip (bettor_paper.Book has the same 1 - max(NO) shape as livebook, assumed equally exposed); the account's WebSocket connection limit for N2; whether Kalshi rejects or ignores use_yes_price after removing it (part C handles both). specs.bot_name: restgate (shared resting-order hygiene gate, research/restgate.py) + restaudit (read-only NULL/paper audit of every maker bot's live order log, research/restaudit.py) + restgate_demo (one-time demo-only probe)
specs.what_it_does:
This is not a trading bot. It is a gate that every resting (good_till_canceled) order body must pass before it is signed. It does five things:
- It stamps cancel_order_on_pause=true on every resting order.
- It sets expiration_time so the exchange itself ends the order at the earlier of the bot's own planned cancel and the market close.
- It forces the market's real exchange_index onto every create, cancel, decrease and amend.
- It blocks re-posts into a crossing or stale book, and blocks new orders in the 60 s after a Thursday reopen.
- It stops the ladder's wasted cancels after the close.

It is worth $0/day on today's bots (measured). It exists so that the maker and reward bots this hunt proposes never leave quotes up into a Thursday 05:00 ET reopen. In the first second after the 3 measured reopens, makers lost -4.78c a contract.
specs.data_feeds:
No new feed.
1. GET /markets/{t} (public) for close_time, status and exchange_index. exchange_index is the authoritative shard: 0 = weather and everything else by default, 2 = crypto and commodities, 3 = tennis, baseball, basketball.
2. Long-lived bots only: the market_lifecycle_v2 WebSocket (activated / deactivated / close_date_updated), and optionally user_orders, to see cancels made by the exchange.
3. Our own live order logs, for the audit:
   - results/ladder-live-orders.jsonl (15,098 placed orders, 09-28..10-16)
   - racereward-live.jsonl
   - dipsell-live-orders.jsonl
4. Demo probe only: POST/DELETE on the DEMO base, plus GET /portfolio/orders/queue_positions.

The pause window is computed in ET from the US DST rule written in code, because there is no zoneinfo/tzdata on this box. Thursday 03:00-05:00 ET is 07:00-09:00Z now and 08:00-10:00Z after 11-01.
specs.decision_rule:
Applies to every body with time_in_force == good_till_canceled, before signing. restgate.rest_violations must return [].

(1) cancel_order_on_pause is True.

(2) expiration_time is an int, with now < expiration_time <= close_ts, and equals min(close_ts, planned_end_ts). planned_end_ts per bot:
- ladder: close_s
- race filler: close - exit_s (60 s now, 115 s in C2-02)
- dip seller: candle hour H + 10,800 s
- long-lived quoters: now + DEADMAN_S (900 s), refreshed at 450 s by an amend that changes only the expiry (it sends the current price and total count, so queue place is kept)
MIN_LIFE_S = 0. A 2 s minimum would have refused 228 ladder orders, including 21 of its 238 filled orders (96 contracts).
IOC and FOK bodies pass unchanged and must NOT carry expiration_time.

(3) exchange_index == market.exchange_index from GET /markets. Every DELETE, decrease and amend carries the same value. Never a default, never `or 0`, never auto-route.

(4) post_only is True and self_trade_prevention_type == 'maker'.

(5) market.status == 'active'. No NEW order whose expiration_time > pause_start is placed in [pause_start - 30 s, pause_end + 60 s). REOPEN_WAIT_S = 60 comes from the measured reopen: -4.78c a contract in the first second, +0.25c at 1-10 s, +1.93c at 60-300 s. An order that expires at or before pause_start passes, so the ladder is unchanged (the NULL).

(6) A post_only re-post goes out only if the book is <= 1.0 s old and the price does not cross. After 2 'post only cross' rejects in one market within 10 s, no re-post there for 5 s.

(7) No DELETE once send time >= close_ts + 1.0 s: the exchange refuses with MARKET_INACTIVE and cancels the order itself. The order's state becomes closed_out. Its remainder stays in pending/limbo until the poller sees it terminal or LIMBO_S (60 s) passes.

(8) Changing a resting order:
- Shrinking at the same price uses POST /portfolio/events/orders/{id}/decrease {reduce_to, exchange_index}, which keeps queue place.
- A price change or a size increase uses amend (atomic).
- Never cancel then place.
Decrease sits behind --use-decrease, OFF until demo probe 4 passes.

(9) Lifecycle events:

A paper quoter replays each finished hour as if we had rested 60 contracts on each side at the best price for the first 10 minutes of every window. specs.decision_rule:
Simulated exactly as a live arm would run it. Parameters are fixed now; nothing is fitted on the paper data except G, the Kraken guard, which uses a holdout.
- Markets: every open KXEURUSD15M / KXGBPUSD15M market with an active program row (period_reward >= 500000 centi-cents = $50, target_size_fp 300, discount_factor_bps 5000). JPY/AUD/CAD are simulated and reported but are not in the bar.
- Window: from open (900 s left) to 300 s left.
- Price: rest S=60 YES at the others' best YES bid and S=60 NO at the others' best NO bid. Join the best price; never improve it (one tick inside measured -$3.6/window on EURUSD). Only while our order's YES-equivalent price is within 0.10-0.90.
- Inventory: net position (YES fills - NO fills) capped at +-60. A side with no room is not quoted.
- Re-pricing: decided at the end of each exchange millisecond. Whenever the others' best on our side differs from our price, including when the others left our price, cancel and re-post at the new best. The new order lands, and the old one dies, at t+L. Until then the old order is live at its old price with its queue place: that window is the pick-off. A landing order that would cross the opposite best is rejected (post_only).
- At 300 s left: cancel both and hold any net position to settlement.
- Fills (makersim rules): by queue, by walk-past, and by cross (a new opposite order with our_yes + its_no >= 1.00).
- Credit: the filing's walk at each whole second on the others' levels plus our live order. A second counts only if both sides reach 300. Credit = $50 x sum of (YES share + NO share) / (2 x 900), with the $1 floor and a 0.9 payout factor (1.0 shown alongside).
- P&L: at settlement, and marked at +10 s and +60 s to the book mid, with a random-sign control.
- Variant of record: S=60, L=300 ms, fifo_prorata.
- Grid: L in {50,150,300,600,1000} ms x queue in {last, fifo_behind, fifo_prorata, fifo_front}; S=100 and S=300 at L=300 prorata; a Kraken guard (pull a side for 2 s when the Kraken mid moved >= G pips against it in the last 500 ms), with G picked from {0.3,0.5,1,2} on days 1-2 and read on days 3-5 only.

Written 2026-10-17, before any FX book was recorded.

When: read after 5 complete weekdays of recording (target Mon 10-19 to Fri 10-23, about 450-470 rewarded windows per pair; at least 400 per pair with V1-V5 passing). Due 2026-10-24T12:00Z.

Variant of record: S=60, join the best price, stop at 300 s left, net cap 60, band 10-90c, payout 0.9, fifo_prorata.

Metric: net per window = credit + fills marked to the book mid at 60 s. Settlement P&L is the cross-check. n = windows; the pooled SE clusters by close time, because EURUSD and GBPUSD share closes.

GO to a live micro test (operator sign-off still needed) for a pair only if ALL hold:
- G1 at L=300 ms: mean net >= +$1.00/window, the 95% lower bound > $0, and the late half (days 3-5) >= +$0.50.
- G2 at L=300 under 'last' (worst queue): mean net >= $0.
- G3: the settlement mean is not below the markout mean by more than 2 SE.
- G4: >= 1 stale (pick-off) fill per 10 windows at L=300. Zero means the engine is blind: void, not GO.
- G5: worst window >= -$45 and worst ET day >= -$150 at S=60, on settlement.

KILL the pair if either:
- at L=150 fifo_prorata the mean net < $0 with the 95% upper bound < +$1.00, or
- mean credit at S=60 < $1.50/window.

Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE: extend once by 5 weekdays (about 930 windows per pair), then GO only on G1-G5, else KILL.

Smallest effect detectable: about $0.70/window on the markout net (per-window SD estimated $4-6, SE about $0.25 at 470 windows). Settlement alone detects only about $3.60. If the measured SD is > $10/window the report must say 'no power'.

specs.bot_name: ratehreward_paper.py -- Treasury hourly ladder reward-pair PAPER recorder (rule V2: far-strike 1c/1c pair + cancel-everything-on-first-sweep)
specs.what_it_does:
Read-only. Every weekday hour (07:00-20:59Z) it watches the 5 Treasury-yield ladders (KX2/5/7/10/30YRRATEH, about 75-80 markets an hour, $10 reward pot per strike-hour) over the WebSocket. On every strike 6-8 bp from the yield implied by the ladder, it places an invisible "ghost" 1c/1c pair (1,000 on the safe side + 1,100 on the dead side, both at $0.01). Second by second it scores what that pair would earn under Kalshi's filed reward formula against the real book. From everyone else's 1c stacks it works out how often a 99c sweeper would have taken ours, under the new rule that all our pairs are cancelled the instant the first sweep shows up anywhere in that hour's ladders. It settles the COST side and the credit-if-paid. It cannot settle whether Kalshi pays a pair from one account; only a signed-off live probe can.

New in this spec (public GETs, about 1,100 calls):
- Programs are still listed for Mon 10-19: 1,092, one on every strike. Ladders are now 15-16 strikes, down from 17-22.
- The sweeper was active in 6 of 14 hours on 10-15 and 7 of 14 on 10-16.
- 6-8 bp stacks were swept at 1.72 per hour: 16 sweeps of 500+ lots over 9.28 stack-hours, in only 5 sweeper hours.
- Within a sweeper hour, 41 of the 50 later sweeps came more than 60 s after the first. The sibling cancel exploits that gap.

Rough per strike-hour if paid and alone (arithmetic, not measured):
- V1, hold to close-600 s: -$4.45 to +$0.88.
- V2: +$0.9 to +$5.0, depending on how many of our stacks a sweeper takes in one burst.

Paper $/day = $0. Expected value if it ever goes live is about $20/day, and the payment unknown dominates that number.
specs.data_feeds:
(1) Kalshi WebSocket orderbook_delta + trade via research/livebook.LiveBook (existing key, read-only market data) for the hour's RATEH tickers. REST book GET only as a fallback, at most 1 per second.
(2) Kalshi public REST, auth=False, at least 0.25 s between calls, 10 s back-off on HTTP 429:
- /markets?series_ticker=&status=unopened|open -- tickers come from the API, never built by hand.
- /incentive_programs?status=upcoming|active -- paged. period_reward is in centi-cents (100000 = $10); target_size_fp; discount_factor_bps; period HH:00:00-HH:59:00 = 3,540 s.
- /markets/{t} -- result and expiration_value, read at close + 3 min.
- /markets/trades?ticker= -- post-close audit against the WebSocket trades.
- /series/{s}/markets/{t}/candlesticks -- only for the --history back-fill.
That is about 150-250 GETs an hour.
(3) Optional: Yahoo ^TNX/^FVX/^TYX 1-minute bars, logged as a covariate only (a Cboe index, not the settlement source).
Not available: the settlement source, Pyth Hermes/benchmarks, returns HTTP 401. So the yield is read off the ladder itself (the interpolated 50c crossing).
specs.decision_rule:
PRIMARY V2 (the only rule the bar judges):
- At HH:00:30, per tenor, y_hat = linear interpolation of K where the ladder's YES mid crosses 0.50. No crossing -> skip the tenor-hour.
- Candidates: 6.0 <= |K - y_hat| x 100 < 8.0 bp. Dead side = YES if K > y_hat, else NO.
- Refuse a candidate if:
  - the hour is in the blackout list (8:30/10:00 ET major releases, FOMC statement and press-conference hours, 13:00 ET coupon-auction hours; the list is committed before the first run);
  - its program is not listed or the list is unreadable;
  - the opposite best bid is >= $0.99 (a post-only order would cross);
  - others hold >= 200 lots above 1c on the safe side (our safe share would be ~0);
  - the day risk budget is full.
- Post the ghost: 1,000 safe + 1,100 dead at exactly $0.01, expiring at close-600 s.
- SIBLING CANCEL: on the first dead-side 1c trade of >= 100 lots on ANY RATEH strike >= 4 bp from its tenor's y_hat this hour, cancel all our pairs on all tenors (cancel time = WebSocket receipt + 300 ms). Post nothing more that hour.
- Never re-post a side after a fill.

When a ghost counts as swept (E_main, pessimistic, used by the bar): any real dead-side 1c sweep of >= 100 lots this hour, on any tenor, at a live distance <= the ghost's + 0.5 bp, that lands before the ghost's cancel time. The first sweep of a sweeper hour is assumed to hit one ghost. Hours with no observable stack get the observed sweeper-hour rate (marked imputed).

Safe-side fill: if y_hat crosses K by >= 1 bp before the exit, charge -$10.

Credit = $10 x (yes share + no share)/2 x counted seconds/3,540, using the filed walk: reference = first level reaching 200, cutoff at 1,000, 0.5 per tick below the reference. A second counts only if both sides hold >= 1,000. The post-July rule applies (no 99c exclusion). $1 floor per market-period, then x 0.9.

Logged-only variants: V1 (no sibling cancel), V2w (band 5-8 bp), V2s (skip the hour after a sweeper hour).
specs.sizing_and_limits:
Paper mode risks $0. The virtual pot of $300 mirrors the planned live subaccount 4 (subaccounts 1-3 are taken).
- Collateral: $21 per pair.
- Day risk budget: 22% of the pot at the start of the day ($66). Checked BEFORE each post as: realised loss + $11 x pairs resting + $10 x pairs within 3 bp + $11 <= budget. So at most 6 pairs are at risk on a fresh day.
- Credits never refill the budget: they land 22-60 h later, in MAIN pool 0.

Live-stage rails (not built here): price exactly $0.01; counts exactly 1,000 / 1,100; post_only; expiration_ts = close-600 s; never a strike < 6 bp from y_hat; never a blackout hour; one pair per strike-hour; stop file; at most 3 writes a second.

Worst day by construction: -$66 at a $300 pot. At a $5,000 bank (pot about $1,000): -$220. Capital stops binding at that size; supply (about 10-15 band strikes an hour) and the sweeper bind instead. At the current bank (about $1,155 main) the $300 subaccount is about 26% of it.

File: research/sweep/ratehreward_paper.py. GET-only: the self-test asserts there is no order endpoint, POST, DELETE or request body in the source. About 40-60 MB, one process (results/ratehreward-paper.lock).
- Log: results/ratehreward-paper.jsonl, about 2-5 MB a weekday. Record types (ev): start, hour_plan, post, score10, episode, sweep, cancel, vfill, hour_summary per variant, day_summary, audit, error, stop.
- State: results/ratehreward-paper.state.json, rebuilt on restart.
- Stop file: results/ratehreward-paper.stop.
- Modes: --selftest, --once, --minutes N, --history YYYY-MM-DD (candle + tape back-fill with the same estimators), --report (the bar).

specs.bot_name: gasreward_paper.py (research/sweep/) -- paper recorder + scorer for a 200-lot top-of-walk liquidity-reward quote in the 9 thin new-state AAA gas daily ladders
specs.what_it_does: Every 3 minutes in the evening window (the last 6 h before close, which is 6 PM-midnight ET) and in the morning window, and every 15 minutes in between, it reads the public books of the near-money strikes in the 9 thin state gas ladders (AK ME MT UT NM KS HI MS WY). For each side it works out where a 200-lot bid would have to sit to hold at least 90% of Kalshi's $100-a-day reward on that strike, never bidding within 15c of our model fair. After each close it replays the public trade tape against those paper quotes (fills, settlement, markouts) and adds up reward minus fill cost per evening for a $300 and a $2,000 paper pot. It decides whether the money position the tester found on a static morning book exists and survives in the evening. It cannot decide whether Kalshi pays that share: only a micro-live run the operator signs off can.
specs.data_feeds:
All public, unauthenticated Kalshi REST via kauth.get(path, params, auth=False). No /portfolio path anywhere.
(1) GET /markets?series_ticker=<S>&status=open (cursor), every cycle, for the 9 thin ladders, the national KXAAAGASD, and control ladders TX NY CA FL OH at the slow cadence. Gives strikes, floor_strike, strike_type, close_time, price_level_structure and yes_bid/yes_ask (used for the near-money pick and the national implied median).
(2) GET /markets/{t}/orderbook, near-money strikes only. Reads orderbook_fp yes_dollars/no_dollars; the unit comes from the field name.
(3) GET /incentive_programs?status=active|upcoming&limit=5000 (cursor), every 30 min. Gives period_reward (centi-cents), target_size_fp, discount_factor_bps and start/end per market_ticker.
(4) GET /markets?event_ticker=<S>-<YYMONDD>, settled events. Gives AAA prints (expiration_value) and results: the last 30 dates at start, then daily after 11:30Z.
(5) GET /markets/trades?ticker=&min_ts=&max_ts=&limit=1000 (cursor), after each close, for every strike that was near-money. This is the fill-replay tape.
(6) GET /series/{s}, daily. Reads fee_type; a maker fee is subtracted if one ever appears.
Budget: ~20,000 GETs/day (an estimate), peak ~0.4/s, at least 0.25 s between calls, 10 s back-off on 429. The cadence doubles if 429s exceed 1% of calls in an hour.
Optional, as a separate process: .sweep/hunt-2026-10-15/r3-aaa-gas-daily-51/gb_rec.py (GasBuddy state averages), recorded but not applied.
specs.decision_rule:
Applies to strike k of state ladder S (the event for print date D) at cycle time t.

(1) Fair value.
- Primary, national-anchored: mu = p1 + 0.765 x (N_t - N1) + 0.389 x (p1 - p2). Here p1/p2 = S's AAA prints for D-1/D-2, N1 = the national print for D-1, and N_t = the national ladder's implied median now (monotone median of top-of-book mids, needs at least 3 two-sided strikes).
- Fallback (logged) and secondary: momentum, mu = p1 + 0.6070252 x (p1 - p2).
- sd = 0.75 x the rms of S's momentum residuals on prior dates (needs at least 5), else the pooled 9-state rms (at least 8), else 2.0c; floor 0.3c.
- fair = Phi((mu - k)/sd). strike_type must be 'greater'.

(2) Program terms: R = period_reward/10,000 dollars, T = target_size_fp, df = discount_factor_bps/10,000, P = end - start in seconds. No program means no quote. LOT = ceil(T/5) = 200.

(3) Ticks come from price_level_structure: linear_cent = 1c everywhere; tapered_deci_cent = the taper; anything else is refused.

(4) Price per side X (YES; a NO bid at q is a YES ask at 1 - q):
- cap_X = min(fair_X - 0.15, best ask on X - 1 tick).
- p_X = the lowest tick price in [0.01, cap_X] at which the filing's walk (racereward_live.walk) gives our LOT at least 90% of the side. If there is none, no quote on X.
- Secondary, logged: the tester's D1 bid = floor(fair_X - 0.15).

(5) A strike is quotable if at least 1 side is quoted and both sides reach T with our quotes added. Rate r = R/P x (sh_YES + sh_NO)/2; collateral c = LOT x (p_YES + p_NO).

(6) Pots: hold quotable strikes by descending r/c, at most 2 per ladder, while total c stays within the pot ($300 for A, $2,000 for B). A held strike stays held unless its r/c falls below 0.5 x the best unheld candidate's.

Scoring, after settlement, with no look-ahead:
- The quote in force is the last snapshot at or before the trade time, and no more than 2x the cadence old.
- Reward accrues R x dt/P x (sh_YES + sh_NO)/2 while both sides qualify. A side stops accruing at its first fill. A strike-period total under $1.00 counts as $0.
- Fills: a taker_side 'no' trade at a yes price below p_YES fills our YES bid. A taker_side 'yes' trade at a yes price above 1 - p_NO fills our NO bid. Ties fill only in the tie variant.
- Fill size: the primary (pessimistic) model fills the full remaining lot; a capped model, min(count, remaining), is also logged. One fill per side per strike-evening: that side is pulled and the other stays.
- Paper day stop: once filled cost reaches 25% of the pot, counting unsettled fills as lost, no new holds.
- Settlement: (y - b) x q for YES, ((1 - y) - b) x q for NO. Maker fee 0 unless /series says otherwise.
- Markouts: the next trade at +5 and +60 min, with a random-sign control.
- net_stress = reward + 2 x pessimistic fill P&L.
specs.sizing_and_limits:
Paper only. The bot uses its own paper pots and never reads a balance or the account.
- LOT = ceil(target/5) = 200 per side per strike, the smallest size that sets the reward reference price on its own.
- Pot A $300: the idle cash at today's ~$1,155 bank, and the size of a later micro-live. Pot B $2,000: the $5,000-bank case. Plus an unlimited "all quotable" view of the whole population.
- At most 2 strikes per ladder per pot; one fill per side per strike-evening.
- Paper day stop at 25% of the pot ($75 for A, $500 for B), counting every unsettled fill as lost.
- Never bid within 15c of fair on a side; never cross.

Worst day for the paper: $0.

Worst plausible live evening, if it ever goes live:
- Pot A, 2-4 strikes picked off at the full lot: about -$150 to -$300, which is 13-26% of the main bank. That is why it needs its own subaccount pot.
- Pot B, ~10-14 strikes on a day the national price moves: about -$500 to -$900. Basis: the worst holdout date on the tape at 200 lots over all 153 strikes was -$229 (national-anchored) and -$481 (momentum), times a 1.5-2x gap between tape and live.

Expected money if it passes AND Kalshi pays the computed share (neither measured): ~$12-15/day now (range $0-75), and ~$50-150/day at $5,000 until competitors respond.
