specs.risks_and_open_questions:
(1) Every dollar is the reward share. The case that makes the money, a small order ABOVE much larger stacks, has never been paid to us. Coin race only proved the case where we sit alone on an empty side, and that credit landed in MAIN pool 0, not the subaccount that posted. The paper cannot decide this; only a micro-live the operator signs off can.
(2) The farmers re-price all day: top-of-book width went 84c -> 16c by 3 PM ET, and KS 3.98's YES bid went 16c -> 95c. Incumbents can join our price (halving our share) or step a tick ahead (leaving ~1/3). The paper holds the share fixed between 3-minute snapshots, so its reward is an upper bound, and it cannot see anyone reacting to OUR order.
(3) Established ladders show only 0-3 toppers per snapshot after 53 days of the same pots. Either nobody found the trick, or those who tried were picked off. The bot logs how long toppers survive on the control ladders to tell which.
(4) New orders attract sweeps. R3-M-01 found that sweeping follows supply, and coin race's live fill cost ran 1.5-2x the tape. The 2x stress is a guess based on that one family.
(5) The fair goes stale on days the price moves: makers resting 30c or more below fair lost 21.4c a contract. The national anchor helps, but its coefficients were fit on tiny samples; they are frozen, not refit. GasBuddy (R3-M-06) can be recorded alongside but is not applied.
(6) Evening books may not reach the 1,000-lot target on both sides (Maine: 2 of 17 strikes on 10-15). K3 kills on this.
(7) NOT MEASURED: whether Kalshi nets the collateral of two resting bids on one market, and whether resting orders on gas (pool 0) lower the balance pinrun (pool 2) sizes from. Both get read in the micro-live dry run.
(8) Programs on the thin ladders are only days old. Terms are re-read every 30 min and each evening is scored on the terms in force. Strikes added during the day get the same $100 over a shorter period, so a higher rate; how often that happens is not measured.
(9) ~20,000 public GETs a day share the live bot's IP. Whether Kalshi's unauthenticated limit is per IP is not measured.
(10) Only 14 clusters. The smallest detectable effect (~$27/evening) is an estimate; the bar is fixed and will not move.
(11) DST ends Nov 1. Windows come from close_time and program dates, never from a hard-coded hour.

specs.bot_name: approvenight_paper -- research/sweep/approvenight_paper.py (PAPER recorder + engine; Trump-approval night-only two-sided reward quoting)
specs.what_it_does: Every night from 18:45 to 08:05 ET it records the full order books of the 9 daily Trump-approval strikes (KXTRUMPAPPROVE) from public data. Each morning it replays the real trade tape against those recorded books, with our virtual 100- and 300-contract bids added on both sides of the most-likely strike. It books Kalshi's liquidity reward ($600 per strike per day, read from /incentive_programs) and the profit or loss on fills together. That answers the one open question: does the reward earned through the 19:00-03:00 ET evening, which nobody has ever recorded, beat what the fills and the 08:00 ET sale cost? It never sends an order, never signs a request and never opens the key file.
specs.data_feeds:
All calls are unauthenticated GETs through a local urllib public_get(). There is no kauth import, because kauth opens kalshi.pem on import.
- /markets/{t}/orderbook, full ladder: the rank 1-3 strikes every 10 s, all 9 strikes every 60 s.
- /events?series_ticker=KXTRUMPAPPROVE&status=open&with_nested_markets=true every 10 min.
- /incentive_programs?status=active|upcoming every 15 min. Pot (in centi-cents), target, discount and window are read, never assumed; past programs include $100 and $300 pots and a 0.05 discount.
- /exchange/status every 5 min and /exchange/schedule hourly. The schedule has a Thursday 03:00-05:00 ET closure, given in ET wall-clock time.
- Morning pass: /markets/trades?ticker=&min_ts=&max_ts=, cursor-paged, for every strike that was ever rank <= 3, pulled a second time to check the tape is complete; /markets/{t} result after the 12:59 ET close; /series/KXTRUMPAPPROVE for fee_multiplier.
- Load: about 24 calls/min (0.4/s), about 19,000 a night.
- No RCP feed. On 10-17 at 02:45Z, realclearpolling.com returned HTTP 403 to stdlib urllib, with both plain and browser headers. When RCP adds a poll is therefore not measured.
specs.decision_rule:
Night = 19:00:00-07:59:59 ET, labelled by the event date. The 10-31 -> 11-01 night is 14 real hours. Quote only when the exchange is open (schedule AND trading_active) and an active program with period_reward > 0 covers that strike.

Primary cell V0:
- Strike: the rank-1 strike, meaning the highest mid = (best YES bid + 1 - best NO bid)/2 at the last 60-s full scan.
- Orders: one YES bid and one NO bid, each at OTHERS' best bid on its side, size min(S, room). S = 100 (the bar) and 300.
- Re-post at the back of the new queue whenever others' best differs from our price or our order is used up.
- Net position capped at +-S; the side that would grow it is pulled.
- If a strike loses rank 1, its orders are pulled and its position is kept.

Fills:
- Trades are grouped into bursts by (created_time, taker_side). taker_side 'no' hits YES bids at yes_price; 'yes' hits NO bids at no_price.
- No trade below our price: fill = min(r, room, X - A); A = max(0, A - X).
- A trade below our price (the taker went through our level): fill = min(r, room, tot - min(A, X)); A = 0.
- Queue at each poll: A = min(A, visible size) for the pessimistic case (the bar), or a pro-rata version as the optimistic bracket.

Credit:
- The filed walk from racereward_live.walk: reference where size reaches target/5, stop at target, weight 0.5^ticks below the reference, both sides must reach target. It runs on others' orders plus ours.
- Dollars = reward x (share_yes + share_no)/2 x dt / period. dt is sample-and-hold capped at 30 s. Closed and gap seconds count 0. Under $1.00 per program period counts 0.

At the first book at or after 08:00:00 ET:
- Matched YES+NO pairs are held to settlement at $1.
- Unmatched contracts are sold into the recorded bids, best first, as one taker order; fee = ceil(0.07 x sum(c p (1-p)) x 100)/100.

Secondary cells (hypotheses only):
- V1: step out for 600 s after a sweep through us or a touch move of 3c or more.
- V2: rest at the filed reference price instead of the touch.
- V0 on the rank-2 and rank-3 strikes.
- V0s: V0 with a night stop at -20% of the pot.

There are 18 cells in total; the bar reads one.
specs.sizing_and_limits:
Paper pots are virtual and no money moves: $200 for the S=100 cell, $600 for S=300.
- S = floor(pot/2/$1), rounded down to 10, max 300. About S x price resting plus S x price held covers the worst capital use.

Process limits:
- About 30 MB of memory, one instance (results/approvenight-paper.lock, an msvcrt byte-range lock copied from racereward_live.InstanceLock).
- Stop file results/approvenight-paper.stop.
- Never over 1 call/s averaged. On HTTP 429: back off 10 s; after 5 in 10 min, halve the call rate.
- No raw writes under 15 GB free disk.

A later LIVE version is out of scope and needs the operator's GO, because it is a new strategy family:
- New subaccount 4 (1, 2 and 3 are taken), funded $200.
- S = floor(pot/2), capped at 100 for 15 nights; post_only GTC orders via ordercli's path.
- Night stop -20% of the pot; run stop -$100.
- The 10-11 coin-race reward landed in the MAIN account (pool 0), not in the subaccount that posted.

Money:
- Paper costs $0.
- If it passes at the bar's floor and live matches: about +$15/night (about $450/month) at 100 a side, on about $200 tied up, at the current $1,155 bank.
- At $5,000: about +$10 to +$50/night (300 on rank 1 plus 100 on rank 2). It does not scale, because one strike carries the pot.
- Worst plausible night: about -$53 to -$80 at 100 a side; -$166 to -$182 or worse at 300.
specs.paper_mode:
Paper only by construction. The file has no kauth import, no ordercli, and no 'portfolio', POST/DELETE/PUT, KALSHI-ACCESS or request body anywhere; the self-test checks this from the source text.

Three parts:
1. Recorder loop, 18:45-08:05 ET:
   - Raw books go to results/approvenight-books-YYYYMMDD.jsonl, gitignored, about 19 MB a night, gzipped to about 3 MB the next morning. The build commit adds results/approvenight-books-* and approvenight-tape-* to .gitignore.

2. Morning pass at 08:05 ET (or --night YYYY-MM-DD):

Cell: V0, S = 100 a side, pessimistic queue, rank-1 strike, 19:00-08:00 ET, leftover sold at 08:00 ET.

Nights counted: consecutive NORMAL nights from the first full night. A night is normal when:
- the rank-1 book is <= 30 s old for >= 90% of the night seconds the exchange is open;
- the second tape pull is identical to the first;
- there is one open event;

- under 1% of trades have mismatched side fields.
Thursday's 03:00-05:00 ET closure is left out of the count. More than 3 non-normal nights among the first 13 calendar nights means the recorder is broken: fix it, do not read the bar.

EARLY KILL after 3 normal nights:
- KILL if V0 credit is under $24 on 2 or more of the 3. $24 is 2x the measured night fill cost at 100, and about 55% of the one measured share.
- Printed but not binding: credit rate at S=300 of $90/day or more on 2 of 3 nights.

FINAL after 10 normal nights (about 10-11 days). PASS only if all four hold:
1. mean V0 net >= +$15/night;
2. net > 0 on at least 7 of 10 nights;
3. summed net > 0 on nights 1-5 AND on nights 6-10;
4. no night worse than -$75.
KILL if mean net is under $0 or fewer than 5 of 10 nights are positive. Otherwise run 10 more normal nights with the same bar on all 20; there is no third extension.

Smallest detectable effect at 10 nights: about $16/night (two standard errors), assuming a nightly spread near $25. The fill side is about $19 from 29 tape nights; the credit side is unmeasured, and the read prints the measured spread.

Any other cell or hour window that beats V0 is a hypothesis, scored only on the next 10 fresh nights.

A PASS rests on recorded books plus the trade tape (source rank 2), with a virtual order nobody reacted to. So a PASS only earns the live test:
- With the operator's sign-off: 100 a side from subaccount 4 for 15 nights.
- Live bar: credit landed in the main account's pool 0 is at least 60% of the engine's modelled credit for those nights AND at least 2x (fill loss + sale cost).

specs.what_it_does: Every evening at each city's close minus 30 h (7-10 PM ET, which is 7 PM local daylight time), it reads the next-day KXRAIN book for about 35 cities. It works out the day's rain chance from the newest NOAA NBM forecast (NBS text) that was provably public before the read. When that chance beats the book's price by at least 10c after the taker fee, it books a PAPER buy of the cheap side and holds it to settlement. It sizes that buy only from size really shown on two reads 1 s apart. It also logs the numbers that are still unmeasured and that decide whether the replay edge survives a live reader: depth, the cost of walking the book for 20 and 50 lots, how the book drifts toward the model over the next 2 h, other takers at our price, and every market's result.
specs.data_feeds:
(1) NOAA NBM NBS text from the public AWS bucket noaa-nbm-grib2-pds (blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/text/blend_nbstx.tHHz).
- Cycles: 18Z and 20Z-23Z of D-1, plus 00Z-01Z of D.
- Method: HEAD for Last-Modified, then GET Range bytes 10000000-21800000. That range holds the K-station block; 486 of 486 archive files parsed from it. Fallbacks are the full file and NOMADS.
- Load: about 84 MB a night, paced at <= 2 MB/s and PAUSED from 75 s before to 10 s after every quarter hour, so the live pin bot's latency is untouched. Nothing is stored except the parsed P06 values.

(2) Kalshi public REST. Every call uses auth=False, never the live bot's key.
- /markets?series_ticker=KXRAIN&status=open: close_time, rules_primary (gives the CLI station), and best price and size for all 35 markets in one call. Also used for the drift reads at Q+15/30/60/120 min.
- /markets/{t}/orderbook?depth=0: at the decision read and again 1 s later.
- /markets/trades: fired legs only, for quote-hour volume and other takers at our price.

specs.decision_rule:
For each open KXRAIN market for target date D:

**Timing**
- Q = close_time - 30 h. Only markets with Q in [22:00Z, 03:00Z] are eligible (today: 23Z Eastern, 00Z Central, 01Z Mountain, 02Z Pacific).
- Decide at the first 15-s tick at or after Q. A decision later than Q+10 min is logged as late and left out of the bar.

**Station**
- K + the 3 letters after CLI in rules_primary, cross-checked against the tester's ST_FULL map.
- An unknown code is skipped, never guessed. Example: CLIDJT for WPB tries KDJT, then KPBI.

**Model: primary is V_NEWEST, the rule the idea's own test plan wrote down in advance**
- Use the newest NBS cycle of 20Z/21Z/22Z/23Z D-1 and 00Z/01Z D that meets all four conditions:
  - our own fetch finished before the read;
  - AWS Last-Modified + 300 s <= read time;
  - every station header names that cycle;
  - P06 exists at all four valid times.
- Skip the market if that run is more than 6 h old.
- P = 1 - (1-p06[12Z D])(1-p06[18Z D])(1-p06[00Z D+1])(1-p06[06Z D+1]).
- Logged for every market but never switched to: V_B (21Z D-1 / 00Z D, the tester's test_fresh rule), V_A (18Z D-1), and the 5c and 20c margins.

**Trade at a 10c margin**
- Buy YES if P - ask - fee(ask) >= 0.10, where ask = 1 - best NO bid.
- Buy NO if (1-P) - (1-bid) - fee(bid) >= 0.10, paying 1 - best YES bid.
- fee = each contract's share of ceil(0.07 x mult x p x (1-p) x 50 x 100) cents, with a round(..,9) guard before the ceiling.
- Our side's price must be between 3c and 97c.

**Fill**
- Walk the opposite bids best first, taking each level that still clears 10c at its own price, up to the lot.
- Paper fill = the size shown at within-limit prices on BOTH the decision read and a re-read at least 1.0 s later. This is forecaster_live's realistic rule. Floor to whole contracts and ignore levels under 1 contract.

**Hold**
- Hold to settlement, one decision per market.
- No exclusions: YES legs under 10c and Mountain legs are traded and tagged.
specs.sizing_and_limits:
**Paper pot**: a virtual $100 (--pot) that stands in for a future subaccount and moves with paper P&L.

**Three ledgers per leg**
- BAR: fixed 50 lots at the two-read fill, every leg, no caps (the bar is per contract).
- 20-lot.
- POT, with these caps (refusals are logged):
  - per leg: cost <= 10% of the pot and <= 50 contracts;
  - per quote night: new cost <= 40% of the pot;
  - held cost <= 70% of the pot, because two nights overlap for about 30-36 h;
  - <= 3 legs per region per night (rain_paper.py's REGION map) and <= 10 legs a night.

**Rails for a later live version only**: a -25% day stop per target date halts the next night; a -40% run stop; a stop file; refuses the main account; operator sign-off.

**Money**
- Paper: $0 at risk.
- Live in a ~$100 subaccount (~20 lots): about $4/day, range $1-8. Worst observed day at 20 lots was -$34; the night cap limits a disaster to -$40.
- From the main $1,155 bank, where the 50-lot cap binds: about $6-7/day, limited by book depth. With fills capped at what the trade tape proved was there: $4.62 a date over the whole sample, $7.09 on the holdout. Worst observed day -$84 to -$89 at 50 lots; a plausible bad day -$150; everything losing on a 10-leg night (10 x 50 x ~45c) is -$225.
- At $5,000: $8-15/day, still depth-bound, same worst day.
- Money tied up: about $76 typical, $170 at the 90th percentile, for about 36 h.

**Backtest rate for the season it would trade (fall only)**
- V_NEWEST: +6.9c a contract (se 3.0, 188 legs / 45 dates).
- V_B: +4.8c (se 3.1, 196 / 43).
- August's +16.9c was thunderstorm season and should not be expected.
specs.paper_mode:
**Paper only**: zero orders, unauthenticated GETs only. The self-test checks the source text for no order path, no non-GET method, no request body, no replay/pinsim/pindata import, and auth=False on every Kalshi call.

**Log**: results/rainmodel-paper.jsonl, times in UTC. Record types: start, run, plan, decision (for EVERY eligible market), fill, drift, tape, settled (for every market), night, error, stop.

**Stop and restart**
- Stop file: results/rainmodel-paper.stop.
- A restart rebuilds the decided tickers, open legs, pending drift reads, fetched runs and pot from the log, so nothing is decided twice.
- Nights missed because the PC was off are logged as missed and never filled in from candles.

**Footprint**: idle outside 18:30Z-04:30Z except for settlement checks every 2 h. RAM under 60 MB (the NBS range is parsed line by line as it streams).

**Commands**
- --selftest
- --once
- --minutes 30240 (21 days)
- --report: the E1-E5 bar lines and a verdict.
- --replay-check: pulls hourly candles for settled paper dates and scores them with the P logged at the decision, so it tests the book, not the model.

**Self-test (plants known answers)**
1. NBS parser on a made-up bulletin that includes a wrong-cycle header.
2. Run choice never looks ahead: a run fetched 1 s after the read is never used, and an 01Z run that lands at 02:05Z is not used for a 02:00Z read.
3. The 10c boundary on both sides.
4. Book walk plus the two-read fill.
5. World A, where the model is the truth and the stale book drifts 30% toward it: BAR net must be >= +5c and drift > +1c.
6. World B, where the book is the truth: net must be < +2c and drift within +-0.5c.
7. Schedule, including the 2026-11-01 clock change.
8. Fee hand values: 0.5 x 50 lots gives 88c, 0.97 x 50 lots gives 11c.
9. Every POT cap at its boundary.
10. Restore from the log.
11. The quarter-hour bandwidth pause.
12. Station mapping.
specs.pre_registered_bar:
Written 2026-10-17, before any paper number exists.

**Window**: the first 20 target dates recorded. If launched by 2026-10-17 22:00Z, that is target dates 2026-10-18..2026-11-06, with the read due 2026-11-07T18:00Z.

**Counting**: n = markets and target dates, clustered by target date. Primary rule is V_NEWEST at 10c, with no exclusions.

**PASS to a micro-live proposal needs ALL of:**
- E1 (plumbing):
  - a decision read inside Q..Q+10 min on >= 90% of eligible market-nights;
  - a run fetched before Q on >= 95% of decisions;
  - fetch finished before the decision time on 100%.
- E2 (replay match): >= 80% of paper legs are also candle-replay legs (same market, same side, using the logged P), and >= 80% of replay legs are paper legs.
- E3 (supply): median two-read fill >= 20 contracts per fired leg (cap 50), and median 50-lot walk cost <= 1.0c.
- E4 (needs no outcomes): mean mid drift toward the model at Q+120 min >= +1.0c over >= 60 legs, with the random-side control within +-1.0c. The backtest gave +2.65c and -0.72c.
- E5 (money): BAR-ledger net >= +4c per contract on >= 60 legs over the 20 dates.

**KILL if any of:**
- E5 net <= 0 after 20 dates;
- E1 or E2 fails;
- E4 drift <= 0;
- median two-read fill < 10 contracts (about $2/day or less).

**CONTINUE otherwise**: 15 more dates, same bar, no rule change.

**Early read after 5 target dates** (due 2026-10-23T18:00Z): E1 and E3 only. Kill only if E1 < 80% or median fill < 5. No money judgment yet.

**What the bar can and cannot see**
- About 84 legs over 20 dates gives a date-clustered se of about 4.5c, so the smallest effect it can detect is about 12.6c.
- A true +6.9c passes E5 about 3 times in 4. A true 0 still passes about 1 time in 5.
- So E5 confirms execution and kills coarsely; it cannot prove the edge.

**Monthly backward re-run** (due 2026-11-16T15:00Z): keep the idea only while the all-sample net stays >= +4c with the date-bootstrap lower bound above 0. The Sept-onward rate goes on its own line.

**After a PASS, with operator sign-off**: micro-live at 10 lots a leg in a new subaccount for 15 dates. Bar: realised net >= +3c a contract on our own fills, and >= 70% of signalled legs filled at the best price.

**READS_DUE ids**: rainmodel-paper-early, rainmodel-paper-20, rainmodel-backrerun.

- research/sweep/rainmodel_paper.py, ~700-900 lines including the self-test.
- --report and --replay-check, ~150 lines.

specs.risks_and_open_questions:
1. **The tester and the refuter disagree on the primary rule.** The tester's next test says use 21Z D-1/00Z D (V_B); the stats refuter says use the newest of all hourly runs (V_NEWEST). This spec pre-registers V_NEWEST, because the idea's own test plan said so before either number existed. V_B is logged as a shadow and never switched to.
2. **Depth in the 6-10 PM book is still unmeasured.** Measuring it is why the recorder exists. The richest legs (NO, +18c in fall) are also the thinnest: other takers found a median of 8 contracts.
3. **One season only, summer into fall.** Winter is unmeasured. The edge fell from +16.9c in August to +6.9c in Sep-Oct (se 3.0).
4. **The stale makers are paid** a $100-a-period liquidity reward per market. If Kalshi ends it, the supply may go with it. The recorder logs the program nightly.
5. **The model overstates low rain chances**, because the 6-h periods are correlated. So YES legs under 10c come out about even: V_NEWEST fall +2.3c on 38 legs, V_B -0.7c on 47. Its 06Z-06Z day is also 1-2 h off the local-standard-time climate day outside Central. These legs are tagged, not fixed, because no exclusion was pre-registered. Mountain was negative in the backtest.
6. **It trades against the running SJ02 rain tail NO desk** (rain_paper.py) on YES legs under 10c, 8 h apart. Harmless on paper; it matters if both ever trade one account. The report counts the overlaps.
7. **New cities appear** (WPB with CLIDJT on 10-17). They are skipped until mapped.
8. **Bandwidth**: about 84 MB a night on the live laptop's link, paced and paused around every quarter hour.
9. **NOAA outage**: the market is skipped, not decided on a stale run.
10. **PC off**: those nights are lost and logged.
11. **Evidence class**: everything so far is replay-class. The recorder upgrades it to "the book really looked like that", which is still not our fills, and E5 alone cannot prove a +4-8c edge in 20 dates.

specs.bot_name: caplend -- lend the main account's idle cash to the forecaster (research/caplend.py planner + tape-replay paper + step scorer, read-only; plus one live flag: pinrun/pinracearm --lent-dollars L)
specs.what_it_does: This is a rule about cash, not a trading bot. It comes with a read-only planner and a scorer. The main Kalshi account never uses most of its cash: 0 of 900 orders and 0 of 20 hedges ever ran short, and 99 closes in 100 needed less than $2.31 per contract of bet. The rule moves that idle cash in steps into the forecaster's subaccount 2. One new pinrun flag, --lent-dollars L, keeps every main-bot limit exactly where it would be if the money had stayed: bet 104, day stop $228.76, late-boost headroom. The forecaster's own --auto-scale (pot/630) then trades bigger. Replaying our own live orders on our tape gives step 1 an UPPER bound of +$15/day; the central guess is about +$4/day, not measured live. The scorer reads the extra contracts at the whole-account level, and the loan is called back if any kill rule fires.

specs.decision_rule:
LOAN ROOM (caplend plan; run while pinrun is flat, before every step and daily at 13:00Z)
- usable0 = sub-0 pool-2 cash.
- bank_eff = pinrun bank (sub-0 total) + L_now.
- SIZE = pinrun.size_for_bank(bank_eff) (104 today).
- R = the sum of (dollars today):
  - 0.187 x bank_eff (day stop): $228.76
  - worst_close_cost(SIZE) = 3 x SIZE x 0.98: $305.76
  - 1.40 x SIZE (two hedged legs): $145.60
  - 3 x floor(0.12 x SIZE) x 0.98 (KXBTCD): $35.28
  - floor(0.038095 x pool-2 cash) (coin race open-stake cap): $46.12
  - 1.5 x SIZE x 0.98 (one boosted market held up by a late settlement): $152.88
  - R today = $914.40
- X_room = usable0 - R = $296.41 today.
- dest_room = 630 - forecaster pot.

STEPS
- Step 0: move the $97.25 of idle cash (sub 4 $42.55, sub 3 $42.17 in pool 0, sub-0 pool-0 $12.53) into sub 2 pool 2. Pot becomes $239.75, scale 0.381.
- Step 1: min($150, X_room, dest_room). L = $162.53, pot $389.75, scale 0.619.
- Step 2, only after a step-1 PASS: min(X_room, dest_room), $146.41 today. L = $308.94, pot ~$536, scale 0.851.
- Never lend past X_room.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS (all while pinrun is flat)
1. The operator runs the ordercli transfer: dry run, then token, then --live.
2. Check that pinrun logs `external` with the Kalshi transfer id, not `unexplained`.
3. Restart pinrun with --lent-dollars L.
4. Restart pinracearm with the same L.
5. Restart the forecaster with the same argv, so its -20% day stop, -33% run stop and 70% commit limit follow the new pot.

HARD FLOOR: if usable0 < R, recall min(L, R - usable0 + $25) to sub 0 and lower L by the same amount. After step 1 the margin is $146, which about $500 of main-bot losses would use up.

LOSS OF THE LOAN: if the forecaster pot falls below 67% of (pre-loan pot + L), its run stop has fired (K4). Recall what is left and set L = 0.

PINRUN FLAG (--lent-dollars L; default 0.0 behaves exactly as today)
- size_for_bank(bank + L); apply_loss_cap(bank + L); publish_size(SIZE, bank + L).
- one_coin_cap room = (bank + L - (1 - MAX_DRAWDOWN) x (hwm + L)) / PRICE_CEILING.
- The start, autosize and loss_cap records carry lent_dollars and bank_eff.
- classify_bank_move, confirm_move, write_hwm, drawdown, the A39 reset and read_bank stay on the RAW bank.
- Start refuses L < 0 or L > 0.5 x bank.
- pinracearm: bank_sizes(read_race_bank() + L).

MARGINAL CONTRACTS (caplend score, every forecaster order after a step)
- base = min(filled, round_half_up(0.2262 x paper_k) - base already asked on that side); marginal = filled - base.
- base is priced at the order's cheapest per-level fill rows, marginal at its dearest. An IOC sweeps cheapest first, so this split is exact.
- Fee 0.07 p (1-p) per contract; the per-order round-up is booked on the marginal leg.

LOAN

specs.pre_registered_bar:
Written 2026-10-17, before any loan, flag or step result exists.

BASELINE (frozen in results/caplend-bar.json)
- Forecaster fill fraction 0.81 (587/726, 96 orders).
- Per-$ +18.2% (60 closes, SE 4.0%).
- Marginal premium ~0.0c (77 orders).
- Fill when the tape showed enough: 0.96 (74/77).
- Main fill on shared same-side sides 0.78 (25 orders, 19 sides, +$2.13 a market, 0 losers).
- 0 cash refusals.

WHEN TO READ: at max(7 ET days, 40 forecaster closes) after step 1, about 9-10 days at 4.4 closes/day. Hard stop at 21 days.

PASS (keep step 1; step 2 may be put to the operator) if ALL hold:
- P1: 0 sub-0 or sub-2 orders or hedges refused for cash.
- P2: main SIZE equals its no-loan counterfactual at every autosize record.
- P3: forecaster fill fraction >= 0.65.
- P3b: live contracts / min(ask, tape offer at our timestamp) >= 0.75.
- P4: marginal premium <= +1.5c a contract.
- P5: forecaster per-$ > 0 AND marginal per-$ > -5%.
- P6: if there are >= 8 shared same-side sides, main fill there >= 0.60 and main P&L there >= $0 a market. With fewer, it is reported, not read.

KILL (recall what is left, --lent-dollars 0, restart flat, same day) on ANY of:
- K1: one sub-0 order or hedge refused for cash (immediate).
- K2: fill fraction < 0.50 over >= 20 closes.
- K3: marginal per-$ <= -10%, or forecaster per-$ <= 0, over >= 40 closes.
- K4: the forecaster run stop fires.
- K5: main fill on shared same-side sides <= 0.55 over >= 12 sides.
- K6: P3b < 0.50 over >= 30 orders.

Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE: keep step 1, extend to 80 closes, no step 2.
Step 2 bar: the same rules over >= 80 closes and >= 14 ET days.

SMALLEST DETECTABLE EFFECT
- Fill fraction and P3b: about +-0.14 (SE ~0.05 on ~64 orders).
- Marginal premium: about 0.5c.
- Per-$: only about +-12-14% at 40 closes (SE 4.9%). It catches a collapse, not a halving.
- Main squeeze: only a drop of about 0.3 in fill, over ~10-13 shared sides.
- Proving a marginal +5% per $ at 80% power needs ~240 closes (~55 days). This test does not do that.

The placebo check must pass first, or the step is not read.

specs.risks_and_open_questions:
1. Operator rule of 10-11 ("every account must size from its own fund"). --lent-dollars sizes the main bot on its own cash plus money parked in sub 2, which the forecaster also sizes on. The tester's no-code brake/frac recipe keeps the letter of the rule, but it drifts off as the bank moves and makes the bet 1/(1-X/B) times as sensitive to the main bot's own wins and losses. The operator decides; the spec defaults to the flag.
2. The money is an upper bound from the tape.
   - Nobody has measured how often other buyers beat us to the offer at 2.7-3.8x today's order size; the control only covers today's size.
   - The extra contracts inherit r28's per-$ (+18-23%, SE ~4%). The full-size shadow's +4.7% is the pessimistic read, and the window is the forecaster's best stretch.
3. The account's worst plausible day grows from about -$300 to about -$390 at step 1 and about -$445 at step 2.
4. The squeeze on the main bot is measured only on the tape (at most $0.2/day). The forecaster sends first on 16 of 19 shared sides. Live, P6/K5 watch this, but they have little power.
5. ordercli's $100 subaccount limit refuses every loan today; it must change first.
6. If v-bankmove cannot confirm a transfer, it logs `unexplained` and does not move the high-water mark. With L added, the boost headroom then reads too low, which is the safe side. Check for the `external` record before restarting.
7. Pool 0: money that lands in sub 2's pool 0 is invisible to the forecaster, so every transfer names exchange_index 2.
8. Transfer BEFORE the restart. The other order over-sizes the main bot by L/11.76 contracts until the transfer lands.
9. Found along the way: pinrun's et_day_key is hard-coded to UTC-4, so after 2026-11-01 its DAY loss cap rolls over at 23:00 EST, not midnight. This change does not cause it.
10. At $5,000 the room is about $1,240, but the forecaster stops growing at a $630 pot. The rest pays only if another side bot proves it earns on its extra dollars.
11. Not measured: live fills and prices at bigger size, the live squeeze on the main bot, and whether r28's edge persists.

specs.bot_name: spotbracket_paper (research/sweep/spotbracket_paper.py) -- buys the BTC 5 PM ET daily-ladder bracket that holds the index. PAPER only; ETH runs as an unscored shadow arm.
specs.what_it_does: At 2, 3 and 4 PM ET (3, 2 and 1 h before the 5 PM ET close) it reads the live BTC settlement index and finds the KXBTC daily range bracket that holds it. It reads that bracket's book, paper-buys YES at the real 98-contract fill price and holds to settlement; the two neighbouring brackets are scored the same way as a control, and ETH is run the same way but never scored for the bar. Its main job is to measure what nothing has measured yet: how many contracts are on offer, and at what price, 1-3 h before the close; whether the candle prices behind the 195-event history are prices we would really get; and a no-fit index monitor that says when the calm since April has ended.
specs.decision_rule:
Market: KXBTC daily 5 PM ET event (ticker {SER}-{yy}{MON}{dd}17), every day of the week. close_ts is read from the market, never hard-coded: 21:00Z until 2026-11-01, then 22:00Z.

Width guard: BTC brackets must be 250 wide (Sat-Thu) or 500 (Fri), ETH 40. Any other width means no entries that day.

Horizons:
- Rule horizons h in {3, 2, 1} hours: decide at close - 3600h + 2 s and finish by +30 s, otherwise log 'late' and do not score.
- Observation-only horizons h in {4, 0.5}: recorded, never scored.

Index: S = the latest 1-s BRTI print if it is <= 5 s old, otherwise the Coinbase ticker (flagged). Spot bracket = the 'between' market with floor_strike <= S < cap_strike + 0.01.

ENTER if all hold:
- the bracket was not entered earlier for this event;
- best YES bid > 0;
- best YES ask is between 0.20 and 0.99 inclusive;
- the walk fills at least 1 contract.

If S is still in an already-entered bracket, log 'held' and do not enter again. A move to a new bracket is a new entry, so up to 3 per coin per event.

Paper fill:
- Walk the YES-ask ladder (1 - NO bids; units decided by the key, never the magnitude) for 10, 98 and 420 contracts.
- The scored fill is 98 contracts at VWAP plus the taker fee: the sum over levels of 0.07 x q x p x (1-p) x multiplier, ceiled to the cent per order. No slippage cap.
- Hold to settlement. P&L per contract = 1{result=yes} - VWAP - fee/98.

The neighbours (+-1) get the same filters and fills, as controls. FOMC day, Friday, edge-near and index source are RECORDED, NOT APPLIED.
specs.sizing_and_limits:
Paper:
- Fixed lots of 10, 98 and 420 are logged; the bar uses 98.
- Two virtual pots, $1,155 and $5,000, updated at settlement. Per entry: lot = floor(min(3% of pot, day budget left) / VWAP).
- Day budget = 12% of pot per 5 PM close (every entry settles at that one close), so BTC alone can commit at most 9%. That is about 100 lots at $1,155 and about 440 at $5,000.
- Virtual run stop at -25% of the starting pot, plus the monitor stop.

A later live version:
- its own subaccount;
- IOC at best ask +1c;
- at most 6 order writes a day;
- pot read from the subaccount, as forecaster_live --auto-scale does.

Worst plausible day (3 BTC entries, all miss):
- -$104 at $1,155 and -$450 at $5,000. The observed worst at 98 lots was -$93.5.
- A 10-lot live test risks about -$10.50 on its worst day.

Money, BTC only (none of it measured on our own fills):
- At the current bank: about +$4/day central. Range -$1/day (Sep 21-Oct 14 rate) to +$9/day (Apr-Aug rate).
- At $5,000: about +$18/day, range -$4 to +$41.
- ETH: $0.
specs.pre_registered_bar:
Written 2026-10-16, before any paper data. BTC decides; ETH is shadow. n = complete BTC close days (all 3 rule horizons decided on time and the spot bracket settled), about 1.7 entries a day.

EXECUTION (readable from day 7):
- E1: >= 98 contracts on offer at <= best ask +1c in >= 60% of BTC entries.
- E2: median (98-lot VWAP - best ask) <= +1.0c.
- E3: median |our best ask - Kalshi 1-min candle ask for the same minute| <= 1.0c over >= 30 entries. A failure voids the candle-based history.
- E4: own 60-print settle = expiration_value on >= 95% of days with full WS coverage.

MONEY (98-lot VWAP, after fee, per contract, clustered by close day):
- Early KILL from day 20 if net <= -6.0c.
- At 45 days:
  - KILL if net <= 0, or E1 or E3 fails.
  - PROMOTE to a 10-lot live test if all hold: net >= +3.0c; neighbour-control net <= +1.0c (otherwise VOID); E1-E4 pass; monitor >= 1.50.
  - EXTEND to 90 days if 0 < net < +3.0c; under +3.0c then is a KILL.
- Odds at 45 days for the money part (day bootstrap of 60 BTC days, 5,000 draws):

| true edge | P(promote) | P(kill) |
|---|---|---|
| +9.6c | 0.93 | 0.02 |
| +4c | 0.58 | 0.19 |
| 0 | 0.26 | 0.50 |
| -2c | 0.15 | 0.67 |

REGIME MONITOR (BTC, no fitted parameters, Coinbase hourly, trailing 60 close days):
- Below 1.50 = KILL, at any time.
- It was 1.92 on 10-14. Jun-Oct 2026 windows never went below 1.57; about 90% of 2025's windows were below 1.50; break-even is about 1.46.

ETH:
- Never promoted on this run.
- A later ETH promotion needs >= +4.0c over >= 60 days AND the pooled ETH history from Apr 1 plus paper >= +2.0c at ask+2c. Today that pool is +0.4c.

READS_DUE (add in the deploy commit): execution read at 7 days, early kill at 20 complete days, the full bar at 45 complete days (about 2026-12-01 if started 10-17).

Every piece already exists in the repo or the hunt folders. No live-bot file is touched, so there is no VERSIONS.md entry; the three READS_DUE items go in the deploy commit. specs.risks_and_open_questions:
1) NEW, measured here: ETH is not an edge out of sample. I pulled 134 older KXETH 5 PM events (Apr 1-Aug 11, via /historical; eth_hist.py, eth_hist_summary.json):
- they made -0.4c a contract; Apr-Jun was -3.1c over 90 events (per event -4.4c, se 4.2c);
- the same method on recent events reproduces +10.6c (the refuter found +8.9c), so the older null is not a method artefact;
- ETH Apr-Oct pooled is about +0.4c at ask+2c;
- ETH's index ratio never moved (1.17 / 1.20 / 1.13).
So ETH is shadow-only, and the realistic money is BTC alone.

2) The BTC regime may already be over: +0.6c over Sep 21-Oct 14, -0.8c in October (14 events), and October's monitor of 1.48 sits at the ~1.46 break-even. EXTEND or KILL is the likeliest result.

3) A paper run cannot prove a +5c edge: a true zero passes 26% of the time at 45 days. That is tolerable only because a pass leads to a 10-lot live test (worst day about -$10.50). The operator may prefer that live arm in parallel from day 1 (about -$0.45/day if the edge is zero), because only live fills show whether the 20-30k maker quote fades after our first fill.

4) Why 2-5 PM ET has been calm since April is unknown, and the calm began the month the ladder moved to $250 brackets. Jump days lose all 3 entries (kurtosis 4.5-8).

5) Depth 1-3 h before the close is unmeasured; it has only been seen 8.7 h out.

6) The WebSocket uses the main API key. If that becomes a problem, the fallback is Coinbase only.

7) The FOMC statement on 10-28 lands exactly at T-3h: it is recorded, not skipped. The 2027 FOMC list must be added before January.

8) Not checked: the same effect on the S&P/Nasdaq daily ladders and on KXBTCD.

9) A live version needs its own subaccount. Whether pinrun's v-safety2 would adopt a KXBTC range position held in sub 0 is unverified.
